title: What you see is NOT what you get!
body:
All the grandeur is simply a front! We arrived with our 2 children after a long trip from LA, and asked to be accommodated in the new wing of the hotel. Our travel agent had requested this on booking our accomodation, as we had been warned about the old section been outdated and bleak. The very helpful young gentleman at the reception told us there was nothing available until the following day. We also got told there were no interleading rooms, which we had also requested when our booking was made. We decided to be taken up to look at the room, and then make a decision. Well, I was shocked to see what the room actually looked like, let alone the fact tat my 10 and 12 year old were offered the same standard room FOUR doors down the passage. We requested to see a manager, who was on the phone!! 
After a good 20 minute wait at the reception desk, I insisted that they upgrade us to a suite until the morning. Finally we were told we had a suite in the towers but the children had to sleep on roll out beds! We decided we didn't have too much choice so late in the evening, so accepted their offer. 
Upon entering the so called suite, we were almost knocked out by billowing cigar smoke that was coming from the room next door! To say our room stank was an understatement! We accepted what it was and made a plan with towels to try and block the worst of the smell from coming through the connecting door in our passage. 
By this stage it was almost 11pm so we decided to order room service, which set us back $350! The service charges were ridiculous. We had come from the Sofitel in L A which is rated around the same as this hotel. It comes nowhere near it! Not even a free bottle of water in your room, let alone the usual gesture of a chocolate on your pillow! The amount of laundry that could be reduced with the simple 'green' steps of re-using towels, would easily allow for free water and a measly chocolate. We had up to 8 fresh towels daily, even though our towels were hung up!
The concierge was extremely unhelpful, and managed to send us to a so called good restaurant, which left one of us with food poisoning!
The Sunday brunch was the only good thing, the spread of food was outstanding! Oh but I forgot to say it set us back $400! The icing on the cake for us in this over rated, pompous hotel! You pay for what you get in life, this was simply a rip off! I will definitely not come back, and look forward to experiencing the Sofitel in NY next time, as it is consistent worldwide!

title: Just Fine, Eventually
body:
My wife and I decided to stay-cation and took the train into the city for a night away from our infant. We arrived early (at 1pm) knowing the room would likely not be ready, but we figured we'd check our bag and come back later. They were fine with this and accomodating, and to their credit the line moved nicely at check-in because most of the counters had staff. I was told I'd receive a text when the room was ready but when no text arrived at 4pm, I called myself and was told everything was in order. Our request was for a room on a higher floor, away from the elevators.
Upon reaching our room, it was on a higher floor (13) but the closest to the elevator possible - not so good for a light sleeper. I phoned guest services and requested another room, and our request was granted. We were indeed still on a high floor (11) and now farther from the elevator (great) but the room had obviously been freshly painted and we could not take the fumes. I called guest services again and was told they would come with air fresheners while we were at dinner. Two complimentary drink tickets were a nice touch from management for the rough start.
Back from dinner, still a noxious odor of paint. I decided I need to personally speak to management and went downstairs. I relayed all which had happened to the sympathetic front desk staff member, and he spoke to a manager and, though I knew the hotel was relatively full, we were redirected to a junior suite which met all of our original criteria (high, quiet). This really salvaged the night's stay and renewed my faith in the hotel after the initial debacle. 
The room was quite clean, spacious, the bed was comfortable and the big-screen TV was nice. The bathroom could have used a spruce-up but was big and clean. We found all of the staff we encountered to be friendly and helpful.

title: Special Trip - Nice Hotel
body: My husuband booked this hotel for my 50th b'day weekend. It is a nice hotel. I agree with a previous review, I think I expected more, the hotel itself was a bit dated. The outside is under renovation with most covered in scaffolding (no noise problems the 2 nights we were there). The lobbies are all very grand, historic and beautiful. The staff was top notch and customer service was very good both check-in and departure. It was conveniently located and we walked everywhere. When visiting NYC again, we most likely would not stay at the Waldorf; I think for the price there are other options we would explore. For wonderful NY bagels, walk down to Ess-a-Bagel ... so good (ask at the front desk, they gave us directions).

title: Elegant with Excellent Service
body: Everything about this hotel was great, but you have to remember it is not modern and therefore doesn't have certain amenities. For example, it is really hard to access with a stroller, but the staff tried to help as much as possible. Overall, the service is incredible and the ambiance is charming.

title: Great hotel for the money
body: Family of 6, 3 rooms. My family has taken a holiday trip to NYC every year for the last 20 years and we always enjoy the Waldorf. Rooms are recently refurbished with comfortable beds and elegant appointments. If you stay overnight Saturday, you must experience the Brunch at Peacock Alley on Sundays. Exquisite dining awaits at a reasonable $75 per person.

title: Iconic
body:
My husband and I were visiting NYC for the first time as a new year treat to celebrate the completion of my cancer treatment. We wanted somewhere comfortable and central. 
Our cab from the airport meandered through the traffic and skyscrapers of Manhattan to drop us off at the main entrance to the WA. Unfortunately the hotel is having some exterior works done and our initial view of this iconic building was blurred by the protective coverings. Once through the 5th Avenue revolving doors and up a seemingly small staircase the iconic lobby appeared and we found ourselves surrounded by the opulence and grandeur for which the hotel is known. Checking in was easy as there were no queues and we took our own bags up to our room although we could have opted for a uniformed bell boy.
We stayed in a standard (deluxe) Queen room. It was an adequate size for a downtown hotel room with an extremely comfortable bed with excellent pillows and high cotton content bedlinen. There was a huge TV screen facing the bed. Our room faced onto the street (didn't work out which one) and we had a view of the opposite hotel rooms - so kept the blinds down when we had the lights on!
The bathroom was a decent size with a bath and shower. The shower took a while to get hot and I had to get my husband to work the handle. This was a bit frustrating as my first impulse on arriving was to jump into the shower but I had to wait for the water to catch up! Once I had it sussed though it was fine.
Free wi-fi is available in the lobby and there is a Starbucks on the premises - at the 5th Avenue entrance. This is a premium Starbucks and charges premium prices - even though they had run out of cinnamon. 
There are several places to eat in the hotel but we didn't check them out as we wanted to get out as much as possible. We didn't use room service - after checking out the prices. I wanted a massage in the Guerlain on site spa but at 180 dollars for 50 minutes I decided against it. 
We enjoyed our stay in this historic landmark. We stayed there for the ambience but if we visit NY again will probably stay somewhere a little smaller and less iconic. The hotel was quiet when we arrived but became very packed as there was a convention of psychoanalysts on during our stay and this made the lobby a little uncomfortable!
On checking out we were charged for an item in the mini bar that we hadn't had but this was soon sorted out. (I had made the mistake of using the mini bar as a fridge to cool my own juice and it had automatically recorded this as a sale).
On our second night at the hotel we were woken by loud voices in a nearby room which was disconcerting. My husband mentioned it to the staff the next day and was told that he should have reported it the night before when it was actually occurring.... 
Staff we encountered were friendly and helpful.

title: No dinner room service
body:
I have stayed at the Waldorf many, many times over the years for both business and pleasure. The hotel is centrally located in Midtown East, and is very convenient to my office. It’s also well located for walking to Broadway, Rockefeller Center and Fifth Avenue. 
One thing I kind of like about staying here is that I never know what kind of room I will get. They are all different but for the most part a good size for New York. I’ve had some really fabulous rooms and also some normal nice rooms. The hotel is old and most of the rooms could use some updating but still they are just fine. The bathrooms are hit and miss. Some of them are quite small but others have dressing areas and are larger. The bathrooms have been somewhat updated, not a total redo but updated. 
On my most recent trip last week I had a few glitches, which surprised me. The first glitch was that the smoke alarm did a beep beep every five minutes. I called to have it looked at and ultimately there was a problem that could not be fixed so I was moved to another room at 11 at night. Ok. They did move me, so that was good. The second glitch which took me by complete surprise is that during the month of January and February the hotel has decided, for economic reasons, not to offer room service for lunch or dinner. What?? This is not a small hotel. I am a female travelling for business and I don’t want to have to eat alone at a restaurant when I don’t have dinner plans. So, if this is important to you just know that you can only eat in your room for breakfast until March. 
Overall I like the Waldorf, and I will continue to stay there. It’s not hip and ultra-modern but then neither am I so it all works well.

title: Famous Does Not Equal Greatness
body:
I’ll admit it, as a jaded traveler I was actually excited about my 1st stay at the world famous Waldorf-Astoria in NYC. But famous does not equal greatness. 
At $263 per night (Jan. 2012), it was “reasonably priced” for NYC. The services at the front desk as fantastic (thanks Caroline) and the place has character. As a Diamond VIP I was upgraded to a Jr. Suite and it is the size of an average NY apartment. 
So what does it lack? Ironically enough, THE hotel that invented room service DOES NOT OFFER room service! I assumed a flagship Hilton in downtown NYC would feature 24-hour room service. No! They do offer some form of limited service during the breakfast hour, but if you think you are getting a pizza & beer to watch the game – think again. 
And no coffee pot? Really? No room service and no coffee pot? They expect guest to bring their own pot from home of waddle down to Starbucks in their PJ’? I’m stuck here for a week so tomorrow I am going to guy a coffee pot for my room. Maybe I’ll ask the manager to take if off my $1,500 bill when I check out? 
Also on the downside, the room is cold and drafty and the bed does not live up to the current Hilton standard. 
I will not stay here again and in fact I am going to look at other Hilton options ASAP. I might move out tomorrow.

title: Disappointing
body:
On arriving at the hotel our car delivered us to an underground enterance. On having our cases taken from us we were then pointed in through a door into the hotel and then found ourselves lost. After wondering around for a few minutes the porter found us and showed us the lift and told us to go to check in in the lobby.
Check in was painless and we were shown to our room. The room was a Queen room bus was very disappointing. The furnishings were old and the décor was tatty. The room was of adequate size as was the bathroom. 
My biggest disappointment was the lack of room service after 10:30 in the morning. I kid you not you can only get room service between 06:30 and 10:30. There is also no tea of coffee facilities in the room so if you want anything to eat or drink you have to leave your room and go and find it for your self.

title: Gorgeous, historical & great location!
body:
The Waldorf Astoria is full of elegance, charm and class. It is located in the heart of New York City. Shops, eateries, restaurants, etc...are easily accessible either by taxi, on foot or the subway trains. On a nice day, you can stroll through the city to Times Square or St. Patrick's Cathedral, which isn't far from the hotel. This stay was during New Year's Eve. Luckily, the weather was wonderful, making it possible to have a comfortable walk to Times Square for the ball drop. There is a Starbucks located within the establishment, which made it convenient for a quick breakfast or snack. There are a couple or so restaurants as well. 
The breakfast brunch buffet is magnificent, fit for royalty! You can array of exquisitely prepared options. The bar/lounge is lovely for a cozy break before dinner or just to relax. Their chocolate martinis are yummy! The staff at the reception were friendly and helpful, although the bar/lounge staff was a bit indifferent. 
The room was small (considering it's much older), but was quaint and clean. The bathroom didn't have counter or sink space, except for a little enclave in the wall. You might not be able to put all of your toiletries in there (somewhat frustrating). Although, your provided mini shampoo/conditioner/lotion do include a designer brand (Salvatore Ferragamo). That's luxury for you! The noise from the traffic below can be a problem. The view from this particular room was limited partial city and another building. Not too exciting. 
If you need to stow away your luggage for a certain period before you check in or after you check out, there is a place in the hotel for it. I believe they normally charge a fee. It was complimentary this time for whatever reason. Check with the hotel first. 
Do take the time to explore the hotel. It is huge and grand! You will discover plenty of history on the establishment, founder, all the bygone celebrities, dignitaries and royalties.

title: Old fashioned but still a must
body: Lots of factors makes this place a must in NYC, the history of this hotel is fashinating as so many people from all over the world have stayed here. The position is just perfect to reach the hot spot in the city, staff was mostly friendly. My Suite was in the Towers where a nice private breakfast room is provided with a low profile service and buffet self service. The Sunday Brunch held in the main lobby was a gorgeous food offering. The only negative note I have is about the steam room which looks terribly poor and low mantained and it contrast with the Spa design.

title: A must !!!!
body:
I have just returned after a week at the Waldorf with a friend. I read all the reviews before I went and was a little worried. I have never been so happy in a hotel anywhere.
The staff are all first class from front desk to bell boys. We were lucky enough to meet a gentleman called Jimmi who had worked at the Waldorf for over 40 years, He made our holiday, nothing was to much trouble for him, he rang us on our last day to say goodbye. even though it was his day off. You dont get service like that in many places.
If you get the chance please stay at the Waldorf Astoria,

title: Beautiful historic hotel!
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for a long weekend. It was a wonderful experience! We arrived mid-day on a Sunday and upon check-in were given an upgrade to a suite. Check-in was smooth and efficient, with a helpful staff. There were always several staff members present in the lobby, by the desk, the concierge desk, on the doors, by the elevators, etc. All were professional, helpful and friendly.
Our room looked out over the side street, and sadly, the entire facade was encased in sheeting, so our view was somewhat muted; however, in January the sky was drab anyway. Our sutie was quite large, with a king bed, fake fireplace, easy chair and desk. The bathroom was spacious, with marble flooring. A large tv and a fridge gave us all the "comforts" of home. 
The bed was very comfortable, with fresh linens every day and a nightly turn-down service. 
Maid service was efficient and un-obtrusive.
We did not partake of the Sunday brunch (arrived too late), nor did we take afternoon tea. We did enjoy a delicious breakfast each of the three mornings of our stay. It was pricey, but delicious; honestly, all our meals in NYC were pricey. 
When one stays in a historic hotel, with an iconic name, a certain amount of ambience is to be expected. We loved seeing the placques and pictures placed through the lobby and hall walls noting former well-known guests and events. But all this would be for nothing if the beds were uncomfortable, the place was dirty or dated. 
The Waldorf Astoria is a grand old hotel that has managed to retain its historical integrity and integrate it with an up-to-date understanding of modern-day hotel requirements for a discriminating traveler.

title: the hotel could not bear responsibility for there personals
body: We were travelled to New York on January 2012.For our accomodation we've chosen this hotel. The day befor departure we bought in Apple store three iphones.They were new in boxes, when we returned to the hotel we put them to the suitcase,but unfortunatly didn't close it. It was our mistake! When we came back to home we and opened the luggage(it was locked during all flight) we saw that one box is opened and the most expensive iphone is stolen. This small incident spoiled the impression of grate city! Choose for your accomodation more reliable hotel. Marina Revenko

title: A tick in the box, but not worthy of superlatives
body:
Forgive me for being disparaging about something which I know is an American institution, but the historical importance of the WA aside, it really is capable of being described as shockingly overrated. I think most people have articulated similar thoughts far better than I can, so I'll say the following...
Dates: 10/01/12 & 11/01/12
Rate Type: ADVANCE PURCHASE / Rate per night: 229.00 USD / Total for Stay per Room: Rate 458.00 USD / Taxes 74.56 USD / Total 532.56 USD / Total for Stay: 532.56 USD
The staff courtesy levels varied from poor to ok, but never quite reaching what I'd call 'good' much less 'excellent', considering it's a 4-5* (depending on where you look). If you're hoping to get treated individually, reset your expectations in advance and you'll be ok. You're one (or a group) amongst thousands and you'll be treated as such.
We were fortunate enough to be Hilton H Gold VIP or whatever the term is, so we received:
- complimentary room upgrade (can't compare to the level below, but I saw no evidence of anything warranting an 'upgraded room' tag)
- 4 complimentary drinks vouchers worth $20 each, and
- a 30% off voucher for the onsite Guerlain Spa for treatments over 50 mins (massages, basically). By the way - these are also available in the Guerlain shop simply by asking for one, if you plan on using the spa.
Since I had pre-advised by e-mail that were also celebrating our engagement, we received 2 additional cocktail vouchers and frankly, that was a generous gift on the basis that the hotel has no obligation to offer anyone anything for free...so for that we were grateful.
But here are the reasons I take issue with Waldorf=Astoria [sic].
1) The check-in really is shoddy for a 5* hotel. It's chaotic and understaffed for an hotel of this size
2) The room temperatures are set at 23c/73f throughout the entire hotel and cannot be adjusted from your in-room controls (why install a redundant temperature control gauge in there then, you ask?). After the first night sweltering in our room I went to reception the next day and was advised that the hotel 'climate' is controlled centrally. I asked how to reduce it and was advised that I could "open the window". Hmmm...first 5* query goes off in my head.
So there's your choice: 23c/73f (our house is usually set at 20c/68f), or whatever melange you get by opening the window and combining 23c with outside air temp at the time.
On this point I'd also mention that as a consequence during the night, we were both gasping for water and in the absence of anything else, I threw caution to the wind and cracked open 2 bottles of water from the MiniBar (schoolboy error, I know). When they subsequently applied a $20+tax per 300ml bottle charge to my bill, I took exception and brought it back to the reception desk. I'd have paid a 'reasonable' charge, but under the circumstances I felt aggrieved. What really made me laugh out loud was when the guy at the front desk looked indignant and explained to me that I had chosen their "Premier" water. I nodded knowingly (in that condescending way that apparently only Brits can do), as if I'd suddenly understood his explanation, and that $76/litre of water ($347/gallon) was remarkably good value!
Then I told him to remove it and stop wasting both our time. He did, but looked very hurt.
3) Without the vouchers we were fortunate to have received, you're looking at $18-24 + tax + tip per drink, which explains why the majority of people in the bars are corporate suits on an expense budget. Again I am conscious that being the W=A [sic], they feel justified in sifting out undesirables at the bar by having high bar prices, but it's as well to be forewarned.
It's an ok hotel, it really is. And if you've never seen art deco hotels like The Savoy, or you live out of the city/state/country and have always loved the images of Marilyn Munroe and JFK staying here in the 60s, then it's probably worth the tick in the box.
But if you've got a budget, want real value for money and are happy to just drop in and have a cocktail to take your photos, I'd suggest that NYC has far better places in which to stay for similar or less money. It's a tourist destination, not one in which I suspect many East Coast Americans would ether stay or would get excited about.
Oh - and I didn't mention it to my fiancee when we were there, but there were plenty of telltale signs that the maid had not cleaned the bathroom properly after the previous occupants had left. I leave that to your imagination, but I hate it when that happens and it immediately turns my stomach..
Hope this helps.

title: 1st Time in NY and Waldorf
body:
My partner surprised me for my 40th a trip to NY staying at the world famous Waldorf.
My first impressions of the hotel was very good and i was very excited, this didnt last long.The staff in the Peacock bar seemed to look down their noses at us, and were quite short and sharp when seating us, not making us feel welcome.
I awoke early on our first morning ( time difference i supposed) and when i read that the hotel had 24hr room service i thought i would treat myslef to a pot of tea.
Who would think that a top Hotel in one of the worlds best cities, could not / would not even provided a pot of tea for it's guest.Our room was comfortable, but old fashioned with wall paper coming of in the bathroom.
However we did not let this spoil our stay and NY and my whole surprise was great, just wouldnt visit the Waldorf again, it seemed that if the staff didnt think you were loaded then they didnt have much time for you.

title: Amazing service, classic elegance
body:
I have stayed here on and off for some 20+ years. I had a bad experience a few months ago, and the management responded quickly to address my concerns and asked me to let them know when I was returning.
Upon arrival, they made sure to personally take me to my upgraded room on the Towers side and there was a small welcome gift from management, and a personally signed card. 
The room was very formal with furniture reminiscent of my grandparents - but this is the Waldorf Astoria, so it's what I was expecting. IT was very "gilded" and yet still comfortable, and quiet.
There was a sizable bathroom, though fairly dated, and the remains of cigarette burns on the side table took a small amount of the elegance away.
As a Diamond member, you receive breakfast vouchers for Starbucks, and also two drink vouchers (which are valued up to $20), along with Free internet. The staff (as they always have been) was excellent throughout the stay.
This hotel has location going for it, a grand lobby, a crazy Sunday brunch (alas, had to be working), but it's really about the history. For me, I generally prefer more modern but I will always have a soft spot for this property, and I appreciate the management responded to my issue, and ensured I had a much better experience on this trip.

title: Go just for the awe and the history, outstanding service
body: But you must be forgiving with the old building. Our room (817) had new heating control which worked fine, but also an old unit below the window which blew cold air all the time, and there was now way to turn it off. Our room also just happened to have a kitchen fume smell to it...must have been coming up from some restaurant...that said...the staff are outstanding, the hotel lobby is gorgeous, the history of the hotel is amazing, pretty good size rooms for NYC, wonderful beds, linens and amenities....

title: Pre QM2 treat.
body: We stayed here for three nights as part of a Cunard package for New Years eve in New York and then a QM2 trans-atlantic sailing back to UK. Our airport transfer from JFK to the Waldorf was also part of the package and we duly arrived at NYC on New Years eve. The main entrance and reception area is magnificent. The corridors to the bedroom are large but bare and a bit dated. The bedroom was large and comfortable. The toiletries in the bathroom were a treat amd replaced daily. The Grand Sunday Brunch Buffet was superb with so much choice from breakfast or roast dinner to Lobster, oysters and loads of tempting desserts, all washed down with a glass of chilled Champagne! At a cost of $125 per person with the strong pound against the dollar it was worth every penny. All the staff were so very helpful, nothing was too much trouble. We would definately like to stay here again.

title: No thanks- I will never stay here again!
body: What a disappointment. Having been to New York City many times I had never stayed at the Waldorf and my husband and I decided to treat ourselves to a "no kids" visit to this historic hotel. First, we arrived to find the hotel under construction although there was no indication of this when I booked the room. The only good thing I could say is that you are able to pull off the busy New York Street and into a covered parking area to unload your luggage. Check in was quick and our Bellman was wonderful and claimed to have worked at the hotel for 40 years. As we walked into our SMALL room the bellman informed us that the only room service the hotel had was breakfast, "a corporate decision". Arriving later in the evening, exhausted from our travels, we were really looking forward to in room dining so we were forced to find local delivery. Unfortunately the local delivery left me sick and at 3am I wanted a sprite or gingerale which was unavailable because not only do they not have room service but they do not have vending machines!! We did have an in room "bar" but it had nothing but alcohol, nuts and gummy bears. When I called the front desk asking for gingerale or sprite they told me that I could walk several blocks over to the CVS- in 13 degree weather- I don't think so! The fun didn't stop there we ordered a coffee maker, but it NEVER got picked up and we never received coffee refills. Let's talk about the room- uggggg. The wall paper was peeling off the wall, the ac/heating vent was LOADED with dust and the bathroom was so small that the door almost hit the toilet. We received beautifully wrapped glycerin soaps that got really goopy but were never replace until we threw them away AND when you take a shower, the curtain blows into you and touches you- YUCK!!!! Oh and one more thing- we visited the 2 bar/lounges which both served up drinks for $18 a piece and Peacock Ally was like sitting in a fish bowl. We asked to order bar food but were told they had no food because the kitchen was being "remodeled" (funny how they are able to make breakfast) but we did receive wasabi peas which went wonderfully with my chocolate martini- NOT!!! I am sorry but I have stayed in hotels all over the world, nice hotels, and this place was not at all what it should have been, especially for the price.

title: Not up to expectations.
body: My wife and I stayed at the Waldorf last weekend. It was fine but I was hoping for so much than that from such an iconic hotel. We stayed at the Plaza a few years ago and loved it. I guess we were hoping for that type of experience. Instead we we let down over and over again. We arrived and walked through the revolving door where a bellman asked if we wanted help with our bags (there are stairs immediately upon entry and no sign telling you how to get to the hard to find elevator) but before we could answer he said he would be right back. After a couple of minutes I just toted them up the staircase myself. We entered the beautiful lobby (really classic) and onto the registration desk where we waited in line like we were in the Post Office. Even though we were early our room was ready and we headed up to a small and unimpressive room that looked like it was due for a makeover. It did have a nice large bathroom but the shower had a slight smell of mildew and almost no water pressure. It was cool so we turned on the heat and discovered we had two options with the ancient looking heater, we could freeze or sweat. On top of these conditions the hotel was hosting a wedding in the lobby that night! We could not even enjoy the lobby and were rerouted into a very crowded and uncomfortable area to try and get one of the slow elevators. We had to wait for twenty minutes. I was amazed that they would inconvience thier guests this way. The dissapointments continued the next morning when we asked the concierge where we could eat breakfast nearby and were sent to a very average cafe. The next mornign we found that we were very near one of the best bagel places in the city and had a much better experience at ess a bagel. Also, would it kill them to put a coffee maker in the room? I will say that we asked for late check out and were given it without hesitation which was very nice and the location of the hotel is fantatstic. In all it wasn't a bad stay just not nearly what we had hoped for.

title: Charming, historic, grand hotel
body:
Staying here is always more than just a night of lodging; it's an *experience*. Now, it may or may not be the experience that you, in particular, are seeking, but it's certainly an experience.
I've stayed here once a year or so for the last 15 years. Some folks say the place has gone downhill. I feel quite the opposite. To my eyes the Waldor=Astoria has gotten consistently better and better at giving us the best of the old, along with the best of the new. This was the first trip for my wife, and she absolutely loved the place.
Of course, the common spaces are grand, formal, lovely and inspirational. The dining options are numerous and uniformly excellent. (Please have at least one drink while reclining in Sir Harry's.) And we were given a spacious, corner, two-window room with a king bed and excellent views on the 25th floor. The room was spotless, impeccably appointed and contained every possible modern amenity, including an enormous LCD TV, a well-lighted closet, a comfortable desk, and two large, comfortable, upholstered chairs.
OK, so there's only space for one person's toiletries on the pedestal-style sink in the bathroom. It's a minor issue (and our only nit to pick). The shower wonderful -- hot, hot, hot, with a strong, strong spray. And the towels were the best you'll find anywhere - super thick and soft.
So go and enjoy it! If you shop around and are flexible, you can get a night here for no more than a cookie-cutter hotel. So why not have an *experience*?!

title: Economical yet luxurious
body: My son booked a couple of rooms at the Waldorf for a 3-night stay in New York. I was amazed at how reasonable the price was considering the stature of this hotel. It is a landmark in NYC and lived up to its historical prominence with its vast candelabras, marbled entrance hall, beautifully appointed rooms and excellent service throughout. The only down-side was the fact that the exterior is undergoing some refurbishment but inside it is just as beautiful as you would expect the rich and famous of bygone eras to have graced.

title: Wonderfully, Gloriously Glamorous!
body:
My partner booked a surprise Christmas break in New York with a 3 night stay at the Waldorf - I knew it's name of course but thought I'd check out the reviews on here before we arrived: I needn't have worried though - yes, our room was a bit tatty but it was clean and large and airy and furnished in such a cosy, traditional way it reminded me of hotels as they used to be - comfortable! Our bed was so comfortable I had a great night's sleep every night! The linen, pillows and duvet were all new; not lumpy or tatty and we had a great view of St Bartholomew's from our window too! 
The public areas were wonderfully glamorous and we felt like the proverbial 'million dollars' as we arrived and the staff, who were courteous and polite and cheerful only endorsed this feeling.
We had a wonderful holiday sightseeing and would happily stay at the Waldorf again.

title: Hark back to years gone by and be treated like a silver screen star.
body: This hotel is truly a historical New York landmark with its opulent and grand decor, its famously ornate chiming clock where many a rendez-vous takes place and most significantly it's attentive and capable staff. They are numerous due to the vast size of the hotel but work harmoniously within their fields to ensure an efficient and dedicated level of service is acheived. The Diamond desk ladies are wonderful and Mary Macias in particular always ensures we have a warm and genuine smile to greet us and provides more than we need for our stay. F & B Manager, Jeff Krauthamer is a stellar part of the team and goes above and beyond for us and other guests using his extensive knowledge of the Hotelier industry and his can-do attitude to always deliver more than expected. Thank you to all at the Waldorf, we are regular guests for a reason and consider this our home from home.

title: Impressions of a 1st time guest
body:
I have stayed at only a handful of 5-Star hotels in my travels; two Fairmont properties and a Ritz Carlton as examples. Admittedly, I am primarily a Hilton / Marriott business traveler. On a recent business trip to NYC however, I found that the hotels I was familiar with were all fully booked. Had Expedia not offered a "head-turning" rate on the Waldorf Astoria, I sincerely doubt I would have ever stayed at this property whether for "business or pleasure."
I fully enjoyed this property and the relentless pursuit of service demonstrated by their entire staff. My room was both elegant and comfortable. While an older landmark hotel, the bathroom was still spacious with wonderful lighting and I had no trouble establishing a Wi-Fi connection at my stylish desk. Many hotels lay claim to "dream beds" but the standard Waldorf Astoria pillows, sheets and mattress that I experienced were perfect in every way. 
While the check-in was quick and efficient and bell captain storage of my luggage for several hours was appreciated, it is the assistance of Graham at the Concierge desk that I will detail. I've always stayed in the Broadway area and had no knowledge of Park Ave area restaurants for a business dinner that would not wreak havoc on the per diem. After some thought, Graham reccommended the Benjamin Steak house and it was frankly terrific. A short stroll away that I can heartily endorse. (I haven't verified this but apparently an individual from the famous Peter Luger establishment is involved in the Benjamin Steakhouse and it shows) 
I am glad that I was able to experience the Waldorf Astoria on a first-hand basis as a guest. I'm also pleased to report that somehow this hotel managed to over-exceed even my expectations.

title: Classic service, nice accomodations
body: I stayed at the Waldorf twice in the last year. The most recent stay was the nights of 1/23 and 1/24/2012. As a Hilton Honors member I was upgraded to a superior corner room on the 10th floor. The famous Waldorf Towers have the top floors of the hotel. I don't know how many they have, but most floors are the regular hotel. I saw the beautiful Grand Ballroom - make sure you check it out if you're in the neighborhood. It kind of looks like Carnegie Hall! The service is outstanding at this hotel, but my room wasn't real special. The furnishings are a bit old and the heating/ac system also is a bit dated. The room was comfortable - but you are not paying top prices here - the regular base Waldorf does not have high prices by NYC standards. The Towers is pricey - and I don't know what the rooms are like up there. The location of the hotel is ideal. Lots of history there. I hear the base rooms are small - so always go for an upgrade.

title: "Don't let the Name fool you"
body: I was too excited after reviewing the pictures online and thinking, Wow, this is where they filmed several movies, the Presidents stayed here. First of all let me say if your a Modern Day person, this is totally not the place for you. I arrived thinking that I would be blown away with look of the lobby just from the pictures, boy was I disappointed. The lobby is average and in fact I've seen better especially for $319 a night. I arrived to my room, thinking ok I know the rooms will blow me away, but instead when I arrived at the room, I wanted to run a way and ask for a refund. The bathroom was super small and OLD. I figured I'd make the best of it, that is until I went to take a shower and shut the door and for some reason it got jammed, I'm thinking what the heck, after me jingling it a few times it opened, but I didn't close again (lol). The doors had cracks in it and it looked as if someone had painted over it with some cheap stale looking paint.... After touring the hotel, I found they had some nice cute little shops, but expensive. On Sundays they serve brunch for $95 per person, but who in they right mind would set brunch up in the main lobby where people are continously walking in and out of the hotel and the food is totally exposed and not covered. I couldn't not believe this, but this goes to show you because of the name you can't assume the its Greatness. The Hiltons need some serious upgrades in this hotel, the corridor leader leading toward the room smelled OLD.... Good luck to those who want to stay here, because next time I'm going to try modern day hotels.

title: A fab place, brilliant location and good staff
body: This hotel is perfectly located and has brilliant staff. I stayed there for 4 days and they did everything possible to make our stay plesant and well. I highly recommend this to anyone travelling to NYC.

title: shame
body: we had a truly unpleasant stay. Nine days in a small noised room without a view for 300 $/day! and with room'wifi only after my strong request after the 4° day! for this price during 9 days it's possible to have a pleasant suite with jacuzzi and kitchinette in all midtown 5 star hotels. Never more!

title: Staff very judgemental
body: The hotel has beautiful decor,and is very 1950,s .Ideal for the older generation. On arrival the place was very busy but there was a lot of staff,so that wasn't a problem. We stayed for 4 nights in which we had a deposit taken of $400 during our stay, didn't mind that but it took nearly a week to clear on the bank statement.The lady on reception that booked us feel very small because she could not find our booking even though i had all the paperwork in front of her,she made us wait ages with a large queue behind us,in which one woman was practically on top of me listening to our conversation.After a long wait she found our room but didn't even apologize for the inconvenience. Rooms were nice with old decor and VERY low baths,not good for someone with a bad back (me).Other staff in the Bars + Reception were very helpful and polite.Even though there was a lot of children there i wouldn't say its a place that children would enjoy because everything is so expensive and dont think they would feel relaxed. It is very expensive to eat and drink in the Waldorf and there are loads of nice places to eat locally so we ate out everyday. Didn't like they never had tea/coffee facilities in rooms,for the price of our stay.They do have a Starbucks in the lobby but the queues were terrible. Do not think we would stay there again because i would like to stay a bit more closer to Times Square. All in all a nice hotel for older people.

title: Good Experience
body:
Spent a Friday night in the city. Booked a room using hotel points. The check-in process took a long time (about 15 minutes), but we were given drink and breakfast vouchers, which was nice. 
The lobby was beautiful, the rooms were just average (small, as could be expected of an older hotel). The staff was very friendly and abundant. There was just nothing exceptional about this hotel outside of the ornate lobby. I guess I had high expectations. An enjoyable stay none-the-less.

title: Living in the lap of luxury
body: The Waldorf in NYC is such a beautiful old hotel. But completely renovated and updated. It is a real treat to stay there -- you really feel like you are in the lap of luxury. Plus it is wonderful to view the history of the hotel from photos on the walls and historical displays in the lobby. The bars are fun at night and the location is great for restaurants, theatres and museums.

title: A gem of a stay
body:
My first time back to the Waldorf in nearly thirty years and it lived up to all I remembered. It is a gem of architecture, worth walking around to notice all of the beautiful touches - light fixtures, railings, carved elevator doors - everywhere you look there is a detail of beautiful history.
Modernizing and maintaining such a historic place must be a challenge, but they seem to do it very well. Yes, there may be a few compromises, but the old world beauty is far worth it.
In addition, the staff was very kind and caring. I became ill my last day there and they arranged for late checkout and other amenities that helped me feel better. It was a gem of a stay indeed.

title: Luxury can cost you
body: The Waldorf is the ultimate in old fashioned elegance. It is not modern like a new hotel. The amenities are everywhere. The Bull and Bear restaurant is classic and delicious. The was limited room service. Be prepared to pay. Breakfast was over $100 for 2. A bottle of vodka from the mini bar was $17. Paying for convenience is one thing, but you pay surcharge just to be in the Waldorf. A very enjoyable stay but if you are looking for value, this is not the place for you.

title: Back in Time..
body: The hotel was undergoing external renovations and the front was shrouded in canvas but, what a beautiful surprise when we stepped through the revolving doors. Low season meant the hotel reception was quite quick. We were given some vouchers to the Spa and a couple for cocktails. This was a pleasant surprise. The room was a Superior one with a walk-in closet (which was a very useful feature to tuck away suitcases) and the size of the bathroom was generous. The place was warm with controllable heating which was good for us who like warm but not hot rooms to sleep in. The feeling was one of being enveloped in secure, calm, gentility. We were there for three days only and started relaxing immediately which I think was because of the lovely, homely, antique furniture and lamps that cast a warm glow. The only thing was that no slippers were provided. We did not bother to ask at reception whether this was an oversight but we were concerned about walking barefoot on a carpet where grubby shoes may have been. We also did not have anywhere to put our robe in the bathroom (the hook on the back of the door was broken) and it would have been nice to be able to have a chair in there. However, the showers were strong and the water hot. On a couple of nights we were awoken by people arguing in the corridor - a bit annoying. The staff were wonderful and very helpful and courteous. All in all, it was a wonderful experience and definitely to be repeated....

title: Bill Overcharge
body: The hotel is old so when the water went out for a day, you work around it. But they added an $85 room service charge that was not my charge and is totally unauthorized. I called and was told it would be sent to accounting, but didn't hear anything for 2 days. I called back and was put on hold supposedly to find a manager, then was disconnected after 10 minutes. I spoke with customer care at Hilton, the parent company, who appears to be trying to take care of it, but given the lack of response at the hotel, it remains to be seen if they will actually correct the overcharge. I'm probably going to have to complain to AMEX because that will force them to admit they don't have my signature on this charge.

title: Hotel a bit disappointing - and a theft
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for 5 nights in January 2012 and I have to say that while there were some positives, I was a disappointed with the hotel.
First the positives, to be fair. The hotel is centrally located and it is easy to get anywhere in Manhattan. When checking in the staff was extremely helpful and welcoming and the concierge was very helpful on several occasions when we had questions. As a Hilton HHonors gold member we were also placed in a large corner room far away from the elevators and had free internet (membership certainly has it's privileges). The bed was extremely comfortable and there was plenty of closet space, with a standard closet for me and a walk-in closet for my girlfriend (perhaps this was due to it being a corner room). The bathroom was large and everything worked.
Now for the negatives. While the Waldorf Astoria certainly has an old world charm, it is also a bit tired and in need of some updating. The elevators had some issues while we were there and it was difficult to get to our room on several occasions. The carpets in the hallways had certainly seen better days. Wallpaper was pealing in the hallways and it was rather shabby. Also, while the room and bathroom had individual temperature control, they were the type of radiators seen in the 1960s (either too hot or too cold and a bit loud). Again, as a Hilton HHonors gold member I qualify for free breakfast at other Hilton properties, but the "breakfast" at the Waldorf was supplied by the Starbucks downstairs and consisted of a coffee, a pastry, and a juice box. Now I realize I'm complaining about something that is given to me for free (poor me), but when other Hilton properties supply a relaxed breakfast in a restaurant setting, standing in line with 30 other people in a tiny Starbucks seems a bit chintzy. Also, there are no coffee or tea making facilities in the rooms, so you have to either order room service or go to Starbucks for this. I think that the Waldorf Astoria is coasting on its name and reputation, and I was definitely a bit disappointed. Why does it seem that the (supposedly) highest end hotels are the most stingy on the amenities?
And finally for the theft. After I had checked out and was on a train to Washington DC I noticed that a beautiful Mont Blanc pen I had in my bag was mysteriously gone. The bag had never left my side during the trip, except when it was in my room. I certainly can not prove that it was stolen while at the Waldorf, but the facts are, 1) the pen was in my bag when I checked in, 2) the bag was only left unattended in my room, and 3) my pen is now gone. 
Apart from the alleged theft, however, my overall impression of the Waldorf Astoria in New York is that while it is in a great location and has a certain old world charm, the hotel, which is supposed to be one of the best in the Hilton chain, does not live up to this reputation. I think there are definitely better hotels for the money in New York and I would probably not stay at the Waldorf Astoria again unless some major changes are made.

title: billing and service issues
body:
as others have said the service in the restaurant is HORRIBLE. so slow, and for a huge amount of money. go to any of the great steakhouses all over Manhattan for the same price, but get good service. oh and no room service except for breakfast? wow.
also as others have said keep a close watch on your bank account. they charged me twice for the room. when i called to straighten it out they acted like i was bothering them and they didn't even care about the mistake. 
the room was nice, but i was certainly expecting more from such a famous property.

title: Great Customer Service !
body: From the moment we checked in with Gina at Diamond Reception, we felt pampered throughout our stay. From reception to housekeeping , any small request was cheerfully accommodated. There is a reason we return over and over to this hotel....not only is the location perfect, but we always feel like special guests.

title: It was fine - just fine.
body:
Several of my colleagues and I stayed here for business since our administrative assistant found an unusually low rate for them through Travelocity. So this review is mostly my impressions, but a few from them as well.
The bellhop promptly brought my bag up to my room, he was very kind and courteous. The room was small but clean, and the bed was nice with comfortable pillows and new linens. If you want to use more than outlet at a time, good luck! There was one outlet free in my room, then two more in the bathroom (I charged my laptop in the bathroom in desperation at one point). The closet was relatively small - enough for me but it might have been too small for two people, but there were plenty of hangers, a safe, and an iron and ironing board provided. The draft coming in from under the window was so strong that it blew the curtain and I had to set my thermostat at 80 degrees just to keep the room comfortable because it was FREEZING in there. Another colleague of mine of a different floor had the same problem. And we live in Chicago, we're used to cold weather but we prefer to keep it outdoors. Now, I like old buildings and I appreciate the history of them. But I feel like there is a difference between "old building" and "poor maintenance." I think the hotel is somewhat coasting on their name at this point. They haven't complately let the place go, but they're not exactly holding it to the highest possible standard either.
One important thing to note: the walls are paper thin. My room was near a supply closet for the hosuekeeping staff and I could hear everything they did in there, as well as their conversations. One colleague could hear a couple of his floor having very loud, athletic... couple time. He could hear it all the way down the hall coming from the elevator. So if you're a light sleeper, this may not be the place for you.
Some male colleagues alerted me to the fact that late at night the lobby was, and I quote, "crawling with professionals." Apparently they were propsitioned multiple times just trying to get to the elevator. The lobby was pretty busy at all times, day and night, probably because it had free WiFi. You have to pay for WiFi in your room unless you're a gold or platinum level HHonors member. $16 per day and it is painfully slow. If you have AT&T for your cell phone note that the 3G signal in the hotel is terrible (not the hotel's fault, obviously, but good to know). My lowly blue level HHonors membership did get me free bottled water out of the minibar, which was nice since as other have noted there was no room service and no vending machines. So definitely let the front desk know if you're a member, and if you're not you should join before you stay there.
All in all I'd say the hotel was fine. Not excellent but not bad, and none of us came home with bed bugs. The location is amazing but I don't know that I would spend my own money to stay there.

title: Brilliant Location to see New York, Elegant but pricey
body: We had room 1140 which was fine overlooking the church, very peaceful room and very comfortable. Large TV (although not many channels outside of news ones), Enough plugs (american style) on desk and lighting ample. Bathroom shower was great too. Surprised there was no coffee making facility but you could order it from reception (not sure why?) The hotel public areas were very upmarket and lots of help although very very pricey to dine or drink in (loads of restaurants, eateries and bars close by so dont worry). It has its own starbucks in the lower lobby. If you want a breakfast exit the hotel on the lexington avenue side. It has a small convenience shop near the lobby too..

title: The Grand Old Lady Still Delivers
body:
Want a modern, minimalist, efficient hotel experience? Try somewhere else. The Walforf is a charming, iconic and generally lovely hotel, but it won't be for eveyone.
The foyer looks as much like a Hotel Museum as a 21st Century hip, wireless accommodation experience, and we love that about it. The hotel is huge, so there is often a queue just to talk to someone at reception, even to collect a message.
We were shocked and delighted at the rate we got for our 7 night stay at The Walforf. Our suite was beautiful.....then next morning we saw the workers immediately outside our window - and I do mean "immediately." The Park Avenue facade is being upgraded, and suddenly the low rate was put into context. But it mattered not - there was no noise and no inconvenience. It was a delightful, warm and comfortable place to be.
Bobby delivered our luggage and gave us the rundown - stop him talking if you can, the man is a human word machine - but listen to him, for his NY wisdom is invaluable.
Internet is expensive by today's standards, but of course we signed on anyway.
Just after we arrived, a pipe broke somewhere and the water system was shut down for the entire hotel - a reminder that the Waldorf wasn't built in the last 10 years. It came back on a couple of hours later.
We had a drink at Sir Harry's (wonderful when it is quiet), buffet breakfast at Oscar's (extensive choices) and a nightcap at the Bull & Bear (the Cheescake and Red Velvet are to die for),
Midtown location means that attracions like Grand Central Station, MoMA, even Central Park are within walking distance, and downtown life is (for us, not gerat subway users) a $12 cab ride away.
As a genuine NY experience, staying at the Waldorf is right up there, and was a highlight of our time in this great city.
I could on, as may have become obvious...we would and will stay at the Walforf again, if rates permit.
Oh, one last thing - the $5 overnight shoeshine service is a brilliant service.

title: Elegant, good location
body: we spent 3 days at the Waldorf Astoria in NY and enjoyed the location (10mn walk to Rockfeller Center, 5 mn for Grand Central) Even if pricey, decoration is so gorgious that we forget about money:) we had the experience of the room breakfast which was a dream ! at the 17th floor view on surrounding buildings was terrific, staff was very helpful and nice. Definitely I would go back when I return to NY

title: Towers rooms
body:
I stayed here last January for 8 nights. You need to love the early 20th century style to love the hotel. I also think that rooms in the tower wing are better than the others and you can also enjoy the complimentary continental breakfast. I had breakfast (wonderful) also in one of the restaurats of the hotel but it cost me 50 USD. The staff is nice and helpful and if you stay in the tower you have a dedicated concierge and reception that is nice because the other reception is always very busy. 
I think it's too expensive for what it is but service and location are good. Rooms need some love and tender and they are now doing some sort of renovation.

title: An old Hotel
body: We spent 5 nights during last January 12. The location is good, being on the Park Avenue near to all the most important attractions and shopping in NYC. But the hotel is quite old (under renovation). We booked a superior double room for about 400 usd per night + taxes but when we arrived in the room we realized it was not a superior... I called the reception and after some "sorry" they change the room. The superior room was at the 12th floor, quite big and nice with a partial view on the Chrysler building. The bathroom was quite old but at the end we were happy. We went twice to the bar and the glasses/ cups were not well clean (do you think is normal to pay 60 usd to have breakfast having this service?) Moreover every morning we had a terrible wake up around 8 am by the housekeepers, they did loads of noise every morning in the corridor. We asked the concierge to book a really nice japanese restaurant and they booked a table for us in a Japanere around the corner telling it was the best one...we were really disappointed about that. Finally they blocked the mini fridge the last evening without advising us and we spent 30 minutes by phone during the night to get the fridge open. We think it was a great hotel maybe 30 years ago. You can find better hotel in NYC at the same prime (Essex House)

title: My most expensive disappointment
body:
I surprised my kids a lavish trip to NYC for Christmas. We booked Broadway tickets with a backstage tour, reservations at amazing restaurants, limo service, shopping excursions, a carriage ride in Central Park, tickets to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island and the icing on the cake: I booked a suite at the Waldorf Astoria, a hotel I have always wanted to stay at given its rich history and its reputation for beautiful decor and luxurious accomodations.
I was so happy with every aspect of our trip with the glaring exception of the Waldorf Astoria. They are in need of a deep clean- not only in their rooms, hallways, public areas and entrances, but in their customer service departments.
We were treated like a nuisance by the house keeping phone center when we dared to ask for linens for the pull out couch, or to be able to have the clock set to the right time (it's locked down tight for some ridiculous reason). When the linens finally did arrive (an hour later- and it was already 10:00 at night) there was no blanket included. And the housekeeping rep was so annoyed by having to come to our room to give us linens ("I have to get back to work"....?) that she actually asked if we "really needed a blanket"...No. It's January in NYC. We'll be warm and cozy in the 20 degree weather.
The maintenance man who came to set the clock insisted on getting into some political arguement with me about the mayor of Chicago, which he initiated. Why?
The worst thing that happened was that there was a function in the lobby on the Sunday of the weekend we were there. NO ONE alerted us to this. No phone message, no paper under the door, no sign in the lobby- NOTHING. When we returned to the hotel after a very long day of sight seeing we were blocked from going to the elevators of our room. Instead we were shuffled to some elevators in the bowels of the building (of which there were several but only one was actually working) along with 100 other guests. All to wait to get onto one elevator to get to our rooms. it took forever and would be infuriating at a budget road side hotel much less the WALDORF ASTORIA. 
When we complained to the front desk manager about the situation we got NO apology, NO remedy and NO compensation. Instead he handed us a coupon for a small coffee from Starbucks. Gee, thanks. He actually said "Well, we told the people who checked in on Saturday." When we said "What about those who checked in on Friday?", he replied "Oh, I guess we forgot."
The beds were horrible, the carpet was dirty, the decor was trying desperately to reflect the history of the building but failed miserably.
I would never stay here again nor would I ever recommend it. I paid an insane amount of money for this horrible hotel- it would have been much better spent at a more modern hotel in a better location with a MUCH better staff. 
Such a shame.

title: a garanty !
body: the classic hotel whit a service excellent, sailence ,quite. location excellent near museums and shopping

title: Excellent service and beautiful public spaces, but the rooms are in need of an update.
body:
I spent three nights at the Waldorf-Astoria on business, and the service, facilities and overall cleanliness of the hotel and guest rooms is excellent. The location is great and allows for easy travel (as easy as it can get) within Manhattan.
The rooms, on the other hand, while clean and well-appointed, are clearly dated and in need of an update. The bedroom was small with somewhat threadbare carpet in places. The bathroom, (again, very clean) was also quite small and did not have room for any of the typical traveler's vanity items. There was some peeling paint throughout thr room, ceiling and in the hallways.
Finally, the room offered only a rudimentary temperature control, and in this case the only choice was heat or fan speed. Granted, it was winter while I was there, but there was no way to get the room unstuffy, which led to a fairly frustrating need to have the heat on and the window open at the same time. A call to the front desk informed me that the guests have a chooice of heat or cool only from April to May, and in September and October, when there is otherwise only seasonally-available hot or cold air.
Overall, great location, professional staff in a very historic hotel. Would be much better if the living history didn't extend to the guest room, however.

title: Cold shower for our honeymoon
body:
I do not ask much when I stay in a hotel: clean sheets, possibility to get the room dark and a shower. You should not take the last one of these for granted if staying at Waldorf=Astoria. 
In addition to basic needs I expected something more when I booked our honeymoon to this legendary hotel but I have to say that I can't recommend this hotel to anyone. Location i great and I even like the old fashioned rooms. But if you get bad service and the shower does not work for a whole week (well, it technically works but you just can't get warm water from there even after waiting half an hour..) those things do not help a lot.
Also they have the crappiest internet deals of all: you take a one week package (more than 100 bucks) and you can't use the same deal with wlan or another computer: it's only the cable or wlan with one computer. :(

title: Great Stay in Central Manhattan
body:
Stayed here for 1 night at the end of January.
The room was large and comfortable with a great view over the Avenue. Only downside was the small bathroom
Saff were efficient and capable.
Will stay again next time in Manhattan

title: History abounds - Rooms could be better
body:
If you are thinking of staying at the Waldorf Astoria you will not fail to be impressed by its lineage and history since its opening in 1931. It is a New York landmark building which exudes art neuveau decoration throughout its public areas. 
You may however be surprised, as we were, to read so many negative trip advisor reviews about rooms in a hotel which has hosted events for every US President since its opening, and has had numerous famous celebrities live there.
The truth is that there are two parts to the hotel, the lower part of the building houses the Waldorf Astoria Hotel, whilst the 28th to 42nd floors house the suites of the Waldorf Towers.
The suites in The Towers which we saw on a hotel tour reflect the higher price demanded, whilst rooms in the Hotel may be small and tend to reflect the age of the building. 
Having read many reviews we requested and paid for an upgrade to our room when we checked in. Ours was a corner room with a king size bed on the 12th floor which was of a reasonable size. We did not experience any problems mentioned about noise on lower floors from the exterior refurbishment works, which I understand are nearly finished now. In our room however the window mounted ventilators were old and their controls tended to be difficult to manage, the old window blinds were frayed, and the shower took several attempts to keep the water hot. This projected an aged and poorly maintained image. That said we found the room clean, comfortable and well furnished and we enjoyed our stay in it.
For us a good aspect of the hotel was the staff who were always pleasant and polite, and assisted with any queries we had. 
Would we would stay there again? Yes we would as the positive aspects outnumbered the negative ones, and the staff made our stay very enjoyable.

title: Disappointed in Waldorf Astoria
body: We booked into the Waldorf for my daughter's 16th birthday. The room was musty, spacious but with a tiny bathroom and very dated. We live in the UK and are used to the faded country style hotel but the Waldorf is not in that class it is just a bit grubby round the edges. I asked to pay for an upgrade to the towers and the lady at the Hilton check in was very helpful. She showed me the options before I confirmed and negotiated a discount for me. I moved to a suite in the Towers and this was much more suitable with rich fabrics large bedroom and bathroom. However staff performance was patchy. Paul our bell person was top notch and David the concierge recommended a fantastic restaurant where we had one of the best meals in a long while. The staff at the towers desk were not so helpful and during our stay we didn't have any input from customer relations. The Tower lounge is very basic not really worth visiting. Having spent some days at the New York Palace Towers where the lounge presentation is amazing the Towers at the Waldorf was lacking. The general feel in the hotel was not welcoming it was busy and transient. The public rooms do reflect the past prominence of the hotel but it doesn't have an up market ambiance now. I would not recommend this hotel.

title: Fabulous Art Deco Hotel
body:
My husband surprised me for my birthday with a 4 day trip to New York and as a NY lover I had always wanted to stay at the Waldorf, so this was a fabulous gift that I will never forget. We arrived at the hotel to be told we had an upgrade to king suite. The staff at reception were extremely professional and genuinely keen to be as helpful as needed, without being over the top. The room its self was gorgeous, a large very comfortable king bed, dressing room and huge bath tub. All extremely clean, crisp white bed linen, soft robes and towels changed everyday whether we wanted them changed or not. 
This hotel has all the glamour of the Art Deco period - yes many might say dated, but for me all the original features from that period remain and it this that's make this hotel so perfect. You can go to any hotel in any city and get that ultra modern minimalistic theme. There is nothing themed about the Waldorf, its all original and very well maintained.
A really nice touch was that the manager at the Waldorf became aware that it was my birthday and sent a bottle of champagne to our room. It was simple gesture but said a lot about customer satisfaction that they clearly care so much about. 
I would most certainly return to The Waldorf ... and would actually find it very difficult to choose any place else.

title: fantastic hotel
body: from start to finish this hotel great staff couldnt do enough for us got room upgrade when they found out it was my birthday and a lovely present and card special mention to marlene caroline and agnes

title: Guerlain Spa = Divine Room Service = needs improvement
body:
My husband gave me a Winter Spa package at the Waldorf Astoria as a gift for my recent trip to New York. The Waldorf is a classic and there is no modern minimalism here. My room was large and spacious and very comfortable. Room service was a bit of a let down on my first night - I arrived and got all comfy in their big white robes and went to order but alas, no menu in the room. Called Room Service and requested a menu to be sent to the room AND to cut a long story short - after 3 phone calls and a wait of over an hour and still no menu I decided to get dressed and go out and get my own food. Not quite what one expects from a luxurious hotel of this standard - I put a call into Guest Services to let them know and to their credit they got a menu to my room while I was out foraging for food on Lexington Ave and my experience the next night was much better.
However - the highlight of my stay was the amazing Guerlain spa treatment - I had a "As You Wish" 80 minute massage, champagne on arrival and use of the spa room after my massage. It was just divine and I will visit the spa again on my next NYC visit even if I am not staying at the hotel.

title: Excellent hotel full of charm, character and elegance
body:
Just got back from the Waldorf Astoria following a 4 night stay and we could not fault this hotel. I’ve read some previous reviews about the standard of rooms being tired and musty. All I can say is that our room (2516) was fantastic. It was large, spotlessly clean and had an extremely comfortable king size bed with a ‘boudoir’ that leads to an impressive bathroom. The best compliment I can give this hotel is the standard of service delivered by the staff. On checking in we were dealt with by Justin, who was extremely professional and gave us a superb standard of service as we’d had some issues with BA losing our luggage. The service from house keeping to the bell captain was equally good
The Waldorf is situated in an excellent location, only a few blocks away from the main tourist attractions. Overall it was full of charm, character and elegance and I would not hesitate in staying here again.

title: Charmed by a charming hotel
body:
A grand hotel with a beautiful lobby area and extremly polite and helpful staff. Would like to particularly thank Wayne at check-in who represented the hotel wonderfully. The hotel is ideally located for exploring the city and close to the rockerfeller centre, grand central station and shopping on 5th & Madison.
The rooms are a bit on the small side and our two doubles were more like large comfortable singles but the size issue is to be expected in manhattan especially given this is an old hotel. Bathroom was fine, rooms were cleaned to a high standard (although it did have a strong smell of bleach when we checked in - but at least we knew it was clean ;-)) 
Breakfast at Oscars in the hotel was delicous with a wide selection of food and drink, set us up well for the day. Enjoyed sipping the house champagne at Sir Harry's Bar in a relaxed atmosphere. Have heard the Pull & Bear is great to eat at but didnt eat there ourselves.
I enjoyed the experience of staying at Waldorf for our first trip to NYC.

title: Let down
body:
I have always wanted to stay at the Waldorf ever since I read an article about it in Reader's Digest more than 20 years ago. To say that I was disappointed would be putting it very very mildly. The room that we were in had such a run down feel to. The bathroom fixtures had rust on them. The first day that we were there, one of the blinds got have stuck and cam down partially. The room service must have seen that every day for the next 3 days but didnt fix it. There was no coffee maker in the room. While one was brought up very promptly, the staff didnt replenish the coffee any day!!! One day wen we came back to the hotel in the middle of day, the house keeping staff had seemed to have just finished cleaning our room and the smell of bleach was strong enough to make you gag!
Having said that, I wouldnt have sat down to write my very first reveiw of any hotel because of the reasons mentioned above. I have stayed in better hotels and in much worse hotels. What prompted this review was - this was Waldorf and one of the to-do things on my bucket list. And thats why the expereince was even more disappointing.

title: Thoroughly enjoyed the stay
body: Stayed here for three nights for a conference. I didn't get to enjoy the outstanding location very much since the conference agenda was packed but found the property to be top notch. Rooms have small bathrooms you would expect with an older property. The HVAC was also dated since it was unseasonably warm but there was no A/C. Fortunately I opened the window and it was very comfortable. Internet was free if you have AT&T service at home!!! The property is dated but charming and service made up for any shortcomings in the physical plant.

title: A grand old hotel -- with a wonderful location!
body: My wife and I stayed at the Waldorf the Sunday before Valentine's Day, since I had a meeting the next day a few blocks away. We took in a play and then had a marvelous dinner at a well-known restaurant before our stay there. And then the Waldorf. Our accommodations were actually two adjoining rooms -- with two bathrooms (a very nice touch so that we could get ready simultaneously). One room had couches and the other the bed, but both had TVs. There certainly was some wear, but not bad and the rooms were well-maintained. I'll grant you that for this up-graded suite the price was not cheap (approximately $450 including taxes), but it was an experience to savor -- including a very comfortable bed. My biggest complaint was the price of drinks in the bar downstairs: if I remember correctly, $19 a drink for simple fare, not complicated cocktails. Still, it was sort of fun to be able to say that we'd stayed in the same hotel as kings and queens and presidents.

title: If you are looking for sleek and contemporary this is not for you
body:
Arrived on a Saturday evening for four nights. There was only a short wait to check in. It would have been a shorter wait if people had not ignored the queue and gone directly to receptionists. We received a very warm welcome from Carolin who upgraded us to a suite in the Towers. The suite was beautiful with a huge living room and bedroom.
Yes it looks dated in places but that is the charm. It was spotlessly clean and was kept that way by housekeeping every day. The bathroom was gorgeous and was huge too. We had room service a couple of times and could not fault either the quality or presentation of the food. We ate in the Bull and Bear one evening. The food was wonderful. The restaurants, bar and room service in this hotel were not cheap but for quality like this we did not mind paying.
I can't write this review without commenting on the staff. Without exception they were professional, accommodating, and friendly. 
We will definitely be returning.

title: Great 40th birthday trip to remember
body: I have just returned from a five day trip to New York staying at the Waldorf Astoria. The hotel was kind enough to upgrade us to a suite as it was my 40th birthday. From the minute we walked in to check in until the end of our stay the service was amazing and we were treated to complimentary drinks vouchers for my birthday. The suite was beautifully decorated, very clean and had excellent facilities. The view from our room was the Crysler Building. The room was very quiet, the bed and pillows were very comfortable and I found the whole hotel very clean and luxurious. Our busy schedule meant that we didn't spend as much time in the room as we would have liked. The location suited us well and I would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel or staying in it again. The hotel made my birthday trip more special and it was our first adults only trip away without our children. It is well worth asking for an upgrade as they couldn't do enough for me. Some comments on this site had previously put me off and I was going to pay the extra to go to the Plaza. So glad I didn't waste my money now!!

title: Can't beat the location of this grand hotel
body: A huge hotel, but it never seemed over crowded and certainly not hectic or noisy, a bustling, well run establishment. Reception and concierge staff were very helpful and efficient. I did not dine in the hotel on this visit. Our room (Deluxe Queen) was small but perfectly formed, a comfortable bed with plenty of pillows, good size television, walk-in wardrobe, desk, air-con. The bathroom again was small, but appeared well furnished and of good quality. The only down-side was the shower pressure was poor, and the bath plug was faulty so unable to bathe (did report it, but no action). The location is fantastic, just a couple of blocks to Saks 5th Ave and Rockefeller Centre or up Lexington to Bloomingdales. Convenient too for the E train subway downtown to World Trade Centre and South Street Seaport, and so much else in close proximity. Full of old-school charm. I booked through British Airways holidays and got a very good price package deal, I'm not sure how good value standard rates would be.

title: Great Service - Older Rooms
body: I have wanted to stay at this hotel for a long time. When I saw the great deals in January, I could not pass it up. I have stayed in a lot of NY hotels and the service here is outstanding. I think that I was greated by 6 different people before I ever reached the front desk. The lobby area is quite grand and beautiful. The rooms were much more bland than I had imagined. I have stayed at much cheaper hotels that have much better rooms (ie The W). Despite having old and dated rooms, the beds were quite comfortable. I had a good nights rest, no issues with noise. There is a nice lobby bar as well as another attached on the east side of the building (Bull and Bear I think). My husband and I enjoyed 5 cocktails and our bill was more than $100. Steep even for NYC. All in all, would I stay here again? No. But I did check a box off of my Bucket List - so it was worth it in that regard.

title: Would Highly Recommend
body:
We have just returned from a 5 day break in New York, our first visit, staying at the Waldorf.
Having read some of the reviews about the hotel being a little tired we were a little apprehensive but have to say that we do not agree with this at all. 
The service is first class, to the door men, reception, bar staff and waiters. Always polite, helpful and smiling, they made us feel very welcome and nothing was too much trouble.
When we arrived we were on the 8th floor of the Astoria, the room was nice and perfectly acceptable. Unfortunately our neighbours decided to have a party and were playing very loud music until 1am. We phoned down to reception and within 10 minutes we heard the knock on their door and it all stopped. The following morning we went to reception and were informed that we had been upgraded to the 39th floor of the Towers! All our belongings were transferred whilst we were out and upon our return we were thrilled to bits. The room was amazing!
