We had breakfast at the hotel which again was great, everything you could possible want, albeit think was very expensive at $40 each! The drinks are all expensive in the bars but the champagne cocktails were just too tempting.
If we are lucking enough to visit New York again I would certainly stay at the Waldorf again.

title: What a hotel to celebrate in!!!
body: My husband booked for us to visit NYC for my Xmas/anniversary/birthday and of course valentines present. I had always wanted to stay at the Waldorf and wasn't disappointed. We arrived early and weren't able to check in but this wasn't a problem as we were happy to go and explore then come back. The gentleman that checked us in was really attentive and we were lucky enough to be upgrade for our stay. The rooms were amazing and we would highly recommend anyone who is visiting the city to stay here.

title: Service Auld Lang Syne in Deco Dreamland
body:
One reason why the Waldorf Astoria only rates 2 stars when you have a cold & need hot tea 7pm on a Sunday nite. A reading from the in-room info book:
Coffee makers are available in your room strickly (sic) per advance request to Room Service. Guests are invited to order coffee with Room Service or to enjoy coffee at Peacock Alley Restaurant in the main lobby, at Oscar's Restaurant or at the Starbucks located down the steps from the Park Avenue Lobby.
Problem? Starbucks closes @4 weekends/6 weekdays. Oscars's & Peacock Alley won't provide take out. Concierge sends you 2 blocks away to another Starbucks...also closed.Room service? $8.00 + $5.25 in room charge +15% gratuity+ City taxes.
Other reasons < 5 stars...uninformed staff, no doorman @ Park Av entrance to help with luggage, lacking in general amenities,maintenance & cleanliness of room.
BUT... The public rooms are glittering & fabulous..&the food served @ at a huge gala in the ballroom was excellent..almost on par w/Bull &Bear...no rubber chicken here. 
And, yes, I could imagine a Guy Lombardo New Years Eve while in the ballroom & cocktails on the Starlight Roof.
 
My room was spacious & quiet & since it faced the interior courtyard, barely a whisper of city noise.

title: Fabulous!
body:
We cannot say enought great things about this hotel. When booking, we advised the hotel we were staying there for my daughter's birthday. When we checked in, there was a birthday gift for her - a really nice Waldorf Astoria chef teddy bear. They also gave my son a nice toy taxi so he would not be jealous. Wanting to impress everybody, they also had a welcome gift for my husband and me - a free buffet brunch for 4!
Our room was large for a NYC hotel and had a separate dressing room with makeup table. Alana, who checked us in. told us she chose this room for our daughter and it was perfect. The room was nice and beds were very comfry. Each and every staff member could not be nicer - each one took time to joke with our children. The rate was extremely reasonable - even if this was not a top hotel. 
We all decided we want to stay at a Waldorf on every trip.

title: Elegant hotel & adequate room
body:
Checked in to the W=A for a 2 night business stay. The elegant entry and sumptous lobby was even better then my sky high expectations for such a storied hotel. The staff was crisp but not particularly warm. 
My room left me with mixed feeleings. I think I was upgraded due to my HHonors status. I recieved a surprising large room with 2 Double or Queen Beds. I was shocked on how large he room was particularly for NYC. The bath was also large and even had an antechamber going into it. Bu here's where the mixed emotions came in. The room itself - the walls, rug, tile, etc. all seemed, well, old and somewhat worn. The bath reminded of something designed in the mid -80's Leona Helmsley/ Trump era. It did'nt seem particularly clean or dirty, just old. The bed linens and the towels were all top notch, but the bones of the room was just old. The climate control seemed to go from nothing to pizza oven. In fact I woke up my first night in a dead sweat and the room was a sauna. And this was after the bellmen had set the tempature for me.
I'm glad I had chance to visit this Grand Dame, but at the rates they charge I would'nt come back until the rennovation is complete.

title: Grand old lady
body: The Waldorf exudes the sort of glamour that new hotels just can't manage. The lobby is spendid, the staff is extremely attentive and friendly, and staying there feels like an "old New York" experience. I first stayed there 15 years ago, and it still has the same grand feeling. The rooms have been updated, but in a classic style. I stayed there with my husband and teen daughter and our room fairly large, by New York standards. The towels were fluffy and replaced daily and the beds were comfortable. The toiletries were really nice--the kind I would actually use. The only dismaying feature was the ceiling in our bathroom was leaking the first morning, and I could tell it had been patched before. The location is wonderful and of course there are restaurants everywhere if you don't want to eat at the hotel ($$$). Also, wi-fi is $15 for 24 hours in the room, but free in the lobby. And there are Starbucks almost literally on every corner in NY, so you can use the wi-fi there, too. The price was not bad at all for a NY hotel room of this calibre--under $250/night. Also, and this is important in NY, the windows were excellent and the traffic noise wasn't bad.

title: 4 Night Stay
body:
We have just returned from a 4 night stay at the Waldorf Astoria.
Wow what an experience. This is a very old hotel, and indeed does show its age, however do not be fooled it oozes elegance and once inside the reception area/lobby you cant help but feel the ambiance of the hotel.
The staff are all immaculate in their dress, and are so polite and helpful it almost irritates (if that is possible). Everyone appears to be wearing white linen gloves and if they are not busy seem to be polishing any item that stands. The hotel is in midtown manhatton in a perfect location. Approx 10 minute walk to the lively Times Square and the Empire State Building. A few minutes walk to the Rockefella Centre and only a short walk to Bloomingdales and loads of designer shops.
We only had 4 days there and decided to try and visit as many tourist attractions as we could, but wished we had more time to explore the shopping areas as prices were certainly better than in the Uk. We also chose to use the tourist hop on hop off bus which we thought was perfect.
All in all if you plan to visit New York if you dont stay here please make an effort just to visit and see for yourself.

title: Historic Hotel
body: I read several articles about the Waldorf showing it's age, snooty staff, and room issues. I was a litte concerned, but once we got there, it was great. We did have a little issue at check in with the room reservation. Our teenage boys are 6 ft. tall so putting two of them in a double bed is asking for trouble. The hotel did not have our suite request with a sleeper sofa, but they found one for us. The lobby is beautiful, the historic artifacts were interesting, the staff was pleasant. The room was old-ish, but very clean. The breakfast buffet at $40 per person was overpriced so we opted for a local spot. You cannot beat this location! Had a great stay.

title: Fabulous
body: Stayed for 3 nights in a junior suite and it is such a beautiful hotel. The room was lovely and spacious and the bed was very comfortable. We did not eat in the hotel but did have a few drinks in the ground floor bar which is a lovely way to finish off the night. Staff were very friendly and courteous

title: Exellent
body:
This was my third visit to New York and it was amazing as usual!
I went with my mum and grandma and between them they had visit new york around 15 times and this was the first time any of us had stayed in the Waldorf Astoria and we will 100% be going back!
It was such a classic, elegant hotel which is full of history!
The rooms where outstanding and also full of history in its decor which we loved. The beds were so comfy and no doubt you will have a great nights sleep there!
The staff were just amazing and helpfull, we had no problems whats so ever!
We did not experience the spa so i cant comment on that but after what i have heard, that is also very good!
It was also great to find out that there was free Wifi access in the lobby which was great for me to catch up on college work!

title: I can't believe how wide those hallways are
body: Great classic hotel. Comfy room, good shower. Everything available here. It was a nice experience for the kids, and when you stay here, it feels like you are staying at a tourist attraction. Beautiful old building with incredible art deco accents. Breakfast is only $95/person!

title: Always amazing
body: Wife and I have stayed there many times when they have a discount period. Always a treat. Everything is special and the location is incredible for everything.

title: Wonderful and elegant
body: We have just returned from 4 nights in a superior room on the 25th floor, it was wonderful! The lobby is beautiful, check-in was quick and very welcoming, our room was fabulous with extremely comfortable beds and quality toiletries. Every member of staff we encountered was friendly and courteous. It was just how I had imagined the Waldorf=Astoria would be.

title: nice place with a few concerns
body:
no doubt this is a classy place. we had one of the "superior rooms" and it was comfortable and attractively furnished. I would say, however that it made very inefficient use of space. The dressing area, which was separated by a door from the main living area was as large as a small bedroom. I can't understand why they put a second desk in there rather than a couch or daybed. There also was an unusually large foyer which could have been put to better use.
My one other peeve is that a $90 toilet is not consistent with a $300 hotel room and when the bathroom has no exhaust fan ( or even window) they could at least supply some sort of scented spray or incense.

title: Take we to the Waldorf!
body:
The name alone seems to bring a smile to the face of the BA Check in staff who ask where i'm heading and throughout the trip it counted as a plus point with taxi drivers etc. In fact one cabbie said that to experience old style new York there used to be two options - the Waldorf and the Plaza and now there's only one as the Plaza has been ruined by Donald Trump.
Bit of a disappointment on arrival to see the famous old building totally shrouded in scaffolding as the stone is renovated but inside it was the epitome of luxury. Beautiful lobby and staff everywhere to provide assistance. Shut your eyes to the eyesore of a Starbucks just inside the door and all is well.
The room was well furnished with a fully stocked bar, large screen TV and wifi. Hanging space was however limited and I ended up having to leave a lot of my clothing in my case. The bathroom was pure marble and silver art deco with Ferragamo toileteries and incidentals such as nail files, cotton buds etc in crystal jars. Fluffy dressing gowns too.
The room was stripped daily but the dusting left a lot to be desired. Think it was done before my arrival and then not until I left 6 days later. Staff were all however very polite and helpful. Maids dressed like film extras from the 1950's Deep South.
Location excellent. Just a quick stroll to Grand Central Station, Rockefeller centre and all the main shopping streets.

title: Great Service, Elegant but aging
body:
Service was first rate and the room was large and comfortable. The bed and linen perhaps the best I have slept in a hotel (or I was very tired)
The room was somewhat dated and you could see the age of the woodwork, moldings etc. at the edges cracking paint and so on. Still it is obvious that for a old hotel they work hard to maintain it.
The lobby is wonderful and grand Basically if you want something different with old time class and charm, this is the place to be. The location is also great, though parking quite expensive.

title: Hype or reality
body: The name suggests old world charm and glamour, which are there in abundance, but a visit to the lobby would achieve the same result. The best thing about this hotel is the location - great for walking to a number of areas at the top of the tourist 'to do' list. However, the service is impersonal and the number of passers by in the lobby can make getting to the elevators a real challenge. I'm glad I went, but wouldn't rush back.

title: Service not so good
body: The Lobby is amazing, such a beautiful place. Check in was wonderful, the young lady was so helpful and kind. The only issue I had was I get there early and they took my luggage until my room was ready. They did text me in a prompt manner that my room was all set, I had to head to a business meeting so I went over to the Bell man and asked if they could just put the bags in my room, I had to leave. The bellman told he he could not put the bags in my room, I needed to do it. I did and was a couple of minutes late to my meeting. World Class service would have probably taken care of that for me. I know I have recieved better service from many of the Hiltons I have stayed at. I am a Gold Memeber of their Honors plan and an Owner at HGVC so I should have gotten free internet as "they" brought up on check in, nope had to call them to tell them to take it off my bill. Small thing, maybe, but if you sell yourself as the best you should be the best.

title: Great property and wonderful service!
body:
Everything you would expect to find when you stay at a Waldorf! Personalized service and friendly people! The rooms might be a little outdated but they have a certain level of old world charm and immaculate cleaning service so it doesn't matter at all.
We stayed here with a very large group and the staff wen t above and beyond to make sure every last request was fullfilled and then some. Kudos to all employees here, because it is you that makes the people come back :)

title: Waldorf Astoria NYC - A lovely Family Stay
body: We stayed as a family, it was made memorable by the staff hospitality. I would like to especially thank Ana Tijan, who was instrumental in making this special occasion such a delightful one. The buffet breakfast service at the Oscars restaurant was excellent and lots of choice for everyone, and would like to thank the restaurant manager Jeff in meeting our special request. We had a lovely 2 double bed suite, with a lovely lounge with classic styling. Also liked the exclusive check-in for Diamond and Gold members when they arrive, which made it more personal and was a nice touch. The choice of restaurants and bars within the hotel is pretty good, and should be able to cater for all ages and groups. The location is also ideal, and within easy walking distance from most tourist attractions. The yellow cabs (taxis) are quite reasonably priced, so we did make use of this when the kids got tiered walking.

title: Not at all what I expected
body:
I had the opportunity to stay at the Waldorf Astoria for one night on a business trip. The price was fantastic (or so I thought). 
My first impression of the hotel as soon as I walked into the lobby was that it was very nice, but dated. The Waldorf obviously attempts to appeal to the traveler who harkens for the traditional upscale hotels of yesteryear. My second impression was the huge line for check-in that snaked across the lobby. I am a Hilton Honors member. Although there was a dedicated check-in desk for Gold members, there was only one employee present and its line looked as though it was moving more slowly than the general check-in line. My wait was about 10 minutes; not bad, but not Waldorf-Astoria.
Because of my status, I was given a one-class upgrade to a bigger room. The space was nice, but the furniture and décor were worn. The desk chair was broken; I could not sit on it. The radiator was dirty, scratched and generally out of shape. The bathroom had not been updated in quite some time. Again, not the worst things in the world, but not what your mind conjures when you think "Waldorf-Astoria." 
All in all, other than the lobby, my experience at the Waldorf was what I would have expected out of an older, mid-tier hotel.

title: It's a nice building to visit but a bit dated
body: Like the title says, maybe worth a visit or the Sunday brunch, but to stay its not high value. We were unimpressed with the room and the fact that we didn't have hot water and that there was central heating that we couldn't alter in-suite. I've stayed in much better boutique hotels at better prices in NYC.

title: We can say we did it!
body:
We loved the Waldorf. This was a girls getaway to NYC for some shows, dinner and just relaxation. We enjoyed ourselves so much. The location was good but not the best but the atmosphere is wonderful, the service outstanding, the beds divine.
Would we stay there again?? Maybe not. Although we enjoyed it very much we went with a budget and it's difficult to enjoy all of the Waldorf on a budget, but we didn't expect anything different, we were at the Waldorf.

title: A tired rip off with
body: I have just spent a night at the Waldorf and would not stay again. The motor lobby looked like an evacuation centre when I arrived, the bell hop suggested leaving my luggage on an open shelf. The rooms are tired and dated and tatty. The public areas are only saved by the inherent architecture but has a distinctly '80s' corporate feel which is depressing. Two martinis $45, orange juice $9, eggs Benedict which was decidedly average $28. And to add I insult to injury, there is a Starbucks in the hotel where a tea that had cost $2.99 at another Starbucks yesterday was $4.25 'because we are owned by Starbucks. I don't mind paying for quality but this isn't it. Avoid, there are plenty of other better hotels in New York

title: I stayed here in the 80s, and nothing has changed.
body:
I had a lovely stay, but I was amazed at how everything was exactly as I remembered it from 20 years ago. The lobby can't be beat and I loved gazing up at the chandelier, but the rooms felt so dated. It was clean, but "worn." The bathroom still had the exact same phone on the wall. As a kid in the 80s, I thought that was amazing to have a phone right by the toilet, but now it just seems silly. 
Location was great - grab a bagel at Ess A Bagel around the corner.

title: Iconic but average
body:
We have just returned from a 4 night stay here. I'm really pleased we have now ticked it off our 'must do one day' list and it was a unique experience, but I'm left with a feeling that it didn't quite hit the spot. The grandeur of the hotel is magnificent but somewhat spoilt by the amount of large groups that seem to fill every available space in the public areas. I think that they must hold many corporate seminars etc as everyone seemed to be wearing a name tag!
Check in went smoothly, we only waited a few minutes. We had booked a superior room as we wanted to make the most of our once in a lifetime stay. The hotel knew we were celebrating a special event and I was a little disappointed not to be upgraded as the hotel was not full and we had already paid for our own upgrade and we were staying 4 nights. However, the room was well appointed and a decent size. The bathroom had almost everything you could want, except a shelf to put your toiletries on and it's amazing how annoying that can be when you have to balance all your wash stuff on the back of the toilet. Bathrobes were good quality and it was very clean. Just a small pointer. As in all hotels, they 'want to save the planet etc' and ask you to reuse towels. I have no problem with this, I don't need a fresh towel every day, but with no heated rail anywhere in the room, it was impossible to dry any towels, so you either put up with a soggy one or change them. The most excellent part of the whole stay in the hotel was the bed. It was the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in, with perfect pillows and linen. The decor was in keeping with the style of the hotel and I found it charming, less so the air conditioning which was fairly noisy and I do resent not be allowed to chose my own temperature and having to work within the limits set by the hotel. The room was too warm for us.
We had pre booked the brunch at Peacock Alley as a special treat as it coincided with our 'special day' Now considering the hotel folder in the room went into some detail about the dress codes for each bar and restaurant we smartened ourselves up a little as was fitting for the occasion....or so we thought... well I could have gone down in my pj's and fitted in perfectly well. I know that dress code is deemed a bit outdated and elitist etc but it was the hotel who said they insisted upon it, yet any old dirty pair of jeans was fine, got a backpack and a few suitcases, that's fine too. So, if you are planning on this sumptious feast whilst you are there don't worry too much about taking any special clothes.
The staff are unfailingly polite and helpful, but you don't get the personal touch, it's a huge hotel and you are only one of many. Perhaps size isn't everything! And what in God's name were they thinking in putting a Starbucks in the lower lobby?? I have nothing against Starbucks, they do a nice coffee, but the lobby is full of people drinking out of paper cups etc, what a blot on the landscape. Also, they should put tea and coffee making facilites in the rooms, it's expensive enough to warrant any extra work created. 
Summing up, it's a 'must see' hotel and I'm glad we have stayed there but next time I'll pick a smaller hotel with a more personal touch.

title: Can't Get Enough of the Waldorf
body: My boyfriend and I just stayed at the Waldorf this past weekend, which was our second time staying at the hotel. Everything was amazing, as always! The staff was super friendly to us, and even upgraded us to my boyfriend's HHonors Gold Status, even though the room was in my name, and I'm only a Silver member. The hotel lobby is gorgeous, and the rooms are elegant. You kind of feel like you've gone back in time to the 1930's New York! We would absolutely stay here again, as this is probably my favorite hotel ever!

title: The Grand Dame of New York
body:
Stayed here for 2 nights. Room was a little old fashioned but this added to the charm.
 Public areas were elegant . Staff were polite and effecient.
The staff at the Concierge desk were very knowledgeable about all aspects of the city.
Would stay here again

title: Iconic Hotel
body:
We stayed for six days in February with our two teenage daughters. We really had a brilliant holiday.
We had adjoining rooms on the 11th floor. Our bathrooms were fine, plenty of space for toiletries. I found a iron and board in the walk-in cupboard which was very useful. Perhaps they should put tea and coffee making facilities in the rooms, to make it perfect. We had a wonderful view of the Chrysler Building from our window.
The beds were the most comfortable we have ever slept in, (apart from home!) with very nice linen and pillows.
Most tourist sights were within easy walking distant. I would recommend the deli at 664 Lexington; it is open from 5am to 11pm, La Baguette.
All the staff were very friendly, helpful and polite, the bell boys are a bit too keen for tips but I loved the maids uniforms.
 The is a business suite near the reception, is handy for internet access to print out your boarding cards for your journey home, payment is by credit card per minute. The BA staffs at JFK were very impressed by the quality of the paper!
Beware of the mini bar; a can of coke is $8........ In ours there was also a piece of mouldy cheese and a half drunk bottle of orange juice!

title: Housekeeping Ninjas
body:
not sure how these Housekeeping ladies do it, but it is amazing. I took out my dont disturb sign, went out for a run at central park and back in 1hr. my room was clean spotless. everyday!!!! amazing service. 
big hotel but they treat you as a person. I didnt feel anyone was rude or anything as some reviews say. I was wearing casuals and am not the elite types but the reception staff was very pleasant.

title: Girls New York Trip
body: This was THE PERFECT hotel for our girls trip! Centrally located, close to the museums, 5th avenue, and our Broadway shows we were going to. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was large for New York standards and everything was clean. We had 2 double beds which was perfect for all of us girls. I'm so glad we picked this place. We barely had to catch a cab or ride the subway the whole time we were there! So convenient!

title: Best Hotel Experience Ever
body: My wife and I stayed for 3 nights in mid-February and this hotel is everything that you'd expect. The atmosphere throughout the hotel is luxurious while at the same time very comfortable and without pretense, From the time that we checked in, the staff was extremely responsive, solicitous and courteous. Everyone that we encountered during our stay was extremely helpful and welcoming. The accomodations are old school luxury while being modern and convenient. Housekeeping service is outstanding and was serviced twice daily. They must have known when we were going to be out because the room was always cleaned when we returned. Room service was outstanding.

title: Always a treat
body:
I've stayed here 4-5 times over the past 2 years and they never fail to impress me. From the Diamond Desk personnel, maids, and even the coffee shop guys, this place is built on service and they don't dissapoint.
The Bull and Bear restaurant downstairs is a great place to unwind after a busy day with great cocktails, food and the people watching is a trip. European cougars on the prowl is a must see.
The lobby is still the best in the city and oozes class and energy. Can't wait to come back.

title: Amazing
body: Not only the hotel is absolutely amazing because of its history and its beauty, but also the staff is wonderfully kind. We feel like being privileged everytime we talk to waiters, managers. Rooms are beautiful, and as we were at 40th floor, our view was incredible. This is THE hotel to choose.

title: Always a pleasure
body: This hotel is unbeatable - service is great - rooms are always nice - plus it is quiet

title: Impressive but expensive
body: We stayed at The Waldorf in March 2012 and had a very nice time. The staff was very accommodating and friendly. The room was just as we expected - small but very nice and clean with quite a touch of charm and history. The location of WA was perfect for our trip. I know NYC is expensive but $95/person for Sunday brunch was just out of the question. If you're looking to stay and really get an old fashioned feel of NYC, WA is the perfect choice. Just beware that you will be walking for every meal because the restaurants are all $$$ and up.

title: It has to be done - even if it is expensive!!
body:
Husband and I have just got back from our NY trip. Staying at the Waldorf Astoria has to be done if you want to enjoy the grandness, heritage and tradition of this well-known hotel. It is very expensive though (but then hotels generally are when you start getting into this price bracket). Checking in was carried out quite quickly, but we did time it right as there were long queues on some occasions. We were upgraded to a larger room on the 17th floor which included a fireplace which was a nice feature. In general, the room and bathroom was well equipped, clean and tidy. You could pick it to bits if you really wanted to but I doubt if anything is that perfect. Unless you are out to completely blow your budget, I would suggest you don't get anything out of the mini-bar ($17.50 for a minature whisky), don't pay for a movie ($18.50) and avoid room service (service was good, but again boy do you pay for it!!). I do think for the amount of money that the rooms cost, complimentary bottles of water should be offered. They cost nearly $9 from the mini-bar. We only ate a small meal in Peacock Alley, which was okay but again very expensive. We chose to eat out for the rest of our meals as especially with breakfast you can wander not too far from the hotel and take your pick of eating places which will cost you far less.
All in all we had a wonderful time in The WA and NY, even if our bank balance has taken a beating!! We would recommend the experience.

title: Really Poor Service
body:
The hotel certainly has an certain art deco charm, and I have to say the rooms, although small (it is New York after all), are probably slightly larger than the average New York postage stamp size I have seen elsewhere. However, the service we received there was embarrassingly bad. After the first night of sleeping on pillows so soft that your face falls right through them, I called the next morning to see if it would be possible to get any other pillows for our room. Yes, they would bring us some foam pillows - thank you very much. Later that day (3pm) when we returned to the room there were no new pillows so I asked again, and again they politely told me - no problem, we will deliver them to your room. When we returned to the room after dinner and they still weren't there I called again, and they apologized and said they would deliver them now (11pm). They didn't. They were very polite each time I called (5 times total), but never once did they actually do what they said they would. One of the people I spoke to said she would inform the manager of the poor service I received, and again apologized. I never heard back from the manager.
The pillows weren't really that important and if they had told me that they didn't have any other pillows I don't think I would have cared. But they kept telling me that they would provide the service, and constantly failed to do so. I was embarrassed to mention it again frankly - and didn't say anything at check out. They don't seem to care enough about their guests, so I will not be staying here again.

title: A wonderfull hotel
body: Great location, the rooms were superb. They actually gave us a free upgrade without asking. The cost of breakfast was crazy so we went down the road and had a similar quality breakfast for one third of the cost We would stay there again

title: "Perfect Location, Older rooms"
body:
Great location! Check in was fast and the Lady at the recepcion was nice. My room wasn't ready until 3:00 pm. They promised to text me when it was ready and before 11:00 am they did it. It was great because we were tired.The entrance and reception areas are spectacular, the room was very comfortable but nothing special, old fashioned. I was surprised with the outdated tv.
The cleaning service was very good but every morning we had a terrible wake up around 8 am by the housekeepers, they did loads of noise every morning in the corridor
There is a Starbucks location in the lobby of the hotel, very pricey.
Not a great experience.

title: 'I wish service was as great as this in the uk'
body: Just returned from a trip to New York with my husband. The staff in the Waldorf are very knowledgable, efficient and helpful. In particular I would like to mention John and Jackie on the reception desk who went that extra mile and provided exceptionally great service. The breakfast in the lounge was really nice and the breakfast downstairs in Oscars was fantastic with freshly squeezed orange juice, smoothies, smoked salmon etc. Our room was lovely, quiet and comfortable with everything we needed. The art deco and history in the hotel is facinating. When we return to New York we will book the Waldorf. Thanks for making our stay a great one!

title: Amazing Time at the Waldorf
body:
We arrived at the hotel by car around 1pm and had our car valeted..Very quick and efficient. 
When we got up to Diamond check in there was no one in front of us so we were able to get checked in very quickly. Our room wasn't ready yet so we left our bags with the bell and took off to explore. The double decker tour bus has a stop right outside the hotel. We find this is the best way to see a city and hit all the main spots.... Very convenient. The hotel itself is wonderful. It was our first time there. When we made it back our suite was ready and we were very happy with the room. It was large, clean and very well appointed. 
We ate dinner at the Bull and Bear on the premises.. We went to the bar first to have a before dinner drink. The service was terrible. It looked like they had 2 people serving the entire bar and serving food. Our dinner was outstanding. The food quality was beyond good and service for dinner was one of the best we have encountered. We actually went back there the following night for an early dinner before starting off for a Broadway show.
We loved that there was a starbucks in the hotel and we were given coupons for a free coffee and pastry for our morning breakfast. 
I have nothing but great things to say about this hotel. They even posted my poscards for free. We will say there again on our next trip to NYC. If you are planning to stay here you will not be disappointed..

title: Wonderful service at a great historic hotel
body: My granddaughter and I stayed here to enjoy a week in Manhattan. We had a terrific time with its perfect location, polite and helpful staff, and very comfortable room. From check-in to concierge to room service staff - all were more than courteous and took an extra step to make our stay just that much better. We purchased excellent theater tickets for Wicked from the onsite ticket agent and had several fine meals in the restaurants and room. We would visit again in a New York minute!!

title: Even better than the first time
body: This was our second stay here and it was even more unforgettable. We had a massive suite this time round with great view of manhatten and chryslyer building. I proposed to my girlfriend on the Saturday evening at the Empire State Building and I arranged for some roses and champagne to be in the room for when we got back and the concierge was extremely helpful with this. We got to experience the fantastic brunch at peacock alley-highly recommended!!

title: Worth It
body: Yes it's pricey and yes it's old but in a good way. I spent a couple nights there just to mark it off my bucket list. It is worth the price. Friendly service with a smile. The hotel has so much history and I would recommend the hotel tour that ends with lunch at Oscar's. It was fun to see the ballrooms and a suite. I can't exactly describe it but you feel special there, well cared for. Go, enjoy it, sit in the lobby and observe, you won't be disappointed.

title: what a weekend!
body:
we had a wonderful weekend at the hotel The staff kept calling to see if there was something they could do. The bed was excellent as were the other furnishings They have an ipod if you want to use it The lobby is fun to sit and watch the people
we booked on line and received a good rate
The location is central and walking in NYC is the greatest

title: Lovely room
body: The hotel is beautiful, if the rooms were a bit worn. We stayed for one night. The location was excellent and the beds very comfortable.

title: 5 day break in new york
body: the hotel was outstanding and yes it was being refurbished but this did not deter from an amazing experience .the staff made you feel like royalty and were extremely helpful and curtious .the location was excellent 10 mins walk to time square and 3 mins walk to grand central station.

title: Not as expected
body:
Communal areas were as grand as expected however our room was tired. The shower just spurted water at you which was either hot or cold alternately (very annoying). Although the room was clean at the beginning of the week, by the end of the week it was really dusty despite tipping the maid $3 each day. 
Be aware that there are no tea and coffee making facilities in the rooms, there is room service at $8 for a coffee when you wake up. 
The well know Peacock Alley Bar staff were very aloof, bordering on rudeness with their inability to hold any small talk. Very expensive and like anywhere in New York children are not allowed anywhere that alcohol is served without eating and even then only between the hours of 12 noon and 6pm. This was very annoying and I was eager to sample the craft beer pubs that are quite famous. 
Be mindful that if you do like a decent cup of tea, the expensive breakfast does not serve a good cuppa (ask for two teabags). 
No WiFi in the rooms unless you pay for it and although a large TV the channels were very restricted to American news channels.
Thinking that the land of America was one of hospitality where people will do anything for you was not the case.
Generally we found that New Yorkers were rude and ignorant. Give me England anyday where people apologise for bumping into you in the street and open doors for you.

title: great service
body: its seems they are getting old as a building but still good and perfect service i love the view ow south manhattan that i can see new world trade center

title: Not worth the price
body:
I'm glad I stayed here so I can say that I've done it. The lobby is beautiful and I love the history of the place. And I loved the feeling of getting in a cab and saying "take me to the Waldorf." That said, a legendary luxury hotel should provide a spectacular experience, and this was not that. I was there two weeks. 
First, the good: 
- Gorgeous Art Deco style lobby
- Beautiful marble bathroom with a medicine cabinet and under the sink cabinet, so there's plenty of toiletry space
- Possibly the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in
- Hotel staff was very friendly on check-in, upgrading me to a better room 
- Bellman was extremely helpful after I checked in, testing all the amenities of my room and showing me how they worked
- iPod dock on nightstand
- Helpful concierge
- Plenty of hangers in the closet
- Shades for the window so the room was nice and dark at night
- Waiters in the Peacock Alley Bar were very friendly, if a little slow. (The bar itself is quite overpriced, but that's to be expected here. I paid $44 for a cheesecake slice and a Manhattan.)
- Beautiful fitness center with great treadmills and free water and snacks, although I would have appreciated a squat machine as part of the weightlifting equipment
- Good location with lots around
The bad:
- When I arrived, there was no doorman to help me with my luggage so I struggled with it up the marble stairs into the lobby.
- I had someone stay with me for the weekend. I asked at the front desk to leave her a key to my room so she could come in before I was off work. I've had no problems doing this at other hotels. The front desk said they had to add her name to my reservation, which is fine but I've never seen another hotel do that. They took down the name, supposedly put it in their system, and then the next day they had no record of her. She had to call me and give the phone to the front desk to ask me questions and verify what was going on. 
- The rooms are shabby - paint chipping, water damage on ceiling that's been painted over, black scuff marks on wallpaper.
- The towels and robes need an upgrade, or at least some fabric softener. Not horrible, but rough and on the thin side. 
- The minibar has no prices posted, but you'll be automatically charged for moving things. There's no space to put your own snacks or leftovers from dinner in it - there's a space where you could wedge things in, but it isn't cooled, as I discovered the hard way. 
- I had a bottle of wine that I left corked and half-full on the dresser. The next day, the cork was missing and half of what was left was gone. So apparently the housekeeping staff stole my wine and left it out to spoil. Nice.
- The hotel guide says there's a charge for the fitness center, but nowhere is it posted how much. I luckily didn't get charged, but I don't know if this was a mistake, or if they've changed the policy, or if I got it free for some other reason. Regardless, they should clarify. 
- Wifi is $15 or so per device in-room.
- Terrible channel selection - no Comedy Central to watch Jon Stewart, and I missed a March Madness game I really wanted to watch because the hotel didn't have the channel.
- The Starbucks in the lobby charges a good $1.50 more than other locations for the same drink - save your money and go across the street to the one on Lex and 51st. 
I didn't have a bad experience at all, apart from the housekeeping staff stealing and spoiling my wine, but I wouldn't stay here again, especially on my own dime. I get better service and amenities for less in the Marriotts and regular Hiltons I've stayed at lately, so I'll be going back to them. Maybe worth it if you get a huge discount and you're just staying a night or two for the bucket list.

title: An old fashioned grand hotel gem
body: This is a place full of history & elegance. It is not for the modern sleek looking wannabes. This was the most beautiful elegant hotel I've ever stayed. We had an excutive floor bedroom with a view of the chysler building that made our mouths drop. From that moment we decided we were not leaving the hotel. From an excellent bed, to superb fawning service, we felt like royalty. they showed us the time of our lives. we never wanted for anything. the walls were damask papered & spoke of years of clientle whom visited our room. We loved it. We had lunch at oscars, food & ambience was just made for us. Cocktails at the peacock alley lounge with a piano playing soflty near us. Dinner @ the Bull & Bear was once in a lifetime. we had a premier seating by the front window in the far left corner, perfect for a romantic evening. Back to our room for a starlit view of the chrylser followed by champagne. The next morning back to Peacock Alley for their brunch of heavenly proportions. My husband tried everything he could in 4 trips. I was pampered from the time I arrived till we gathered our luggage @ the bell hop in the garage to pick up our valet car. Lifetime experince. We can't wait to go back again. Next time 2 days, with the spa and late night drinks at Sir Harrys. This was a reminder of the time when men were men & women were dames. It was so Mad Men classic all the way. Hands down our favorite hotel of all time. we'll do the towers for our anniversary next year for a few days. We won't leave the hotel then either. Thank you Waldorf for the most memberable time in my life.

title: Unfaded Grandeur
body:
I jumped on a special offer to stay here for business - all NY hotels are expensive anyway and the WA was not so much more so we thought why not?
This hotel is so large that it spans a whole block. There are very smart shops in the lobby area and several restaurants to choose from. We had breakfast in Oscars which was about as good as it gets but cost us $100 for 2 owch, we thought it was worth it it was that delicious and meant lunch could be skipped anyway.
When we arrived at the hotel we were given an upgrade so we had a suite as big as a NY flat which was fabulous.
Everything about it was so luxurious from the incredibly comfortable beds to the well appointed bathroom. 
I would love to go back to this marvelous bit of NY history.

title: THE Waldorf equal sign Astoria
body:
It restores one’s faith in corporate America when an institution with as glorious a past as The Waldorf=Astoria refuses to rest on its laurels and works hard to remain a class act to this day. Yes, it is an equal sign, not a hyphen and it is THE WA whereas WA's in other cities are simply WA with the lowly hyphen. Presidents have rested their weary heads on its pillows. Corporate titans make billion dollar deals in its meeting rooms. Movie stars hide out from the paparazzi in its suites. Yet common people without any of the VIP treatment accorded the former can still luxuriate in its surroundings and feel they received a great value for their money at this landmark hotel. Indeed the place is bustling with guests from all over the world and most look like average tourists and business people who have chosen The Waldorf=Astoria for the same reason - it is iconic, and it is still very good. A mommy in casual clothes pushing a baby in a stroller would feel just as comfortable in its fabled lobby as some high-priced ad man meeting a client in the lobby bar.
Here is a list of some of the features of The Waldorf=Astoria I especially liked.
1) Efficient check-in despite the formidable array of reception desks resembling a small airport. A smiling check-in clerk that politely spared a couple of minutes listening to my chit-chat even though there was a line behind me.
2) Free wi-fi in the lobby and enough private nooks furnished with deeply cushioned club chairs and sofas where one could set up shop with a laptop. It is inexcusable in this day and age that hotels still charge for a basic necessity like internet access. Waldorf does charge for it in the rooms, but at least it is free in the public areas.
3) Rich, old world décor featuring lots of wood, brass and deep pile carpets with floral design, and better yet, all of it properly maintained instead of showing wear and tear.
4) Top-notch equipment in the fitness center and probably a big enough area for the number of guests it attracts.
5) Incredibly fast elevators with hardly any waiting.
6) Starbucks on the premises and the hotel’s tacit admission that guests would be better off with Starbuck’s superior coffee at normal prices rather than the high-priced stuff from its own restaurants.
7) The additional security of key card access required to take the elevator to the rooms between 6PM and 6AM. Since it is such a great idea, why not make the key card a requirement 24X7?
8) Efficient check-out that doesn’t even require going to the desk downstairs. The bill is slipped under the door the night before, if it is okay, just call in your acceptance from the room phone and leave.
9) Now the rooms! Actually quite spacious for Manhattan, equipped with such thoughtful amenities as a safe, iron and ironing board, coffee maker on request, the thickest, plushest towels of any hotel, light bulbs that are not weak as in most hotels, of course period furniture, the same floral design carpeting that are in all public areas that must have been quite the fashion back then. But there was one problem – the thermostat in the room does not seem to be adjustable. The pre-set temperature was fine for us, but shouldn’t the guest have control over how hot or cold the room should be? This is not the Y for heaven’s sake. As for the bathroom, it certainly was much smaller and looked dated compared to the sprawling bathrooms they are building in the newer hotels. But it was clean.
10) The location? Fantastic! Plenty of places to eat in all price ranges within a five to ten-minute walk. The 51st Street Subway literally facing the hotel and for more options, the Grand Central barely a 10-minute walk. If you like exploring new cities on foot, most of the major attractions are within a 10 to 30-minute walk. We even walked to Broadway twice. Taxis are less than $10 to most places, thanks to The Waldorf's central location, but like cops and waiters, you can’t find ‘em when you really need ‘em. Sorry, cops and waiters – just a joke. Allow ample time for the 8PM Broadway shows because the line for the cab will be long.
All in all, we were amply rewarded by our choice of The Waldorf=Astoria and when visiting Manhattan again, I would not hesitate to stay there again. Actually, this was a father-daughter trip for her spring break from college. Now I owe the wife a stay at The Waldorf equal sign Astoria.

title: Wonderful Public Areas, Average Rooms
body: The hotel's public areas are a wonderful combination of grandeur and elegance, the rooms less so. They have everything you need, but all a bit faded - worn carpet, scuffed and chipped paintwork and wallpaper. The bed though was hugely comfortable and the sheets were high quality, though the towels and bath robes were not, the former in particular being small and rough. All-in-all, in need of a makeover in order to maintain parity with the competition. The hotel is in a good location for the main tourist sites in Manhattan and for accessing public transport.

title: A Fairytale Come True
body:
Taking in the sights in New York? Try to catch a tour of the Waldorf Astoria. Although much of New York includes the shows on Broadway and famous deli delights, a meal at the Waldorf Astoria will delight you.
If you are lucky, you will catch a guided tour through the historic Waldorf Astoria via a Trolley Tour Bus ride. At arrival, you will be greeted with smiles from the very courteous staff at the hotel. Continue on with your tour and catch the shop displays and memorabilia encased in glass. Be treated with kindness and respect from the front desk to the shoe shine station. Be served with tasty delights that will melt in your mouth by the Waldorf Astoria wait staff. From start to finish your journey will be a step back in time. You will be stepping back in time with hand carved marble and sparkling chandeliers. So much to see that you will come back again and again! 
Need to freshen up? The Waldorf has “powder rooms” that will make your mouth drop. Be treated like a celebrity with personal service, hand lotion, fresh towels and probably the cleanest mirrors ever! Why yes…it IS ME! You will be enchanted with the historic aura of the “Starlight Room” where Ginger Rodgers and Fred Astaire danced under the stars. Yes the ceiling actually moved a hundred or so years ago. Today the air conditioning system is now seen from above but one can imagine the stars and the spirits of those whose footsteps once walked through the halls of the hotel. 
Interestingly one would imagine men wearing a tuxedo and women dressed in expensive clothing when checking-in at the hotel…Look again! Dressed casual but no doubt expensively, the line to check-in; is long but orderly. Some guests bring their children to the hotel with them and it is remarkable to see them running about like children in a playground. One would wonder why a hotel that does not have a swimming pool would be a choice for parents. Famous people may come from all over the world to stay at this old landmark and one would wonder “why” when the bedrooms and suites are not nearly as glamorous as some fancy Hyatt Hotel down the street. There is no doubt it is the historical ambiance that brings the elite to this well groomed landmark of New York hotels. Just stand near the center of the foyer and look up at the big clock and check your watch…perfect timing. Yes timing is perfect for a great tour…go now!

title: A Great New York Hotel
body: On arrival our check-in was warm, friendly and efficient. Our room was extremely comfortable, well-appointed and spotlessly clean. Breakfast was excellent. The building itself and furnishing exude a wonderful ambiance of nostalgia which along with an outstanding level of service from all the staff we encountered made for an immensely enjoyable stay. Its location is great for exploring the best that New York has to offer as well.

title: Trip of a Lifetime ?
body:
This hotel is without doubt an icon from a glamorous age and will not disappoint in terms of beauty and elegance. However having booked a twin double suite for myself and two teenage daughters and promised the bed sizes would be large doubles as with all American hotels, and big enough to accommodate us, we were surprised to find a large suite yes, but containing 2 large singles not doubles, this did make our stay a trifle squashed. when I complained they offered me a camp bed for an extra 50 bucks each night!!!! Sorry not good enough when I had just paid £3,000 for this trip before buying anything else!!!! I found the staff both rude and somewhat condescending, in other words I wasn't rich or important enough to be polite to. Many of the guests are also of this ilk. The hotel is open for any Tom dick and Harry to wander through and they do, taking photos as they go which somewhat undermines the exclusivity!!! 
New York is fantastic, but save your dollars and go for a Hilton instead.. Shame on you at the Waldorf......work harder at treating all of your guests in the same manner, whether they are VIP's or not.

title: A family tradition - well appointed luxury hotel
body: My family has stayed at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC several times over the last 7 years. We always have a good stay both in the Towers and the main hotel. Rooms are usually larger than most NYC hotel rooms and are always well appointed with a traditional decor. The staff is professional and helpful. It is not inexpensive and neither is parking ($60/night) but it is a treat. There is a Starbucks on the Park Ave side of the building - slow but conveinant.

title: Simply the best!!!
body:
My husband stayed here on business last week and since it was so close to my birthday, I got to tag along. I was so excited to get to stay in this historic hotel...I always read trip advisor and was a little apprehensive. So I emailed guest services and told them about my trip and that I would be celebrating my birthday. Well it was 1st class all the way...from start to finish. Jackie in the front office checked us in and said we were upgraded to a suite! She even went and got me a Waldorf birthday card. She walked us to thru the lobby and introduced us to the bellhop and even he wished me a happy birthday! Every time I went thru the lobby, he remembered my name and asked if I needed anything! Oh and the room...I mean suite, was fabulous! Overlooking Park Ave and it was really big...even by NY standards. 
So my hubby worked and I shopped and was exhausted the 1st night. Knock at the door and there was a box of chocolates and bottle of wine! I loved it! Thank you Waldorf!!
I think the people that complain about anything at this hotel are just being picky!! Yes, I am sure some of the rooms are in need of a redo. But if you aren't satisfied, then ask to move!! I found the hotel staff to be so nice and they really went out of their way to make my trip special!
So read up on the history of this hotel and make your reservation! I took so many pics and loved wondering around the lobby. 
I also found the bed and linens to be the most comfortable ever...I am going to contact Hilton and ask about the brand. The hotel tolietries are Ferragamo and smell wonderful. So needless to say, I think this hotel is wonderful, and the staff knows how to make each guest feel special.

title: Amazing time
body:
I was getting worried after i had booked because some of the reviews referred to tired rooms and poor service - We spent 4 nights here, the service was amazing, the place is full of history and charm, the room was great...
We did make use of the e-mail sent to us before we arrived and opted for a very cheap upgrade to a king at 25 dollars per night - well worth it...
Its the waldorf, its famous and it exceeded our expectations... 1 thing to watch for, there are a number of additional charges for room service which for example changes the cost of a pot of coffee from 15 dollars to about 24 dollars so do watch that one...
The staff were very kind and very helpful in recommending great local places to eat that were reasonable priced, we had some great thai food at a place down in Hells Kitchen on recommendation from staff, so it is well worth asking them..
Well done Waldorf

title: Classic NY elegance but not true luxury any longer
body: This was my 10th time at The Waldorf Astoria and while one will still be seduced by its grand lobby and lovely shops I am truly convinced that the hotel needs some serious updating/refurbishment. My room was upgraded one level slightly larger (for which I was appreciative) as I had been the one who booked 15 other rooms for a group function. While the check-in process was very pleasant and my room size spacious, the rooms for our entire group were run down looking---carpets in need of cleaning and worst of all-- almost none of our heaters/air conditioners worked causing us to not sleep well due to the high temperature in our rooms. When I called for assistance the only option was to go from a very hot room to having the windows open and being very cold---to their credit they responded immediately to my request. On the plus side: Room service was delicious, courteous, prompt, in large servings and actually worth the typical hotel price for it. The housekeeping was friendly and efficient. The toiletries were plentiful (Ferragamo) and rooms were furnished with excellent linens and lots of towels. If you can get a very good price on the hotel it's worth it.

title: Waldorf Astoria
body:
After staying at the Waldorf in NYC for five nights I have to say it was worth every penny.
The hotel lived up to all expectations, the staff were really kind and helpful.
The beds were so comfortable, the pillows and sheets were out of this world, I have never had better nights sleep.
If you get chance to stay at the Waldorf do it, it is worth it.

title: Incredible Experience! The only place to stay in NYC
body: My wife and I recently celebrated our anniversary at the Waldorf spending six nights at the hotel. Our experience can only be described as remarkable. A tremendously friendly and helpful staff. The room was fabulous. The individual bars and restaurants were all special and wonderful. The hotel delivers on the iconic experience you dream to have at The Waldorf. Very impressive in every respect. Would go back anytime and we feel this has to be the best place to stay in New York. Perfect location for walking to the best of New York.

title: Pure perfection
body: I stayed at the Waldorf earlier this month with my mom and sister and it was incredible. Before I even arrived I was in contact with the concierge, Celso, who did an amazing job putting together and itenerary for us. We stayed in the Towers and our suite was quite spacious for 3 ladies who don't travel light. The check-in for the Towers is not in the main lobby and it was peaceful, easy and the staff was wonderful. Breakfast in the lounge each morning was the perfect way to start our day. I cannot say enough wondeful things about The Waldorf and the professional, friendly and efficient staff they have. I highly recommend this hotel for any occassion ~ it is pure perfection!

title: Very nice
body: We stayed here this past week and had a good time. Our room was nice, somewhat quiet on the seventh floor and a nice view. Service for the most part overall was very good. We were checked in upon arrival around 5 pm without delay- went to Bull and Bear for a quick drink prior to going out on the town- the bartender here was not real friendly or quick to serve but maybe a bad day for him. We did later have drinks in Peacock Alley and very friendly and good drinks- Some of the elevators do have problems and some areas are a little worn- but for the most part pretty good. The Starbucks in the lobby of this hotel does have a "B" rating which is a little strange...We did order room service twice - it was fast and the food was good- You will pay the WA prices however...if you are looking for OUTSTANDING service you may want to try The Carlyle- from the moment you step in that hotel you are well served- I will return to Waldorf Astoria if I can find prices under $300 per night- It is currently being renovated and the outside is hidden behind mesh-

title: Hotel was great but service less than desirable; great location
body:
This is an icon in the hotel world and I wish I could stay here more. I'm a HHonors diamond member and it seems that this property that doesn't really matter. Hilton is very inconsistent lately on how each property treats the HHonors benefits. I never got water and certificates for breakfast, etc. They weren't available at check in for some reason so they were supposed to be brought up. When I left early the next day they never showed up. 
The room was well appointed but the sink had a slow drain and the shower head was loose. It was a bit challenging taking a shower the next morning. Other than the small things that make a big difference, this is a classic NYC hotel.

title: Amazing hotel, amazing room, amazing service
body: My husband and I used points and stayed at the Waldorf for one night prior to taking a cruise from the Manhattan cruise port. Since we are diamond members we usually get an upgraded room. This time was no exception. We were given a King suite room which had a living room with a fire place, a huge entry way a bedroom, a make-up/parlor room and a huge bathroom. The hotel was decorated beautifully and service was amazing. We had a cocktail in one of the hotel bars and the service there was outstanding as well.

title: Long Weekend in New York
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf for a long weekend 22nd March - 26th March. We had a fabulous one bedroom Suite, we had booked a Junior Suite but when we arrived they upgraded us. We were on the 24th Floor and the view was amazing, being able to see in many directions from the multiple windows in our suite. We had two marble bathrooms, which for us was great to have a bathroom each.
The bed was very very comfortable, we both slept very well. Food and drink was very expensive, we had breakfast in Oscars and it cost $98 for the two of us but what a breakfast. Do it at least once, if you can.
The staff were lovely and so helpful, except perhaps for the doormen, who for a prestigious hotel, frankly were disinterested. However, I would stay at this hotel every time I am in New York. In once word.......fabulous

title: Nice property, excellent stay
body: I went to the Waldorf on MLK weekend. We booked 3 rooms, including 1 suite. The suite was very large, with an impressive master bathroom. The kitchen was from the 50's. There were 2 other rooms, each the double beds deluxe rooms. These were small, but cozy. They have an excellent lobby, with true elegance. I will be booking this hotel next year.

title: Awesome
body:
If you are staying in new York this is the place to stay. Top notch staff and right in mid town, nothing is far away. 
Even if you don't have any activities planned, they can help you out

title: Brand Does Not Live Up To Reputation
body:
I spent one night at the Waldorf Astoria, for a work event, and it did not live up to the brand's reputation.
Let me start with the good points. The hotel is in a great location...walking distance to just about everything (MOMA, Madison and 5th Avenue shopping, Central Park). The architecture and grandeur of the hotel is amazing--it is like stepping into history.
The stepping into history is also the downside. The hotel is in need of a major overhaul, as it has not been properly maintained. They are in the process of renovations. Unfortunately, the first room I received was situated on the 4th floor roof, which was being worked on. It was bad enough to hear the drilling but the workers were able to peer directly into my room. That was enough for me to request a new room. 
The second room was much better, and as other reviewers have stated, the newer tower is much better. The room was nothing special and the chipping paint on the door and leaking faucet were all indicators of wear and tear.
The service was good--definitely not becoming of a 5-star hotel. After being on hold for 20 minutes to get my room changed--I ended up gathering my suitcase and going directly to the front desk. The agent who assisted was very nice and helpful.
Overall, I would not recommend. It's nice to tour and get a piece of history and then move on to more modern times.

title: Lovely...
body: We were very well looked after during our honeymoon in early March. The staff is exceptional and the property has an old world charm. Our room was a spacious delight. We cannot wait to return to this most wonderful place.

title: Staying at the Waldorf
body:
The two of us stayed at the Waldorf Astoria during a short break to New York in March this year. We paid a little extra for a superior room and had a view right down Park Avenue from the corner of the hotel on the 13th floor (through the gauze netting! - yes there is scaffolding up also as the hotel exterior is being refurbished, the view only being partly obstructed).
The room itself was fabulous, in a classic art deco style, with a bedroom, small storage room, separate dressing room and separate bathroom, all of which were very grand and a little dated, but that just added to the experience.
We spent some time wandering around the rest of the building, marvelling at what it must have been like in it's heyday, because it's by no means shabby now, despite all the negative reviews that caused us concern before we went.
In summary, if you are expecting a modern, minimalist, clinical experience then this is not the place for you, however, if you are visiting New York and want to stay in somewhere iconic that you will always remember, then it may be for you.

title: Tired and old
body: The Waldorf is meant to be an iconic property in NY but now it just seems old. I stayed 3 days on a business trip and the room I had was just about functional. The cabinet in the bathroom did not close. Everyone expects a tip for doing the bare minimum. Only thing nice was the check in experience at the front desk, which was quite welcoming. The location of the hotel of course is also great. All in all not worth it for the rate they charge.

title: Old in a good way, and in a not so good way....
body:
I stayed at this hotel last week on business in a regular room. The exterior is undergoing renovation, but I did not notice renovations on-going on the interior.
The entrance and interior common areas are old school New York elegance, from the decor to the uniforms of the staff, to the bars and restaurants. The service is excellent, and very professional.
The rooms, on the other hand, are simply old in appearance. The wall paper is pealing, there is paint on the marble in the bathroom, the shower is old and without sufficient pressure, and the toilet looks like it has not been changed since the 1970s, and works that way as well. The door to the bathroom is a pocket door which is badly in need of replacement. The pocket door concept is a bit tacky, but it is needed because the bathroom is so small.
But the bed was new and very comfortable, and there is a nice large flat screen television with all of the amenities.
If the price is really right, I might stay again. But this is not lavish, opulent, old-school luxury New York as far as the room that I had was concerned.

title: Great location: Convenient to mid-town landmarks.
body: Attended a conference based at the property so received a discounted rate. Don't think I would stay here without the discounted rate. Regardless, a historic property with great service, restaurants, and an impressive lobby. As a HiltonHonors member, we were supposed to receive 2 complimentary water bottles daily in our honor bar, but this only happened once during our 4 night stay. So we had to call for the bottles 3 times. Room size was pretty standard for Manhattan. Comfy bed. No charge to use the workout facilities despite what was advertised. Be sure to check out Steve Cohen's Chamber Magic shows in the Towers. Truly amazing!

title: Convenient, Comfortable
body:
It's the Waldorf and an iconic NYC landmark. Yes, it's a bit outdated, but the rooms are a little larger than most of the other hotel rooms that I've stayed in. Bed was very comfortable, lots of big fluffy pillows. Our bathroom was fine. The bathroom cabinets are outdated, but no issues whatsoever. The only downside for us was that it was hard to regulate the temperature and we felt a little stuffy.
I thought the hotel staff was very friendly. There was a NYC buzz about it with tons of people milling about. We also had a drink at The Bull and Bear, which was really nice. 
And finally, extremely convenient to all of the major stuff you want to see.

title: Beautiful hotel, close to many sights
body: This hotel is stunning. It’s really close to the public library, which is next to Bryant Park (a great place to sit and relax, or have something to eat). It’s perfect for a couples weekend getaway <3, as it has the feel of old New York romanticism.

title: Old and musty
body:
The good bits first: extremely friendly staff, beautiful public spaces, super comfortable beds and a great location. 
Now for the disappointing bits: the safe in our suite didn't work when we checked in, you have to pre-order a coffee maker if you don't want to spend mornings in the queue for Starbucks in the lobby (or pay an extortionate amount for room service), the bathrooms look like they haven't been updated since the early 1960s and our ceiling showed clear signs of water damage. Nowhere near as nice as The Peninsula.

title: Insight into a bygone age!
body:
Ok, so you're staying at The Waldorf Astoria in NYC! Are you expecting neon lights and tacky furniture? Or have you opted to stay at this hotel because it is a glimpse at the past? You would probably be aware that this hotel is a little past its sell by date. Any hotel re-built from the 1930's original would be. But I can honestly say I thoroughly enjoyed every bit of it. I have stayed twice now, and I will definitely stay again. 
Check in is smooth. The suite I stayed in was a little dated, the furniture was not of the highest standards, certainly not new. However, the ambience of the place, the atmosphere, the walk down memory lane which includes a wander among the showcases near the lobby is such a joy that I recommend anyone to stay in this hotel at least once if they can. Even if you do not like it and you really need a more modern environment, at least you can say 'I stayed there' and I do believe you will not be disappointed.

title: Walk in the footsteps of presidents and celebrities
body:
The minute you work into the Waldorf’s opulent lobby, you feel you are walking in the footsteps of U.S. presidents, heads of state, socialites, and celebrities. The hall ways and lobbies could tell a million stories; photos of some of its famous guests hang on walls and in display cabinets.
The location is perfect, it is just a short walk to the Rockefeller Centre, Radio City Music Hall, and you can also explore the city's landmark buildings such as Chrysler, Empire State and Rockafella, which are in easy walking distance. Grand Central Station is also a short walk away.
We had a few problems with our original room allocation but this was ratified quickly and professionally, and we were upgraded to the next level of room. Check in was very smooth, with plenty of check in staff on duty.
The room on the 9th floor was a good size, king size bed, walk in wardrobe, marble bathroom and a nice size flat screen TV. Nice view of the Chrysler Building. We loved the main lobby and bar to just sit and admirer the hotels art deco and people watch. We used the bars a few times but not the restaurants, we did use starbucks for a grab and go a few times. My only complaint would be being charged $21 for two very small cups of coffee one night in the main bar, so be aware this is the Waldorf and this is New York, so expect to pay big prices for the hotel food and service, especially room service and the Sunday brunch. Overhaul a memorable stay at The Waldorf Astoria, and it is nice to have a change from an ultra modern hotel and step back into time, and admire architecture and furnishings you just don’t get any more.

title: Terrible Service/Rude Staff
body: I stayed at this hotel for two nights as part of a conference. The decor was ornate and felt outdated. The woman that checked me in was actually quite nice and helpful. The rest of the stay from the housekeeping to the bellhop to everyone else I encountered could not be bothered and were quite unwelcoming. Not to mention that each morning I was woken up by the sound of carts (or something like that) barreling down the hallway repeatedly. I would not stay here again.

title: Classy, relies on it's name a bit
body: I stayed here with my wife for four nights in march. The room was nice, bed was incredibly comfy and the hotel location was great. However the decoration was a bit out of date and overall the place relies a bit on it's name. We paid approx 1200 dollars for 4 nights room only.

title: A step back in time
body: I normally stay in modern hotels but decided to book 5 nights at this iconic hotel. It was just what I was expecting and more. Enjoyed the old charm and opulence of the hotel and had a lovely comfortable room in The Towers an the 41st floor with access to the Towers Suite for continental breakfast. The staff were great, can't fault anyting, I would definitely stay here again.

title: Old hotels have theircharm
body:
Staying at the Waldorf Astoria for a conference was not the best way to enjoy this old hotel, but it made the conference elegant and fun. The hotel retains much of its character and does go the extra mile to give guests a great experience. The building's age does show through with inconveniences like no water for a morning due to a plumbing mishap, uneven heat and cooling, or difficulty with wireless internet. The situations were resolved fairly quickly and to my satisfaction. 
The meeting rooms were elegant and the conference food was very good. I do suggest the hotel work with both the coffee shop and Oscars to expand capacity in the coffee shop and hours at Oscars.

title: Just Wonderful!
body: I stayed here with 3 friends for 4 nights in early april 2012, we had booked the hotel along with flights with an internet travel complany and got a great deal, we booked a room with 2 double beds to minimise the cost. when we arrived the lovely Wayne on reception did us proud and we were given a room with 2 double beds as expected but it also had a "boudoir" dressing room, beautiful bathroom and a vestibule area, so for 4 girls was ideal lots of space to get dressed and store all our stuff it was on teh 7th floor. Wayne also sorted some special vouchers for us as the trip was to celebrate my birthday so we had free cocktails on the night of our arrival and a free breakfast for all four of us the following morning which costs $41 each! and was a wonderful buffet breakfast. We loved the hotel its elegance and history and location and the price, the staff were all friendly exceptionally helpful and couteous. Lots of little complimentary details that just helped make the trip easy, like left luggage facility on our last day, free internet for check- in and printing for boarding passes etc. will recommend time and time again thank you Waldorf form 4 UK ladies who had the time of our lives in NYC!!

title: Historic? No, dated
body:
We stayed for a night to sightsee and shop. This is a grand old building with a great location. Aside from the bellmen and the extremely miserable people who work in the Starbucks outlet in the lobby, the welcome was consistently warm and friendly.
We were allocated a very small room on the 15th floor. This was reasonably well-fitted in a very old-fashioned style but was also quite worn in parts. While we could cope with the small bedroom, the boxlike size of the bathroom was much more of a challenge. There really was no room in there at all and, for this standard of property,and given our gold Hilton Hhonors status, we'd have hoped for much better. 
This hotel trades on its name and its history but for the most part the place just felt dated and in need of a refresh. We moved on to the Conrad at Battery Park which, for the same price, provided a far better experience and a real taste of luxury. Waldorf Astoria next time? No thanks.

title: Landmark Disappoints
body: Our New Years experience was runnied by indifferent unhelpful staff. we rounded off a skiing trip with 3 nights in this iconic new york hotel. While this hotel oozes charm and represents the best of New York the treatment of the hotel staff all but ruined our stay. We transfer in at 11pm from our flight- with 3 children our rooms were on opposite ends of the floor, and neither acceptable nor in line with our booking- some 4 hours latter- at 3 am in the morning and one bed short we were finally able to sleep. the service did not improve the next morning with half promises and a dishonest approach to the problem another 4 hours were wasted until the issue was resolved and adequate accommodation provided- oh yes, a 50% refund of one room for one night was offered as compensation! not what one would expect from a hotel of this standing.

title: Fantastic Hotel!
body: Me and my 6 friends stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for 4 nights in March 2012. We were there for my friends 40th birthday. Before we went, I emailed the hotel to ask if we could have an upgrade as we were sharing 3 and 4 to a room. When we arrived at the hotel we were delighted to find we'd been allocated a suite each with 2 bathrooms. We were also given a voucher each for a cocktail to have in the bar. The hotel itself is very grand with a stunning lobby. The staff at the Waldorf were very helpful and professional in all areas, from bar staff to concierge and reception staff. The rooms were very clean and spacious. The hotel is located 5 mins walk away from the Rockerfeller Centre, 10 mins walk to Grand Central Station, 15 mins walk to the fabulous Times Square and 15 mins walk to Bloomingdales. A fantastic location! Our rooms were booked on a room only basis which wasn't a problem as there were many places to eat breakfast near the hotel. If you're stuck for places to go in the evening, ask concierge as they have a great deal of knowledge of places to go. We all enjoyed our stay and will definitely staying again!

title: Great location and value for money
body:
I really enjoyed the historical displays and information as well as the splendor of the carpet, chandeliers and art deco interior. Yes I agree it is living on its past reputation, but it was one of the cheapest hotel options on our package deal! Our room wasn't made up but we wanted a twin not a double as they thought. They gave us a free cockctail each to enjoy in Harry's as it was a birthday, and that was the nicest drink I have ever had!
There is a great Dehli to eat breakfast just 2 blocks away when leving the Waldorf entrance by their steak restaurant. Turn right, go past the tour bus company touts, and its on your right.

title: Not what I expected
body:
The NYC Waldorf Astoria is a historic property in a great location, but my fascination of the property ends with the stunning lobby. 
The guest rooms are small and exceptionally dated. The windows were covered with plastic rolled shades. Heavy curtains attached to the wall with hooks that had pulled though the wall. Climate control was provided by a loud under window unit that blew air onto guests when trying to get work done at the desk. Wi-fi was $16 per day. The dresser was too small to completely unpack my things. A mini bar had for fee items that guests would instantly incur if moved (magnetic registry).
I stayed at the hotel for a business meeting and found it less than ideal. The meeting spaces were crowded. Breakfast and snacks were poor. Starbucks coffee in the lobby was significantly overpriced. Sunday buffet is $100 per person. Save yourself money and stay across the street in luxury.

title: You pay for history. Don't expect more.
body:
I was very disappointed. I am an adult male traveling with my mother making two beds a necessity. We are meticulous about making sure to book rooms with two beds or we don't book at all.
