So I'm sure you can see where this is going. We showed the check-in staff our exact paper that specified our room was to have two separate beds. We were told there were none available. The staff, however, was very accommodating and told us they could get us a roll-away and then upgrade us to a Suite. Fine, I'll rough it for one night.
So we head up to the room after being told the roll-away is on it's way. 30 minutes pass, nothing. We call back. Another 30 minutes pass, nothing. Only upon the third call (1:30AM) do we finally get a roll away. We sleep.
So the next night we go to the front desk to get keys to our suite. "OK, now this suite is going to have two beds?" "Oh well, it has a couch that turns into a bed. Yeah, but I didn't pay $300 a night to sleep on the COUCH! "This is a four level upgrade, I'm sure you will find it satisfactory."
Ummmmmm...no, actually. I appreciate your effort and generosity on such a large upgrade, but if our problem is that our room has only a single bed, upgrading us to a nicer room with one bed doesn't solve the problem that needs to be solved!
So that was that. We paid $300 a night for one of us to sleep on a hide-away bed for a week. Lame.
The AC units in the rooms are useless and you're discouraged from opening the windows. It takes the strength of the Incredible Hulk to get them open anyway, at which point you're met with the loud buzzing of generators.
The bathroom is the (only) highlight. Our suite had a fantastic tile walk-in shower. Shower head was high and heated up plenty fast. Sink was granite with plenty of space to put your stuff. The usual fare was provided.
To cap off the trip, for some reason the very last night they decided to remake the sofa instead of just leaving the bed down. Around we went again. Called at 5:00, come back from dinner, no bed. Called at 7, nothing. Called again at 8...finally someone came to make the bed down.
Common areas are beautiful (you have to sneak your way into some of the ballroooms) and I did feel for them, that has to be expensive to maintain, but that shouldn't fall on us. Con your way in to take pictures of the common areas, but stay somewhere else.

title: worse hotel ever
body: Check in process was slow as we were apparently getting a better room! We booked a suite which was a room with an old sofa at the opposite end of the room. The bathroom was very small and the wallpaper was peeling off. The toiletries were poor. The room looked nothing like the pictures on the website, old, outdated and felt unclean. We asked to move rooms but were told there was nothing else and that we could change on the final night, this proved not to be the case on the final night. Dont order room service the food is terrible and very expensive. The next day I got up very early determined that the room wouldn't ruin my holiday. I showered and washed my hair only to find the hairdryer didn't work. I rang reception, they apologised and said one would be sent up straight away. 40 mins later I walked down to reception as I still hadn't been brought a replacement. The building itself is very impressive but relies on its name and past reputation, no-one famous appears to have stayed in yrs, I certainly wouldn't stay again. The bar is expensive and not very impressive. Location is amazing, handy for everything and plenty of taxis outside. The staff are fairly miserable and the cleaning staff in room didn't even move an empty coke can. Everything apart from a made bed was how we had left it that morning, (the coke in the minibar was actually out of date, fairly embarrassing.) On the last night, there was some confusion and they had given the promised room to someone else!!! They did offer us a free night on the towers this didn't compensate for the lack of service and awful rooms. If you want to see this hotel, go for breakfast dont waste your money staying here!!! x

title: Great service and location, if a bit dated
body:
Our stay at the Waldorf Astoria was one of the best hotel stays in a while. Service throughout all aspects of the hotel was consistently outstanding: from checkin (where someone called to followup a little while after we got to our room), to housekeeping, and the restaurants. It was truly hospitality as it should be. 
As others have indicated, the guest rooms are a bit dated and small. Fortunately, we knew that in advance and got stayed in a suite. Even so, the bathroom was the same size as the regular guest rooms and it is difficult to navigate something so small. How did our counterparts of 70 or so years ago do it? :) 
The location is great: along the hear of Fifth Ave, a couple of minutes from Rockefeller Plaza, St. Patrick's Cathedral, etc.

title: It grew on us
body: Stunning lobby and communal areas, rooms on arrival looked a bit tired (rather used to hotels with designer bathrooms and trendy window dressings!) , but the hotel just grew on us - we really felt as if we were sharing a little bit of New York history. Staff were excellent. I would stay again. The reason for 4 not 5? Why do they have to charge 15.95 per night per DEVICE for in room wifi. We got fed up with going to the lobby to use wifi- and I'd have thought it would be better for the hotel to waive this fee and not have people loitering in the lobby just to use the wifi. Without this issue, it would have been 5 stars.

title: huge and dated
body: vast hotel in real need of modernisation. Meeting rooms were bizarre and dinner was disappointing

title: Lovely Hotel
body: We found the hotel to be exactly as it says in terms of standards and space. The room was very spacious and the level of service was impressive. It is expensive however it is a great hotel to launch your New York experience. It is close to the subway, cross town buses to the ferry, but also to delicatessens and some lovely eateries. (buy a weekly for the subway, it is money well spent) Only a 15 minute walk to Times Square and Broadway yet far enough away to be able to escape the noise and bussle of the square. Easy to get to all you need to do in New York.

title: Check your bill
body:
We stayed five nights. The room was clean and comfortable but nothing special; yes,they knew it was a special occasion. Breakfast is expensive but the perfect service makes up for that. Dinner at the Bull and Bear is very expensive but very good. The public rooms are something special though some of the the bars are dark and crowded. The biggest blot is the squalid Starbucks - totally out of place. Because of our special occasion we were rewarded with breakfast vouchers for Starbucks - what an insult! When I went to pay the bill I found $198 that should not have been there; it took a lot of trouble to get it removed and I will be checking my credit card statement very carefully.
By all means stay at the Waldorf but don't let them see your credit card.

title: Old yes but not outdated !
body:
The Waldorf Astoria in NYC may be old but the staff is exceptionnal. Eveyone wants you to feel comfortable and 99% of the time will NOT accept tips ! They work for you and are very aware that the customers are the priority. I highly recommend this place, not cheap but worthed every cent. About the being old part, it has it's charm, very homy...
Will have a hard time choosing another Hotel next time !

title: The lobby is exquisite and enchanting but the magic stops there!
body: The bedroom was clean and comfortable and made up to a high standard everyday. However, the decor and furnishings were old and the air conditioning unit left much to be desired. The lobby is beautiful and there is a lovely relaxed atmosphere with people often milling about to use the free wi-fi only available there. We had booked five nights but were contacted by reception half-way through our stay to say we should have checked out, and that we'd only booked three nights. This was quickly disproved and it had been an error by the hotel staff. However, the member of staff dealing with the query was rather unhelpful and unapologetic despite this being obviously upsetting and unsettling to my mother, whom i was traveling with. There is also work being conducted to the front of the hotel. I paid for a five star hotel to get away from the daily unpleasantries back home and certainly did not expect to be rudely awoken each morning by thumping and banging and on one occasion a workman standing outside my window!

title: Nice but rooms nothing special
body: My daughters and I stayed 5 nights. Our room was clean, comfortable but nothing special. The public areas of the hotel are beautiful and it was a lovely experience for us to stay here. The location of the hotel was perfect for us, with some great places to eat within walking distance.

title: As expected
body:
Check in was very OK. The lobby is very nice and has an atmosphere of old heritage. Polite receptionist who was friendly and gave us a room on the 26.th floor. I belive we were upgraded, but not sure. 
The room was spacious with a large flat screen TV, double bed, safe, mini-bar, AC, bath tub etc. We were given free wifi access at check in.
We got vouchers for complimentrary breakfasts at Starbucks which is located at ground floor. 
All in all I would say that the staff was friendly and helpful. The public areas at the hotel is nice. I find that the rooms are the largest drawback at the hotel. The room we stayed in should have been given a make over.

title: First Time at Waldorf Astoria
body: My wife and I recently went to NYC and stayed at the Waldorf Astoria. I must admit that the hotel is still grand, and the lobby areas, and the public floors are amazing. We are Hilton Honors members, and the Waldorf is part of the Hilton program. So, upon check-in we were upgraded, and all of the staff that we encountered were first-class, every hotel in the world should be at this level! As for the rooms, they are clean, and a bit dated, and if I could suggest any improvements, it would be in the rooms, as the heating and air had issues, and just an overall facelift would help. But I would definitely stay here again, you're in close proximity to many NYC attractions. The restaurants are incredibly overpriced, but there is a Starbucks located inside the hotel on the Lexington Avenue side (I think that's right). Or you can walk out of the hotel to a food cart or deli within a few steps. Overall I enjoyed it immensely.

title: Good, but falls short of its own aspirations
body:
I got upgraded to the Waldorf Towers, so these comments are with respect to the expected standards of a very high-end facility. I had a nice although not overly large, corner room. It was clean. No sign of the bedbugs that are such a problem these days in NYC. The bed was comfortable, the towels thick, and the provided robe was comfortable. It was fun using the provided remote controls to make the shades go up and down and the blinds open and close. The bathroom was all marble, something so needless as to itself be fun. But, all in all, not the experience it could and should have been. Here are a few issues: 1. While the automated blinds and shares were fun, they failed to keep out the light. 2. There was a a considerable tangle of wires behind the desk, leaving no place to plug in chargers. 3. The TV was a HD plasma, but only analog signals were supplied, resulting in a poor quality picture with people appear short and squat. There was a surprisingly limited number of channels from which to select. There was a TV in the mirror in bathroom, but it didn't work properly so that it had only two channels. The rugs in the halls needed shampooing. The switches were extremely fancy but their internal illumination couldn't be turned off, thereby resulting in their emitting sleep-disturbing light even when it was dark outside. The shower head was too large for the amount of water provided resulting in a concentrated rather than dispersed stream of water.
None of these are terrible, but its disturbing that there are so many of them. If I had paid the full rack rate for this room, I would have been irritated. As it was I was merely bemused.

title: Historic Landmark
body: If you're a history buff or enjoy the atmosphere of by-gone eras, then you'll enjoy The Waldorf Astoria. The location is fabulous and very central to many of the "must see" sights. Our room was large and had been redone at some point, but the carpet is old, the sofa was old, and the room decor was very "grandma-ish". The price point is high but what isn't in NYC these days? The buffet breakfast was good, but certainly not worth the price, but then again, it's NYC. Would I stay there again - no - I would be just as happy in a more modern hotel in a smaller room, that was less of a tourist sight in itself.

title: Disappointing
body: I have just returned from my stay at the Waldorf Astoria hotel and would have to say it was a very disappointing experience, upon arrival the guy at the door informed us that there was a lift to take you the lobby to the lobby so that you did not have to carry your suitcase up the stairs when we walked past the lift we had two cleaners shout at us from across the door asking us where we were going, not a good start, we went to check in only to be told that the room we had booked (two double beds) was not available, that it was only a request, and the hotel tried to honor requests, something that should have been pointed out before we checked in. Eventually we were offered a two bed room (smoking) which was fine as one of us smoked but wasn't ready, they said they would call us when it was ready, at 7:30 pm still no call, but when we went back to the hotel the room in fact was ready just didn't call. I had travelled from Ireland. Overall,a very disappointing, overpriced experience, and robe honest I wonld not recommend it, the hotel is out dated and could do with a make over.

title: A rip off from start to finish, service appalling
body: We stayed for 2 nights, safe did not work after 5 times of reporting it and 5 times of taking our valuables to the holel safe. The hotel told us 4 times they had fixed it and had not. Room was old, very old. The bathroom was small, very small and the shower was weak and slow to say the least. We were "upgraded" to the towers but in reality they had run out of useable rooms (so the receptionist told us "off the record"). The continental breakfast was so inadquate we had to eat again outside the hotel straight afterwards. Would I use this hotel again??? Not ever.

title: Fabulous !
body: Best stay ever in NY, classy, big rooms, clean and well appointed. Very upscale old style. Will go back there !

title: Beautiful and iconic
body:
The hotel is stunning in it's aged grandeur. The foyer and reception areas are truly beautiful. We were so pleased that we picked The Waldorf.
The staff are really helpful. We mentioned that we were here to celebrate my wife's 40th birthday when we checked in and were upgraded to a fabulous executive suite. 
Ocassionally there was only one concierge on duty, but we were informed this is as a result of cost cutting since the hotel became part of the Hilton group and not the way it used to be. The concierge's were really helpful, even if overworked - dealing with telephone calls, whilst dealing with the queue of people in front of them.
The location is great, within walking distance of Times Square, Empire State, The Rockefeller Centre, Grand Central etc. 
We would have no hesitation in staying here again, and highly recommend it for those who want more ambience, history and warmth than the newer modern hotels around.

title: Charming but a bit dated
body:
Just completed my east coast trip with a 2-night stay at the Waldorf. 
As a HHonor Diamond member, we were upgraded to a 2-room Park Avenue view suite. However, some of the windows look out to scaffolding, as the property is undergoing some remodeling, so we can only enjoy "partial" Park Avenue view. 
The suite is very spacious, but a bit dated. The bathroom is very small, but clean, well-stocked and functional. 
We read all the reviews before booking, so we expected the room to be a bit dated with old fixtures and furnishings. In my opinion, they actually added to the charm of this hotel.
All in all, a pleasant, but not perfect stay.
Pros:
Great location. Walked to 5th Avenue shopping, Central Park and easy access to subway train (the only train available was 6 while we were there, since E and M were closed).
Large room(s)
Charming public spaces
Con:
Although we are in a non-smoking room, the vent in our bathroom would have heavy smoke wafting out of it at times.
Some staff and concierge are friendly, but some seem to have an attitude... maybe it's a New York thing?
The A/C didn't work the first night, but after reporting it, it worked great for the rest of our stay.
I believe people are generally disappointed with the property if they paid a hefty sum to stay there, have high expectations and didn't do the research before booking. This isn't the best hotel we have ever stayed in, but we did enjoy the hotel very much! Will consider coming back to this hotel if we ever visit New York again.

title: Run down
body: Over priced!... the room 768.. was very small...too dark.

title: Classic, not Modern
body: Stayed here on Saturday as a birthday surprise for the evening. The hotel was clean and courteous, however the room was very old looking and the "double" bed was rather small. The hotel looked like it was decorated from the 80's, very dated, with floral wallpaper and rugs. I guess that is what the hotel is known for though. There was something on our bathroom floor, we called the front desk and they sent someone up immediately to check it out. They could not move us as the hotel was booked for the evening, but they were apologetic and offered to have someone reclean the room. There was no ice machine on floor 28, only on floor 17 so that was a little annoying. I think the hotel if for the older sophisticated crowd. If you are looking for modern I would not recommend this hotel especially for the younger generation. It was an experience and I am glad to check it out, but I don't think I will be staying there again as I think NYC has better hotels for a more affordable price with better amenities.

title: Does not worth it
body: this hotel does not worth $ 1 , it is dirty and outdated . it needs complete renovation

title: Lovely Waldorf
body:
Stayed for a 3 night break in February. Price was superb - presumably special offer as the exterior was being renovated.
We asked for an upgrade on reception (told to do so by friends; normally wouldn't have the nerve) and the man on reception, who was pleasant and courteous, upgraded our room to a lovely one, large by NY standards, and gave us some complimentary drinks vouchers to celebrate a birthday.
The only downside was the left luggage man was rude on our last day - he should have a job as a NY cabbie. I believe the service is subcontracted and the Waldorf should pay attention in this respect.
A wonderful nostalgic hotel and for the (minimal extra cost) over a bog standard midtown hotel when we booked was a bargain to stay here.

title: A Lovely Stay at The Waldorf
body: Stayed here for 6 nights in April. The hotel exterior is being renovated currently but this didn't impact on the old world glamour of the place. The reception area is just beautiful and a great place to sit and people watch. Our room was fine and over looked Lexington Avenue on the 9th floor. We never heard any noise from other rooms in fact the only noise was from the sirens and horns of passing cars. We ate in both Oscars and The Bull and Bear. Both great food but expect to pay Waldorf prices if you do the same! We loved the framed black and white photographs on the walls of famous people who had styed at The Waldorf it just added to the glamourous feel of the place. If it's good enough for every American president then who are we to disagree??!

title: Wonderful Astoria!
body: We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria in March and it has been the very best hotel we have ever stayed in. The Waldorf Astoria was truly wonderful in every way and the hotel made our trip to New York even more special. Thankyou so much Waldorf Astoria for making our stay truly unforgettable! We hope to return some day. Thankyou, thankyou, thankyou!!!!!!!!!!

title: Very disappointing!
body: Because of my Diamond status with Hilton Honors, I was told that my room was upgraded. If that's the case, I'd hate to see the room I was originally assigned. The Waldorf used to be one of the top hotels in NYC. However, it appears that the rooms have not been updated since the '50s. The wallpaper was peeling, carpet was dirty and worn, heating/air conditioning did not work. No matter what setting, the same lukewarm air came out. My hot water did not work in my shower. I called once, waited 15 minutes, then called again. Still no maintenance after 45 minutes. I finally took a cold shower. I would never stay here again, even if they offered me a free room.

title: Wonderful stay at the Waldorf
body:
Have recently returned from a seven day stay at the Waldorf and when asked what was the highlight of our trip to New York...the answer could only be the hotel! We were under no illusions about hotel before we arrived, having read many of the mixed reviews on this site and are finding it difficult to understand some of the criticisms of the hotel.
We had a wonderful standard room on the 22nd floor with views over the church and Park Avenue which was decorated in the style we would have expected and hoped for in a classic older hotel. It was slightly smaller than some might expect but spotlessly clean. The art deco features throughout the hotel were beautiful and as our week progressed we appreciated them even more as we were much more aware of the finer detail.
We took the tour of the hotel which included lunch with a Waldorf Salad in Peacock Alley.The guide was excellent and her enthusiasm for the hotel and its history was obvious. This includes a visit to one of the suites in the Towers and the function suites.Worth seeing! At fifty dollars each we felt it was good value for money.
We did not eat at any of the other restaurants in the hotel.....they are expensive but probably not anymore than similar restaurants in the city. Sitting having a nightcap in any of the bars was a very pleasant experience with good service and great for soaking up the late night atmosphere of the hotel! All staff were very warm, courteous and helpful at all times.
In conclusion, staying at the Waldorf was an unforgettable experience, where, if you let it, you felt as if you were soaking up the history of the building as you turned every corner!
Maybe we were lucky but if you allow yourself, you will enjoy it just as much as we did!

title: Fabulous Waldorf!!
body: We stayed at the Waldorf for Easter for 4 nights as were attending friends wedding and must we had and amazing stay. We were upgraded to a mini suite on arrival (without asking for one). Our room was huge with a kitchen and the bed large and comfortable. The staff were there when needed and when we had a problem with the bathroom they sent someone within 5mins to sort the issue out. Nothing was too much trouble and everyone was polite and friendly. When we arrived back at our room to find the maid exiting she closed our door and made us use our key card so security was top notch. We most definatley will be returning to the Waldorf but will next time make sure we do the Sunday brunch as it looked out of this world and a shame we had plans that day! Blooming brilliant!!!!

title: Cavour60
body:
The only irritating problem we met at the hotel was when we arrived at 7:00pm after flying to NYC from the other side of the world. At this evening-time we had to wait after in-checking over one hour before our room was ready. Not best possible recommendation for W-A. 
Due to the fact that this is an old hotel building some furnishings and equipment in the rooms may be quite old-fashioned, but generally nothing big to complain about.
The beds are indeed very comfortable and guarantees you best possible rest.
The service is over all good, polite and helpful.
In the breakfast room on 26th floor you have a good chance to enjoy entertaining stand-up comic, when some self-important - a very few - guests try by all manners to show the surrounding how bored they are to be among ordinary and unimportant common guests.
I can guarantee that this is a professional and highly amusing show to start a nice day.
The public area with its charming atmosphere gives an extra touch to the stay in this in so many
 ways historic hotel.
Over all a very memorable experience with a strong feeling: we be back.

title: New York, New York!
body:
Unfortunately the fascade was covered in Scaffolding when we arrived but this hotel is a beautiful classic, with a stunning lobby which has a real buzz about it and free wi-fi!! 
An excellent location for exploring the city and the staff freindly and helpful. nothing too much trouble.
Some of corridors could do with a revamp, and double glazing wouldn't be a bad thing in the rooms to the front, there was there was a bit of a draft and noisy sirens all through the night, but thats New York. 
Bar and restaurants were expensive as usual in the level of hotel but all in all a good stay.

title: Never Fails to Impress
body:
My girlfriends and I had a wonderful 2 night stay at one of the greatest hotels in New York, The Waldorf. We were warmly greeted and courteously taken care of by Benito. Benito stored our bags for us until we checked in. I knew we were early, but started the check-in process with Tim at the Gold desk. We had brunch reservations and were in no rush to check-in. Brunch was spectacular--endless gleaming trays of lobster, shrimp, oysters, Beouf Wellington, Lamb, chicken..too much to mention. I had lobster Eggs Benedict..oh yummmm. Caviar, sushi, even the Waldorf Salad was on the buffet--sweet eaters will have their sugar fix with the gorgeous array of deserts, complete with chocolate fountain. Of course, we can't overlook our attentive waiter, Farhad and thank him for making us feel that this brunch was just for us, and never rushed us during our 3 hours at the table, yes 3 hours....
I am so glad Crystal completed my check-in process. Our room was just awaiting 'inspection' so we ventured to the gift shop. I was so honored that Crystal found us in the gift shop and brought our keys to us, going out of their way must just be the norm for the Waldorf! By the time we got to the room, the bellhop was waiting for us. To our surprise it was Servando....oddly enough he had been our bellhop the last time we were there and made us feel like we were old friends of his.
Our room was a mini-suite with a separate living room, pull out sofa, 2 bathrooms, 2 tv's. The room was our home for 2 days and we felt very comfortable. Our beds and pillows gave us all sweet dreams at the end of the night. 
Our second day began with a tour of Guerlain spa. Thanks to Veronica who showed us around, we were immediately smitten and we all booked a spa treatment on the spot. I booked the Imperial Massage with Anita, wow, relaxing to the max! Someone booked a pedicure with Rodica and loved it! Each massage suite has it's own shower, changing area and toilet....we all felt as though we could have spent the night in one of these suites! We enjoyed some champagne afterwards, which was such a treat! 
The Platinum martini at the Peacock Alley bar is worth a try. Try to get an extra blue cheese stuffed olive, they are delicious! Onto the Bull and Bear for dinner. I've got to say our meal was plentiful, Porterhouse, onion rings, truffle fries, spinach....no matter how good a meal is, it's the experience that goes along with it that makes it extra ordinary..and we have Abdul to thank for that. He was the perfect server for us, he smiled a lot, was there when appropriate and even brought us cookies for desert! 
We were just about to walk down the stairs to leave the hotel when Benito was at the top taking our bags from us. What an honor to have the person who we first said hello to be the last person we said goodbye to. Waldorf, thank you, thank you for making us pumpkins feel like Cinderella's. Only 360 more days till we're in Girl heaven again!

title: Memorable stay!
body:
Ok so it's mainly memorable because my boyfriend proposed in our room at the Waldorf, but I'd have still given it 5* regardless! We stayed here for six nights. Good underground car access area so you can get in and out of taxi off the street and straight into the hotel. Porters are extremely friendly, as were reception staff. Work being done on outside of the building so couldn't appreciate the external architecture but the lobby was very grand, though a little confusing it was so big!
We booked a double but got upgraded for free to a junior suite, meaning we had a lounge and extra bathroom, great bonus. The rooms were very big, modern and clean. They were well-maintained daily by cleaning staff. We were on floor 23 and had no noise issues from outside or in the hotel. The only issue we had was that we expected a hotel of this size to offer free wifi but it was quite expensive to use.
Location is superb, close to all the central sites and very close to the big department stores so you can pop home to drop off your shopping before going out somewhere else.
Just to add we booked through Expedia so got an extremely good deal. When we mention to people where we stayed they assume a high cost but we feel this was a great value hotel for what we paid.

title: Beautiful hotel
body: Me and my brother went to New York for a long weekend, we stayed at The Waldorf Astoria in a Deluxe Double with 2 Double Beds, it was a lovely spacious room. On arrival, our bags were taken and kept until check in, after we arrived in our room, our luggage arrived moments later. The staff were friendly and helpful, you soon get the hang of tipping and they are gracious and courteous when accepting it. We had drinks in the bar on the first night which were fairly expensive but to be expected in such a prestigious hotel in New York. The atmosphere in the hotel is welcoming and quite magnificent, I would definitely stay here again next time I visit New York.

title: Wonderful Waldorf
body: I booked a room at the Waldorf for one night at the AAA rate. When we checked in on April 14, the very nice woman at the front desk gave us a complimentary upgrade and we ended up with a beautiful, big, corner room on the 30th floor of the Waldorf Towers, facing uptown. She also gave us a $30 coupon for their spa, and complimentary breakfast. The room was divine. Breakfast on the club floor was delicious....tasty mini croissants and fresh fruit, fresh squeezed orange juice, and many other choices. The location in midtown is great, the fantastic lobby and art deco accents add to the experience.

title: Top NYC hotel
body:
The service is wonderful. The lobby check-in was busy but the staff is very effecient and lines never seem long. The standard rooms are of average size but very well furnished. The beds are very comfortable. Distance to sights midtown are within walking distance but the hotel is removed from the tourist area. Subway is just a few blocks away, buses, and Grand Central Station for trains are convenient as well. Guests rely more on taxis as this is upscale and there are usually several limos are parked out front for their customers. The concierge desk is unbeatable for any assistance.
Keep in mind the location is not far from the UN, and very popular with diplomates and not unusual to find Secret Service with their lapel pins and ear wires strolling the area with a take charge attitude. Wouldn't want to stay here when the president is in town as I once did a few years ago.

title: Elegant, Sophisticated - a great stay!
body: I loved this hotel.... However, we booked a "deluxe double" but the room they gave us didn't look at all "deluxe" to me so, I rang straight down the reception and gave them my feedback. They were very accommodating and took my comments on board without question, we were immediately upgraded to a room on the 16th floor with a boudoir and a gorgeous bathroom. But it wasn't available until the following night so they gave us a $50 room credit. Its a real shame we didn't get this room when we arrived but it was worth the wait! The hotel has a Starbucks near the entrance (very good for breakfast) but beware - if you go down between 7.30 - 9.30 you are likely to be in a 10/15 min queue. I met a friend for drinks in the bar - two glasses of wine and two mojito's came to around $120, very expensive! We ate out so I can't comment on the food. The staff are extremely helpful and the housekeeping staff excellent. The hotel is very central - its a few blocks away from the Rockafeller Centre, Times Square and 5th Avenue. The sightseeing bus stops right outside (a good idea for a first visit - top tip though, stay on the bus for the whole tour before deciding what to visit, that way you get a good idea of whats where and the distances between - New York is a BIG place to walk!). We visited Woodbury Common Outlets which were good.... not the best "Premium" outlets I've been to but good enough for some bargains. You can arrange the bus from the hotel but beware, it drops you back somewhere completely different to where you were picked up! I travelled with my mum to NYC, she loved the Waldorf too - we are hoping for a return visit someday.......

title: Great location
body: Stayed here on a leisure trip to NY. It's central location ensures that most sites are within walking distance. Our room was large and quiet. The bath did not drain properly on the first morning but this problem was rectified immediately by housekeeping even though we hadn't highlighted it. Didn't eat breakfast there as it's $40 a head and I personally couldn't justify that given the options available in some many nearby cafes. The decor may not to be everyone's taste but we had a large TV, a very spacious room and didn't require cabs/ public transport, it's very hard to find fault with this hotel.

title: Waldorf NYC
body:
Stayed at Waldorf Astoria for 6 days 5 nights, Excellent position for Walking to to sights of New York, Staff at the hotel very helpful and obliging,we were a family of 4 sharing the room was of average size, the ensuite bathroom was not that clean and the sinks and toilet blocked on two occassions,the shower was very poor, plumber sent in and wiped the floors with towels allocated, then left them in the room,did complain, received an apology of sorts, not, in my opinion, what should be expected of the Waldorf.
The room had no view, other than that of another skyscraper,that was very close,the outside of the hotel had scafold all around and no work seemed to be happening, also one side of the building was covered in netting.
Fabulous experience visiting New York and had a great time pity about our room and sanitary arrangements

title: Elegance and Location
body: We go to Waldorf every year about the first of April, this year I booked the Queen and it was more elegant than the King rooms I've had before, check in was a breeze of only a couple of minutes, the room always clean and the whole experience is special. Centrally located we can walk or take the subway to wherever we wanted to go. Just plain excellent.

title: what do you expect?
body:
We booked through booking.com and got the standard room on the 15th floor. Room was fairly spacious but the decoration was 'dated' with old carpet.
No upgrade and coupons for us, helas....We arrived too early and were asked for a telephone number so that the reception lady could ring us when the rooms was ready; we are still waiting for the phone call....
Staff is very professional and friendly though and the hotel is a real landmark.

title: Overrated
body:
This is without a doubt a beautiful property. The door service was excellent, concierge service okay. It is, of course, a pricey place to stay. What was really galling was the "nickel and diming" that went on as full paying guests. Wi Fi was $14/day. They charged to use the fitness facility. There are no coffee makers in the room, but there is a Starbuck's in the hotel; however it had had no sitting room We purchased coffee and oatmeal, and tried to then sit in the restaurant with it, but were told there is a $25 charge to sit there were we not ordering from their menu. The ice machine on our floor did not function the 5 days we were there, so we either had to go to another floor or order from room service (which of course meant tipping). The bar is obscenely overpriced, with the "well" champagne being $25 per glass.
I cannot see us returning to this hotel with that kind of attitude towards it's customers. There are way too many other choices in the city.

title: Classy Hotel in a great location
body:
Really enjoyed our stay. Great service and professional staff. The location was great especially when we started exploring the neighborhoods of the hotel. Instead of going towards Time Square I recommend to go the restaurants around 3rd Avenue. 
The lobby is quite amazing and the bar with the piano player is a lovely place to relax in the evening. The bar staff recognize every guest which makes you feel very welcome. 
Sadly the airconditioning in the rooms is not very good and even blasts out hot air during the night. As you couldn't open the windows the rooms were very warm in the night. But that is my only complaint. Everything else was great.

title: Classic hotel....
body: I would echo what others have said, the entrances and foyer areas to this hotel are fabulous and beautifully maintained. The staff are extremely efficient and polite and are very helpful but this is a four star hotel so I would have really expected that and they delivered. The service was good but it is a large hotel so a little impersonal for me. We were also upgraded to a mini-suite which was lovely but I have to say I was a little dissapointed the bedroom and bathroom were lovely but the small sitting room was dare I say a little shabby... I know they are in the process of refurbing so I know it won't be like that in the future(hopefully). It is in Midtown (East) and there are so many attractions nearby it makes it a brilliant location as a base ... it is a thrill to be able to say I went to New York and stayed in the internationally known Waldorf but I would probably stay somewhere smaller where service is a little more personal next time.

title: Classic Hotel Not without Flaws
body:
I was here recently for meetings in a Suite and wish it had gone without a hitch giving the money that was being spent. Check-in: Room was not available at check-in (which was fine given my arrival time), but a text was to be sent when the room was ready. I never received a text and when I checked back in at 6 pm, the panicked desk clerk initially thought that the room was still not ready. I was supposed to be having a series of meetings in the suite and needed to get the suite number to everyone. Crisis was averted when the cleaning crew confirmed that the room was indeed ready.
The Suite itself: The suite was huge - big living room, small entryway, big bedroom, a big dressing room and a huge bathroom. Traditionally furnished, the rug needed replacing as it was stained, but the bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. I thought the room/bathroom were also very clean.
Room service was excellent - very quiet when refreshing the beverages/food during meetings and reacted quickly to various requests.
There is something to be said about staying in a NYC "Institution". Overall, despite the snag at check-in, my stay was pleasant and I'd definitely consider holding other meetings/staying here. Although, given the expense, if I was on my own dime, I might make a cheaper choice of hotels.

title: Terrific stay, lives up to expectations ...
body: Although the rooms are a little dated, I suppose thats part of its charm. Staff were nice, place was clean, its got the history to boot. I went there with my fiancee and we really enjoyed our stay. No complaints.

title: Great place to stay one time
body: We had a great stay at the Waldorf. After reading many reviews, I made a point to email the hotel and request a room with an upgraded bathroom and a functioning AC. The request was met for the most part. We had a superrior king room that had a beautiful large bathrrom that looked newly updated and included a separate shower and bath. Unfortunately, the AC was obviously very old and worked about half the time - suprising for a hotel of this price and supposed caliber. The service was great and the lobby areas are stunning. Food in the hotel restaurants was extremely expensive (think $36 cheeseburgers) but we knew this going in. Overall we enjoyed our stay very much. However, I have no doubt that we could have done better for the price that we paid. We had always wanted to stay at the Waldorf. Now that we have done this, we will definitely stay somewhere else next time.

title: Fantastic Service, So-So Rooms
body: The stellar customer service and lobby are the only reasons I would choose the Waldorf on my next stay in Manhattan. The rooms are an average size for NYC standards but dated and in need of some TLC to bring them up to Waldorf standards - particularly the bathrooms. Room was clean but old A/C unit was very noisy. Bathroom were very small. The mid-town location is convenient and you are close to Grand Central Station, which is also a plus. The lobby is grand and well-worth a slow stroll through to people watch and check out the beautiful ceilings and tile work.

title: Heating excuse and poor service.
body:
Totally agree with Lisa V below. we complained about the lack of heating every single day to be told the same excuse ( the building is regulated ) it was so cold outside we were wearing gloves. A porter eventually brought us two heaters after two days, one was broken and the other was covered in dust. after more complaining, which just spoils your holiday really doesn't it?, we were offered a free one night stay... Big deal we are hardly going to return across the Atlantic to stay in a cold dreary hotel for one night. 
We refused and were given a lunch credit of 200 usd. Sounds great until you realise the room cost us 700 usd per night and lunch is an average of 85 dollars each ( there were four people in my family so the credit wasn't enough).
The room was a good size and the beds were delightful with feather duvets and pillows but I do agree with other reviewers on the tired look of the rooms and the lack of attention to detail. If you want to stay here for the point of saying you've been then try not to pay too much and take a warm cardy.
One final point - the room service menu was missing in our folder and even after requesting it, it never arrived. This seems to be common so don't take anything from the mini bar, it's censored for weight, or it will cost you dearly and don't order tea in your room it is priced at eight dollars a cup!

title: Amazing
body: We have recently returned from our first trip to New York. We stayed at the Waldorf. The staff could not do enough to help. They upgraded us to the Waldorf Towers where the suite was amazing. The charm and ambience of this hotel sums up the New York experience. I cannot recommend enough and would certainly return there give the opportunity.

title: One of the World's Finest Hotels
body: It was an absolute pleasure to be able to stay at the Waldorf. We got a great deal and took a double room big enough to cope with our family of 4. The place is fabulous and dripping in History and nostalgia. As you would expect the staff were so friendly and helpful and some of the nicest people you would meet. They appeared happy to interact and interested in us as guests. I definately would try and revisit if ever I went back to NYC.

title: An interesting place to stay
body:
The Waldorf Astoria is an interesting hotel. The history of this Art Deco style establishment is incredible.
I am glad that my husband and I stayed there.
(8 nights in total,in a Junior Suite )
The location of this hotel is good, the service, overall, was reasonable.
The foyer is incredible however and the lobby is usually a hive of lively activity.
(please note: we were there in April)
Overall:
7 out of10

title: Great location, great brand but.....
body: This is my first time back in the hotel since the 1990's and while it still has the ability to wow, there were signs the hotel may be trading on its laurels a little. For example room not in great condition - superficially very grand but look at the small stuff and it's evident no one has looked at the detail - lint in vents, heavy over painting on door hinges, loose AC controls, screw hole in the back of bathroom door etc. not quite what things should be (or were!). Hilton HHonors continues to disappoint relative to other loyalty programs - but that's not the Waldorf's fault.

title: Good to say we've stayed there but would only go once
body:
Been to New York a few times before but this was my fiancé’s first trip so thought i'd splash out. 
Firstly this is a grand hotel and even if you're not staying here you should venture inside just to explore the lobby. 
Check in was quick and there are plenty of desk Staff to assist you. You get a map of the city when you check in which i thought was a nice touch.
You are then shown to your room by a bellman who gives you a quick run down of what the hotel has to offer.
We upgraded to an exec room which was a decent size. Although the decor probably hasn’t changed for a while, i’d say it was in keeping with the theme of the hotel and i had no complaints.
All in all i was happy with the choice we made however, because it was so Grand i did find it difficult sometimes to relax around the public areas. 
The majority of the guests appeared to be from the “fur coat brigade” if you know what i mean. Nothing against that however when you’ve spent long days walking around the city it would have been nice to have slumped on a sofa with a beer, without feeling like having to get changed into a shirt and trousers first.
We are returning to New York in December and this time we are staying at the Distrikt. Not because of anything negative at the Waldorf, but we think the atmosphere will suit as more.

title: Always Good
body: Centrally situated with great access uptown and downtown, the Waldorf remains a favourite with awesome beauty. Good service and willing staff all fits in with the legend. Best rates available online on the hotel website about 3 weeks before arrival.

title: An icon, but service could be better
body:
We stayed at the Towers as part of a group and we were very excited about it. You don't get to experience a hotel of this historical significance, this fancy and this expensive that often. In addition, the Towers is a more exclusive part of the hotel, with its own check in lobby and private elevators.
The lobby of the Waldorf Astoria is, of course, memorable. The iconic clock, the elaborate woodwork and ceiling, all of it is awe inspiring. As we got here early, we left our bag with the bell captain and went to explore Manhattan. On our return, we checked in and got to our room.
The room was smaller than we expected and somehow disappointing, or at the very least, short of our high expectations. Of course, the bed, sheets and pillows were of the highest quality and comfort. The bathroom was very small, with almost no shelf room to put toiletries. 
At the Towers, you don't get an ice bucket where you can go get ice from the traditional ice machine. No... You call room service for them to deliver your ice. It took almost an hour. However, the ice arrived on a silver platter, in a silver bucket, and a silver spoon to scoop it with. It also came with monogrammed glasses. Very nice touch. When we ordered ice the following day, it arrived much quicker.
We also received a beautiful monogrammed box of chocolates. I am not sure if this is given to all Towers guests or if it was part of our group perks.
As a guest of the Towers, you receive complimentary access to the continental breakfast in the Towers lounge on the 26th floor. It is a very elaborate continental breakfast, with smoked salmon, nice cheeses and cured meats, along with fresh fruits, warm hard-boiled eggs, fresh pastries, bread, cereal, etc. The lounge was packed and service lacked, with empty plates piling on many tables.
The Waldorf Astoria is of course a Manhattan landmark and, as such, it was great to stay here. If I was spending my own money though, this is not where I would stay as it is very expensive.

title: First Rate Service
body: I have stayed at the Waldorf a couple of times now, very consistent with their service and a good location for your New York experience.

title: Absolutely Amazing
body: wr recently stayed for two weeks at the Waldorf. We were slightly nervous, having read some of the reviews posted herebut were so pleased with our decision to stay. The staff were all lovely, the lobby was amazing. We were so lucky to be upgraded to a gorgeous suite with a view of the Chrysler Building. The suite was very large and luxurious, however my Mum was staying in a regular room, which was also lovely. The location was just perfect for visiting, with the subway just outside the back door. People should remember this is a very old hotel, so the rooms were a bit draughty, but that's what heaters are for! Highly recommend.

title: Thermostats in all rooms have been disabled
body: I used to stay at the Waldorf on business and loved it. But I had not stayed there for many years and wanted to "treat" myself and my son this past weekend. We awoke the night we checked in extremely hot, and discovered we could not operate the thermostat. Try as we may to turn it down, we could not. We called the front desk after awaking several times and were told we could not set the temperature in the room, only turn it on and off. The temperature in all rooms is set by the hotel and we were only allowed to control the air flow. We turned it off but were still sweltering an hour later. We could not turn on the air to make it cooler. The front desk's solution was to offer to have a maintenance man come to open the window (this was five in the morning and i did not want visitors at that hour). The next day at our request they had housekeeping open a window so it would not get so hot in our East Facing room. But though it got warm in the day, the evening was quite cool. That night the only way we could regulate the temperature was to put a rolled up towel in the window crack so it would not get too cold, but to move the towel to allow in air when it got too hot. I think that a hotel of this caliber ought to afford guests the ability to control the temperature in the room with something other than a rolled up towel. We were told this was just something we had to live with an older hotel (having no control over the thermostat) but i have stayed in many older hotels which had thermostats in the room which the guests could control. In fact I have never seen this at ANY hotel and i am 55 years old. We got very poor sleep both nights. It was really unbelievable that a hotel that is this expensive and has a reputation for luxury has disabled the thermostats in the rooms. Very, very disappointed.

title: Simply top drawer, had a memorable stay
body:
First, the Diamond check in (Mary) was exceptional. Spent so much time with me, I almost felt guilty :)
It was the first hotel I can recall that actually had a Diamond desk check in. Plenty of help and service for a Hilton property in the USA. Honestly, I felt like I was back in Japan. It was an added plus that they upgraded me to the 41st floor (out of 42 floors) while using an Expedia reservation. That doesn't happen very often. Hotel was exceptional, definitely one to remember. The only downside was the valet parking was something like $50 per night...expensive for sure, but I had to wait over 30 minutes for my car, and I called in advance. Very inadequate valet parking. Hotel was great though, and again, thanks to Mary!

title: Old World Elegance Needs a Makeover
body:
Spent a long weekend in NYC and wanted to stay near but not in Time Square. Decided on the Waldorf Astoria.
We valet parked our car and was greeted by a bellhop who graciously welcomed us to the hotel. He assured us our luggage would be promptly sent to our room as soon as we checked in at the front registration area. Upon check in at 3:15pm, we were informed our room was not ready yet. The clerk printed out 2 complimentary drink coupons and informed us to have a cocktail on the hotel and the room would be ready in less than 30 minutes.
Upon returning to the registration area, we were taken to the Diamond Level Registration room. The clerk stated our room was still not ready and offered another set of drink coupons. I informed her that we were already given free drinks an hour ago and we were ready for our room. The clerk asked that we sit in the lobby and she would personally see that our room be made ready ASAP. After 40 minutes the clerk came out to the lobby and provided us with our room cards.
The room was a 1 bedroom suite with a wrap around balcony. Unfortunately, the doors leading to the balcony were locked and could not be opened. The curtains looked like they were over 50 years old with the little balls dangling from string. There were 4 sets of curtains and each one was missing many of the balls. The couch was so dated and used that when you sat on the end you immediately rolled toward the middle.
The rest of the furniture was decent but worn as well. No visible chips or scratches, just old looking.
The two flat screen TVs in the room worked well. Unfortunately, the hotel does nit subscribe to HD stations, so many of the stations were fuzzy.
The first night I called to the front desk and asked for wake up call and to have someone come to our room the next morning to set the time on the special clock radio. Unfortunately, neither request was performed. Luckily we set our cell alarms as a back up.
On a positive note, there is a Starbuck's location in the hotel, as well as another 20 within walking distance. In addition, the valet parking includes daily in-out privileges unlike most of the hotels in Manhattan. You simply call at least 30 minutes before you need the car, and it's waiting for you when you arrive.
In conclusion, the Waldorf Astoria is a nice place to stay. However, until it receives a much-need makeover, expect old-world charm of the 30s - 40s and your grandma's furniture.

title: What can you say - it is the Waldorf Astoria
body:
This is really a landmark hotel - It is probably worth staying here just to enjoy the sense of history and tradition that the hotel really captures. It is also a very amazing building, and the hotel is so opulent and striking.
We stayed here in January, for a weekend, to end our three week stay in NYC, after staying at Hilton Times, Square (fantastic hotel!), and Millenium Hilton New York.
My mum had a queen executive suite, and I had a Deluxe King room. The rooms were very spacious, and nicely furnished. The bed was probably the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in actually, and even though I'm a Hilton Diamond Member, I don't normally concern myself with how the bed is, but I really noticed the bed in my room at the Waldorf.
It is true, that the Lobby areas are immaculate, and that the bedrooms look a little worn or faded, as other reviewers have mentioned. In my mind, this was mainly due to the carpet, which really looked very old, and a bit dirty. The furniture and room itself, and bathrooms in both our rooms were very lovely. That said, the rooms were very quiet and really very comfortable. My room was very spacious, though my mother's suite was a little on the small side.
But visiting New York, and staying here, is a real experience. There is definitely something quite amazing about exploring New York while staying at the Waldorf Astoria, I would definitely recommend it for this alone! 
The service was sometimes truly exceptional, and at other times, not so great. Some staff seemed a bit too pre-occupied with how great they were, to really actually serve you attentively, which is a shame. 
One thing that was a little disappointing that the room service was not available except for the Towers. Also Oscar's was closed, except for breakfast. This was for the winter quiet season. With the old carpet, it kind of added to an impression of stinginess that you don't expect from the Brand hype. 24 hour room service is standard now in hotels all around the world of a much less calibre, so this was really weird to see the note explaining no in room dining except in the towers?? Being Diamond guests, we received not upgrade of any kind, and were given the rooms we booked, (one was a suite), and were told the hotel was full at check-in when queried about whether we received any upgrades for our stay. Also, when I booked a queen executive one bedroom suite, I asked the hilton reservationist if it included an executive lounge access, and she said yes-- though there was no executive lounge for this room type when we checked in. 
That said-- I would definitely recommend the Waldorf Astoria, and it is a real experience and treat to stay there. We dined in the Bull & Bear, which was lovely, and bought the discounted Diamond breakfast coupons, to have the buffet breakfast in Oscars, which was also lovely (the omlette chef is a great feature). The cocktails in Peacock Alley and the other bars were also great.
So wonderful stay overall, and I actually found the rooms very pleasing and comfortable. It is a shame that a few small things created a certain sense of stinginess that other reviewers have mentioned, and that contrasts so strongly with the spectacular public areas. 
I would definitely stay here again on a return trip to NYC, just to enjoy the history and ambience of the Waldorf Astoria. It is quite a fascinating hotel.

title: In need of a facelift but was very clean
body: I think The Waldorf Astoria continues to be a popular place to stay solely for its name. The hotel seems to be stuck in the era it was built- 1930's. It was very clean--it just felt tired (or as if you're staying at your grandparents home.) The rooms were large - in NY standards - but a very small bathroom. The sheets, pillows and bedding were all extremely comfortable. It wouldn't be my first choice to stay again as I enjoy more contemporary accommodations however it was clean, the rate was good (with my AAA card) and I had a good night sleep--so that counts for something.

title: Probably not worth the money
body:
We stayed there on a Hilton Honors award certificate, so I probably shouldn't complain, but this hotel is a bit over rated....Beautiful facility, no doubt, but it's the people that really make a difference, and by and large, the employees at the Waldorf are lacking in basic customer service skills. 
First, we get to the hotel with our bags and the doormen don't lift a finger to assist --- there is a flight of stairs from the entrance up the lobby area that we had to carry our bags up --- not a big deal for us, as we're in good shape, but I have to wonder about folks that couldn't handle it...maybe someone would have offered to assist, but honestly, I didn't see anyone getting help. 
We check in and they give us a room upgrade because we are Hilton Diamond members --- great! But the upgraded room was just so so, nothing special and even though we requested a King size bed, we got a queen. Realize that NYC hotel rooms are small, but this one was REALLY small. Internet connectivity was spotty at best --- had to have someone physically come to the room to hook us up (after telephonic tech support was unable to help). The room was extremely warm and even with the air on high, we were unable to cool it down. Asked for turn down service both nights --- never got it. Room service tried to deliver a meal to us that we didn't order; got a wake up call one day that we hadn't asked for; had a few questions for the concierge --- they behaved as if they didn't want to be bothered -- I kind of thought that was their job! 
Did the hostoric hotel tour the next morning -- tour guides were very nice and informative, but the included lunch at Oscar's restaurant (in the hotel) was pretty bad. Service was poor; food was not good quality, but quite expensive. Wouldn't eat there again. 
Overall, not the "wow" experience you would expect at the Waldorf Astoria. Given the choice between the Waldorf and another higher end/luxury propery, we'd probably go elsewhere. 
Again, beautiful hotel with a rich history, but I think it's seen better days.

title: Its the Waldorf
body: Location is perfect, and it keeps the essence of the history hotel that it is. The bathrooms could use remodelation wihout loosing this essence. Howevere everyhting was fantastic. one bad thing its that you can hear elevetaros passing by from the bethroom.

title: Five star service
body: When you enter the lobby of the Waldorf Astoria, you know that this place is special. The Waldorf IS New York. They don't build them like this today. It is worth a stroll through the lobby even if you aren't staying here just to see the beauty and grandeur. The rooms are large, beautiful and exude charm. The bathrooms are usually very large as well and often have a separate dressing room. The location at 50th and Park can't be beat. But what makes the Waldorf so special is the staff and the service they provide. They exceed our expectations every time we visit. If you are looking for small, ultra modern rooms, then the Waldorf is not for you. However, if you appreciate architecture that cannot be replicated today, beauty and impeccable service, there is no better place in New York City than the Waldorf Astoria.

title: What a disappointment!
body:
Very disappointed in this stunning looking hotel. It looks so wonderful inside - but the staff were pretty unhelpful, very snooty, and they all looked very unhappy (which is always a great clue about well/badly a place is run).
Just a generally glum vibe and poor service throughout (I think this is the only hotel I stayed in on my tour of the Eastern USA who HASN'T sent me a customer satisfaction survey...says it all too doesn't it?

title: Waldorf - 1930's glamour
body:
A very stately hotel, the lobby area and bars are glamorous but unfortunately this does not relay through to the rooms, we stayed in a suite which was fabulous to have a lounge area but the furniture could definitely do with a bit of a glam up.
There is a great amount of history with this hotel and it was a tick off of my "to stay at list" so it would be a shame for guests to turn away for a small make-over!
Definitely recommend the location as it is close the metro station and cabs are readily available outside the hotel - if you dont have a limo :-)

title: 2nd time at the waldorf NYC
body:
i have to say the stay we the Waldorf Astoria both times has got better and better, room and service is fantastic. but what can i say its the Waldorf...
thanks guys for are lovely suite...

title: Iconic Hotel
body: This hotel is so iconic, and there have been some very unfair reviews on it. We booked online with the hotel direct and got a very good price for the room, comparable to staying in a much lower grade hotel in Midtown Manhattan. We requested a corner room based on other reviews and we were given this. The room was large and the bathroom was a good size for a NY hotel. The hotel is very clean and there is a lot of attention to detail. Fresh flowers all around the hotel including the landings. We used the restaurants and found the food to be really good, a little on the pricey side but what would you expect in a hotel of this quality - comparable to a London hotel of the same grade. All of the staff were extremely polite and friendly - they were not gushing and all over you which some might class as being "snooty", I think people respond to you how you respond to them and I was always courteous to the staff and I found them helpful, chatty and polite in return. The public areas are without doubt glamourous and decadent and do not disappoint. The apple martini's and steak in the Bull & Bear restaurant were fantastic as was the service. Please do not be put off by any negative reviews because you will be depriving yourself of a real treat. This is a wonderful, grand dame of a hotel. If they "update" it, they risk ruining it and making it like so many other characterless hotels. Loved this hotel and would definately stay here again. Only one small point - would have been good to have coffee machine in the room, but my old travel kettle and a jar of coffee did the job!

title: I got Bed Bug Bites!
body: Came here last weekend for a 50th birthday celebration. Three people in our room. Room was outdated and old but the bathroom was redone and was nice. The lobby was lovely. We went to the bar for a drink and appetizer before going out for dinner and when we arrived all the tables that were empty were sitting filthy with dirty glasses. No one offered to remove them for us. So we left and did not stay for a drink. Champagne was delivered to our room as a gift from a friend and the man that brought it would not open it for us. But really the worst part was when I got home a couple days later my back was itchy with a rash. I asked my husband to take pictures of it and we now realize it was bed bug bites from The Waldorf. I normally stay at the Benjamin or Affinia hotels but because it was a special birthday we thought it would be fun to stay somewhere "fancy" eek never again!

title: Beautiful Hotel
body:
Stayed at the Waldorf over Easter 2012 - we were lucky enough to be upgraded to a suite on the 24th Floor, The room was amazing, large reception HUGE living area, bedroom, walk in closet and marble bathroom... :) they also knew it was both mine and my hubbys birthdays when we were at the hotel and as we walked into the room had left us a HUGE piece of birthday cake and 2 bottles of water as a gift - lovely touch and much appreciated....The staff are very helpful and full of info about NYC This was our second visit to New york so we knew the area etc, dont think as a location that the waldorf is in the best place, its quite a walk to times square, central park etc but just to say you have stayed in this iconic hotel takes that problem away... Make sure you have a look round the little gift shops, they have lovely jewellry etc and very reasonable prices... However i wouldnt recommend eating or drinking in the hotel, Sunday brunch was $90 per person (£60) lovely little deli just round the corner did bagels for $1.79!!!!!!!! Also the bar prices - dont think there was a glass of wine under £30 and jack daniels was $105 STILL unsure as to what you get for $105 dollars surely it cant be a shot!!!!!! We bought a bottle of duty free vodka and once there got a couple of bottles of coke and made our own drinks in the room!! 
We did the ususal attractions whilst there, Empire state, rockefella centre, would definitley recommend getting the New york pass if you want to do all these things as it saves you a fortune when you add it all up - i would add the bus tours as well the hop on hop off ideal for getting to all attractions - dont miss the skyride in the empire state building - really good! also would recommend the sunset cruise with circle line - we set off and the sun was setting just as passed lady liberty!! WOW - the photos are amazing, then the manhattan skyline in the dark, truly amazing!!!! And make sure you walk the brooklyn bridge again - an iconic thing to do and the views are tremendous... Grand slam in times square for all your NY souvenirs - the shops in times square all charge different prices grand slam are the cheapest and they have a very wide range of everything, got to be done - NY tat hasnt it!!! ha.... Ate at planet hollywood and found it a bit of a rip off, however the Hard rock still amazing, cheap and food delicious.. (the shop is amazing too) if you like pandora - much cheaper in NY - little shop just up from times square towards central park - martinique jewellers - ask for yogi shes lovely and will sort you out good prices....
To sum up - lovely hotel, wouldnt think twice about staying again (if we could get the same sort of deal that we got this year that is ) but wouldnt pay a stupid amount to stay there are better locations but to say you have stayed in the waldorf i suppose HAS to be done :):):)
hope this helps

title: Disappointing
body:
This hotel is full of history and the common areas are well maintained. However, our superior room was in poor condition- the curtain rod was rusted, paint was chipping from the back of the bathroom door, the shower backs up so we were ankle deep in water by the end of our showers.
 The bartender at the peacock lounge was quite nice, as well as the cocktails and cheese selection. As for the rest of the service- poor. We did not receive our complimentary bottled water once without having to ask for it; and when we did, it took room service 30 minutes to bring up 2 bottles of water. We did not receive turndown service once in the 3 nights we stayed. The staff was unwelcoming. Every time we exited through Lexington Avenue, there double decker tour bus hastling guests. 
We expected a great deal more from the Waldorf=Astoria. We spent our final 2 nights at the Hyatt 48LEX across the street and had a wonderful experience.

title: Weekend at the Astoria
body: Great long weekend at the Waldorf Astoria. Location was ideal for walking to many attractions. Concierge was very helpful with restaurant recommendations. Internet access in rooms was available for the "token" (the hotel's description) price of $14.95 a day! Take the hotel tour. Very interesting. There is no pool (if that's important). Good fitness equipment (included). Have a drink in the lobby bar. Old hotel with character.

title: Waldorf Astoria New York 301 Park Ave
body: Very disppointing understanding its an old hotel but for the price the rooms should be updated, the cable did not work, the carpet smelled like urine, toliet stopped up, room electric went out. I would not recommend this hotel until its updated. Ask for wake up calls never happened and share my concerns with the hotel manager.

title: A birthday treat.
body: Earlier this year I was treated to a visit to the Waldorf Astoria. Right in the middle of mid town between Park avenue and Lexington, the New York subway is just to the side of the hotel. The hotel itself is set back in time, when all things were done for you at a cost (That was the way to live) We stayed for 4 day's, it was worth it. Just to go and see the clock in the front lobby. There are lots of places to eat on Lexington within easy reach of the hotel. Seeing the sights is easy, grand central station / radio city / the top of the rock / time square, are within walking distance. The empire state / 9-11. don't forget the shopping when you are in that area, century 21. Take a good camera, you will need it. All in all it is one place that I hope not to forget for a long time.

title: NYC Girls Getaway
body:
The Waldorf Astoria is a legendary hotel in a wonderful location, close to everything necessary Times Square, Grand Central, 5th Ave and Central Park. The hotel has definatley lost some of it's luster as the carpets in the lobby, hallways and rooms are old and need attention. Rooms are typical NYC size but there was enough room for three women to share and be comfortable. I must give kudos for the number of outlets available in the room to charge phones and tablets and for hair dryers and flat irons. Room was very stuffy and when we inquired at the front desk we were told that the rooms could not adjust the temperature so we had to open the window and they delivered a fan for our use. Staff at the hotel was hit or miss, 50% cordial and even helpful and the other 50% rude and dismissive. For example: when we checked in (we had three rooms) we asked for a room with a view and we were told that we booked our rooms with a third party and would get the rooms that we paid for, needless to say we were all on the 10th floor and the view was a concrete wall. i have stayed at many Hilton properties and this was the first time that I had to pay to access the internet and to print anything outside of boarding documents. 
A few suggestions on things to do while in NYC: Real New Yorker Big Apple Tour, a private tour that you can customize to fit what you want to experience. Thank You Max for taking us into the neighborhoods to expeirnece areas outside the usual tourist sites. I definatley recommend!!! Since we were such a large group (8 ladies) it was sometimes difficult to get around without having to hail 2-3 taxis at a time. Thankfully we met Howie of Howie Limo Service 917-532-7716 and he or one of his employees would pick us up in one of the many cars in Howies fleet. Howie and his employees were always very professional and went out of their way to make sure that we were taken care of even making suggestions. Excellent places to eat near the hotel: New York Lunchonette 135 E. 50th, Ashton's Alley 825 3rd Ave., Bar Americain 153 W. 52nd St., Buvette 42 Grove Street. Buttercup Bakery 2nd St.

title: Waldorf living on its reputation
body: When we walked into the Waldorf lobby we were immediately impressed by its grandeur, but when we got upstairs to our room (after a two hour wait for it to be serviced) disappointment set in. The location is great, the staff reasonably friendly and helpful, but our room was awful - small, worn furniture, bathtub finish peeling, and only one window which overlooked an airshaft. On the plus side the location is great, convenient to midtown and right at a subway station. Like many New York hotel the food costs were excessive - Sunday brunch was $95 plus tax, tip etc

title: Great Anniversary Trip
body: This place is absolutely beautiful inside and out. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The location is convenient to Times Square, Theater District, Central Park, 5th Avenue, Grand Central, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Radio City, Rockefeller Center and hundreds of places to eat and shop. Go out to eat unless you have money to burn.

title: A piece of NYC history but not worth the price.
body: The rooms are large by NYC standards but the decor is dated, even dingy. The lobby is the highlight. My breakfast of fruit, toast and tea came to over $60 with tip and taxes. The room was extremely warm and the air conditioning didn't work, although the service staff very kindly came up and opened my window to cool it down. Needless to say, it was a restless night of sleep because of the noise and damp. I don't think it'll be back :-( there are too many other good options.

title: Great location but not impressed by some of the service
body:
We arrived for a four night stay as a group of four, two couples and were greeted warmly at reception, we were directed to our rooms and our luggage arrived in due course, no problems. The room was average size for a twin double and was clean and well decorated as was the bathroom. We all met up in the bar later and were amazed at the prices, $107 for 2 glasses of wine, a tonic water and a single malt whisky, but hey we thought, it's New York.
As we ate out every night I can't comment on the restaurant quality however by the numbers attending they seemed popular enough.
My only complaint was the service. At the bar of the main restaurant and were told to "try the other bar" and given a flick of the hand in a random direction when we returned (10.30pm) from an evening out and asked for a drink. At the travel desk, we were treated like a nuisance and fobbed off with blunt and unhelpful answers to questions, a touch of snobbery I felt.
The consierge service was very helpful on the other hand as were the hotels porters who were excellent.
Overall I would say it might be worth a short visit just to add the hotel to your list but I will definately not be returning.
Beautiful hotel inside, great location in the city, plenty bars and restaurants nearby and a few blocks from Times Square but it is overly expensive, even for New York, and a couple of the staff could use some help with their attitude to paying guests.

title: Beautiful but overpriced.
body:
The hotel is beautiful and has lots of history. Everything is tremendously overpriced. We were a group of 10 women on a girls trip. The rooms are small and the beds even smaller. We had no control of the temperature of the room and we all burned up the first night. Called many times and was told they are on a 2 pipe system where they have either all heat or all air conditioning for the entire hotel and that the whole system was turned off. We were given a fan and told to open the windows. Really? For $300 a night per room. The next day they turned on the air and the following 3 nights were fine. Not a hotel I would usually have considered, but I was part of a group. 
Then we were treated rudely buy the waitress in the lobby bar. I know this was New York but you would think the staff in a hotel like the Waldorf Astoria would know better. 
The location is great. Close to St Patricks, 5th Ave, Broadway, Times Square and Central Park. Walking distance if you are into walking. Also has a stop on the hop on hop off route. That was convenient.

title: Celebratory Stay May 2012
body:
We chose the Waldorf for our special occasion - my partner's 40th birthday and our wedding in Central Park. I'm not sure we would have opted for such an illustrious hotel for a "normal" trip.
The public areas of the hotel are beautifully decorative - there was definitely the "wow" factor for us as we entered the lobby for the first time. On arrival we were greeted politely and treated to a small gift of two free cocktails to help with our celebrations. There is free Wi-Fi in the hotel lobby, we did also pay for Wi-Fi in our room one day as we were having to spend some time there. You should note that if you are using more than one device to connect you will be billed twice, but you can get this refunded when you check out.
Our standard room was perfectly adequate for our needs (2 adults and one 3-year old) - would have liked slightly more clothes storage space but otherwise the room was great. No view of the city although we were on the 16th floor, on retrospect I perhaps should have asked for a view - will know better for future hotel bookings!
We utilised valet services in the hotel to have our wedding garments pressed, all done excellently, obviously at a price.
The rooms were cleaned daily and were spotless, the house-keeping service is excellent. I found all of the corridors and public areas were clean all the time we were there.
We did have a couple of drinks in Peacock Alley. We were pleased that we were welcomed into the bar even with our daughter in her stroller. Whilst we didn't feel like your typical Waldorf guests, we were treated with respect and care by the staff there.
One down side to mention was the accessibility issues with the stroller - we had to access the hotel via the motorcade entrances to get an elevator one floor up then a different elevator to our floor. But we managed!
Check out process was so easy - a couple of calls to collect our bags and to check out and we were good to go!
Overall a very pleasant stay - I doubt we would stay there again as this was a really special occasion.

title: could do with a facelift
