body: Recently stayed for 3 nights at the Waldorf - first impressions were good as the ground floor and the reception lobby were very impressive, dark wood panels and a large brass and marble clock dominated, however when we got to our floor it was very non-descript and the room itself was a bit tired looking (particularly the bathroom) and could do with a bit of redecorating. We didn't eat in any of the restaurants so I can't give a review of them. The location of the hotel is quite central with Grand Central Station, the East River and Times Square all 3 or 4 blocks away.

title: Honeymoon..
body:
I treated my wife to a 4 night stay at this amazing hotel as it was a once in a life time opportunity. I booked room only and was glad of that as on arriving at the hotel I enquired about adding breakfast, which would be an extra $40 per person per day. So decided against that at we had breakfast out everyday, much cheaper.
We had a king superior room on the 12th floor which had an amazing view of the Chrysler building. In all the hotel was everything we expected it to be, just a shame that we will probably never be able to stay there again.

title: Avoid the Sunday Brunch
body:
Stayed 3 nights. The Bull and Bear restaurant was excellent. However the Sunday Brunch on Mothers Day was grossly overpriced. $125 per person. The service was extremely poor. Had to ask repeatedly for refills of coffee and water. The final insult was the 18% tip for the service which was automatically added to the tab.
Room was pleasant, reasonable size, very comfortable bed.

title: Waldorf Can't Live Up to Its Reputation. Very Disappointing.
body:
When making reservations at the Waldorf, I had expectations of historic accommodations and fantastic service. The reality was a fail on both levels. Rooms are clean but shabby. The biggest disappointment came from the level of service. Apathy abounds on all levels. It took us 45 minutes to get checked in, and when rooms were finally located for us (despite having been reserved months ago), we were told we could not yet go into them until housekeeping visited. This was at 8:00 at night. The bell hops couldn't answer any questions about directions around the hotel, stating, "We're only here to handle bags." The host at the lobby bar took several minutes to acknowledge our presence, as he was busy texting on his iPhone.
Clearly the Waldorf is experiencing a crisis of Branding. It's a shame, as this was once a grand place to visit. We could have stayed in a far more accommodating hotel for significantly less money. Next time we will.

title: Charming, historical
body:
I stayed for five nights in May with a sister and we were generally pleased. The public areas are stunning and the numerous photo displays of historic figures who have stayed at the hotel are fascinating. I was prepared to be disappointed with the sleeping floors, but was quite pleased. The hallways were in great condition and very elegant. 
Our room looked into the courtyard, with minimal view, but that was okay, as we weren't there much anyway. The room itself was clean and well-kept, albeit aging. We appreciated the in-room safe, iron/ironing board, and flatscreen TV with lots of channels. I was disappointed that we did not have a coffee maker, but I had packed a small water heating pot, Via instant, and my own mugs, so we made do. 
The room service charges are ludicrous, but there is a Starbucks open limited hours on the Park Avenue side entrance and the hotel is smack in the middle of the city, with endless options for food in all price ranges in the surrounding blocks. 
A subway stop is right on the corner of Lexington and 50th St, where we bought a $29 pass good for unlimited rides on the city's great bus system.
The staff was wonderfully polite, friendly, and professional.

title: NYC's Great Wonders
body: Just an amazing place, a time capsule of the past in so many ways. From the Hallways and the rooms with a grandness....All of the Pubs and the Check-in absolutely stop you in your tracks and make you think of the past, the artwork, carvings, elevators and decor. And then who was here , there are pictures from the past on display. And yet I wonder all the people busying around, texting and ipads.....However, all that put to the side.....are the sounds of very pleasant, sincerely happy and helpful folks who make this tiny city within a city run. Here is just a little taste; as I come and go in the hallways there is a proactive good day sir, how are you, can I help with anything? Then while I sit at Oscar's bar, the bartender asks and then asks whats your pleasure.....usual, then after my question, he begins to tell about some unusual things such as the House home made bitters , 3 to be exact (a surprise for you to find out) to use in some drinks,Manhattans. And again while he was busy , seeing me twist a city map...googling advice and directions with other staff to solve my questions. Or how about a need for One Rose for a dear one, I intruded on the Florist staff downstairs busy with a reception shortly, the folks in charge made the time to bend and fold an artwork of a creation and a single rose,like the Waldorf itself.....and when I asked how much? he commented " is this is going make someone happy" yes I said.....bring it to them quickly was his reply. And Grandest of all is for me One of the Many helpers, or Godmothers who truley iron out the wrinkles. Jackie. Yes I did have an issue , a headache that was my fault and could not solve it...How they are swarmed with little to big issues and in a timely fashion form, fix, solve and take care of you specifically and yet multi taste many others in a sweeping fashion...I am truely amazed...First I did not actually see her feet touch the ground, I think I saw a wand and like a school boy who skinned his knee, it was better, forgot what happened, told me she loved me....well I felt that way; and off I went. I have been here many times over the past many years, but What I just realized is that As much as the Waldorf has a grand maturity to itself, its sparkle and elegance is truely the folks that bring it to life and make it run every day.....because THEY CARE. Thanks see you soon!

title: Honest Review from a experienced traveler...
body:
Ok, I should state this first:we can stay at the 5 stars such as four seasons and I also love staying in some hometown inns that are budget types..but the one thing I cant stand is a place that charges 5 star rates and is a run down hotel. I have a hilton honors card and am upgraded at all hotels, the upgraded room (which the front desk said is one of the best) was a complete dump. Imagine staying in Aunt Marges attic or basement---that smell was pungent in our hotel hallways, rooms, and areas...long hallways, outdated, dilaplated, and overall a complete waste. I dont care if its a Waldorf Astoria-this place has horrible service, slow, too small for the hotel crowd, outdated elevators...and worst of all its overpriced. I think the last time this place had a renovation was when it opened, the bathrooms were ugly, ill decorated, the bathtub hasnt changed since it opened...i could go on and on and on...and i truly dont write bad reviews unless they are nessesary... AVOID THIS HOTEL UNLESS YOU ARE 70 YEARS AND OLDER AND LIKE A RETIREMENT HOME ENVRIONMENT WITH A MILDEW SMELL.
anyone who thinks this hotel is a good hotel in a review hasnt been out much..i can say that

title: Don't bother!
body:
Don't bother staying at this establishment as the service, level of cleanliness and quality of rooms are probably better at a Holiday Inn. Our room smelled of pet urine, there is absolutely no venilation in the bathrooms, the shower was falling apart, the linen was tattered (including the spa robe), etc. Expect beauty and grandiosity at the lobby-level, but not beyond. 
Do your self a favor and continue your search. I will never stay at the Waldorf again.

title: Pure decadence
body: Lovely hotel,well placed looked after from the minute we arrived,we were under no illusion that the place would not be expensive to drink/eat in and how right we were but as I was told "this is the Waldorf sir" if you want a reasonably priced drink nip out onto 48th towards 5th and you will find a couple of Irish bars where you will be well looked after also.The Waldorf was amazing I loved sitting in the lobby people watching with my Starbucks coffee in the morning.got to give a mention for Torro on the door this fella looked after us and was not a "stuck up" as some of the others were thanks "Torro " you should be on the NYC tourist board what a help this fella was.the reception staff very very pleasant

title: Please don't make the same mistake that we did!
body: Unfortunately we strayed from our normal hotel to stay in the iconic NYC Waldorf Astoria. Do NOT make the same mistake! Our "luxury" one bedroom suite was a total disappointment. The bathroom had a single sink with barely enough room for one person. Forget the idea of a luxurious bathroom, it did not exist. Our suite was supposed to include a kitchenette or wet bar. Apparently an ice bucket will suffice for this criteria at The Waldorf Astoria. With so many great hotels in NYC, please don't waste your time or money on the Waldorf. Come in and have a drink in the bar, say you've had the experience,and move on! And yes, we made our concerns known to the front desk staff and via email to management ....while they are quite professional in delivery, the message is the same..."too bad".

title: Historic venue
body: The location is perfect for walking around some of the major New York attractions. Check in was tediously long, and the room was average. The decor was tired and the bathroom was old, and peeling - even at the bottom of the bath. However, the public rooms were spectacular, and some of the shops within the building are interesting. Staff were helpful if a little overstretched. There is a buzzing atmosphere and there is always something to watch - eg wedding, people. The beds were really comfortable and sleep came easily, whether due to the walking or comfort. One of those places which must be done.

title: Historical, old New York City, Fabulous lobby.
body:
The Waldorf Astoria is such a beautiful old hotel with so much history and romance, that I keep coming back, despite the fact the rooms are not always perfect. Yes, you might see a little bit of peeling paint on the heavy bathroom door and I noticed an uneven rug section up against the threshold of the door. The desk chair we had in our room was a little dated and I really wanted a few more outlets. Despite all of that, I still love the Waldorf-Astoria for the feel, ambiance and service.
The fitness room is very nice, plenty of towels, bottled water and helpful staff. In the past, I was told there was a fee to use the fitness center, but if such a comment is made, be sure to ask to join the Hilton Honors and the fees will be waived at all times. Regarding fees, one complaint: the hotel charges for use of internet in rooms (free wi-fi in lobby and public rooms). Hilton Honor cards of the higher categories can have the fee waived. Check with hotel for details.
The Waldorf Astoria lobby is worth time spent just sitting in the comfortable chairs and watching the busy day. The hotel staff is extremely attentive and will promptly assist you in any way. Ask for a refrigerator to keep basics and snacks handy. Hotel meals a bit expensive, but it's New York and the Waldorf has such a great location, finding places to eat nearby is very easy.

title: STAY ELSEWHERE- 5 Star Lobby, ZERO star Room
body:
Me and my husband are having our 30 days holiday in u.s and stayed at top end hotel in every stop. We have just came from Ritz Carlton at San Fransisco(highly recommended), like waldorf we also requested concierge level of service, and Ritz didnt not dissapoint. The same could not be said with Waldorf. We cancelled our booking at The Trump Tower and decided on THE WALDORF ASTORIA instead. Upon arrival we were greeted with script type service of "Welcome Sir" standard and nothing special, we then got shown thru the 5 STAR GRAND LOOKING LOBBY to a LITTLE DOOR which leads us to our room elevator. From there on its ZERO star. The room at "THE Waldorf Astoria" is no where near elegant or character like it described. our CONCIERGE LEVEL room was detailed with peeling wallpaper, blotchy paint at the ceiling, and aged old bathroom which I was stunned to find there is a rolled up Anti-slip mat at the tub which i thought was a left behind water pipe from the maintainence. I totally agreed with this reviewer's view except our room smell like smoker's lounge...

title: Couldn't have been better!
body: We spent four nights in the Waldof Astoria. Everything was perfect, from the large, newly-renovated room facing Park Avenue to the always-helpful staff. Everything was clean, elegant and beautiful. The location is ideal, only two blocks from Fifth Avenue and Rockefeller Center and one block to the Lexington Avenue subway which can take you anywhere in the city. This historic hotel is a must for your special visit to New York City.

title: Personalized Service
body: We stayed at The Waldorf Astoria over a long weekend for our daughter's birthday. The lobby is opulent and evokes a feeling of wealth and grandiose. Our daughter received a personalized declaring her 'in residence' and was also presented with a teddy bear. Both seemingly small gestures went a long way in winning her as a very satisfied customer even before crossing the threshold into the room. The rooms are very large and do reflect features of an historic property. The ceilings are high and room square footage is very generous. The bathrooms are not large, but are adequate. Many updates have been recently completed. We enjoyed our stay and would stay at the property again.

title: Another Excellent Stay
body: My son and I explored New York in April using the Waldorf Astoria as our home base. It is in a great location for exploring midtown by foot and other parts of the city through the extensive subway system. The hotel is itself a landmark and worthy of a tour. Nearby sites include The Rockefeller Centre, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Radio City Music Hall, MOMA, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and much more. The hotel itself has a great deal of charm and character. It is not a spot to stay if you want everything modern and unmarked. This place has seen some wear and tear that simply adds to its character and appeal. The staff are fairly helpful but I was a bit disappointed with the amenities allowed to Diamond members. But we came to New York to explore and we did that. I recommend any of the bars in the hotel for a night cap. On virtually any side street nearby you can also find an Irish pub with plenty of good fun.

title: A great weekend in NY - nice break on a business trip
body: We came to relax and sightsee in NY and we did. As others say - great hotel history. Do take the time too look around the hotel. We had reserved a non-smoking room but when we arrived - after arriving at about 1am from a 5 hr flight- we discovered the room seemed to be a smoking room. It may have been intended as an upgrade. Odd. Ash trays were present. Curtains and bedding smelled of smoke. In the morning we asked for a change, so we had to pack up - and they moved our luggage over to the other tower location (downgrade?). Next room didn't have a view and the bed was not very comfortable. Nor did we have convenient access to the little exec lounge for breakfast. At least the second room didn't reek of smoke. The room itself was comfortable with adequate amenities. Best is the location - convenient to look around. Yes, we thought the brunch was over priced as another reviewer mentioned - so we simply avoided it and went out of the hotel. Bull and Bear was fun...but pricey - great food and service. Overall ok - just wished they had not mixed up the reservation when we arrived at the hotel - my wife really didn't feel well with the smell of the smoking on everything. Bar was fine and drink service at the bar was good. We did enjoy a few of the sights of NY.

title: Nice lobby, ok rooms
body:
The entrance and the lobby are amazing. Very elegant, very classy.
The rooms are veeery spacious! very comfortable, but very old. Not talking about old nice, but old without maintenance. They need to change doors, apply paint and fix many stuff. For the amount of money, the rooms should be much better.
The location is the best you can find!

title: Great service, small trip up, great recovery
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf for a four day weekend and were given an upgrade from a one bedroom suite to a one bedroom separate suite when we arrived and the bedroom was good, the sitting room spacious and the service all you would expect. 
The toilet was blocked when we arrived, and they sent someone up to unblock, but it blocked three more times over then next day and they moved us into an even nicer room. Thank you Vanessa for great service!!
One caution. You might want to get on a higher floor on a Saturday night, as the ballroom was right below the 5th floor suite and the music came through the floor, loug, good, but distorted... We did not really need the in room entertainment and was the second factor in our room move.
The brunch in Oscar's is excellent, the service first rate, the staff accomodating and gracious. This is my fourth, but not last say here.

title: Disappointing
body:
I stayed here about 20 years ago and decided it would be a nice treat for my 80 year old mother. I was so disappointed it was positively embarrassing. We stayed on the seventh floor. The corridor smelt musty, reminiscent of a cat litter, as were the rooms. The carpets, paint work and fittings were tired and the air-con was decrepit. My mother’s room was so cold when we arrived they brought a portable heater in. The bar downstairs was overpriced and staffed by inattentive waiters more interested in chatting up a woman at the bar than offering us drinks. I had to ask them to serve us after we’d been waiting 15 minutes. I did complain when we checked out and they reimbursed my internet charge - $17. Wow. I will be writing to them.
There is no doubt that the hotel is an architectural icon which makes the mediocrity of the rooms and service so much sadder. My recommendation would be to swing by, marvel at the art deco interior and stay somewhere else.

title: "Great Location"
body: The location is excellent, the foyers are beautiful, however the rooms are tired looking. We had two rooms first room was on the 6th floor - deluxe queen room (had to be relocated due to water bulge in bathroom ceiling from bathroom above) second room was on the 13th floor which was nicer than the previous room however possibly the time has come to invest some money in the rooms so they look as nice as the foyers do. Price paid for room did not equal value for money.

title: Great in places
body:
Writing a fully objective review when you stay somewhere on Hilton points is always less easy. Especially when you get upgraded. So, up front, we paid nothing for our room, and in fact were given a suite with separate living area, on a high floor, with a grandstand view of the Chrysler building. Sweet (as well as suite).
(Generally Hilton treat their "frequent fliers" well in the US. In the UK they couldn't care less about you much of the time).
Always interested in the cost and indeed the value of things, the room would have cost us about 800 bucks a night if we'd been paying. So I'll base the review on that.
It's an historic building, trying to be a 21st Century Hotel. No-one should be surprised if it's fraying a bit, and I suspect the cost of putting everything right would make even the Hiltons of this world baulk. So some of the rooms will have their problems.
Overall staying here is an experience not just a stay. We liked it.
The niggles (and some of these are related to the property and are therefore observations not complaints, but the whole point of this website is to let people know what to expect when they stay places)
- noise. Not from the street (on the 19th floor even on a holiday weekend Friday night) but from within the hotel. Noise travels - from the corridor, the upstairs bathroom, the upstairs bedroom (my wife and I applauded that bravura performance. I took notes).
- other noises. Almost certainly the scrabbling of tiny mouse feet in the walls. It's an old property. They will have mice.
- the plumbing is a bit quirky and the bathroom small, even in a suite.
- if I'm staying in a suite with a living room big enough to live in, why so mean with toiletries? (1 shower gel, no shampoo).
- a coffee maker would have been good. Yes I know higher end hotels often say they want guests to get *good* coffee, and hence the need for room service. But it's 19 floors down to Starbucks in the lobby, and when I want coffee I want it NOW not in 30-45 minutes from room service.
Now the better bits
- excellent check in experience - courteous and helpful and quick
- the living room in our suite was huge and very comfy, a proper space to relax in
- cocktails - pricey but great
- the Bull and Bear bar we loved. The bar food was excellent (nearly 30 bucks for a burger is of course expensive, but what a burger) and the service friendly and attentive (thank you Gail) 
- we also tried Sir Harry's, with equally great drinks, but the service there seemed stand-offish, and they didn't seem to mind people being VERY drunk. Drunk to the point of making us feel uncomfortable and taking our drinks with us to our room.
- a really very good gym.
- being able to charge Starbucks (in the hotel lobby) to your room when you don't want to pay the price of dinner for breakfast is a useful touch
Overall - it's a grand old dame of a hotel which, as these hotels always are, is fraying at the edges and impossible to maintain to the standards of a new build. But it is lovely in many places, and whilst it's expensive food and drink wise, that's largely justified.
I'd stay here again on points. We used the Waldorf as a treat at the end of a NY-Boston-NY trip, I'd have been disappointed at the value if we'd paid. Overall, you need to know what you're getting when you stay here, which in my view is an experience, with a bit of a "Lottery" in terms of what you get room wise. 
Pays your money, takes your choice.

title: The grandeur has faded
body: The Waldorf was ideally situated in NYC for our needs. There was a subway stop a block away that took us to any place we wanted to go. While we were there (middle of April 2012), the exterior was being renovated, but it didn’t impact our stay. When entering the Waldorf, the reception area was beautiful. I tried to imagine what it must have been like ‘back in the day’. However when we reached our Jr suite, the beauty ended. Our room looked very ‘tired’. There was nothing impressive about the furnishings. The sink was leaking and the toilet didn’t flush properly. There was also paint peeling in the bathroom. The room was also very warm despite having the AC turned down as low as it would go. We had to leave our window open during the day so it would be cool enough to sleep at night when we returned. As a diamond member in Hilton’s loyalty program, we only received certificates for pasties and a beverage at the Starbucks located in the hotel. We were not allowed to use the club lounge which so many other of Hilton’s fine hotels allow diamond guests. I would recommend staying here if you’re able to get a decent price though – just don’t expect anything out of the ordinary here.

title: Very pleased we stayed
body:
My husband and I stayed for 3 nights (Tuesday to Friday) and really enjoyed it. We arrived a couple of hours earlier than the start of check-in but were able to leave our luggage and my husband was sent a text message when our room was ready, which was only about 40 minutes later. We were also upgraded to a bedroom with a larger bed, which was a kind gesture. The bedroom on the 17th floor was lovely and very clean.
During our stay we spoke with a gentleman at the hotel who helps guests purchase theatre tickets. The price his the broker gave was more than we were willing to pay so he looked up the price being offered on the show's website, which was much less.
We would love to return to the Waldorf providing the price was right.

title: Great service, location and room
body:
I booked this hotel before Christmas for a 5 night stay at the end of May as it was the only hotel that was a reasonable price for New York (surprisingly!) with a good location.
I had heard of the hotel so because of the rate that we had the room for I expected that despite the opulence of the foyer and suites we would have some old very small room. I couldn't have been more wrong. The room was very large, the bed extremely comfortable and the bathroom was up to date and on the whole very clean.
There was no view out of the window, but the room was very quiet.
I did not use any of the restaurants or bars as they were all very overpriced. I used the gift shop (also over priced, but that is to be expected) to buy a postcard. When I enquired about how to get a stamp they sent me to the business centre who sent it free of charge.
I found that the staff in this hotel were not too "in your face" polite but were extremely helpful and courteous.
The lobby areas are stunning. Even if you're not staying it is worth just walking through! 
I would only stay in this hotel again if it offered the same value for money iagain for its location, as I expect that I somehow got a good deal, or other hotels were close to fully booked and their prices were higher. 
Positives: Relaxed and polite staff, larger than expected clean and modern room, the lobby
Negatives: Expensive (but it's the price for a fairly central hotel in New York I guess)

title: Loved it!
body:
We were upgraded to a suite with two rooms and two bathrooms. We checked in late on a flight from Dublin and the wonderful desk clerk after asking us about our trip, said, “Let me see what kind of room I can get you.” 
He got us a very beautiful upgraded suite!
We hosted several wine receptions here, which everyone enjoyed. The hotel is historic and lovely. The rooms are comfortable, quiet, clean, and spacious. The two bathrooms and two large walk-in closets were appreciated and the bed was divinely comfortable. We love historic old, luxury hotels and this one did not disappoint. Also loved the quieter, but still central location. The staff, especially room service, the front desk, and the theatre concierge, were all first rate. Highly recommend the Waldorf Astoria.

title: What can i say...
body:
What an amazing hotel. 
As soon as you walk into the Waldorf you feel the history and perfect experience that you would expect. I have dreamt of staying at this hotel for years and my husband booked it as part of my birthday celebration surprise.
The service is second to none, from the moment you check in, to the maids, butlers and room service staff.
We stayed in room 2727 and as this is on the 27th floor I have to say that I have never experienced such a speedy lift as this. The room has a door bell, large seating area and short hall way. The bed was huge and the view made me really appreciate how tall the buildings are in New York. The bathroom was smaller compared to the large size of the room, however, with the traditional art deco fittings I felt as if I had been transported back to the 1930’s which is exactly what I wanted. 
We had cocktails at Peacock Ally, this is a great place to people watch and truly appreciate the history of the hotel.
Room service was at the excellent standard that you would expect from an American hotel and seeing as though the Waldorf was the first hotel to ever offer room service, it had to be tried. My Husband had onion rings that were huge and the desserts were massive, the food arrived within 20 minutes and was of an excellent standard.
I cannot recommend this hotel enough. It lived up to everything that I have dreamt it would be and you really feel like you are staying in a part of history. I can’t wait to go back.
I could go on and on about how great this hotel is but if you are looking for luxury, class and history with a friendly service this hotel is for you.

title: An old hotel with a great location
body: It's not a bad hotel but it's not great either. It's just the location which makes it so atractive. The hotel it's too big so everything is far away. The service is good but slow. The decoration of the rooms reminded me my grandma's apartment. I couldn't believe when I was asked to pay usd 15 daily to have wifi. The rooms are already enough expensive to have to pay it as an extra. One day the shampoo and soap in the bathrom was not renewed and I realized about it in the middle of a shower. It took about 20 minutes until the service brought them to the room. Our room was spacious but the room of my kids had no view and the window was so small....

title: Quintessential historical hotel
body: Things we love: location of hotel, size of room (HUGE by NY standards), linens, showerhead + bathroom, workout facility...all were updated and well appointed. Cannot wait to return

title: Waldorf New York
body: Great service, Fabulous historic hotel, nice display in the lobby. Try the brunch at Oscar's, egg casserole was great!

title: Great hotel in a great location
body:
This was the first time I've stayed at this hotel and glad I did. The hotel is located within walking distance of different subway stops, Times Square, Grand Central Terminal, and Central Park. The interior of the hotel is beautiful and elegant. The exterior is being renovated, but construction is always going on in NYC. There are entrances on both Park Avenue and Lexington Avenue.
The room was huge, much bigger than I was expecting. I usually have trouble sleeping in hotels but I had no problem sleeping. It was quiet every night and the blinds keep most of the light out of the room. If you are a HHonors member, you get a free bottle of water per day of your stay.
Be advised that many of the people staying at this hotel are there for business so they will be dressed in professional dress. Some of the restaurants/bars have a dress code. But there are many tourist walking around in shorts and t-shirts.

title: One of our best hotel stays!!!
body:
My mom and I visited New York for two nights this weekend.... We travel often, and have stayed at Waldorf Astoria properties all around the world....And we both admit.....While we have enjoyed ALL of our stays.....This was by far the best and most elegant! Previous reviews talked about the rudeness of the staff....."We" found the staff to be most helpful.....most hospitable...quite professional......and offered customer service "Waldorf Style"!!!! The hotel is quite convenient to many stores and restaurants......
Cabs were plentiful!
Needless to say......while the price was a bit much......it was worth every penny!! We look forward to staying again and again!!!!

title: Corner room with view of Park Avenue
body: I think your experience will depend on the room. I've stayed at this property three times and each time had a corner room which gives you more privacy and space. This is still a grand dame of a hotel in mid-city, art deco w/ a beautiful lobby. You can feel the history. However, if you tend to prefer quiet and relaxing you might opt for a smaller boutique hotel uptown. The Waldorf is owned by Hilton and is a bustling hotel but a great location for business and Broadway.

title: Rooms very comfortable but the wait at reception is interminable
body:
We've stayed at the Waldorf many times over the years, so I was pleased to see that the refurbished rooms are a delight, the beds are comfortable, the rooms are a decent size and everything works - except possibly the bath but then this is America!
The one drawback of the whole place is that queue (line) at reception. Why does it take so long to book in? And to add insult to injury no matter what time we arrive our room is never ready, even at 8pm in the evening. Normally we've just got off a transatlantic flight so would love to have a shower and a lie down, but no it's a sit in the entrance hall (majestic though it is) for half an hour whilst housekeeping complete the room service.
So why do we keep going back? Well the location for one thing - very central, Oscar's for another - excellent breakfast, and yes the rooms, because once you are in them they are just what you need after a long flight - quiet and spacious.

title: THE place to stay
body: Our first family trip since 1997 - and the children are now all grown up. We wanted to make it memorable and staying at this amazing hotel was worth it. Our rooms were spacious, not particularly modern or even recently updated, but in excellent condition and reasonably roomy. I've stayed in better rooms around the world but to judge the Waldorf on that alone is to miss the point. The whole hotel is a fabulous experience with so much history. The staff were friendly and our thanks to the concierges who answered our endless questions and made our bookings speedily and efficiently. It is the most central location, everywhere was in easy reach, and that alone is worth it's weight in gold. I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else when I go again.

title: First time in NYC
body: We are Hilton diamond and were allowed early check in at 1 and upgraded to suite without asking. We had a comfortable living room, king bed and 2 bathrooms for the 2 of us. All very nice. Signs of age gave character and were no issue with us. Everyone was friendly and helpful from arrival to departure on a busy memorial day weekend.

title: EXTREMELY POSH BUT FRIENDLY HOTEL
body: We stayed here for 4 nights at the end of March and can only describe it as opulent luxury. We had a smoking room which was massive and had everything you could possibly want. The restaurant and bars are wonderful. A little on the expensive side though. The hotel is in a great location for all the fantastic things to see and do in New York. You won't be sorry if you book this hotel.

title: Fantastic
body: The Waldorf Towers were worth every dollar. The view from the 28th floor was unbelievable. The newly remodeled rooms had all the modern amenities. Service was impeccable.

title: Just average, hotel is let down by customer service.
body:
We decided to stay despite some poor reviews because of its history and iconic nature. However I can only describe the waldorf as average. We learnt a week or so before travel that renovations were ongoing but after being assured by the hotel this would not affect our stay we went ahead. Unfortunately they did affect our stay including being without water for 8 hrs one evening and no power another morning, and although I do appreciate these things do happen its the way that these issues are dealt with that should show the quality of the establishment, unfortunately Waldorf failed.
Overall is was nice to say I'd stayed, our room was good, the bed was very comfy and the public rooms are impressive but I wouldn't stay again.

title: Nice place, VERY Pricey
body:
I spent 9 days in a fairly nice room at the Waldorf. The service is great, the staff takes good care of you, and the hotel is clearly old, yet well maintained. My issue is really two folks. 1) EVERYTHING is so expensive. A few drinks at the bar? $200 Need a shirt dry cleaned? $22 The breakfast buffet at Oscars? $40 I mean WOW. I have been in NC a lot and these prices are a bit crazy. 
The second issue is I was with a group for business, we were all staying in suites and our CEO requested a smoking suite (which they confirmed in the reservation), however they never made the room available to him, apologizing, but not even discounting the small room (I think they knocked $50 off the suite price). Nine days and they could not move him? Crazy in my mind. Our next trip will find us in another hotel. It is cool to say I stayed at the Waldorf, but I would never do it if I was spending my own money.

title: Most perfect hotel experience
body: This is the best all-round hotel in the country. The guest rooms, the public areas and the restaurants are all cared for and tended to by the most wonderful staff of caring individuals. Front desk, please leave the light on in the room we just stayed in because we're coming back for more just as soon as possible.

title: Our monthly conference destination.
body: I stay here at least once a month for a due duligence meeting. They now have a room with my name on it.

title: Bad experience, no follow up
body: Typically, I enjoy the old world charm of the Waldorf Astoria in New York. My room was of a decent size, but unfortunately, my experience was a disaster this time, including a horrible brush with customer service. The tv did not function in my room, and I immediately called to have it fixed. When I had returned to my room 3 hours later, it was still not functioning. Another call to the manager on tap, and I was assured that a) it would be fixed in the morning or b) I would be moved to another room (it was already past midnight at the time). I was also offered a free night stay to make up for the inconvenience; an operable tv in the room is not really a big ask. The next morning, I went to have breakfast at Oscar's included in my room rate. The woman who assisted me that morning was an absolute nightmare. The front desk had given me a single voucher to cover two days of breakfast for the duration of my stay. The waitress at Oscar's yelled at me, grabbed the voucher, and told me that I would have to wait on line to go get a voucher for the second day. It was a horrible experience. I went to the front desk to complain, and again, I was assured that a) my tv would be fixed and b) they would send me a voucher for a free room to compensate for the horrible service I had received during my stay. Well, the tv was finally fixed, a full 24 hours after I had arrived. The voucher? It never arrived. I have never had such horrible service in my life, and it's doubtful that I will return to the Waldorf Astoria in New York -- so many other options in the neighborhood.

title: Service beyond any other.
body: Jackie, Ms. Waldorf Astoria, sees that you are treated with kid gloves. Guest get their every wish with respected and white glove quality service. The service is beyond any other, and you are informed we want you to be more comfortable than at your home. Clean room, wonderful restaurant, friendly bars with international patrons, every one of the employee are tenured, which speaks well of the ownership, though it has just changed. One did get comp breakfast coupon, however with new ownership their is now a charge. One concern, if you are with an elderly or disabled person, you need to ask for a commode bench. Yes, expensive!

title: Beautiful hotel, first class staff
body: I cannot say enough about this hotel. It is the perfect location to be a tourist in New York City. The staff allowed us to check our bags in and tour the city before our check in time and after our check out the next day. Our room was amazing, big, and first class. If you have the opportunity to stay here, Do it! You will not regret it. As we were only there for one night we did not experience everything the hotel has to offer, however our stay was more than comfortable to say the least.

title: Room smelled like vomit - would give zero stars if I could
body: I generally agree with the prior reviews complaining about how dated the rooms are and how the rooms reeked of smoke, except the junior suite we stayed in smelled like vomit rather than smoke. It was so bad that it made us sick and we actually decided to leave the hotel rather than take another room for the night. The hallways are not much better. This hotel is a total, overpriced disaster. Having lived in Manhattan, I know full well how expensive things are there, but it is as if this hotel goes out of its way to encourage you not to spend money there-e.g., $11 for a bagel/cream cheese...really? Customer service is phony and poor - check-in took an absurdly long time, and our bags arrived in our room hours after we arrived. Lobby would be ok, but the hordes of people streaming through the lobby at seemingly all hours negates any positives that you might attribute to the lobby. Location is ok, but that would generally be the case with any of the midtown hotels. There are MUCH better options in NYC at this price point. I'd definitely look elsewhere.

title: A stay in the Big Apple
body:
We booked our weeks holiday in New York through British Airways Holidays. BA were excellent, the only problem was coming home trying to get around Terminal 5 for our connecting internal flight. It was chaos trying to find where to go with staff directing us in so many differing and wrong directions.
That said our stay in the Waldorf met all expectations, the room was out of this world, so comfortable. They do say in their brochure that there are tea and coffee making facilities in the room but they have been taken away and you are expected to go to the lower ground floor and purchase coffee in Starbucks!!!
Our first morning we decided to have breakfast in the Hotel, it cost £60 for the two of us,plus 20% tips (that seems the normal rate for NY) So the next day we found a diner close by for £10 which was fine. Average meals eating out in NY seem between £50-£80 including a bottle of decent wine. Go down the side of the hotel 59th street down to 2nd avenue for some really good restaruants where the locals go.

title: BEAUTIFUL HOTEL
body: BEAUTIFUL hotel, fantastic location for sight seeing, comfortable relaxed atmosphere, the only complaint we had was that the guy who checked us in never made eye contact with usat all and went through the check in process as though he was reading from a script, we weren't sure if he was bored with his job or just down right rude, as he was our first contact we felt a little bit uncomfortable and wondered if all New yorkers were going to be like this,however this was not the case as everyone we came into contact with after this we found to be really friendly, I have no complaints about the hotel at all and it was a pleasure and privilege to stay in this wonderful iconic hotel

title: Great location iconic hotel
body:
A beautiful hotel with lovely reception areas and bars
Rooms are small and simple but very comfortable
Great location for exploring the city
Bars very expensive in hotel but good atmosphere

title: Waldorf Astoria NY - not for us!
body:
Just my opinion but I found the Hotel to be a bit shabby, Its very grand in the reception area, (although the carpets are lifting - beware!) all the staff were helpful, but the rooms are so dated and small, the bathrooms were basic, and no tea/coffee facilities which was pretty annoying. (we've spent a fortune in Starbucks this week! 300 dollars plus- its located just inside the Hotel)
Also, we had a double room which only had 1 door of wardrobe!!! omg.
Our 3 children were in the next room and only had a double wardrobe, I really think that this is inadequate. (they also had a bath full of water every time they showered)
Eating in the Hotel is so over priced.
The seating areas downstairs are so limited that it was almost always full, and therefore difficult to use free wifi, as you are charged in your room (fair enough).
The flat screen TV's have poor reception, and the remote didn't work properly, even when exchanged, neither did it in the next room where our children stayed, in the 6 days I was there I had replacement towels each day and twice I unrolled the towel after showering to find that the towel was soiled - yuk.
It is in a great location, that was a plus.
Just bear in mind that there isn't anywhere informal within the Hotel that you can just sit and relax.
Each day when we returned to the hotel, we had to just go and unwind in the rooms for lack of anywhere to chill.
There isn't a pool or any leisure areas, there is a spa - but I didn't try it, it was very pricey.
Would I stay again, No.
New York is amazing though, and the people are so friendly, I would love to go back, but just stay somewhere else.
Hope this helps some people (my childrens ages were 16, 18, 20).

title: Go for the history and atmosphere
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf for a business event and we were there for less than 12 hours. Overall, it's a beautiful hotel - the lobby, the banquet hall, etc. The room was paid for by the company, so keeping that in mind:
Check-in took a very long time. Our attendant was very nice, however, we think she may be been in training as we were standing there at the desk for at least 15 minutes - to the point that we asked, "Is everything all right?" We had booked a king bed room, and they had us in a double bed room - I believe they upgraded us to the Waldorf Towers (although I don't recognize any of the rooms in which we stayed on the website), but I don't know if we originally had booked in the Towers or the Hotel. We were on the 28th floor.
The elevator and hallway were very pretty, I did not notice any signs of aging in the Tower, however, I did notice a smell in the hall - maybe it was a smoking floor? Our room did not smell of smoke. The room itself was very nice - marble floors, separate tub and shower, and a walk-in closet. There was a nice view of Park Avenue and St. Bart's church below. The water pressure was virtually non-existent and when you used the sink, the stopper held the water in the sink. In the shower, it was a tiny bit better. Be careful walking around the room, the bed frame stuck out several inches from the bed, and we banged our shins on it a couple of times.
Later, when we went to sleep, we could not figure out how to turn off the light underneath the sink, nor could we determine how to close the opague shades at night, so with the lights from outside, it basically looked like daylight in our room. We were so tired and it was late, so we decided not to call the front desk to have someone come up to the room. The bed was very comfortable.
At the very least, you should go visit the lobby of the hotel if you visit NYC. You could find similarly located hotels with room rates that are about the same.

title: Classic hotel. Great location.
body: My bf surprised me with a birthday trip to NYC. He booked a junior suite at the Waldorf. The room was spacious and well supplied. The hotel is older and it shows its wear in places. However, the fundamentals are still solid. The bed was comfortable. The bathroom was spacious, especially by New York standards. The service was above average. The housekeeping crew were friendly and unobtrusive. The location simply can't be beat: close to subway, Rockefeller Center, the heart of midtown and Times Square. For a whilrwind romantic getaway, it was the perfect taste of old New York.

title: Wonderful stay in mini-suite
body: We used Hilton points for a standard room but luckily as gold members got an upgrade to a mini-suite. Large room with large bathroom. Absolutely fantastic. Gold members get other perks also. We loved our stay here. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the staff very friendly. We would love to stay here again.

title: Best customer service again
body: Once again checking into the Waldorf was a pleasure. Mary at the diamond desk assisted me and was as lovely as could be. I am in a great room that appears to have new carpet. Coming back to the Waldorf for me is like coming home. I'm very used to the facilities and seeing the same people at check in is refreshing. I understand that renovations are on the way but I must add that I miss my Starbucks complimentary "coffee " cards. I hope they will bring that back after they assess their position after the renovations. All and all I adore this place and it's staff

title: Miss the Starbucks
body: Recently stayed at the Waldorf and was extremely disappointed to find that they had closed the in-lobby Starbucks. I stay at this hotel 4 times per year for business and always appreciated the luxury and convenience of this amenity. It will be sorely missed ! It was something that for me distinguished the Waldorf from other NYC properties.

title: Wonderful Waldorf
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria for 4 nights, had booked superior rooms through British Airways and couldn't fault them. We had a bit of a wait for the rooms to be ready even after initial check in and been out to see some sights so as we had a further wait we were offered complimentary vouchers for a drink in Sir Harrys Bar so that was fine! We had rooms on 8th & 16th floors both with two double beds, the lower floor room was very spacious with a view of the top of the Chrysler building and the 16th floor was slightly smaller but still spacious and had a view over Park Avenue. The beds were extremely comfortable and we were all glad to sink into them after hectic days sightseeing in New York city. Location was great, short walk to Times Square, Grand Central, even Central Park was not too far for us. All the staff we encountered were polite and helpful
Highly recommend the historic tour of the hotel, we did this on our last morning at a cost of $50 each which included lunch in Peacock Alley which was very enjoyable. Our guide, Karen was great, really friendly, extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the hotel. We got to see a lot of the hotel including beautiful function rooms and a suite in the Towers - a snip at $6,500 per night! 
I would definitely return to this iconic hotel, it certainly made my first visit to New York very special.

title: new york
body: stayed at this hotel on recent trip five adults cant fault the hotel or service from staff spotless all the usa goverment stay here so must be good even during are stay barak barma stayed there how exciting will defo stay again

title: The Queen of Hotels
body:
If the walls could speak in the Waldorf Astoria they would be able to tell a fairy tale in every room.
The Hotel was a luxurious Hotel and also nowadays it sets a very high standard. I specially appreciate that you can see the history at every corner and many of the people working there seem to be there already for a very long time.
Sure, the rooms are not immaculate but the effort of the Team is great! Specially make sure you either enjoy any of the great Buffets (Oscar for Breakfast or the Sunday Brunch)
Windows can be opened (why not) and I would recommend this place to any in NYC! I just love it!

title: Experience
body: Fantastic experience. The staff couldn't have been more helpful and although very expensive we had breakfast on our last day fabulous so we also had lunch that proved to be the climax of a fabulous stay. May not have all the modern amenities but it sure has lots of style.l

title: Great time in New York
body: My wife and I recently went to New York to take our niece and her friend as a gift for graduating from college. We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria. My wife and I have each been to New York 2 dozen times or more. It is one of our favorite cities. We have, over the years, stayed at many hotels. However, after our stay at the Waldork Astoria, we will attempt, in the future, to stay there. The hotel is old, but has been updated. Somehow, the hotel retains all of the charm of the past. The service from check-in to departure was wonderful. I noted one prior comment regarding the Starbucks in the lobby - it was open when we were there during the first of June. We were able to book as small suite at a very good price considering New York. Both the bedroom and the sitting room was bigger than many hotel rooms we've stayed at in New York.

title: Straight out of the films
body: Fancy feeling like a queen for a week? My wonderful partner took me to this fabulous hotel for my birthday. It was beautiful, immaculate and luxurious. Would recommend to anyone!

title: fabulous stay in NEW YORK at the one &only WALDORF
body: We stayed at the Waldorf during our recent holiday 25/05/2012 - 01/06/2012 we had two rooms on the 17th. floor my wife and I shared room 1751,whilst my daughter amd her husband shared room 1753. Both rooms were excellent and suited us in all respects.WE DINED ON TWO OCCASIONS and food presentation,variety & quality was exceptional and costs were competitive. We would have dined more often but we were always on the move seeing the sites. All staff were quite superb and most helpful particularly the excursion desk which secured us all best seat tickets to two of the best shows in town.(WICKED & JAMES CORDENS ONE MAN TWO GOVERNERS which is absolutely hilarious ).S o all that could be said is well done Waldorf.

title: Overated
body: I was surprised to read many positive review on the Waldorf. I have stayed there several times on business. Each time I was given a small room, frayed looking. Last time the bathroom smelled like dirty rags. The mirror was faded. The rug partially torn. The soap dish too small for the soap bar. The computers in the business center had filthy keyboards that had never been cleaned, ever. There is no coffee machine, nor room for any in small rooms. The linens, towels, pillows and soaps are nice. But there are so many nicer hotels to stay in for the money it is astonishing to me that so many peole would give them a great review. The public rooms are nice, with a lot of history, but the hotel can not live off it's famous name withouth delivering the same quality as the competition. They do not. It seems the best reviews come from people who were upgraded to Suites. I suggest you try a Suite if you want to stay at the Waldorf, otherwise I can name you 10 better places to stay.

title: Can't wait to stay again!
body: Where do I start. We stayed for 7 nights in a superior room and had fantastic service, friendly staff, unique rooms, full of history. Our room was spacious with large windows and a view of the Chrysler Building. The ensuite bathroom was adequate although not huge, but had a lovely powerful shower and towels were replenished when required. We did the hotel tour which was followed by the most delicious lunch in Peacock Alley Restaurant with the famous Waldorf Salad. The location was ideal for Times Square and Broadway which were within a 10-15 minute walk and surrounded by shops and restaurants.

title: First Timer - Very Nice Experience!
body: As a student of history, I greatly enjoyed my stay at this landmark property. Teeming with mementos from the Gilded Age and the Turn of the Century, the Waldorf transports you back in time. Spend time inspecting all that there is to see in the massive lobby, including the display cases that house famous photos and treasures of the rich history of this amazing property. A very pleasurable experience, and I was able to secure very cost-effective rates on Hotels.com!

title: Old World Charm - Priceless!!
body:
I managed to get a late winter rate which made a superior room at the Waldorf affordable to my budget, just. Now I'm afraid I've been damaged for life, as I cannot imagine staying anywhere else the next time I visit New York City!
The room was fabulously large, large enough to fit all the shopping I did over the 8 days I stayed there. While the bath a some of the decor could do with a spruce up, the wear to some furnishings really just added to the charm for me. The bed was very comfortable, the room fittings and decor appropriate for this grand old hotel. 
I completed each day enjoying a whiskey in the lobby bar. Cheers to Mike for his wonderful service.
Can't wait to get back to NYC and the Waldorf.

title: Perhaps the Most Overrated Hotel in NYC, Tourist Trap
body:
Though perhaps the most famous hotel in the city, it is by far one of the most overrated and overpriced hotels in the world.
Yes, the lobby will wow you with classic design and elegant appointments. It is everything that a grand hotel should be. Large and open, with an urban and classic feel and look. However, beware of fool's gold, because the rooms are actually worn and tired.
Because of the sheer volume of rooms, the lobby is a whirlwind of commotion and chaos. Checking in feels like a cattle call to get all of the tourists in and out as quickly as possible. There is no personality, no charm and certainly no genuine feeling to the front desk staff. It is all business to get to the next person as quickly as possible.
Migrating towards outer hallways, the hotel is simply beautiful. Marble everywhere, very expensive floral arrangements and a veneer of old world class. Again, don't be fooled. The rooms are extraordinarily small. The wall paper was peeling, the carpets were torn and the bathroom downright filthy. It was so bad, that I actually requested another room in the hopes of getting a better room. No luck. The room that I moved into was in similar condition. Dirty toilet, saggy matress and used towels in the closet. Zero attention to detail. None whatsoever.
At the end of the day, the Waldorf is a "grand hotel" for tourists that never travel and want to stay in a name hotel. You will get ripped off and the only people that could be impressed with this average, at best, hotel are those folks that don't know any better.

title: Old world traditional value but misses on the room
body: Growing up in NYC I always wanted to stay at the Waldorf, my parents always preferred St. Regis; now I know why. The Waldorf lobby is spot on old world tradition, dark wood, high ceilings, lots of staff to assist, seemless check in. Things change after you proceed to your room, unless you're staying in the towers you will be in a seemingly old room. Once you start down the hall from the elevator you'll notice that feeling of the lobby is stripped away and nothing stands out. The rooms are well appointed, flat screen, very comfortable bed, nice bathroom. But the everything else is old, I had to put a towel under the front door because of the large gap that allowed hallway noise; they need to replace the doors and get new wallpaper. The shower was narrow and took a bit of manuevering to not to have water hitting you in the face.

title: This grand old lady is in the middle of a makeover
body: Maybe l expected too much from this place, but l was not impressed with this place. The enterance and lobby area was as grand as ever. The staff was very classy and attentive, however I was expecting the suite we were in would be taken care of much better than it was. There was peeling paint, and wall paper which could have easily been taken care of. The ceiling plaster in places was chipped and cracked. There was also lots of noise bleeding into the room from the elevators and from people talking in the hallways. Maybe this is part of the character of a place like this, but l'm not into that.

title: Take a tour, stay elsewhere
body: I stay here on business a time or two a year, totaling a couple weeks. Been coming here like that for 15+ years, including events in the ballroom. It's the Waldorf. An institution. Great history, great pictures on the walls, great people watching. Average rooms and many need cleaning if not makeover. And I don't even know what it costs, but can guess. The lobby is beautiful. The Bull and Bear Club is where deals get made. Take a tour, soak in the history, but stay elsewhere and save money for a better room. (And last time, the meal in the main ballroom at a major event was below average.)

title: Our home from home
body: The Waldorf-Astoria is an imposing and prestigious Hotel in Central Manhattan that provides the highest level of security in the whole of NYC and the most gentile of service which is why the President of the USA and all visiting dignitaries always stay here. My Husband and I however stay here for this and many other reasons, mainly because we are a long-staying Diamond guests and our family at the Waldorf are just lovely people who can't do enough to help and assist where possible. Jeff Krauthammer, GM of Food and Beverage goes out of his way to accommodate our business and personal needs in the hotel as do Jackie, Mary, Agnes and Gabriella in the fun-filled Diamond check in room. The Housekeeping staff are the most cheerful I have ever encountered in any hotel around the world and Oscar's famous breakfast buffet sates a rumbling belly every morning with its thick cut Canadian Bacon, freshly prepared eggs, blintz's, pancakes, oatmeal, fresh fruit... delicious! Thank you Waldorf and we'll be back soon!

title: New York Landmark
body: We just returned from a couple of days in NYC at the Waldorf. It is a well know landmark located in Midtown--about 3 blocks from 30 Rock. Nicely situated to many well known areas, it is easy to walk all around and see many spots. The hotel itself is not new and is in the midst of some work but it has plenty of charm. The lobby area is very nice and the people all helpful and courteous. The rooms are not huge and show a little age but not in a negative way--age with style. And since you are in NY you should be OUT of the room and taking in the city.

title: Fabled Waldorf Astoria Impresses
body:
Although I'm not typically a fan of older hotels, one cannot help but be impressed by the old world charm this fabled New York City hotel holds, and the art deco architectural details both outside and through out the property are truly amazing.
I did not have a chance to enjoy the hotels' amenities or visit any of the three hotel restaurants, but I did appreciate my slightly quirky but spacious corner room on the 11th floor with high ceilings, large closet and small work space.
The hotel is very convenient to Midtown attractions but beware that this iconic property means that the lobby is always busy. Hotel guests mingle with curious visitors coming to photograph the lobby and or attend one of the many events the property seems to always host.

title: WONDERFUL.......Kept pinching ourselves......were we really staying here!
body: My husband and I and our two teenage sons recently stayed at the Waldorf Astoria and it certainly didn't disappoint. The entrance lobby and check in area are a sight to behold and from the moment we entered the hotel we were so excited that we were staying in such an iconic hotel. We had two rooms, the boys in a double double room and we had a deluxe room with a king size bed. The bed and bedding and pillows were soooo comfortable, infact I looked at the label thinking I might purchase some back home....it was called 'The Bed' by the Waldorf Astoria(have since looked and it is a bit pricy but certainly worth it!!). The hotel information book in the rooms tells you to explore the hotel and we did.......the Grand Ballroom on the 3rd Floor, the Silver Corridor also on 3rd Floor....wow!! On the Saturday of our stay we returned to find a bottle of champagne in our room compliments of the hotel!!!. House keeping made up the beds each day and even made a little pouch with the flannel to house the toothbrushes....just the little touches make a difference. Loved sitting in the lobby on a morning waiting for the boys to surface, beautiful comfy sofas and chairs in breathtaking surroundings with beautiful floral displays dotted around. Fabulous location, so handy for the sights of New York. I would recommend this hotel 100% and in fact I have!!!!!!

title: Mutton dressed as Lamb, look but, DONT STAY!
body:
Our stay was at the end of a five month tour round the world, and we felt this was a safe hotel to book as this is "THE" Waldorf Astoria, and having good experiences with the brand elsewhere we thought we would finish here in New York. 
We were wrong! 
I can only retell our experience here, but I spoke with other guests and heard many similar stories. I can only presume that good reviews for this hotel are from those who did not stay here or who have never stayed at a good hotel.
The first room was old, tired, and not clean. It actually had broken glass on the floor of the bathroom, we couldn't believe it. We went back to reception and were assured an upgrade in light of this, so we went to a smaller room with a smaller bed! This was unacceptable, so we went back to reception again! This time we were given a large suite of two room size and were then informed that there was no water on our floor due to maintenance. (actually we were told it was the whole of midtown without water, even though the water was working elsewhere in the hotel)I must say we were offered compensation for no water, a voucher for their own spa at a value that meant you had to spend more, unreal.
So finally, three hours later we got a room that was clean and didn't have wallpaper peeling off the walls, no joke the second room had broken lamps and peeling paper!
We stayed here for four nights (paid in advance, won't do that again!) and by the end of the stay we had TV problems, bad housekeeping, curtain issues (blinds stopped working!) and met with several managers.
These managers did try to compensate us for our problems, however at no point did this really work, the rooms were all bad that we were moved to, the offer of a car to the staten island ferry one evening resulted in us being threatened with being stranded there by the driver, and the complimentary meal that we had at the Bear and Bull (I think thats the name) was mediocre to say the least. Had I had to pay for that meal there I would have been very angry at the state of the food for the cost.
This is a tired old hotel, that according to two managers we spoke with, hasn't really got any perfect rooms, as they all need a little something, no joke, we even met with the building maintenance manger!
Please visit this hotel, see the ballrooms, see the lobby, this is great but don't stay here. No free wifi, no coffee or tea makers in the rooms, and massive prices for a really run down hotel. Coffee from room service was $8 plus a $5.25 per person charge, plus a 15% gratuity plus state tax! A $15 dollar coffee is acceptable on a desert island 20 room boutique hotel but from a run down motel it is not. 
This hotel is mutton dressing as lamb. I am a hilton Gold Member and can not recommend this hotel even though I love the brand, This should be their flagship hotel and in fact I have to say it was the worst Hilton we stayed in.
I can only hope others do not make the same mistake as us, it was a real shame to have our travels finish with what should have been a glamourous great experience at one of the worlds most famous hotels and instead it just never came out that way.

title: Awesome
body: This hotel is everything that you'd expect. The rooms are fantastic, the staff couldn't be friendlier or more helpful. The hotel is not new, so if look hard enough, you'll find issues but part of the charm of older hotels is that they are old and this one is still very gracious.

title: Classic luxury
body: Like walking into the past, real classy luxury, old fashioned service and attention to detail. Even if you don't stay it's worth walking through the lobby - especially during their famous Sunday Brunch. Suites and rooms are comfortable and well-equipped, but best to avoid the temptation of the mini-bar if you can (ouch!!). Great location for Time Square and the main attractions.

title: Fantasic Stay At The Old Dame
body: We booked a Double Queen room at the Waldorf Astoria in June 2012 for 6 nights. Walking in to the old dame you could feel the nostalgia and the important role this hotel once held in the city, I doubt that it still has the highest position within the hotel business these days but it still a fantastic hotel and we got great deal. We were greeted by one of the staff who directed us to the diamond reception where we had seats whilst we checked in within 5 minutes. We were on the 7th floor in room 731, the room was very large with 2 double beds which were extremely comfortable a 42" flatscreen TV with drinks cabinet - a bathroom with a shower and a bath, large mirror with good lighting & toilet. We also had a rather large dressing room with safe, ironing board etc. The bed linen was changed and the roomed cleaned every day. The only draw backs were that the room faced on to the air con units which were a bit noisey and because we were the first room on the landing you could hear the lift bell now and again. But all in all I loved the Waldorf Astoria.

title: Worth every penny - spend a night there!
body:
My girlfriend and I stayed here a few months back when we were in town for a wedding. While we got a discounted rate through the wedding, it still set us back a pretty penny. We were tempted to stay with friends instead, but figured that it was a special occasion, so what the heck? Boy, are we glad we did.
Unlike some luxury hotels that get by on their reputations, the Waldorf Astoria delivers everything you'd expect from one of the finest hotels in the country. From the moment we walked in, we felt like royalty, even though we were clearly not their normal clientele. There was a bit of a wait to check in, but the staff was super friendly to us and very helpful with our requests.
And the room... wow! This might be the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. We laid down and immediately fell asleep for 3 hours. It's that good. There's also a surprising amount of space for a New York City hotel room.
The only thing stopping me from giving the hotel five stars is the price - you get an incredible amount, but you're also paying for the fact that this is an iconic hotel. There's probably better value elsewhere. Still, if you're looking for a place to stay for one night for a special occasion, I can't speak highly enough about the quality of our room and the professionalism of the staff at the Waldorf Astoria.

title: She's great but in need of some TLC
body: I have just got back after a stay here and I enjoyed it very much, it's a wonderful building with lots of beautiful features but she's showing her age a bit now. The first impression of room 710 was "wow" but after a while when the shower doesn't work properly, a huge chunk of the bath surface is missing, the plug points on the wall are faulty, the carpets frayed, the paintwork chipped and after dropping the lid of my handcream under the bedside table, it hadn't been moved and the carpet hoovered for a long time! The plus was an amazing bed, a huge TV, a walk in wardrobe and near silent air conditioning so it didn't stop my enjoyment totally, but the little niggles do irritate and at prices which start at $299 a night, it should really be perfect.

title: Everything you expect - and more
body:
We had a suite on the 14th floor - great view out of bedroom window and very nice - old and quirky to some extent but then again that was what we wanted and the standard of the suite was first class but previously had a box room on 7th floor which was dark and no views except for a brick wall.-- so we upgraded
Don't let that put you off booking - just make sure you have a room with an outside view of the world
This hotel is like a museum with rooms - there is history and Art Deco all around you -- it is unreal and simply fantastic
The Sunday Brunch takes up the whole lobby - even if you dont eat it you MUST see it to believe it -- out of this world
Bars in hotel are all great - Bull and Bear was our favourite
All of their staff we met were first class and VERY well trained to give fantastic customer service

title: Worth a visit
body: This hotel is quirky and is like previous reviewers have mentioned is showing her age, however, you don't stay in a hotel of this age and expect contemporary furnishings/bathrooms. We were upgraded to a junior suite, which was spacious in New York terms; the beds are fabulous and comfortable with fine cotton bed linen. The drinks are very pricey, as you would expect, so we ate out all of the time using various Delis for breakfasts that are more than adequate providing a good selection of food. 2 gin and tonics in Sir Harrys bar are $39 to give you a feel of the pricing. Service is patchy as this is an extremely busy hotel, but in the main we had no complaints. It’s a great location and most places are within walking distance or the subway station is just 1 block away. We got a good deal with BA holidays combining the flight and hotel as a package.

title: Great option for New York
body: As other guests mentionend, this Hotel is special. The great Art Deco Lobby is fabulous and every time, you walk through, just great. After a room in the 5th floor at our first stay, we now traveled with 3 people and had a very spacous one bedroom suite on the 21st floor with a spectacular view. No question, the rooms are a bit worn out and some TLC would help, but overall a good option with spacous rooms and modernized bathrooms. A coffe maker, offered in most hotels, woud be an improvement, but Starbucks is across the street (don´t use the one in the Hotel, long lines). The staff is very friendly and helpful. The location is unbeatable: closed to central park, great restaurants and breakfastplaces the next blocks to the east..

title: a Classic!
body: No matter where we stay in NYC - our favorite has to be the "Waldorf"...the Hudson halls too dark, the W rooms too small, the Marquiz too crowded...the "Waldorf" NYC is it definitely perfect. Never lets you down with its classic, historic, glamorous lobby, chandaliers, decorative walls and ceilings, airy and lighted hallways, spacious rooms and incredible service. :)

title: great location and historic charm!
body: We stayed in this hotel for the weekend while we were in town to attend a wedding. The hotel is well-situated, close to Grand Central Station, Central Park and lots of shopping. The lobby is beautiful and reflects the historic charm of this hotel. Our check-in was quick and easy, and the staff was very accommodating, allowing us into our room three hours before the designated check-in time. Our room on the 13th floor was spacious and clean although the carpeting and chair were very worn. Overall, our stay was great and we would recommend this hotel!

title: I enjoyed the stay
body: Though I like the towers better, The main WA was clean, the service excellent and the AAA price outstanding. We ordered room service which was delivered quickly, presentation splendid and the staff professional. Though pricy, it was worth being able to sit back and be served in our room in comfort ! Parking in the hotel is expensive, there are many parking opportunities close by. We enjoyed our whole stay at the Waldorf !!! We come in often.

title: Great hotel
body:
The hotel was fantastic. My teen age son and I booked a double-double (two double beds) for the weekend. 
The woman at the check in counter was friendly, quick and extremely helpful. She got us into a rooom a little early and answered questions about tours, attractions and dining. She was as knowegable as the concierge.
The room was larger than average and decorated very nicely. The beds were among the most comfortable that I have ever had at an hotel- fantastic.
The concierge was very helpful and giuded us to whatever attraction was on the agenda that day.
The hotel in general is obviously old but has been kept up well. There were places in the room where repairs were done years or decades ago and you could see the fix (like a new piece of molding where the old one was broken) but they were done cleanly and well. This made the hotel feel like and old house that has character. Nothing seemed cheap. 
I would stay there again in a minute.

title: A very special experience
body: A friend and I recently stayed for four nights at The Waldorf. Before we left I e mailed the Hotel to request a room with a nice view if possible as my friend was celebrating a special birthday and I received a very nice response from David O'Keefe, the Rooms Manager. When we arrived we had a wonderful surprise that we had been upgraded to a room on the 24th Floor. The receptionist was charming, with a big smile on his face when he advised us of our upgrade and handed my friend an envelope with two complimentary cocktails. Our room was ready for us at 1 pm and we arrived to find a beautiful suite with two bathrooms, very welcome for two ladies sharing the room! The view was amazing, the beds, mattresses, masses of clean towels all outstanding. It was wonderful to have such a comfy room to return to after pounding the New York streets! The staff are all charming, nothing is too much trouble and the front lobby is historic,very busy but always with something/people to watch, great fun. We did not eat in the Hotel, but did use a couple of the bars which were buzzy and fun. The location of the Hotel is very convenient for all the sights. The hotel is a little dated in parts, but to get the space that we did in our bedroom in a major city far outweighed the slightly faded upholstery and I would far rather have friendly, accommodating staff than some of the snootier people you find in the more modern city hotels. A wonderful stay, thank you David and all the staff at The Waldorf, I hope to return one day.

title: Disappointed but historically interesting
body: I recently stayed at the Hotel for one night. I was disappointed by my experience at the hotel personally. It was very opulant but I found my room to be very dated. I think it needs a make over. Also, parts of the hotel were blocked off to accomodate a wedding. It was very interesting historically because it has existed for so long.

title: Wonderful experience. Thank you.
body:
I fully recommend that you stay at the Waldorf. Historic, interesting, comfortable and luxurious.
The staff are highly professional throughout. The rooms are wonderful - we got an upgrade to a king bed double, and it was a truely lovely room. Furnished nicely, comfortable bed, functional bathroom and a useful sitting area to relax. The hotel bar is very nice (although somewhat expensive). We did not eat at the hotel or use the spa, so cannot comment on these areas. 
The Waldorf is in a perfect location for exploring the city, and is a landmark in itself. However, I understand that they are just starting to undertake refurbishments at the front of the hotel (June 2012), so check in advance whether or not this will impact your stay. My guess is not, given the professionalism of this hotel. Stay here. Do not hesitate.

title: Just Experience
body:
Loved Hilton chain for a long time, finally get to stay at the pinnacle of Hilton chain - the Waldorf Astoria, just excited.
Room is not spacious but very much enough. Hotel staff are very nice but there was a problem, when I was checking in, the front desk lady said my room was not ready so I will have to come back later, she will call me when it's ready. So I waited for over an hour, then came back to the hotel, tried to check in again, this time, succeeded. SO, where is that phone call?
Nevertheless, it's worth it.

title: Not luxury
body:
Room smelled, the carpet was wet in some portions of the room. I opened the window and paint chipped and cracked and went everywhere. The box of tissues in the bathroom was wet!?
This is a classic hotel and could be nice if they were to work on the upkeep and updates. They probably have some very nice rooms - but this one was bad and I've heard from other folks staying with me that the rooms were old and smelled.
Disappointing.

title: Just average....poor service
body: I stayed here with my daughter to celebrate her 16th Birthday. I wanted her to have a special experience in a historic hotel instead of a typical modern other hotel with no personality. While the lobby is nice, it was very dark and we did not want to spend any time there. The room was fine but the toilet ran all night long.
