Lots of outlets in room which was nice but $17 for 24 hours of internet connection is a little pricey. My big complaint though is we were just a number. We had to stand in line to check in (15 minutes), our room wasn't ready and they made NO effort to get it ready (we had to wait three hours), when we went back to pick up keys we had to stand in line again. When we stored our luggage we had to stand in line again....you get the idea. Service personnel were nice and friendly but definitely not enough on a busy summer weekend.

title: Beautiful Lobby Shame About the Rooms
body:
Stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria on Saturday 23rd June 2012. The lobby and reception area are stunning, really beautiful. But the check in queue was terrible. There was a massive queue which moved very slowly. Finally upon arriving at the reception desk there seemed to be trouble with our room, check in was from 3pm and we arrived a 4pm. It took around 30minutes to sort the problem out. We didn't seem to be the only ones with this problem. We were "up-graded" to an executive business room. Upon entering the room on the 13th floor there was an immediate smell of cat urine. The room was relatively large, especially for an NYC hotel room. The bathroom seemed clean and the bed was comfortable. I tried to open the window which proceeded to fallout of its brackets (lucky I caught it as it would have landed on the street.).
Had a drink at the Sir Harry bar on the Sunday afternoon. The bar server took quite a while to come over to us to take the drink order as he seemed more interested in the group of four woman and flirting with one of their 18 year old daughters. 
I am glad that I got to stay at the waldorf astoria just to say I have stayed there but there are certainly a lot better hotels in NYC in the same great location.

title: Centrally located historic building with large rooms!
body: Perhaps the best hotel I have stayed at in several years. Everything was exceptional. The check in was very quick considering how large the hotel was, and the check in staff was very friendly. The room service was fast and the hotel staff did not hesitate to send anything we requested to the room. The room was very spacious and clean, and bed was comnfortbable. I appreciate the historic aspects of the hotel, so some of the bathroom amenities and fixtures were slightly dated as one would expect. Overall, a fantastic experience at the Waldorf.

title: Very nice but a little dated
body:
When I booked I went to trip advisor for reviews. Definitely a mixed bag. My thoughts are this. It is somewhat a quiet location. You didn't hear horns all night long. With that being said, you weren't right at Central Park or Times Square. The reputation of this property is legendary and it is cool just to say you stayed there. I was surprised at the very competitive rates that were quoted. Roughly $250 per night from the HIlton site. Everything in the room was good. Everything worked, bed was comfy etc.
We didn't use the property for much other than sleeping, but our flight was delayed coming in and ordered room service when we arrived. The food was good, but not worth $105 for two people. 
Staff was friendly and relatively helpful. It was worth the price we paid but can't imagine paying what this property normally charges. It is an older property so it is in need of renovations, but still it is the WALDORF ASTORIA!!

title: Could have been great
body:
My husband and I stayed here for one night in early June, the night before we were meeting friends in the hotel for the famous Waldorf's Sunday brunch. If I were to summarize our approximately 24 hours of this first Waldorf Astoria experience, I would say it is akin to being on an historic cruise ship that retains some if its former glory but needs to take more care in living up to its name. 
We drove up to the hotel and were surprised to find that, unlike most city hotels, you do not pull up to the main entrance to meet a valet to park your car -- you drive around to the side of the hotel to pull into a covered entrance inside the building to meet a valet, get help with your luggage (if needed), etc. This is actually very nice. Weather isn't an issue and you are sheltered from the comings and goings of the street entrance.
As others have mentioned, the lobby is notable for its old world elegance. You do feel transported back in time. We forgot that there are over 1200 rooms in this hotel until we got in line to check-in. That's when it started feeling like a cruise ship. To be fair, we were trying to check in early and patiently waited 20 minutes to get to the front desk. Our room wasn't ready, but we were graciously told that when we returned we did not have to wait in the long line again. In order to store our luggage, though, we had to travel down to another level to check said luggage. 
After a late lunch we returned past the time our room should be ready, and it was. As we were meeting friends for brunch the next day and didn't want to have to checkout beforehand, we requested a late check-out, which was cheerfully granted. We went back downstairs to retrieve our luggage. The decor of the room looked like what you imagine an old elegant NYC hotel should look like -- high ceiling, lots of gold and yellow and drapery, etc. We did notice a slight mildew smell in the room, but frankly since we were really tired and needed a nap, we didn't call down and ask for another room, not wanting to have to run around the hotel more. The bed was comfortable. The toilet handle had to be held down for a while to complete a flush. We didn't notice until the next morning that there was no hair dryer, even though it's listed as in every room, and we discovered a long black hair in the tub (cannot be our's). I realized the mildew smell had inflitrated our clothes.
After a nice lobby brunch (they set it up the food right in the lobby itself, with ropes delineating the brunch from the guests standing in line to check in/out and you get seated at cruise-ship-like tables in several dining rooms), we decided to check out and tell the front desk about some of the room glitches. I had written them down just to let the hotel know that they fell a bit short of what we would think the Waldorf Astoria experience might be. The front desk attendant was apologetic and appreciative of the list, and offered us an upgrade to a suite for the next time we visit -- she said a letter would come in the mail with this offer. We felt that was a nice response. 
After waiting 16 days for this letter, I called the hotel manager's office to follow-up. I got a concerned staff member, who had someone look into it and return my call. This person apologized and promised to send the letter out. I commented on how this had been a lot of work to get what was supposed to be compensatory for a "less than Waldorf" experience, and she then offered to make it a complimentary night instead of just the upgrade. She also offered to email me that day with a confirmation of this offer plus her personal contact info. I very much appreciated that response! However, after 4-5 days of not getting any email, I ended up calling the manager's office once again and spoke with my contact. She investigated, returned my call and this time said that a supervisor for the front desk would FedEx me the letter with the offer and should the original letter arrive, to ignore it (the "original letter" never did). I pointed out that this had taken me a lot of time and effort just to get what was promised, and that this did not seem like the Waldorf way (she said it was not). The FedEx letter with an apology note and the free night in a suite offer did arrive as promised.
So, in sum, while the staff all had extremely gracious manners and the architecture/decor had palpable history and elegance to it, the actual experience of staying there was OK. Getting the hotel to "make good" on its goodwill promises took way more effort than it should have. However, after my persistence the hotel did acknowledge its little shortcomings and did offer us a complimentary night to let them show us how it should be done. We believe that the glitches we experienced can be rectified with some attention to detail -- our visit could have been great, and we are willing to see if the next time it will be.

title: Well, it is the Waldorf...
body: Hey, if its good enough for James Earl Jones I think I can make it work too. The lobby is quite a spectacle, it feels like there are actually several lobbies and you have to find the right one to check in. Everything is just enormous, the lobbies, the hallways, i was there a few nights and just barely scratched the surface. I'm a little irritated that the gym is a separate fee. That just seems ridiculous to me. $300 a night and you want to nickel and dime me for $10 that i cant expense? Whatever, thanks a lot. The room was perfectly comfortable, to be honest when i travel i only care that i've got a comfortable bed, a strong shower and a nice cold AC and this had all three. Again, the gym is a miss, I just can't see paying $10 to run a few miles in the morning. All in all, this is one of my top picks in midtown.

title: A few days of luxury and a surprise at home
body: The room is very comfortable, clean, clear and quiet. Staff was friendly, helpful and made me feel at home. There are too many histories to tell us about this hotel in the lobby that you feel like a super star in Hollywood. Unfortunately when I arrived home they discounted me $58 in my credit card although I had nothing to pay in the check out.

title: Underwhelmed
body:
I was so ridiculously excited to stay here until I started reading the reviews here on Trip Advisor and started to worry a bit. I hoped that my stay wouldn't be like the others and kept my chin up. That was my mistake. 
We arrived a bit before our check in time and used the valet. I've used valet at other NYC hotels and it's never been an issue but here it was a [--]. They really didn't help point you as to how the heck to get to the lobby and were really rude. We had no idea where we were going and after a few tries we found it but it wasn't for the help in the valet area. Our room wasn't ready yet so they told us it'd only be about 30 minutes at most and we decided to wait. 45 minutes later our room STILL wasn't ready so we decided to hit the bar (their own brand of champagne is pretty decent I must say). After about 2 hours total of waiting our room was ready and I was informed we'd been upgraded from our Junior Suite. 
We got to the room and I was pretty excited as I was told this was a suite, yay! We opened the door and almost were physically knocked over by the stench of cigarettes and cigars. It was horrid!! What made it even worse was that my husband had just quit smoking days before the trip so that made things a lot more difficult. After all of that waiting, we didn't want to sit and wait MORE so decided to hope it dissipated and headed off into the city. I will note that our suite WAS very nice, 2 full bathrooms, a bedroom and a living room. The decor was a bit dated but it was still a nice space. I also have seen others complain about the lack of hair dryer and neither of our rooms had one. 
The next day we got a phone call asking how our stay was and I told them about the rancid smoke smell (mind you this was a non smoking room). They said they'd bring an air purifier in the room while we were out to hopefully make it better. I don't think they ever did that because the smell never got better. 
That night while sleeping I woke up when I was bit on the foot by a spider. In the bed. I know this could happen anywhere but this is the last place I ever expected this to happen at. My foot swelled up and it was pretty painful for a couple days. Again, it could happen anywhere but happening at a hotel of this caliber is kind of surprising. 
Finally upon leaving we were told to call 30-45 minutes before we needed our car which we did. When we got to the valet though we had to wait ANOTHER 45 minutes for our car, which had I not planned for delays, would have made us late for our flight. 
After seeing my complaint about the spider bite on Twitter the Waldorf did email me and ask what happened. However when I told them what happened, I never heard a response. 
It was an OK stay but I don't think I'd do it again. The hotel definitely has seen better days, the service wasn't nearly what I was expecting and the rooms (although big) were ho-hum. Bummer.

title: The Grand Old Dame
body: I first stayed at the Waldorf nearly 20 years ago and it still retains its "old world charm" and slightly faded grandeur. The front entrance is closed due to renovation so one loses the impact of entering up the grand staircase and walking though the grand open space. The front staff were efficient and friendly and most apologetic about the renovations and my bag was quickly delivered to my room. The room was a good size and the bed was very conmfortable. The bathroom needs updating as does the overall decor and having a wirless router on the desk looked a little odd. Overall it was a pleasant experience but next time I am in NYC I will be trying somewhere new and saying goodbye to memories of the past.

title: Gorgeous hotel ever!
body:
A pure European taste reminding us good old days.
A fancy lobby, but the cloak was a bit complicated located underneath.
The room was quiet and wide enough with a bit outdated bathroom.
What surprised me was room service not available for dinner so that I ended up going out suffering from a nasty jet lag.
Overall, very gorgeous hotel, I want to stay with my family someday.

title: Great Trip
body: Great time, kids and everyone one had a great time. Hotel was beautiful, service was amazing. Looking forward to another visit soon.

title: Amazing, Transports you back to Sinatra Era!
body: We were staying in the Astoria for the June back holiday and the hotel was everything I expected and more. We arrived to a glamourous welcome but too early for our room (11:30am to be exact).The reception staff told us to start enjoying New York and took our number, kindly advising us they would text us when the room was ready. In less than an hour we received a text that the room was ready! The room was splendid, truly casts you back to Sinatra days with opulent, traditional glamour, traditional decorations and all decorated immaculately! Unfortunately our room was right by the lift so we rang reception to complain about the slight noise from the lift and within 15 minutes the staff moved us to another room. This was an even better room with a bathroom almost as big as the bedroom! Really helpful staff and a stunning hotel! Great central location too, just 2 minutes from Central Station! Fab breakfast too, homemade Granola is a true delight!

title: Impressive as always!
body: Folks, this hotel is an architectural masterpiece. Amazing attention to detail and the historic photos throughout the property are a real treat. I stay there 6 to 8 weeks a year and I have never had an unpleasant experience. I check in with Jackie in the Diamond reception area and am consistently impressed with her positive attitude and the top shelf service she provides. The Waldorf is a special place, excellent service, and impeccable location.

title: Great experience
body: Excellent room, great location, comprehensive service in every aspect.

title: An Impressive New York Landmark
body:
Even though this beautiful hotel is currently under refurbishment, aside from the scaffolding in front of their main entrance, you would never know.
I recently stayed here for a New York weekend and found it was the perfect location. Close enough to Time Square, Radio City Music Hall even the Empire State building to take a nice stroll around the city. We walked to Central Park and the Plaza Hotel - in fact, we only took a Taxi to and from the airport.
The room itself was lovely. We stayed in the 21st floor in a King Superior room. The view was beautiful and the room was quiet, and beautifully decorated. The room was very clean and lots of lush towels (they even supplied conditioner which is rare in hotels but an essential item for me). Our room had a large walk-in closet which housed the robes and ironing board. Good water pressure, no loss of warm water and the beds were very comfortable.
I am a Hilton Honors member which in some cases gives you perks you would not otherwise receive. 
The lobby and bar are very nice with live piano music in the evenings. If you want something a little more "clubby" there is a bar right across the street which has a DJ in the evenings.
I was quite content with staying here, and would gladly do so again. 
An impressive stay at this impressive landmark.

title: Charismatic and Impressive NYC Landmark
body: Could not fault many aspects of the Waldorf Astoria after our recent stay in New York, from the moment we arrived at the hotel until our departure the staff we friendly and very knowledgable and only to happy to assist. The hotel is currently under refurbishment so access to the hotel has changed but this does not hinder any entry or exit to the building. Within walking distance to many restuarants and Times Square and short taxi ride to many other attractions. Visited the resturants within the Waldorf and the Bull & Bear is a little expensive as most mains are in excess of $50 but their nips of alcohol/ glasses of wine are very generous and the service is above average with attentive staff so not a place to visit if dining on a budget. If you enjoy buildings with heritage and charm as well as modern luxuries will not be disappointed with the Waldorf Astoria. Highly recommend.

title: Very Comfortable, Gracious Accomodations
body: Just a quick warning - the Park Ave entrance was closed last week for renovations. This made entering and navigating the hotel a little tricky. The management could have done a better job communicating this with arriving guests. But, once inside, I felt very comfortable and cared for. My bed was really, really wonderful and I slept really well. The bathroom was a little small but I expect that in an older hotel. I would have given it 5 stars if they had handled the renovation issue better.

title: NEED TO KNOW
body: Park Ave. entrance and lobby closed for renovation. Scaffolding outside interferes with views from some rooms. Extremely loud construction work (jackhammers) directly outside windows a few mornings. We were extremely well compensated for our inconvenience. Ms. Judith Beck is an outstanding asset to the organization. Classic, elegant, historical property. Incredible public spaces. Our rooms old but very clean and well maintained, small bathrooms, minor issues. If you want to sleep in this might not be a place for you or book rooms in the towers.

title: Work and Play...
body: Stayed at the Waldorf for a conference that was being held there...the only remotely negative thing that I can say is that the hotel is being updated, so getting in at first was a little tricky. However, once inside--you'd never know that there was construction going on! The rooms are comfortable, clean and convenient--touches that other places forget about these days...like plenty of outlets to plug in laptops, phones, etc. Bathrobes and nice toiletries...everything about the Waldorf just seems a tad more luxurious! The staff is very helpful--I needed a later check-out and they were happy to oblige...over all, it was a wonderful stay and I hope to return!

title: I did not feel welcome in this hotel! a complete disappointment
body: I booked this historic hotel in NY for a holiday with my kids (15 and 17). I knew that it was a historic building so I didnt expect any modern facilities and I was fine with it. In the first place the hotel entrance on Park avenue is being remodeled at the moment, so when we arrived at 10:30 pm we were dropped at the garage entrance, but that doesn't excuse that they were not signs and NOBODY was there to receive us. We were totally lost and no kind of assistance from the personnel of the hotel was offered, we had to carry our luggage thru stairs and nobody offered any help. When we finally made it to the lobby, the reception was very cold and not every welcoming. The room was ok in size and decor but simply FILTY AND DISGUSTING!! my son has allergies and the room was dusty. the bathroom was ok, the housekeeper didn't clean our room one of the days, they had plenty of time to clean it..we left 9 am and return at 5pm and our room was not clean. Forget internet in your room (i know that not every hotel offers internet but at the rate that they charge, I was expecting at least that), you have to pay US$15.00 a day. I dont know if they do it on purpose to keep their lobby looking busy because only in the lobby you have complementary internet service, therefore is always packed with people using their electronic devices. The rooms are not well insulated and it hard to sleep with all the noise. At the rate that they charge I advice you to find any other Hotel in Manhattan, the Waldorf is not worth it, unless you want to be in a historic place.

title: It's ok, needs some remodeling
body: Great location (midtown east) to many attractions. Short walk to Rockefeller Center, (3-4 blocks), 5th avenue shopping area (3 blocks), Grand Central Terminal (7 blocks), Time Squares (8-9 blocks), and Central Park (9 blocks). If you don't like to walk more than 5 blocks, there are subway stations nearby, hop-on hop-off tour busses stop right at the hotel (Lexington and 49th St., you need to purchase tickets in advance, they take you to Time Squares where you can transfer to other bus tours), rickshaws, and it is easy to get a taxi at the front of the hotel. There are many shops, restaurants, cafes, pharmacies (CVS, Duane Reade) within walking distance. The Lobby is beautiful. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Many are from other countries. The house keeping staff gave me extra shampoo and lotion, constantly asking if I needed anything else. Rooms are a little bigger than most in the city for the same price. However, I agree with some comments about the need to remodel some rooms. You can see the cracks on the edges of the ceiling, doors, windows, etc. Paints are falling off the ceiling especially in the bathroom. You can get complimentary coffee maker or tea kettle if you are Hilton Honors member, but you have to request it in advance. They rather you order from room service or purchase at Starbucks nearby. You need to call for late check-out or luggage storage. The entrance on Park Ave is closed for remodeling, it was confusing at first since the hotel address is on Park Ave (front). On the confirmation, they asked us to enter through 50th St. for valet parking ($60 per day). The other walking entrance is on Lexington Ave, it took us awhile to figure out which is the front and which is the back entrance. My daughter got sick after one night stay, she slept through the next two days of vacation. I am not sure if it was due to what one of the reviewers mentioned of allergies. My daughter never had allergies but the room was very clean, perhaps was the construction or just the heat (95+ degrees, it was reported heat wave in the city during our visit.) The room was very cold and we adjusted the temperature on the thermostat but it didn't seem to work, so we turned it off and then turn it back on when the room got hot. It was the same with both rooms- too cold. We decided to stay at Waldorf because of the 4-star rating, the reasonable room rate (promotion or AAA) at the time and we want to have the experience of staying at the well known historical place. There are many nearby hotels; Marriot and W Hotel are right across the street. Intercontinental, The Roosevelt, and a few other hotels are nearby. Grand Hyatt is not too far. Overall it was not too bad for us, we pretty much were out visiting many attractions and exploring the city all day and basically came back for shower and sleep. It really depends on what your purpose of stay and what kind hotel you want to stay in.

title: What a beautiful grand hotel!
body: I was a little concerned about staying here because of some of the reviews I have seen. Fortunately not one thing about this classic old hotel was negative. Every person we came in contact with was warm and welcoming, from the reception desk to the cleaning staff. The entire place just sparkles, and makes you feel as though you are royalty. Our room was 610, no view to speak of, but the room itself was spotless, and had so much charm. Bed was super comfy, and the bathroom was larger than I have seen before in city hotels. There was some renovation going on, so some of the hotel exits (main Park Ave for example) were closed off. No matter, since the hotel takes up a whole city block you could find your way out with no problem. One other thing to note is that I found this a very quiet hotel, you could hear some street noise ( the lullaby of manhattan :) ) but not bothersome at all. Heard no noise from rooms on either side of us, and no loud cleaning staff in the mornings. I will stay here again!

title: Great Hotel
body: If you want to be in central New York, you couldn't wish for a better location. The rooms are luxurious in an era gone by fashion, with lovely toiletries, and as one reviewer mentioned, even umbrellas in the rooms. Unlike one unfortunate reviewer, we were met at the entrance of the hotel, our luggage carried into our room and experienced the zip in/zip out check in process. The staff were very polite and helpful with tour/show bookings, restaurant recommendations, etc. and it was nice to be greeted like an old friend every time one came back to the hotel. Free internet access was only available in the main lobby and predictably the lobby was always full of hotel guests using their electronic devices and hence nowhere to sit, unless you ate or had a drink in the lobby restaurant. Despite this, I would stay at the Waldorf again.

title: Beautiful historic hotel
body: I thoroughly enjoyed staying at the Waldorf last week. I was only there for one night, but it was a pleasure to stay in a hotel with great pre-war detail and a sense of elegance. Although my room was not one of the renovated ones, it was still beautiful - a small corner room with two large windows, each with old-fashioned deep window sills. The closet had the original doorknob from yesteryear, and the marble bathroom was gorgeous - already re-modeled. Also, the room was very quiet. The gorgeous lobby is quite a scene and oh so busy. I suspect it's because the hotel charges $16 per day to use internet service in your room but nothing if you access it in the lobby. I found the concierge to be knowledgeable but rather abrupt, but he did suggest an outstanding restaurant nearby for dinner. The hotel is very, very busy, and doesn't feel relaxed. I did however, enjoy my stay very much, and would stay there again if I could get another excellent price from Priceline.

title: No Other Hotel Even Comes Close
body:
Prior to our arrival, I contacted the Front Desk to check on a few items. Tim at the front desk was more than amazing. The personal service and attitude he portrayed was what all the other hotels have forgotten over the years. His attention to detail and true willingness to help far surpassed the front desk texperiences at other hotels. Tim, THANK YOU!!!!! for making this a true eperince of a lifetime. 
The Concierge was also a true find in this city. Reservations were obained on our bealf of some of the finest restaurants. 
The Bell Man, Bobby, was like an old friend who was enthusiastic about his home town. He gave us suggestions and wanted to answer ANY questions we had about the great city. I felt like he was a true friend and could call upon him anytime.
Make sure you take the historic tour! The history is interesting for all ages and it includes a fabulous lunch in Oscar's! A must for each trip as you get different tidbits of info from each guide. I would do it again.
The ladies in housekeeping were also very caring and friendly. Always stop to say "Have a great day!"
I do not think I could stay anywere else ever again. No other hotel could come close.

title: Upscale and friendly
body: While this is an older building, it has the old world feel.The rooms were quite large. 1101-09 look into the ongoing construction but there was no noise. The staff is extreamly helpful. The breakfast in Oacar's is a great buffet while the price of 43.00 high but a not so bad value in NYC. Three great bars.

title: dont leave valuables in your room
body: hotel is in a great location the rooms are a bit shabby and could do with being up dated.drinks in the mini bar very expensive $8 for small bottle of orange $8 for 7up. the staff were very freindly and polite. the main problem we had with this hotel is that my wife left her handbag in our room we thought it would be safe in a hotel of this quality,how wrong we were her credit and debit cards were stolen and used the hotel said they would look into this not heard anything from them would not go back again there are better hotels in new york

title: ROOM UPGRADE
body: We booked on the hotel website, with the possibly of upgrade at ckeck in $ 69.00 extra each day ti the towers hotel. This worked out really well we were upgraded to a beautiful suite.

title: Timeless Elegance personified. Treated like royalty!
body:
We like to book our final night of vacation at a fancy hotel so that's the lasting impression we take when we return home....and boy did the Waldorf-Astoria in New York City deliver!!
We've been in several of these historic hotels from yester-year and found that although opulent and never lacking in their fine treatment of guests, they tended to have small rooms and lacked modern amenities. 
Not so with the Waldorf. 
We had a lovely suite, complete with king-sized bed, small kitchenette, lots of room to move around, and luxurious decor.
The only thing that was less-than-perfect was the $15.95 charge per day for internet in your room. But many lesser hotels charge the same fee, a small price to pay regardless.
From the time we pulled up in the carport we were treated like royalty!
We checked in too early so they graciously stored our luggage, took our cell number so they could call us when our room became available (which they did within an hour) and then they brought our luggage to our suite and gave us a full explanation of the services available to us.
Every time we entered the hotel someone held the door and greeted us warmly.
You don't have to lift a finger when you stay here. They see to your every need and do so with such grace you can't help but feel valued. Class act every step of the way!
I'd highly recommend staying here, even if only for one night, the impression will last a lifetime and leave you yearning for the dignified days of yore.

title: Disappointing
body: We are currently staying at the Waldorf and I am completely underwhelmed. We received absolutey no notice that the hotel is undergoing refurbishment...meaning we have to enter and exit via a revolting, noisy garage. The bell hops offer no assistance with luggage and more than once have sat back and watch me struggling up stairs with my son's stroller. We are staying in a one bedroom apartment...very tired looking. Whilst I get the old world charm I feel like we are perhaps staying with an eccentric wealthy old aunt...the furnishings are threadbare and the room is very dark..ther are no overhead lights just dim lamps. We have another 3 nights here...I won't be returning. Ps. Despite the huge cost for the room wireless Internet access is not free nor is the gym.

title: Thoroughly enjoyable experience
body:
Hotel staff were friendly and efficient . Rooms were clean and comfortable.
Food and drinks were slightly on the expensive side but you do not get charged for the great atmosphere so well worth it.
Great location for exploring the rest of NY.

title: Not at all what I expected from the "Great Waldorf=Astoria"
body:
I was extremely excited about staying there when we made the reservation. I knew that is was going to be vintage but never in my wildest dreams did I expect that it would due dingy and grungy. For a 5 star hotel I expected 5 star accommodations. However I felt as if I was paying 5 start prices for 2 star dwelling. 
What is it you may wonder? Well let's start with the stains I had on my beautiful white linen which I asked them to change. Then my tub had multiple stains in it, I felt like taking a shower after I took a shower, needless to say I showered in my flip flops. The wall papers were peeling. The light switches were filthy, they were so bad that even though I had wiped them down with lysol wipes I still refused to touch them. So I kept the lights on... well the room was dark so keeping the lights on did in fact come in handy. 
Then there was my bed debacle... my bed was terrible. I woke up with the most terrible back ache as a result of the springs poking me in the back. Called guest service and told them about is they sent up a bed board... AKA sheet of ply. I explained to the "lovely" gentleman that it's not the firmness I have an issue with it's the springs... his reply "We don't have spring beds here at the Waldorf" I looked at him like are you kidding me I'm not going crazy. Anyhow we insisted and they assured me that every room has the same exact bed, purchased in the same time frame, we all then agreed on them bringing us the "newest of the old beds" to swop out the mattress. Then guess what?!?! They showed up with a tempurpedic. I thought to myself didn't they say all the beds were the same. While I am grateful that they finally fixed my issue with the bed I was less than delighted that it took them 7 hours to agree that my issue was valid then another 2hrs to remedy it. Considering I hadn't slept the night before due to discomfort, I was not a happy camper with the time it took to solve my problem. The rest of my week was uneventful however I still had to deal with the below standard level of cleanliness. I counted down the days to my departure, then off to the other hotel (Millennium Hilton) I went, which was amazing.
Would I return? Highly unlikely... My 2 pet peeves are:
1) Cleanliness. I need a clean room period! The decor can be vintage but I will not stand for grungy and dingy
2) Don't make me feel like I'm crazy. If I call to report something I am dissatisfied with,don't try to convince me that my observation isn't so. Listen then try to remedy, that's how it should work. Don't listen and try to convince me that my situation is inaccurate.

title: Hotel of by-gone days
body: When our car arrived in the drive port, we were greeted by friendly porters who tagged our luggage and told us it would be in our room (it was). The front desk was fast, friendly, and arranged for a suite upgrade for very little. Our corner room was spacious, clean, with eight fluffly pillows on the king bed. The towels were soft and the robes a nice touch. The layout is full of small details that most hotels never include and are too numerous to mention. The concierge was very helpful, providing guides to all the attractions. The hotel's location to events made it within walking distance to most venues. However, a cab ride was only $5-7 on average to Times Square or Central Park. We had cocktails in the Bull and Bear, reasonably priced and very comfortable with no waiting. The security here is extremely good and we felt very safe the entire time. The room includes a large safe (we never used ours). Shopping is close with Fifth Avenue less than five minutes by cab. I will forever remember our stay, one of the most pleasant of any hotel in my sixty years of life.

title: Did not live up to, never mind exceed my expectations...
body:
My choice of Hotel was one that I last stayed at in 1975 when working for the company, and after making a booking on Agoda, I wrote a short note on the Hotel's Facebook page to say how much I was looking forward to coming back. After a few hours, they responded saying how happy they were I was returning and looked forward to my visit. 
When I checked in, the Receptionist treated me like "a nobody", did not welcome me back, and gave me a sub-standard corner room. There was no Banana in my room - or even a Welcome back note from the GM. Come to think of it, for the 4 nights I was there, I did not see any Management in the public areas...
My room (1448) had a stale odour, chipped wash basin, one of the blinds did not have a pull string, some walls had torn wall paper, one of the photos over the bed had "a stain" on the glass (I hate to think what that was...), one of the air vents was stained, and I had to pay for Wi-Fi although I'm 100% sure Agoda said it was inclusive.
I was allowed two bottles of House drinking water per day from the automatic mini-bar. On two days, they were not replenished and I had to request them.
One day, I returned to the Hotel after doing some shopping. The cab pulled up at the Hotel entrance and I opened the door in front of the Doorman who was busy counting his tips. To help get out of the cab, I lifted the bags off the back seat on to the ground, in front of the Doorman. Do you think he helped me? Dream on!
I invited a friend for Dinner at the Hotel - in one of their signature restaurants - a steak house. Our so-called Waiter was the most un-attentive individual I have ever encountered. It was like it was such an effort for him to serve us. I heavily discounted his tip!

title: Nice Experience - One Visit Is Probably Enough
body: We booked our trip via BA & got a good deal. We made it clear from the start it was a special treat for our daughter's 18 birthday so "extra little touches" would be appreciated. Prior to our stay I emailed the hotel direct to arrange flowers for the room. The email was acknowledged several days later & forwarded to their in-house florist - heard nothing further......I emailed the Bull & Bear, again in advance to make a restaurant reservation this time it took two attempts from me to get a response, eventually 2 days prior to our arrival, securing a table for our first evening. On arrival check in was not without problems. We did arrive earlier than check in (again I emailed beforehand) our room wasn't ready, we were asked to return in 1hr 15 which we did. The receptionist (same person) told us we had been given incorrect info at our first attempt. We pointed out it was indeed himself who we had seen but he had no recollection.....Eventually we were assured our "nice room" was ready. We entered the "nice room"- yes it was indeed a nice room however on entering a wall light exploded with a loud bang, shattering glass everywhere. I spoke to a housekeeping lady outside who came to look at it - she appeared astonished. I think we saw a further 6 members of staff who all came to survey the broken glass. We were told the room would be cleaned but I insisted we were given a different room. Shards of glass had made it into the bathroom, onto window ledges, carpets, furniture, bed linen - everywhere. It was over an hour until an alternative room was found. We were given a suite (upgrade) however there was a compromise of a camp style bed for our daughter's use, she was OK with that. Our daughter was handed a welcome note with a complimentary breakfast voucher which thrilled her, and a huge piece of birthday cake left in the room for her made her day! Overall a pleasant stay, terrific food and great catering staff. Great housekeeping but for us to have stayed for 4 nights was a lovely treat, we would have no reason to return. Poor comminication via their website and a bit of a 'shambles' at the front desk - not what you would expect really.

title: Resting on its laurels
body: The Waldorf Astoria has a beautiful lobby. The rooms were small and worn. The concierge was a total snob, and I paid 22.00 for a martini in the lobby bar! Guess everybody needs to stay at the Waldorf once in their lives, but once is definitely enough.

title: Great place for my birthday celebration
body: The Waldorf Astoria is my favorite hotel in NYC. It can be pricey, but I have always managed to find a reasonable rate. This last trip was a whim, a quick visit to celebrate my birthday. The service and courtesy of the staff is my favorite thing about the hotel. While checking in, the desk clerk happened to ask what brought us to NYC from Panama and I told her I was celebrating my birthday. She immediately gave us some complimentary coupons, Midway through our stay, I received a note in my room saying the staff hoped I was enjoying my birthday weekend. I will always go back because I love the service and the personal attention.

title: So disappointed
body:
I was so excited to be staying here but what a let down.The concierge watched me arrive by taxi
And no effort was made to assist me up the stairs.
No a seat to be found in the lobby it looks like an Internet office as wifi is free in the lobby
Eventually after a good check in I gave the bell boy $5 to take my luggage up.
My room was lovely but to my horror the wall paper was peeling and the tv didn't work.
I called room service for a kettle and bottled water to the tune of $21.
The breakfast is like a Sunday brunch.
As I am a solo traveller I was seated at an out of the way table to be forgotten about.
Thank goodness I was joining Insight Tours and Gorden the tour leader took over as the information giver and organizer of our luggage to be collected.
All I can say is I've stayed at the Waldolf NYC

title: Elegance and Charm describe this landmark hotel
body: On my many trips to NYC, I've never stayed here, but wanted to. The rooms are more than I usually allocate for hotel expense. AmEx was offering a special rate, and I paid with points. It was truly a first class experience and very centrally located. There was not one staff member that was not expecting to assist in any way possible. In room mini-bar pricing outrageous, even room service was much less for the same item. The lobby as previous reviewers stated is grand, with it's beautiful artwork everywhere, even on the ceilings~truly the epitome of old world charm and elegance. It is a place that everyone needs to say at least once in their lives!

title: Did not live up to expectations
body: We used my husband's Hilton Honor points for a quick mini trip to NYC with our twin ten-year old boys. I wish we had chosen another hotel. I am a bit of a hotel snob, so I was hoping the experience would be a treat for my "non-hotel snob" husband and boys. The Waldorf is grand and old, but just visiting the lobby or eating at one of its high-priced eating venues would have fulfilled my need to experience this old dame of a hotel. The rooms are small and old. The beds were comfortable, but also small. One other reviewer compared their stay to visiting an old aunt's home - antiquated, peeling wallpaper, etc. There is also construction taking place on the Park Ave. side and one of my son's wanted to point out that our room had a terrible view and the tv did not work well. The staff was friendly enough, but the lobby was hectic and every seat occupied (mostly by people taking advantage of the free wi fi in the lobby). With so many fantastic hotel choices in NYC, next time we will stay elsewhere.

title: The best!
body:
Stayed in a suite, best room i have booked! Couldn't fault anything!
If anyone faults this hotel they have a problem! :)

title: The Worst Experience in a "luxury" Hotel
body:
My First Wedding Anniversary and I decided to Splurge in a nice Hotel in New York so The Reputation of the Waldorf Astoria Was Great Right? WRONG I felt that I just loose my Money First the System was Blocked So we Could not check in We Have to Wait for about 3 Hours in the Lobby! when the room was Ready OMG what a shame of hotel LUXURY room If I Were the hotel Manager I just can´t let this Rooms Offered. the Closet Looks loke the one in a MOTEL and the Bathroom is the Worst Really the Worst I´ve Ever Seen Tiny, Old, Terrible it was Depressing.
Look the Photos and Tell me what you think

title: Lively lobby but no honey
body:
Recently stayed at the Waldorf - superior room. Con's - Park Avenue renovation is a major inconvenience that somehow slipped any kind of notification that the west end of the hotel is under siege. The Lexington Avenue entrance is a joke. Since the Starbucks was on the Park 
Ave entrance - the morning coffee we had go down the street to the Radisson for the grande blast. 
Given the recent story about having bees on the top of the hotel it would be nice if the honey was available in the gift store. It was not. Another gripe was the hotels pick of newpaper - nothing says New York more than USA Today. WSJ or NYT please. Maybe we could see more positive new stories about the Waldorf besides the notion that they want their stuff back - amnesty. Given the size of hotel it is astonishing that a hotel of this caliber does not have a world class pool. If the Waldorf had pool facilities - it would smoke the Plaza, Four Seasons, Plaza and St. Regis in short order.
PROS - Once again proximity to 51st metro, 53st metro lines, Grand Central Terminal and a few stone throws from Times Square is a plus. It is close to 3rd ave for eateries, close to Hammacher Schlemmer E57 for gadgets. Breakfast at the Brasserie on East 53 is outstanding. 
Sour cherry baklava at Gulluglu on 3rd ave. The highlight of the Waldorf Astoria is the lobby it has life! like Grand Central Terminal.

title: Not as good as i should be!
body: This hotel must be one of the most over priced hotel in the world! We payed 657 USD/Night for a out dated rather small twin bed room without breakfast. One thing is for sure, I will absoluteley never ever come back! PS: The lobby was rather nice!

title: Very good, great Priceline.com rate ... costly breakfast
body: Hey, the Waldorf is still one of the best hotels in NYC. Great location, great shops and restaurants. I travel to NYC a great deal for business and I always look for different places to stay in midtown. This time, I decided to try the Waldorf. I was lucky enough to get a great rate through priceline at $199/night which is a significant discount from the regular rate of $500-$600/night. The hotel is going through some exterior renovations, but inside its still wonderful. The only complaint, if you can call it that, is the cost of breakfast. Expect a breakfast consisting of eggs, toast, english muffin, coffee and juice to cost $55.

title: Do yourself a favor and stay here!
body: Words cannot express how our stay went while we were in New York City at The Waldorf=Astoria. It was one of the best times we have had, and it all started at the front desk check-in. We were upgraded to a Junior Suite for our 15 year anniversary(we cannot thank you enough). Everyone of the staff were so kind and welcoming everyday of our 8 day stay there. We had a 2 room suite with 2 bathrooms and 2 walk-in closets. They have bathrobes and umbrellas in the room for you to use. Plus, the beds are the most comfortable ones you can get! We had the best nights sleeps at any hotel we have ever been to. The location is unbeatable, no matter where you want to go in the city you can get there easily by walking from here. Or, if you have one of the bus tours they stop right outside, so that is another added touch. But, I truly recommend walking and enjoying this beautiful city. This is an amazing establishment and everyone who works there seems to love the place too. It is a historical, classic New York City hotel at it's best. Thank you to all the staff here. This is a wonderful experience, don't miss out on your trip to NYC!

title: Be pampered
body:
This hotel pampers. But only for the ones who have bucks to burn. The bed is (sigh!!!) sheer heaven. I love the SALVATORRE FEREGAMO toiletries !!!!! And crystals and all the glamorous touches in our room. David of the front desk is a darling and everyone makes you feel like royalty. 
Hubby was happy we made an excellent choice. Walk the lobby and feel like royalty.

title: Love the hotel but not without breakfast
body:
We stayed for a week at this lovely hotel on a bed only basis mid June. The bedroom was v spacious as a deluxe king size. The extractor didn't work in the bathroom, so if you wash something it didnt dry. The bath plug needed to be changed which they did. It's an amazing and busy place, others have written of the wonderful lobby and lifts, wide halls. Our stay coincided with a heatwave, may be more extreme than usual and with high near 100% humidity levels outside. The hotel has a super efficient v cold aircon in it's common areas, the room thankfully can be adjusted, in our case we turned it off and opened the windows overnight. In most of NY the heatwave had the effect of buildings lowering the aircon temp to what felt like freezing. It is prudent to take layers to wear at this time within the hotel and outside.
One of the things that didn't help is not having breakfast included, no tea making facility. It is a good idea to bring a travel kettle. The areas to go to find a breakfast, seemed longer and harder in the heatwave and humidity, sometimes it became brunch. I ended up with an airways infection and fever later in the week.
On a positive note, we loved the hotel, the history, but it needs to have the basic amenities too.

title: Family Trip
body: There cannot be a better place to stay than The Waldorf-Astoria when in New York City! The price you pay is definitely worth it; the staff is the best I've ever encountered and the rooms are impeccable. Will definitely stay again and again!

title: Grand old hotel
body:
So I just got back from 2 nights at the Waldorf and I have to say for an old hotel it still has some moves. 
My room was clean, and well taken care of. No dirt or dust at all as to be expected with a hotel of this sort. Other reviews had said that things were crumbling or had just seemed old but I didn't experience any of that. Everything was in ship shape. The lobby is amazing. Overall a very beautiful hotel. There was some construction going on the outside but it in no way impacted our visit. No noise or real disruption. 
The staff were super friendly and helpful. They did a great job but room service in terms of bringing bags up to our room was quite slow. 
It was very centrally located and getting around New York was very easy. Also we had a fantastic view of the Chrysler building. 
One big let down was no free wifi. Come on it's 2012. It was nice that each room had it's own router, but when you're staying at a hotel of it's reputation, level of service and price it just seems cheap to nickel and dime people for wifi especially when there's free wifi in the lobby.

title: Overrated
body:
The Waldorf Astoria lives off its name. The rooms are quite rundown and in need of serious TLC.
The main foyer / reception area looks great with the clock and all that, but you'd probably be better off staying in a "normal" hotel and having a better quality room and saner pricing.
Breakfast in the hotel's restaurant, for example, costs as much as you'd expect to pay for dinner in a good restaurant and is mediocre.
You can get a more economical breakfast in the Starbucks on the ground floor.
All in all I won't be returning.

title: Very tired!
body:
The lobby was very elegant and check-in efficient. We went with friends - 2 families. Our rooms were so dreadful to start with (dingy, old and stale), that we went straight down to reception to complain. The receptionist was amazing and managed to move both families, although the hotel was very busy. Our upgrade was to a small suite with a sitting area and 2 bathrooms. The bathrooms were very small and old with incredibly dusty vents - as long as you didn't look up it was ok! The room was old, and the dust behind the bed and bedside cabinet was amazing! But the sheets were clean and white and we were satisfied. Our friends had a different experience moving 3 times, but eventually ending up in the Towers - huge apartment with silk wall paper! Breakfast was the only meal we had in the hotel and we only did that once as the price was staggering - we were silly not to check prices beforehand, but you get charged for orange juice that they just pour for you, pay for coffee separately etc - nothing is included except if you have the continental breakfast! 
The lobby is very grand and the location is great. We also used the gym, which was very well equipped. If you want old and grand then this is great, but it is old!

title: Walled-off Astoria
body: Just stayed at this hotel, the third time in my life and probably my last. Arriving at the hotel I discovered that the hotel's main entrance on Park Avenue has been walled off, a fact not disclosed anywhere on the the hotel's website. But that physical appearance,due to ongoing construction faithfully symbolizes what is going on inside this property. The guest feels unwelcomed and shunned. The Front Desk staff is robotic even when feigning joy as they "congratulate" you on the important occasion that brings you to the Big Apple. The Concierges show complete apathy, disdain and ineptitude when making recommendations. The Lobby bar staff shoos you away if you dare step into their domain within 30 minutes of closing (1 am on a Saturday!). When criticized about this, the bar host cited "a NY law that requires the bar to stop serving customers 30 minutes before the bar closes." The housekeepers sound like a stampede as they start their day apparently gossiping aloud at an ungodly early hour in the hallway's supply room. No need for an wake-up call here. The physical plant is sorely outdated and unkept, albeit clean. The buttons on the antique room phones and remote controls have even lost their spring. The rooms smell musty and the a/c is sorely inadequate in the peak summer heat. Overall, stay away feom this hotel until further notice unless you want to feel walled off in the Astoria.

title: A Grand Historic Hotel ! Classic New York !
body:
I have been staying at the Waldorf Astoria for many years when I am in New York.
The Waldorf Astoria is a grand historic landmark - opened in 1931. The Waldorf Astoria is New York at its very best. The history that this hotel represents is legendary - as it has been the center of New York Society & Business for generations. The Hotel is huge, over 1,000 rooms & about 45 stories.
The Waldorf is located in mid-town Manhattan in a very nice & very centrally located area of the city - a great location to serve a " base " while in New York. Located only a few city blocks from Grand Central Station.
Overall - the rooms are great & the service is excellent. 
Restaurants - several wonderfull restaurants on site. My favorite is the Bull & Bear Steak House on the lower level. The Bull & Bear is a classic & classy New York Steakhouse - very expensive, but well worth it. Business casual dress is an absolute must.
The rooms do vary in size - the rates clearly reflect the size & location of the rooms. My advice, do your homework & ask specific questions about the rooms when booking a reservation. If possible, try to get a room on the upper floors, better views & less noise ( from the streets ).
The service, historically, has been superb - as you would expect from staying at a historic luxury hotel.
Recommendation - check out the various online reservation sites when making a reservation. There are many special packages that are often available, especially special weekend rate packages. Remember, it is New York, do your homework ! The rack rates are very expensive, but if you do your homework, you can save a considerable amount of money.

title: Honeymoon Location
body:
We had a fantastic time on our honeymoon at the Waldorf Astoria. The staff catered for our every need. The location of the hotel was brilliant. Our room was very clean and comfortable. Would certainly recommend to others.
Our only negative was that we booked into the hotel during its restoration process. Would have been nice to view the hotel in all its glory, never the less, we heard no noise from the workers.

title: As infamous as its Salad
body: Just had a weeks stay at the Waldorf and I have to say it lived up to my expectations, yes there is work going on to the main entrance however access is just as easy from the Lexington Avenue entrance with accessibility to most area's not hindered due to this restoration. I have to mention that the rooms are a little tired and maybe a subtle upgrading might not go a miss however the rooms are still very clean and everything that you might need for a stay is to hand. The Waldorf's location is second to none and found that with its central location all the shopping area's and sights of interest are within easy reach and walking distance (make sure you have a comfy pair of walking shoes). All the staff seemed very helpful when asked a question and all to happy to help in anyway they could, all in all a very pleasurable stay.

title: The myth is busted!
body: After 6 months of planning and looking forward to staying at the fabled Waldorf Astoria we were very disappointed in the place. The front entrance was a no go zone due to reconstruction, meaning we had to use the tradesmens entrance in 100 degree heat. The queue for check in rivalled the airport. After a whole day of delays across the country and arriving at 1am the concierge tells me my room isnt ready! At least they shouted me a drink. For the money I think i would stay somewhere else!

title: Fantastic
body: Celebrated my 40th birthday with 5 nights in the Waldorf Astoria and it did not disappoint. With ourselves and another couple travelling, we had two excellent rooms. Staff very friendly, everyone speaks, good morning etc. Ensure you treat yourself to breakfast at the Peacock Alley restaurant or a beer at the Bull and Bear, both excellent, although pricey. My only regret is that we did not do the Waldorf Astoria Hotel Tour to take in all the sights, although on our last day I did get a sneak look at the Grand Ball Room on Floor 3. Even though we are from the UK, are have an interest in American history and the walls are adorned of black and white photos of Presidents, Kings and uens who have stayed at thh Waldorf. Also, you see hotos of famous actors attending gala dinners there etc. The place is stepped in history......Brilliant, will go back some day.

title: I'd like a John Daniel's....(Pacino)
body: Ever since seeing Scent of a Woman I have wanted to go to e Waldorf and order a John Daniels at the bar. I finally got around to it and, despite the $17.42 price for a single JD, it was superb. The hotel is quite nice and my room spacious. I was a bit put off by the cashed up bogans in the foyer but I think that they were probably more sticky-beakers, rather than actual guests of the hotel. Service was swift, room was spotless, concierge aloof but ok. All in all, I have always wanted to stay here and I finally got around to it. Would definitely go back and would recommend. Even though my room was a cheaper room, it had a great view of Park Ave. loved it. Also if you do stay there, there is free postage for hotel guests in their business centre up to a pound a parcel. I sent 8 parcels home. Giddy up.

title: Great experience
body:
We stayed here for a week in April and loved the hotel. Some of the reviews say that it isn't up to the same standard as hotels that are of an equivalent cost and are typically more modern. If you expect white modern rooms with gadgets everywhere you will be upset. However if you want a room with character and old-school style you're in the right place.
The room, and hotel in general, were very clean and service was impeccable. On the first day I wanted to change up a large sum of higher valued USD bills into smaller bills. I was expecting this to be an issue but reception were more than happy to do so which involved collating the money out of multiple tills. In addition, having booked a king size double room and only having a queen size available on arrival, we spent the first night in it, decided that it was big enough and the lady on reception compensated us with vouchers for the Starbucks and cocktail bar....a very nice touch that a lot of hotels wouldn't bother with.
The only gripe was the lack of free wifi / internet in the room. However, this gave a perfect excuse to go and sit downstairs in the lobby or corridors and check Facebook in a luxurious environment. Besides - you're in New York, do you really need to spend your days online?!
We would definitely return as the hotel was a great base to explore the city from and the room was lovely in it's own style. One last thing - we were very impressed by the taxi attendant on the last busy day when we were trying to get a ride to the airport, someone attempted to jump the queue handing him a large bill as a 'bribe', he didn't even look at the note's value when telling him to get to the back of the line :-)
Top tip - the corridor by the gift shop always has seats free to use the free wifi.

title: disappointing
body: staff friendly but expect all of the inefficiencies of a large institution....calls for customer assistance on hold for 5 minutes each time; A/C broken in our suite, wait in line for concierge....stuff you might expect with a discount hotel. Probably won't be back.

title: Perfect for first visit to New York
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf for four nights with our two young children and it did not disappoint. Having read reviews about the lengthy check-in I was worried about what would await us (in the extreme heat and with two tired children) but it was quick and easy with very helpful staff. It was a shame not to see the hotel in all its glory as the scaffolding was still there in places but you can easily access the hotel from Lexington and 49th Street, and it was no problem with a pushchair. 
The hotel is perfectly located for walking to Fifth Avenue, Madison Ave, Central Park, Union Station, Empire State Building, Bryant Park etc, great for sightseeing as it was our first time in New York as a family. Our room was big and spotlessly clean - the decor was perhaps a little dated but to me it was part of the hotel's charm, you are staying in a piece of history! If you want modern then stay at the W across the street. The only negative was that the aircon was noisy and with the temperature at 38 degrees outside we had to have it on. It is worth taking time to wander around the hotel - the decor is beautiful and very 'of the era', plus there are interesting photos on the walls of famous guests. Also take a look in the Grand Ballroom on the 3rd floor, it is spectacular! 
All in all a great experience and I would definitely recommend it.

title: mixed feelings : very good hotel , but booking system needs to be improved.
body: When we arrived at the hotel , we were very disapponited : we reserved a mini suite (6 months in advance and prepaid!) , but there was no mini suite available , so we had to accept a downgrade to a normal room for the first night. This should not happen in a Waldorf! However , for the remaining nights we got an upgrade to a suite on the 23rd floor. That was really great. So , the service given by the reception desk (thanks Cedric!!) was very very good.

title: Great location but ........
body:
Great location and some of the staff were great--liked Gwen the bartender!!!!
We had a couple of experiences that gave us the impression that some of the staff were not "customer focused" and condescending.
I always wanted to stay at the New York Waldorf Astoria but at the end of my two week long vacation, this hotel which I thought would be a grand finale was a fizzle.

title: Wonderful Hotel
body: We loved it here! Everyone was so nice and very friendly and helpful. Our room was beautiful. We loved the lobby. I only wish we could have stayed longer! Check in and check out was smooth and quick. Very organized. We were really happy with our stay here.

title: Great stay!
body: I had a wonderful stay at the Waldorf=Astoria this past weekend! I was concerned about many of the reviews recently written, but was very pleased with my stay. Yes, the Park Ave lobby area is under contruction so that was a minor issue, but it was very easy to find the main lobby for check in. Beautiful lobby and excellent service at check-in. The room was clean and very comfortable. Had a little difficulty managing the temperature control in the room. No matter what temp I put the air conditioner on, the air stayed the same temp. So, at night, I just turned off the air and was fine. All in all, it was a wonderful stay, and I certainly would not hesitate to go back for another weekend at the Waldolf.

title: Quiet glamour in the heart of the city
body: I stayed at the Waldorf for a few nights. The room and common areas were all very quiet and clean and comfortable. I really enjoyed my stay. The staff was very nice, all-smiles, making for a great place to stay.

title: Nice but won't stay again
body: My husband travels for work and is a "Hilton" guy so 2 of our 3 nights were paid for with points, which is why we stayed here. The staff was wonderful to us and very helpful. The lobby is beautiful and the room was "nice" in a historic way and was clean and in functioning order. However, our tastes are a bit more modern so it wasn't really our style. Also, my biggest complaint (though probably wouldn't matter to some) was that there was no coffee maker in the room. There was also no place to get coffee that you could bring back up to your room in the entire building. From what I understand, there is usually a Starbucks in the building but it was unavailable due to the renovations currently going on. I thought because of this they should have provided coffee in the lobby. Instead, everyone had to walk a block over to the Starbucks down the street. This was a pretty big deal to a caffeine addict like myself.

title: WORTH EVERY PENNY !!!
body: Stayed here in July , had booked a small suite but on arrival we were upgraded to an executive suite .WOW. It was fantastic , massive and immaculate . The staff were lovely , tip your maid on arrival and she will leave tons of extra towels , toiletries etc . Reception is busy but they have lots of desks and we never waited more than a few minutes . Eating in the hotel is expensive but the food is superb , you have to do it even just for the memory . Gift shop in hotel was really nice and classy and cheaper than the rubbish in the tourist areas . Buy your snacks and drinks in there to as it is cheaper than surrounding shops and mini bar . I have been to NYC six times but nothing compares to our trip to the Waldorf . AMAZING !

title: Awesome Experience
body:
My wife and I stayed here on our honeymoon this summer. Overall the Waldorf Astoria was awesome! We booked our room on Priceline, doing the negotiator thing, and got a room for $150 a night, for five nights. We figured since we did one of these deal things we'd get the smallest, least expensive room they had. Instead when we were checking in the person working there asked why we were in New York. We told him it was our honeymoon and he responded by saying that he would make sure we got a nice room to make our stay even more memorable. He got us a suite with king size bed, large sitting area, and two bathrooms. The room was huge and very nice! We couldn't believe it.
Everything else about our stay was also wonderful. All the staff people we dealt with were great. The room was clean and very comfortable. I will agree with some other people who have left reviews that in some places it is showing its age but this in no way took away from our experience. It was such a cool place to stay. My wife and I debated about which hotel to stay at in New York and we were both so happy we went with this one. It was incredible!

title: Couldn't be better
body: I should start by saying we were quite lucky right in the beginning of our stay since we were part of a very large group and were given a terrible room (no view and plenty of noise coming from an unknown source, probably some equipment in the Spa, which we were right next to) - the lucky part is a couple within the group didn't travel and we were given his (much better) room, otherwise I feel the great experience we had would have been terrible because the hotel was packed and there seemed to be no other available! With this solved we could start enjoying all the great things the Waldorf has to offer, from great service (the consierge was tremendously helpful during all our stay) to an out of this world breakfast. Free wi-fi in the lobby is a plus, as were the wonderful cocktails at the bars, however be prepared to pay A LOT for said drinks. We hope to return soon!

title: Honey, I m home!!
body: It is all about the people. I have had the pleasure to spend lots of time at my NYC home. After all, it is the Waldorf. Charm at every turn,property and people wise. I love, love, love walking through the door and I feel as if it is my home. Big smiles, the team wanting to know where I am and truly are. AC isn't t perfect, beds are great, cocktails are great at peacock alley(ask for Crystal(mgr), Austin or babu. The best! It all centers around Jackie, Mary, gena, rebbekah, Agnes, servando, michael, George and many others many others. Consider yourself the luckiest person ever, if you end up here...kudos to Eric long for having the best ever team!

title: We loved it!
body:
We came to NYC the weekend before the July 4th holiday to enjoy the city for a few days until we took the train out to the Hamptons. Enjoyed dining Saturday night and then Sunday brunch and a matinee around Columbus Circle and Central Park. We opted to take cabs everywhere - always easy for the doorman to catch one for us (but is wasn't raining). But, time before we used the subway, which is very convenient.
We arrived a bit early and went to the main Waldorf Astoria lobby to check-in. The Tower check-in is lovely, but tip... it is on street level where the cab or shuttle drops you off. But instead of making us go back downstairs, the very nice desk clerk called down and worked out a great deal for us - we were upgraded to a slightly larger king bedroom overlooking the cathedral. I am a Hilton Honors member and we have stayed at the Waldorf on a previous trip. I think they do like to reward return guests. It was worth the slight splurge to book the concierge level king - see booking tip below.
Our room was very spacious and on a higher floor, the bed and pillows plush with nice linens. A light bulb was out in the closet when we arrived, but we let the Tower desk know on our way out that evening and when we returned, the light bulb had been changed. 
We enjoyed a nice snack of sliders and wine in the main lobby at the Peacock Room? when we arrived (opting not to go outside on an adventure). We were hungry - although pricey at $75 for 3 glasses of wine and a shared slider tray, the french fries were beautifully prepared (appreciated by my chef husband). It was a great location to people watch - my husband swears he saw Scarlett Johansen walk through the lobby while I visited with 1 of 3 concierge available to make a quick dinner and brunch reservation.
After our late snack, I stopped off at the Geurlain? spa in the Tower section and they worked with our schedule to fit us in that afternoon. My husband had a massage and I tried the reflexology therapy. We were given wine and an apricot nut mix while we waited for our scheduled appointment in a quiet lounge area. The robe is a one size fits most... my husband is a larger man (did I mention he is a chef?) and it was a tight fit for him. But they were generious with the wine so he really didn't care too much about the robe!
Everyone was very friendly and helpful - bellman, doormen, desk staff... Didn't really see maid service, but we had nightly turn-down and the room was very clean and nicely appointed. Lots of towels for just 2 people.
Only disappointment was that the main entrance from Park Avenue was closed for renovation, which cut off access to the terrace lounge. If you've never been there, you would not have known construction was on going from the inside or that a part of the hotel was closed off. Although it's only for a few months, I really missed walking through their grand entrance. Summertime in New York and every building seemed to have scaffolding and construction work going on.
We loved it!

title: Luxury hotel in NY
body: Absolutely fantastic hotel. Great location. Incredible facilities and service. Free wi-fi in the reception area. Staff most helpful and courteous, always there if needed but in no way intrusive. Wish I could afford to stay there every year. Has spoiled New York for me, because I will never be able to visit again without staying there!

title: Didn't want to leave!
body: My husband and I were in Manhattan in June 2012 for 4 days on a combination business/vacation trip, and had a GREAT experience at the Waldorf Astoria! During our entire stay, everyone on the hotel staff, from the doormen, to the bell staff, to the front desk staff, the restaurant servers and especially housekeeping, were incredibly friendly, professional, knowledgeable and accommodating! We loved it! There was a slight mishap with our room assignment when we checked in (they gave us a room that was already occupied by other travelers - oops!), so they immediately more than made up for it by upgrading us to a corner suite with an incredible view of the NYC skyline, including the Chrysler building and East River. It was amazing! In addition, the 24 hour room service menu was extensive and all of the food was delicious and delivered to our room exactly as ordered and within the time frame promised. Their restaurants and bars were also wonderful, and the hotel tour was incredibly interesting! Last year, we stayed in the Waldorf Towers, which were also luxurious, and where we likewise had incredible views and even a private balcony! We can't wait to go back!

title: beautiful old hotel
body: Very beautiful, most helpful concierge, convenient to the theatre district, Times Square, 5th Ave and Central Park. We will definitely stay here next time we visit NYC. The place is very kid-friendly, many places to eat around the hotel. We especially liked Ashland Alley.

title: I missed something ...
body: Because I honestly don't love this hotel ... and realize that most folks do. It's old and, honestly, I felt like I needed to be about 20 years older to stay there based on the folks hanging around the lobby. I also had this strange room that maybe used to be an apartment ... I could never totally figure it out. That said, it was super clean and comfy but could use some refreshing (smelled kinda closed up). Beware of the drain in the shower (at least in my room) as it is this massive hole and I lost two things down into it ... things I wouldn't lose in a normal hotel bathroom, like a razor. The staff is nice enough and absolutely gets high marks for being super attentive.

title: EXCELLENT EXCELLENT EXCELLENT !
body: My fiance and I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for 4 nights at the end of july and it was without a doubt the most beautiful hotel we've ever stayed in. The location is great, walking distance to everything. The staff is very friendly and the room service is impeccable. If I could give it more than a five star I would. The lobby is beautiful as well as very secure, you need your hotel key to have access to the elevators after 6 p.m. which I found comforting. Everybody in this hotel is friendly. It is a pure joy and makes New York an even better city ! Will definitely be staying here again on our next trip. Worth every penny.

title: Excellent Location -- Great Prices
body: When I booked this trip for my 14-year-old daughter and myself, I looked into competitively priced hotels. When I saw that the Waldorf Astoria was consistent with and even better than moderately-priced hotels, I didn't hesitate in booking it -- I wanted to brag that I stayed at The Waldorf! We were not disappointed -- upon check-in (we were a little early), they didn't have any of the queen bed rooms we we reserved, so they upgraded us to a king. My husband and I stayed in NY when we were younger and on a more limited budget and had a room we couldn't both walk in at the same time -- this room was fabulous -- the bathroom excellent. We didn't splurge on any of the restaurants on site -- they looked very fancy for a teenager and I, but the location was very close to everything we wanted to see: Rockefeller Center was a short walk, not to mention great shopping, Times Square, etc. Very pleased with our stay and the staff was excellent!

title: Charming?........Not to be confused with Very Tired and Worn
body: Stayed at the Waldorf for 2 nights with my son. A number of reviewers keep saying is the Waldorf, history, charm etc, and they are right, it is the Waldorf and my image of it before going was one of luxury and cleanliness. The first impression of the hotel is nice lobby although there was a damp smell (the main entrance is currently undergoing refurbishment which was a bit of a shame as we would liked to have seen it). We were allocated a room on the 21st floor by a very helpful clerk at the check-in desk, we arrived about 2pm but couldn't check in until 3pm, The clerk gave us directions to Bloomingdales and off we went, leaving our cases with the Concierge which was a bonus. Upon our return, we went to our floor (via a very fast elevator), the corridor also had that 'smell' and upon opening our room door the smell was overwhelming, a damp sort of odour covered by lots of 'shake'n'vac'. The room was dull and had a very small seating area (I had upgraded to a suite) with very worn furniture crammed into every space, the bedroom had two double beds it, the one thing I love about hotel beds is the crisp white linen, the linen on the bed looked and felt that it had been washed so many times it was ready for the rag bag. The light shade had holes in it and the furniture was so chipped that we thought someone previously occupying the room was a budding carpenter. The room didn't meet my expectation of cleanliness and my image of what the Waldorf Astoria would be - I was very disappointed as was my son as I had built this up to be a luxury hotel. I returned to the front desk to advise that I was not happy with the room and was given another room by another helpful clerk on the 14th floor. This room was also a 'suite' and consisted of 2 beds (same quality of linen) and another room which appeared to be more of a big walk in closet with a chair at the dressing table and another chair (again the room smelled as did the furniture). The bathroom would I am sure have been nice in its day however it wasn't the cleanest with marks in the bath. The toilet was in a recess in the bathroom which was a bit odd with double doors (broken at the top and bottom). There are cheap plastic blinds on the windows which were very dirty with finger marks of people putting them up and down. Overall this room was slightly better than the previous one but again didn't meet my image of the hotel. The clerk did phone and I did tell her it was a bit better, I did not want to go through changing rooms again given that we were only there for 2 nights. Maybe this is the accepted standard of room in New York for the price (we paid £250 per night). I think some reviewers are getting confusing charming with tired, worn and smelly.
