There is history in this hotel which I like but it doesn't let Hilton away with not spending money on the accommodation where the ordinary traveller stays. Overall, not a great hotel experience of a hotel promoting luxury and certainly not worth the upgrade (although relatively cheap - the pictures on the website make it look better than it actually is) of what was a special holiday for my son and I. I would say that the staff were were very nice and professional and are a credit to a hotel which is of a poor standard.

title: Excellent stay at Waldorf
body: We rented three rooms at the Waldorf Astoria. Everything from the staff, to room service, to the restaurant was excellent. My granddaughter's complaint when we got home was that her bed mattress was not as comfortable as the Waldorf's. Everything was spotless. You would never know that this hotel is over 100 years old.

title: Jewel that needs a little polish
body: This is one of great hotels of American maybe the world. However, she seems a bit tired these days. We had a suite in which we checked in around 1 pm. The front desk said they would call us. Appreciate the idea. As of 5:30 we still did not receive a call. Back to the front desk, room was still not ready. Staff said room would be ready in 20 to 30 mins. Gave us free tickets to the bar. One adult and two kids.....one of us was happy with that. 45 Minutes later ....back at the front desk room no ready....One adult really not happy as we had dinner reservations at 8 pm in Little Italy. That got us breakfast buffet...eh....appreciated the effort. The suite living room was a very nice size...put a very comfortable cot in that room (for one adult) Bathrooms are not what I expected for such a upscale hotel. Pluses are comfty beds, large closet, nice size rooms for NYC, Starbucks down stairs, but best of all is location, location, location. A couple of blocks from subway, Grand Central, Grey Line bus tour, 30 Rock, Times Square and Broadway. Love that

title: Awesome Mother/Daughter Experience!!
body: What a once in a lifetime experience I was blessed to share with my daughter for her 21st birthday! As soon as we stepped into the luxurious lobby of the Waldorf Astoria, we were treated like royalty! We stayed 6 nights in a King Mini Suite on the 16th floor and I must say, it was worth every penney! The bed was so very comfortable and the bathroom was very adaquate in size - and spotless!! The suite also consisted of a roomy living area and small kitchen with sink and refridgerator. I can't say enough praises and thanks to our bellman, Mohammed. We are so blessed to have known him. Our first night in NY, he gave us an amazing and informative tour of the historic Waldorf (the ballroom is fantastic!) AND even a small tour of NY after he got off work! In fact, all employees at the Waldorf were fantastic, helpful, courteous, friendly, and gracious! Staying at the Waldorf was such a wonderful and memorable experience that I, nor my daughter, will ever forget the time we spent there! Without a doubt, NY should be proud to have such an iconic, beautiful, luxurious, and historic hotel!

title: surprisingly good value, but skip the restaurant
body: Stayed at the Waldorf Astoria in midtown manhattan earlier this week. This is an old hotel and it shows its age in many ways. Nonetheless, rooms are reasonably spacious and the hallways are wide and well lit, feel safer and less "closed in" than many hotels. Bedding probably needs to be replaced, it has seen better days. It was actually the best priced upper tier chain hotel in midtown when I looked (about $339 per nite, compared with over $500 for others in area).Lots of construction on the facade, which made for zero views outside windows, and a bit of inconvenience because they closed off park ave entrance. Terrific lobby, although the newstand could be better placed with better signage. Good for business travellers on east side of midtown, I imagine that tourists who want proximity to Times Square area (which I avoid like the plague) would probably want to be closer. Worst experience was the lobby restaurant: wildly overpriced for breakfast, it doesn't open until 7 am, poor (indifferent) service, and I waited over 25 minutes for eggs (after asking waiter 3 times for help) before getting exasperated and walking out. I should have known better. Didn't see starbucks across the street, or I would have gone there to begin with.

title: Old or historical?
body:
The hall of the hotel is defitenetly historical, the room was old. First issue at check-in. I booked on their website a room of 450-600 squared feet for $ 199. It was probably an error, but that's what they sold me. At check-in they did not want to give me a room of that size, but a standard room. After some "negotiation" they offer me a discount of $ 100... everybody happy!
the room was old and badly maintaned. few details to give an idea: nails of the previous guests on the carpet, laundry bag being recycled, bath tube in orrible condition all broken. It was clearly repainted, but probably with the wrong paint that had progressively gone away with the water. The point is that it does not happen in a day but over a period of time. Housekeeping has never reported or maintenance never did the job. 
Be careful also on the extra, because all services are charged and they are also expensive. no coffee machine in the room and never few toilet amenities. 
Overall the room was lacking a proper care. the room is old, but it could have been cleaned better.

title: Loved the Waldorf!
body: We booked three rooms at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC for a girls getaway and were so glad we did! The ambiance from the moment you walk in is incredible, and the lobby is as majestic as it looks in photos. Tthe customer service was wonderful from the check in, to the concierge, to the bellman, to room service etc. If we required something extra in our room, they were so eager to please and quick to accommodate. The rooms were really lovely and spacious for NYC. The room we were in had a nice sized lighted closet which doubled as a "dressing room" when the bathroom was in use - with four of us in each room. The bathroom was bright, very clean, spacious and pretty. Two of our rooms overlooked Park Avenue and the third Lexington Ave. The views weren't anything spectacular but classic NY street views I guess. Also there is currently some construction going on outside the building which isn't the most attractive, but it really didn't affect our stay in any way. There is a well stocked bar fridge in each room but it was so pricey that no one from our group decided to partake. We did lots of walking - to Times Square, Central Park, Bryant Park, 5th Avenue etc. and the hotel is nicely situated to be a comfortable walk yet not in the heart of Times Square. There are a couple of choices of restaurant/bars in the hotel which is kind of nice to wind down an evening - again a tad expensive, but then most NYC restaurants are like this. In short, I would highly recommend the Waldorf NYC to anyone who wants to soak up a little classic and historic NYC. It's an icon afterall!

title: From check in to check out...
body: ...flawless. I was expecting a pleasant stay, and in a historic hotel, but after reading other reviews I was lead to believe my surroundings would be dated and the accommodations marginal at best...not true. Everybody has their own definition of perfection, and honesty this landmark, nestled in an ideal location on Park Avenue in walking distance of nearly everything, is mine. From congenial employees to amazing deserts to a spacious comfortable room it just can't get any better. I simply can not get over how friendly the staff was...I mean every-single-person (including a couple of guys laboring in the hallway). And the bed slept so well my girlfriend wanted to pack it up in our suitcase. Now mind you I was a sales manager for the Ritz Carlton for a short time, and I have experienced a few of the best hotels in the world...So this review does not come lightly. A perfect launch point for my favorite Andrew Lloyd Webber musical...and no phantoms in here. Bravo!

title: Wasn't terribly disappointed, but not as good as expected
body: You can tell the hotel was once something special, but Hilton has really let it slip; especially considering what they're charging. Staff was excellent, but the rooms are ancient - I felt like I was visiting my grandparents house. Hilton desperately needs to pony up and gut the rooms.

title: Puttin' on the Ritz / Luxury / Boring for the Young
body:
Let's face it: the Waldorf-Astoria is one of the most famous hotels in the world...and once of the priciest. I normally could not afford a hotel like this, but I stayed here in the off-season in late January, and got a great rate.
Staying here is an experience: you see the richest folk not only from America, but from around the world. I walked in with my t-shirt and torn jeans just to annoy them, lol.
Whatever you need, whatever you want....you can get here through its 5-star service. It's beautiful and historic. I like the small touches: you find first edition book from the 19th century in the rooms. 
However, it's boring if you're young (like me), and don't expect to meet anyone of our age group here.
Otherwise, stay here if you can afford it, and experience true luxury. It's just like the lyrics of that song, "Puttin' on the Ritz."

title: In spite of the ongoing renovations this was a great hotel
body: I have tried so many of the different hotels of Manhattan that at one time I gave up on them and started to rent a flat for a few days whenever I was in NY. After all it is a place to sleep. The City has so much to do that I cannot imagine staying in my room. But I also do not want to be sleeping in a tiny, old, tired, noisy room either. So when they had a special because of the renovations going on, I jumped on the opportunity and booked it for my 3 night stay. I must admit I was pleasantly surprised. With the exception of not being able to use the Park Ave. entrance, the ongoing renovations were not intrusive to me. Knowing of the construction, I had brought ear plugs with me so I was not at all bothered by any noise. I had a nice big room, with all the bells and whistles one can expect from a short trip... the service was good, especially the way they pay attention to you upon arrival when you get in line to check in... my one complaint was the business center, run by Fedex where the computers seem to be from Noah;s Ark, and I was not able to download an attachment after 16 minutes and they had to reimburse me. Only 3 computers? Seriously???? I guess most people who stay there bring their IPads along! But when you are flying these days and do not want to carry much of anything with you, it is great to be able to find a good center to check emails etc...

title: Waldorf Astoria New York
body: The age and the history behind the hotel made it worth staying there. Keeping that in mind it's a old hotel so you expect the musty smell in the room. Open a widow for thirty minutes and the smell is gone. The fixtures and marble are not the newest or the shiniest but they are clean. The bed was amazing. After walking all day we appreciated a comfortable bed. I called the hotel before we left to ask about the hotel dress code and received a lot of attitude. I was expecting bad service based on the phone conversation. However, all the the staff were very gracious and accommodating. Only the tourist wear shorts & jeans, so the guy on the phone was right when he advised "dress business casual." If you want to fit in as a New Yorker, women wear a comfortable dress, men dress like you are a golf pro. There are stores for snacks, liquor, and plenty of restaurants nearby. Over our stay was enjoyable at the Waldorf Astoria New York.

title: Lives up to Expectations...yet challenges them...
body: I typically prefer more contemporary hotels versus the historic ones in the realm of the Waldorf, Plaza, or Drake etc. The Waldorf shocked me. I've traveled to New York many times - the last of which I stayed at the Marriott Marquis, a wonderful John Portman designed hotel. The Waldorf is undergoing renovations at this time - particularly on the Park Avenue side and I am guessing the rooms are changing as well. Due to the construction the entrance into the hotel is labyrinthine - when you do emerge in the lobby you are greeted with opulence of another era. The room that I was given was a contradiction to every single image that I had of the Waldorf...this was a room that would not have been out of place in a W hotel - newly renovated. I actually went back out in the hallway to make sure that I had not stumbled into another hotel. The kindness and the attentiveness of the staff reminded you that you are staying at something special. If you are not familiar with the Waldorf building itself, its size will astonish you as well. This is a sizeable building. I would definitely stay at the Waldorf-Astoria again, if you travel to New York City often, do yourself a favor and stay here at least once.

title: Great stay in an historic hotel
body:
I stayed at the Waldorf with my family for 6 nights recently and thoroughly enjoyed the comfortable lodgings, great service and historic atmosphere. While the hotel is undergoing a face-lift at the moment, the staff went out of their way to make our stay comfortable and convenient. Speaking of convenient, the location can't be beat...it's close to just about everything, or within a short walk to the subway and Grand Central Station. 
The beds are comfortable, and the rooms are large and clean. However, the thing that stood out for me was the service...from Eric at the door, who welcomed us and helped us find our way, to Shioban (sorry if I misspelled it!) at the reception desk, who was cheerful and efficient. Room service, albeit pricey (what's not in NYC?), was rapid and the choice and quality of the meals good.
I would definitely stay here again.

title: Fabulous Hotel
body: Just spent a week at the Waldorf Astoria on our first visit to New York City. The hotel is absolutely fabulous and as we were celebrating our Silver Wedding Anniversary we were happy to push the boat out. Restaurants and bars in the hotel are expensive but there are plenty of others in the locality and we were happy to go out to eat. The reception area is just as I imagined it would be. Our room was a bit tired but had everything we needed for our stay and we had a great view over Lexington Avenue. Scaffolding on the exterior meant the main entrance was closed but this was never a problem as there were entrances on all the other streets. A great location for visiting all the sites and easy walking distance to Times Square. All in all a fabulous trip and would have no hesitation in recommending this fabulous hotel.

title: Disappointed (again) :(((
body:
I called to reserve a couple nights at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC. We had stayed a couple years back at Christmas time and were really disappointed, as there was alot of renovating going on that we weren't told about when we booked. We thought we'd give it another try this summer. When I booked, I told the Waldorf Astoria what happened during our last trip and that we were hoping to make up for it this time. 
We arrived at the hotel to find.........more renovations going on. Seriously? A good bit of the hotel was sectioned off and we had to walk around back each time to enter through the garage/valet area. The building was surrounded by scaffolding. Not only that but the beautiful front entrance that we remember last time was not even accessible. The only place to sit and relax (besides your room) was the check in lobby, where there were usually two people sitting in one chair!
This was not worth the money and there was nobody around to help you with anything. The only time I spoke to the staff, they were behind a desk. After you check in, you're pretty much on your own. 
We had a broken toilet seat upon arrival, we called a couple times to have it fixed. It never was addressed.
This will be our last time at the Waldorf.

title: Still a great lady!
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf from Wednesday 20th June - Saturday 23th June.
It was part of a special occasion (30th anniversary) and the price wasn't too bad.. £200 a night. More than we would normally pay but had got a bit of a deal...would have been almost double.
Before we arrived we'd read a number of reviews and decided that it sounded like a great hotel- in its day-but maybe a wee bit of living on past history.
Wrong!! 
It was a delight from start to finish!
Getting out the car at the main entrance actually wasn't anything special--we could have been arriving at any one of hundreds of hotels in Manhattan---OK they did have some flags flying. Once in though we really did see the grand old lady in all her splendour!
The marble floors and the chandaliers were beautiful, the air thick with the sense of richness and money!
We only went because we got a reasonable deal, and were quite pleased to be saying that 'we were staying at the Waldorf'
The staff everywhere were imaculate and the guy at check-in would have looked at home modeling suits.
We were slightly early for check-in and although the room wasn't quite ready he took us through the whole process so that when the time came we walked to a seperate desk and got our key.
All the public areas were carpeted with a thick 'sink into' carpet that just felt plush! There were old fashioned chairs all over the place that were soooo comfy.
We had thought that the public areas would be good but that the rooms might be a 'past it'--nice but nothing special.
Wrong again!!
The room wasn't particularly big but what was in it was of very good quality. From the furniture to the curtains which were thick and quality... like the carpet...and the bed..ahh the bed was lovely! Real good quality sheets and bedding.
Bathroom was not huge but had a bath and a great shower, huge soft white!! towels,
We didn't have anything to eat or drink in any of the hotel bars or resturants but according to their website prices were quite high.
It was within reasonable walking distance of most of the sites.
All over the place were pictures of all the greats of stage, screen & politics who had stayed over the years..
All in all a great old lady that still has the wow factor! A special place for special occassions...go!

title: Hotel in the middle of town
body: Nice hotel,busy area better to walk than to drive. Rooms were nice bathroom old fashion. Lots of renovation around hotel is was a pain to find valet parking that by the way is fifty dollars a day.For the price in the middle of NYC is not bad

title: Gets better every time we come!!
body: I love this place. You get treated like royalty and it is perfectly located. If you want it, room service has it. Try taking a picky eating kid, you will have no problem. Best beds in town and cleaner than an operating room. Prices are very reasonable for the value yoy will receive. The beds are great to jump up and down on. It's like having a trampaline in your room. I would suggest asking for a higher level room as the views are simply amazing in this classic hotel.

title: The Best of The Best
body: We stayed from August 2nd through August 7th, and have just returned home. It was the most memorable trip we've had thus far. We travel lots, making at least 10 trips every year. The customer services we received were the best we've ever encountered. All service team members were always willing to assist us in all of our needs. They all went far above and beyond our expectations. They were prompt, friendly, kind, and treated us like VIP's. The hotel is centrally located. The interior is as grand and opulent as it is depicted in history books and travel guides. The exterior is currently under renovations, but that does not impede the flow of foot or vehicle traffic. It is very easy to get a cab as the doorman are always available to hail one for you. Our suite was clean and pristine upon check in and remained so during our entire stay. Prices are in line with it being New York, but be aware that internet access cost is approx. $17 per day, per computer. And the cost of snacks and soda's, and liquor in the mini-bar is over $7 and up, which is a bit pricey. But we do plan on staying at the Waldorf again on our next visit to New York. Love this place.

title: Hotel with history
body:
I just returned from four nights at the Waldorf and I did enjoy my stay.
The hotel history, clean rooms, and central location pushed this hotel to 4 stars for me.
Lobby bar is fun and served our visit complete with good entertainment on Sat. night. after returning from dinner.
Housekeeping did a wonderful job for us, Checkout a breeze. Taxis are always there and available. The art deco design adds a layer of New York style. We walked all over Midtown and also used subways a block away.
Lobby restrooms are currently unavailable with a re direct to 3rd floor. Some remodeling is also occurring outdoors and scaffolding was noted. 
Not sure all would agree with my rating because there are so many hotels in NYC. I would say this was a good fit for me on this trip.

title: Disappointed
body: Never stayed here before & will never stay again. I'm sure it was fabulous back in the day, but it is now musty & tired. They boast a "complimentary" continental breakfast in a private room. Our key never worked to the "private room," so we had to ring the doorbell & bang on the door every day in order to get in. The staff never got the drift that they needed to leave the door open. Other guests were complaining about it every morning. One morning, the room was so crowded, no one else could get in. No one told us that we couldn't get ice without calling room service, but we figured that out pretty quickly. Sometimes we got our ice before we had to leave the hotel or go to bed - & sometimes we didn't; the service was very slow. Hotel rooms in NYC are typically small, but they usually make up for it by providing a dresser &/or other storage solutions. We had a family of 4 with virtually no storage - there was no dresser to speak of - but a few small drawers tucked in next to the honor bar. The room was plenty big enough to hold a dresser. Incidentally, there was not a price list or menu for the honor bar, so we had no idea of the cost of anything. We requested one & got a partially copied piece of paper that did not contain all of the prices! The line to check in was very long, so by the time we got to check in, we felt rushed. No one gave us any information about the hotel - it was 3 days before we figured out that there was another entrance to our hotel, on 50th Street. The front lobby was closed due to renovations, & everyone was using the Lexington Ave. entrance. Just disappointed in this has-been hotel, especially given the exhorbitant room rates - will never stay here again.

title: A wilted Rose
body:
I am an old hotel aficionado and staying at this landmark was definitely on my bucket list. I must say though that I was very disappointed and considered changing hotels but didn't want the hassle of it so I endured the pain of paying $400+ per night for a room I felt was worth $250 tops. 
The room was dreary and dated although very spacious. We had a chair with no legs that looked like they scooped it up in a dumpster!! (see picture) Housekeeping was bad...I felt like borrowing some supplies and doing it myself. I had to give a big tip to get some soap...didn't leave any till I left a tip. Speaking of soaps - I've seen better amenities at motel 8. 
However, the beds were AMAZING!!!!! I kicked myself for not checking out the type of mattress. Huge perfect pillows. 
The hotel charged an extra $10 (? I think or 14) for room wifi...what a rip. My daughter really wanted to order one thing room service...to see the little carts, silver, etc. so a small teacup size plate of french fries cost us $18. 
ok, I guess one shouldn't bother staying here unless you are a rocker feller!
I agonized as I imagined all the beautiful boutique hotels we could be staying in for that dollar. 
I would have to sum up with the worst thing about this hotel and that is the revolving door entrances and the snotty, lazy doormen who would see you struggling and stand there with their arms crossed. Really!! Every time!

title: Sleeping giant
body:
We checked in to 2 suites as part of our tour round USA. The hotel is undergoing refurbishment therefore lobby is at the back entrance which resulted in a chaotic arrival. I read about the closure of the main lobby in reviews but it was not mentioned on Waldorf's website. The lobby is beautiful but the lighting could be brighter. The check in was friendly but we had to pull our own luggage as there was no help available. The 1 bedroom suite is spacious but no whao factor.The tv was plasma not lcd therefore the tv pictures were not the best quality. The 1 bed suites has 2 toilets & bathrooms therefore getting ready in the morning was very convinient. The ironing board and iron was the same as less expensive hilton's and the bed linen was also very ordinary although the bed was very comfortable.
The staff are very nice and are always ready to please..
The location of this hotel is fantastic as we were able to walk to central park, times square, UN hq etc.
The room has a musty smell which is probably due to the age but I'm sure it could be sorted but maybe the hotel are not ready for the outlay when they still have people who would come there in the present state.
I expected to see a very luxurious hotel but all I got was a luxurous bill but at least I can say I've been there

title: Amazing stay
body: I stayed here in May, my Daughter was getting married in Central Park and she stayed here too (with her future Husband). From the moment we arrived we were made a fuss of, the reception staff were lovely and nothing was too much bother for them. One of the ladies serving in the bar was very helpful, telling us all the good places to go to and writing down directions for us. The hotel itself is beautiful and has lots of history to it, they have a 'museum' area with plenty of memorabilia to look at. The rooms are a good size and the suites gorgeous, room service was good with the exception of one day where they forgot to put out the shampoo, I went to reception and asked for some and got a huge apology with vouchers for free breakfasts for us all, wow!! We ate in the restaurant for breakfast every day - that is an experience in itself, its all you can eat buffet style with a great selection to cover all tastes, just remember if you want a fried egg ask for it 'over easy'. We had an amazing time in New York, the location of the hotel was perfect with places such as Times Square, The Rock, Grand Central Station, Bloomingdales and Fifth Ave a short stroll away. Any other places are a quick cab ride away and the Hotel porters at the front will hail you a cab anytime, just remember to tip them a couple of dollars to say thanks. Overall our stay was perfect and I can't praise the hotel enough.

title: A mediocre stay. So disappointed :(
body:
For as long as I can remember the Waldorf Astoria has been the epitome of luxury, service and fine hospitality.
This month I was fortunate enough to be visiting the USA for a once in a lifetime trip with my sister. We decided to stay at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC. This was to be the highlight of the trip to the USA. Unfortunately the trip did not live up the many years of excitement and high expectations.
Let us begin with our arrival. We arrived around 9.30pm and were dropped off in “the garage”. No staff waiting, no one to help us with our bags, no sign to reception. Finally after we looked like deers in headlights wondering where to go and what to do someone told us he would send our bags up to our room, I said “How? We haven’t checked in yet”. He just looked at me. So I finally said where is reception? He pointed and said through that door and left. For a 5 star hotel this was not impressive.
We joined the queue and waited 15 minutes to be served in an ice-cold reception. To say it was freezing was an understatement. The air conditioning was up way too high, most guests could be heard complaining about it. When we reached the reception the lady said three things to us; checking in? may I have your credit card and here is your key. Disgusting. I had to ask where the lift was, where breakfast was, if I could have a paper, was there turn down service, where the concierge was. I was offered not one piece of information about the hotel.
We went to our room and found there was a shower over the bath. We rang straight away to reception and advised we requested a room with a shower only. We were told that the hotel was fully booked that night so we would have to change tomorrow. I advised that was fine. We were told to have our bags waiting in the morning when we went out for the day and we would be moved during the day. This did not happen. The next day we went out to explore and came back to the hotel at 3.30pm. We went to reception and asked for our new room. We were advised it was not ready. We went up to our first room and my sister decided to have a sleep. I rang reception and advised that she was having a sleep, do not disturb us until 5pm. I was advised very rudely that we would be contacted when the new room was ready as soon as it was finished being cleaned. I said I understood this but please hold it until 5pm as my sister was having a nap. Oh I’m sorry Ms. Kelly I was told we will ring you as soon as its ready. Finally after going back and forth for 15 minutes reception finally understood that we were not going to move until 5pm. I went out shopping came back at 4.30pm and my sister advised she had received a call and a knock at the door during that time. She did not answer. Such a simple request – this is not hard to adhere to.
The second room was fine with a lovely bathroom. No hair dyer though?
On each day we went to the concierge and asked for directions to different locations. Not once were we offered a map. I had to ask both times if I could have a map.
I had a spa appointment with Rodica. She was brilliant, very welcoming and positive about the hotel. The only staff member to smile at me during my whoel stay except for the room service staff.
Housekeeping was quite disappointing. They made the bed and replenished the towels, and emptied the bin - that was it. They did not throw out empty bottles nor do general tidy up which we experienced at the Peninsula in Beverley Hills.
A charge for internet in the rooms? $15 a day? In a 5 star hotel? Not good enough.
Finally - the renovations being undertaken at the hotel. Not once were we advised about this – before or during our stay. No note from management to apologise for this disruption, which began about 8am each day with the banging of machinery and equipment and continued throughout the day.
In summary, the stay was mediocre. I was expecting the highest service, attention to detail and friendly approachable staff. What I received was far from this. I doubt I will stay at the Waldorf Astoria again which is sad thing as most of my wonderful memories in life come from exciting and memorable visits to renowned hotels around the world.

title: Room odour
body: I had reserved two suites for my daughters birthday. We arrived at the hotel and had to find the entrance as the hotel is being renovated so there is no entrance of Park Avenue. When i got to the front desk it was busy so we waited in line for 15 mins when i eventually got to the desk there were no rooms ready but they were being made and the hotel would contact me via a text,normal check-in is at 3.00pm we left our luggage and went on a walk. I had not been contacted at all and it was 3,30pm so we headed back, agin we waited in line and when i explained they were to contact me they apologized and offered drink coupons. We headed up to our suites on the 14 floor the room had damp/musty odour but we so tired that we decided to stay. The next day i asked the front desk to send up a manager to smell the room, a manger from house keeping came up and agreed that the room smelled he offered to bring up a odour machine but we would have to leave the room,or he could spray air freashner or as last resort he could check with front desk and see if a room was available on a different floor.We ending up moving to the 8 floor to a smaller room the shower handle fell off, the phone on the bed side table did not work and the electrical outlet on desk was damaged and the wires were visible. When i phoned down to the front desk the lady was extremely apologetic and ask if we would like to be moved again i said no as this was our last night. I would not rate this hotel higher than a three star the lobby is beautiful but that as good as it gets. I have just checked my master card and there are charges from the hotel yet when i checked out there was no additional charges another thing to sort out!

title: In need of a little update
body: We stayed here for fours days and as I've never been to NY I thought the iconic WA was a good place to go. The pluses are that it's location is great for access to Grand Central station and is a few blocks from Times Square. It's negatives ar that although Inunderstahd it's old romantic and historical past, it needs to cater for a more modern client. Paying the price we did we were astounded that there was no in room coffee/tea maker. When my husband asked if one was available on the second day we were told that because he hadn't asked for one when we checked in there would be a charge for this now....(I don't think so thank you very much)! I loved the decor and of course the main entrance (it IS getting updated at the moment so entry is on to Lexington rather than the usual Park Ave.) but I fear that by not also offering decent wifi in areas other than reception is a little short-sighted as at various times every seat in reception was full with people frantically tapping away on their phones. The hotel is okay for a short stay, rooms a little on the small side and although the staff seemed very polite and biddable, I think next time we might try something a little more modern.

title: A taste of Old New York
body: The Waldorf offered a really great price one week this summer for advance payment. We jumped on this and were so glad we did. The Waldorf is a beautiful hotel, it needs a little spiffing up, but it is still wonderful. We arrived a little earlier than the official check-in time, but decided to see if they had a room for us. Fortunately, they did and they even upgraded us for free to a corner suite! The room was very nice with a view of the Chrysler building. It was very clean and had several nice amenities. They also have a fitness center open 24 hours for free use. Everyone we interacted with from the front desk to the maids to the concierge was really friendly and helpful. Plus, the location of the hotel is perfect, right in midtown and within walking distance to several of NYC's major sights. There were a few things that prevented me from giving the Waldorf an "Excellent" rating. The first was that the television service was terrible. When you turned on the TVs they started up on the hotel's main channel (which is pretty normal) but the volume was always blaring. The clickers/remotes were low on batteries and it was very difficult to turn the volume down and change the channels. Also, the picture was terrible and not a lot of the channels even came in. Ordinarily we don't really watch TV on vacation but the olympics were on that week and we wanted to see some of the events. Another thing that reduced my rating was the main Park Ave lobby area was under construction so we didn't even get to see that beautiful area, the bar and restaurants on that side of the hotel were closed, and we had to enter/exit on Lexington or 49th street, which was kind of a pain sometimes. I do understand that a hotel of this age must do restoration occasionally and I actually appreciate that they do it, it was just kind of a bummer. All in all we were very happy with the Waldorf and had a great trip, in part due to the efforts of this hotel.

title: Grand hotel
body: The hotel was undergoing renovations to the lobby. Everything is very smart and grand looking. The room was beautiful. Had a separate lounge with faux fireplace which gave us a lot of extra space. Bathroom had lovely accessories. Didn't go for the forty dollar breakfast as there are so many places nearby. Location perfect and not too hectic. The only gripe is the high Internet charges for such a prestigious and expensive hotel. Otherwise excellent!

title: Needs to get with the times
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf last January, mostly holiday part conference (at the Hilton). The Waldorf's draw is it's history - period. Apart from that it's just a large hotel catering largely to conventions, still dining out on its cache of being famous. Get real, Waldorf - $15 per day for internet access? We had a junior suite, which was generously sized, but the bathroom is in serious need of updating - it looked old, tired and grubby. I liked the proximity to Grand Central, but apart from that it's in a pretty quiet area.
Probably the best aspect of our room - between the neighbouring buildings we could peek out and see the Chrysler building - nice!

title: Classic hotel
body: This is a classic hotel. I stayed one night on points here. Pretty nice stay, but not overly impressed. The hotel is a bit dated. It would need a face lift (however keeping the old charm of course). Tried the famous Waldorf salad. Wanted to try this hotel for one night, but probably won't stay here in the future on regular rates.

title: Wonderful Experience
body: I treated my daughter to a break in New York for her 21st birthday. She was treated like a delicate princess, champagne and the most delicious birthday cake delivered to the room. Free cocktail vouchers awaited us on our return on the 2nd day. Room was excellent, large comfortable bed, hot powerful shower and plenty of storage space. Great location, within walking distance of times square, broadway, fifth avenue etc. Would recomend to anyone planning a New York trip...............I intend returning in the very near future.

title: All hat and no knickers
body:
Recently stayed at the Waldorf and, although a beautiful building inside, was surprised at the lack of affordable eating. The prices in the eating place inside the hotel were sky high and not particularly offering the kind of food we like. We had to go out locally to the American Diner to get a satisfactory meal (wonderful loc bagels!).
We were also caught out by what we thought was a fridge and searched inside for water, moving some of the bottles around. What we did not realise was that we were charged on the room bill for the bottles we had moved, even though these were put back unopened. (Some £40 odd for very small bottles of wine!). This issue was resolved by our travel agent but independent travellers to the Waldorf may not be so lucky.
There was also an issue with room service. We ordered early morning tea. We were served very nicely with ONE teabag for the two of us but this teabag would not infuse no matter what we did and we ended up with cups of hot water and milk. When the room service waiter was questioned on this he admitted that the staff, too, had trouble infusing these teabags! So why did they continue to serve them? Strange.
The hotel is currently being renovated outside and there is scaffolding around the buillding but when the work is finished it will look much smarter
Not a hotel we would stay in again as we did not feel very "looked after".

title: MEDIOCRE at best.
body:
We checked in at 2 pm and left our bags returning shortly after 5 pm. Finally they secured a room. We were reserved for a King Superior and asked if there were any Hilton Honors upgrades. We received the standard lines from Fevan, such has "it will be a lovely room" and "I'm sorry we're FULLY committed". In other words, there's not a chance you're being upgraded. She gave me a King Superior room 803 which overlooked a construction site, with a promise that if anything became available she would call the next day. Of course we never heard from her again. After we got to our room I called the front desk and asked for a manager to come up and appraise our view. The front desk said that would not be necessary and we would be moved the next day. We also had to call for the luggage, they just left it until we arrived in the room several hours later. 
The next day, we were told to have our bags packed and ready by NOON and the hotel would automatically move them. The next day we were ready as promised. At noon, the front desk said, "oh we're working on it. Do you have anything to do this afternoon?" In other words, nothing had been done.
We went to a matinee and came back around 5 pm. Still no room and another big hussle to find a room, only to receive an "upgrade". We shold have demanded to view it first. We received an "upgrade" to a one bedroom Suite 17A. It hasn't been remodeled in years. tattered carpets, old furnishings. In the bathroom there was a heating unit in the wall that had of all things masking tape in double and triple runs taping it on all four sides to the wall so that it would not fall out. What kind of management team would allow maintenance to pull that stunt? In addition a lamp was broken at check in. Since it was already late we had them come up and fix it the next morning. We did not request another room change because we were completely over the hotel and the nerve of the front desk to shove us into this room. 
We received a bottle of Champagne and fruit/cheese plate from our company. Besides the cheese and one full apple there was a "sprig" of four grapes. Why bother? Was our cheese and fruit plate the one that got the last of the grapes? I'm sure that cost my company a fortune so why don't you put some effort and quality into it. Had it not been left in the room I would have called and asked for a new one to be brought up. Except, the wait would have been excruciating. 
It was a wasted four night stay. In general, people from all over the world visit New York City and many of them will splurge to stay at the "historic" Waldorf Astoria. They certainly fulfill the "historic" part of the equation. Quality is another issue. The hotel is filled with tourist buses of guests who stay here because of its iconic history. My group stayed here and it cost a fortune. Our one dinner was fine, no problems and the servers in the banquet department are excellent. Breakfasts were fine but the buffets for the most part were all exactly the same. The public rooms are beautiful and have been redone. The Grand Ballroom and the 18th floor dining room and meeting rooms are also stunning. 
We have stayed twice previously in the Waldorf Towers and had no problems. Our rooms were nice and once we were upgraded to a suite. But our experience this time was horrible. I could have easily demanded satisfaction and I would have eventually forced a response, but after the delays and run around with the first room change, we had no hope in the ability of the front desk personnel or their managers to succeed. They were indifferent at best.
I'm in New York for meetings at least 4 times a year. There are so many great hotels that are within a few blocks of the Waldorf for guests to stay. No one needs to go through what we experienced. I get the feeling that many of the people who have written reviews are tourists coming for a special occasion that want the history a big 1000 plus room tourist hotel can provide. If you want to be part of the rat race, one might as well stay at the Marriott Marquis on Times Sqaure with their hordes of tourists. Actually the rooms and service are probably better. As I said, we will not come back, even to stay on the Towers side. I'm in hotel rooms 50-75 nights/year and this is the worst stay I can remember.

title: Old and faded but still with charm,large rooms for Manhattan
body:
Stayed here for five nights in August. The rate we got in the sale when we booked in January was really good. We were in a King Deluxe room. The room was certainly large by Manhattan standards. If the modern tv and telephones were removed then you could be stood in a room from the forties,it's that dated!
 We really liked it though. The lobby area of the hotel is stunning,although at the moment the main Park Avenue entrance is closed for renovation.
 The location is excellent for tourism. Ten minutes walk to Times Sq. Ten minutes walk to Central Park, and a block from the nearest subway station. Disappointingly,the Wi-fi costs a bit. I paid $60+ for four days of internet service. It annoys me that hotels that market themselves as a premium brand then charge silly rates for internet,when a $40 Days Inn or similar can offer the same service for free.
 Would probably stay here again if the price was good, but not if I was having to pay full price for the room.

title: New York amazing, but Waldorf should take lessons from Royal Carribbean
body:
Having read other reviews, both the good and bad ring true to my experience. Check in and out were a breeze and we were allowed to stay in our room later as well as no wait for a room to become available, even though it was two hours before check in. Rooms are as described by others, dated and poorly designed. The tv was poor which was a disappointment when we wanted to see the "Bolt" and Mo Farrah and all they showed was beach volleyball. They expected my 14 son and 16 daughter to share a bed! The bellboy explained that we could request a cot (campbed) to put in the wasted space they call the sitting room,which was a brilliant idea. The reception staff tried to charge us an extra 50$ a night for this, after suggesting I top and tail with my daughter! It took us years to get her to stay in her own bed so not going back to that now! Joking aside it was a 4/5 star hotel and not a campng trip. Anyway, we stood our ground and they agreed to it for free. But then I spent the rest of the time avoiding reception as I don't like making a fuss. However, my daughter had her own room for the holiday and we didn't have to step over hairdryers, straighteners etc whilst my son had a lovely bed all to himself.
Very grateful for the advice from reviewers about charges for so much as moving a bottle in the mini bar as we usually stick our softdrinks in for when we get home. Instead we made great use of the ice machine outside our room. 
New York was the best holiday of our lives so that is why all the niggles or disappointments in the Waldorf were forgotten. But all the reviews I had read on the Waldorf added up when I got there. The most recent experience we had of American hosptality and service was with Royal Carribbean and the Waldorf could learn a lot from them.

title: Very good, but my expectations were higher
body: The Waldorf Astoria has built its reputation on elegance and luxury. In this case, it's also in Midtown Manhattan, centrally located for business or pleasure in Manhattan. The lobby is spectacular, the service I received was courteous and professional, and the room I experienced was spacious, very comfortable, and, quiet (important in the city that never sleeps). The hotel staff has is prepared for the international traveler, and I heard several languages in dialogue between staff and guests while there. My corporate room rate made this, all-in-all, a very good experience. BUT, I also noted that my room furnishings were 1950s era, the wi-fi was an expensive add-on, and my basic breakfast (bacon, eggs, hash browns, toast, juice, coffee) was above $50. ,I would stay again (and probably will on business at the corporate rate), but it is not the special experience that you might expect from the Waldorf-Astoria in New York.

title: Employees steal money from the room
body:
When staying there my wallet with big amount of cash, credit cards and documents was stolen from ythe room. Though it was obvious that it was stolen by hotel employee, "investigation" gave no result. no damage was reimbursed. They didn't even report to police.
It's awful.

title: Classy hotel, needs facelift
body: As you walk into the exception lobby with the reception to the left, a stunning clock and arch through the centre and a exquisite bar area on the left you are left opened mouthed. We got the park elevators uptodate the 14th floor where we had a suite. The room itself was good but in need of a makeover. It had a small but practical bathroom and a similar sized seated area. The bed was big and very comfortable. Service was excellent and amazingly for the US, service is already included in the bars and restaurants in the hotel.

title: Disappointing
body: I was disappointed in this hotel compared to its amazing reputation - which was not there in the flesh! You had to queue for reception - for ages - whenever you wanted anything - had to bring your own bags up - I was not expecting this after stays in other hotels that were supposed to be of the same calibre. The room was grubby and very dated, and service generally was poor. The bar staff had a serious attitude on, even after a generous tip! Having said that, it was cheaper than I expected - so maybe, considering its location, it was not a bad deal. I just think that the expectation was high so the disappointment was also!

title: Terrible experience
body: Arrived with my husband and two young children for what we hoped would be a memorable one night stay in NYC. Wanting a full cultural experience we booked a room in the famed Waldorf Astoria. Our room, 1217, smelled musty and the bathroom had hair from the previous occupant on the sink counter, on the floor, on the tub surround, the wall as well as the door. Upon calling guest services to complain I was told no rooms were available to move us and that housekeeping would come to re-clean. We left for dinner and arrived back to discover that while turn down service had been performed, that every single hair was still in the bathroom. This, despite a voicemail from guest services that all has been taken care of. I immediately called guest services and after waiting on hold for 12 minutes decided to give up. I took photographs of each and every hair to show management in the morning. Unfortunately our stay only got worse. The tub would not drain during my husband's shower the next morning so it filled up neatly half way and 40 minutes later was still not empty. Neither I nor my children could bathe before heading out for the day. Upon checkout I complained and after being told I would be "substantially compensated" I was informed they would knock $100 off of our dinner bill at Bull and Bear. I had sat there watching the staff person type away furiously for 10 minutes to arrive at this conclusion and at that point I just gave up. I believe our entire dinner tab should have been picked up since the bathroom was pretty much filthy and non-functioning for our entire family. Considering we had been drenched from the rain the night before and we could not bathe it was horrible to have to walk around the city feeling grimy. We traveled all the way from Alexandria, VA for this? Shame on the hotel and it's response.

title: Hey, Its the Waldorf
body:
I almost cancelled my reservation when I read recent somewhat negative reviews of the Waldorf. But, based on past experience, I decided to chance it. To be sure, the Waldorf rooms do seem a bit tired and the renovation of the Park Ave side of the hotel temporarily eliminates some of the nicer bars and facilities. But, there are so many positive aspects to this hotel. Let me count just a few.
First, the reception area and all common spaces are luxurious from ceiling to carpet. The rich woodwork encourages guests to just sit in one of the hotel lobby chairs and pensively look around. I was very impressed with the way that the hotel blocked off the Park Ave side first floor construction. You literally had to have been in this hotel previously to even know there was a large area under construction. The hotel cleverly blocked the passageway beyond the elevators with quality woodwork and decorations that belied all the quiet work beyond the wall. Second, the customer service is superb. Two examples - when registering for my room in the evening, I was given gracious assistance by a very friendly hotel clerk who took me to an adjoining office when she noticed a line out front. I was even given a modest upgrade too. When I got to my room, I realized that my suit was all wrinkled from the rain storm that evening. Because I had an important business meeting early the next morning, I called the valet service to see if someone could press my suit late that evening. A very agreeable gentleman was at my door within 5 minutes, and returned 20 minutes later with a perfectly pressed suit and pants. 
Third, while the room carpet and furniture did look a bit worn, the room was spacious by NYC standards, the bed was exceedingly large and comfortable, with plush pillows. The bathroom was small in size but had a great shower. (Next to a quality bed, is there anything more important than a good shower head?) The room was quiet, the hallway wide and stylish, and the wifi service strong and consistent. 
Lastly, the location is great - close to a lot of the financial business offices, grand central station, good restaurants on Lexington, 3rd and 2nd Avenue. I've stayed at many quality hotels in NYC including the nearby W hotel, Doubletree and Marriott Marquis, but when I can find a competitive hotel rate at the Waldorf, it will remain my first choice.

title: Old and used busy hotel
body:
I guess my expectation of this hotel vanished once I got thought the beautiful and impressive lobby and all the bling of diamonds on the way to the lift.... The room was small, but standard for NYC . The carpet was so used and faded, the walls had chips all over, the furniture had scratches and the air con was incredibly loud. In the bathroom there was some sort of fan/heater that looked like it was made in 1970... And it was sounding its about to take off!
Every time I came down to see the concierge the line was at least 5-10 people....I waited, but every time ended up going back up. Surely they could provide a few more desk considering the amount of people and the reputation the hotel once had for service. And a hot chocolate takes 45 minutes to come up with 2 reminders, and it was cold and disgusting not to mention overpriced. Disappointed , would not stay there againe, considering all the other options NYC has to offer. The hotel deffenetly needs a facelift or something, it's old, it's overused and overpriced for what it offers.

title: Below Expectations
body:
As a Hilton Gold Rewards member I stay at Hiltons all over the country on a regular basis. I earned two 'Free Night Certificates' over the last year and decided to use them at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC for the weekend. My boyfriend and I arrived by Taxi around 1pm on Saturday. The taxi drop-off was downstairs and there were no signs pointing toward check-in or the lobby. (After asking we found the lobby upstairs, relatively easy.) I waited in line for about 5 minutes before the next desk agent was available. (At the time, I did not see the Gold Honors check-in desk.) I was told our room was not ready and they would call when it was available. At 3 pm I was texted that the room was available. 
Room:
The room was on the 22nd floor, not much of a view. The room was tiny and the fixtures were old and not in good condition. While I appreciate the historical aspects of the hotel there were certain things that could/should be nicer, especially for the price! The wallpaper was lifting from the walls, door corners/creases were miscolored and dirty, the toilet did NOT stop flushing until you wiggled the handle every time, the shower did NOT drain, the big screen TV was nice but the cable was not HD which made the image blurry on every channel. However, the bed was nice and comfortable! 
Amenities: 
There is no pool/jacuzzi. The business center is not free. You must pay for internet usage and printing! We were unable to print our train tickets. There is no complimentary breakfast, not even for honors. The hotel offers 2 drink coupons in any restaurant/bar at the hotel. We took advantage and ordered two $20.00 drinks at the Peacock Lounge. Drinks were pretty good but not worth the high price tag. (Again, glad I didn't pay) With a drink purchase they do offer mixed nuts/wasabi peas/olives on a tray which was a nice touch. The gym is nice.
Service:
No one went out of their way to be kind/nice during the stay. Typically, Hilton employees have been extremely nice and interactive throughout a stay but not at the Waldorf. 
The entire experience did not impress us, or live up to the Waldorf experience I was anticipating. We will stay at a different Hilton next time and won't recommend to friends either.

title: Once Great Hotel, now showing signs of wear, felt ripped off!
body:
Booked for four days at the end of July with Trailfinders (paid £912) and realised later I could have got it for 2/3 of the price by booking direct with the Hotel or online, Trailfinders assured me that this was the best price they could get (Why such a company can't secure decent discounts is beyond me! or do they consider over £300 to be a fair markup?)
Lobby fab! Grand and imposing, you could imagine being there in it's heyday mixing with the stars! Now full of Guests on laptops taking advantage of free WiFi (Exorbitant to use in rooms!).
Public areas beautiful, Grand Ballroom must be seen for it's cathedral like expanse!
Our room was worn & tired looking (they need to re-invest in this badly)!
Breakfast encompassed every taste possible, freshly squeezed orange topped up every few minutes & every sweet & savoury foods you can think of (mind you at 40 bucks each extra it should be)!
Overall, a Great experience, marred by a feeling of being ripped off (particularly by Trailfinders)!

title: Loved the Waldorf Astoria
body: Loved the hotel and the staff were wonderful. We stayed in a two double bedroom and it was nice. Beds were very small double beds and the bathroom was very small, but we didn't mind as it was a historic hotel and was very beautiful.

title: My Birthday Celebration
body:
My husband booked this hotel thru expedia and got a somewhat good deal. When I went to check in, the guy (Winston) at the desk was extremely friendly even though the check in process took several minutes but it was worth my wait. I was upgraded to a better room with partial view of the city, late check out and complimentary breakfast for 4. 
I find that the room was OK, my expectation for the room was higher seeing that it was the Waldorf after all. The beds were comfortable. The AC could not be adjusted, either on or off. The bathroom was clean. People were generally nice. I would stay at this hotel again.

title: I had another expectation
body:
We had booked this hotel because my husband is a Hilton Gold Reward member. It was our 1st visit to NYC and we would like to do it in style and it was very quick that we decided to stay at Waldorf. We arrived in the evening from another entrance bcs the hotel was being renovated. Too bad, we couldnt make any proper pic of the hotel from outside.
The lobby area looks very nice but crowded with hotel guests who needed internet wifi connection. 
The bedroom is large with 2 double beds...a very good bed/mattress in my opinion. Rather small bathroom. The condition of both rooms are quite worn out but tidy. Had a nice view from our room looking out to Chrysler building. 
We didn't dine in the premise, therefore we can't write any review about it except that we received 2 vouchers for complimentary drinks and it took ages for the bar staffs to attend us, though some of them had walked pass us few times.
With the taxi, it was a few minutes ride to the centre of Manhattan. There are some restaurants and cafes around the hotel and other hotels but mostly office buildings or banks.
I had expected more glitters and glamours in this hotel but I didn't see nor feel it.

title: AMAZING HOTEL IN NYC!!
body: Our stay with our family here was amazing. From Mary at the Diamond check in area all the way down it is run top notch. We loved the location and our room. The service is great. Any request was addressed instantly and completed. We will definitely be staying here again and can't wait to go back!

title: A very select and luxury hotel!
body: We had a 3 night stay in New York this summer with 2 of our sons. We've decided to stay in a very good hotel: we've chosen the Waldorf. We arrived on a saturday that was very busy for them: nevertheless we were welcomed and obtained a room with 2 double, and an average view. After the first night, we were wondering about the smell of the room: the font desk immediately reacted, apologized and changed our room in a luxury one bedroom suite and a huge view on Park Avenue:it was really very large and comfortable! we were very happy in this room and appreciated the quick reaction and commitment of the front desk (Mrs Laurie and a young man called David, who dis his best all along our stay to help us). The lounge was a little busy, as the reviews say, but not old at all, with a good food all along the day, very easy to have brkfst in the hotel before leaving for a long day n NYC!Housekeeping is very efficient, rooms are obviously very clean and comfortable, and the lobby with the clock is soooo nice! of course at the towers you have a dedicated check in and a personalised service. We do recommend the towers at the Waldorf for the rooms and the service.

title: Family fun in New York
body: Stayed at the Waldorf for seven nights at the beginning of April 2012. We are a family with teenagers. The hotel was fabulous,location was great my only advice would be book for at least four nights when visiting New York there is just so much to fit in. we stayed for a full week and still didn't do everything.

title: The Grandest of them all!
body:
The entrance doorway had a plaque "The Presidential Suite", not false advertisement at all. I did not have the oppurtunity to stay at this property, just yet. I am a Waldorf Astoria employee in New Orleans, and had the chance to tour this beautiful place! The lobby is very historic, and beautiful! I was also able to tour the Presidential Suite. This room is very accomodating and full of history. Every president in the US since the 1950's or so has stayed in this suite in NYC. Think about the amount of hotels in Manhattan, that include suites. This hotel HAS TO BE doing something right if every Leader of America has stayed here! Each president has also donated something to the Waldorf Astoria hotel to this suite. The suite had a dining room, a foyer, a living room that could possible seat 20, and a huge full kitchen! The bed was set up for a king with drapes and curtains above. 
 The motto for Waldorf Astoria hotels is "Each one, the grandest of them all" and this hotel definitley is the Grandest of New York City! I am highly anticipating my return to the big apple to stay at this property, follow up review to follow!!

title: Avoid it until the construction is done
body: It is recently under construction (2012 summer). Location is not really good compare to other high end hotels in NYC. Keep checking the rate, and you could get a REALLY good deal. By the way, both Waldorf Astoria and Waldorf Tower are not for fashionista.

title: Excellent experience
body:
I recently stayed at the Waldorf Astoria Hotel, I was impressed on the interior design and the rooms were really gorgeous.
In addition, being on Park Avenue in midtown central to it all.
complimentary limo from hotel, service by CSL Transportation.
Nothing beats the experience.

title: Olde World Charm mixed with 21st Century Service and Pride
body: The Waldorf Astoria, New York is like no other Hotel in North America. While continually striving to reach the pinnacle of current day amenities and service, the ongoing restoration of decades of history are brought together seamlessly by current General Manager, Mr. E. Long and his loyal and professional team. Mr. Long is a selfless promoter of culture and history, as the newly renovated Waldorf Astoria will soon, upon completion of restorations, proudly display. This is also evident in the manner that his team members selflessly carry out their daily duties with professionalism, service and pride. Pride, Professionalism and Service are most definitely terms best describing Waldorf Astoria Associates. From the Front Office Management Team to the Front Desk Staff, to the Bell Desk, to the Concierge, to the Food Services Division - Restaurants, Bars and Banquet Staff to the Housekeeping Staff, the Waldorf Astoria exudes pride and confidence. We have been fortunate to be long returning patrons that always look forward to our next visit and always dismay at leaving. Thank you Mr. Long for being the conscientious caretaker of an American Icon, The Waldorf Astoria.

title: Can't say anything bad when you get upgraded!
body: Until now, we have never stayed at the Waldorf. We have had several banquets and stopped in the foyer to see the grandeur as we showed people that were with us. We decided to stay there only because our favorite hotels were booked....again. We were not expecting much because we were staying in the main hotel not the tower. Our black car service dropped us off at the ground level due to the foyer being closed off for.... guess.....CONSTRUCTION! So anyone new to the hotel will miss the best part! Anyway, it was quickly forgotten because some reason they upgraded us at the same reserved price to a suite in the tower on the 40th floor! Don't know why, but wow what a luxury delight! The room had a small foyer, living room, a separate bedroom with french doors and a bathroom. All the small touches were included. So, I fully intended to review differently because of what I had heard about the tired old rooms but, I was living pretty good on our stay and I'm not going to look a gift horse in the mouth!

title: Disappointing
body:
As a Hhonors Gold member, no upgrade was given. Indeed a quite horrible room was offered.
In the roof, a ridiculously damp area was seen (photo included) and in the morning a vast quantity of paint from the ceiling had reached the floor.
Rooms are small, damp and not well cleaned. The bathroom was past it and doesn't feel in the right position as if it was added on at some point in time.
The WORST thing about this hotel is the attitude of some members of staff. I emailed in advance of my visit and was advised Golds get a discounted breakfast at Oscars (reduced to $20). On enquiry at check in this was not offered but I was told who the manager was and given his name.
When I went to speak to said manager, he denied that he was in fact the manager (despite his name being that of the manager). He did, however, agree to speak to me. I was dealt with in the most poor fashion and they point blanc refused to honour the benefit claiming it had ended just 3 days before my visit.
Exceedingly poor service especially when Hilton claim you to be a "Gold VIP".
Gold benefits offered were 2 bottles of water in the room (Waldorf Astoria branded), 2 drinks vouchers for the stay (value $20) and internet access.
Of course, the apparently free bottles of water appeared on the bill and had to be challenged.
My advice is to stay elsewhere - this hotel has a nice lobby, but staff with less charm than a doormat and rooms more dowdy than a nursing home.

title: Great hotel great location but a little tired
body:
We stayed here for four days and got a great deal on price line. The room was roomy but a little tired but the bed was oh so comfortable.
The bar and restaurant are excellent but very pricey.
Staff are excellent and Martin who checked us in was very professional. 
Location wise the hotel is excellent and you can walk to most places.
If you visit it is a must to go to the TKTS ticket bureau in Time Square..you get half price show tickets here for that night..it's well worth it!
Overall price was reasonable.

title: Old world glamour
body: Stayed here July 6th for 3 nights and was kind of expecting to be a little disappointed as was expecting so much from this icon of New York. I was NOT disappointed at all, walked in and my mouth dropped but the sheer beauty of this place, yes there are more opulent rooms with more modern decor in other hotels but if that is what you want then I suggest you book one of those hotels. If you want to immerse yourself in old world glamour and style then you will not be disappointed by it. Just around the corner is a lovely bar at St Bart's which is relaxing and food is lovely. Waldorf is a great central location to get to the sights and I would recommend this hotel as an ideal base.

title: Great Experience
body:
Stayed for 4 nights in a suite and later upgraded to a luxury suite. The hotel is as grand as I expected it to be, and the staff was excellent, specially Jessica who checked us in and took care of us throughout the stay. Walking distance to Central Park, Broadway, shops and restaurants this is a must for anyone traveling to NYC, will return.
NOTE: Breakfast buffet at Oscar's is expensive and not memorable.

title: A trip back in time
body: We did a two night post cruise at the Waldorf as my Mum who is 81 has never stayed there so it was a special occasion. We enjoyed our two nights there, room well maintained and superbly located on the 26th floor (Concierge Level) with great city views and we had a lovely dinner at the Bull and Bear Restaurant, enjoying the famous Waldorf Salad, superb rack of lamb, and New York Cheese cake (expensive but worth it!). That said one has to take into account that this is a hotel which is has been around for a long time so it does not offer anything for those looking for modern amenities ... if your looking for that type of hotel then you need to look at the Conrad or Westin....this hotel has its own character and eccentricities e.g. the the bathrooms are a bit dated and you need to have patience with the plumbing, lifts are the originals ones but fantastic experience,...but it all makes it part of the stay in a hotel of this age and the only negative I found was that whilst the staff in the Bull & Bear were very friendly, as well as the Concierge staff too, the Reception staff did not really make you feel that welcome and gave me the impression of "going through the check-in motions" ...which when you pay $500.00 a night you´d expect a little more warmth to their welcome!

title: Wonderful stay at the Waldorf
body: Stayed for 4 nights, hotel is very ornate and old style luxurious, highly maintained and clean throughout, staff and overall customer service excellent would recommend this hotel if you want an iconic location to stay close to all places of interest. As all over New York don't be put off by the scaffolding outside the main entrance as its everywhere in New York but you tend not to notice it after a while, room a little noisy from the traffic at night but think that would be same everywhere in New York

title: Horrible Experience At Waldorf with Pictures to prove it!
body:
My experience at the Waldorf was horrible. The check-in was slow but the place is busy so I had no issue. I had to wait about 20 minutes. 
I believe I was given a room which should have been offline and since I booked through Priceline they decided to give me one of their not so nice rooms. I called the front desk to find out if they could change my room but I was told they had no other rooms available so then I just sucked it up.
After my stay on August 8th I sent an email with the photos attached to their guest relations email but have yet to hear back from anyone. 
I would have expected better from the Waldorf.

title: What else can you say about such a historical venue?
body: We were astonished when our tour company told us they had fixed us up with a stay in the marvellous Waldorf Astoria as part of our package. For historic value alone it was breathtaking and given that it is such a opulent hotel it was extremely good value. Our room was on the tenth floor, very nicely decorated and as one would expect in excellent order. The staff mostly were extremely helpful, particularly Michael on the theatre desk and Elliott on the transport desk who were always courteous and never condescending (unlike some on the reception desks). A brilliant central location ideal for a long weekend or that extra special treat.

title: Met my expectations
body: The hotel is classy and beautiful, it has a lot of character and it met all my expectations. The size of the room and the hallways was big for NYC, if you compare with newer hotels. The room was very clean and although we didn't have a good view, we were never in the room - so it wasn't important after all. The lobby bar was always welcoming and fun, they had live music and the service was great. The location was good for a first time in NYC, close to central park, times square, 5th Ave., subway stations, etc. Free WiFi in the lobby only.

title: Lots of wow
body:
We booked 5 nights through Priceline and got a real bargain, but had to stay there just to say we did. There are renovations going on outside so maybe that's why were able to stay for $200 a night.
Let me say this place is nice! Our room was big enough for two rooms in some hotels and it looked great. We overlooked Park Avenue from the 9th floor.
We didn't eat at the hotel because it's certainly very pricey. The staff was extremely good and everything was spotless.
It is well located for most activities and we always felt safe in the neighbourhood.
One little thing that bugged me was they charge $16 per day for wifi that most hotels offer for free. It seemed a little odd for a "premium" hotel
It would be an incredible place if you had an unlimited budget, but if money matters to you at all you'd best think hard about this one.

title: Waldorf Hotel New York
body: Had to stay there because of the name, however a little disappointed. We arrived at midnight. Travelling from 7.30am in the morning so we were very tired. i have 3 children 8, 11 and 14 and they were exhausted. Although the foyer area was quiet, it still took them 1hr to check us in. we asked if the kids could eat something and their response was "the kitchen is closed". They mixed up our rooms and were disappointed with the way everything was handled. even though the rooms were nice and didnt have a problem for the remainder of the stay, it left a bad impression and probably would not stay there again.

title: Beautiful Old World Hotel
body: My wife and I spent our wedding anniversary at the Waldorf. We had never stayed there before. It was a wonderful experience. Our room was large, tall ceilings, with a beautiful view overlooking Park Avenue. The bed and the pillows were incredibly comfortable. The bathroom was large and finished with marble, very elegant. The hallways outside our room were wide, beautifully decorated and well maintained. We knew we were in a special place. We had cocktails in the bar right off the Main Lobby, which were unusual and delicious. Our waiter was excellent, going so far as to bring my wife a small sample of one of the ingredients in her cocktail when she asked him about it. Check in and check out were a breeze. The location of the hotel was perfect, we could walk almost everywhere. When we took a cab, the doorman grabbed us one right away. It was a perfect weekend in a nearly perfect hotel.

title: Great Stay, the most comfortable beds
body:
I loved my time at the Astoria. From the location, customer service, housekeepers, the bed, and the gym, it is perfect. 
We came for business and we were so pleased with the interaction with the staff on how responsive they were and helpful they were with their suggestions. The housekeepers were very accommodating and very professional. 
The beds are something I could stay on all day, and the Gym is better than some gyms I have paid for.

title: Best pillows ever
body: Good bits first. Very nice polite staff and the reception area is very grand. Beds our lovely and the pillows are by far the best i have ever had the pleasure to rest my head on. Bar is very nice if you like to spend $31 on one beer and a vodka with sprite. Stayed in a queen bed room which apart from the bed was the same as any 3 star hotel. Bathroom was small and no better than a holiday inn or comfort hotel. On the whole this is a good hotel if you get a great deal but not if you are looking for 5 star rooms. Can only speak for the Cheapest double bedroom not the suites. Great time in NY but would look at staying in a different hotel next time.

title: Five Star Service lives
body:
Having worked in a customer service role for ten years and having spend a lot of time in hotel rooms travelling with work I am more often than not disappointed with the service I receive. Recently I have found myself being surprised if my expectations are even met. However I am pleased to say our trip to the Waldorf Astoria was such an incredible experience my belief that five star service is out there is back. 
David and I flew out to New York to get married. When we told Wayne who checked us in, he immediately upgraded our room, and handed us tickets for a complimentary drink at Peacock Alley Bar and a complimentary breakfast at Oscars (which was exceptional). On our wedding day we came back to Peacock Alley for champagne and a second drink came with their compliments. None of which we asked for or expected. 
Every staff member we encountered was helpful, friendly and always said hello when passing in the corridors.
The rooms were exceptionally clean and smelt great (unusual for a hotel) with great art deco decor. The bed was amazing, the most comfortable I've ever slept in, including my own! 
I cannot say anything negative about our stay and are so grateful to all the staff at the Waldorf for going over and above to make our stay that little bit more special. We both can't wait to come back and will be recommending the Waldorf Astoria to everyone.

title: Beautiful Hotel and the best bed you've ever slept on...
body: Despite the construction blocking the entrance to the stately hotel, the accommodations are top notch. The lobby is beautiful and the staff is very nice. Our room was on the 7th floor with a city view. The room was clean and very quiet. We could not hear any outside noise. I'm not joking about the bed either - I fell asleep in minutes and did not want to get up. It was so comfortable! The hotel is quite glamorous and really caters to their clientele. I highly recommend this hotel for any type of celebration or a "just because" stay. You can tell the hotel was old - but it had an charm about it that you really can't explain. A must see for anyone staying in New York City.

title: All its cracked up to be
body:
Yes, this is a classic, awesome hotel. Great location just a few blocks from 5th Avenue and Times Square and surrounded by great restaurants and bars.
The front entrance is under construction which is the only disappointment. The lobby is classic and grand. The staff was top notch at check-in and throughout the hotel. 
The rooms are a nice size for a NYC hotel. Very comfortable, clean with no complaints.
