Had drinks at Bull & Bear Bar and Sir Harry's and both are elegant and what you would expect at this landmark. Did not eat here but found a nice sushi place on 33rd called Nomado 33. 
This hotel should be on your bucket list.

title: Beautiful Landmark Hotel
body: I thought this hotel was beautiful and had a great location (heart of midtown). It was very close to Grand Central Station, which was very convenient. The atmosphere is def for an older crowd, not the young hip scene (so it was quiet and kinda boring to be honest). Otherwise the room was wonderful and spacious for NYC. Service was great, no complaints.

title: a big disappointment
body:
I was looking forward to this hotel more than the rest on our recent trip to USA, so disappointed. I know it is old, being built in 1930, but the smell on the 23rd floor as you got out of the elevator was offensive and like it was from 1930 it smelled so old and musty. Luckily once in our room the smell was trapped outside, the tiny double bed was bad, my husband is 6 feet 4 inches so feet hung over the end. we were certainly snug trying to both stay in the bed together.
i did ask if all the floors smelled this bad, they seemed in denial.... First i was offered another room for an extra $400 per night, then $300 a nights, then finally a smaller room for an extra $79 per night, they missed the point, it stunk. we then were shown 2 other floors (12th and 8th), they did not smell as bad as the 23rd floor, but the noise would have been worse room smaller and had to pay more!!!!!! so put up with the stench for 6 days. this was the most expensive hotel we stayed at but by far the worst. I am comparing to Bellagio in Vegas over $100 cheaper per night but flawless, Hard Rock Hotel in Orlando, again $100 cheaper per night and Ritz Carlton LA again $100 a night cheaper, but no comparison. I had to prepare myself each time we went to the floor covering my nose and mouth and run to our room. we wanted to do the hotel tour, but the 23rd floor smell cured that idea, we spent as little time on the hotel as possible, no food, no drinks, no time... all was better spent as far away as possible. When we booked we were offered an upgrade to the towers for $39 per night, which i accepted, but was told when we got there it was not avaialble after speaking with other guests and other people apparently it is never available. I loved New York and intend to return but NOT to the Waldorf Astoria. If you wish to see it just go to the lobby, that is as good as it gets.

title: Classic Elegance and 5 Star Service
body:
I have just read a review from someone who stayed in the Waldorf for their wedding in NYC and thought I could have written exactly the same thing!! 
We were gettting married in New York last week and chose the Waldorf Astoria as our hotel for the week as we really liked the history behind it, had seen it in numerous films and also liked the location of it for ease of sightseeing.
I wasnt necessarily expecting anything amazing, I had read reviews on here and also had friends who had stayed stating that it was a little bit 'tired' although they still felt that it was a 'grand' place to stay.
We had mentioned when booking that we were getting married in NYC and the lady at check in mentioned this to us. She handed us an envelope saying that was a little wedding gift to us (which was a voucher for some cocktails in Peacock Alley). She then preceeded to say she would see if she could upgrade us (it may have been our honeymoon but we were still in a budget so had only booked a standard room). We ended up getting a beautiful one bedroom suite - view wasnt amazing but I wasnt expecting a view in a midtown location so wasnt disappointed. The room was extremely spacious and the bed was the most comfortable bed we have ever slept in. Since coming home we have 'googled' where they get their pillows from as we want to recreate the experience at home - have never had a nights sleep like I have here!!
The living area of the room was lovely, very elegant and when the photographer met us on our wedding day we had some beautiful photos taken in here, so really added to the memories of the day.
When we arrived back from our wedding, there was a bottle of champagne waiting for us in the room, with a tray of chocolate covered strawberries, a nice little treat which we enjoyed for breakfast the next day!
We couldnt fault the service that we encountered - I didnt really expect to get any special treatment for our wedding because this is something that they deal with everyday and from the calibre of guests they have, I just thought we'd feel quite anonymous as if we didnt really matter to them, but by the end of the trip I felt the complete opposite. All the staff were extremely friendly, and even random cleaning staff in the corridors always said hello and wished us a good day.
The only slight thing that let the side down was that when we had our cocktails in Peacock Alley, the waiting staff, although friendly, were extremely slow and I felt like they were just chatting amongst themselves most of the time, such a contrast when everyone else had seemed so attentive. They are forgiven as the cocktails were lovely and overall it was a good experience but they could definitely do with a slight improvement.
If I could afford it, I would definitely stay in this hotel again - It was a shame that certain areas in the hotel were closed due to refurbishment as I would have loved to have seen them but I'm sure that they will be beautiful once finished. 
Yes, the hotel might not be to everyones tastes but if you are looking for timeless elegance with old fashioned service to match then this is definitely somewhere that should try at least once!!

title: treated like royalty
body: I admit my review is colored by the fact that we got a ridiculously amazing upgrade for no apparent reason from a regular double queen room to a HUGE luxury suite that rivals anything I've ever seen in a Manhattan hotel size wise (hilton honors, AE Gold?). A nice entry way/foyer with bar, a gigantic living room (HUGE), a great bedroom area, then a large space off the bedroom with a chaise lounge and oversized mirror (the largest I've ever seen) and a cool bathroom with two sinks, bath and shower (and the hot water actually worked) and the bed was super comfie with great linens. So we really enjoyed our stay, service was attentive, the Bull and Bear was cozy and nice for drinks (okay, yes, the drinks are crazy overpriced at $19-21 a cocktail - literally) but since we had such a huge space, we enjoyed wine in the room and invited friends over. We were at the Waldorf to see the Chamber Magician who was awesome (Steve Cohen - don't miss him!). So for a one day NYC visit, we couldn't be happier with the hotel choice but again, we were treated very generously with an unexpected upgrade which was great and the staff was super friendly and helpful.

title: Unfortunately not worth the Prices Charged
body:
I have been to New York on numerous occasions, but this time decided to fulfil one thing on my 'to do' list so stayed at the Waldorf Astoria. I have always wanted to stay at this iconic hotel, and to be fair we got a pretty reasonable deal on Expedia, so went ahead and booked.
Unfortunately, the reason for the good deal is probably due to the extensive renovation work being done at the moment. This, however was not made clear at any point before we arrived. One evening they were even relaying the carpets so half the lobby was shut off! There was no noise from any of the works, but large parts of the hotel were shut off, including the Park Lane lobby which I had been looking forward to seeing.
The communal areas (that were open) in this hotel are simply stunning and of a very high quality. This includes the lobby, restaurants, ballroom, restrooms and the corridors to the hotel. The rooms however do not meet the same standard. Whilst they are kept clean they are very small in comparison to other hotel rooms, and the beds were smaller than a double. The beds were very comfortable and the pillows amazing, just not really big enough to sleep 2 comfortably.
One thing that really frustrated me was the lack of tea/coffee making facilities in the room, something I consider a basic in even cheap hotels. Apparently, they have recently been removed and now to get a drink you have to phone for room service - no prizes for why they want you to do this when it costs $5.75 per person for any room service and this is before you even order - so by the time you add on the service charge (yes this is extra) you would be looking at around $12 for a coffee - simply not acceptable. Despite this complaint when I did go down and spoke to the Peacock Alley restaurant and stated all I wanted was a take-out coffee for my room, and where could I get one seeing as it was 8pm and all the coffee shops in the area were shut - they did provide me one in a take out cup free of charge, so I thought this to be excellent service. They obviously saw my distress :)
I found the staff at this hotel to be very friendly and helpful, and staying here was good owing to the history of the hotel. However, the hotel does not justify the prices it charges any more due to the small rooms and overall lack of facilities at the hotel. Even with the deal we got, I could have stayed in a variety of other hotels that would have been around the same price, or cheaper, but would have got much more for our money.

title: beautiful and comfortable
body:
It was a surprise stay from my boyfriend as we wanted to have a memorable last night in NYC. He paid about US$360 for a junior suite, I think. It was really spacious and beautiful. Toiletries from Ferragamo, amenities incl iron and hairdryer. However something amuses me was that, I noticed in American hotels, they do not provide slippers and complimentary bottled water, unlike Asian hotels. Bfast and complimentary wi-fi were not included too.
We called housekeeping to request for toothpaste as we had ran out of it, but it took 3 calls before it was delivered. The housekeeping said in our 2nd call that they had delivered, but we didnt receive anything.
All in all, the room is really nice though nothing extraordinary. I love the English-styled interior. There's smth interesting about the lift doors as they look like just another room door. There is a spa, restaurant bar at lobby. It's within walking dist to Central Park and the high end boutiques in 5th Ave. The hotel is undergoing some renovation, thus we had to enter/exit by a route that was confusing.

title: Regeneration
body: My stay here between the 24th and the 27th of august 2012 was really memorable. This hotel is being recreated and this is really commendable.The place has really been transformed from the last time I was here which was in 2008. Security was fantastic,you can only gain access to the elevators with your room key card. I will definitely come back here.

title: A Trip to New York
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for a week in June 2012. This holiday was an expensive treat for us but as I’d never been to New York before we decided to do it in style. The rooms are lovely, very cosy, clean and comfortable. The food was great but we only ate once in the hotel as we wanted to venture out. It is expensive but certainly worth doing once. A typical round of drinks for 4 people (3 wines and a beer) costs approx £35 and a meal for 4 people (drinks included) is approx £350…depending on whether you have a starter/pudding etc. We also ate at the Smith and Wollensky Steakhouse and it was fantastic, again expensive, but if you only do it once it’s definitely worth it. It’s really buzzing too with a really good atmosphere. The other ‘must do’ place we ate was The River Café which is just the other side of the Brooklyn Bridge. This was the most expensive place we ate (total bill for 4 was approx £500) and food wise wasn’t actually as good as the other 2 above but the views are spectacular. We stumbled across an Irish Bar called the Pig n Whistle which was great. Great atmosphere, great food and very reasonably priced. In fact we drank here most nights as the atmosphere was so good.
We did all the usual tourist stuff. Central Park is lovely to walk around and we were lucky enough to have great weather. The Empire State Building is certainly worth a visit. We got roped into buying fast track tickets from guys outside but you don’t actually need them as you only save about 10 minutes. The bus tour is definitely worth doing. We went on the Gray Line tour and the guys who did the talking were brilliant, very funny, and informative and kept our attention the whole way. The World Trade Centre is emotional, as you would expect and certainly puts things into perspective. God Bless all those people who lost their lives…and their families. What they’ve done is a wonderful way to remember them. Be prepared for about an hour queuing though.
We did go shopping but to be honest England does have some great shopping malls now so I wasn’t as impressed as I thought I would be but then I didn’t go to shop, I wanted to see the sights and I wasn’t disappointed.

title: Unwavering service, great hospitality.
body: I travel on business quite a bit-needed a luxury hotel for my clients and myself, and was impressed after the recommendation from my favorite agents over at flymebusiness.com to stay here if I really wanted to make an impression. I figured I could make the splurge since my agent got me a super deal on my business class seats. My clients were very happy with their stay, admiring the decor and energy of the place. I hope to come back to this hotel when I'm back in New York. I should probably send my wonderful agent a gift basket for this recommendation.

title: Was a classic. Great Lobby. Not such great rooms.
body:
Stayed for a business conference at the Waldorf. It was a classic. The hotel is past its prime & relies more on its history. 
The staff was very professional. My room & the bathroom was very small and "worn." One of the smallest rooms I ever stayed in. A martini at the bar was $21. Valet parking takes over 30 minutes to get your car. 
You can see the best part of the Waldorf by walking through the lobby on your way to a better hotel.

title: Disappointingly ill-maintained and dirty, mouldy room.
body:
Stayed this summer for a weekend with the family. Room was large and at some point in the past would have been well appointed. Unfortunately we found mold ( or "mould" in the UK ) literally everywhere in the room and bathroom. See the attached pictures. The room card/key was added to show that the pictures are of our room.
Poor state of repair and shoddy patchwork especially on the doors and door frames.
Mattress' edge was also mouldy under the seam (picture was out of focus and could not upload it).
Nothing was done about it. Hotel was full and we could not be moved. Lots of apologies but no solution from the front desk. Pity. Service was otherwise average.
Food on Sunday morning was typical brunch fare and three times the price of the nearest spot, a block away.

title: Did not live up to expectations & poor customer information
body:
Having stayed at a number of American Historical hotels we decided to opt for the Waldorf on our recent visit to New York. 
On the good side, the room was not too small (2 queens, 2 adults and a 15 year old), clean and the beds were comfortable. However, due to building work on the front entrance we didn't have a good view of New York due to scaffolding, but this building work did not impact on our stay apart from having to use the back entrance on a number of occasions. The concierge was very helpful for restaurants etc 
We never ate at the hotel, however on returning from a long day sight seeing thought we would like a cocktail in the bar. It was only 9.30pm and the bar was shut! 
On another issue, on checking in, as is routine we were asked for a card. Perhaps with hindsight we should have used a credit card but instead used our pre-paid travel card as security. At no point during the check in process did the receptionist advise how much would be "held" on this card. We did not use any of the hotels services and assumed, foolishly, that nothing would be taken. 
It was only some 10 days later (having only stayed 5 days at the Waldorf) that this particular card was refused and it transpired that the hotel had taken a $500 "pending" amount which, to date, still has not been reimbursed, even though we are back in England!
We initially tried to call the hotel whilst still in America, but were kept hanging on without help or offering to be called back. Emails have never been answered and consequently I feel the service is shocking. Even a response to advise why there had been a delay would have been helpful. 
I feel very let down as I was looking forward to staying at this hotel during our visit and, by comparison to the other hotels we stayed in was the worst!

title: Worth the money!
body:
We stayed here with another couple in August and were not disappointed! We opted for the upgrade which was to a tower room. The rooms are beautiful and clean with high ceilings. The location is convient. The beds are comfortable and the bathrooms are large and elegant! The check-in was a bit disappointing. There were many people behind the counter, but no one was "available," I understand that they were probably busy doing something, but an acknowledgement would be nice for someone who is paying a good amount of money to stay in your hotel. The bull and bear steakhouse is a nice bar, but if you are looking for a quick, cheap drink this is not where you want to go.
Overall, the rooms are worth the money and we would love to stay here again and enjoy the free breakfast that comes with the tower upgrade.

title: NTC Holiday
body: Hotel is located only two blocks from 5th Avenue. Great location for seeing all that NYC has too offer. Close to Rock Center and St Patricks Church, and only about a twenty minute walk to Times Square and the Theatre District. Rooms were spacious and clean. Walk down to 2nd or 3rd Avenue for some not so expensive restaraunts. Got a great price for airfare and room from Cheap Tickets.

title: After all this is the Waldorf Astoria
body:
Spent 3 nights in the Hotel, great service.
Loved the room and beds, Location is amazing.
We were there while renovation happened so the outside was all covered and inside the hotel they had work happening at night in the lobby so it was very loud to a point you could not sit and have a drink.

title: Once was enough.
body: My husband and I recently traveled to New York City in celebration of our wedding anniversary. We wanted to stay someplace extra special and chose the Waldorf based on its historic background, reputation as a top property and location. The location did not disappoint us, however, upon our arrival and after having settled in, we decided to try and grab some lunch at Oscars. My husband ordered a meal from the menu. After 20 minutes we had to ask the status of the meal and it should be noted that the restaurant was not busy. When he received his burger, he was presented with french fries that a very long black hair in then plate. We got up and left and of course did not pay for the meal and never returned. The renovations caused confusion at the front of the hotel as we were told to go out through the back entrance, even though access to the street was open. Renovating is obviously needed as there is a dingy, yellow dated look to the hallways of the hotel (wallpaper was also pealing). On a positive note, the staff was accommodating (ie., our tub, sink and toilet did not work/drain correctly, but they immediately addressed these issues). The room was nice, but again, is in serious need of updating... not great for the price, just nice. The bed was very comfortable but coffee makers and the replenishing of the coffee cups and coffee are not the norm. Also our room over a seven night period was never vacuumed. Overall, staying at the Waldorf did not diminish the great time we had during our week stay. But next time we travel to NYC, we will definitely stay somewhere else.

title: Mythic Hotel
body: We booked one bedroom suite (num A10) that could easy accommodates 4 people, the room is huge. With its legendary lobby, the service as well as the staff, everything was just outstanding for this mythic Hotel. I would definitely recommend this hotel for romance and business as well as for families of 4.

title: Luxury hotel
body:
I have stayed at the Waldorf Astoria before and loved it which is why I decided to stay here again. The location is excellent as it is just a short walk to Grand Central Station which has several subway lines running through it. Times square is just a short walk away where there are many bars and restaurants and another large subway station. Fifth avenue is just two blocks away which is perfect for shopping. The hotel is very luxurious and grand inside. There was no queue at reception to check in so we were very quick. We stayed on the 15th floor and unfortunately did not have a view as beautiful as last time (the Chrysler building), but this was to be expected. Our room was fairly spacious and the beds were extremely comfortable. There was a huge TV and a desk/vanity. The air conditioning was adjustable too. The bathroom was lovely and clean and had plenty of room for beauty products in the cabinet. The shower was nice and powerful too. There was plenty of hanging space in the wardrobe and there were a few drawers in the chest. There was also a mini fridge with a large selection of drinks and snacks. The staff at the hotel were all very lovely and always greeted you when you would pass them in the hall. 
The front of the hotel was undergoing renovations so unfortunately we could not access the hotel from the Park Avenue entrance and had to use the Lextington entrance. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting New York as the location is perfect as it is not too near the bright lights of Times Square but is close enough to walk there. It is well worth the extra money for this hotel as you really do get what you pay for.

title: Still A Great Place To Stay
body:
I stayed at the Waldorf many years ago and again last week. It is no longer the 5 star grand edifice it was, but it is still a great hotel and an unbeatable location which will never change.
Yes, it could use some updating, but I love the art deco style in and around the lobby area that has been maintained. The walls between rooms are solid. I like the privacy this allows rather than the paper thin walls I found in the more modern hotels. 
The location in eastside mid-town is outstanding. The subway entrance at 51st and Lexington is convenient and with a little effort in understanding the subway routing map, you can get anywhere very easily. Buy the MetroCard and use the subway to get around. The subway system works and the cars are air conditioned (the subway station itself during the summer is very warm and uncomfortable).
I found the staff friendly and helpful.

title: SUPER OLD SMELLY ROOMS
body:
I am a huge Hilton and Waldorf Astoria fan - but was HUGELY disappointed by this hotel. I love all the bars in the hotel, the grand entrance, the front desk staff - but the room - how do I put it - was simply awful.
I swear the chair looked like it was the same chair that had been thier since they opened and had never been cleaned. THere was no way to get any temperature control in the room. You had to walk down 10 different hallways to get to my room and I was a Hilton Gold Member. If you have no status - do not stay here even just for the bars. You can come in and see the lobby and enjoy that. THe hotel is not worth the price.

title: A Classic hotel but...
body: We stayed in the Waldorf in mid-August and I was underwhelmed to say the least. They are doing construction on the entrance so be prepared to use the car park walk-way and wait with lots of other people for two elevators to take you to the lobby for check in. However, the check in was smooth and the staff were friendly. It is a grand and beautiful hotel with a top notch location to be sure, but way overpriced for the service received. There is no in-room coffee, no newspapers at your door, no complimentary breakfasts, and the in-hotel restaurant stopped food service at 10:30 forcing you to use room service if you needed something to eat. (I know, grand hotels don't need to use the "perks" to get you to come back because they are just that - grand hotels.) But I must admit, the bed and pillows were some of the best ever for getting a good nights rest and the room was spacious and comfortable.

title: Wow, the Waldorf and all that, but...
body:
Without question, the Waldorf is a very prestigious hotel. The location can't be beat and the decor of the hotel was pretty amazing. The staff were amazingly good at their jobs, and everyone was very friendly and helpful. The lobby was beautiful. It was really a privilege to be able to stay there with my beautiful new wife.
The room...ehh. The amenities were very nice and my wife really wanted to steal the pillows, but the room was not as clean as I would have expected. There was dust behind tables and a hair in the shower, among some other admittedly minor things. Do I care about stuff like that? No, not really. But when you bill yourself as a 'luxury hotel' in the middle of the biggest city in the world, make sure you can back it up. 
Otherwise I can't complain. It was pretty awesome.

title: nice but you need to be rich to eat in the hotel
body: The best aspects of the hotel are its position in new york and the very friendly staff.The room was a little dated but adequate. My main problem was the cost of eating in the hotel.My party consisted of two granparents and two teenage grandchildren.We arrived before the room was ready and had travelled from washington so a meal was in order. We went to the Peacock restaurant which was located just by the lobby.My grandson ordered burger and fries 32 dollars.The real stunner was when we went for breakfast in Oscars. No prices displayed and only buffet breakfast available.The breakfast was good and plenty of choice but no better than the one I had in the Omni shoreham in washington for 23 dollars.The bill came for breakfast in oscars at the waldorf 191 dollars for 4,acost of 44 dollars plus tax.

title: Great stay at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC!
body: I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria on the evening of September 4th, 2012. Delays into LaGuardia Airport caused me to arrive well after the check-in time of 3pm. I arrived at the front desk at 11:30pm and was told that the king bed room that I had reserved was no longer available. To compensate, I was upgraded to a luxury room with two queen beds, a sitting room and a beautiful art deco bath. Double the square footage to boot! What a treat after a long day of travel. This is my 4th time staying at the Waldorf and each time I am reminded of what a great value it is for the service and the location in Mid-Town. Great lobby bar/restaurant as well. Thanks to Andrew from Deleware who gave my husband and me great tips on where to eat. All in all, a terrific stay!

title: Because you can!
body: I stayed only one night at the Waldorf during my week long trip to NYC. It being my first trip to NY and I wanted to experience as much as possible from the city. The first 2 nights I stayed overlooking the iconic Central Park, which was beautiful. The Waldorf, too is one of those Iconic NY landmarks and I wished to experience a stay. I have to say at this point, the room rates were extremely reasonable compared to other hotels in midtown NY, and I was pleasantly surprised when I was upgraded to a suite :) The classic decor and ambience of hotel was what I was expecting and I enjoyed just sitting in the lobby bar, drinking a champagne, listening to the piano and people watching. Of course it was busy being July and full of tourists just like me but it was nice. The hotel was undergoing some sort of facelift, so the entrance was a bit tricky although this did not impact on my stay. The rooms were big, clean and comfortable, obviously if you look closely you will see some "age spots" but nothing of any concern. The location is central and an easy walk to all the midtown sights and shops. I ate out of the hotel with a friend on the night and the hotel recommendation of the little Italian within walking distance was excellent and appreciated. Anyway, I would recommend a stay here, because you can and it is old time NYC.

title: a Great Waldorf and Cole Porter's piano.
body:
Great location in Midtown.
The Hotel was everything what we expected, Hotel lounge was even more than expectation, what a feeling entertained with live music played with Cole Porter’s piano, extra vibes for Pianist and us, with same time fantastic cocktails.
We stayed at seven nights and legendary service as well as the staff were all very lovely, the queue at reception to check in and out were very quick. Concierges gave us good tips for very best and different jazz clubs, etc. 
The room was comfortable and spacious enough for us, the bed were comfortable too with very best pillows, the wardrobe has room for luggage and the bathroom was lovely, powerful shower and plenty of room, in the mornings was newspaper at our door. The air conditioning was adjustable.
We stayed in the Hotel in July, the front of the hotel was undergoing renovations, so we used mostly the Lexington entrance which was also closer to several subway lines.
Value for money, we would definitely recommend this hotel for couples

title: Charming Ole 'Lady'
body:
Unfortunately we didn't have a room at the towers but at the 'normal' hotel, but it didn't matter, the hotel is an old fasioned hotel with a location and a history that cannot be surpassed.
The lobby is extremely beautiful - any minute one could expect to see Bogart or some other 30's star looming in the hallways.
We arrived directly from JFK and was greeted at the check in which was fast with friendly and professional staff.
The room was great - rather large from NY standards, and the bathroom was beautiful - small but enough room.
The perks a the hotel is, as mentioned by others, close to non-existing:
No in-room coffee, no newspapers at your door, no complimentary breakfast etc and the pricing at the in-hotel restaurants are pretty expensive - but hey it's New York City for 'ya, and there's plenty of restaurants nearby.
As mentioned the hotel is old fashioned, but there's wifi is in lobby only and not in the rooms -  why ? In this day and age wifi is standard in nearly all other hotels, so why not here ?
If deemed too expensive then why not charge e.g 5 usd pr room for wifi ?
But that said we had a really nice time a the Waldorf Astoria.

title: Great times at the Waldorf
body: We stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria fron August 23rd to August 27th, 2012. This was part of a 5 day motorcoach excursion from Ottawa. The hotel is very central where you can explore midtown Manhattan on your own easily reaching the Rockeffeller Centre, Central Park and Broadway through the Theatre District to Times Square. Although the Park Avenue lobbey was under construction during our stay and completely closed-up, we really enjoyed our surroundings in this fantastic building. Our room on the 7th floor was nice, clean and adequate. The staff we met in the hallway was always nice and polite. On the second last day of our visit, for a small fee, we had a guided tour of the hotel, seeing the Grand Ball room and the different suites. We did not dine in the many restaurants however, there are many small eateries just a few blocks around the hotel. The green downtown loop of the Gray Line "Hop On - Hop Off" bus stops beside the hotel on 49th avenue (stop #17) which makes it easy for anyone to visit any part of downtown. We really enjoyed our stay and would recommend this grand hotel to anyone wishing to appreciate New Yourk City.

title: A Step back In History
body: We had a wonderful 4 night stay at this grand old lady in August 2012. It was like steping back in time. From the wonderful & very helpful doormen throught to excellent domestic staff we had a delightful stay. The only saddness was that renovations of the outside were occuring - so the glory of thisbuidling was underwraps. However this was quicly made up for the richness and ambience inside. One surprise was that there was no coffee or tea making facilities in the room - otherwise no complaints. I would recommend staying there on either a Thursday or a Saturday - which we didn't) as thay run tours of the Waldorf Astoria - how I wish I could have done that. Maybe next time?

title: A landmark hotel, but rooms are outdated
body:
It's a classic hotel with a rich history. The location in the heart of Midtown is hard to beat. The lobby is impressive, the staff very friendly and helpful. But the rooms seem like they haven't been refurbished since its glorious days in the mid-twentieth century. I found my room to be reasonably clean and comfortable nevertheless. 
But what really put me off is that things didn't work as I expected them to work. There was no way to control the air-conditioning, which was cooling down my room too much. The hotel staff was helpful and brought me a space heater. But I couldn't help feeling a bit weird sitting next to a heater while it was warm outside on the street.
There was a cheap looking flat-screen TV in the room, which didn't fit with the furniture. And it didn't work either. I had sound but no picture. 
I wouldn't complain about this in an average no-name hotel. But from the Waldorf I expected more.

title: Lovely Historic Detail . . .
body: Spent 2 nights. Wonderful location close to everything. Main lobby just renovated and brings back the grandeur such an establishment should have. Need to extend renovations to rooms to maintain a high end status. Room was OK, clean and beds very comfortable. Lack of amenities such as coffee, water, hair dryer a working remote control for tv. These amenities are available at Hilton Gardens but not at the Waldorf?? Even tv has only about 12 channels!! Of course I was not in NY to watch tv so that was not much of an issue. Would recommend a stay to at least see it but in present state it did not live up to my expectations.

title: Lots of character.
body: The room had a great view of the city. The room was on the 42nd (top) floor so needed a room window air conditioner to supplement the central air as it was so high up. It was a little noisy to have it running and didn't quite cool the room down as much as good central air would have but it was OK. For the price per night it should have been more than OK. Lots of construction going on in the hotel at the moment. The lobby and public spaces are beautiful. The rooms are very nice. The front desk staff was impolite when we checked out but all others were fine. The decor even in the ladies' room and elevators was quite amazing.

title: Not the epitome of service and grandeur
body:
We had high expectations of service from a hotel that we thought would be the epitome of service and grandeur. Our stay started off on a negative service note when we checked in. There are separate check in desks for gold and diamond members. Since both had guests ahead of us, we waited in front of the diamond desk. When the gold desk clerk finished with his guest, he summoned a guest who was waiting in line in the general check in area. While he was helping that guest we asked the other clerk (there were 2 clerks at the desk) if he could help us since we were diamond members and wondered if we could check in at the gold member desk. He said yes but he would help us as soon as he was done. Just thought that it would have been nice for him to have asked us if we needed help since we were waiting in the diamond line right next to his desk. Anyway, epitome of service and grandeur the Waldorf Astoria is not. First the positives: the room was large and the ceilings very high. The bathtub was the largest I have ever seen. I'm 6 feet tall so it was the first time I was able to stretch my legs out in a tub without having my knees stick out of the water. We were given two complimentary coupons for cocktails which we enjoyed in the bar. Would have liked to have been able to order appetizers but all that was available was nuts and olives. Some of the negatives. There were 2 wash clothes in the bathroom that was piled in a heap next to the Kleenex box. Not sure if the maid forgot to shape it into an arrangement or if they were previously used. Was not able to connect to the complimentary wifi service. The first night I called for service and did not receive assistance til after we left for a show. When we got back that night, the service tech left a note that the problem was fixed. I did not try to get online til the next day and found that I still could not connect with my ipad. So I called again and no service tech showed up and we left for a tour. When we got back 6 hours later, we still had no connection so I gave up because we had to leave for another show. 
 The view from the room was the roof of a lower level. It was strewn with litter and some construction debris. We realize that the hotel is under renovation but some effort should have been made in cleaning up some of the litter so the view from the window is not so unsightly. Our contact with the waiter, bellman, concierge and doormen were not remarkable. No one seemed to go out of there way to give extra service or friendliness such as we recieved from the Le Parker Meridien New York City the previous night.

title: A grand old faded relic
body:
An iconic hotel that is now sadly begining to show its age. Stayed here after a transatlantic passage in September 2012 for 2 nights. The staff where excellent and very polite however, there where not enough staff on the desks at reception and we where kept waiting for 20 minites to check in which for a hotel of this calibre and price is just not unacceptable. The hotel with it's ballroom and special function rooms must have been spectacular at its peak, sadly the rooms and overall decor now seem a bit jaded and it just seemed to be dark everywhere.
A few saving graces was the concierge who was able to obtain tickets for a Broadway show when other outlets failed (albiet at a price) and a very good central location.

title: Historical Hotel with dated rooms and weird crowd in the lobby
body:
I booked the hotel for a quick weekend trip to NYC. I had high expectations given the price I paid for per night (over $450 per night). The lobby is grand, but it was ruined by the crowd that seems to always be hanging out there. And it's not that the check-in/check-out was slow, it was actually very fast. It just felt like people were sitting on the chairs there, staring, chatting, reading newspaper. It made me feel like I was at a public house or a coffee shop, not a landmark hotel. 
The room was cozy, I got upgraded to a King bed room that's decently-sized. But here are the two major complaints I had: 
1. For every channel that worked, at least 2 channels were not working. So out of the 30 or 40 channels on TV, probably only 15 worked. I mean you are a four or five star hotel, get your cable company over and fix the dam channels. Or don't show them at all! 
2. There was no hair blow dryer in my room/closet. I looked for it every where, including the "on top of the shelf in the closet" they told me. I called the guest service and asked for a hair blow dryer, Cynthia (I think that's the name of the girl) said "are you sure you don't have one?" I am sorry, if I already have a hair blow dryer, you think I want to call you and ask for an additional one? On top of that, the first time I called, 10 minutes later and still no blow dryer, I had to call them back and ask them not to come because we had to go out and we had a dog in room. The second time I called, the woman (someone else) asked the same question if I am sure I don't have one, I almost exploded. Then 30 minutes later without a hair blow dryer, I was ready to go down to lobby with wet hair and yell at someone like a crazy woman, someone finally came with the dryer. I cannot believe it took that long for someone to send me a hair blow dryer. For a hotel like this, 10 min should be the maximum wait time. Now if you are Holiday Inn, maybe 20min...
Would I be back to the hotel? Probably not. There are too many other good hotels to choose from in NYC. In fact, I already booked Setai Fifth Ave for our Nov trip. We will see.

title: Oldorf/Newdorf
body: Upon arriving with my wife and two children and learning the room would not have the two beds requested,the helpful,patient and professionally courteous front desk clerk informed us,as we had to dash off to the theater,our room would be ready by the time we came back. As promised along with drink vouchers we had the two bed room. Ok, this is the Waldorf...the room was small, it's New York, however the bathroom was very small and cramped, the paint on the bathroom door, that had to be an original door, was painted over so many times with no prep work, it looked like a tenement apartment. That along with the tattered base boards and worn rug, I could not believe this was one of the jewels of New York City. A discussion with the manager ensued and the next day we were moved to the Towers portion of the Waldorf. Separate entrance and elevator, bright hallways clean and spacious rooms. concierge area with complementry breakfast, chocolate covered strawberries sent to the room on my birthday ,this is what one would expect from the Waldorf. The hotel's main lobby was beautiful and the location could not have been better. It's a historic hotel with with excellent staff, but stay in the Newdorf and not the Oldorf.

title: Disappointing Stay
body: Stayed in August over a long weekend with family - 2 rooms. We are HH Diamond members. Both rooms not ready at check-in. 1 ready at 4PM so we all checked in there while we waited on 2nd room. By 5PM, still not ready. Another trip to the lobby. Moved us to a different room. This room had a bad musty odor. Another trip to the lobby. Moved to a room in the towers. Room OK, but very dated (peeling wallpaper, doors that won't close, etc). Upon checkout, took valet 1.5 hours to retrieve car. Will be moving back to the Hilton or HGI in Times Square next trip.

title: dripping with history
body:
I have been staying at this hotel for over a decade and had the pleasure of being on property during the unveiling of a months long remodel of the Park Avenue lobby. What a room ! Honoring the fabulous Art Deco motif, the room is brighter and a sleeker. Just grab a coffee and hang out in this bustling spot for a bit.. This updating is also going on in the rooms where I have experienced a mix of REALLY tired old rooms, and just plain tired old rooms. This past stay I had a fabulously updated room with marble bath and vanity and a walk in shower. It was a deluxe King room. 
The staff is professional and formal without any pretense. The front-desk check in/check-out process can queue up from time to time. But you can be greatly entertained by the comings and goings in the lobby during your wait.
You can't beat the location for Times Square, Central Park, Broadway, Rockefeller Center, or the Metropolitan Museum of Art - if you have your walking shoes on. They are all within walking distance. Catch the Subway a block away for a ride downtown if needed.
It's not often you have the opportunity to be in such a place literally dripping with history. If you can get over the fact you may not have a whiz-bang room, this is the place to stay in mid-town.
Or, just request one of the updated rooms and perfect your stay

title: Could have been great but...
body:
This is a beautiful, older property but seems to be overlooking, or neglecting, so smaller issues.
First, the positives: 1) the Park Ave entrance has reopened allowing guests to take full advantage of the hotel's convenient mid-town location; 2) public areas are gorgeous; 3) elevators seem to do a decent job of handling all the guests; 4) mattress and pillows are very comfortable; 5) some nice touches such as an umbrella and robes in the rooms, a non slip mat in the bathroom, and several luggage stands tucked away in the closet.
Now the areas for improvement: 1) mold in the bathroom - around the tub and even on the ceiling; 2) heavy layers of paint, especially in the bathroom, are cracking and peeling away; 3) the blackout shades are a joke - by sunrise the room was quite bright; 4) surprisingly, there was no turn down service.
Overall, the experience was fine but the location was the only significant benefit to staying here.

title: Loved the Waldorf
body:
We had a group of 6 people who were supposed to spend a week in NYC, but at the last minute, we had to cancel one reservation for 3 people. The Waldorf staff was extremely accommodating with the cancellation. 
Three of us continued on with our trip and checked into the Waldorf. The location was great and the concierge suggested a fantastic restaurant around the corner from the hotel. 
We did have one challenge, which was resolved well above our expectations. The hotel had a flood which affected our room. The hotel staff moved us from the Waldorf to the Waldorf Towers. We felt that the staff and management truly understood the impact the flood had on us and took very good care of us during the remainder of our trip. I'm sure we would have still be very happy in the Waldorf, but I'm pretty sure when I return to NYC, I'd want to stay in the Towers again.

title: Rather dated
body: The lobby in the Waldorf Astoria is impressive and it is well-located. However our room was quite small and in general it was nothing special. I wouldn't particularly recommend it unless you get a good deal (which we did).

title: Always a great stay
body: Once again while in New York We stayed in the Waldorf. Service from booking till departure is nothing short of great. All the staff went out of the way to assist including organising and booking events to attend for us. Although it was dissapointing the foyer was be renovated we did the tour of the Hotel and got to see areas not normally seen including some of the special suites. All the of the restaurants and bars provided great food and drinks as well as exceptional service. Special Thanks to John the concierge who organised a great 4th July cruise for us.

title: Not what we had expected from such an iconic name
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria as part of a package arranged by Cunard after crossing from Southampton to New York on the Queen Mary which all went very well indeed. At the end of the trip we were transferred (together with a number of other guests) to the Waldorf Astoria hotel by Cunard. The entrance was very unimpressive since it was covered by scaffolding and we were taken round to a side entrance where there appeared to be no proper reception for us and our luggage. The driver of our transport tried to contact someone but to no avail and we just milled about not knowing where to go or whether we should wait for luggage to be taken to our room. It was all very haphazard and chaotic to say the least. Eventually a porter arrived and said he would take care of all the luggage and that we should check in at the main entrance some distance from where we were dropped off.
We did this and the reception clerk said our room was not ready but that it would definitely be ready by 3pm. at the latest and he took our mobile number and said he would contact us if the room was ready earlier, as he thought it would be. 
We were quite anxious to change before going out in the city as it was very hot but this was not possible.
We went out and about and returned at 3pm. as we had not heard anything to find that the room was STILL not ready.
We then had to wait a further two hours before the room was available. The reception clerk offered us two free drink vouchers but we did not think that was generous for the inconvenience we had suffered and we asked to see the manager.
She was apologetic and we asked if they would make breakfast available for the three mornings we were there as we had booked on a "room only" basis. She then offered to give us $150.00 dollars credit on our account to spend with them as we wished and we accepted this,thinking that would easily pay for three breakfasts.
We went down to breakfast the next morning and had the buffet breakfast which was nice and then got the bill which came to$118.00 including the mandatory service charge of 18%!!!
Apart from this we were very disappointed that there was a lot of work going on in the hotel including a full strip up and relay of the floor area in the main lobby which went on in the evening when we were hoping to have a quiet drink in the bar and listen to some music.
The room was quite nice but no WiFi which normally we find free, even in modest hotels, and the general service was adequate but in comparison to the fantastic service we had just enjoyed on the Queen Mary it all seemed a little offhand and casual.
New York was super and we had a great time there and in fairness the concierge service in the hotel was really excellent,so 3 stars is all we could manage for this VERY expensive hotel.

title: Nice, traditional hotel in a great location!
body:
I have just gotten back from NYC, watching the US Open. During my stay the lobby entrance which connects it to the main lobby/reception was being restored. Not a problem, and after all, is was worth seeing it brand new!
I had an upgrade to a jr. suite and it was amazing. Lots of space for luggage, desk, drawers everywhere, eletronic safe, tv in both room and living room. Bathroom was OK, but I found it a little too small for a 5* standard.
Everyone at the front desk was always thoughtful and helpful towards all my needs. So was the bell service. Housekeeping did its job well everyday.
Good thing about the hotel is its location. It sits on an entire block between Park Avenue and Lexington Avenue, and 49th and 50th. (49th is the only street with no access to the hotel).
You can just walk to 5th Avenue or even to Times Square.
I wont't give this hotel a 5* rating because everything is way too expensive (USD 16 for a bottle of water, for example).
if you are looking for a traditional hotel with good service, great location and lots of glamour, this hotel will easily fit your needs. It has so much history that you can even have a tour of the hotel with breakfast included (cost of USD 50 per person, of course).

title: What a Disappointment
body:
We were looking forward to be part of history at the Waldorf!!! Not really, We got there around 02:00PM after a long journey and not enough sleep, the building is under renovation from the outside all around (WILL BE COMPLETED IN 8 YEARS). Main entrance on Park Ave was closed, Car had to go through 50th street to a side street entrance, waiting in line of cards (single lane), dropped off the luggage on the side, luggage were tagged then we walked up few steps to take an elevator up one floor then walked to the lobby. Had to wait in line in a crowded lobby for 15 minutes, room was not ready, asked to come back in an hour or so.. came back 90 minutes later, still not ready, they gave us a couple of tickets for drinks at the lounge..had the drinks and waited for about 45 minutes. Went to the front desk and asked for the manager who checked what was going on with our suite..few minutes later were told to go to our room and gave us the keys..It was almost 05:00 PM..It was a very nice spacious suite at the 17th floor on Park Ave..which was great..The windows were fuzzy and obstructed with construction materials.
The furniture is very old and outdated, the rugs and pictures on the wall were not well maintained and poorly designed, lamps did not have working light pulps, curtains and shades were outdated, bathroom is huge but missing some towels and amenities. Elevators use room cards to access your floor and it was a challenge to make the card works and responds to make it work. The hotel shop did not have a good service, the young lady in the shop had an attitude and was not very cooperative to help the customers, I wanted to buy one of their jackets with the hotel emblem but did not have my size. I was told they have it in the stock room but could not get it right away and they would contact me at my room when they bring it.. No one contacted me for 24 hrs..when I went to check if they got it, I found another employee who did not know anything about what I was talking about!!! I got mad and walked away.
Our flight out of New York was late in the afternoon, I asked for a late checkout and I was told not possible (Although I am a Hilton Honor Gold Member). After an argument, I was given until 01:45 PM to check out...By the way, the business center has nothing for free, I had to pay for Internet, printer, and fax via my credit card...
We stayed there for 4 nights but I do not think I enjoyed my stay and I would not go back to this hotel (at least for the next 8 years)????????

title: Too many annoying details on an aging property for the price
body: If you like old style hotels, this is what is supposed to look like. But for that price, you would assume that the furnitures in the room not be scratchy and damaged, that the bath would have been modernised since the 70, that they would not charge you $20 a day for internet connection (not a wifi), etc..They seem to pass serious time going from room to room to maintain but really it is a major revamping that is needed.

title: Fantastic!!!!
body:
My son and I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria from the 30 August until 4 September 2012 and we could not have asked for a better hotel to stay. And the weather was brilliant too.....Everything was perfect. We had a problem with a leak and damaged cameras...but the staff promptly moved our room and paid for all the damages.
My sister had stayed here for her 30th and I thought I'd do the same for my 50th. From the time we arrived we were treated like important guests. 
The breakfast is pricey in the actually hotel, so we found one just across the road, an all day breakfast place....the people in there were so nice and so was the food,
In fact the whole experience of being in New York will never be forgotten, it has left us with nothing but brilliant memories.
Thank you to all the staff for making that happen :)

title: Slightly disappointed
body:
Been before so knew what to expect. We were informed by Virgin that the Park Ave entrance was being refurbished which was fair enough, we knew Starbucks was closed also. What they failed to tell us was that half the hotel was closed off too, including Sir Harry's bar & the piano bar.
So poor communication on their part.
We weren't too bothered as there was still two other bars plus a huge array of choice outside of the hotel.
One thing to note also is that the toilets are being refurbished too so you have to get the lift to the third floor for a pee, not ideal.
We did get a room upgrade with a balcony & a huge closet which was great, there were a few frayed edges regarding decor but all in all very happy with the room.
As is tradition we had a meal in the Bull & Bear which was fantastic. 
All things considered a great experience, just not too impressed with Virgin not giving us the heads up regarding the works.

title: Service with a smile
body: I have read a few recent reviews and have to agree that the outside scaffolding does take something away from this Grand Hotel. However I have stayed here previously and the scaffolding will not always be there. All my previous visits to the Waldorf have been because I could get a great deal and this time was no exception. This time I had a 2 double double rooms for a cheaper price than a Holiday Inn Express. i use the Waldorf because it is in a great position for the tourist. The rooms are not modern or spacious but they are clean and very comfortable. Free wi fi is available in the Lobby but only available free in the rooms if you were a higher level Hilton Honours guest than I was. I do feel that in todays modern techno age it should be free to everyone but I have stayed in many luxury hotels throughout the world and a lot do charge ridiculous prices for internet connections. However some top hotels are completely free, especially if you hold their Loyalty Cards. The service in the hotel is without question First Class. The price of everything is high but why not treat yourself if you come here. It is an experience you will talk about for a long time. I arrived in a stretch Limo (not too expensive if there are a few of you and you do your research) and was surprised not to have my cases whisked away immediately. On previous occasions my case was taken from me and delivered shortly afterwards to my room. This time we had to pull our wheeled cases through to the lobby. I did not eat or drink in the Hotel but have done so previously and been impressed with the service. This time I found some very nice Breakfast Diners within a 200 yards of the exit. Another good touristy thing is that the hop on hop off bus stops right outside the Hotel and I never had to wait more than twenty minutes. if you are reasonably able you can walk to Times Square, The Rock, Central Park and The Empire State Building without difficulty as Manhattan is very flat. To sum up this is an Iconic Hotel that I would encourage those that can afford it to stay in. The rooms are adequate and the service is tremendous. look for bargains.

title: Landmark Hotel & Great Location but...
body:
I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for 6 nights in late July when I was there with a group. I'll try to be concise and give some things I noticed during this stay.
1) The Park Avenue lobby entrance is under a major renovation (the famous one shown in movies) so you have to enter on the Lexington Avenue side or via the Valet Parking area. There is protective scaffolding that encircles the entire hotel - a complete eyesore and a pain if you are dragging suitcases while trying to get inside.
2) There is construction noise during the day depending on where you are staying in the hotel. When I was there the loud vibrations of saws were definitely annoying (I was on the Park Avenue side) The hotel was sold-out so I didn't bother complaining, especially since I was barely in the room during the day. Still - buyer beware.
3) Expect a line for check-in during peak times, I noted this everyday as I walked through the lobby. The staff is very nice and definitely keep the line moving but I came in from a 95 degree, 10 block walk with suitcases and was dismayed at seeing the long line. However, they have GREAT air conditioning so I cooled off quickly.
4) Hilton Hhonors members, even lowly nobodys like me, get 2 free waters per day from the mini-bar, just confirm this at check-in just in case.
5) Avoid the line at checkout - use the zip checkout option on the phone (TV checkout didn't work for me) I waited in line to checkout and they clerk advised me of the phone, I hadn't thought of that, even though I am a veteran traveler (lots of hotels have abandoned this since desks can be understaffed)
6) This is a landmark New York City hotel. Expect a high price, eclectic rooms, and of course strange smells, varying water temps/pressure, and weird noises. Like every New York City hotel (unless it is new construction and even then...) the Waldorf has its share of these. Easiest rule of thumb, don't get overly upset if you have no hot water. Give it 5 minutes and try again, that seems to work every time. These older hotels are very finicky.
7) The hotel is a great midtown location, close to Grand Central. Quick walk to the 6, E, and M trains at 51st and Lexington. Or if you are coming from downtown and went to skip the local, take the 4 or 5 to Grand Central and walk up - 10 minutes or so.
Overall, it was great to stay at a famous hotel on business. If it was my own money I doubt I'd pay the premium to stay here. New York City hotels serve a purpose, a place to shower and lay your head. Spend all of your time enjoying the best city in the world, not in your room.
Miscellaneous comment: The staff was very friendly and nice.

title: Great location in Central Manhattan
body:
I spent 5 nights at the Waldorf during Easter 2012.
The hotel has lots of charm and history and a luxurious art deco feel.
Rooms are very clean , quite a good size and have wonderfully comfortable beds.
The location is perfect for exploring Manhattan and is very close to Grand Central Station.
Room rates are very reasonable and I'd definitely stay there again.

title: Old School Glamour
body: The Waldorf Astoria is old school at it's best - the glamorous interiors thrill you on entering, the staff the most friendly I have ever encountered in a Manhattan hotel, the room spacious and luxurious. Everybody, and everything we encountered during our 4 night stay was beyond my expectations - even to the point of being offered an umbrella one morning on our way out, as "it may rain later". Champagne in the Peacock Ally is a must - to people watch, take in the beautiful decor, and simply enjoy a moment listening to the pianist play Cole Porter whilst New Yorks finest head out for the evening ...... The renovations do take a little away from the exterior, but once inside you are in a magical place where nothing seems to be too much trouble ....... the Waldorf Astoria cocoons you in a world where everything is just fine!

title: A Gem In Manhattan
body:
Although not very modernized this is still a terrific hotel in the middle of centtral Manhattan.
The rooms are quite nice.The beds very comfortable. The housekeeping very hospitable. Theyb try to make your styay a pleasure. 
The restaurants are kind of expensive but you can walk and find dining everywhere of any taste and every budget. The location is the best for tourists. You can walk pretty much to everything in central New York. 
Overall a great place to enjoy a stay in New York. If you want to venture furher you ca even walk down Lexingtion Avenue to the nearest subway station.

title: Over Priced
body: My wife and I stayed at the Waldorf for six nights. We thought we would only visit NY once so lets do it in style. When we arrive the place was surrounded by scaffolding as part of a facial/reception area(?) renovation--would have been less of a shock had we known. Room was a Deluxe (snobby speak for a standard room), the furniture was far too big for the room, so moving around with no shoes on was a bit tricky as there were some sharp corners; the spout where the water came into the bath was almost held in with some mastic, and the time it took to get the shower running each time was ridiculous. I also had to get an extra clean done because of sharp objects in a very old carpet. The renovation works also meant all we could see out of the window was scaffold and safety sheets. Room 1623 was our room, we should had asked for another or booked a superior I suppose but we had unpacked before we found these issues, so decided to stick it out. Service was very good, but everything is very expensive. A bottle of mineral water from the mini-bar is $8.71. And don't move ANYTHING in the mini-bar!! I was alerted to this by another reviewer; they will fix it for you (refund the charge, 'cos it registers if you pick something up), but it just more hassle. We did not manage to get a price list for the mini-bar, so be careful. The place is very nice and calm/controlled, but you know a couple of drinks in the bar in the evening will set you back $45--and their nothing special. Glad we did it but would not stay there again.

title: A bit shabby for the price
body: Agree with the comments below that the scaffolding outside the hotel, and outside my window was disappointing and the lack of warning was unprofessional. Stayed 2 nights in a junior suite but felt it had nothing to offer above a normal deluxe room. The bathroom was very tatty, and the carpet of the room looked like it had been there since the 50's. Another big frustration was the number of times I was put on hold when dialing room service or the front desk. It became a joke in the end. Staff were very pleasant, but overall not the experience I was expecting. Over-priced for what you get, despite the very good location. There are better options in the same area.

title: Not worth the money
body: This hotel has a great name, but in reality it is the worst five star hotel I have ever stayed. Old fashioned bathroom, rusty shower and although I am a deep sleeper, I've been waken up several times during the night by people speaking in the corridor.

title: Great location for Midtown attractions
body:
If you like your hotels modern and boutique-style, then don't choose the Waldorf Astoria. But, if you want something a bit different and a taste of how it used to be for the rich and famous (and still is for many!) then stay at the Waldorf - it is a little piece of history! We chose to stay at the Waldorf Astoria recently for our first trip to New York city and as part of my 60th birthday celebrations and we were not disappointed. We had requested a quiet room on one of the higher floors, away from the lift, and this is exactly what we got. Our room was 1775 - a large, corner room at the Lexington Avenue end of the building, with three big windows - one giving us a perfect view of the Chrysler Building. The bed was mega-comfortable with deep mattress and huge pillows - absolute heaven to sink into at the end of a tiring day of sight-seeing and walking the city. There were a couple of armchairs and a huge flat screen T.V., plus a large desk with mirror above. The bathroom was small but beautifully appointed and above all, the whole place was beautifully clean. Our room was serviced every day by our lovely cheerful maid to a very high standard. Not a bed-bug in sight (although we did go armed with bed-bug spray which we never had to use, thank goodness!). Our check-in was handled very efficiently and pleasantly, plus we were given complimentary drinks vouchers to use in any of the three hotel bars as a gesture towards my birthday celebrations. The hotel itself is amazing and has retained its air of grandeur, with art deco galore. The newly renovated lobby (on the Park Avenue entrance) is a breath-taking marvel of marble and art deco - we took loads of photos but they really don't do it justice. 
The hotel was perfectly situated for what we wanted to do in the city - Rockefeller Centre, Grand Central Terminal, Chrysler Building, Radio City Music Hall were all within easy walking distance. There is a subway entrance a couple of blocks down on Lexington Avenue, so easy to get your Metro Cards and use the subway if you want to, which we did when visiting Lower Manhattan, Greenwich Village and Central Pak. We did not eat in the hotel as could not afford their prices, but there are plenty of good restaurants in the local area to choose from, plus delis galore to get breakfast in. We used the local Starbucks every morning to get our early morning tea and coffee fix before going out for the day. 
Only drawbacks:- air con in the room was a little noisy (but we used ear-plugs so didn't really bother us) and no free internet in the rooms which, considering the hotel is used by a lot of people on business trips and people can access the internet via their mobiles, seems rather out-dated these days. These two things are the only reason why I have not given the hotel a five star rating for our stay. But only small things - on the whole, we really enjoyed staying there.

title: clean and comfortable, great location
body: we were able to walk many places from the hotel. Penn station only a short cab ride away ($10). nice, helpful staff. do not eat here, very overpriced, even for NYC. many great options just a few blocks away. would stay here again. beautiful atmosphere.

title: Class and style
body:
Stayed at the Waldorf on a recent trip to New York with my Mum. I chose this hotel for its history and elegance, for which we were not disappointed. On arrival the lobby was beautiful and transports you back to a different era.
Although our rooms were not ready when we arrived, we were checked in and left our bags with George (the extremey helpful and friendly concierge). We were sent a text to confirm when our rooms were ready, which was also helpful. 
The rooms were of a good size, with great views over St Bart's Church. The beds were incredibly comfortable. After a full day of walking the Manhatten blocks, it was a welcome comfort. The rooms were kept cool, which enabled you to snuggle into your duvet; although we were shown hw to adjust the temperature, should we need to. 
The hotel's location is exellent as well. Close walk to Bloomingdales and Time Square. 
The two downsides that prevent me from giving an Exellent rating were: 1) there was no kettle or tea/coffee making facilties, which is a must in my opnion; 2) there wasn't a mixture of pillow types. The pillows were all hard, which suited me, but my mum prefers soft. Other hotels I have stayed in have a selection, so you can find what suits.

title: Disappointed
body:
We had pretty low expectations coming to the Waldorf because of its age and assumed outdatedness, we apparently had not set the bar low enough. We travel quite a bit and like to stay at some of the nicer and more historical hotels around the world. This was the main reason we booked the Waldorf, more of a sentimental favorite really. Plus this was a relatively dead time at the hotel so we could get a nicer room at a better rate. We expected the rooms to be in bad shape and the furniture worn and rustic-check. We expected everything to be way overpriced and of modest quality-check. What we did not expect was the service and room offerings to be so disappointing. 
It all started at check in. I had paid for the room all weeks in advance to get a discounted rate. So knowing check in was at 3 I didn't think we would have much issue showing up at 7 pm. Wrong. The backed up checkin line told the whole story. While the hotel did not seem very full, rooms were not ready "due to the cleaning staff falling behind" or so we were told. So 4 hours after checkin we were told to go hang out at the bar and maybe in another hour or so a room would be ready. Oh I forgot to mention the girl did offer me an upgraded room if I didn't mind paying a slight up charge of 199$ additional per night. Ill pass. At this point after she clicked around on the computer for 15 minutes I asked to speak to a service manager. She said ok but then seemed to click it into gear and start looking harder for a room. About 5 mins later she says that she has a room, then she doesn't, then she steps away to talk to someone and comes back with a room. About 25 mins in total standing at the front desk, this is after sitting in line a while watching them do this to other guests. So off to a bad start.
Next we get to our room, just a basic king superior room w no frills. We settle in to find the mini fridge leaking water all over the floor. I had smelled the musty odor upon entry but it took me a few mins to find the puddle. Also one of the lamp lights was broken so we killed 2 birds w one stone and called for maintenance. They did come and fix the light, as for the fridge we came back to a slightly less leaking unit with towels laid out on the floor below it- classy Waldorf.
Don't let me forget they were having water issues during our stay as we came back one day to find a notice that our water would be completely shut off from 10pm til the next day. Not a few hours mind you but half a day, sadly it didn't surprise us, almost expected at this point. I had to double check my bill to be sure we were at the Waldorf and not the Super 8.
Our other major letdown came at the Bull and Bear Steakhouse. I've been there a few times before and the service is hit or miss. This day we had reservations for dinner and sat in the main dining area. Service was so slow. Rarely did anyone come over to assist w wine or water options. Almost unbelievable compared to the service at similar level restaurants around the U.S. after ordering steaks it was over 45 minutes until we saw our food and the restaurant was not slammed in the least. Our bill was about 300$ for 2 and I wish we would have just hit up the Shake Shack again, so sad. Steaks had little flavor really. I did enjoy the au gratin potatoes tho!
Overall this was a big bummer of a trip to an old legend. Hopefully with all the renovations they are doing they will overhaul the service as well. A few things we did like: toiletries were great! The ferragamo shampoos and soap stuff was awesome, probably some of my favorite out there. I also got a lot of use out of the alarm clock/iPhone charger, very handy you don't need to bring your cord!

title: amazing experience
body:
wonderful hotel,staff couldnt do enough for us. We were there for my daughters 18th birthday and they upgraded us to a suite and gave us cocktail vouchers to celebrate. the staff were all lovely, the hotel perfect. rooms immaculately cleaned every day. hotel central so easy for sights.
only tiny negative would be no coffee making facilities in room.

title: Waldorf Wonderful
body: My spouse and I planned a special weekend in Manhattan and chose to stay at the Waldorf Astoria. The grande dame delivered an excellent experience. The front desk greet us cheerfully and got us promptly to our room, even though we had arrived several hours early. The lobby was immaculate and filled with guests waiting for friends or just relaxing in its ambiance. Our room was spacious, immaculate and well appointed, giving the appearance of a recent makeover. The bathroom was large, with the quality of fixtures one would expect from this property. The hotel's location in the middle of Manhattan makes it convenient to trains and any point on the island.

title: A piece of American History, opulence.
body:
The greatest hotel experience ever. From the moment you walk in off Park Avenue you know you have arrived somewhere special. The plush interiors the glorious reception all smack of Art Deco opulence. To know of all the stars that have graced this old dames makes you feel part of the experience, you can still sense their prescience as you stroll the corridors. The room is so original it it was a real treat to stay there, some say this place is tired looking, but I have to disagree, if they were to modernise this wonderful hotel the charm would be taken away. It is a place to soak in history and we loved it. The bed is a dream, every night I muttered I love you to the wonderful mattress and bedding. The little touches like the original lit light switches and your own front door bell all add to this perfect experience. Please keep this hotel as original as you can. Location wise, how good 2 blocks over from 5th Ave, just a block down to Grand Central, 10 mins from Rockerfeller, the same time to Central Park, times Square was 15 mins away. This hotel is not the cheapest in New York, but it was worth every cent! We shall return.
Long live The Waldorf Astoria.

title: Magical .... as expected
body: We like a few others had some issues checking in and had a problem with our room but so what! Mistakes happen, people are human and the staff were extremely apologetic and more than made up for the errors. This didn't spoil our stay at all. We stayed in a beautiful room looking South towards Grand Central Station. Naturally it's expensive, it's on one of the most desirable streets in the World and this coupled with the heritage, history and character of the hotel makes it feel magical as soon as you walk in off Park Avenue. We were lucky enough to enjoy breakfast - Eggs Benedict, given that it was invented here, we felt it was a must. If you are looking for new furniture, new carpets and a fresh brightness then forget it. If like us, you want to experience true old world New York, dark wood, art deco, dated furniture (sometimes on the tired side), then this hotel is for you. Oh and Marty who helps hail a cab on Park Avenue just tops it off. When you chat to him you just know you're in "New Yoik" !

title: Very nice, but not as luxurious as expected
body: My husband and I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for one night to celebrate our anniversary in NYC. We waited in line to check in at the lobby, although the line was unexpectedly long, it was our turn to check in rather quickly. We really didn't mind the wait, we were so excited to be there. The gentleman checking us in was extremely nice and professional, and very helpful as he made a reservation for us at the Bull and Bear while we checked in. I had also mentioned it was our anniversary when I made the reservation over the telephone and the hotel provided 2 complimentary drinks for us, which was a great way to start the weekend! We had also opted to purchase an upgrade during the reservation process, if it was available at checkin. The gentleman saw that, and did upgrade our room from a standard queen to a luxury queen for only $59 extra. Considering this was the Waldorf, we didn't think this was a bad deal. Before we went to our room, we had our complimentary drinks at the Peackock Alley bar, right across from the lobby. Everyone there seemed very happy to be there, as were we! We finally made it into our room, and I have to say, I was a little disappointed. Afterall, we did upgrade to the luxury room. Besides it being a larger room, it really wasn't very luxurious. Although the room was clean, and the bed was comfortable, I was expecting more luxury.The luxury the Waldorf is prestigiously known for. Perhaps newer bedding, drapes, carpeting and furniture would have been nice? Everything was very dated. The bathroom drain ring was missing and you could see straight down the drain. Not something you really want to see, especially in the Waldorf. We ate at the Bear and Bull before we went to our show for the evening and we were expecting pretty high standards, unfortunately, we were disappointed again. The food was extremely expensive and just OK. The restaurant was also kind of empty... Overall, we might go to the Waldorf again, but I think I'd do some research to find something a little nicer. We did enjoy our weekend and the older room didn't spoil it. The location of the Waldorf is great, as it's in the middle of everything, broadway, shopping and plenty of restaurants. If you can get a room for a decent rate, then go for it. But if you want to splurge, I'd find another luxury hotel to go to. Sorry:(

title: Throwback Elegance
body: I took my daughter to New York for the end of fashion week. Since we have stayed at the Waldorf on previous occasions, we were familiar with the hotel. But the experience only gets better with time....as does this Waldorf! Mary at the Diamond desk is the best! David (hotel mgr.) was great as he made my daughter feel as if she was the one in the fashion show! Great accommodations and service by ALL! Sunday brunch is probably the best in the city......stop eating on Thursday if you plan to attend!

title: Heaven
body: We recently spent a night at the Waldorf Astoria, all I can say is WOW! we got one of our rooms early in the morning, so we had the continental breakfast on the 26th floor. This was no ordinary breakfast, there was bottled water Voss, omg, I could not believe it. There was fresh deli meats Ham and Turkey. Lox, all types of teas and more.
