Our room was great, we stayed in the Towers, when you stepped off the elevator it was as if you had stepped into Buckingham Palace. The bed, oh the bed, when I fnally got to bed I swear the comforters welcomed me and enclosed me in their warmth. It was like I was floating, I slept like a baby. The staff was very nice and I enjoyed the Piano player Saturday night in the Lobby. I would love to go back again..There was a group of 20 we had a great time.

title: 5 days @ the Waldorf
body:
I and ny wife spent 5 days at the Waldorf Astoria from September 14 to Sept 19.
Except for the first night, the stay was wonderful. The first night we were on the 9th floor overlooking Lexington Ave. Since we are used to it being quiet at night, it was very difficult because of the noise from the constant traffic.
The next day with the help of Aileen of the hotel staff, we moved to a much quieter room on the 13th floor that was in a much quieter section of the hotel.
The hotel is a mixture of modern and old style decor and the main entrance on Park Avenue was reopened the week we arrived. They had restored it to it's former glory by revealing the mosaic floor as well as making the whole foyer come alive. They have also redone the Starlight ball room as well. We managed to see this a part of our tour package except for the Startlight room as President Obama was due to visit that day. We saw the magnificent 4 floor salon which had just finished shows as part of fashion week.
the hotel rooms them selves are an eclectic mix. For example in our bathroom, the taps for the shower were at one end of the tub and the shower head was at the other.
The mixture of old style furniture with modern TVs and Cisco routers takes getting used to but one gets used to it.
The food is fabulous but expensive. On Sunday night we had a light dinner at Peacock Alley. It consisted of a Waldorf salad each and an order of Lobster Sliders along with a couple of drinks each. it was excellent and cost $168.
I recommend a stay at the hotel once in ones lifetime.
if you can afford the stay it is worth it.

title: Not all it's cracked up to be...
body:
Very noisy room (2616) where I could hear every lift grinding it's way up to the upper floors, and on top of my $299/night I had to pay $19 a day for internet access....$19 for each device!! Mad... 
Also the windows are absolutely filthy. Not what you'd expect of a supposed 5 star hotel.

title: Jubilee getaway
body:
We flew into JFK weekend of the queens jubilee a warm welcome at the reception, speedy check in first room we were put in was grotty BUT having stayed here before complained and the duty manager arranged a room move and upgrade we were given a junior suite which was very nice during our weeks stay we also had president Obama stay in the hotel over night, good service all round, New York was as good as ever, it was nice to see it in the summer as we have only ever seen it in the winter no wind chill factor this time! Excellent food & drink. Good flights with BA.
Will return soon.

title: Elegant Hotel with Historic Reception
body: The lobby and entry way are historic for this classic hotel. Service is wonderful including maid service and the concierge. Monies being spent on the lobby, however, should be spent on the rooms. My son and his new wife were given a dated room suite with peeling wall paper and a closet that couldn't fit her wedding dress. Our room was fine, but the television wouldn't work for two days as a guest disconnected the cable for our part of the floor and refused to cooperate to plug it back in. I'm a Hilton Honors member and consciously try and book rooms accordingly. The pictures of the new couple in the lobby were priceless as the new lobby renovations opened just in time. This fine lady deserves a 4 out of 5 for her historical beauty.

title: Iconic, but is that good enough?
body:
We stayed 5 days at the Waldorf, and really had no cause for complant.
The doorman, the concierge, the check staff, are all what you would expect from such a renowned hotel.
We stayed in a deluxe suite (one bedroom, one loung room & two ensuite bathrooms). 
Which was a free upgrade from what we had booked.
The rooms themselves where spacious & decorated in a manner befitting the period. 
The bathrooms, though old in style, worked well, so again no complaints.
No free WIFi in the room, and only congested (ie un-usable) free WiFi in the lobby. 
The hotel is huge, so there is a lack of personal intimacy that is evident in smaller boutique hotels. And there is a hefty price put on the "extras", ie phone calls, mini bar, meals, WiFi.
I get the impression that people are going to go there, just because it is iconic. Hence the hotel does not have to try, to keep, or attract new patrons. Subsequently, you can probably get better value for money elsewhere in Manhattan. You are paying a price premium to stay at an icon. However they did adjust our bill when we complained about a US$50 New York to LA phone call, so they are still geared toward customer satisfaction. 
Would I recommend it?
Yes, just to say you have stayed in it. But it is not that special to justify a prolonged stay.
There are better, cheaper, less-iconic options available.

title: Disappointment in the Big Apple
body: Big diappointment in the Waldorf after years of absence. The hotel accomodations were wonderful from location to lobby, but not the room at almost $600 per night. Room 764 was noisy and the bathroom was a large disappointment with extremely tight quarters, cleanliness, and limited hot water. I was told by staff when I complained about having to take a cold shower one evening that it may take 15 minutes in the am to get hot water for the shower. My cold shower was in the early evening and I never got hot water after 15 minutes.

title: The Waldorf is the Wonderful!
body: I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria this last week and was extremely pleased with the whole experience. The Hotel is a true piece of history, wonderful to explore and enjoy. The rooms are lovely and well maintained. The staff is helpful and kind. I would recommend the Waldorf to anyone planning to visit New York and want a memorable stay there.

title: Beautiful Hotel
body: Stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for 3 nights prior to boarding a cruise. The hotel is beautiful and full of character. We had a superior double/double to sleep our family of 4. Rooms were spacious and the beds were super comfy. No tea or coffee making facilities which was a little disappointing considering how much we had paid. Food and drinks were pricey so didn't eat or drink at the hotel. There's a great breakfast van (Tony's breakfasts' just over the road where you can get a bagal with Bacon, egg, sausage for $3.50...bargain and tastes really good!!! Well located between Park Avenue and Lexington Avenue. Close to Central Station. Easy walk to all the sights and central Park. About a 20 minute walk to Times Square straight up 49th street. Would recommend this hotel.

title: Nice hotel but needs some work
body:
We arrived to this hotel around 11AM via taxi and the 'unloading' process was a bit chaotic. You need to pull into a 'garage' and there was a long line of cars that stalled us. The bellman took our luggage right away and advised us that it would be brought up the room when it was ready.
We entered the hotel and was greeted by a nice guy at reception. He spent about 10 minutes trying to find us a room with two double beds. He found one but it wasn't ready yet, so he took our cell number and invited us back in a couple hours. About two hours later I received a text message saying the room was ready. We returned and picked up our keys and went up the room. We opened the door and immediately were overcome by a strong odour of urine. My travel partner started to gag. It was disgusting and embarrassing that the Waldorf would actually invite a guest into that environment. So with a hand over my nose, I called guest services and was on hold for about 15 minutes. As I waited I found food on the floor from the previous guest. Gross. Eventually the operator came back on and told me to go downstairs to the front desk. In other words, they did not help us at all. 
So down we go and noticed there was a huge lineup. I found someone who ushered us to the front of the line and we were greeted by a gentleman who apologized for the issue and offered to find us another room right away. He searched for what seemed like 15 minutes and could not locate a room with two double beds. So he gave us an upgraded suite with one king bed and a pull out sofa. He also sent up a roll-away bed. 
The suite itself was very spacious. Incredibly spacious for New York. It was also cleaner and not smelly. However, the bathroom was incredibly small. Very unproportionate. While the suite was clean, it was definitely dated and you could tell there was wear. As an aside, the sheets for the pull-out sofa had long black hairs all over them. I assume it was from a previous guest and maybe they had not been cleaned? Gross. I called housekeeping to send fresh ones up which they did.
On the last evening of our three-night stay we were surprised to find a nice fruit/chocolate tray in our room for no apparent reason. It was a really nice touch and made my travel partner smile. 
We stayed at the hotel during the start of the UN General Assembly and it was really neat to see the elegance that presented itself with all of the visiting heads of state and dignitaries. I wonder if these folks stay in the same type of room that we were given, if so, I would feel a bit bad for them. The hotel definitely needs some renovation. 
We got a pretty good deal on the property. Would I pay full-price based on what is posted on the official website....NO!!! Not even worth half of the listed price. Too bad because the history on the hotel is amazing.

title: Great
body:
This was where we stayed for my first ever visit to New York, and boy was it good! Granted there was some cosmetic work being done on the building at the time, but it was something out of this world, you really feel like you've been thrown back in time :) Especially if you go and take a peek at the ballroom! 
Staff at check- in were more than helpful, our rooms weren't ready when we arrived and still weren't ready after we'd gone for dinner, so the staff sorted out some free upgrades for both rooms :D
The room was spacious, not a great view, but it is in the middle of mitdtown remember, so its all just roads and tower blocks. My only critisism of the room is that the windows can't be opened by guests, so you can't get any fresh air in the room, and I was feeling a bit under the weather after 7 days of Air-con :( 
The location is fab! The main selling point of the Hotel I would say, everything is either within walking distance or a very reasonable cab ride. Grand central staion is less than 500 yards away :D 
I don't think the hotel would be worth it if you were paying full price, eg without the upgrades and discount due to rennovation, but it is a very nice Hotel.

title: Distinctly average for a hotel of this calibre
body:
The Waldorf Astoria is a hotel with great history and a great reputation, unfortunately the service they give their ordinary guests does not meet this standard. I have not had to queue for more than 10 minutes to check in to a hotel purporting to be luxury before, but had to do so here on my recent visit.
The rooms are quite large for New York City and each is equipped with a large TV and a iPod dock/alarm clock. The bed was extremely comfortable and a variety of pillows were provided. I did not, however, see a pillow menu (though this may have been something I missed). The room was decorated in a classical style, but the decoration showed its age (the wallpaper even peeled slightly in one place). The bathroom also showed its age, and the faucet leaked when using the shower. The toilleteries provided were high quality feragamo products. 
There were also extra charges (or you were required to request) things that should have been provided for free. During my stay I requested a tea set (shocked that one was not already provided). This was brought without any tea. Wi-fi inside the hotel rooms is also an extra charge.
Overall, I had a comfortable stay but expected more.

title: Has seen better days.
body: Hotel is on the expensive side, but not out of place for Manhattan. Location is fantastic, central to all major attractions and shopping. Room was not vacuumed, which was disappointing. Amenities very ordinary. No extra service. Staff are helpful in the lobby but non-existent at the doors.

title: Beautiful, historic hotel
body: The Waldorf Astoria is beatiful and in a great location in midtown. It is within walking distance of Central Park, great shopping, and Times Square. The rooms are a little dated, but very nice. Our closet was huge- which was great to hang our clothes and store our luggage. The beds were very comfortable!

title: Our far from perfect Honeymoon.
body: The hotel was a real disappointment. We were expecting something really special for our honeymoon and it was special, just not in the way we had expected. We were made to wait for our room, on the promise that they were finding us something special. It was terrible. Holes in the carpet, chipped glass tables, helpfully at just the right height for our child's head. There were holes in the wall, broken fittings and the window seal was gone so we couldn't see out of it for condensation. Oh, and the bath was full of hair, none of it ours. Not exactly 5 star. In fairness they did move and upgrade us but it was not the way we had imagined starting our honeymoon. The other room was far better but there always seemed to be some issue with service - no one answering at the front desk 3 of the 4 times I called, waiting 50 minutes for toothpaste that didn't arrive, the toilet flooding, which was moped up by a lovely lady from room service but then the wet towels were just left there, nobody came to clear them up before we left over a day later. Overall the Waldorf seems to struggle with its size, unable to service the huge number of guests that pass through its admittedly spectacular doors. I would not recommend staying here, we were really disappointed. But at least it wasn't some important occasion like our honeymoon. Oh no, wait, it was.

title: First Class - as you would expect
body: Went to NYC for a bridesmaid luncheon for my niece. My sister-in-law talked me into staying at the Waldorf. I was not disappointed - it was great. Everything you would expect. Beautiful. Lovely rooms, (we had four and none is the same) great service, comfortable beds, expensive of course. It's not something I could afford to do probably more than once in my life - but it was a "memory" experience and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I recommend everyone do it once.

title: awful room
body: Booked a deluxe king and were given the most depressing room. We had a bed two bedside tables a dresser and one old arm chair. I don"t know how they have the gall to call that deluxe. The bathroom was very small and the sink unit was made of chipped formica. The staff are however very well trained and very friendly. The public rooms are grand if a little dated.

title: Classic old hotel, bit worn around the edges
body: Stayed on a room only basis. Was our first time in NYC and were not sure about where to stay. The reputation of the hotel is a lot grander than the hotel it's self. Staff very helpful, good location, but would choose a different hotel on a return trip.

title: Royalty Palace : )
body: The Waldorf Astoria is beautiful, charming and ecclectic. The service was excellent! I took my daughter for a graduation gift to NYC to shop and we stayed 3 nights. I LOVED the Waldorf. The historical feel is beyond words. So much of the old is still there with the modern touches of the new. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to have a life lasting impression of 5 star / royal/ top notch Hotel!

title: Terrible experience!!!
body:
I must say that I was very excited to stay there, however, my experience was terrible. This place needs some major renovation. The paper on the wall was peeling off. The chair in the room was dirty. My deluxe room had so much light peeping thru the windows and main door that I could not sleep for two nights when I was there. The air conditioner in the room was making so much noise..it was like helicopter right outside your window. 
The toilet was so bad..you have to flush it at least two times for everything in the bowl to disappear. And one time..during night..I flushed the toilet and water will not stop..the toilet kept running. This is not what you expect when you pay $700 per night for a room.
I must say that the location is great, otherwise it's a bad place to spend a night. Stay away from this place.
Also..I had to wait 20 mins in line to check out.

title: In dire need of a makeover
body: Stayed here on business. Very much the grand old dame but in need of a face lift. Rooms are a good size but tired. Staff who appear to have worked at the hotel for a very long time but clearly not enjoying it any longer. Service pretty unpredictable. At breakfast it took ages to get service, finally had to get up and fetch a waiter! Wouldn't stay here of choice. You could see the potential if a really good hotel group got its hands on it. However it's living on a bygone era.

title: Neat place to see but not to stay
body: Well, it is certainly a landmark with a lot of history and a great location - it is a shame that they haven't/couldn't keep the rooms in decent condition. Rooms experience equal to an old cheap $49 per night interstate motel.

title: The ONLY Place to Stay in New York City
body: Sure, NYC is a city with a million hotels, but there's only ONE Waldorf. This classy lady sure shows why she's been a landmark for...forever. Staff that jumped with enthusiasm, nice sized rooms and perfectly central to Central Park, Times Square and Rock Center....the lady is PERFECT. Check in is smooth and very refined...food is fantastic...every need or request immediately attended to....GREAT JOB ALL AROUND.....I booked through Magellan Tours and the rate sounded too good to be true...I'm very pleased to say that it was just as promised.

title: The best hotel in NYC
body: I love the Waldorf as it is by far the most grand hotel in all of NYC. From the moment you walk in you are greated by the breath taking lobby. My first stay I had a suite which had two double beds in the bedroom and a huge flat screen tv; a living room with a huge flat screen tv and a huge bathroom. It was my birthday so I was greeted with a bottle of champaign. My most recent stay this past June I stayed in a large room with a large bathroom and good closet space. My room also had a great view of Park Ave. The rooms are a good size are very clean and the beds are very comfy. I truly love the old world feel this hotel has. I would recomend this hotel to everyone. The staff is great. George the bellhop is very kind and will answer all your questions the best he can. Also Peacock Alley in the lobby serves great burger slidders and fries (however it is on the pricey side but it is the Waldorf after all).

title: Same old Waldorf
body:
This was my second stay at the Waldorf, and I think I can sum it up this way: you can stay at more luxurious hotels, but you can't replace the feeling of getting in a cab and saying, "Take me to the Waldorf". I can't tell you how many-odd cab drivers I've had to give directions to when I stayed at other hotels. But they all know the Waldorf. The rooms aren't updated and may not be worth the full price (watch for a deal instead), but the common areas are classic New York. The staff is amazingly helpful and polite - I think the "Broadway Tours" staff helped me with random things at least a half-dozen times in a few days: sending mail for me, calling the correct staff member for an odd request, etc. There's nice beds and bathrooms are decent (not updated, but clean), and large-ish televisions. Mention you're staying for a special occasion and the reception desk may find you an upgraded room and offer you free drink tickets for a celebration.
It's not the best location for walking to tourist spots, but there are quite a few restaurants within walking distance (and Grand Central for ANY train), and lots of stations for the 6 train nearby.
Oh, and go on the tour: we were in the Presidential Suite two days before the president visited - fun to go home and tell your friends you were in the same room as the president!

title: Classy Hotel with a wonderful Bed!
body: Loved the location as we made a weekend trip to New York City. Walked to Broadway for a show in less than 20 minutes and then it was less than 10 minutes to Grand Central Station to take the train the next day. The staff was extremely courteous and the bed was heavenly. It was a grand hotel. Only wished I could stay longer.

title: Great hotel, great location.
body:
Fantastic base to see the sights from. You can walk to most of the major sites including Times Sq & Broadway 15 mins, Rockerfeller 5 mins, Empire State 20 mins, Central Park 15 mins and with the tube station right next to the hotel the Statue of Liberty is only a short ride away.
The grandeur of the place will take your breath away as you walk in. Very helpful staff who cannot do enough to help. Some reviewers moaning about the rooms but we didn't notice anything shoddy. Okay, the odd door requires a lick of paint but nothing that you would rate down the hotel for. 
We upgraded our room to including a living room, not really needed but we though while were doing NYC we might as well do it in style. This also granted us a second bathroom, again not needed just a nice touch.
Had drinks in the bars, fair prices and good service however we ate at the Bull & Bear and in my opinion I found the food awful. My wife didn't think it was anything special either. We had the steaks, tough, chewy and full of gristle. I didn't tip and I didn't stay for dessert. 
There is an excellent Irish bar called Connolly's just around the corner that serves excellent home made food and I do mean excellent and at good pub prices. 
Would definately stay here the next time we visit the big apple.

title: Excellent as usual
body: Great place, great location, good value. Close to Grand Central Station and top of the Rock. Within walking distance to Times Square and Central Park. There is also a tour bus stop on the side of the hotel 49th street.

title: Great Hotel and Location AAA++++
body: First stay at the Waldorf, very pleased. Bed comfortable, staff friendly, great location in the city, walking distance to many attractions and subway. First class stay!!! Lot's of history in the Waldorf. Would return, highly recommended.

title: "Timeless Elegant Hotel "
body: Dreamed of staying at the Waldorf Astoria New York forever. Finally, had the opportunity to make the dream come true. It was better than we ever dreamed. Arrived by cab from NY Penn station, about a 10 minute ride under $10. Bellman were everywhere opening car doors and hotel doors. Entryway of white marble w coordinating white marble columns and not as grand as I expected. However, once entering lobby of hotel a rush of majesty and elegance was before you. Wonderful pattern carpet of jewel tones, golden twinkling chandeliers and old world dark wood furnishings with a host of service agents waiting to attend you. Was promptly escorted to service agent, greeted with a smile and received compliments on everything from my head to my toe. I was wearing Chanel and they notice. Reserved king suite in the Towers which we were excited to experience. The agent asked us to wait a moment so she could speak with her manager. Upon her return she stated she had approval to offer us other accommodations in the Tower. We said ok and were escorted through the small private entry of the Tower next to the beautiful lobby bar/restaurant. The elevator took us to the top of the Towers and upon exiting we immediately saw a security attendee posted on the floor. The hotel agent walked us to our surprise suite and open the door. As we entered the foyer all we could do was gaze in excitement and appreciation from what we were getting ready to experience. We had been upgraded to the Royal Suite Residence of the former Duke and Duchess of Windsor when they visited New York. The apartment was decorated in French furnishings with wall coverings of Tiffany blue with gold leaf patterns through the living and bedroom areas. From the baby grand piano, to the woven gold and cream carpet and to the magnificent fireplace, details of royalty abound. The dining room had a seating for sixteen with a small table for two placed along the window facing 50th Street. A small nook kitchen was off the dining area. A continuation of the French flavor flowed to the bedroom with a fireplace and sitting area. The residence suite entire length overlooked 50th street. Wow!! What a view!! The agent shortly left and all we could do was make calls on the phone about this upgrade at the treasured Waldorf Astoria New York. We were the envy of all we call. To make a long story shorter - we didn't get out much since it was a special occasion for us as a couple - the suite was so consuming, Ordered in mostly everyday. The bow tie service was impeccable and the food was delightful. We ate at the table for two and enjoyed the skyline and night lights. Yes, expect the pricing to be Waldorf Astoria pricing- after all it is the Waldorf Astoria. Enjoyed the signature Waldorf Astoria champagne and took a bottle home. Will keep the bottle forever! The City was great, but even better was the Royal Suite Tower Residence. Thank you Waldorf Astoria it will be an memory I will always treasure and hope to relive again!!!!

title: Excellent location, stay at the Towers!
body: Beautifully located in the city centre! Fifth Street runs parallel to it, second street up, whilst Centre Park is 10 mins walk. If you stay in New York and you do not have too much time this is the area you should try to book. We were upgraded to a Suite in the Towers and had a fantastic time there, it is not cheap but you feel you are part of history. The breakfast lounge in the morning was always busy and the selection is not very extensive however, there was always a choice of good quality pastries, breads, cereals, yogurth, fresh fruit, and smoked salmon. if you like eating the Sunday Brunch is recommended.

title: Cedric at reception made the stay
body:
Had a great experience checking in. Cedric at the front desk was super nice and was kind enough to give me an upgrade to a jr. suite. 
Room was clean and well equipped.
Only downside was that my room was on a low floor and picked up a fair amount of street noise (ambulances, etc...)

title: A "Grand" Hotel
body: We booked this hotel through Expedia at the very last minute because of the great deal we were able to get. When you step into this hotel, it really is like stepping back in time. Everything is so elegant and grand and you can imagine the many people that have passed through over the years. The room was neat and clean and the beds were very comfortable. Although, our bed was a full-size and a little tight compared to our king-size bed at home. Loved the big sitting window sill!

title: Old NYC charm
body: This iconic hotel is beautiful and charming. It is a lady of a hotel that boasts a grand entrance and spacious rooms. In a modern, fast paced world, it is nice to sit in the elegant lobby and imagine the stars, presidents and famous people who passed through her opulent hallways. A true treat sitting in one of the greatest cities in the world!

title: DONT LET THEM FOOL YOU
body:
The hotel is a part of history yes and the public rooms are grand. But in this day and age the powers at large arent into custome service or reputation in the future.
ROOM 
 My wife and I had an odd shaped room which had an alcove with a couch jammed in the corner making no sense to any deco. The couch was old, dated and something you would find in a dumpster. The shower was the size of a telephone booth if anyone remembers what that is. The heat was non-existant and the room was cold. The curtians were well worn and ripped. (room 1701) I travel a lot so IM not some dummy
SERVICE
i wanted coffee at 620 am and didnt want room serive to wake my wife up so I went to the lobby. NO COFFEE itll 7 I was told to go to the Starbucks located in the Marriott two blocks away.
Despit the hotel being "fully commintted" the wonderful "Harrys bar" was closed on Sunday nights....really? The in room mini bar features $20 for a can of beer $10 for a water
NO HOT TUB
Unless you join the spa for the day. $$$$
THE STAFF
Very nice all around but the problems that they deal with comes from the top of the chain whom only sight is $$$$ really $95 for brunch? The Bevely Hilton provides free coffee until the shop opens so does the Chicago Hilton NOT NY
If you go be prepared for grand public room but the hotel rooms tired. I do not understand how such an icon like the Waldoff could be in this kind of dissary. sad but the future of travel

title: Really tired and mediocre
body:
Don't believe all the hype about this place. It's in dire need of a top to bottom cleaning and refurbishing. The whole place is tired looking. The carpets in the rooms and hallways are worn. The one chair in our room (an upholstered, high-back, desk chair) was completely worn and almost unusable. 
The linens are wonderful -- but I don't like a soft bed -- and this bed was way too soft. The draperies are tired and look dusty. 
The hallways are also tired and need new carpet and painting. New lighting is needed in both the room and the hallways. 
The elevators are barely functional. You wait for about 15 minutes to get an elevator from your floor to the lobby. There seems to be no problem going the other way. But apparently the down elevator buttons on the guest floors don't signal the car to stop. So you end up using the up button to catch an elevator, ride to the top and then go down. It was annoying.
My advice -- do some research -- find nice accomodations. They are out there. When you're paying this kind of money, you shouldn't have to stay in worn, dingy rooms.

title: Old school glamour
body: Never thought I would be able to stay in the Waldorf, but an offer on Expedia was cheaper than the hotel I usually stay in when I go to New York. The building is amazing, so glamorous. Our room was perfectly comfortable, a good size, and luxurious bathroom. The hotel gym is basic, but very clean and served our needs. Whenever we needed service, the assistance was excellent. Great location. Only criticism would be that wifi wasn't free - if Starbucks can provide wifi for free, I would expect an expensive hotel to do the same!

title: Classic New York City
body: I have stayed at the Waldorf Astoria celebrating a number of special occasions. It is among our top choices when visiting NYC. I think that being a Hilton Honors member is helpful and you can request an upgrade (depending on your membership status) and a room with character. I say with character because really each of the rooms are unique. There's so much history at the Waldorf and you can imagine the glamour of the old days. On my 25th anniversary and on my 50th birthday, the hotel offered us two wonderful rooms, a bottle of champagne, and chocolate covered strawberries. We've eaten at Oscar's for breakfast, the Japanese restaurant for dinner, and the Peacock for breakfast and pre-dinner drink. While all are pricey (US dollars not Euros), they are all very good, particularly the Japanese restaurant. The Waldorf is centrally located in mid-town and is close to Madison and 5th Avenue (Saks Fifth Avenue), and Grand Central Station. I've also taken a nice walk up to the Asia Society.

title: AMAZING.... Will not stay anywhere else
body:
What more can I say about this Hotel than its beautiful, super clean, friendly, welcoming i could go on and on and on... WOW!
I visited New York with my boyfriend and friends in the first week of September and it was superb, the hotel was undergoing some renovation but never once seen a builder or a dust sheet nor did we hear a drill or rubble or any noise from these works.
The Hotel has the most beautiful ball room what could make you imagine you could be part of Phantom of the Opera it was captivating, along with the elegant hall ways and twinkling chandeliers, and all the staff are so friendly which are also a credit to the wonderful hotel, the lady's in house keeping were also so friendly and chirpy in the morning, so much so you looked forward to meeting them in the hallway in the morning.
We stayed for 1 week and the only fault we could find and thats hard to fault was the price of the breakfast, but wow what a breakfast.
I for one said that the stay at the Waldorf Astoria is the place to stay when in New York, We plan to return in April May of next year and will not look at another hotel
Well done Waldorf Astoria, Keep doing what you are doing because its Fab x

title: Elegant, grand, peaceful. Beautiful bed.
body: Stayed 2 weekend nights as part of a longer NY visit. Enjoyed the grand dimensions of the rooms and public areas which provided a sense of calm and spaciousness compared with modern hotels where every square inch feels costed and utilised. Room 1105 looks onto scaffolding but was very quiet (on the weekend). The current renovations/external scaffolding didn’t impact our stay at all. As expected at a Hilton, the bed was perfect – huge, luxurious, great sleep. Location is good as long as you’re happy to walk a few blocks to things. Recommend the ‘market’ at Grand Central for beautiful fresh food (salads, fruit, bakery, seafood, etc). Also recommend allowing some time to look around the hotel, the foyer, conference & function levels to take in the memorabilia, photos of famous guests/events etc. for a sense of the history. The large scale of this hotel (>1000 rooms) means that it feels rather corporate, not boutique, and the service varied considerably depending on who you encountered. We really enjoyed our stay.

title: Storied Hotel--well worth a visit
body:
The luxury and service here keeps pace with its grand history. Had occasion to grab a suite because of last minute travel and was very pleased with everything. Great staff, Clean rooms and public areas, Excellent location. 
It has some quirks but the lustre and elegance from days gone by make it a must visit property.

title: poor service
body:
we had high expectations for the waldolf astoria, when we arived our toliet was broken and our tv was fuzzy, we also had one double bed when we were meant to have two. The next morning we went down to reception and asked to have our toliet fixed and could we have two beds as this what was booked, the lady seemed distracted and said it will be done in three hours, this was fine as we had alot to see that day, we came back around 8hours later to reception it was a different lady and said that our toliet had been fixed but she couldnt see anything about the change of room/beds, i explained what had happened and she just kept putting the blame on me because I 'didnt get the womans name' and nothing can be done as 'i didnt get the womans name', she said it was to late now and to come back tomorrow.
Lucky it was done the next day but we only had 4nights there and two out of the four were disapointing.
I was shocked at the bad service.
The highlight was the amazing bed : )

title: Iconic grand hotel
body:
Just celebrated my anniversary with a weekend in NYC, my husband and I chose the Waldorf because of its history. We requested an upgrade if available and were lucky enought to get a fantastic suite on the 7th floor looking out onto park avenue. We were so impressed with the amazing suite at a fraction of what it would normally cost if we had booked it outright. The hotel and the room were elegant and grand and really made our weekend special. On Sunday we had the amazing brunch which was everything it is made out to be! 
Only negative was the size of the hotel, which makes it impossible to get any personalized attention that we like to get from small boutique hotels, but we were well aware of this when we booked due to Other reviews on this site.

title: An Elegant and Historic Hotel, however.......
body:
My wife and I planned a four day visit to NYC this month in celebration of her 40th birthday. To mark the occasion I redeemed about 160,000 Hilton Points and booked us in at the Waldorf Astoria in NYC. I am a Diamond member with Hilton so I try to use my accumulated points and stay in their nicer hotels for our vacations.
The hotel has a long and storied history. The building lobby is very elegant with copious amounts of marble, brass and Art Deco adornments. The halls are lined with black and white photos of world leaders, politicians and movie stars. You can certainly feel the history in the place. There is also an incredible antiques shop in the lobby with some of the coolest statues and carvings I have ever seen.
The hotel is very well located, just a few blocks from Rockefeller Center and about a 15 minute walk from Times Square. Park Avenue, Madison Avenue and 5th Avenue are just steps away.
Those are all the good things about the hotel, but there are also some improvements to be made.
First - I booked our room nearly two months in advance. I specifically reserved a King bed as my wife and I were traveling together and being married and all we generally like to share a bed. When I checked in at the Diamond desk I was informed that there were no King (or Queen) beds available. Apparently the hotel was "very busy" that day. The concept of a "Reservation" seems not to apply at the Waldorf. Instead, my wife and i were put into a room on the seventh floor at the far end of the hall with two double beds, "Fred and Wilma" style. No effort was made to follow-up or remedy the situation at a later time even though we were there for four days. I was somehow reminded of Seinfeld at the Rental Car counter. 
Second - The hotel, while elegant and historic needs some updating. The lights, wall-plates and bathroom fixtures look like they were last updated about twenty years ago. The bathroom vanity, toilet and shower fixtures are all worn and tired looking. The shower-head and water pressure were unimpressive. We also had a challenge finding electrical outlets to plug our mobile phones, iPad's etc. into for charging. They are scarce and difficult to reach. 
Third - We were looking forward to dining at the hotel but were completely put off by the prices. New York City dining is expensive, granted. And we were staying at a luxury hotel, granted. But there is a difference between expensive cuisine and highway robbery. We stopped in to the Peacock Alley for a drink and quick bite before heading to an evening show. For one beer, one glass of wine, a salad and a plate of three small sliders $85. We also stopped in the Bull and Bear for two drinks - $36. If you want Brunch on Sunday, $95 per person and $65 per child under twelve. I like fine dining and i'm willing to pay, but pricing like this is an insult to the guests.
I'm glad to have stayed at the Waldorf to see the history and benefit from its central location but we won't be back anytime soon. We stayed at the Ritz Carlton in Sarasota FL earlier this year and had a far, far better experience. The Waldorf seems to be a hotel that is comfortably resting on its laurels of yester-year rather than seeking to earn new ones.

title: Charming and elegant
body: We enjoyed 5 nights at this hotel whilst in New York for a wedding. We have previously stayed at The New York Palace (one of my favourite hotels) but thought we would try here this time. The room was had reserved was large and comfortably furnished with plenty of room for our baby's cost, pushchair etc. Large rooms like this can be difficult to find at city hotels. The location is great and the best shopping is all within walking distance as is Central Park and many other attractions. The reception and public areas are elegant and you could easily spend time there just watching the world go by!

title: Exploring the Big Apple
body:
Recently stayed at the Waldorf. The lobby is rich and gorgeous. The rooms? Not so much. They are okay. Took cold showers most mornings as hot water runs out. No coffee makers in the rooms. Either put clothes on and go downstairs or order a pot at $18. Seems a bit ridiculous for a hotel of this reputation. Surely they could furnish a little coffee pot. Cocktails are $18. Even for a simple rum and coke. Too expensive. 
The beds are wonderful. The service is very good. Location is perfect. I walked to the Today show every morning. 
I probably would not choose to stay there again.

title: Great Stay in NYC
body: Nothing beats a beautiful weekend in NY, with the Waldorf as your base. Elegant,and up to date, over the top service. the accommodations were FIRST CLASS. As a Hilton Diamond member check in and luggage handling was expedited and personal. I don't think our saty could have been any better

title: The Name's the Thing
body: I don't really have much to say about the Waldorf since we only spent one night, used none of the services and left. The location is great; a short walk from Grand Central Station, the bell staff was hard working and respectful, the beds were awesome and we can now say we stayed there. Otherwise, it was a clean room in a busy city.

title: Luxurios weekend in NYC
body:
We went to NYC for our anniversary. We decided to splurge and stay at the Waldorf on the concierge level. The room was lovely. We were disappointed with the Astoria Lounge where we were supposed to go for complimentary breakfast etc. We were there for 3 days. We tried each morning, but the lounge was not large enough to seat the number of people there. We were never there that there was an open table. Therefore, we would go to a restaurant for breakfast. 
Nest time I would stay at the Waldorf, but I would not spend the extra money on the concierge level.

title: A Big Disapointment
body: Having grown up in NY, I had always wanted to stay at this iconic landmark during one of our NY visits. It is now out of my system. The room was a nice size (especially for NYC) but definitely had seen better days. Plus, a world class hotel without HD TV? Our bathroom, while updated, had a shower that didn't drain properly. At 5PM on our first full day (we only stayed 2 nights) had to call housekeeping to clean our room. The view of the scaffolding outside the room made it difficult to tell if it was night or day. There is nothing on the Waldorf website to indicate ongoing construction. Since my husband and I had just returned from some exceptional hotels in Hawaii, the Waldorf's shortcomings were glaring. And my husband is a Hilton Diamond member too. Very disappointed and won't go back.

title: Bugs
body: Arrived in NY on a Sundat night. We had tickets for The Book of Mormon, so checked in quickly and headed out to the theater, after a wonderful evening with my son we returned to our room. The room was very dated and in dire need of a renovation. I am a Diamond member of their rewards program and was using points for my stay so I figured they gave me the room because I wasn't paying. The paint was pealing and the wallpaper was falling off the walls. I was prepared to make do for the night when I found bugs in the bed. I packed our things , went to the lobby and requested a manager. A young girl did her best to hadle the situation. I told her we wanted to leave and said they could keep the points. She apologized, offered to put us in the towers, and send a comp for a future stay. She showed us another room, had the head of housekeeping check it with and gave us a credit for use on the property. The tower room was very nice and updated, what I would expect at a Waldorf. The trip was marred by the bugs. I threw out my luggage, brought my clothes to the laundrymatt, and keep checking my home for bugs. The head of security left us a phone message apologizing, but I never got anything in writing and never got the certificate to come back as promised. Upon check out I had to ask for the credit promised(we hadn't even spent the whole thing). Despite the fact that the towers room was nice, I don't think we will return to this hotel. I just can't get over the first room.

title: Iconic hotel
body: Hotel knew we had booked for a special birthday (thanks virgin holidays) and from arrival looked after us really well -upgraded to suite with views of Chrysler building and 60 dollars in vouchers for drinks in any of the bars. Hotel is a little tired but so well placed for all NY sights and shops. Would definitely stay again

title: Waldorf or Palace Hotel?
body: My NY office is located in between the Palace and Waldorf Astoria Hotels and has a corporate arrangement with both hotels. I therefore stay one of either hotels when I visit NY. I don't remember how many times and days I stayed there but if you need to make a choice then I prefer the Palace better. Both hotels unfortunately are rated 5 stars but when compared with hotels in Asia, they are both sub-standard. Rooms at Palace is slightly better off then Waldorf. Restaurants at Palace is also better. Anyway, you will not find a good hotels in NY unless you have minimum of junior suite room. So my conclusion is that don't expect too much.

title: If it's good enough for the President...
body:
Well, he wasn't actually staying there, but Obama & Romney attended a dinner at the hotel this week whilst we were staying there. We'd already eaten so turned down the invitation. I was actually quite surprised at how light the security was - yes, the streets were full of NYPD, 49th & 50th were both closed and a barricade of sanitation trucks were used to keep anyone from driving a bomb in to the lobby, but we came and went unchallenged.
The hotel was our home from Monday to Friday. We were surprised at how busy it was constantly throughout our stay, there was a queue (orderly) for reception and we were given a room on the 14th floor, on the south side, 49th street. Having read other reviews we were surprised at how quiet the hotel was, we slept great (also due to the excellent king sized bed!). The hotel is very grand and a lot of work has been done to restore the lobby areas on both sides.
Thanks to the Concierge (Richard), we were able to negotiate the hotel AND the subway in NY - he is very helpful and knows everything you will need to know.
The hotel is in Midtown East, an easy walk to The Rock, Times Sq, Broadway and Empire State.

title: Given the history and luxury, an absolute must for any visit to New York
body:
I stayed here in a King Suite, which consisted of a bedroom, bathroom and living room. The rooms were quite large and were very nicely decorated. The hotel is full of history and photographs of famous figures visiting the Waldorf adorn all of the corridors. The lobby is magnificent, as is the Park Avenue entrance.
The food and drinks at the Waldorf are not cheap, but the cuisine is excellent. I recommend splashing out for at least one dinner in the Bull and Bear. Our meal there was incredible. 
Oscar's serves an excellent and extensive breakfast buffet, with very friendly waiters.
This was my third stay at the Waldorf this year. Each visit has been superb and I definitely consider this to be my home from home in New York.

title: One night of Luxury
body: I spent one night in this amazing hotel with my 3 sisters. We shared a suite as thats all we could afford but it was worth it. Such an amazing hotel. we were close to everything we wanted to see and didnt mind calling it home for one night. We were walking on air. I would love to go back there some day. Thanks to my great sister who organised it.

title: Old time luxury
body: We had a nice stay in a suite with bedroom, living room and two large bathrooms. Loved all that space. Classic, old time interior and sophisticated first impression, but some details tell the building is old and would need something... Enjoyed a lot anyway. We had also a nice view into north on Park Avenue. Excellent location in eastern Midtown. If you want old time luxury and classy look, this is the place if the price is not the issue.

title: Classic Service and a wonderful stay
body:
We were apprehensive after reading other TA reviews, wondering if we were about to encounter a problem. NONE. Our King room was spacious and spotless. While it did not have much of a view because it was in the center of the hotel, it was extremely quiet. The staff was always helpful and gracious. We were there during the Al Smith dinner and the hotel operated flawlessly. Only folks staying in the Towers had to deal with FBI SWAT, and they were treated well. 
Much of the hotel has been meticulously re-furbished to the era of it's origins. The art deco detail is amazing. It's like staying in a museum with room service. 
My only complaint was that the common areas of the hotel were really, really cold. Arctic cold for women in fancy dresses. Not so bad for men in suits. Seems like that could be fixed. 
To save money in Manhattan, walk over to Hell's Kitchen or even a local diner or pizza by the slice joint. Don't eat (or drink) in the hotels. Stop at a convenience store and buy your water and snacks. There are plenty to choose from. Take the subway. Ask the NYPD cops for directions.
 Also, I don't like bugs of any kind, but reading some of the TA reviews makes me wonder if a more serious fear of bugs colors reaction to rooms. We found ZERO evidence of bugs of any kind, and we were at the WA for several nights. No bugs. No bites. Nada. 
Enjoy the Waldorf. It's history is pretty cool.

title: Don't stay there - it's dated
body:
Don't stay at the Waldorf-Astoria unless you stay in The Towers. The lobby is old time luxury, very impressive and grand - but that's where it stops! We stayed in a very spacious suite in the main hotel, but it was in bad need of renovation. The bath was cracked, no key to open the storage cupboard, so we had to use a knife! The wall light was flickering all the time (unless it didn't come on at all). The air conditioning was noisy. But I have to say the bed was very comfortable and the linens luxurious.
In addition there was a very long queue in the lobby for reception to check in (whenever we went past this was the case). I also had to telephone the hotel urgently one afternoon - it took four calls, as they were busy and they kept hanging up. The coffee shop closed at 1.30 lunchtime! When we asked for coffee after a very mediocre limited menu lunch (admittedly it was a Saturday - but should this make a difference at a top class hotel?) we were told they had closed now, and we would have to transfer to the lobby lounge for a coffee!
I can't think of one reason why I would ever stay there again - and certainly would not recommend it. However we were told that The Towers block was fine.

title: Disappointing and Depressing
body:
I really enjoyed staying at The Waldorf many years ago; but that was then and this is now - maybe I've been spoiled by fine hotels around the world, but our recent stay was nothing less than depressing.
But first, the good points: classic rooms and bathrooms from a bygone era, quiet ..... and that's all I can think of.
The bad points: our large King room was dark, dingy and the bathroom was worse than a cheap hotel in the middle of nowhere; no coffeemaker in the room; astronomical rates for food and lodging; no turndown service; zero amenities; overall service only fair.
If you are going to NYC and want a LUXURY hotel in a good location, this is NOT the place for you.
There are many other hotels in this price range which have excellent locations, much brighter rooms and better service.

title: Could not use the business center
body:
The hotel was great. I wanted to print something, and it was not allowed at the business center. I had to buy a printer. 
I had a great time. I really liked the art deco interior. 
I had breakfast at Starbucks downstairs, like I usually do at home.

title: Old New York its worth it (probably)
body: Stayed for a week in oct . Hotel is old style New york you really get a feel of the past the lobby is amazing, location is bang on . We stayed in a king room which was very big, batroom was tiny and needed updating . Staff were friendly but of course they are as everytime they do something you got to tip them!! Had dinner in the bull and bear which was excellent. Had some drinks in the bar which was really nice and the bar staff were top notch. It is pricey in almost every aspect and prob not value for money at 2500 for 7 nights.But all that said i loved it ,its just the feel of the place the history that goes with it you dont get that with many hotels in the world if price isnt a problem stay there you will really feel part of New York

title: Luxury and Service
body:
Our suite was elegant and spacious; the king bedroom, bath, foyer and separate living room offered a generous amount of space. As expected, anything purchased from the hotel was very expensive. (room service, snacks). 
The included "continental" breakfast is like no continental breakfast I've had before! Bountiful varieties of fresh fruit (perfectly ripe), breads and danish, cereals, hard boiled eggs, meats and sliced cheeses and simply delicious lox and bagels. 
Also, I tend to sleep poorly in hotel beds, but this was was a great combo of soft support, with lots of pillows.

title: Tired, dated, cold, filthy and small room...extremely disappointing
body:
What a disappointment.
Having visited NY 29 years ago and stayed at the "super exclusive" Waldorf Astoria, I decided it was a must for my trip to NY this year. I cannot believe I went to the effort to book it....and more to the point, I tried to book it for my entire 10 day trip! Thank goodness I couldn't get a room for the whole time.
This hotel is riding on its previous coat tails. It was extremely disappointing. The lobby is grand, but our room was cold (couldn't turn the heat up at all), small, the bathroom was absolutely tiny and full of mould......it was as clean as this ancient bathroom could be, I'll grant them that... The location is OK, but we ended up at The Plaza for the rest of our stay and you just cannot compare the two hotels.
I will never go back to this dark and depressing hotel.

title: A TASTE OF GRANDNESS
body:
What I am about to say could happen at any property but I would not expect our experience at the Waldorf to be experienced at other prestigious properties around the world. This property with its 2 ton clock in its lobby is definitely slipping. The management should understand that it is the small things that count more than the icing on the cake. 
To start with I have been at the Waldorf several times in the past and it was always on the top of the list but this time the hotel seems to have lost its touch somewhat. First when arriving in the under-hotel entrance the service and treatment was at its best and the bellman was great and very helpful. When we took a stroll through the lobby to the main entrance from Park Avenue we noticed the plain look of the entrance and no longer is the grand chandelier is hanging displaying its beauty, yep gone. Walking up the stairs to the lobby while passing through the foyer I looked up to the ceiling and the tile is missing, the area is now painted a cheap silver and were the tile once was is now just an outline where the tile was. The workman never cleaned the area of what appears to be grout or cement which is still showing. An unfinished job looks terrible to say the least. In the main lobby looked about the same and still preserved its richness.
We arrived on Sunday the month of late September about 13:30 and after looking about went to the reception to check in. We were told our room was not yet ready and would have to wait until 15:00 or so. We were told we could take lunch at the buffet or eat around the corner at Oscars to kill time. We also were told we (receptionist) will send you a text message when your room is ready. Ok fine and off we went to have a bite to eat and look about. When 16:00 arrived and not message had arrived we headed back to the hotel and the receptionist stated the room was not ready, wait a moment. After several minutes (10) and a couple of calls we were told they had an upgraded room in the Waldorf Towers and sorry about the delay and there is two bottles of complementary water in the mini bar for us. No cookies or treats which is the usual gift plus water given upon check in at most Hilton family hotels to diamond and gold members. I asked about this and was told we never heard of this.
In the room we found the following discrepancies: the sink stopper was stuck and had not been moved in years, no throw rug in the bath, one pair of slippers in the closet (can’t but two peoples feet in one pair of slippers), when painting the bathroom the painters never removed the speaker cover or vent so paint was plugging nearly all holes and the vent grill had paint over an eighth of an inch thick, painting about the room was in the same condition as well as the hotel hallways very thick. Chips, dings and other damages were just covered with paint without blending the damage and some receptacles were not removed for painting just painted over, called down for another pair of slippers and they did show up later. The curtain on one window had come loose from the traverse rod and remained in that condition for the balance of our stay. The body cream in the bath was not replaced and had been used by the previous occupant. Proof of this was the bottle was half empty and cap pressed back on. A final observation was the room did not appear to have been vacuumed or dusted during the time of our stay. In fact there was not a vacuum cleaner seen on the floor when the maids were cleaning our rooms. 
Every day, we had two new pair of slippers in the room even though we had the ones being used in the closet. The room was very pretty and we had plenty of room and a good view from the windows.
I made some inquires not of the check in staff but the workers and found out the hotel is a Hilton family hotel but there is a management company running the property. I must say that it is very noticeable that Hilton is not involved in the day to day routine of things. Some Hampton Inns I have stayed in are better in some respects. Some of the staff at this property appears not to be happy with the management company and the way the go about accomplishing things and policies but in place.
We had several drinks at the lobby bar while in residence which I found very expensive. For a Dewar’s and water and Tanqueray and tonic the price was $17.00 and $18.00 each which is double the nominal cost in the finest restaurant.
Now we usually stay at the Hilton on Avenue of the Americas and find this hotel very adequate for our stays and we always use the executive floor rooms and the lounge is much better than the Waldorf.
The bottom line is, would I stay at the Waldorf again whether in the main hotel or the Towers, I must say NO. The property is nice, pretty room settings and staff good but the property just does not stand up to its original level years ago and the appearance and conditions of certain items just doesn’t measure up.

title: Real spacious suite
body: We liked our stay at Waldorf Towers. We stayed here for 3 nights. Our suite was really, really large on 36th floor. Rooms are clean; staff very friendly. Free Breakfast buffett was also included. Well, the hotel is not cheap, but in our opinion it is worth it. Perfectly located to explore Midtown Manhattan by foot (5th Street, Times Square, etc.). We will come back!

title: Grand but....
body: Second visit to this great hotel...we had to change room as the first one was not up to scratch..cracked sink/grubby bathroom etc...always hassle changing so not a great start but alls well that ends well!..I think the hotel is due a makeover now and is living on its past reputation....would I return?...not sure.

title: Old charm luxury
body:
As others have noted this hotel is a little worn and the thin walls and doors makes the rooms a little noisier than you would expect from a modern, sound proof, luxury hotel room. 
Other than this, it's an excellent hotel. I think the main reason for staying at the Waldorf should be the charm and history of which it has lots.
Our room (2204) on the 22nd floor had two very good beds, a two-chair sitting group, bathroom, small walk-in-closet (with iron and safe) and a desk. At that floor there was no street noise but we were close to elevators and could hear them from a distance and also when neighbouring rooms opened and shut doors. 
Wifi was available free of charge in lobby but extra in room at $18,50 per day. 
I have seen others complain about cleanliness but I did not see any of that, our room was cleaned perfectly.
Service is mostly excellent and friendly. 
During our stay both President Obama and Mitt Romney were campaigning and visitied hotel for a fundraiser, which we thought was a fun bonus (you might think otherwise If you don't enjoy secret service and police blocking traffic, but overall it went smothly)

title: Not Great For Diamond Members
body: This hotel has a beautiful lobby but the rooms are in need of repair. Beyond the check-in reception for diamond members it drops off quickly in service. They use to provide breakfast for Diamond members like every other Hilton brand of hotel but they took this,away. They also do not offer the Diamond member benefit for the Waldorf hotel brands. I have stayed here numerous times but I will choose one of the other New York Hilton hotels from now on. I will always be impressed with the history of this hotel but it is no longer the flagship Waldorf that goes to the Cavilieri or other Waldorf's in the chain. The suites I have had have been nice and the Tower is great.

title: NYC icon, but brand being milked...
body:
Oh dear. So at one time this place must have been majestic. The foyer is wonderful and some of the staff were excellent, but I guess it stops there. There are two key issues: i) under-investment and ii) unions. Its a real shame - this place has so many inherent positives: location, grandeur, history. Feels like she's being milked based on past glory.
Unions: this is a union hotel. Staff often cannot peform basic functions that a hotel of this alleged status should offer without blinking (but don't blame all staff - some are awesome, some definitely "union"). Need a conference room at short notice with a speaker-phone? No dice - "IT" have to "set it up" (err...set up a phone?). Need coffee/water in the business centre at 3am? Actually, its a mail room, and nope - you can get room service up 20-floors at $13 and then carry it down though...or walk down the street a block and sort yourself out. Need your 5 bags left with the Bell Captain for a few hours? No, carry them down to the storage room.
Underinvested
Outside of the Reception areas (amazing), rooms are proper vintage...and not in a good way. Ours smelt of wet, stale carpet; leaving the window open sorted it out, but the noise levels go up. Small shallow bath, shower curtain set-up, loose taps/missing fixtures. There's adequate room on the desk to work. Internet setup was fine. Mobile reception fine. 
Worth seeing once, but never again. Suppose thats what milking the brand is actually all about though.

title: Rooms are desperate for some TLC
body: I gave the Waldorf another try during a recent stay in NYC for an event in the hotel ballroom and was disappointed yet again. Rates were approaching $500 (close to $600 with taxes!) and the rooms looked equivalent to what you'd find in a $100 NYC room. Beyond the beautiful lobby and service are dated rooms that are in desperate need for an update and TLC. The carpets look to be about as old as the hotel is. The bathrooms look at least 15 years old and are not at all comfortable. The A/C is loud, as is the noise level from hallway traffic. The rest of the room leaves nothing to offer. I've heard the suites are much nicer, but if you plan on staying in a standard guest room you will be much happier at the many other options available to you just blocks away. Sorry Waldorf.

title: OK but not great
body:
For the tariff we paid to stay at the Waldorf, you would have expected a wonderful room, but on arrival at my room, I found it pretty average. I would have expected the bedspread/linen to be wonderful but was very disappointed. The bed was comfortable with lots of comfy pillow, but the whole room has quite an aged feel to it, not worth the price we paid.
It did have a fantastic view of the Chrysler building from our window.
We had breakfast one morning, but at $40 per person, expensive and very average. Why do American have to "cremate" their bacon, it so tough I couldn't eat it. 
Beautiful foyer with a lovely clock which chimes regularly. Also the price of their hot drinks was over the top, at about $10 each.
An experience to stay at the Waldorf, but I don't think I would stay there again.

title: No shower gel lets the old lady down
body:
the Waldorf Astoria can be characterised as a Grand hotel, that's showing its age in the bedrooms, but can still hold its head high and haughty in the public rooms. 
You know when you choose to stay here that you are going to be charged ridiculous prices for the priviledge of gracing the hallowed spaces of such a grand hotel ($240 for the Sunday brunch for two, $50 for 2 martinis), but hey, that's part of the experience. And actually, you do feel quite special if you go with the flow and just soak up the NY high society atmosphere.
But it's the little meannesses that show the crone side to the old lady. Wifi is free in the very defined area of the lobby but $16/day in your $400 room (it's free in the $100 Hyatt Place...). And the worst crime, the bathroom toiletries extend only to a shampoo, conditioner and a hand cream. NO shower gel! Just how mean is that! One of the luxuries of staying away is slowing down and having the time to take a leisurely bubble bath...only no shower gel = no bubbles. Dreadful. 
We found an excellent breakfast available just around the corner (58th & Lexington) in Brass for half the price of the (quite good) Oscar offering. Somehow it's sets the day off all wrong when you've been dinged for over $110 for breakfast for two. It crosses the line from "Expensive but goes with the turf" to "They're having a laugh at my expense".
Our room was in quite good condition, some small tatty and grubby edges that would really need a complete refurbishement to deal with, but we kept the lights turned down low and enjoyed the fine linens on the bed and plush furnishings.
We didn't have much interaction with the staff after checking in, but found the reception and concierge charming and helpful, and most corridor passes prompted a very friendly greeting. I thought our waiter in Peacock Alley was pretty useless and graceless, although the barman was delightful.
Overall, we enjoyed our stay, perhaps by setting our expectations right going in, but probably wouldn't return on our own budget.

title: Historic but that's where it stops
body: Hard to beat the history or location of the Waldorf but that is where it stops. We had an upgraded room and it still didn't even have a bath tub. Tiny bathroom with a tiny shower. At $500 bucks a night I was very disappointed. Skip the history and spend less for more at other hotels in Manhattan.

title: Wow
body:
2 stars for the location. That's it.
The "deluxe" room we stayed in over the weekend was both suffocatingly small, and the bathroom resembled what one might find in a $49 Motel 6 outside of Omaha. The paint in the bathtub was cracked in a half dozen places, and the cabinets were crooked (not by design). There was a vent that was caked with lint and it appeared as if it hadn't been cleaned in months if not years. For $800 a night, this is truly unacceptable and shocking.
You are much better off staying at a smaller property where the staff can actually take care of the rooms.

title: Waldorf Astoria New York
body:
I've stayed at the Waldorf many times, both with my husband and on my own. While I agree with some other reviewers that yes, the rooms are small, it is Manhatten real estate after all. I've found the rooms clean and neat, with modern conveniences like flat screen tvs and historic touches like marble fixtures.
Staff is always attentive, and the one time I had a problem with that flat screen they sent a maintenance person to fix it within an hour.
I love the historic ambience of the hotel, and the proximity to many mid-town attractions. I usually stay twice a year. I can walk to theatres, restaurants and museums. New York is a city made for walking, and mid-town a great location.
I also feel very safe there when I am on my own. New York can be overwhelming when I'm overtired, and the Waldorf is a haven from my adventures.
Yes, the restaurants are expensive, but again, it's Manhatten. The food is consistentlfy good and they change the menus to reflect the seasons. Last time I visited I went to Peacock Alley for a light dinner and cocktail before my play started and everything was delicious.
Yes, there are more modern hotels in NYC, but I keep going back to the Waldorf for the charm, the ambience, the service, the location, and the attention to detail. I feel like I am in old New York, with just a touch of the modern day to make me comfortable.

title: Not worthy of the stature
body: Waldorf Astoria was the choice of hotel for a special weekend in New York for myself and my fiancee, we had high expectations but were sadly let down, the room etire was tired and in need of enhancement, the heating system was not in working order unless you required cold air, tea and coffee was not as standard in the room unless ordered via room service at extra cost. Wont be staying there again..

title: Big name, historic elan, but aside from service not that great on the merits.
body: If this weren't "The Waldorf" and didn't have the historical charm, there wouldn't be much of a reason to stay here. The front-desk service was top notch--very nicely done. But "historic" sometimes = "a bit ragged," and that is true here. Carpet, walls, etc. look a bit worn. The room was a good size for an old place, but the bathroom was cramped and had a distinct mildewy smell to it. And our room was really cold (I like hotel rooms cool, but this was too cool). The front desk said that it was because it's a "historic property" and they hadn't yet turned the heat on yet for the whole building, so they were piping in "neutral air." Not sure what all that meant, but the only way to get the room warmer was to turn off the air entirely. It's really expensive, and I didn't think it was really worth the price (granted, I'm not blown away by historic properties or big names--if you are, you might feel differently).

title: Birthday trip to America
body:
My husband had always wanted to visit New York so we made plans to visit for his birthday this year. We booked 4 nights in this wonderfully iconic hotel. It's impressive, very central to the main sights and the staff are very helpful and welcoming. I work in the interior design market and my first impression was the hotel looked tired, our room was a little noisy but one comment to reception meant we were quickly and effortlessly moved to a much better room. As the days passed I became really fond of the hotel despite the fact that some areas will need upgrading soon, I would visit again with no hesitation. The trip was enhanced by the fact that both Obama and Romney were at the hotel whilst we visited. We cant believe what has happened since we flew down to Miami with the Hurricane hitting a few days later. Our best wishes go out to all the local New Yorkers who made our stay so special, fantastic city!
One little tip for those who enjoy a little cocktail from time to time, the hotel has honey bees on the roof and they use the honey to create a wonderful vodka based cocktail...wonderful!

title: Disappointing 'luxury'
body: We chose the Waldorf Astoria because of its history and five star rating for our trip of a lifetime to New York and had high hopes of a luxurious and relaxing break. The lobby was very impressive and the checking in staff were very friendly but as we made our way to our room, little things started to leave little 'chinks' in our dream. The walls and paintwork were scuffed, broom cupboard/cleaning cupboard doors were left wide open in the middle of the afternoon and even the cleaning trolleys were left in the middle of the corridors. As we entered our room it became apparent that the photos on their website of the double deluxe rooms hadn't been taken in our room. The door hinges were rusty, the lock on the toilet door was broken, there was dirt and dust in the air conditioning vents, the mini bar door didn't close properly so the drinks weren't cold, the juice bottles were squashed and no longer drinkable. This was all very disappointing and discovered within an hour of checking in. The folder left in the room giving you all the information you should need had vital pages missing regarding checking out. I tried to wash my hands after using the bathroom and found no warm water. Thought nothing more about it until i went to have shower... having left the tap running in the bath for over ten minutes we soon established there wouldn't be any hot water this side of Christmas! When we ordered a pot of tea which supposedly allowed for six cups, they only supplied two tea bags! So much for five star... we obviously were given the 'cheap seats'.

title: Tired and over priced
body:
The Waldorf Astoria has a beautiful lobby, steak house and bar/lounge. The reception was quick and efficient. BUT once past all the glitz and glamour of the down stairs area it's just a tired old hotel badly in need of refurbishing. We paid over $600 per night for a Sunday and Monday night for a two bed room with chipped tiles in the bathroom, curtains which didn't close properly and off white linen. Also the same rooms available for under $300. So much for early booking.
It was a dream of mine to stay at the Waldorf because of it's reputation. I am sorry I didn't keep the dream intact.

title: Amazing customer service, great value, definitely recommend!
body: I absolutely loved this hotel! I stayed here on October 14th - 16th and from the moment I walked in, my breath was taken away. The entrance way is stunning and the attention to detail is impeccable. When I was checking in, Doug was the one who helped us. I have stayed at plenty of hotels in Manhattan, many with good customer service, but this was another level. Doug was so friendly and kind, even my guest was surprised. He asked me about my day so we started talking since the check-in process was taking a bit of time and I was telling him how I was sort of having a bad day and when he heard it was my birthday, he wished me a happy birthday and told me he was going to try his best to see if there were any other available rooms (comic con was in town so hotels were booked). In the end, he upgraded my room to a spacious room up on the 23rd floor and our bags were brought in by the staff. He also asked me if I wanted 2 complimentary drink vouchers to any of the restaurants at the hotel. I accepted them but didn't end up using them but I thought that was very kind of him. The room had a semi-view, a full closet, full bathroom, a large desk, mini-bar, and tons of areas to store away your things. It also consisted of two medium size windows, hd flat screen tv with tons of channels, and a ridiculously comfortable bed sheet set. Their beds are so comfortable! And you can't beat the amazing location. So close to subways, so close to amazing shopping, etc! It was so easy and fun to walk such a short distance after a long day of sight-seeing. I've visited Manhattan a bunch of times but we always find new things to discover! And I know some say the Waldorf is a little bit outdated and not suitable for people under a certain age but I'm 24 and I have to say that I am a fan. I don't think it would hurt to update the furniture a bit, a little bit like the Wynn hotel in LV is modern but classy. Anyways, I think no matter what kind of hotel you stay at, whether its a beautiful, historic hotel or a modern, fun hotel - I think the service is the most important thing that can make or break your experience. In this case, my guest and I were blown away, yet again, by the amazing service at Waldorf. I would gladly stay here again and highly recommend it. I have absolutely no complaints!

title: Beautiful lobby, great location, dated bathroom
body: The lobby makes you feel like you have entered into a world of extreme luxury. However, our room and in particular the bathroom was very small and dated. It was also very noisy, much noisier than other hotels in the same location. They need to put in better windows perhaps. I did enjoy my stay but would not rush back.

title: Great hotel in a great location
body:
Stayed here in February, had a great stay, room was just a bit small but the location could not have been better. Concierge service could not have been more helpful but the theatre ticket service was a bit pricey and certainly a lot pricier than could be had elsewhere.
Although the room we had was a bit small it still had all I would expect from a hotel of this class. The bed was great and if I was just staying one or two nights, the room would probably been fine, but too small for longer stays.
Downstairs in the lobby and bar area was nothing short of excellent and I couldn't fault the reception or check-in/out.

title: A first class stay that a hurricane could not spoil!
body:
I do feel sorry for those people who have posted reviews on how the Waldorf looks 'shabby' and 'tired'. They must have been really unlucky with their rooms and / or service they received, as I couldn't fault it.
The lobby has been refurbished and looks fresh and opulent. Queues at reception for checking in? Well, it depends on the time of day. We arrived at 1pm and had a very short wait at reception. The booking was for my 40th birthday, and 2 drinks vouchers were waiting for me on arrival (worth $40 - thanks to the tip-off from Virgin Holidays). I smiled and asked nicely for a 'room with a view' and the receptionist said if we could wait an hour she would secure me a good one, so we went sight-seeing for a while and an hour later she sent us a text to say it was ready. Our room was on the 16th floor, was very large with windows on 3 sides, and had a fantastic view of the Chrysler Building - wow!
I couldn't see anything on the 16th floor on indeed in our room that was 'past it'. The bed was extremely comfortable and had beautiful, fresh, white bed linen. There was a huge flatscreen TV and an ipod docking station which I didn't expect.
The wi-fi is free in the lobby but can get slow and busy at times, as the lobby is also open to the public of course. I used the business centre PC's on two occassions at a rate of 40c per minute. You just put your credit card in to activate.
We had cocktails a couple of times both at Peacock Alley and Sir Harry's bar. Expect to pay around $20 for one but they are very good - and very strong!
