It was bizarre being in the Waldorf during Hurricane Sandy - the staff didn't deviate from their normal behaviour, even though it got very busy and I'm sure there were lots of frantic customers. It was like being inside a safe haven that Sandy could not hit: no power failures or breaks in service. It was only when I stepped out the Park Lane entrance to have a nosy that I realised a tree had come down and just missed the hotel scaffolding - that was a close call.
The only negative would be the fact that the hotel is still swathed in scaffolding on the ground floor. They don't mention this on their website and try to downplay the renovations. In fact, the renovations are part of a rolling programme and will be going on for years. It was just slightly disappointing to arrive at the hotel and walk under the building work.
All in all, I rate the Waldorf highly. Nothing there is value for money, but you would be a bit misguided to think that it would be! Go there for the art deco surroundings, the opulence and really just to do in once in your lifetime.
Extra note: Our holiday was booked through Virgin Holidays who were absolutely fantastic during the storm crisis. Not only did they book us 2 extra nights there in the same room (thanks, Mr Branson!) but they got us on a special extra flight ASAP out of JFK as soon as it re-opened. Really exceptional service.

title: Nice location nice hotel
body: Big grand lobby. Remember that this is an old hotel so there are some scratches and creaking noises. We were there during Hurricane Sandy and were very pleased with the way the staff did their best to make the guests comfortable. This is a pet friendly hotel and it seems all pet owners knew it. The lobby was a gathering place for people as well as their fur friends. Our suite was very comfortable. Very comfortable bed. We had two complaints that were easily taken care of. #1 Although there are no smoking floors/rooms, they said they do not enforce it. There was a large party which took up our whole wing of which we were the only ones not a part of the group. They were all smokers and they all had their hotel room doors open and they hung out in the hall. We were moved to another wing. #2 The concierge desk staff was less than gracious. We felt like we had either really stupid questions or we were bothering them. We just went to the theater desk staff who were over the top wonderful. I wish I had remembered their names. Super helpful. Overall, it was a great trip.

title: Elegant but dated
body:
I was excited about staying in the world famous Waldorf Astoria in NYC. The lobby and adjacent areas are elegant and tasteful. The room was ok, but not exciting. The view was horrid, but then I didn't pay extra for a room with a view. As a Hilton Gold member, I'd been hoping for a better accommodation -- apparently they provided an upgraded room, but it just didn't seem so (not sure how the more basic room would have been). 
There was something disconcerting to me, and at first I thought I was imagining it --- the room smelled like cat urine. I remarked to my friend, and she said that she smelled it but attributed it to foul air freshener. It was most noticable when returning to the room from being out. The hallway definitely did not have the same odor, but the minute the door to the room was open, there it was. I've had cats, so unfortunately I know that horrid smell. 
You know, I really wanted to love my experience at the Waldorf, but it seemed that there was something a bit off, left and right...
The bathroom was nice and spacious, but the water didn't drain well while showering. Tromping around in an inch of water while in the shower isn't appealing.
There was WIFI, but it was so slow I couldn't bear to use it. The television was nice, but the remote didn't respond properly (in the end, we decide the batteries were probably nearly dead --- just weird to have these issues at a hotel of the Waldorf's stature). 
We had a drink in the hotel bar (I'm trying to remember the name of it -- not the one open to the lobby, but another, dark panelled place). The service was not good. My friend ordered the specialty drink at the top of the menu, and was told that they didn't have the main ingredient -- again, seems weird for a place with a presumably fine reputation, to operate that way. Why would they not have the ingredients for their "signature drink"? The waitress brought our drinks, then never came back to our table. Eventually she came back and never asked us if we wanted another. You notice these sorts of things when you have high expectations during a visit.

title: Great location
body:
We arrived just before hurricane sandy, the lobby was very impressive and the Hotel boasts an impressive history with pictures the rich and famous who have visited over the years. Well they wouldnt now! The first room we were shown had two ' double' beds in!! Then take that to the fact that everything in USA is so big -- these beds were less than double UK size but slightly more than a single. I asked for an upgrade - which I got at a cost to a suite. 22m. This was a bit better and has a view down Park Ave Decent sized suite but the rooms are a little tired and could do with a refresh. This is at best an average Hotel with a fantastic history , however the situation is fab. Just a ten minute walk to Grand Central Station or Times Square. All in all if I visited NY again -- I wouldn't stay here!
 No doubt our stay was effected by the Hurricane as lots of things were closed, New York is a fantastic City just to look around and if you get a good deal at the Waldorf then stay but it is only average. Our original room was a superior delux but the upgrade was to a suite and cost $190 per night. Oh one last tip, use either dollars, travellers cheques or your card. We took English cash and the best conversion rate was $ 1.22 per pound!!!

title: Disappointing.
body: We booked a package with British Airways hoping to stay in a famous, elegant, wonderful hotel as a once in a lifetime experience for our family. British Airways are amazing by the way and could teach the Waldorf a few tricks about customer service! The lobby and entrance is indeed amazingly beautiful and one cannot fail to be impressed by its grandeur, elegance and history....but the World has moved on since the 1930's and expectations have too which I think the Waldorf and the Hilton group have seemingly not appreciated, and are trading off of an image which doesn't bear fruit in reality. We had booked 2 suites for 3 nights (as there are 5 of us) We were told at checking in that we were being upgraded and got quite excited given that anything above a suite might be a wonderful gift given our 'once in a lifetime visit' but, when we got to our rooms, they were exactly as I had booked...no upgrade there then. The suites were clean and tidy but not a patch on the grandeur of the lobby and a bit of a let down from what I had expected. I am used to staying in normal 'business class' hotels and the rooms weren't really anything substantially different to those one would expect in this class of hotel, and certainly not opulent or inspiring. On the surface of it, eveything seemed pretty good but after a couple of days the faults were evident. The shower door was coming away from the wall so the door was tricky to shut, the air con had a mind of its own and sleeping in 24.5 degrees was trying! The mini bar's door didn't shut properly and was so expensive it was mind blowing...7 Dollars for a branded Coke is just racqueteering. This sort of thing doesn't add value, it just highlights the ridiculousness of this establishment's arrogance and attitude towards (attempting to) milking its guests. The bottom line is, if you're stupid and rich enough to pay these completely made up prices, we are happy to take your money from you. There was no free WiFi in the rooms, you had to use the lobby which was so busy that the WiFi was so overloaded that using it was almost impossible. My daughter got food posioning and was very sick. She was ill in the bedroom, but it took 40 minutes to get a maid to help me...obviously I don't expect anyone to clean up my kids' sick, but I did ask for a bucket or bowl as she was being sick every 20 minutes, the maid gave me the bin and told me she would try to find something else but my daughter then covered the bathroom floor...we never did get a bucket and had to use the bin and towels. I had to 'borrow' some cleaning fluid from a passing cart to clean up the toilet and floor and carpet myself. She had been sick in our travel bag so all our clothes needed laundering but the hotel wanted 27 Dollars to launder ONE SHIRT so I had to fill the bath and tread them with my feet to get them clean. At least the air con being stuck on 24.5 degrees enabled me to dry it all quite quickly over the vents though! They say that they pride themselves on service but this was not evident to me. I could go on but I would end up writing a book. I think you get the idea from what I have written so far though. Bottom line is that I will, one day, go back to New York, but certainly will not be spending that kind of money to stay in that hotel again as it was so disappointing versus my expectations and their advertising and reputation. Live and learn though eh? a distinctly 4 star experience at over 5 star rates.

title: Great Service, but everything else leaves much to be desired
body: Was booked to stay at the Waldorf for four days for the NYC Marathon. Since the marathon was cancelled at the last minute, we ended up leaving after 2 days, and I am glad we did. The service from everyone was top notch. Check-in was friendly and efficient, and when I had a problem they were quick to resolve it. However, the rooms were in poor condition, worn carpeting, sloppy paint, and the window about fell out when I tried to open it! Also, the hotel's mechanical system is set up to either heat or cool, but not both. When we were there, it was set to "heat", which meant the only way to cool the room down at night was to open the window (and let in all the noise from the city streets below). Bottom line was, you can either not sleep because it's too hot, or because it's too noisy. Did not eat at the hotel because of the cost (Sunday brunch is $98 per person!). Also, like others, I was hoping for an upgrade due to my Gold status with Hilton, but upgrades were not offered. My advice is to stop by and walk through the lobby and the beautiful public spaces, but stay elsewhere! Not even close to being worth $500/night.

title: dissapointed
body:
good points 
art deco great looking building. great lobby and bar area.
bad points
very tired rooms, we were on 10th floor and the whole areas looked dirty and worn. Our room was ok but bathroom needs updating and smelt of damp or worse. room heating did not work.
very expensive breakfast for 2 adults and 1 child $135.00.
we stayed during hurricane Sandy and the hotel did not come to any harm and we felt quite safe although we did have the fire alarms go off at 4 in the morning on our 1st evening so that was quite disconcerting. We knew what we were getting into cost wise before we booked but on reflection i would not pay top dollar for this experience again at the Waldorf. I expected standards to be higher and feel that the hotel is living off of it's past glory, i wish that was not the case. 
hope this helps as i feel it is an honest review.

title: Gorgeous public areas, average rooms.
body: It was my old dream to stay at this legendary hotel, so for this trip to NY I did book the Waldorf Astoria for 2 nights. In general I would say I was expecting more. Yes, I have to admit lobby and public areas are up to the expectations - absolutely fantastic with old world charm - making you feel like in 1920s'.You can spent a lot of time walking around and looking at fine pieces of art in different public areas - it is so amazing. At the same time you don’t have to pay for the hotel to see all these facilities any New York visitor can do this absolutely for free - you just have to enter the hotel and make your own small sightseeing tour (exactly like I did last year during my previous stay at NY. While for hotel guests the main thing should be level of service and hotel room and latter is definitely not the strongest part of the hotel and your experience will heavily depend on whether you will be staying at refurbished room or not. We did book Deluxe room and for the first night we were given really bad one: everything was dated both in the room (worn wallpapers) and in the bathroom (dated equipment, mold in some places) - I would rate that room not more than 3* at maximum. In addition the hallway on our floor was dated as well. I went to the reception and asked to change the room for refurbished one, they told that hotel is almost fully booked (which was true) and that they will be able to provide another room only for second night. Next day it was done and can tell this new room was way better (and only because of this my rating is 4 out 5 otherwise it would be less). First of all it was located on newly refurbished floor - hallways were absolutely fabulous, Room itself was much bigger, furniture and wallpapers not new but definitely in much better state, separate "mirror" make up room leading to the HUGE bathroom - this was the room which indeed can be associated with Waldorf Astoria name. Separate word about service - all staff were very polite, all request were fulfilled in timely manner - when I found that there were not enough bath amenities in the room (shampoo, shower gel and etc) and also slippers were absent I did call housekeeping and in 10 min everything was delivered and the amount of bath products was really huge - it was separate bag for each of us full of different high quality toiletries - mixture of WA branded and Salvatore Ferragamo "Touscan Soil" products. At the same time the service is absolutely impersonal - yes they are smiling but you can definitely see that there is nothing behind this smile! We didn’t eat or drink at the hotel so can't comment on this. The location is fantastic - in the middle of Manhattan, all major sightseeing sites are within easy walking distance, severla subway lines in few min walk - great location to explore Manhattan. Also they have huge luggage storage area where you can leave your bags on the last day absolutely for free – which is very convenient. All in all we did like the stay while not as much as were expecting. Hotel management definitely have to work on the refurbishment of all rooms and floor hallways as it seems for the moment hotel mostly relying on the famous name and old merits, while they have to be aware that this will not last forever. Tip: For those willing to stay in order not to spoil the stay would definitely recommend to contact the hotel upfront and ask for refurbished room.

title: Not a bad hotel to be evacuated to.
body:
As a consequence of the impact of Hurricane Sandy on NYC we spent several nights in the Waldorf having been evacuated there from our hotel on the waterside of Manhattan and before we could get flights back to the UK. . I suppose the true test of any hotel/staff/management is in a time of crisis. If that is the case then the Waldorf passed with 'flying colours'. I will always be eternally greatful to the management of the hotel for allowing us to stay for an extended period and for finding a room for my daughter so she could be with us when the hurricane hit. At very competitive and reduced rates. 
The hotel itself is slightly dated in terms of facilities but it is such an elegant building with a stunning lobby and tasteful bar areas. Breakfasts are a tad expensive and I always bemoan hotels who don't have coffee or tea making facilities in the rooms.
Once again a big thanks to all staff and management for handling the crisis so admirably and I suspect working for several days on the run without going home.

title: Rooms need updating
body: Early October in NYC is always wonderful. My husband's business trip took us to the Waldorf, where his law firm took over the entire building. The public spaces are stunning, but room 822 was small and dated with a view of a flat roof. At $500 a night, I felt like it was expensive for size. The room was very clean, however, with a comfortable bed and flat screen TV. Further, we enjoyed the bars in the hotel, which were cozy and filled with charm.

title: Unforutnately disappointed
body:
me and the girlfriend checked in on the 25th october 2012 for four nights and I'm sorry to say this is one of the most forgettable hotels I've stayed in. Our first two nights were disturbed by the heaters in the wall waking us up and then we got moved to another room, then the emergency alarm woke us up at 4am in the morning. 
I did not think the staff were helpful and I personally did not rate the actual hotel rooms.
I wish this could have been a positive review, but i regretufully give it one star.

title: Wonderful Waldorf!!!
body: After getting a super deal on Priceline, my girlfriend and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Waldorf and were in awe of the history and architecture. The staff was superb and the beds were the most comfortable I have ever slept on.

title: ouch!!!! those Internet acces fees
body: great hotel,luxry in an old classical style. The only rip off the high internet access fees $19.00 plus taxes and its per devices so if you happen to use your laptop, your Ipad and your cell for wi-fi. It will cost. I know this is a high end hotel, but at those prices most hotels in that category wil give you free access, or if not only charge a single fee for any device on the account. Free wi-fi in the lobby, but not that great, you have to find a good spot.

title: Very good hotel, but lousy wifi policy
body: This is obviously a great place, with all the New York grandeur and glamorous feel. The area is lovely, staff friendly and the rooms were surprisingly spacious. We didn't expect that in NY City! A little dated, but you know that when you are going to an OLD place. The only thing we were not too pleased about, is the Internet policy: $15 per day, per device, and only free Internet in the public spaces, and not a great connection either. Sure, the Waldorf is all about tradition and the good old days, but in this respect they should be catching up with modern times.

title: Step Back in Time
body: Staying here is an experience everyone should enjoy. There are very good offers available and it could end up cheaper than another hotel not a tenth as good. The building and rooms are incredibly beautiful and have been maintained and restored to an extremely high standard. To cut a long story short I will just say that staying here was an uplifting and truly memorable experience

title: Hurricane Sandy
body: My friends and I were at the WA last week when Hurricane Sandy hit the northeast. The hotel never lost power, thankfully. The staff should be commended and compensated for working through several hectic days. From housekeeping to kitchen to restaurants/bars, and the spa (Marie is amazing!), everyone remained calm and friendly. Services were abbreviated but still very reasonable. This was my second stay at WA in NY and it was just as enjoyable as my first - even with a hurricane outside!

title: Old world style, but mind the price
body:
Normally, this hotel can be quite expensive. US Presidents, celebrities, and foreign dignitaries have all stayed at this historic hotel. But I would only recommend staying here if you can secure a discounted rate - either through a travel website, special promotion, or group rate. Service is great, but the amenities are dated, which is part of the charm.
One of the greatest assets for the Waldorf Astoria (part of the Hilton family of hotels) is the location at the heart of Midtown Manhattan. Several subway lines are 1-4 blocks away, and Times Square is within easy walking distance. Depending on your itinerary, it's hard to beat the central location.

title: Another great experience!
body:
This was my second time staying at the Waldorf and it was yet another great experience. The location is within walking distance for most attractions and if not it is only a short cab drive away. I also like that it is located within mid-town but without all the craziness of Times Square. The room had double beds, which were super comfy, very clean, quiet, and actually quite a nice size. Everyone I met that worked there was very nice and helpful and I liked that you have to use your room card at night in the elevator.
Went to see the classic Lion King, which was amazing, along with checking out The Met (art museum not opera house), and the library for their Percy Shelly exhibit. Also checked out Steve Cohen's magic show at the Waldorf Towers. This is a definitel must see NYC show! One of my new favorite steakhouses in NYC is BLT - DELISH! The Boathouse in Central Park was great too, especially since it was perfect weather to sit outside.

title: Nice Hotel!! Antique, but very glamorous!!
body:
Spending a night at WA is a kind of " felling wealthy" !! It is really gorgeous, although is a bit overpricing, but nothing pays a good comfort!!
You need to try it once!! Very central, you can walk to everywhere, and appreciate the great atmosphere of New York City, or better saying " The big Apple". Despite,staying at WA makes your trip more much exciting !!

title: Glamorous bus station?
body: The Astoria should be brilliant. Great location, lovely building and history to match. But it wasn't. Rooms were a little tired and in need of refurb; we were on the 6th floor and natural light wasn't good. The most disappointing thing was we had booked for one night after the NY marathon (it didn't help that the marathon was cancelled) but our anticipated luxurious special night just didn't deliver. Hotel staff felt like they didn't really care and were going through the motions and the lobby was constantly rammed with people, so much so that it felt like it was a nice waiting area in a bus station. Really expected a lot and were were very disappointed. We were told they had several cancellations so it wasn't that they were too busy; just felt like they didn't really care and were relying too much on reputation from previous decades. Having stayed at other luxurious hotels in the last year I can confidently say the Astoria is resting on its laurels and doesn't appear to be doing much to make each guest feel special.

title: Just not my style ...
body:
If you're looking for a place with the old style glory this is it ... I was there for an event and although our room was nice and big, and had been renovated ... without being completely gutted there's just some age you can't cover up. The food was outrageously expensive and the waitstaff at the event that I was at was COMPLETELY uncaring of how they cleared the table .. totally noisy (during presentations) and unprofessional on so many levels. 
I will say this though that they did not charge me for the last two nights I had reserved when I had to get out to avoid getting trapped in NYC during the hurricane ... that was a nice and unexpected surprise -- very professional.
Note: the building is undergoing renovations as other reviews state ... this makes certain things inconvenient ... and take your ear plugs ... the 4 a.m. garbage pickup with old windows makes for an EARLY morning.

title: Grand hotel but tired
body:
Returned to New York and felt we needed to stay here to say we had done it. Hotel is lovely but tired. Staff were very serious and the atmosphere was very pretentious. Room was ok,
Bar and seating area were clean but busy and too many people.
Warning to all we decided to eat breakfast at the hotel, choice was very good but be sitting down for when the bill arrives.
Lots of nice restaurants close by.
All in all a nice trip but there are better hotels in New York. Was nice to arrive in Boston where the staff were smiling and friendly.

title: Nickel & dime you to death/Poor Service
body:
What a disappointment of hotel...stayed for 5 days from 20th October with my family in a one bed suite with great expectation of it being amazing. Well on arrival we were taken to a room with a flooded unusable bathroom which then took three different calls and three different staff inspections to get us moved, not because it wasn't obvious we needed to be moved but because in a 5 star hotel different teams didn't speak to each other. Also while we waited to be moved a broken rollaway bed was delivered and then taken away by staff even though we had prebooked it. My family desperately need to use the bathroom after a 7 hr flight from London and a horrendous 4 hour journey from JFK (another story) and we were directed to use the bathrooms in the lobby (the men room was also flooded in he lobby). The hotels idea of making this right was not to comp us dinner (which we had to have in the hotel room because it was so late but to send us milk and cookies).
Also this was an expensive suite yet the room didn't even had facilities for making a coffee, the internet was a ridiculous $19 per 24 hours, access to the gym was an extra charge, breakfast which was very so so was $44 per head....I know that NYC hotels tend to charge for most things but this is a hotel with its hand out from the minute you walk through the door.
Finally on the day we left we had a late flight and brought our bags down to the lobby and at check out no one asked us about our stay (perhaps they didnt care) and when I asked for my bags to be stored by the bell captain we got into a bizarre conversation about how the bag store was in the basement and he could take it down for me if I wanted (Isnt that your job?) or i.e. if I tipped him.
A hotel who's culture is based not on service but on milking its clients...very disappointing

title: Good hotel
body:
We stayed here for 5 nights. ( for the marathon..)The rooms are big, bedding is really good. Bathroom fine, the only thing I don't like are showercurtains that when you shower it wants to cling to you... but that's a minor detail. Rooms are clean. The hotel itself is very large so not very personal. Service is good. We rented bicycles and could put them in the storage overnight, that was perfect! We had breakfast once at the hotel, quite expensive ($105,- for 2 persons). 
If this hotel wasn't in the package deal for the marathon we would not have stayed here. It was good but well, not what I would choose.

title: Very Disappointing
body: Stayed at the Waldorf for a night because I worked late and had to be in early the next morning. I decided to treat myself and spend the extra Honors Points instead of staying at the nearby and cheaper Hilton Garden Inn or New York Hilton. Mistake! While the public areas of the hotel are breathtaking and the staff exceptional the guest room was small, had old outdated scratched and knocked-up furniture and bad climate control. If you decide to stay at the Waldorf do yourself a favor and ask to see the room first. Next time i'll stay at a 'Hilton' branded property where the rooms are always in tip top shape - if a bit boring.

title: True perfection
body: Although me and my friends didn't stay here, wish we had, we had lunch at the height of hurricane sandy! Sandy who?! ;-) Well, just, perfect. Nothing more to say. Perfect! The food was just to die for, a buffet lunch and champagne! Happy Birthday indeed to my friend! A birthday not to forget that's for sure!

title: Oh no, No coffee in rooms
body: This Hotel is in a good place to make your visit to New York, easy to see all you want. All the staff are helpfull. Rooms are clean Beds very nice easy to get a good nights sleep. Bathroom clean no shower cream only soap they do put small amounts of shampoo, conditioner and body cream, pleanty of clean towels two dressing gowns. There is a hairdyer. Pleanty of storeage space. An iron and ironing board (perhaps they are there to stop the ladies getting homesick LOL) There is a mini bar Be Aware of the prices I had to request a price list and No we did not use it, prices are very high, so went and brought wine (in supermarkets wine is 6% there is a wine store on Park Ave 60th st closes at 5pm) and cans We had breakfast one morning for three it was 138 dollors so not cheap, we had the same breakfast at Oxford cafe for 25 dollors. No coffee or tea in rooms You need to pre order this before you arrive

title: Great staff at a great hotel
body:
Spent two nights here while attending a conference. Tim, at the front desk made and extra effort to find a very spacious business king room for us. He also gave us several hilton honors comp drink coupons as i mentioned it was a special occasion for us. Ram at concierge printed out our boarding passes for our return trip...after I asked where the business office was. i was expecting to get nicked for printing, often the case nowadays, 
Bed in room was top notch as were the linens, towels and robes.

title: Guest Services Manager John [--] Should Be Fired
body:
I have never been so poorly treated in my entire life. It seems the condescending Mr. John [--] never learned that customer service is a part of the hospitality business. My husband and I travel to NYC monthly. We enjoy The Mark, The Pierre, The Palace and the Four Seasons. The lore of the Waldorf Astoria drew us to stay here. While there were highlights, our interaction with Mr. [--] ruined them all. Our luggage was ruined by a pipe burst and this man shoved his card at us, made us feel like we were the problem and apparently has a supiority complex. He didn't even apologize ( thankfully his colleague, Brian I believe, did and was much more considerate when he saw we were unhappy). 
I can't say all bad things. The hotel tours were wonderful. We received insightful and witty tips from the Twitter account, it was so fun to engage! The steaks in Bull & Bear were perfection and Jessica is a darling. George is one of the best servers we have ever had. The Towers suites are breathtaking. Check-in was professional and pleasant. Mr. Matt Lane was ever so helpful. 
The Guerlan spa is so beautiful and luxurious. A true urban oasis. Anne was pleasant and knowledgeable. 
We won't stay here again because this hotel has hired a manager who thinks that working and this hotel gives him some sort of entitlement. Mr. John [--] its certainly not luxury nor on knows how to provide luxury service. A shame. We'll spend our money elsewhere. 
Go to Bull & Bear and skip the stay.

title: Great Breakfast
body:
Stayed here with my sister after a 7 hour delayed flight from Dublin, we got to the hotel at 2am and the staff were so nice. We got upgraded to the biggest room I've ever seen.
The hotel itself is old fashioned grandeur at its best. Great location of 5th Ave and you could hang out i the lobby and watch the great and the good of NYC.
The breakfast was a treat, our waitress, Grace ( from Dungloe 40 years earlier !!) took a shine to us, we got extra everything :)) Great stay .

title: Needs focus on details
body: My wife and I recently stayed 2 nights at Waldorf during what was to be NY Marathon weekend. We originally booked 4 nights, but due to the race cancellation we left NY early. In any event, we booked thru a travel agent and had arranged for a queen bedroom, upgrade upon availability, and free breakfast. When we checked in, they claimed no upgrades were available as the hotel was sold out. So, after what seemed like an eternity the front desk person selected room 839 for us. He asked for a Credit Card which i promptly gave him, and he disapearred to another room with it for a few moments. He came back and said my card doesnt work ( well it did then and it does still now). I gave him another one, and he said that one was fine. ( I still dont know why he went to another room with my card, kind of concerning) He then gave us the keys and wished us well. I asked about how we get our free breakfast, and he with confidence responded that we dont get free breakfast. I suggested he re-look at his computer as I had already confirmed twice with the hotel prior to arrival that perk. The clerk realized his error and gave us our vouchers.....Room 839 was generally fine, and what i expected for the hotel/NY. However, I did expect that the pocket door to the bathroom would work. Instead, those people in the restroom / shower get to share their experience with other persons in the room. Not a 'feature' i would expect at a Waldorf. I didnt bother complaining to the hotel during our visit, as quite honestly i was just ready to be out of the City given the marathon cancellation. Would I go back to Waldorf, yes maybe. Would i go to Waldorf over The Palace at comparable rate. That would be a tough sell.

title: Staying at the Waldorf astoria New york
body: The experience was magnificent. The room was great. Small wardrobe. Nice size bathroom. Fresh soap daily. Not much of a view though. The staff were always helpful. Did not eat there. Breakfast was US$40.00 pp! It was close to a Starbucks. The foyer was lovely. Fully intended to have a cocktail there, but never found the time! The location is excellent. We booked early, and were pleasantly shocked with the price. There is a accommodation sale for the month of August in New York. Nearly every hotel has a room sale. There are shops at the hotel. Did not shop there. There is a postal service there. The beds had 4 pillows each, and were so pleasant to sleep on. No tea or coffee making facility though.

title: paint it, polish it, varnish it. Its still a turd
body:
Why is one of the most famous hotels in the world ranked 178th in New York ? read on. I have waited 6 weeks to write this review because of waiting for a response from The Asstoria re the many problems we had whilst staying there. It is only because of the satisfaction I have had from Kuoni that I will now share our experience. 
 We booked a 4 night stay at the Asstoria as part of a package tour to the USA. 5 nights in Vegas (Ceasars Palace) Excellent. 5 nights in Boston ( Nine Zero ) Out of this world. Then the Asstoria. 
 Our check in went well and the place really did look impressive. I asked if a package which I had arranged to be delivered to the Asstoria ( with prior consultation with the Asstoria) had arrived, I was told No. On arrival at the Queens room We could not help but think it looked very very tired, and lord knows why they would call it a Queen room coz I don't personally know the Queen but I am sure she would not stop in one of them. Her Corgis might. My wife asked me to have a look at the wardrobe, It measured 2 foot across, inside was the wall safe and a 2 dollar ironing board. There was room for two of her dresses and everyhting else was/would be creased to high heaven. I quickly worked out that I would be living out of my suitcase. We went out within 1 hour to explore New York and arrived late that evening after a good evenings night out. As soon as we got to our room we got ready for bed. I tried to flush the toilet and there was no water. It was the same with the Shower and taps. My mate next door rang me and said they had the same problem. I rang the reception and they told me "There was an unforssen problem with the water" and that they could send some bottled water up to the room so we could clean our teeth. I did not have the nerve to ask how many bottles it would take to get rid of a Number 2 or to have a shower with. The 2nd morning we got up and water had returned as you would expect. Also posted under the door was a letter of apology and it said we could have a free upgrade when we next book the Asstoria. We went down to the reception and I asked re my package, I was told it had still not arrived, I contacted the Supplier in England who asked for my full address via email so they could confirm the package had been sent. We had a good day in New York and had a quiet evening in our room. 
 We got up that next morning and my wife had an terrible sore throat with the air con vents blowing on her all night. I turned the vents in the opposite direction and they were thick with black dust.I left a note on the dressing table asking for the vents to be cleaned and also for someone to have a look at the dressing table lamp which we could not turn on. This lamp was in the corner of the room where my wife could use the only socket to dry her hair. I went to reception on our way out to view New York and asked re my package. It Still had not arrived. We had a good day in New York and returned to the Asstoria. I asked re my package and it still had not arrived. On arrival to our room the problem with the air vents or lamp had not been resolved
 That night we went to our room and my mate told me to do the same as he had done the previous night and turn off the air con as my wife was really suffering by now and to lift the windows a couple of inches, you couldnt lift them much higher anyway because of some catches on the windows. The windows were as stiff as anything, eventually I managed to lift a window an inch and as I put my fingers under it to lift it, the window suddenly dropped and trapped the end of my finger cutting it open. I was livid. after a plaser and a large Baileys I was in bed doing my best to try and chill out. (The bed was really comfy). About 10 minutes after trapping my finger, there was a knock on the door. It was one of the service guys, He asked if we ahd taken a shower in the last half an hour. I told him we had taken a bath. He asked us not to use the bath or shower again during our stay as the bath had emptied its entire contents onto the ceiling below us and was causing a massive bulge ready to burst at any time. I was livid. I told the guy of our problems whilst staying there and by this time I had had enough. I apologised to the guy for having a go at him but I was shaking with rage. About 10 minutes later the night shift manager rang and asked us to move rooms. Basically I told her in no uncertain terms what had gone off and that at 9.45pm sat in bed in me jim jams I was not moving. My finger was throbbing, my wife was run down with her sore throat etc and we were asked to move. In essence I told her "to get stuffed" and that I could not wait to get out of the Asstoria". That night we did not sleep to good.
 The following morning I asked re my package which was the last full day which we had in New York/Asstoria. Again I was told it had not arrived. I turned on my wifi and recieved an email from the supplier in England which said "The package arrived at the Waldorf Asstoria On the 11th Sept", 3 days BEFORE we arrived there. The package was signed for by a Mr Manny Rivera. My head went. I went to the desk and asked for my pacakage. They told me they could not find it. I asked them to speak to Mr Rivera. I was told he was not at work that day and they could not contact him. I was shaking with rage. It was the straw which broke the camels back. I told my wife and 2 friends to disappear as I was "about to kick Off". I asked at the reception desk to speak to a manager. I was told they would fetch one. I was stood like a numpty for 10 minutes and no one had come, so I asked an oriental woman behind the desk " Has anyone asked for a desk manager to speak to me yet, "she said she was a manager and no one had told her I was waiting to see someone". I told her she "had 30 seconds to get a witness at what I had to say and find a quiet room or we can do it in the main reception room", (swear words omitted). I sat down with this young lady and her male associate and laid into the pair of them for 10 minutes, I effed and blinded til I was blue in the face. I was offered free spa treatment, meals in the Bear tit resturaunt or whatever its called. I told them to get lost, I did not want anything off them. How could I lay on my back trying to chill out on my last day having had 3 days of hell in the Waldorf, when my friends were exploring NY we had made plans months ahead. I told the pair of them that the only thing I wanted was my package. I was assured that everything would be sorted. package, light, air vents. We spent the rest of the day in NY and had a good day.
 On arrival at our room we could still not use the bath or shower for our final night, In four nights stay we could only use the bath/shower once. but the light and air vents had been cleaned. To work the table lamp you had to turn on the bathroom light at the other end of the room to make the circuit, eh. We had a lovely letter of apology from the room cleaning manager apologising for the problems and a nice bottle of wine and a box of chocolates. I then asked my wife "wheres my package". It was mowhere to be found. I went down to the reception desk and asked "where was my package", I was told that it could not be found. Once more I was raging. I was then asked for a "tracking number", I told them they were "taking the micky". The tracking of the package would only guarantee its arrival at the Waldorf Asstoria, Which it did when it was signed for by Mr Rivera. It would not say which shelf he had put it on, or pocket he had put it in. I went back to our room and told her if she so much as looked at the chocolates or wine then I would end up in Alcatraz. We checked out the following morning and the package had still not been returned from someones pocket. I was told that it would be forwarded to me me when found. Really. 6 weeks later after initial email contact with the Waldorf Asstoria saying they were "looking into it". I started getting automated emails, I spoke to Manchester City FC whoi had sent my package/football shirt, they told me to set up a dispute with my credit card company. This I did and I eventually recieved a full refund. 
 All of this has left a bitter bitter taste in my mouth re the cesspit of an Hotel called the Waldorf Asstoria. Kuoni gave me a 25% cash refund of my stay there. I waited to see what they had to say before writing this review. 
 Quite frankly as far as I am concerned the people were supposed to make my stay in New York a special 50th do are the scum of the earth, who not only made our stay the worst possible but also robbed me. I sincerely would like the Waldorf to respond to this matter, but i do not hold out much hope. So i now hope people will now realise why the Waldorf Asstoria is now rated 178th hotel in New York. If you want to stay in a place with History find a cave with paintings on the wall, as i am sure you will be happier. Me as far as I am concerned re the Waldorf Asstoria, "You can paint it, Polish it or Varnish it. Its still a turd. If the Waldorf Asstoria wants to turn there hotel around then they should sell it to The KIMPTON Hotels group.

title: Nice Time, a little dated...but historic!
body: We just returned from a weekend trip to NYC. We stayed at the Waldorf from Friday to Sunday. We actually used Hilton Honors points, so we didn't pay for the room. I am actually glad that was the case because I probably would have been a little dissapointed had we paid high prices. The hotel was very clean, just a little too old for my taste. But, I feel you have to stay there at least once in your life. It was very opulent and historic. The staff was very nice, very helpful. We actually didn't eat there, but the Sunday Brunch looked awesome. We stayed in a regular room, it was just a little small. (which is typical of NYC hotels) It could have used a little updating. But, the beds were very comfortable. The shower was very good. And there were robes in the room. All in all, a great stay, but was glad we didn't pay $1200 for two days to stay there.

title: Nice Hotel
body: Perhaps our expectatives were too high on the Waldorf because even if the rooms are nice with plenty of space (for NY STD they are very big), the commons areas are very nice, the service was OK and everything worked fine in general, we didn't experience anything unique, which we have experienced in other Hotels for a lot less money.

title: Nice, old fashion.
body:
Excellent service, spacious rooms. 
The position of the hotel is definetly one of the best in town. A lot of nice restaurants near the hotel. Hotel restaurants are excellent, but $$$ plus. 
Would recommend for NYC.

title: "old fashioned class"
body: My family and i stayed here in august and we has a brilliant time,we only stayed 2 nights but the beds were to die for and the roomn was big enough for the four of us. we didnt eat at the hotel but there are loads of places to eat around.

title: Skip it.
body:
We stayed here last weekend for to catch a show on a Saturday night. The place was very busy, but the service was still very good, the people couldn't have been more helpful!
However, the first thing we saw when we opened the door was the wallpaper peeling off the wall. The bathroom had actual hair caught in some of the wall screws, and the TV remote only worked from one specific angle. The room was big, but the plugs on the side of the desk to charge phones, etc, didn't work. 
And the number one reason why we would NEVER stay there again-- the thermostat in the room was broken. By the time we got back from our night on the town- we didn't have the interest in calling to complain- but that heater blasted roasting hot & dry air at us all night. It ended up being 75 degrees by the morning. It was tourture. 
Also, the housekeeping opened our door at 9 a.m., on a Sunday, to see if we were still there.... check out is at 11 a.m. Awful.

title: It was a long stay.....
body:
We stayed at the waldorf during Hurricane Sandy. Flights were cancelled so we had an extra six night stay. it was easy to extend the stay and they didnt rip us off which was good - we heard a few people saying that their hotels had overcharged for the extended stay.
Rooms were nothing special but clean, toileteries were refreshed every day. 
We had to have room service due to the storm which despite how busy they were was efficient. Breakfast was expensive but delicious!
We could hear the traffic of NY which was hard for us as we live in the country - not the hotels fault clearly but quite frustrating for us!

title: Not quite what we expected.
body: Stayed here on points recently. At a cost of 70,000 per night, I expected to be blown away as I was the Chicago Astoria. Not so... the rooms are very very small, average amenities but the bed was very comfortable. As a Diamond member, we were not upgraded period. We were given a coupon for two drinks at the bar and a coupon per day for the Starbucks on site, it provided one small coffee per person. I was more impressed with the location than the actual hotel itself. The concierge was helpful in directing us to local eateries and even made the reservations for us. Other than that, probably should have stayed at the Millennium Hilton at the other end of Manhattan.

title: Two Words - Crystal Potter!
body: The Waldorf and the Waldorf Astoria Tower is our "go-to" place in NYC. We are constantly told "Welcome Back". I have no idea how they know that. At the Peacock Bar, the Hostess, Crystal Potter, after our first trip there during this stay, not only called us by name, but also knew what we were drinking. I'm a HHonors Diamond guy, but never have treatment like we get at this property. Congratulations to Eric the Manager, and his entire staff for making every trip here feel so special.

title: Elegant, Old Property
body: We stayed here in the towers last weekend. Very nice one bedroom suite on the 36th floor. Beautiful layout and well kept property. Difficult checking in....we were informed that our room was not ready, so we had to store our bags and walk around Manhattan in our dress clothes. I didn't understand why they didn't offer to us to wait in the executive lounge while the room was being prepared. Nonetheless, the room was in good order exept for the fact that they gave us the room next to the maids closet, which was quite noisy. For $800 per night, I guess I expected more. The buffet in the executive lounge in the morning was okay, nothing special. No evening appetizers or such. Every afternoon cookies and coffee were offered in the lounge, but that was it. Great location, close to everything. All of the employees were extremely polite, well trained.

title: Classy. Living museum
body:
The Waldorf Astoria. It's a legendary place, and I was most impressed with the building.
The maintenance of the older property will always be difficult, and it was understandable that there will be a few issues, but there does need to be a heavy clean for the room I was in.
I didn't expect to see dust on the crevices of the door, nor mug rings on the surface at the TV at the WA.

title: Art Deco opulence at it's bestl
body:
If it's uber chic modernity that you're after, this isn't the hotel for you. If elegant old buildings are your thing....they don't come any finer than The Waldorf. At check in we had to wait, but only because Rebecca wanted us to have a great room ( which wasn't yet ready) because we were staying for a week. The room was massive, with a separate dressing area and sumptuous bathroom. If you're not used to being in the U S get them to explain how to turn on the water for bath or shower. ( I got confused). It's true that in places the room looked a little tired and there are no tea/coffee making facilities, but there are ways around that. There is construction going on at the moment, and therefore quite noisy during the night, but not enough to keep you awake, unless perhaps you are a very light sleeper, in which case, ask for a room not facing Park Avenue.
The Lobby, and Reception area are breathtaking and it is difficult to hide your admiration for a building so exquisite. The staff are very friendly and accommodating, room service is something else, a very elegant affair, but pricey....but hey what do you expect. Peacock Alley is lovely but extortionate. All in all, you get what you pay for. If you come to Waldorf, expect to pay handsomely for it, but for a trip of a lifetime....what the hell. Absolutely brilliant in every way

title: Waldorf falls short
body: What could be a great hotel in a great location is a mediocre use of the name...the rooms are small and in spite of the high price tag the hotel incredibly has the affront to charge for wifi! This is 2012 not 1999, and any hotel who charges "extra" for a basich service, and it isn't cheap either, gets a bad review. What is good is the location. There also also long waits at reception.

title: Posh, but basic
body:
The Waldorf Astoria, wreaks of splendor, oozes with money. The attention by the staff is fantastic, all the staff we met, wanted to help and assist, from the bell hop on the front door, which we had the pleasure to be with for an hour whilst waiting for our car. To the maid who wished us a pleasant journey as she watched us with our suitcase going towards the lift.
Once checked-in we went to our room. The room wasn't the most spacious one I have been in, but was OK. Two large beds comfortable enough. After calling reception twice for a firm pillow, we decided, that after the nine pillows that had been delivered, we weren't going to get a firm one. The TV was large, and channels a plenty. But there was no tea/coffee facilities, which makes this room, OK, not one to kick back after a hard days walking and shopping to rest in. The bathroom carried on the basic approach with old fittings, and a bath that couldn't fill up fast enough as the water drain through the closed plug.
The windows need double glazing. Because at around 2am all trucks in New York city have to drive backwards and make that beeping sound, or thats what it sounded like from our room. 
When in the Waldorf, you must eat the Waldorf salad... and yes it was nice, although the accompanying bread had seen better days. The whisky and beers were also nice.
This hotel is nice for conferences, meetings, and its location, but if you value money more than the pretentious of staying near the city center then choose elsewhere, otherwise you will be disappointed.

title: Historical
body: After several days we spent In Hilton Garden NYC (excellent) we moved to WA, as it was planned before, not by us. The hotel of course has a great historical value and as a museum could be on the long list of uncountable attractions in NYC. Unfortunately, the room standard was not as high as expected. We had problems with hitting, safe, electricity etc. Very kind room service was really helpful in this case. We had breakfast included and the Oscar food proposal was also very nice. The unpleasant side in restaurant were waiters, waiting only for the tips and roughly mentioning that they are expecting 15% gratitude and not being satisfied with 2$. I can’t see a reason, in all incusive buffet- type (self-service) breakfast a 15% tip! Another unbelievable thing for such an high level Hotel – wifi for 18$ per day! If I return one day to NYC, I would surely prefer Hilton Garden. But of course, I am happy, I had the chance to see W-A and stay there for few days!

title: Great rooms but stuffy service
body:
Stayed one night as where I had been staying in Chelsea was not able to accommodate me for all the extra nights I spent in NYC after a trip to Portland, Maine fell through. Found a room for a good price on booking.com and thought I'd treat myself a little.
Check in is a little hectic but for a hotel this size that is to be expected. The check in queue moved fairly quickly though.
Room - well appointed apart from the bathroom which is a little dated. Also for someone not terribly familiar with ancient USA plumbing a sign of some sort to pull the knob out for hot water would be a good idea. Bed very comfortable with a gorgeously soft doona. Great sleep quality. mini bar - a little pricey but that is to be expected of a hotel of this calibre. 
Had an issue with the wi fi and it wasn't recognizing my room. Spent 10 minutes on the phone trying to get it sorted and then they sent someone to my room to figure it out; who arrived promptly - he couldn't fix it so gave me a complimentary promotional code to use which gave me the access I needed, so I could get some work done. Bit of a stuff around but they did the right thing with sorting the issue out and not charging me for usage.
Didn't go to any of the restaurants or bars as most had a dress code and I had no jacket with me; as the majority of my trip was holiday. I find the idea of dress codes a little outdated.
Would I stay here again? Only if I remember to bring a jacket and tie.

title: Excellent service at a tough time
body: We were there on the weekend after hurricane Sandy and the hotel was packed to the gills with thwarted European marathoners. Nonetheless, the service was impeccable and the room , though small, was nicely furnished and super-clean. I do agree with the earlier poster that here ought to be either in-room tea/coffe or coffee service in the lobby for guests. And the newsstand ought to stock the Financial Times. But these are quibbles -- overall a top-notch experience.

title: Iconic, amazing hotel
body:
Simply the best. Nostalgia overcomes you when you arrive, great service, exceptional attitude and sheer luxury. The location is very good with numerous taxis to take you anywhere you desire. The hotel amenities are wonderful as is the breakfasts! 
Great stay

title: Lovely but small room. Helpful service
body: We were upgraded upon check-in. Room was small but clean, nice bathroom and comfy bed. Big kudos to Javier in security.... We checked out this morning and tonight I realized I left a brand new leather jacket hanging in the closet. I called the hotel and Javier located it within a few minutes. Phew!

title: A classic - Iconic - In the 80's I'd have been delighted - Now dated.
body:
It's the name that you grew up with, the communal areas lobby, bars are faultless, I booked on a BA Flight and Hotel package at a very attractive rate, maybe some rooms are being modernised... mine was clean, but dated.. Okay, so the room was a little passe, in style, non of the fittings stood out,and maybe waiting to be refurbished - however I'd expect the little things to be better - the towels and toiletries not of the quality I'd expect, En Suite was just old marble and fittings / shower curtain and shower - just dated - with a light buzzing in the wardrobe, which I couldn't switch off, Air con a little difficult to control, a mini bar with no pricing, no coffee facility - I could have asked and didn't !, the TV channel list under glass next the bed, was out of date - maybe this was a deliberate theme !! 
I didn't have breakfast as was on business and getting up early, but room service seems inline with other mainstream Hiltons.
For business - fine, for my money I'd spend the extra and go W.

title: Great comfort, high prices
body: I loved the accommodations -- very comfortable, well maintained, an old feeling of luxury. The prices were too high -- but this is NYC. The location is great -- easy to get around midtown and the East side. Room service was fine -- but the bagels in the restaurant (for breakfast) must have been made of gold.

title: They don't make them like this anymore!
body:
Check in was extremely friendly and nice and I was treated to a lovely corner room on the 22nd floor. As others have said, the rooms are a bit small but mine was very clean and orderly. 
The best aspect of the Waldorf are the public spaces. The lounges, lobby, restaurants all reflect a lost era. They even have a dress code which I had not seen since my stay at the Greenbriar. There as no enforcement that I could see but at least they made an effort.
Of course coffee is expensive! With fairly reasonable room rates, all of this luxury has to be paid for somehow. It seems some people wants Walfdorf service and luxury at Hampton Inn prices!
My only complaint (and it is significant), is that my bathtub did not drain. I called three times before it was repaired. Not so good from a place like this!
Otherwise, go ahead and treat yourself.

title: Take the tour!
body: Had an amazing experience at the WA. Guest service was excellent from all staff, genuine friendliness from George who we met in the lobby area and saw a few times during our stay. Barbara led our hotel tour and what a great lady she was, made us feel at home while sharing the incredible history of the hotel. Our room was clean, spacious and luxurious. The beds were the best we have slept in at a hotel, bathroom was marble with nice amenities and lovely scented soaps. We dined at Oscars which had an excellent quality buffet and delicious desserts, loved the red velvet cake! We were so fortunate to stay a the Waldorf for a special 60th birthday trip and we would return in a heartbeat if the opportunity arises. The location is idea for seeing all the major sights of NYC.

title: Always a treat.
body:
I've stayed at the Waldorf-Astoria many times over the years. It's always a treat. The service is always top notch and they truly care about maintaining the property. Only small drawback - be a little patient with the showers: some rooms are more updated than others; sometimes the transition mechanisms for going from bath to shower are a little tricky.
One minor issue in an otherwise fabulous hotel. I love every opportunity to walk through the lobby!

title: Fantastic experience - and even Sandy didn't spoil it
body: Our stay at the Astoria was part of a special birthday visit with our two children - 10 and under. Room was lovely, bathroom clean and the shower great. Service was fantastic and everyone was really helpful. We were there during Hurricane Sandy and although they ended up a bit short staffed the only thing they reduced was room service on one day when you had to request maid service if you wanted it. They laid on additional tours of the hotel for those of us who were stuck in as the storm came in. We wouldn't have done something like that normally but it was great and we got to see bits of the hotel we wouldn't have done otherwise and really learn about the amazing history of the place. Would recommend the hotel, the tour (I think they do them to a lesser degree normally) and simply the experience of staying in this famous location.

title: The lobby was worth the price of admission.
body: We can now say that we stayed at the "Waldorf". This is a very beautiful hotel with a pretigious history. Marble everywhere, exceptionally helpful and courteous staff (except one bartender who spent too much time hitting on young women instead of tending to regular customers), and a perfect mid town Manhatten location on Park Avenue. Our room was a little small, but comfortable. Yes, it is very expensive! This is something we will probably do only once in our lifetime, but we have no regrets.

title: I'm giving it three stars because I'm in a good mood.
body: I waned to take my girlfriend here because she's always dreamed about it. Dreams meet reality. We are well traveled and I've stayed here before, about ten years ago. This place seriously needs to be remodeled. The lobby is classic and ornate, but our suite which we paid dearly for was seriously rundown. Everything is just old old old. For example the fabric in the arm chair was worn out. Really? I realize this is a world renowned landmark, so then they should not hold this place out as 4 1/2 star accommodations because it really isn't. It's a rundown hotel that seriously needs to be revamped. We are here for a few more days and now I will try to change our suite over to the tower area which I have read is less rundown. Then there's the simple things, like the need for a quick area with coffee and snacks and maybe even gifts. They have tons of old retail space here selling Chinese antique pieces, and jewelry, but today's modern traveler wants home away from home with a coffee and snack shop. So my recommendation is to never stay here, but instead walk in and enjoy the ornate lobby and take a few pictures with your traveling companion or friends in the lobby and then move on and stay in a real hotel… It hurts me to say this because I stayed here before and attended grand banquets and had such a good time as a younger man, but this place ain't happening anymore!

title: Musty to Magnificent
body: I booked a room for a 5 night stay at the Waldorf. After meeting my friend at the lobby bar - check out Cole Porter's piano - we went to our first room - lovely fabrics and drapes, comfortable beds, hardly any room for anything, a strong, musty smell, inside views of hotel walls, and a broken leaking sink. Not what I was expecting. My friend has H Honors Diamond status so that entitled us to an upgrade which was provided the next day. Second room was a large one-room suite, but only 1 bed and a foldout couch - oops! We met with Mary Macias in Diamond Reception who arranged for transfer the following day to our magnificent one bedroom suite with our own living room, fireplace and a view of Park Avenue. Now THAT's the Waldorf Astoria. She also arranged for Room Service to provide us with a coffee maker so we could brew our own while getting ready in the mornings. When we picked up our new room keys, Sedrick from Belgium escorted us to our suite and followed up with a phone call to make sure everything was all right. It certainly was!

title: November 2012
body:
I had heard some quite negative reviews about the hotel but our experience was entirely positive.
The restaurants were however quite expensive as was the mini bar.
Centrally situated for all the main things to see.

title: Great Fantastic Stay
body:
Waldorf is somewhat expensive but worth the money. The location is best. Near everything in New York City. Near subways also. Within walking distance of Times Square. 
The rooms elegant. The mini bar a bit on the up side. The restaurants amazing. Loved the piano bar. 
The lobby full of grandeur with all its marble. The staff very accommodating and professional. Overall would highly recommend.

title: Great value
body: Wonderful mid-town location close to major shopping venues. Great lobby bar (Peacock Alley) and fun historical ambiance. Only two things kept me from awarding all 5 stars: very poor shower and inoperative stopper in bathtub; refusal of bellhops to help secure a taxi for trips shorter than airport.

title: Shocked!
body: I can only imagine what this place was in its day. Probably one of the dirtiest hotels I've ever been in NY. Shocked that Hilton lends its name to this. The hotel is allegedly under renovations but don't worry you won't see any workers. Some of the personnel have too much attitude an you wonder if they still think they are in 1982. Maybe because all the carpets are circa 1982. Don't stay anywhere below the 7th floor, you won't be able to regulate your room's temperature. When I called downstairs to complain because my room was too warm, the lady at the front counter asked me to open a window. When my shower and toilet got clogged the service man showed me the black mold inside the toilet. Don't dare to move a chair, the dust bunnies might bite you. The antique reproductions in many common areas are pretty tacky, buy real antiques they are not that expensive and they will give the hotel the charm and personality that it needs so desperately.

title: Great experience!!
body: From the Bell man that greeted us, to friendly maids, to "Daria" our server twice at Oscars, we felt appreciated at every level of our stay!! Thank you Waldorf for making our celebration of my wifes 50th birthday special. The hotel itself and its location speak for themselves, perfect! Congrats Hilton, the combination of an elegant historic hotel, and the customer service make this a home run!!

title: A little tired but well worth a visit
body:
We stayed at the Waldorf for 3 nights as part of a 10 day trip to New York and whilst it is a little tired in places it only adds to the historical charm of the place. The lobby is impressive but does get extremely busy at times, our suite was ample for our stay and the staff were all very helpful and polite. We didn't eat in any of the hotel restaurants but did have room service which was overpriced for what it was - almost $100 for a pizza, fries, side salad and two cans of coke.
There are other hotels I'd like to visit in New York but I would be more than happy to stay here again.

title: fabulous hotel
body: a business traveler here - great, grand scale hotel. Very clean and very helpful staff. Easy approach to public transportation and a short walking distance from everything that is NYC. The only issue I have is the charge they impose on WiFi connection; foolish and unnecessary. Its about time no hotel charges for internet access.

title: Probably would not stay here again, but the lobby is something to see
body: In all fairness, we stayed here after getting a last minute deal of $289/night for the Thanksgiving holiday. I had read the reviews about the hotel being tired and outdated and still jumped at the chance to experience this hotel, particuarly at the holidays. First off, we told the desk at check-in that we were there to go to the Macy's parade and confirmed that we should leave the hotel at 5 a.m. and arranged for the very important wake up call at 4:15 a.m. which never came - good thing we also set our phones or we would have missed the parade. Disappointing for a hotel of this caliber. Our room was a queen bed and was small, but fine for two adults. The bathroom was tiny, but workable and for folks who have cruised and stayed in other historic hotels, not a big deal. Most importantly, it was clean and the bed was comfortable. I tried to use the way overpriced laundry service ($22 for jeans) but called just before the 10 a.m. pickup time to be told that "the truck had just left, but we can get you expedited service for the upcharge." No thanks and again, not what I would expect from this level of hotel. I should also note that when we were dropped off from the airport by our taxi, no bellman appearaed and the doorman did not even try to get us help with our luggage. Some elderly women from Germany actually approached us trying to find the elevator due to the same reason and there is not one. We eventually lugged our bags down steps, back a dark corridor to an elevator and found our way to the lobby no thanks to the housekeeper sweeping the steps nearby or the doorman. Thus, we should not have been surprised that on Saturday morning when we asked the bell captain to please send someone up, it was a lot longer than the 15 minute wait he promised before someone appeared. I do have to say that the man who helped us with our bags at that time, was the best representative of the hotel we had. He was very friendly and helpful and was the first person who seemed to take an interest in us. Too bad he is not working the front desk. I am still glad we stayed at the Waldorf so we have experienced it, but would probably just go somewhere else next time and I am glad we did not pay their traditional price as I would have been way more disappointed. The hotel is beautiful but the service was definitely lacking - though it was a very busy holiday weekend so that must be considered. Still, a guest of a luxury hotel should not feel like an inconvenience to the staff.

title: Pretty Nice Stay!
body: I loved the feeling of luxury and fanciness when I stepped inside this hotel. I gawked at and could not get over the nice appearance of the halls and lobby. The rooms were a little on the small side (we didn't get a suite) but it was a very good stay and I slept fairly well. They have lots of advertising throughout the hotel, and there is no swimming pool because the hotel is like 120 years old. They spa looked very nice, but I didn't go there. My favorite part, though, was the ladies bathroom just outside the lobby. It was so COOL! There was a room full of mirrors, and a big mural, and then you go up a little set of stairs to seven stalls that are equipped with marble sinks! My brother said the men's bathroom wasn't as good, though. My point is that I recommend this hotel very much.

title: Attention to detail lacking severely
body:
A grand old hotel with a wonderful atmosphere and great mix of customers.
However....
Before my trip I wrote to the hotel to ask them to arrange a special sweet treat for my partner's birthday, which I would of course pay for, to be delivered to our room on the day. No response to my correspondence but thought being a five star Hilton property they would deal with it. The day came and nothing happened, not even a call from guest relations to confirm this. So we went without.
I also contacted the hotel to confirm my payment details. No response. Turns out on arrival they had the wrong details as suspected. When checking my bill on the last day I was assisted by a preoccupied and rather sarcastic lady on reception.
Signage and directions are confusing downstairs. Took a while to find our luggage on leaving.
The room had a lovely view of the Chrysler building but was more 3* thank 5*. Stains, peeling wallpaper and tired furnishings.
That said, some work is being carried out in the hotel so at least some investment is going into this great, iconic property. And about time.
But The Waldorf Astoria team let the place down in a big way. Must improve. Would never stay here again but I hope the hotel gets back to it's former glory.

title: Another Amazing Stay at the Waldorf
body: My fiancee and I recently stayed at the Waldorf for the third time and this was absolutely the best! When we arrived we found out that a computer glitch had caused our reservation not to work, but we were easily able to make one right away. As Gold HHonors members, they were kind enough to upgrade us to a gorgeous room in the Towers! We also really appreciated the complimentary drink we were each given in the bar of our choice, which is always a nice little perk.

title: Great Hotel for a Great deal
body:
We decided to go into New York on a Saturday night to see a broadway musical spur of the moment. On the morning of, we decided that it may be best to try and stay over night. It was Thanksgiving weekend so we knew getting an affordable room in Manhattan may be hard. We went online and I found a really great deal for this Hotel. We reserved a Queen Deluxe room and was only $40.00 more then a Holiday Inn a few blocks away. We knew we had to book this room because it was the Waldorf Astoria....how often would we come around a deal like this.
The Hotel Lobby has a classy historic look to it but there were a lot of people taking photographs inside. The staff was very nice to us as we were checking in. Our room was clean and spacious enough for the two of us and the bathroom was neat, orderly and very clean, and had two bathrobes with the Hotel Logo waiting for us. We were on the 41st floor with a room on the North Side. The room does have a mini bar but be mindful, it is very expensive. There was a Mini Bottle of red wine for $185.00...
We had a drink down in the lobby lounge. Make sure you have enough in your wallet.
Overall, our stay was what we expected from an expensive Hotel. We did wish we could stay a few nights, but the one night we had was more then what we could have expected. My advise, check on line and book late and you may find an outstanding deal as we had.

title: Beautifully Elegant Gracious Hotel
body: From the moment the doorman assisted us with our bags and my husband and I stepped into the exquisite lobby, I knew we were going to experience something special. We were not disappointed. This was an anniversary trip and our first stay in New York City. We have been to many citiies around the world, London, Paris, Munich to name a few but had put off going to the Big Apple until now. Check-in was a wonderful experience made so by a very helpful and friendly young lady. We were so happy to discover we had been upgraded to a gorgeous suite with an amazing view. We were also given vouchers for free drinks in the Bull and The Bear no small gift as drinks run anywhere from $18.00 and up. We treated ourselves to the world famous Waldorf Salad in the Peacock Alley restaurant along with a properly made martini and congratulated ourselves on being one of "The People" surrounded by opulence and luxury. We also discovered The Waldorf maintains their own beehives on the roof and the honey is used in many of the recipes at the restaurants. I love atention to detail and this hotel does not disappoint. From the glittering diamond-like chandeliers down to the art nouveau inlays on the elevator doors, every where my eye rested, there was a piece of beauty to be admired and appreciated. The staff was excellent, from the servers in the restaurants to the bartenders at The Bull and Bear, we dined in The Peacock Alley twice, enjoyed libations in The Bull and Bear on 3 separate occasions, to the wonderful staff in the Guerlain Spa, the concierge, the bellman and even the white-gloved housekeepers, everyone was gracious and kind, exactly what we'd expect from a hotel that once entertained the likes of Queen Elizabeth II and F. Scott Fitzgerald. We actually stayed at the hotel on 2 separate occasions, 2 days when we first arrived, we left for a Canadian cruise, and then returned for a 3 day stay. On our second visit we stayed in an executive king bed room for the first night and then paid for the additional upgrade to a luxury suite with the spa treatment package for the remaining two nights. I do have to say the king bed room did show some signs of age, heavy door into bathroom a bit difficult to close, but the furnishings were still lavish and the beds were so comfortable, we still felt pampered and happy. The location of the hotel in the city is perfectly centralized for enjoying quite a few of the main attractions and shopping. We will definitely stay at the Waldorf on our next visit to New York. We can't wait to be transported back to the luxuriously decadent world of The Great Gatsby.

title: The Waldorf NY
body: A nostalgic trip down memory lane to a hotel that is proud of it's history and status! Don't visit if you like minimalist style this hotel is art deco extravaganza!! Its a real treat staying in a place that still holds functions in the ballrooms where guests arrived in full evening dress and your going up in the same lift as them returning from your site seeing in boots and jackets !! We stayed 'room only' so didn't partake in any food or extras but if you can splash out its worth it for that experience alone. The hotel itself is very central so we only needed to walk everywhere and you felt like you were spoilt staying in the middle of all the action!. A rare treat - slightly tired in parts but overall you help be impressed by the attention given to the hospitality and welcome.

title: Fading Glory
body:
Worth staying for the location and the public areas. The historic interior is fantastic. The rooms are a bit sad, like wealthy relations who have fallen on hard times. At this level, a complete hospitality tray should be standard in every room. We were in a queue until a coffee maker became available.
Comfortable bed but such a large gap around the door that blackout masks needed to be worn to ensure sleep. Would like to stay again but only if a significant revamp of rooms is undertaken.

title: kind of ok
body:
the shiny glamour of other days is lost...patina turned into rust.
service kind of ok (concierge did not respond to emails)
limotransfer to jfk 439$ instead of 169$ as competitors....why??? 
rooms partially dirty
switches loose
air condition broken
windows dirty
only the clock with the bell in the lobby reminds of better times
what a shame, such a huge name wasted on such low mediocrity
not again!

title: Real value for money
body:
The Waldorf Astoria is everything you could wish for if you go for room only. The external appearance is undegoing renovation but that aside, it was everything we could wish for (and more). Yes it lacked some of the familiarity you may get from smaller and cheaper hotels, but when in a hotel of this size, what do you expect. Every single member of staff were polite, courteous and only too willing to help if and when approached. We arrived before Thanksgiving to be greeted by a computer failure but enough staff were on hand to help out and only too willing. When we explained where we had travelled from and how long, the check-in staff handed us a $20 dollar drinks voucher each to make us help us relax after a long journey (without prompting). 
Our Queen Room was large enough for our needs, with a large bathroom, ample storage room but lacking any tea/coffee making facilities. To pick fault though would be simple knit-picking. be prepared to not even open the mini-bar fridge or you will be charged $13 per day. Suffice to say we had the monety refunded tho !
The facilities and amenities are superb, the lobby's and foyers are dripping in history. The food and drinks ae expensive but thats what you get in a hotel of this standing. To pay $145 per head for the Thanksgiving Day buffet was a tad expensive but if you don' want it, then don't pay for it.
Excellently located 4 blocks north of Grand Central Station, 3 blocks east of 5th Avenue and all its shops, 12 blocks south of Central Park and 15 minute stroll from Times Square, ideal for getting around with the bus trips picking up from outside the south door.
What more could we have expected ?? Not a lot and everything we hoped for.

title: Tired, Crowded and Service-less
body:
Arrived for my first stay here and a business meeting. Check-in required a 20 minute wait in line...not a god start.
