We needed a private room for dinner to prepare for a meeting. It was so expensive, I won't even post it. The food was"okay" and nothing extraordinary. The service started out well but in the middle of the meal our server disappeared for about an hour...yes an hour.
The room was big with a comfortable bed. It looked rather old, with the exception of the bed which was both comfortable and new. The large flat screen was also new. However, there were dirty light switches, old rug and an older couch that took away the magic. No newspaper was offered nor was there an offer for help with bags. I should not as well that my business partner had a large blood spider, as he called it, in his bathroom.
Finally, my leaving experience was the worst for me. I sat down in the restaurant in the lobby for breakfast. It took 15 minutes to be asked if I wanted something to drink and another 15 minutes to receive it. That is pathetic. When I complained, I received a complimentary coca cola. Uh, thanks. This, I'm sure, is not the service that the Waldolf built it's name on. I'm very disappointed and will not return. I spent several thousands of dollars there on one night and dinner and would not value it nearly at that level.

title: Meh...
body:
I stayed here in May 2012. I was expecting more since it was the famed Waldorf Astoria. I think its reputation is what people go for. It is super expensive and I don't think you get what you pay for. Yes, the lobby is nice and the ballrooms are gorgeous, but the rooms were not as nice as I was expecting. It was all very old. My friend had a suite in the towers and again it's all very nice (and huge!) but old. I think their trying extremely hard to hold onto yesterday. The location is great though. 
If you have the money and want experience the Waldorf, then go for it. Otherwise, just stay somewhere else for less.

title: RECOMEND TO OTHERS =)
body:
we stayed in this hotel for 6nights and had a double room for 4 people, it was very spacious and clean with the maid cleaning the room and changing the sheets everyday. Room service was prompt with a good selection of food to choose from however it was very expensive! 1 pizza and 2 portions of fries was $70!! without any drinks. 
The location was quite far from places like 5th avenue, bus stations and times square which meant we had to get taxis everywhere..
On arrival when we mentioned the spa to the receptionist she tried to sell us a different room which made the spa cheaper, when we told her we were not interested she continued to tell us that it was a good deal to upgrade and didnt let it go which was VERY annoying!
However the rest of the service was very good - the porters were helpful giving directions and hailing taxis for us
The hotel was very busy and popular but we had a very nice stay would recomend to others =)

title: Beautiful History Told in NYC
body: Loved the Waldorf. It's a gorgeous historic hotel. The room was great, clean and spacious. I would definitely stay there again. If you want to get away and see a different crowd the W is right across the street. The brunch is amazing but, make sure you make reservations prior to checking in. You would still be able to get brunch as long as you arrive early. The room service was great and the food was very tasty. It's definitely a five star hotel for service and ambiance.

title: The Grand Old Lady is still going strong
body:
I have stayed here twice before and have to admit we love the majesty of the lobby and the size of the rooms. They have many room layouts but we have always gotten large corner rooms, with plenty of room to spare. It is an old hotel, but they take excellent care of it and I love this place. The staff is polite, efficient and courteous. The hotel looks like something out of a Carey Grant movie and has more history than similar hotels in NYC.
The location is perfect for a weekend trip to the city or a business meeting on Park Avenue. You will not be disappointed staying at the Waldorf in New York.

title: Nothing spectacular
body:
Firstly this trip was booked in Jan 2012 but on arriving at Waldorf Thurs 22nd Nov we waited for at least 20 mins at front reception desk while a staff member tried to locate rooms. There were 7 people in our party but our rooms were 8 floors apart. The rooms wern't spacious at all
and we had to ask several times before we were given the correct amount of towels and robes. However the icing on the cake came when after checking out of the hotel they proceeded to charge mine and another member of the party's credit cards for payment of the rooms that had already been paid. Waldorf indeed!! more like Faulty Towers !!

title: Excellence? Beautiful? Try Indifference and Inconvenience.
body:
We only had one night in the city and wanted to make our limited time there count. We were so excited to be staying in the famous Waldorf Astoria. I had made reservations for four adults, a month in advance, and saved the confirmation to prove it. We were put into a 10'x14' room with ONE queen bed, peeling paint, and adjacent to the elevator shaft. Immediately we contacted the desk about the incorrect sleeping accomodations, clearly they had made a mistake. Their proposed solution was to bring up two cots and charge us for them! It took two hours of going back and forth with management for them to move us into a room with two double beds. When I asked if they could offer us anything for the inconvenience and irreplacable time we had now lost in the city, the front desk manager extended a $50 credit to be used in-room. 
A week later, that $50 "credit" was actually billed to my credit card! And I still have not been able to resolve the error. No establishment has a right to inconvenience paying customers so blatantly and unapologetically. There was not even a trace of integrity shown by any of the staff we encountered. Despite having the confirmation in hand, they tried everything possible to spin the fault my way rather than just take responsibility for their errors. I am disappointed, embarassed to my family (planning was my responsibility), and just deeply saddened by the way things turned out.

title: The old queen still reigns
body: This hotel has almost more history than any other. It is well-located in the heart of Manhattan between 49th and 50th and betweeen Park and Lexington Avenues. Much has been renovated but the hotel is still oold and a bit tired in some respects. We attended a meeting held there and it was so convenient to stay there at a discounted rate.

title: Needs renovation
body:
İ have stayed in Waldorf for three nights during a meeting. i have chosen the place as it is the congress hotel.
i expected a lot . but i thinks that rooms needs renovation.
our room was a standart one .
Lobby is great alot of people are there for weddings and meetings.
location is great but there a lot of hotels around also.
you can use wifi only at lobby without fee. we payed alot so why asking for wifi at rooms. 500 -600 US .
Worst part is our room there is a stinking odor.
AC is old and very noisy.Electric swithches are old. bathroom is small but clean.
TV is good . Big LCD
Everthing seems a little bit dated. So it is an old hotel but with renovation İ think it can get back to is glory days

title: Not overly impressed
body: Expectations were too high to deliver. The grand entrance and lobby were spectacular; old world charm with a warm and inviting character- such a shame this didn't carry through to the rooms. Our room was musty and quite small, nearly no room between the two queen beds and the wall paper needed serious restoration or replacement. We did request extra conditioner - delivered promptly, free of charge and wrapped in a cute little posy. At the bar we females sat, drank and promptly left after my mother-in-law received inappropriate advances from a resident and staff.

title: Girlie Trip
body: Stayed 19th Nov 22nd Nov We booked hotel in Jan for speial birthdays in our party of five, when we checked in we ask for 2 joining rooms or a large 2 bedroom room. Two of the party emailed before stating it was a special trip and that could we have rooms together, but no same floors but miles apart. The hotel room we had was lovely quite a large room with mini bar but no tea and coffee making equitment, the other room was a bit bit small for three adultshaving 2 double beds. Its a grand old hotel full of charm, found it a bit out of the way as before stayed in Milleium Broadway in times square, but still enjoyed our stay. Very busy checking out as rather packed in reception due to it being used for a thanksgiving buffet. Make the most of the free wifi in reception.

title: Way Past it's Prime
body: The Waldorf is world known as an icon of of luxury. When I visited NYC, I wanted to try the Waldorf. It was my first visit and my last. The shine is definitely off this apple. The visit started with a long line to check-in. Upon entering the room (closet size), the decor was drab and dated. The bathroom had mold in the tub and the sink did not drain properly. When exiting the bathroom, there was a downward slope in the transition to the bedroom. Both my wife and I slipped. We notified housekeeping, but nothing was done in the two days we were there. On our way to dinner, we took the elevator and then a nightmare began. We pushed the lobby and when we arrived the door would not open. We pushed the door open button and the elevator shot up the the third floor and no door opened. Tried again and we shot up to the fifth floor. We pushed the lobby again and the door would still not open. We called security and after being asked if we knew how to operate the elevator, someone came to the door and told us to be cool and they would be back with tools. Finally after 20 minutes, we were freed. The hotel offered a credit of $100 towards breakfast. In the morning, we were told the credit only applied to the restaurant serving the buffet. The buffet was disgusting. Cold and brown colored food. We received the check and the $100 didn't cover it. Upon check out, we waited 45 minutes for our car after a $100 two day parking charge. The attendant was only interested in the tip and so was the guy bringing up the car. The bill was over $1000 for two days. This is a hotel that is living on its laurels and not worth you spending a nickel there with so many other great hotels in NYC. I am also disappointed in Hilton who now own the hotel. The Waldorf is not up to their usually high standards. Our advise is find another hotel and avoid the Waldorf.

title: Just another business hotel
body: We came here for a small family event, sort of a reunion. We picked the Waldorf because it has an important place in my family's history. We were disappointed with how the hotel is maintained, very disappointed with the indifferent service. On the plus side, the rooms and baths are large. The location is amazing. This wonderful old place deserves better care.

title: Wireless Internet
body:
just returned from 4 nights stay in the Waldorf Astoria, Manhattan and have to say I think the hotel is stingy beyond words for charging me (customers) $18.95 per day to have wireless access in rooms. We were paying $300 per night to stay and I think this is a very poor sign of customer service and downright money grabbing. The hotel itself is as would be expected superb from the level of room fittings, to service and food. We dined once in the restaurant where food was excellent, though the filet steaks were a little on the small side and service slow. There appears to be a small number of staff for the size of restaurant. At $288 for a three cours meal for two with no alcohol it is not cheap!! Had probably the best pizza ever via room service - the base was to die for!!
All in all a very happy customer but come on Waldorf - this is 2012 - drop your charges for wireless.

title: Sooooo Disappointing
body:
This is the first review I have given, but feel so strongly about the condition of this hotel that I felt I had to report on Trip Advisor. We have visited some of the best hotels in the World, but I am afraid this was not one of them! Although the Waldorf has a reputation of 'splendour, luxury, granduleur, amazing service' etc, this fell very short in reality. Admittingly the lobby area was very striking, but that is where it ends. The rooms are very very disappointing and far from being described as 'luxury' or 'delux'. The rooms are small, there is no air conditioning (boxed looking heaters on the wall blowing out cold or hot air), no mirrors over dressing table or plugs near enough to plug in hairdryer, very small bathrooms with cream coloured bath (which had cracks and big chunks out of it), sink and toilet (seat broken), small shower head over the bath with a nylon cream curtain!, soap but not shower gel (unhygienic), very limited shelf space (but a bathroom cabinet!!), no ventilation in bathroom, rusty vents on walls in bedroom, lots of surface cables hanging out of walls, walls around the windows in very bad disrepair, mould and wallpaper and paint peeling. I could go on. 
We were moved from a Queen delux to a King delux which was supposed to be an upgraded room and in fact it was smaller!. 
We would certainly not use this hotel again. I have given it 1 star for the Lobby area, but whilst in the very long queue for check in, we were told by security that they daily book in between 300 and 500 guests. Be prepared for long waits!

title: You can't help but love this hotel.
body: This is my third stay at this hotel and I think you have to be impressed. We stayed here to do some Christmas shopping and all the New York Christmas things we love to do. We got the superior king room with the AARP rate of 495.00 per night. It was a large room with lots of closet room and a large bath. When we made the reservation they gave us an option to upgrade if available at check in for 25.00, we did not do this but I will when we go back. The room does need some touching up, wall paper peeling in places scratches on the furniture ect., which surprises me they have not taken care of these things they are such easy fixes. The colors are dated also and will need a make over soon, but for New York I was pleased with our room. I love this lobby sitting in the Bar and people watching is an event in itself. I let them know we where celebrating our 23rd anniversary when we made the reservation and they gave us gift cards for free drinks in the bar, Thank You that was nice. Just to give you heads up they are in the middle of doing restorations outside of the building and there is scaffolding everywhere so your view may be obstructed, this is going on all over town even St. Patricks. We arrived on Friday and left on Tuesday, the weekend was packed everywhere and Sunday and Monday was much better so keep that in mind when planning your trip. There is nothing better to me than New York City before Christmas and The Waldorf Astoria IS classic New York.

title: Honeymoon in Waldorf Astoria New York
body: Everything was excellent Eat at the restaurant food/service great. Loved the floral arrangements in the lobby. Special thanks to Tom for the historic tour. Jr Suite was spacious and a great view. Cant wait to be back. Loved everything about the Waldorf.

title: Amazing
body:
Stayed here for 4 nights in early December.
The Hotel is fantastic, but it also had its problems.
I was wary about going here because of all the comments about the hotel being 'tired'.
The hotel is without doubt, a landmark in New York, and with that a price tag to fit. The rooms we stayed in were beaufitul, old furniture, old decor, but not tired. It was pristine, elegant and grand.
Due to a couple of issues, we were moved rooms and upgraded to a suite. This issue was something that shouldnt have happened, but the hotel offered their sympathies and quickly rectified the issue. The suite was fantastic, with a balcony and a view.
The concierge services at the hotel helped make the holiday. If you want a reservation at an exclusive restaurant, just ask Concierge, if you want tickets to a show, just ask. These things come with a cost, but if you can't afford the full package, then stay somewhere else.
Breakfast, dinner, and the bar were also fantastic.
In general, it would be hard to pick fault at this hotel and whilst we did have our problems, the hotel made sure to try and rectify it - for this reason, I don't need to tell you what the problems were.
Would book here again in a heartbeat.

title: fab hotel should be 5 * not 4
body: 2nd time stayed in waldorf . each time rooms great and staff can't do enough for you. Informed hotel or luggage being delayed and they upgraded our room to the towers , plus vouchers for cocktails. Also had allergic reaction to the feathered pillows, contacted reception & they changed them to hypoallergenic straight away.

title: What a dump of a hotel
body:
This hotel stay was terrible but the service was very good!!! I was traveling for work and it was a choice of this or Intercontinental; both hotels are terrible but they are both preferred hotels with my company.
The moment I walked off the elevator, it smelled like cigarette smoke.
Here is what was wrong with my room (953):
Blow dryer blew the lights in the bathroom
Bathroom shower didn't drain
No temp control - room temp was set at 72
TV remote didn't work (that's understandable)
The room overall was dingy, wallpaper peeling off, overall lots of wear and tear.
The bed was actually decent and the location was convenient given my office was 2 buildings away.
I have no plan of staying there ever again, I will wait last minute to make my travel reservations in hopes that the hotel will be booked.

title: Raggedty Rooms..... Needs Work
body: The rooms at the Waldorf are definitely showing their age.... It is down right dingy..... the finishings are old, fixtures in bathroom are rusted, cracked, stained, half patched..... the carpet is dingy.... pretty much a disaster..... Further, the bathroom was not cleaned properly as I found hairs all over that were not mine... YUCK, YUCK, YUCK!!!! The rooms are in definite need of an upgrade...... Wish they would make the same investment on the rooms that they made on the lobby and hallway areas.... Very disappointing for the amount they charge per night..... Also, the room service lady taking orders was a little rude... she needs to get an attitude check if she is going to be dealing with guests. I will not choose this hotel again until they make some upgrades. My money is better spend somewhere else.

title: Tired
body:
It goes without saying that the Waldorf Astoria is an iconic New York City hotel. This hotel has passed its prime and it is in serious need of refurbishment. I have stayed here with my husband, parents, children...Each time giving this hotel the benefit of the doubt ,wishing that the next time I visit, it will meet the expectations of such a landmark; only to be disappointed again and again. 
The beds both in the hotel and in the towers are incredibly uncomfortable, there is no temperature management in the rooms, the thing that bothers me the most though are the chambermaids. Almost every time we have stayed there the chambermaids have come right in! No knocking, no door bell ringing, nothing!
Sadly, I have had my last stay at the Waldorf.

title: Did Not Meet Expectation
body:
My wife and I stayed at Waldorf in NYC. We were excited to stay there as it is one of the most famous hotels in the wor One night was free on Hilton points and then we paid $800+ for the 2nd night. To start, we had to wait 15 minutes to get to a front desk clerk, then took another 15 minutes for them to determine our room would not be ready for another 15 minutes. It was 6:15pm. There room check in systems must have been from the '80. 
The room was very average and somewhat run down. I realize it's vintage, but 
Our room was never made. No clean (or folder) towels, no bed make. 
I had to wait in-line agian to get a new room key (2 reservations because of the points) Another 25 minutes this time. 
Avoid the hype, stay somewhere else.

title: disappointing
body: This should be one of the best hotels in NY, but unfortunately it was a bit disappointing. It took very long to check in and the service was not too good. Room was very nice, the bathroom however very outdated.

title: Second Review--I'm dropping the Waldorf's rating
body:
The Waldorf is the perfect place to stay when the Parade ends and the Holiday Season officially begins. For someone searching for a slice of American nostalgia nothing says Season’s Greetings more than the Rockettes annual Holiday Show, strolling down 5th Avenue, grabbing a bag of chestnuts just roasted by an open fire, or taking a carriage ride through Central Park.
The location of the Waldorf is perfect for all things holiday. Walking at a normal pace will get you to St. Patrick’s Cathedral in 2 minutes, Saks 5th Avenue in 3 minutes and Rockefeller Center in 4 minutes. 10 minutes and you will be at FAO Swartz, the Apple Cube or Central Park.
This is my second year at the Waldorf at Thanksgiving. Last year I stayed in a one-bedroom suite in the Waldorf Towers. The room was wonderful. It was exactly what I thought a NYC hotel suite should be. (Review posted 12-30-11)
This year I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria-Park Avenue. I was in Room 1627. This is a Luxury Corner Room with a balcony (yes a balcony) that overlooked the corner of Park and 50th Avenue. As a note, a balcony is a wonderful idea on paper but a ridiculous idea in NYC in last week of November. No matter how nice the weather is…you will freeze. A balcony is unprotected and any wind is relentless. Do not pay for this upgrade. It sounds romantic but it is, in fact, stupid.
There are two things that made this room a good value: 
The first is the bathroom. It doesn’t have a tub…which I think is a plus. I find it more pleasant to step in and out of a shower than a tub. I also find a shower floor less slick than a tub floor. And a stand-alone shower rarely has an awful germ-infested shower curtain that you fight with during your entire shower.
The bathroom is large but not too large. It can easily accommodate two people at the same time and has plenty of shelf space for your items. Our bathroom was on the building side not the hall side of the hotel. This gave us another window in the room.
The second thing which makes this room a good value is the walk-in closet. The walk-in closet is the size of most hotel bathrooms. Not only can you hang all your clothes, store your luggage and still use it as a dressing room…if you have a child under the age of 12 and want to be creative…
…store your luggage somewhere else and use the walk-in closet as an extra bedroom. The hotel will provide a cot. Tell the child they are “hotel camping.” (If the child complains--threaten to put them in the bathroom…the cot will fit in there, also.)
Now for the bad news about this room:
The balcony was sealed off so we couldn’t use it even if we wanted. Next, when we booked the room we booked it based on the following description:
"Spacious and richly appointed, our Luxury Rooms feature a living area with sofa and chair in a traditional decor..." "... provides 370-400 sq. ft. of space."
The actual bedroom (sans bathroom and dressing room) was smaller than most hotel bedrooms I’ve been in. It had one small chair, a tiny desk, an armoire (with the television on it), two very small end tables (with no drawers), and a desk chair. If there was a living area with a chair and sofa both were invisible. But, I’m glad we didn’t have this amenity. The room was so small that neither of us could walk in the same area at the same time. I fear more furniture would have put us outside on the balcony in the cold November air.
If I had to estimate the square feet of the bedroom, meaning the actual room where the bed is located in Room 1627, I would estimate it is probably less than 185 square feet. I think it would be interesting if the hotel took a measurement of the room and let me know how close I am.
I also need to address another issue about the hotel.
Last year I complained about our housekeeper. I said that I wasn’t going to let her poor performance stop me from giving the hotel a five-star rating. I didn’t think it was fair to punish the hotel for one employee’s action. Sometimes you get a bad employee. It happens.
But, doggone if it didn’t happen again.
I have discussed this with the manager and I hope the situation gets resolved. As is my policy, I did not allow the hotel to compensate me for “stress” or “hardship” or anything else. They offered and I declined. I tell you this so readers are clear that my intention is not to slam the hotel but to give an honest review.
The day of Thanksgiving we did not depart our room until 1:30 pm or 1:45 pm. As we left our room we walked by three housekeepers who were in foul moods. We thought they were in a foul mood because they had to work the day after Thanksgiving and could not attend the sales. (This would put me in a foul mood.) We knew they were annoyed because we could hear them talking and the tone of voice indicated obvious irritation.
Around 1:30 am, as we were getting ready for bed, my partner asked for the time. I looked at the hotel clock and noticed that the alarm had been set for 7:00 am.
We know that we didn’t set the alarm on the clock.
How do we know this? Because we checked the alarm Thanksgiving evening before we went to sleep. Why did we check the alarm that evening? Because we didn’t want to be woken up. Was the alarm set? No. Which is why we did not wake up until noon. And why we did not leave our room until 1:30 pm.
It would be easy to say that the housekeeper accidently hit our alarm and turned it on but that is unlikely.
How do I know this?
Because the alarm on Thanksgiving morning had been set for 9:00 am. I know this because I made a comment about it when I made sure the alarm was turned off that evening. This means someone took the time to set the alarm clock for 7:00 am. 
So who set the alarm clock?
To the best of my knowledge, the only people in our room were the housekeeping staff. Last year our housekeeper was unusually annoyed with the hours we kept. When we remembered how annoyed the housekeeping staff was when we left our room the mysteriously set alarm clock made sense.
I discussed this with the housekeeping manager and explained that he has a systemic problem with his staff. Although the hotel advertises 24-hour housekeeping it appears that the staff is not aware of this. Their level of stress when you do not vacate your room by a certain time is abnormal for a hotel that advertises 24-hour housekeeping service.
He explained that the staff will clean your room anytime you want IF you let them know. It appears what I have been doing wrong is not telling anyone that we are late risers and do not require housekeeping until after 2:00 pm. Had we known that we needed to call housekeeping we would have done this and spared the staff two years’ of stress.
So, if you are planning to stay at this hotel and you plan to get a late start please call housekeeping and let them know. They will be happy to accommodate your schedule.
The sophomoric stunt that housekeeping pulled on us was out of line but whatever is causing the staff that much stress needs to be resolved. An unhappy staff will always take it out on customers. Which is why I’m going to ding the Waldorf on housekeeping this time. When a customer has the same issue two times in two years with the same hotel it’s a management issue.

title: Very Disappointing
body:
My work collegues and I had saved for 18 months for this trip to New York, and decided to splash out on the accommodation. The Waldorf Astoria has a reputation as an iconic New York hotel, and we hoped it would be a luxurious experience. We didn't wait very long to check in, our rooms were not ready on arrival, but we had arrived before 3pm. Our party had 3 rooms. The rooms were quite pleasant and spacious, but nothing special and in need of some redecoration. The bathroom was very dated and it was difficult to tell quite how clean it was. We had various issues during our stay, none of which were resolved. Room 1, ran hot, the air con did not work. Room 2, the safe and air con did not work, the windows did not open. During our stay the hotel hairdryers blew the fuse and we were without electricity in any of the rooms for over an hour. We did notify the front desk about the problems we were experiencing. They did give $100 dollars credit to each of the rooms with faults, to use at Oscars for breakfast. We really enjoyed breakfast, which we had on our last day. We were squeezed into a corner of the restaurant, but the food was lovely and the choices plentiful.
The main problem that we experienced with this hotel is the unauthorised use of our credit cards after we had settled our bill and checked out. I was charged $154 3 days after I got home, for breakfast for 3 people. I had used the credit awarded by the hotel and settled the rest in cash. My collegue was charged over $700 for various items, all of which had been paid for when we checked out. We both contacted the hotel by email for several days and had no response. I then rang billing and was told I would be phoned back, which never happened. I emailed Hilton Group customer services and got no acknowledgement. In the end we both contacted our Banks to investigate and try to get the money back. Eventually, after 14 days, we both got an email from billing saying they had no idea what we were disputing. Another few furious emails ensued and I have now had my account credited at a worse exchange rate!! My collegue is still waiting. There was no apology from billing until I demanded one. The customer service at this hotel is atrocious.

title: Improved I think
body: Stayed a few years ago and was disappointed but I think the ongoing renovations have improved things. My room seemed fresher and more up to date. And the hallways seemed brighter (new lighting). But my overall feeling is that there are better values for your dollar. I was a little annoyed that there is no coffee in the lobby since the restaurant doesn't open until 7am. Couldn't they do a classy set-up, given the room rates, that kept me from having to dart around the corner to over-pay at Starbucks? I will say one real positive is the wireless router in my room. With the layout of this old building that's probably the only way to provide consistent wifi, so kudos for their including that.

title: Waldorf has turned it up a notch....
body:
I have stayed at the Waldorf numerous times over the years, but this year, I could feel a noticable difference in the property. Physically it was immaculate and felt like the premium, luxurious hotel it aspires to be... and the service, well the service has taken a dramatic turn upward. Every associate we encountered to some step to make their contact memorable. The doorman, the host at the restaurant, the maid we met in the hallway... The most notable though, was a front desk associate. We returned from an event to pick up the keys for our 3pm check in. It was almost 4. There was obviously an issue and my wife was noticably distressed as we had to get freshened up and back out for a tight schedule of events. The associate realized this quickly and immediately took control. She walked us up to the room and the issue, a previous guest had left some of thier belongings in the room, was settled as she physically removed the belongings. Without her intervention, we would have waited in the lobby until a supervisor could free up to handle the situation. Extraordinary effort that took a potentially visit changing situation and made it into a "wow" experience. Kudos! 
Room was great. Property has never been better. Waldorf is back and competing with all the big boys in New York luxury.

title: Memorable stay
body:
We have just returned from a fabulous 4 night stay at the Waldorf,We booked Capricorn limousine service through the hotel web site for transfers to and from the hotel to JFK,communication via emails with Elliott was first class always quick to respond once emails were sent.,excellent pick ups on both occasions and exceptional meet and greet and drivers.
We arrived at this iconic hotel first impressions on entering the lobby area do not disappoint, on check in are room was not quite ready so we decided to start are sightseeing early we were informed we would receive a text in half an hour once the room was ready which we promptly did,we had booked a luxury double/ double room as there were 3 of us and on returning to the hotel we had been given a complementary upgrade to a one bedroom suite room 10A which was a nice surprise.
The suite was huge and nicely furnished yes there are one or to knocks on furniture but thats from people who do not respect other peoples property,if you want to step back in time and like art deco then this is the place for you.
All staff members we came into contact with were all very curteous and friendly, would we return the answer is yes thankyou for making are stay in New York a memorable one.

title: Nice size rooms
body: The rooms are larger then a regular room in NYC. The hotel is beautiful though because of its age the plumbing isn't the best but acceptable considering its been around for awhile... The lobby is impressive and the size is amazing in NYC. Nice wide hallways & overall a nice hotel w/a beautiful spa.

title: Very impressed
body:
I have stayed, on different occasions, at the different best hotels in New York. I had never stayed, however, at the Waldorf Astoria. We went just after the hurricane Sandy hit NY. 
As we all know, this is a hotel built quite some years ago, but it has been kept up and looks perfect. The service was impeccable, and staff very attentive. Our room was very nice and comfortable. 
A mal-functioning heating was immediately replaced by an electric heater. And because of the "hardship" they gave me a hundred bucks on checking out. Now, that is caring for your customer!
The Waldorf Astoria has always some kind of promotion or another, so even though the list prices or name would scare some people away, look it up!

title: Great history, beautiful hotel, so-so room
body:
I stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria for one night on business. I was really looking forward to my stay, and have to say I was a bit disappointed. The hotel itself is full of history, icons and the lobby and public spaces are beautiful. 
The room was disappointing. It was average in size for NYC, but the finishes were old and worn down. The tub had a slow drain and there was obvious damage on the bottom of the tub. Paint on the ceiling of the bathroom was flaking and outlets and switches were old and ragged. The room was very clean, just in need of a face lift. 
Beds were comfortable. Room service was great. Staff was friendly.
Would I stay there again? Probably not. For the high price tag, you can find more modern hotels with better accommodations.

title: Very pricy, but absolutely stunning.
body: I stayed here four times in my life, and I always feel like a princess. My mum uses hotel points for this-- we could never actually afford it otherwise. Once, they bumped us up to an executive suite for free for a week, and they treated us like royalty. The rooms are elegant and beautiful and old fashioned, and the food is amazing. Afternoon tea is wonderful, and the room service, though pricey, is incredible. They will make anything you want. Anything. I asked for broccoli with cheese late one night and I was expecting just that-- but it was an actual sauce, so tasty, and not even on the menu. The concierge is helpful with booking Broadway plays, although I lived in New York for years and prefer getting deals on plays. If you want good seats the night of the show, though, and are prepared to pay, the concierge at this hotel will have them for you without question. If you can afford this place, I highly recommend it. I've never had a more enjoyable hotel experience in my life!

title: Great Nostalgia thru-out, room and service ok
body: The hotel thru-out is very impressive with a huge lobby and some very nice restaurants/bars, but left unimpressed with the overall service and room. Check-in took abnormally long, with gentleman continually have to leave desk to check with manager to unblock a room? When asked, "isn't there already a room?", oh yes sir. While there was about 10 bellman, many standing around waiting for the other to due something. The room was on Park Ave side and very noisy, felt like sleeping in a parking lot. The ceiling in bathroom, a softcloth drop ceiling, making one wonder what mold merks above it.

title: Waldorf Astoria, 29th nov-1st Dec 2012
body: Our first trip to NYC and like many others chose this place due to its name and reputation as a top hotel. Had a superior king room, on the surface clean, behind the bed filthy, bathroom not too clean. Had to wait up to twenty minutes for the water to heat up! when it did become lukewarm, the water ran a dirty mud like colour, it then took an hour and a half to drain the bath. We complained many times and told to have patience and leave the water running! I expect hot water as standard in any hotel never mind this one, we had to go out after a journey from Manchester without having a bath or shower! Plugged the phone in for the socket to fall out of the wall wires exposed and everything cold have been electrocuted! Looked at the curtains to notice the tie back hooks were hanging out by their wall plugs! Windows so stiff you needed superman to open them, unable to adjust the heat in room so i was cold. Room 1656 beware if you get the room ask for another, New York was fab, would never stay here again, the public areas might be beautiful but you want a lovely fully functioning room, no point in just a glossy exterior.

title: Top in NYC - Still!
body: This hotel has it all. Classy overall hotel decor and clean well decorated rooms. Great service and restaurants. It has tremendous history and ultra-modern technologies all at play... The rooms are larger than other standard rooms in the city and offer everything one could want. Service is great and very prompt. One of the top 5 hotels in New York City... still.

title: Iconic
body:
When booking this hotel you are booking for the history, location and the ambiance. The rooms look like they haven't been renovated in a long time but that is part of the charm, its like staying in your great aunts apartment! You may not chose to decorate your house this way but it's cool for a couple days.
The linens in the towers are very nice and the beds are quite comfortable. The TVs and Bose equipment is great. 
All of the employees were very polite and helpful. 
I really liked the separate entrance for the towers, it feels like you are staying in a much smaller hotel. The continental breakfast in the club room was a welcomed experience.
Everyone must stay in this hotel at least once.

title: Disappointing
body:
My mother and I stayed in the famous Waldorf-Astoria towards the end of November and were very disappointed with our stay in such an iconic hotel. 
We arrived late, on our first night and were told that the only Deluxe rooms left were smoking rooms; we had specified for non smoking when booking. To be fair to the Waldorf they did offer to try to move us in the morning, but we didn't feel this necessary at the time as the room was spacious with only a faint smell of smoke. We found the bathroom comfortable although the toilet seat was broken However, when we eventually climbed into bed severely jet lagged we discovered that the bed side - over bright - table lamp was broken and fixed in the permanent on position. We called down to reception around 10pm to ask some one to come up and help us. Over an hour and 3 phone calls later maintenance showed up to fix the switch broken lamp so we could finally go to sleep. 
On our second morning in the hotel disaster struck. My mother discovered an extremely large cockroach lying dead in the middle of our floor. Shocked we called down to reception and a lady from house keeping responded promptly followed by two security guards - which we found odd in it's own right. They packed the bug in some kind of tube and assured us that they would fumigate the room and move us to another room for the duration of our stay; we needed to only pack up our bags and by the time we returned in the evening they would be waiting in our new room. 
To our surprise when we returned in the evening we had been upgraded to a suite - which we found to be a nice gesture. 
It took the hotel well over an hour to locate our luggage and bring it to the new room, but we were happy to sleep free of cockroaches. 
The rest of our stay was rather un-eventful, and the majority of the staff were helpful and supportive of our issues. It seemed to be a lack of organisation - of no ones fault in particular - that lead to the majority of our problems. 
I would not stay at this hotel again...or recommend it to any one. I do, however, acknowledge that we had a bad experience and I would advise people to read around other reviews to get a more well rounded idea about what the Waldorf-Astoria is actually like.

title: One of a Kind
body: There are so many hotel choices in NYC and even in New Jersey your decision to stay here has to be based somewhat on what you are doing in the city and what kind of hotel style you like. The Waldorf is such an historical gem I find it fascinating to wander around the lobby and the hallways of the hotel looking at the pictures on the walls and memorabilia in the various showcases. People watching in the elegant lobby is also great fun and our room was clean and comfortable and so I have no complaints about our November 2012 four night stay. I also like the location as you are away from the noise and congestion of Times Square and Rockefeller Centre but close enough to walk to both. This was a second trip to NYC and we have stayed at the Waldorf both times. This time around we took the guided hotel tour which took us into some areas we hadn't previously seen and provided historical info about the hotel which was quite interesting. We might try a another venue if we go back again just for something different but certainly I would stay at the Waldorf again.

title: FAILS TO MATCH ITS REPUTATION
body:
Whilst we enjoyed our stay at the Waldorf , there were disappointments which we do not expect from an hotel of its reputation. Though the room was the smallest we have had in a five star hotel, it was very well appointed and comfortable. For breakfast or morning coffee the Oscar Room was excellent as was the Bull and Bear Restaurant for Dinner. Both had highly efficient, friendly staff and the food was excellent
However, the hotel is let down by the Peacock Alley - a bar/restaurant off the lobby. Whilst we enjoyed a lunch at the bar and a snack on our first evening, on other occasions the service was not up to the standard of the rest of the hotel. On one evening we were shown to a table located by a wall on the outer area of the room. There was no light on the table or near it - it was not possible to read the menu, never mind see what you were eating. We asked to move, explaining the reason and were relocated to our satisfaction. However, the greeter continued to try to use the table, showing two further sets of clients to it who again asked to be moved. She made no attempt to rectify the situation or to bother about the experience of the clients.
Additionally, as the hotel clearly obtains a high proportion of its income from corpòrate events, as mere residents it was regularly impossible to find a place in any of the bars once the corporates had decanted en masse for their breaks - at just the time when residents were wanting a pre-dinner drink. Additionally, there was a detailed dress code, outlined in the room information pack, relating to the various public areas. We welcomed this and responded positively to it. The Peacock Alley required "elegant" dress - yet there was no attempt by staff to keep to this when the cor`porates arrived or when people came in from outside the hotel. The code therefore became an empty piece of posturing, leaving us feeling overdressed on occasion.
It was a pity this area did not live up to the rest of the hotel - the check-in, concierge and housekeeping staff were all friendly, helpful and efficient. However, we would not stay there again nor would we recommend it to friends - unless they were attending a corporate event of course!

title: Iconic & not to be missed
body: We stayed three days over a weekend as a family in a Junior Suite on a visit from England and enjoyed every minute of it. The rooms though expensive were not stupidly so given the location and history. We'll be back!

title: Fading Beauty
body:
This was our third, nonconsecutive Thanksgiving at the Wladorf Astoria (2001, 2010 and 2012). Always pre-pay since I have found the Hotel extends a small discount. I booked a suite plus two additional rooms.
Suite 860 has not been updated since our stay in 2001. The first room I occuppied 890, I was greeted with a broken bathroom door (As if someone punched the door. The door was cracked with two small holes and two different color paints on the door) The wall oin the bathroom, over the door was covered in black mold 6 inches by 1 foot. If the door was in good repair I may not have noticed the mold issue. The Housekeeping supervisor was summoned to my room and had no explination but offered to clean the bathroom. I was changed to room 867.
Peacock alley: We had Thanksgiving reservations for the 3pm seating. We were finially seated at 3:30pm (not too bad). The table had no silverware, napkins nor glassware. The hostess stated she just wanted to seat us and someone will be over shortly to complete the setup of the table. Oh no Turkey. The buffet kept running out of Turkey (I am not a fan of Turkey but come on, its Thanksgiving)
Oscars:
When I made the room reservations, my the written e-mail confirmed a $50 breakfast credit at Oscars included with the suite reservation. I reveiwed my parents incidental charges prior to checkout on Friday (they stayed in the Suite) and NO credit not was applied. The front desk agent stated,"that was NOT part of your room rate". I asked to speak with the front desk manager, he checked my reservation on line and stated the same. I stated,"this is an easy fix, we can solve this now or I can dispute the charges with my credit card company" I was credited and later that day when I reviewed my reservation on line, it clearly stated on the second page of the confirmation, a $50 credit will be applied to breakfast at Oscars"
No evening houskeeping service. During previous stays, houskeeping would freshed up the rooms, replace towels etc while we were out. The houskeeper for the 8th floor could be seen sitting in her office in the main hall of the 8th floor yet she never seemed to make it to ours rooms. Both in 2001 and 2010 the rooms were straightened while we were out.
Upon checkout I called the 1-800 number to complain. Saturday evening at 6:55 pm I recieved a call, on my cell phone, from a manager. I was at the country club with friends and family just sitting down to drinks in the lounge (Yes, some of us still do that) and asked him to call back on Monday or Tuesday. No call was ever recieved.
12/9/12 I was in NYC for the weekend and decided to give the Walforf a second chance (Fool that I can be) and had breakfast at Oscars. I was seated at a table with dirty linen. Specifically a dirty napkin. I asked the hostess for a replacement, she said,"Maybe if you arrived earlier this would not be a problem (it was 9:30 am) and then she took a napkin from a dirty table that was just vacated and handed it to me.... Classy.
Steady yourself, This is the worst part.
My parents recieved at letter from Ana Tijan, Director of Rooms, Waldorf Astroia, outlining my complaints and offering them a free upgrade on their next stay. I was protecting my elderly parents from the multitude of issues at the Hotel and much to my embarrassment, Ms Ana Tijan was nice to outline all the issues in the letter. I spoke with Ms Tijan on 12/14/12 to tell her how embarressed I was with the letter and her response was,"I sign a lot of letters that other people write"
I was transferred to the GM, Mr Eric Long, spoke with his assistant, and I am waiting for a response.
I suggest a visit to the lobby, it is fine exapmle of art deco. Yet, there are many other fine Hotels in NYC to stay.

title: Wonderful hotel
body:
Travelled on the 9th December 2012. 3rd trip to New York and 2nd time to the Waldorf.
Had a little hick up upon check in but finally got our junior suite we had booked (very busy).
2 full bathrooms, bedroom separated by a proper door and sofa bed in a massive living area.
Some may say the decor is shabby but you have to remember this hotel is never empty and considering the age of the hotel I was presently surprised how elegent, clean and comfortable the room was. A few marks here and there on the walls I would accept.
We have previously stayed here in a superior guest room and found this also a stunning elegant room.
The only slight down side is the lighting, 3 lamps only I feel is insufficient for the size of the room.
Perfect position, fantastic views - just stunning.
I will definitely be back.

title: Wonderful
body: Got a great offer to that hotel and didn´t think to long about taking that chance! When I got there I even got a complimentary upgrade to the Waldorf Towers and really loved it. Spacious room, wonderful lobby, great central location. Always again, but i doubt to get a similar offer!

title: Classic Grand Hotel on Park Avenue!
body: Love this very classy "Grand" Hotel. Stayed 4nights in an upgraded room which was very spacious room. Very attentive staff. Breakfast buffet expensive, but then this is NY where everything is pricey. Central location within easy walking distance to many sites, Rockefeller Center, 5th Avenue, Times Square, etc. Will return.

title: It's name sells it
body:
On arrival, the Waldorf looks impressive, despite the building works going on around the hotel. The lobby is grand and impressive and there are staff in abundance waiting to help you with cases; checking in; tours etc. When we checked in we were told we were receiving a complimentary room upgrade from a double deluxe which we were obviously delighted with and were impressed with the service we received from Doug, who checked us in. 
However, I'm starting to wonder if this was just a line because when we arrived at our room, on the fifteenth floor (Room 1572), the room was tiny - especially because there were four of us sharing. There were two double beds; a small sized bathroom and one wardrobe between us which, if this was a room upgrade, I wonder how small the original room was?!?! I have to say, I found the room to be the biggest disappointment of the holiday. Although it was clean and tidy, it failed to possess any of the promising grandeur of downstairs and as this was an expensive holiday, I had hoped for more.
The mini-bar was electronic, so if you even touched anything, it would register that something had been removed and we were charged $17 for 2 bottles of water that we didn't use!! When we called downstairs, to tell them we hadn't had anything, they were helpful in cancelling this charge but it did help us to see how expensive the hotel really was.
The location is close to Bloomingdales and Central Park - both within easy walking distance but for the likes of Times Square it was easier to hop into a cab. Luckily these were usually outside the hotel on a regular basis, so they were easy enough to get.
Though I loved New York and would definitely return, I would stay in another hotel because I felt the Waldorf was relying too much on it's name to sell it and once they had your money and custom, they didn't seem too fussed in helping you further.

title: Bday wknd with the Waldorf
body:
The Waldorf is an amazing, magical place. Filled with history, charm, incredible architectural detail, and the BEST people who make you feel like you are so special. The hotel knew ahead of time that I was coming up for my bday and they made sure to acknowledge it by sending up a special treat *(bottle of champagne) and a note. Thank you to Meg Towner of the Waldorf!!!!
Steve Goldenberg, security at the hotel, saw me wandering around the hotel, taking photographs and stopped me to give me a booklet filled with history of this legendary hotel and collectible pen. He let me in on some very interesting facts and history of the hotel as well. Him taking time out of his day to share information about this legendary hotel helped to make my trip even more memorable. 
It is moments like this, those personal connections between guests and hotel staff, which make you feel like a hotel is not only a hotel but a second home. It is those connections that make you want to return again and again and tell everyone what an amazing experience the Waldorf=Astoria provides. 
Carlos Solis, the Bell Captain was friendly, very helpful, and always with a smile. I noticed a woman who was very rude to him. I stood nearby watching in disbelief. However, Carlos took her awful attitude in stride. Always with a smile, remained polite and professional. Mr. Solis went out of his way to help anyone who needed attention, I know because I was one of those people. He welcomed any issue a guest had, whether you were running up to him with a smile or an attitude. Mr. Solis shined.
Everyone at the Waldorf really makes you feel so welcomed and so special. There is nothing that can replace history, attention to detail, and GOOD PEOPLE!!!!!
When I stay in NY, I will always return to the Waldorf.

title: Sophisticated lady
body: Contrary to other reviewers, we found this a really great hotel, full of history & Art Deco/nouveau class. Staff are efficient, helpful & not over-efficious, just good at their jobs & friendly. Try for a "superior" room overlooking Park Ave or Lexington Ave it's worth the extra for the comfort & quiet.

title: "The Grand Old Lady"
body: We were upgraded to a superior double on the 20th floor. It was very quiet with no street or noise. However, during the day, the maid service could be heard talking loudly inthe hallway. The room and bathroom was quite small compared to today's standard of luxury hotels. It was nicely decorated and furnished in a by gone era mode. The hallways featured interestng photos of guests from JFK, Nixon to Frank Sinatra. If you can place yourself back in time, you can enjoy your stay here, otherwise it would be better to stay at a newer hotel with current expected space and ammenities.

title: A grand old place
body:
The lobby is superb & the staff are very helpful without being intrusive, but the rooms need a refurb
We had a one bed suite which was large very clean & comfortable but no view & very noisy. 
The cost of a can of coke from the mini bar was £5.00 approx ridiculous price. To drink a bottle of beer at the bar was£9.00 no one can justify these cost. We ate in the Bull & Bear restaurant & would not recommend this as it was nothing special & cost £200 for2 with only 1 glass of wine, had better meals for a third of the cost in NY. The staff make this hotel as everyone is so pleased to help. Get up grading your rooms & I would return.

title: Excellent Diamond Reception area
body: I just wanted to share that Mary in the Diamond Reception was amazing. It really made me feel that it was worth giving my business to Hilton all year. I came to NY for a girl's weekend with my best friend and her sister, just an overnight, but she made me feel that i was staying the week. I would stay here again!

title: Yotel NYC: Young, cool, good location
body: My spouse and I spent three nights around New Year's Eve. The hotel is cool and contemporary, like staying on the star ship Enterprise. The room design is EXCELLENT - perfect for a long weekend in New York. The staff of the recently-opened hotel wasn't ready for a massive twenty-something crowd, which overwhelmed the hotel guests who were just trying to get around the building after midnight. There were LOTS of European families. Also the Clinton/Hell's Kitchen location is a short walk from Times Square and across the street from a 24-hour CVS, a grocery store, a Subway, and close to fun bars and restaurants such as Chez Josephine. We will DEFINITELY hope to stay there again, soon.

title: Location:Great Hotel:Mediocre
body: Stayed here a few days around NYE. Woke up to an insanely obnoxious noise going off and some guy (declaring he was either the commander or from mission control- which was even more annoying, as I sat there wondering if he was some 16yr old that found the intercom button or was really a manager that could vouch that it was not an emergency and something was being done to stop the heinous sound) on the intercom saying to ignore all alarms...Hmm..what if there actually was an emergency- I would probably be six feet under instead of warning people about this hotel. Everything just seemed for the lack of a better word, cheap...like you're living in some off brand Ipod. It comes fully equipped with what felt like the most inexpensive ikea mattress they could get, and the head of the bed has to be raised in order for you to actually walk in the room. And lets pray the guy you're with doesn't really have to go to the bathroom because there's no door and no vent for the bathroom...yikes. While the design of the hotel is "modern", it just feels like you're living out a Jetsons episode and leaves something to be desired. Albeit the location is near the subway and times square, which is really all we needed and the primary reason this review got any stars. Advice: overlook the tempting price per night of the Yotel and get a hotel with real character and management experience.

title: MORE LIKE A YOUTH HOSTEL THAN A HOTEL
body:
Where do I start...........this place is a joke
Booked this supposedly hotel for me and my partner due to the reviews, what a BIG mistake. As soon as we got there we looked at each other and regretted it, we are in our 30's so we are not old, stuck up or prudish. We walked in and was greeted by very loud music and loads of young adults (18-21) everywhere. Anyway regretably we checked in and within 30 mins checked back out. Our room was tiny with no privacy in the bathroom not even a door, just a curtain. The bed is sat up so when you have laid it out you are crawling over each other to get round the room. The walls are paper thin that we could hear people in the next room and EVERYTHING they were doing (if you catch my drift). 
When we checked out was told by a the reception staff that I would receive a refund due to it not living up to the reviews and we left and checked in to alot nicer place. It wasn't until driving away that you notice it is in a very dingy part of town where i would not feel comfortable walking out in the dark, alot of shops are boarded up people hanging on the corners of streets and would take approx 20 mins or more to get to time square at least. The hotel have refused to refund me so am now taking it further due to the reviews of it being a stylish hotel near times square that is a complete and utter joke!!!!!! I would not recommend this to families or anyone that would want to enjoy there stay but only suitable for a very tight budget, between the ages of 17-21 and you are really not fussy at all as we would of rather stayed in a tent as there would of been more space... we are just glad that we were able to find somewhere much more suitable and right near macys for the same kind of price that this hostel had charged us

title: Unique Experience in the Heart of It All
body: Uniquely situated close to theaters, shopping and Times Square. Although, the rooms(cabins) are listed as small, the cabin provides a relaxing and spacious atmosphere with its design to conveniently store guests' personal belongings. Also, the moving bed allows flexibility when resting or deciding to spend a day in to cuddle. The hotel is clean and the staff are helpful and courteous. Being able to grab my in-cabin breakfast tray to get an a la carte breakfast or the 24 hour complimentary hot beverages are great! Plus the points earned with the Stash rewards program is a bonus.

title: Right hotel, right place, wrong staff and management
body: I stayed there two nights for new years eve, payed 5 star fee , got two star service, door men and luggage delivery guy apparently was smoking good stuff......I gave my room number to him TWICE..after 45 minutes waiting; no delivery...... I had to walk downstairs (since check in at 4th floor wont help), found my bag and delivered it up stairs by myself since I couldn't trust them.......when I complained; they were trying to buy me a beer.... I think that's the only courtesy service you get when they drop the ball.....fire alarm went off twice at 2 am new years eve due to an stupid issue...guests were freaking out ....elevators were almost shot down... they kept their party keep going.....thanks god it was not a real fire otherwise we all would be fried.....bottom line if you are looking for a professional upscale place to stay this is not your place....but if you're trying to celebrate your 21st birthday; pass out drunk loud and don't care about others and have lots of money...go ahead you might like it....I WOULD NEVER GO BACK AND WONT EVER RECOMMEND IT EITHER TO MY ENEMY....

title: A unique experience
body:
The only thing I would have changed about this place is the fact that it had no real bathroom doors. Their is no real privacy when in the bathroom showering, changing, or on the pot..
The lighting was not the greatest in the bathroom. The bed was very comfortable. The gym was really quite nice. A good variety of cardio equipment but only 1 of each time (with the exception of the 2 treadmills). The equipment was new working condition. The gym was truly one of the best I've been to at a hotel. I would just recommend that they have some sort of disinfect available to wipe down the equipment after using. Good location if you are going to see a broadway show. Lots of restaurants within walking distance.

title: Excellent quality/price ratio
body: Loved the experience and will certainly repeat the next time we travel to New York! The "hip" concept and atmosphere, combined with the very reasonable rate for the quality of the hotel and location, make Yotel an outstanding choice.

title: YOTEL
body: came to party, they facilitated. this is the only place i will stay in NYC from now one. Seriously $170 per night in midtown, that is amazing. i was with a buddy we had a blast. hell yeah Yotel.

title: Great Location, high price, small room, poor breakfast
body:
Location is really good, 5 minutes by walk from Times Square
Price too high for a very small room and a ridicolous breakfast

title: Great Hotel
body:
This was our first time in NYC and this hotel's location was brilliant. 5 mins walk to the subway or bus station and times square The room was small but had everything we needed. The hotel was funky and had a good vibe. The first morning we got down to breakfast at 10am and there was nothing left, when asking a member of staff she said it was too late and they cannot offer us anything untill brunch at 11am. This was annoying but after the second morning we realised we hadnt missed much as it was only a small choice of muffins.
The Staff were young, friendly and helpful.
If you would like a nice meal try Bianca's in Soho, great value and excellent food!! And if you would like the best burger in the world u must go to Shake Shack, theres one just round the corner but expect queues!!
We would definatley choose this hotel again!!!

title: Yo! Stay at Yo! :O)
body: I Spent A Night At Yotel On 1/5/12 With My Boyfriend And We Were Extreemly Satisfied! The Guy Who Helped Me Check In To My Room Was Super Nice & Knowledgable About The Hotel. The Fourth Floor Is Very Nice! The Room Was Pretty Tiny But TIDY! Everything You Might Possibly Need Is In The Room And It Is Well Organized. I Love The Fact That The Bed Moves Because I Get Better Sleep With Elevation As Oppose To Laying Flat (Don't Ask Why, I Just Do). The Bed Was Super Comfortable! I Found NO And I Mean NO Stains On My Sheets Or Towels So Major Plus To The Room Attendant For Their Attention To Detail. I Will Definately Recommend Yotel To Anyone Who Appreciates A CLEAN Hotel! :)

title: Amazing Yotel!! Must stay if visiting NYC
body: When I arrived at the hotel the staff were very friendly and helpful got us checked in straight away. Our room was so relaxing and had a great view, the shower was out of this world!!! Definitely staying here again on my next trip!!! oh and the food was amazing!

title: The "real deal" in NYC
body:
I had stayed in Yotel's "cabins" in the past, so for this business trip I decided to try their "real" hotel in New York's West 40s. The hotel has a groovy vibe, which is very New York and rather fun. Check in was problematic, and the automated kiosk could not find my reservation, but I checked in with staff and all went well. My corner room was on a low floor (11th), but was spacious with a large bed, and was comfortable. Media players in the form of a TV and clock radio with iPod connection was up to date and worked beautifully. Heating worked well.
The bathroom was large, but was odd: There was a large transparent sliding glass panel as a door. This means that when one guest gets up early (in the dark) to shower, he cannot help but wake up the other guest because the door lets out large amounts of light and noise. In addition, the room appeared to have been fit out for handicapped folks, with railings in the bathroom. The shower was simply a slice of the bathroom with a curtain over it...no provision for keeping water in the shower area so every time I showered it flooded the bathroom. Really odd.
Yotel needs to put more storage space in the bathroom for toiletries etc. And there is plenty of room in the bedroom for more storage space, which was inadequate for two people.
I ate in the Dohyo restaurant and was very pleased. The bar is incredibly overpriced, however ($14.00 for a vodka/tonic? Give me a break!). Apparently the restaurants are outsourced.
All in all, however, considering the price and the location (excellent for Times Square and the theatre district), this hotel is a winner, and I will very likely return.

title: a human hotel
body:
Being in NY for 4 days and staying at Yotel was a great experience. Small is so beautiful. Cabin space is designed in a way you feel in a big environment. White makes sunlight crispy and gives a happy feeling. Windows that open in a hotel! Yes! I felt like at home, not in a hotel.
Great place! Staff is also very casual and helpful.

title: Cabin space for one, maximum 2
body: Well thought out space planning. It was like being in a ships cabin. Not intended for extended stays or for those traveling with lots of baggage/clothing. Clean and neat but privacy is creatively arranged between the toilet/shower area and the bedroom. Actually, they are all one room with sliding glass panels and curtains for division (so if you are 2 people, you had better like each other a lot!). Hated the "rain head" shower head. There was no way to direct the water. "Complimentary breakfast" was tea or coffee with muffins. No butter, no juice and no DISH! Also sitting in the center section, reserved for those not eating an al a carte breakfast, required being Yoga-like flexible as the tables are at slightly higher than floor height and you need to step into your seat from above. Overall it was such a good deal (I got it through groupon) that yes, I would go back again. It is 3 cross-town blocks from Times Square.

title: Excellent Getaway Spot
body: This hotel was not only impeccably clean, but the staff was so helpful and courteous! I would 100% stay here again on my next trip to New York. The room was cozy and clean and the location was in a very accessible part of Times Square. Excellent!

title: so futuristic!
body: as soon as we arrived the staff were on hand to show us how to book in - we were taken to our rooms - on the 23rd floor - fab views - we were shown the galley where you can get coffees and chilled water 24hours a day. The staff in the hotel were always friendly and helpfull and the hotel was spotless. The bath products are wonderful and can be purchased at the hotel, which I did!! We never heard a sound during the evening from any passing guests. The hotel is really funky and it all seemed to work like clockwork. I would definitely go back to this hotel and recommend it. The hotel is perfectly located for Times Square.

title: Imagine a room inside a huge white Ipod...
body:
Loved this hotel. Initial reaction is that it isnt very big. It is very tall though, has over 20 floors. Checking in is a doddle. Simply put your details into a simple touch screen panel and it creates your key. They do have reception staff on hand for local advice, but you have no need to speak to them besides. Entire hotel is spotlessly clean. 4th floor has a couple of bars and a restaurant with an outdoor terrace. all these areas were very quiet in january. most US hotels are room only but u get coffee and a muffin here. If u want a cooked breaky its extra cost. Drinks pricey, a pint and disaronno with coke came to $21. Bar area lacks atmosphere though.
Rooms are said to be small but are perfectly adequate for a couple. Room under beds for cases. Clothes hanging area with drawers and shelf. Bed can be made into a sofa at the push of a button. Flat screen tv with shelves and aux lead for ipod. table & chair. Bathroom has a window with large sink area and large shower. Complimentary shower gel shampoo. Hairdryer ironing board, iron & safety deposit box. Choice of tv channels can be boring. Fresh towels daily & bed made. Every floor has a room with free coffee and water, also a microwave there too. (microwave meals sold locally). Lunch in restaurant was expensive but of a high standard, tasty. Japanese style. Waiter gave me a coke with no alcohol in (didnt inform me until i asked, that there was no disaronno left even though we could see a full bottle behind the bar!) The waitress was very slow bringing dessert n the portion was tiny with no spoons until we had eaten it with our fingers. they received no tip at all! staff came across a bit thick/slow at times. Location seconds from times square. subway is reliable to see all the new york sights. Got a local shuttle bus to and from newark airport for $15 each, each way. much cheaper than taxis. Would stay again just for the lovely rooms.

title: SUCH a good time! If you don't go your a .............
body:
This is such a good concept! Simple, clean, trendy, fair pricing and great service! Yes your not getting a massive room full of old furniture so if thats what you want from a hotel, your going to hate it!! However, for everyone else its just the mutts nutts!! Hint: if you can, pay for the upgrade to the corner rooms..... OMG the views and being able to lie in bed and open the blinds (their electronic!!!) to look out over Manhatten at night! WOW!!
We stayed for a week and had the best time... and will be going back. NEW YORK.... whatta town!!!

title: supa fawnky!
body: It's like walking into a space ship! The lobby is mission control, your room is called and looks like a cabin, there is a little area with free coffee, water and vending called the Galley. The night we walked in at midnight, there was awesome music playing in mission control. Then when we got to our room (With complimentary upgrade btw) it was very sleek and not a sound could be heard from downstairs. Awesome place to spend a weekend getaway in the City of all Cities.

title: Perfect value for money
body:
It was the best surprise of my trip to New York. 
Small but well appointed room; super fast wifi; trendy look and hotel filled with young peoples.
Free breakfast! I just couldn't believe how good this hotel was. This place is perfect, I was in New York for 3 days and if I need to go back; I won't hesitate. Go go go

title: Loved Yotel!
body: The Yotel is a great place to stay, it's new, hip, chic, modern, and very comfortable and well thought out. Loved the reclining queen bed!

title: Great for short trip, affordable, ideal location
body: We stayed only 2 days/1 night in NYC and enjoyed the Yotel. The best part was that we arrived by train very early in the morning and took a $6 taxi ride to the hotel and were able to check in immediately. No worrying about storing our bags, etc., and waiting until the afternoon. The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating and the efficiency of the Yotel was amazing. The "cabin" was very small, but comfortable and my husband and I slept very well in the bed, which was neither too soft nor too firm. We didn't like the bathroom (knew this from other reviews) because of lack of privacy and no exhaust fan. I would not recommend this hotel if you are staying longer than a few nights. The room is VERY small, and if we had more than an overnight bag, we would've use the Yobot to store our bags because there really isn't room to move around in there. Luckily, we were on the go a lot and only used the room for sleeping and cleaning up. Being right off of Times Square was a fabulous treat and there were plenty of places within walking distance to eat/drink, etc. I would stay there again if going to NYC for a short period of time.

title: Chic, central, and clean!
body: Courtesy of an awesome Groupon deal, I recently stayed for four nights in a premium queen room. Room was on the 25th floor - amazing views, minimal noise. The hotel personnel were wonderful. Dan helped me with my bags, showed me the ropes, and recommended places to eat/visit. The lovely folks at the desk on the 4th floor knew my name and greeted me daily. The general hotel ambiance was great! The room was immaculate, well thought out, and all I needed. The hotel had easy access to the theater district, and is surrounded by great dining and plenty of public transportation. I've already recommended Yotel to friends, and hope to stay there again soon.

title: What a fun hotel
body: I loved staying here. The room rate was great, but more important the room was great as were the overall amenities. It's a totally different take on what you would expect in a hotel. The rooms are very well appointed with fun features and a great use of space. Check it out! I loved having the Galley to get my fix for tea or hot chocolate whenever I wanted it!.

title: excellent hotel
body: great design, great location! very comfortable bed and well appointed rooms

title: Space age but personable
body:
My husband and I and another couple spent the recent holiday weekend at the Yotel, using a Groupon deal that made this both an enjoyable and economical stay. The hotel is a superbly designed concept (using the theme of aircraft/cabins) that creates a truly efficient and comfortable use of space. While highly automated (self check in, self-baggage storage ROBOT!!) there was *always* a highly solicitous human to help out with check in, check out, hailing cabs, etc. 
Each room is truly small: bed, desk, shower bath/toilet, smallish spaces for hanging clothes, under-bed suitcase stowage. However, every surface is cleverly and thoughtfully designed to serve and remove any claustrophobic feel. The bath amenities include a hair dryer and two kinds of liquid soap. You will need your own extras. I found the futon-style bed a little firm, my husband did not. The place is gleamingly clean and sparkling white -- which helps with the small spaces. Every floor has a free LAVAZZA coffee galley (with teas and cocoa, too) that was a godsend during our cold-weather stay.
 The free breakfast was decent coffee and passable muffins: what is better are the ultra-mod green lounging pods next to the huge windows on the city. If it had been warmer, there is an outside patio that looks inviting. There are plenty of nearby delis/diners, and a CVS across the street.
The clientele runs to people who are much younger and cooler than my group, but we nonetheless felt quite happy here.

title: Amazing Experience
body: Having purchased a Groupon for a weekend at the Yotel, my wife, two friends of ours, and I stayed there for a three day weekend in January. From the moment we walked into the place, it was clear that this hotel is well thought out and seamlessly executed. From the cool, ultra-modern look, to the subtle details, to the attentive and helpful and not-in-your-face staff, Yotel gets it right! Comfortable bed. Attractive room. Free coffee/espresso/cappuccino/latte on each floor. Free FUNCTIONAL WiFi. Free gym. And of course, the ultra-cool robotic storage unit in the street-level lobby. My only request of the manager was that they not change anything. We really were that blown away and will DEFINITELY go back.

title: Excellent ALL the way around!
body: Best hotel experience ever! Staff is A++ and treats you the same as they would their CEO. From the second your feet hit the sidewalk of their establishment, they walk you through everything. They literally greet you at curbside and get you settled in quickly. Very pleased with the cleanliness and the cabin crew. The room is perfect in room size. Only complaint (and it's not really a complaint) was the bed... a little hard for my taste but you don't lose any sleep over it. The "towel warmer" is a sweet touch. Plenty off storage space for your luggage even if you choose not to utilize the Yobot. Which brings me to another awesome benefit of this hotel... They will hold your luggage after you've checked out until you are ready to leave for the airport. The staff aides you in getting transportation to the airport and at a good rate AND in class! I will recommend the Yotel to anyone! It truly doesn't get better than this! Thank you to the staff for giving us a wonderful stay!

title: amazing
body:
omg what a hotel, the staff,the rooms, the breakfast muffins. it was all fantastic. 
it was all so clean and tidy, i cant wait to go back again , i would recommend to anyone goin to NYC, only a short walk to Times Square an even closer to Hells Kitchen for food and drink, 
the beer in the bar was rather expensive $8 a pint, so we went to Rudys Bar N Grill on 9th avenue, 5 mins away, for $2.50 a pint or a pitcher for 7.50,
the rooms are made up everyday

title: I love the Yotel!
body: The Restaurant was great, they had the best fried rice I've ever had. The Hamachi was great too. The cabins were so nice, comfortable and clean with just the right amount of space. Such nice touches throughout, I was very impressed. I will definitely stay there the next time I'm in New York for a show at the Javits. You can walk to the convention center!

title: Luxurious Experience
body: I found out about this hotel by using bing. As soon as I saw it I knew I had to go there. I live in NJ , which is not too far to travel and decided to go the the NY location. From the moment I got there it felt simply surreal, like I was dreaming or something. There was so much to explore and the food was to die for and very affordable..I highly recommend this hotel. I had stayed in the Waldorf Astoria last year and didn't enjoy the experience half as much as I enjoyed the Yotel.
