The staff there are very helpful and so you can be as autonomous as you like, starting with the touch screen check -in, or receive as much help as you need. The entire hotel, especially the rooms have the feel of being on a cruise; and i love the fact that the bed slides out for when it's time to sleep... . I recommend that you go to this hotel at least once just for the heck of it. it's an experience you will not regret.!

title: A lovely stay at the Yotel.
body: We have just returned from a weeks stay at the yotel, and we are really pleased. Prior to arrival we requested a room with a view which we were given. The check-in staff were very helpful, and when we finally arrived to the room we were even more pleased. The room had a unique feel, and was very clean. The shared "kitchen" with free tea, coffee etc was very handy and the happy hour at the bar was very good value for NY. Very good location to times square, and very good value for money overall. Would stay here again next time were in NY.

title: Groupon Confusion
body: I booked this hotel two months in advance via a Groupon offer. At present, two weeks after my stay, I am still trying to sort out how I got double billed. By Groupon and By the Yotel

title: great idea, terrible experience
body:
1. VERY rude crew
2. not that clean
3. HORRIBLE bed

title: Unique and Good Experience
body:
This was our first overnight stay in NYC and we loved it! (We live so close to the city, the only reason we stayed was because we got the room for half price through Groupon). The hotel is a short walk from Times Square. You can even walk to it from Penn Station. Most of the hotel is decorated in white with lights which gives it a futuristic and very pristine look and feel. My niece and I stayed in a premium queen-sized cabin. The room was very small but liveable. The bed was somewhat hard (like a futon mattress). The size of the bed was OK for us but might be a little tight for two adults. In the bathroom, the toilet and shower were enclosed behind sliding glass doors. The shower is not fully enclosed (the water doesn't go all over the floor though) and the heated towel rack is a nice touch. We ate dinner and breakfast in the Dohyo restaurant. The dinner plates looked and tasted beautiful. If you're into fish, I suggest the spicy tuna roll, the grilled salmon and the halibut sliders. We ate at the communal tables where we sat on the floor. The ambiance of the restaurant at night was very chic (There was also a club that looked very interesting but being that I was with a teenager, I did not go in). All of the staff we interacted with were very nice and helpful. I would definitely stay here again.
Pros: The room rates are good value for the money with or without any discounts, the hotel is within walking distance from the train station and Times Square, the restaurant is really nice.
Cons: The premium cabins are small. If you are not traveling solo, I would suggest getting a first cabin room that has a bigger bed and a little more space. The Dohyo restaurant was more of a grown-up restaurant. I would not recommend it for people with babies or toddlers.

title: Great price for a great Yotel !!
body: Hotel in a great area !! The price was great and the room was perfect.

title: Funky fun in Midtown
body: A group of 4 couples took advantage of January discounting to enjoy a weekend at the Yotel. The hotel is fun and funky with very modern touches. The room is tight but perfectly fine for a couple. Very clean. Bed is a firm futon; several in our group did not like the firmness. Lots of communal space on the 4th floor for dining and partying. Perfect location for NJ visitors - you can almost throw a stone at the Lincoln Tunnel entrance.

title: I love this hotel!
body: This hotel was conveniently located by CVS and Times Square. It was clean, modern, and efficient. Great for a girls trip or a romatic weekend. I will use this hotel again.

title: May the Force be with you.
body:
My friends and I got a great rate for Yotel, and it was perfect for what we were looking for. It's no frills (no fridge, small room, sans shower cap, room service etc.) but VERY CLEAN. 
The only problem we had was Robot Dude holding our bags. We checked out, then checked out bags in w/ Robot. When it came time to claim our bags again, I punched in our *bin* code, got distracted and missed our luggage being delivered. This held up our leaving the hotel for about 45 min. due to now, we can't re-enter the code because the *bin* is EMPTY as far as Robot was concerned bc he believes we already removed our luggage. We had to wait for the mechanic to get off lunch, and even then it took them a few tries to claim our luggage. The holding-luggage concept is cool, but mind your friend calling you from the front of the hotel because Robot Man waits for no one.

title: Good hotel, attitude could be improved
body:
As others have said, Times Square it is not! However, it's only a couple of blocks out and it seems lots of other places do the same. Easy self-check in at the computers in the lobby. The room was clean, small, but perfectly OK for what we wanted. The moving bed was really good for making more room during the day. Sheets are a bit too small and untuck themselves completely everynight. Covers are two sheets with a duvet in between - a duvet cover would have been better but it was fine.
The bathroom set up is a little odd but I can't see how it would cause anybody problems. There is a sliding glass door across the front of the toilet/shower bit. This, coupled with the floor to ceiling curtains means you have complete privacy in the bathroom, unless one wants to use the sink while another is in the toilet or shower, and you would get that in any hotel with a regular bathroom. Floor to ceiling window so you can gaze out over the city while cleaning your teeth.
Complimentary hot drinks on each floor are really good. There's a microwave and fridge in case you want to be organised and get your food in advance. Housekeeping was good, we left our Do Not Disturb sign on the door the first day as the room was chaos. They left another one over the top to say they'd tried to come but had seen the sign and if we wanted fresh towels etc to give them a call, and they left us a voicemail too.
They have a Happy Hour at the bar, but the staff do look down their noses at you somewhat when you use it. We had a few beers, sparking wine for $4 each, and they do food. The only catch is they expect you to keep presenting yourself at the bar to get your food as if you've got it on the happy hour deal, they don't tend to deliver it to your table! You can't sit at the bar so you have no choice but to sit down. Similar with the free breakfast - they offer it but when you take them up on it they look down their noses at you and make you sit at specific tables because the majority are reserved for those ordering breakfast from the menu (and paying at least $15 for the priveledge) which very few people were doing.
Free computer use and printing which is good. Free luggage storage with the Yobot. Nothing to stop non-residents turning up and using any of these facilities as there's no room key check to get up to Four where they are all located, but you need your key to get the lift to the rooms and into the galleys for the tea/coffee.

title: Fantastically Quirky Hotel
body:
What a quirky & innovative hotel, really helped to make our experience in NYC an enjoyable one, the staff were excellent, very helpful & always willing to go the extra mile.
Rooms were small but well laid out, only minor gripe would be lack of storage space, but for the amount of time you spend in the room it is kind or irrelevant.
Bed was excellent, infact had a better sleep on these beds than the ones at home. Liked the way it turned into a futon during the day to save space.
Bathrooms were fine for us, but if traveling as a group of friends then open plan may be a little inappropriate.
Inclusive breakfast was adequate, not really enough to keep you going all day but ok to stave off hunger until you can find some food when out & about, must say the al a carte breakfast (the ones you have to pay for) looked excellent.
Location was excellent, 2 blocks from Times Sq & subway.
Very good price for the location & quality of the hotel!!

title: Great stay
body: We arrived in the middle of the night after a delayed flight from Houston. It was very easy to find and the distance to the subways was just a couple of blocks. We liked the design of the hotel, rooms, Yobot. The room was small, but we have recently traveled to Japan and experienced small rooms there so we were comfortable here too. Everything was efficiently laid out and the space was utilized well. We found the bed comfortable, but it also helped we were exhausted and fell right asleep! The Yobot was fun to use.

title: Quirky and purple!
body:
Stayed here for 3 nights over the New Year as part of a package (Vegas, New York and cruise on QM2 back to Southampton) so did not choose the hotel personally. BUT we thought it was an amazing place with friendly , helpful staff. We arrived at 07.30 and were able to leave our bags there while we had a look around. We were very impressed with the location .We had booked a New Years Eve party cruise and had been worried about how we would get to it as lots of people had told us we would have problems getting around on New Years Eve. However it was just a short 10 mins walk to the Hudson River and it was so straight forward (Circle Line cruises). 
I have mobility problems and we were allocated a Disabled room on the 19th floor and it was was huge. When we entered the room the view was breathtaking. It was on a corner and had floor to ceiling windows. Amazing. We were right next door to the kitchen which had a fridge and tea and coffee making facilities which were all complimentary. There was also a microwave. There was free internet available and you could have up to half an hour access. Only problem was that you had to stand up.
Anyway, we would love to go back to New York and would definitely try and stay at Yotel again.

title: Great modern hotel
body:
We arrived on the 26th Jan and stayed for 5 nights. Check in was very quick and easy. 
The room was very clean and well layed out. It is compact but I would expect this in NYC. The amenities are great as well with free wifi and hot drinks available. 
We had a few drinks in the bar which had a well priced happy hour and found the staff very friendly. 
The DohYo restaurant in the hotel has a good menu and the food tasted great. Just a shame we couldnt make the unlimited brunch at the weekend.

title: Cooooolest hotel I ever stayed in!
body:
I stayed for 7 nights on business with my colleagues. It was for a trade fair of which the place is just 4 blocks away from this hotel. This design hotel is also located just 5 minutes walk from Times square and Hell's kitchen. So we enjoyed nice dinners after the fair every night. 
The entrance does not look like a hotel, but a night club which we loved! Staffs are very nice and everything in there is sooo cool. We definitely love to stay in this hotel the next fair.

title: Great value for money
body: We are a couple in our 50ies, this is unlike anything else we had experienced before. Funky, modern, spotless, functional, friendly staff, soundproof rooms. Roms were, as expected, more the size of cabins on a cruise boat then a regular hotel, but than again travelling to NY we needed just a crash space. No breakfast, but good coffee and muffins gave us a great start for the day. The toilet having a glass door did not cause any problem, as a separating curtain was there to insure privacy. Walking distance to nearest metro/ sub station is10 mins( Times Square).

title: Super stay, convenient location
body:
We stayed here in January. Yotel is only blocks from the Port Authority and Times Square so the location is perfect! Also, it's very easy to get a cab if needed. The rooms are small, but well
Laid out and very clean. We had a Premium Queen Cabin and it was fine for 2, but absolutely no more than that. The restaurant was expensive for dinner. There is a tapas style menu and the portions are tiny. There is a very nice complimentary continental breakfast every morning.
There was a 24 hour CVS directly across the street. That was great for forgotten items and snacks.

title: Ultra-Modern
body: This is a wonderfully appointed and staffed hotel. The rooms are small but very well organized so they don't feel cramped at all. The bed is motorized and converts to a sofa or a lounge. They have a free comtinental breakfast with a wondeful assortment of muffins. The WiFi is free as well. It is located in walking distance to Times Square and the Theatre district. Be sure to check out the robot that will store your bags if you arrive early of want to do more exploring after you check out.

title: Great place!
body: Loved the hotel, the cabins are great and wonderfully designed, clean and compact. Free Internet, free hot drinks, drinking water, breakfast is fine coffee is good and muffins freshly baked, location is perfect, only few minutes walking to Time Square. Kind and helpful staff. Will definetly be back!

title: TERRIBLE staff
body:
the yotel location is good, and the price is ok. however the crew is really bad, they seams to be unprepared or just lazy and unpolite, here's and example - i tried to put my luggage in the yobot machine and an employee just took my bag of the machine and said "this is too big, you cannot store there".
i've stored some food in the galley - because yotel does not have a fridge inside the room- and someone just got my food.
also, i stand there for 7 days, and my room was only cleared twice, can you believe it??

title: Really liked the Yotel
body:
Took advantage of a Groupon offer and stayed at the Yotel on a Friday night. We got there after sunset and were able to see the outside of the hotel all lit up in purple. Check in was a breeze. Went right to the kiosk, typed in confirmation number and received room keys in minutes. We were on the 18th floor in a Standard Queen room with a view of downtown Manhattan. I agree with all the other posters, the room was spotless. It was small, but with the high ceilings and big floor to ceiling window we did not feel claustrophobic. It did remind us of being on a cruise ship. The shower was big and also spotless.
We did not eat at the hotel restaurant, but we did walk through it. On a Friday night it was hopping. It reminded us of a scene from the Jetsons, very modern with purple lighting. When we returned later that night the bar area was still going strong. The bar and restaurant are on the 4th floor, however up on the 18th floor it was quiet. We could not hear any of the bar noise.
Will go back and visit again.

title: Very clean, great staff, unique rooms.
body:
Yotel was a fun clean hotel. Check in was easy mainly because the staff were there to assist you. Check in was quicker than I ever experienced. Our room (909) was great. It was a corner room and the staff indicated it was a little bit bigger than the other standard rooms. The room it self was very very clean. It was fun and unique. The view through the floor to ceiling windows was awsome. There is plenty of privacy when using the bathroom just by pulling the curtain across. If you are noisy or smelly when you use the toilet you might want to bring some spray. There is a glass door in front of the toilet to keep it separate from the bathroom but I didn't see or hear a vent for... "steam". The window does open at the bottom which was a nice surprise. The bed wasn't the softest but I got a great nights sleep. Each floor has a galley with a ice/water machine, soda machine, ,microwave, minifridge and most important a coffee machine. The coffee was actually good. The galley was also very clean.
The staff was excellent. They were super helpful, very friendly and were always checking on you to see if they could help. I haven't experience staff that great ever. Overall the hotel was clean, unique, and the staff were friendly. The cost was good for NYC. I will be staying at Yotel next time I go to NYC. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: Yotel, NYC
body: Loved it! If you like your iPhone go there. It looks like an iPhone and it is as intuitive.

title: Yotel - NYC
body: My fiance and I spent two nights at the Yotel. It really is all you need if your visit to NYC is site seeing. We were hardly in our room, we just needed a CLEAN and comfortable place to sleep. The room is small but it doesn't really seem that way at all. It is perfectly put together. If you are going with someone that you are not that initmate with, well the bathroom might be awkward b/c there is little privacy. One thing I have never understood about other hotels is the drama and wait of checking it. Fast, Easy, Quick!! Definitely recommend!

this is a real nice place to stay quiet clean very comfortable , small but perfect

title: simply a great deal and great place
body: takes a moment to get your head around it but has a wonderful vibe and feel, while feeling very swanky but being very affordable. everything was super cool and fun and can't say enough good things, i'll come here again and again.

title: Trendy, fun and great location for walking NYC
body:
I love the Jetson-like appeal of this funky fun hotel. The retractable bed made the room feel spacious while my husband and I got ready in the morning - I've stayed at other NYC hotels without that luxury. The rooms were clean and comfy. The club was rocking right up until 4 am - great DJ's. My only "complaint" would be a little more upscale breakfast. The muffins were good with a large selection of flavors but we would have loved a little fresh fruit.
We loved being able to walk around Hell's Kitchen and Times Square easily. Even made a 15 block trek to Central Park with ease. We would definitely stay in this location again.

title: Concept is great but service and quality are better
body:
Disapointing experience with this hotel
Definitly not to recommend for a family trip.
Could be fun with fortunate friends to shine in a hype mood.
Breakfast is a shame.
They bet a lot on the concept not on the quality of the global experience.
Despite the default the crew was doing his best to balance the default of the hotel.
Hype and trendy right now, probably forgotten in 2 or 3 years...

title: Great Design and Value
body: Yo! Tel is awesome. The rooms were so cute and comfy - and I loved the coffee maker down the hall. The staff was friendly and it was a great location for going to a Broadway show. I wish that they would figure out a way for the hotel room doors not to slam - because it was pretty quiet except for this. Parking was only $39 per day. Loved it!

title: Good Hotel But Very Noisy Weekend
body: Good Dollar for your buck! However, if you are there over the weekend, you better hope you don't have those silly teens running about on your level! 3am in the morning, running up and down the halls scream and partying all night long! And when you try to call Mission Control: no one picks up. Weekdays was great! Clean tight space, but good enough for the tiny getaway.

title: Excellent Hotel and Close to Everything!
body: This hotel is very nice and clean. The Port Authority and MTA is only 2 blocks away. The staff was very nice as well. i also loved the bathroom.

title: Way cool --even for New York City
body:
Great location! Upscale, cool and easy. Fast check in on your own with room keys dispensed at the terminal. Lounge on 4 is superb - cozy and intimate or inviting and fun. Outside seating in warm weather and Happy Hours every afternoon. GREAT weekend brunches!
Many elevators to whisk you to your well equipped cabin with 24hour complimentary hot beverages and ice water readily available nearby. Cabins are really cool -- everything you need in practical space. The automated bed extends out for sleeping very comfortably and is perfect for "homework" or web browsing with the back retracted to a comfortable reclining position. It is a very hip and cool hotel. GREAT Staff members who are invisible until you need them, when they seem to appear immediately. GO, STAY AND ENJOY.

title: Pocket Rocket
body:
This cool, lively, funky hotel is a little gem. Check in took 1 minute, really helpful & friendly door staff, compact room which stored everything with room to spare for 2 people over a week. Bags of storage space, really light and very clean/well maintained. The only downside is the bathroom as it's not too private. Each floor has a Galley for free tea, coffee, ice, water so plenty of refreshments on tap. 
Outdoor patio is big and I am sure perfect for summer drinks. 2 bar areas, 1 which is higher energy, perfect for a late night blow out when our night wasn't ready to end after NYC bars. Didn't try the menu but asian fusion, decent breakfast (at hotel rates) & free muffins and coffee for those looking for a quick & free bite first thing. 
Location was very good, 10 minutes max to Book of Mormons, 5 minutes to On the Rocks (a great whiskey and world beer bar, all candles and bar stools) and of course 5ish mins to Times Square. You can also avoid the touts with a few minutes detour and get into other parts of NYC. 
Yotel feels like it's got great energy, could be the funky lift music, the light and simple, compact rooms or just that it's got a bit of NYC star dust!

title: Good, clean hotel room, but with restaurant issues and not safe for kids.
body:
I stay for 3 nights during the super bowl 2012 weekend from Friday to Monday. I got a very clean cabin at a very competitive but variable rates (Friday: $99, Saturday: $129, and Sunday: $89, excluding taxes). I had a good stay but had issues with the restaurant kitchen chef's inflexible policy. Before each order, I made sure to let them know that I don't eat salt and running egg or sunny side up egg. The egg must be over hard and well cooked. No salt in my food either. No fat. 
On the Sunday brunch, I was served fried rice with a running egg. I asked the egg to be cooked thoroughly and hard to my liking. The waiter was kind enough to take the food back to the restaurant kitchen chef during my brunch. But after 10 minutes, he came back to tell me, "I am sorry the kitchen chef told me that the menu could not be substituted". If other words,No. You have to eat whatever we cook as is during the brunch. No substitution. I was chocked but said nothing. Then 20 minutes later, I asked the waiter how can I get rice?. So he said "do you want rice without the egg" I said yes. He went back, got the fried rice with egg, ditched the egg in the garbage bin, and brought the fried rice to me. so I accepted.
Eventually, I asked the waiter how were the gratuities shared among the staff in the restaurant? He told me they were pooled in common and shared among everyone on the restaurant staff, including the kitchen staff. So I knew that I had to reduce my gratuities and gave them 1%. 
In conclusion, if you have a medical condition, be aware of the fact that, excepted the steak cooking, the food menu and preparation cannot be modified during the brunch, to suit your need and medical condition. No "substitution" is their word. Therefore, their restaurant is simply not suitable for everyone, although the service is good. Their breakfast was cheap: muffins and coffee or tea only. No juice.You have to pay for anything else. It is a reap off! 
On the inside-room safety side, the windows can be opened by kids easily, on the 12th floor at least where I stayed. So beware if you are going to stay with kids, unless it is a baby. Don't leave them alone in the rooms. I will no stay there with my kids. I have four kids but I travelled alone this time.

title: Just "WOW"
body: What a great hotel. I booked it through a groupon promotion and wasn't exactly sure what to expect and I was so very delighted with the outcome! The hotel is very fun and funky and immaculately CLEAN. The cabin is so functional and loved the moving beds! The only thing to be wary is that if you are staying with someone else in the room and need a lot of personal space, the room is really designed for people who are quite comfortable with each other. The bathroom doesn't really close off from the rest of the room and is only separated by a curtain and partial glass door. Other than that, I LOVED it and the robotic luggage storage system in the lobby is way cool. The staff was extremely attentive and helpful. I will go back to YOTEL for sure! Hey - groupon users... check out the "Shake, Rattle, and Roll - Dueling Pianos" show at Tobacco Road. It's only a block away from YOTEL and lots of fun!

title: Absolutely amasing experience
body:
Firstly WOW, the view from our window 19 floors up was breathtaking, read so many reviews about small rooms but when r u in them ?? The bed moves in and out which gave u lots of room loved all the quirky gadgets shower and toilet were funny being see thru but wat people dnt mention there is a curtain u can pull across which separated the bathroom. Shower gel was really good which u can purchase from reception. Staff are lovely and helpfull. 
They do have a galley on each floor that contains free hot drinks and microwave. The only criticisms of our stay that there was no cutlery in galley and most times the machine was not working. We reported it but were told to go to another floor which was also not in use would be better to have tea making in rooms and free muffins and coffee r brill but for breakfast? I would have liked to have seen cereals and maybe toast instead.
Free wifi and printing and no charges for local phone calls 
Overall a special unique experience and would definitely stay again. brill location, circle line ferry 2/3 blocks away and bus terminal just up the road recommend gray line bus tours.
Eating in times square expensive hells kitchen is better priced.

title: Great Location, service, rooms not for everyone
body: Return leisure trip to NYC, was able to secure a great rate/night ($84.15). Located just 2 blocks from Port Authority Bus Terminal, great for airport transfers and subway to anywhere. They refer to the rooms as "cabins", if you have ANY desire for any private bathroom time, the cabins are not for you. There is no door, just a draw curtain. The shower door will pull across in front of toilet but it is glass. Very minimalist and tight no room for unpacking except the bed. Oh yes, the mattress was awful. Some reviews said "hard" mattress, that was an understatement. Not sure if they have other sleeping options, you might want to ask. Staff was always accommodating. Again, not for everyone, however where can you get a room in midtown for under $100.

title: Funky Hotel
body: This hotel was in a good location, easy walk to Times Square and awesome restaurants in Hells Kitchen. The rooms are fairly small (not too much smaller than typical NYC rooms though) and are set up nicley. This hotel is clean and has a nice restaurant/bar. The Yobot (baggage storing device) was probably the coolest thing about this hotel.

title: OK....
body: I stay there for almost one week, every floor provides the coffee machine, but my floor that one was faulty, and over a week nobody fix it..., room won't provide any amenties, only 2 bottles of soap, no shampoo, provided. The breakfast provide the muffin, and it's fine. My hushand called to hotel and try to connect to my room, he rang for 4 times, but still nobody answer the general line. This is a hotel if you stay only one or two nights, not for business trip which they can provide the services what you need.

yotel was better than I expected!
room is clean, and as well as brekfast bread 
but the room was a little small for two. 
I think it's suitable for solo.

title: Overnight in an Apple Store
body:
I have totally mixed feelings about this hotel... In fact, I've never stayed at a place and been so undecided on a moment-by-moment basis whether I really like it or not. 
Overall, I'm arriving at the conclusion that this is a 2.5 or 3 star hotel wrapped in a 4 star facade.
Their mission (according to the Get To Know Yotel guide) is to provide a "first class" experience at an affordable price. On the surface, we see some of the hallmarks of first class -- most evident in the Yotel's very specific and controlled branding. The aesthetic -- from room design, to packaging, to the lack of maid's carts (staff carry laundry by hand) -- is consistent and very polished. The linens are pristine. The rooms tiny, but cool, glossy and absolutely clean. The restaurant and terraces are party spots for a stylish crowd. In this sense, the Yotel wildly outshines other lame hotels in its price class. 
But then we get down to the practicalities of staying there. Instead of little shampoos, soaps, toothbrushes, etc, your Yotel room offers a combination shampoo and body wash (no conditioner) and a pack of tissues. You can buy additional hygiene items on the 4th floor, but no conditioner. I forgot toothpaste... For 3 dollars, I got a disposaable toothbrush and one of the tiny single-serving size tooth pastes -- in super cool packaging. I'd rather have what I really needed (a legit travel-size toothpaste) and forget the packaging. And why not offer conditioner for sale if you don't have it in the room? I bet they have lots of requests for it. As someone who usually stays at 4 and 5 star hotels, I always trust there will be decent shampoo and conditioner; I never travel with my own anymore (given the airlines' strict limits on carry-on liquids). 
When I travel for business, I'm a heavy room service user. I often sit in bed and work with a tray of salad or some granola and coffee next to me. Not at the Yotel. There's no room service whatsoever. If you're hungry, head to the restaurant on the 4th floor. I could totally deal with this option if it were open for most (or all of) the day, but every time I seem to go down there, it's closed. So frustrating! Especially because this is the one NY neighborhood without decent food options. So really, if you get hungry at 11AM, good luck. The "continental breakfast" (read: muffin assortment) has been swept away an hour ago, the "a la carte" kitchen is closed, and the nearest food (save Subway) is blocks away. 
Think you'll just hit the minibar in the room? Think again. During the Yotel's expedited check in process (which is strikingly similar to an Apple store check out process), I was surprised they didn't take a card for incidentals. Now I know why... There are no incidentals. Absolutely none. In one sense, it's refreshing... I feel like my money is going where it matters (to the room cleanliness and visual appeal). At other moments, it's entirely frustrating (when I'm starving at noon and attempt to get a sandwich downstairs only to find the "restaurant" has been taken over by house DJ's and a fashion runway. 
Location-wise, I have the same mixed enthusiasm and concern I have with the rest of the hotel. Yes, it's close to Javits (where I'm working the next few days) and yes, it's an affordable cab ride to anywhere in the city, but to get to the subway or ANY real food options, it's a several-block walk around the Port Authority.
 Meanwhile, as I type this, I'm enjoying free WiFi provided by the hotel, sipping on good quality free coffee served with the muffin assortment, so there again... Mixed emotions. 
Would I recommend this place? Would I come back? I really have no idea.

title: THE place to stay in NYC from now on. FACT!
body:
I honestly can't rave about Yotel enough. I've stayed in the airport ones many times which are great and convenient but you'd never want to stay there for longer than a few hours. YOTEL NYC was hard to leave.
First let me address some of the (few ) complaints people wrote on here.
1. The beds were not hard - in fact i had a fantastic sleep
2. The bathrooms don't lack THAT much privacy. There's curtains and frosted glass. 
3. The staff could not have been more welcomin or friendlier - in fact they went out of their way to help.
I stayed for 2 nights in a standard (premium) cabin and then due to a mistake with my original booking they kindly upgraded me to a corner suite. If i'm honest, the corner suite did have amazing views but it felt like i was cheating the real yotel experience.
The standard cabins are more spacious than some rooms i've stayed in NYC -they are fun, well lit - nice big tv, soundproofed, clean - really - if you think they are tiny cabins with no soul - you couldn't be more wrong.
Location is perfect- close to subway - great restaurants nearby.
Yotel is a vibey, exceptional place to stay in NYC for a fantastic price. I would never even consider looking to stay anyway else again - Yotel will be hard to beat.

title: Fun hotel, good value & central location
body:
After reviewing the Yotel web site and other reviews I was apprehensive, but it turned out great and would totally stay there again. Be prepared for an ultra modern property catering to the solo traveler, tourists and younger/trendy people. Staff, restaurant, bar and night club all provided exceptional service and value.
Areas that need improvement:
No shampoo, conditioner or lotion provided.
Motion sensors are slow to pick up movement. I don't like walking into a dark room when I left a light on...
TV picture is too dark and not alterable.
Lighting around bathroom mirror is not bright enouph.
I would not recommend the Yotel for older couples, families with children or anyone sharing a basic room do to the bathroom configuration.

title: Cool Hotel
body: This hotel is great, location about 4-5 blocks away from times square and 2 blocks away from the Metro & everything else is very walking distance. Once you walking the hotel there is people who help you check in the computer and they was friendly & helpful with giving hints & tips about New York. The room is small but very cool. And the lobby turn to a nightclub with locals & hotel guest get in for free and no need waiting in line. Didnt drink so im sure the price for drinks are expensive. Free muffin, tea, & coffee for breakfast and every floor have a kitchen which is great. Kitchen have pure water dispenser, tea, coffee, vending machine, ice, & microwave. Once in New York, go to Joe's Shanghai for there famous soup inside of a dumpling and the delicous hot & sour soup, and everything else there are the best chinese food i ever ate. And also Bali Nusah Indah a very good Indonesian food, people are friendly, food are tasty and its only 2 blocks away from the hotel. And on 9th street there are a lot of restaurants also to try. Overall this hotel is great, cheap if you get a Groupon..

title: New York Weekend
body:
I was really looking forward to the 'experience' of something different with this hotel, and I have to say I was not disappointed. The cabin was actually a little bigger than I expected and the whole look and flow of the property was seamless and made me feel like I may be in a spaceship. I didn't have any need to encounter the crew much but when I did they were very helpful and courteous. The check in and check out process was quick not ever needing to speak to a live person and just using the kiosk made both processes less than 5 minutes. Although, I did ask to get a higher floor room, per suggestions of other reviews I've read on here and it was definitely quick and easy. The location of this place couldn't be better, close enough to public trans and times square but just enough away to not be in a crazy busy area.
The only complaint I would have is that if you happen to get a cabin next to a particularly rowdy group you will be able to hear them through the walls or if they are in the hall. I would assume that this is an easy fix with a simple phone call to mission control or a room change request. I myself didn't mind enough to call or ask for a change.
If you eat there definitely eat in the restaurant rather than your room, the food is awesome but the quality definitely suffered when I schlep it up to my room.

OK.
Let me begin by telling you how picky I am.
PICK.Y with ALL CAP's
This hotel is SO MUCH FUN, amazing people watching, super fun and nice staff, THE BEST BRUNCH EVER! The rooms are clean and super simple BUT sleek at the same time. This is the VIRGIN AMERICA of hotels, similar VIBE. The location is great every part of NYC is just a hop skip and a jump. I was

title: Dont Stay Here If You Need A Decent Sleep
body:
The location is excellent 3 1/2 avenues up from 7th avenue sub way stops which is also the heart of times square. Free wifi all over the hotel is a massive plus and cable tv in the room is also very good.
If you need a good nights sleep dont stay here you wont get any, stayed 4 nights got 1 night of decent sleep, the bed is rock hard it may look "cool" to see it change from a couch to a bed but its better off remaining as a couch. The staff are friendly if you need something and I guess not being in your face is a good thing but having no presence at all is bad. Needed their help once and had to ask them twice as they had forgotten about it 3+ hours later. Knocking on your door at 9am on your last day only to say sorry seemed like a ploy to get you up and check out early. Instructions on how to get to your room need to be made clearer on check in, to be told your room is on the 4th floor when actually its the 17th is a bit lazy of the staff member. The hotel seemed to still be doing decorating inside and there wasnt really much on offer with the "restaurant" just offering a limited choice of meals seemed more like a cafe then a restaurant that you'd expect in a hotel ?

title: Very nice and clean.
body: This hotel is very nice and clean, the rooms are light and beds are confortable! my triple room was fantastic! There are no noise at all, breckfast is simple but good. Good free connection. It's not very close to the subway...

title: wow what an experience, great nights sleep!!!
body:
Fantastic hotel, modern, minimal, clean, and funky. The experience from start to finish was great. The minute you step into the lift you start to feel the vibe, you know youre in good hands!! nothing was too much trouble for mission control.. The great things are you have a galley at the end of each corridor with free coffee ( decaff and normal) and ice/water, microwave and vedning machine - assessable 24/7, free WIFI in your room, lovely spacious shower with funky body washes. yes everything is compact, but it works. We stayed happily for 5days and 4nights without getting too crowded. The bed is automatic so is it out of the way. It bugs me when people say dont stay here if you need a decent sleep - hello? the rooms were very sound proofed were didnt hear a peep, no traffic either, and if youve done new york justice you will have walked your socks off all day and just crash when you get to your room anyway!!! any sensible person would be proactive and takes earplugs just in case.
The beds were deliciuosly comfy anyway. Complimentary muffins at breakfast were also lush. We loved every minute of it, our friends staying in at hotel nearby were sutiably jealous.

title: Funky, contemporary, super staff and excellent location
body: Very funky and contemporary accommodation, the best I have had in NY on a budget. From checking in via machine on the ground floor, seeing the infamous YOBOT in action, it was a most pleasant stay from start to finish. Staff were very friendly and could not do enough for the group of us that stayed in the hotel. Any queries were swiftly dealt with by MIssion Control (4th Floor). If you are there for work, the food is supplied separately by an outsourced company from the hotel. The room was akin to an airline cabin, the bed was in a lounge like position and could be lowered for bedtime. All very clean, comfortable with room service daily. The galley at the end of the corridoor was available to all for hot drinks/fridge/water and ice - no facilitied in the room. All other conveniences were provided in addition with the amazing view day/night of the river and of NY from 22nd floor. It was only 10 min walk to Times Sq and taxis were always available to your destination. The subway is just before Times Sq and we were able to get the bus to Woodbury Common, only 5 mins around the corner. Highly recommed YOTEL for your NY accommodation and will definitely making reservations on our next trip to NY.

title: Fabulous, fresh and buzzing.
body: Such a fresh and new feel to this hotel. Everything was so easy without any hassle or red tape. All the staff were so helpful, particularly the Concierge and it was refreshing that they genuinely were never 'tip hanging' when they did anything for you. I loved the room, it was comfy, spotlessly clean, excellent view, day and night. There were free hot drinks from the galley on each floor, There was even a fridge and microwave in the galley for use. The fresh muffins and coffee for breakfast were great. The location couldn't have been bettered. Best of all though, it was always buzzing on the 4th floor where the bar and restaurant were located and yet we heard no noise whatsoever in our room. I wish they would build a Yotel in all cities. Please stay there, it's great.

title: Amazing
body:
Thank you YOTEL for the most amazing stay with you recently.
After check in we went to our room on the 20th floor - what a view. Room lovely and clean - minimal/list themes/ lines and crisp linens on the bed. Towels changed daily - thank you. We enjoyed three nights wonderful sleep in our soundproofed room, and awoke refreshed. Breakfast was wonderful, freshly baked muffins and oodles of coffee/tea to start the day touring the big apple.
Staff could not be more helpful. Check in at Ground Control was great, and Mission Control is a haven of information, as is the Concierge, but beware, do not forget your pass key, or Security Control will be called to escort you to your room. This was not a problem, as it conveyed that Security and Guest Safety was paramount, which I was happy about. Also a nice touch is that calls can be made for free in the hotel room to local areas to NY ie Boston, Yardley in Penns.
I would like to thank all the staff in this amazing fun hotel for making us feel so special and would like to say thanks to Abel for his lovely emails prior to our visit. 
I thoroughly enjoyed my brief stay in your wonderful city and we hope to come back and stay in Yotel, a very .special place - I know we will be looked after.
Cara 1956

title: The rooms reminded me of a trip to a private mental hospital.
body:
The decor of the rooms reminded me of when I was a child and visited a family friend at a psychiatric hospital- all rounded corners, nothing of true comfort in the rooms, or any real types of personality beyond over hyped purple lighting placed behind the rounded cornered tv cabinet done in white. There was absolutely no personality to the room, not even an ice bucket....lol, exactly like a mental hospital in where there is nothing left out to hurt yourself, even the bottles of shampoo/body wash are bolted to the walls and there is a white curtain hanging needlessly in the middle of the room to partition off the bathroom from the sleeping quarters that reminded me of an Emergency Room. 
I really did not enjoy this hotel at all, to the point that I checked out several days prior to when I originally planned on leaving the city, and checked into another hotel. 
They brand themselves as a higher end hotel with all of the amenities of home.... if that home is a mental hospital than they would be correct. They do not provide a mini-bar in the rooms, and the location is an odd one so going out to get a beverage or a snack in the area is sketchy and undesirable to do. There is no mini fridge provided so you cannot even keep something cool in your room, and not even an ice bucket is provided, which to me screams "cheap" and completely unconcerned about their patrons level of comfort.
I travel often, I mean I am the type that is the ideal patron to want return business with, also meaning I have been to many many hotels and I have never seen one so lacking and barren before in all of my 45 years. 
No real shampoo or soap is provided. You must wash both your hair and body with the same items. The last I knew, they need different ingredients. There is no conditioner provided, not even in the "mission control" center (which was also annoying and I will tackle momentarily) so if you need any, you must trek out to find a store in which to purchase these items. No q tips provided, not cotton balls, absolutely nothing at all but bottles of wash that are larger bottles bolted on to the wall, which kind of skeeved me as then I also knew and thought about all the other naked people that had stood in that same shower using these same items..... yes, I know it's a hotel room, but one of the true measures of a good hotel with excellent understanding of it's patrons, is delivering a sense that no one else stayed there prior. Using the same bottles that strangers used while naked, even if in thought, was not pleasant. Oh, but they do provide you with a mini packet of Kleenex, you know the kind, that you kept in your pocket while in kindergarten. I am a grown up, staying in a place that bills itself as higher end, I want a full size tissue to use that I don't have to wrestle with to blow my nose.
I wanted to jot a note down for directions to a store, so I could go buy a bottle of conditioner, and they didn't even provide a note pad to do so with. 
The space to store your items? There is none. Your entire time there, in this tiny room, you must stare at your suitcase, adding even more of a closed in feeling to the room. There are 2 small drawers provided under where you must place your luggage to use, which is under whe you put your luggage so you must first move your luggage if you want to access it.
The beds..... how they can even refer to these as beds is beyond me. They are nothing but futons, and not even glorified ones at that. They are so hard that I would have preferred to have slept on a chair, had they provided one. The bed linens were cheap and itchy. My suggestion would be to the owners of this hotel to go sleep at the "Night" hotel for a night to see what a real bed, that is pure luxury, is about because this was nothing more than something my children may have slept on when in nap time at day care.
Complimentary breakfast? While the assortment of muffins was nice, having provided hot eggs and toast would have been a nicer touch, and in honesty, probably cheaper for the hotel to provide in cost comparison. 
Beautiful terraces? I wouldn't know, as when I tried to go out onto one of them, I had 5, yes 5 staff members come chase me off of the terrace,telling me I was not allowed to be there. It was completely funny that it required 5 of them to come tell me this, as I am all but 5 feet 4 inches and 130 pounds, and maybe if they hadn't chased me off the only thing I was actually enjoying about the hotel, I may not have chosen to take my business elsewhere or be writing this review. 
The location is horrible and in a part of the city that is not convenient to other areas, it's a several block walk to Times square in an area that is rather sketchy, next to the Port Authority, read, having to deal with derelicts to go buy a bottle of conditioner that had not been provided, putting my safety into question.
There is a nightlife there, that I will say is "hip" and would be my only real reason to ever return, even though it was complete chaos and not well directed. When you walk off of the elevator on the 4th floor, the mission control ( more like mission impossible) floor there is no indication on where to go and you are immediately thrust into the overflow of there events and party area, leaving for confusion on exactly where to go, once you are able to find the " mission control area" it is again filled with no real personal touches. They offer kitchy little items for sale like little miniatures of their rooms, but not much to offer in what travelers may really NEED, like conditioner, q tips, although there is a toothbrush for sale, and umbrellas, but more of what they seem concerned with is selling cheap trinkets of the hotel.
My encounter with this hotel is a complete shame, as someone who truly appreciates uniqueness to a hotel, such as the architecture of this building, if I had felt like something other than a guest at a mental hospital, with it's lack of true design, and having 5 attendants come to rush me off the terrace, I might have returned with my 3 teenagers for a weekend in the city, or on one of my many other business trips into the city, I come in at least twice a month for 3-4 day stays ( can you say return money?) but I found it completely lacking in any personality. any real concern for it's guest, and a total lack of comfort. I don't even want to mention what happens when you realize that if you go down to "mission control" to find out if you can get a bottle of conditioner" if you forget your key, you can't even get back up to your hotel room on the elevator. I understand his is probably due for hotel security, but maybe try adding real staff instead of kiosks, and it would again add to the comfort of it's patrons maybe it might be a 2 star hotel.
I believe half of the high markings have been done by a younger crowd with no real money or idea as to what true comfort is, which is sadly misleading to other consumers who actually understand what a good hotel remembers first, it's customers comfort, and that would start with providing amenities like ice buckets and losing things like emergency room curtains in the middle of the room to partition off the bathroom from the sleeping closet, as that's all the rooms are, a closet without any real personality.

title: Yotel was better than expected
body: It far surpassed hotels that cost three times as much. Would definitly stay again.

title: Fun to experience once,but....
body: We found the Yotel to be an interesting and exciting experience, and a good value. The room was immaculately clean. However, It was lacking in warmth, and it felt just a bit uncomfortable. The room was so small, and the mattress was too thin. I would get cranky if I was cooped up in that room for more than one night. I would recommend this place to try for a one night weekend stay. The Sunday brunch there is also a very fun experience.

title: Unique Hotel in a Good Location
body: Although we hadn't been to NYC in several years, we decided to spend the weekend for our wedding anniversary. I found Yotel through a third-party booking agency when making the airline reservations. The location and price were appealing and we weren't disappointed. Although it appears to be geared toward a younger crowd, it provided a great base for us to celebrate our 29th anniversary. Service was very good; staff very pleasant and efficient; and the food in the restaurant was excellent. We normally book king rooms, and were a little apprehensive with the expandable queen bed arrangement, but it was just fine. Although the room was small, it was very clean and functional. It's an easy walk to Times Square and the theater district. We took the subway from 42nd and 8th Ave. to the WTC and the 9/11 Memorial, caught a show, hit a couple other restaurants, and went to the Top of the Rock at Rockefeller Center, as well as eating at the hotel restaurant - all within 36-hours - largely due to the convenient location. We'll probably go back to Yotel New York next time we go to Manhattan for two or three days.

title: nice hotel
body:
I spent 2 days in yotel
nice interior, hotel was very clean, location is two blocks away from the time square.
There is a nice lounges and restaurant too. The only thing I did not like about the hotel was bathroom door. I stayed in Queen Cabin, and there was no bathroom door. 
If you visiting the city alone, it is nice place to stay with good budget.

title: Just right!
body: Came for a quick visit to the city. Yotel is conveniently located near Theatre district. Very cool adequately sized room for 2. No frills, good security. They were running special pricing which made it very attractive. Very international clientele.

title: Amazing price, Amazing Location, Amazing experience!
body: We went to Yotel to watch the superbowl and to go to restaurant week. This hotel is in SUCH an amazing location!! It's 3 blocks from times square literally right there next to everything!! The rooms were AMAZING and I never write reviews but this hotel deserves a great one! The standard rooms are small but they have a great set up with flat screen tvs and a walk in rain shower as well as a towel rack to heat your towel while your in the shower! The whole set up is an amazing experience and a must see with the robot and all! If you want a hotel for a great price and a great stay this is the place for you!

title: Great location - fun hotel
body:
My teenage son & daughter, husband and I stayed here for one night. It turned out to be a great location - 3 blocks or so from Times Square. We chose this hotel due to good ratings on Tripadvisor, the location, and a reasonable price ($229 via priceline). Yotel has a luggage robot which was an awesome way to drop off our luggage prior to check-in (and after check-out too for that matter). Our "cabin" was larger than most I believe since it was handicap accessible and/or intended for up to 4 people. The sofa converted into bunk beds which was cool. The one draw back to that though was that a "crew member" had to do the conversion and we had to call three times before someone came (finally at 11pm and with only 1 thin blanket per bed!). We had a nice view of the city looking north through large windows. The window blinds were automated, but did not really darken the room enough in the morning. Our other complaint was with the bathroom - the outer door did not close properly which resulted in even less privacy (not so much to begin with). And the sink did not drain well normally, and the plug would not pop back up once in the down position.
But there were a number of pluses - our dinner at the restaurant (tapas style) was delicious. The free morning coffee was excellent (muffins were so-so). All of the "crew members" we dealt with in person were extremely friendly. And the overall atmosphere was fun.

title: Everyone should experience Yotel
body:
Excellent concept for a hotel, it sets its self apart from the normal boring accomodation..
Had a great time. Will definatly go back!

title: great location, clean..
body: this hotel was very clean, and staff was very helpful. it was close to the subway- and great for my walk to the javitz. the food was great in the lounge..fun place to stay- would love to come back in the summer.

title: Modern Experience
body: small cozy rooms, awesome modern shower only problem is the there is no wall for bathroom, if you stay alone your okay, if you have a guest with you they can hear you go to the bathroom. dance club is nice and restaurant is awesome but the staff was no where to be found especially late at night.

title: Unique fun hotel
body: Our one night stay was a great experience at Yotel! With a good price, good location and cool vibe this hotel exceeded our expectations. Our Queen cabin was clean and comfortable. While small it was nicely designed giving sufficient storage. The bathroom,divided by only glass and curtain, was an unusual design that at times did not allow for the privacy that we might have preferred. None the less it was functional and adequate. Body wash/shampoo was delightful. The slide out bed was quite comfortable and when retracted allowed the small room to have a more spacious feel. Cruise ship designers should make a note of some of Yotel's design elements! A Sunday brunch was in full swing when we arrived and looked like a fun event for a hip young crowd. Altho we stood out as both too old and too square to fit in it was fun to observe the group. The coffee and muffin breakfast the next morning were a nice extra. We will definitely stay here again.

title: Husband's Surprise 35th Rondevue
body: My Hubby was taking pictures of this hotel as soon as we stepped in the room. We partied so hard that we missed the great "Free Breakfeast" but we hope to come back in the summer for a fabulous roof top party. Great Venue!

title: Great Experience & Fun Place!
body: This place felt more like an overall experience then just a hotel. Everyone was very nice & helpful. The food at the restaurant was delicious & our waiter was great! It seems like there were a lot of tourists, but that is neither here nor there. The breakfast in the morning was a great plus. Stayed only one night for Valentine's Day but wish we would have had more time to enjoy the atmosphere here. Rooms were tiny but & perfect for just 2 people. However the decor & layout was very unique & fun so we didn't mind the size. Would definitely recommend & will return here!.

title: ultra modern hotel
body:
stayed three nights in this funky modern hotel, small but equally cosy rooms with fab electronic bed that moves up into a sofa. free coffee and muffins for breakfast and free galley kitchen with drinks and ice etc
staff were very friendly and helpful, nothing was too much trouble. very close to subway, times square and all amenities. Would recommed also a trip to HMS excalibur which is just at end of road frm hotel - head for the river!
too cold to sit outside on terrace but this looks like it would be great in the summer months
would definately stay here again and would recommend to all

title: Definitely Worth the Stay
body:
We have just arrived back to Ireland from a four night stay in the Yotel, NYC. The hotel was in a fantastic location two blocks away from the Port Authority Bus Terminal, in the heart of Times Square. We opted to get a shuttle bus from JKF airport at $56 return. However, if we had of known we would have just opted to buy a $29 7-day metrocard for the subway. You can take the subway train directly from JKF to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. 
The hotel was very clean. We had a premium cabin which some people say is small (the bed is retractable), considering you are never in your room this was definitely not an issue. 
We didn't eat in the hotel restaurant but we had the breakfast muffins and coffees each morning which really set us up for the day. There was definitely no need to buy breakfast!!
I would definitely recommend this hotel and would visit again when coming back to NYC.

title: Excellent hotel at a reasonable cost
body: My daughter and I spent three nights over President's weekend. Although the room is small, it is extremely well designed. There is a place for everything. We did not mind the curtain for a bathroom door at all. The hotel is centrally located. The muffin and coffee breakfast was plenty for us to start our day. The staff was exceptionally nice and always available. We appreciated the complementary hot beverages and cold water available on our floor.

title: Hip Hotel in the heart of it all
body: very modern hotel with an asian feel that is close to everything. I would stay there again.

title: Excellent Hotel
body:
We stayed at Yotel for 4 nights. We took the subway from LGA and walked down from the 42nd Port Authority Bus Terminal subway stop. It's about a 5 minute walk or you can catch the 42 bus. We arrived in the morning and were able to check-in, we requested an upper level floor with a view and they were able to accommodate us with a room on the top floor (27th). The rooms are big enough, we never felt cramped. The mattress was a little hard, but after a long day out there's no problem falling asleep. The room was cleaned well daily. The only negative was that after showering there would be an odour from the shower drain. You can also hear noises from the hallway at night. 
The galley kitchen on the floor are very convenient we used the coffee machines daily, the one day the machine was faulty. I used the fridge to store my left over pizza which was there when I returned. 
The complimentary morning muffins were great.
You are able to store your luggage once you check out using the yobot for free.

title: Almost faultless accommodation in a great location
body:
If there is funkier, more-contemporary and better-value hotel than this anywhere in New York (let alone Manhattan) please let me know.
I had a great seven nights in one of these 'cabins' (think space ship rather than cruise ship!) in February 2012. 
There has a lot of thought gone into this hotel and not just into the very special design cues - whether it is the functional, well-appointed, highly-contemporary rooms (four, not three, star I would have thought) or things like free safe, complimentary wi-fi, coffee and muffins for breakfast, every-level kitchens (with free coffee on tap), free internet lobby and frickin funky public spaces (including bars with weekend and weekday events and offers). Unfortunately, I was too busy sight-seeing or recovering from several sessions around the 'hoods to take advantage of the Saturday and Sunday afternoon bar brunch parties which are popular with locals and feature food and drink offers as well as some house DJs. I bet these are a blast in the summer when the terraces are open! Indeed (with Pacha New York around the corner), this is the kind of hotel that Ibiza has been crying out for!
Staff here were also unfailingly friendly, helpful and discrete.
Just a couple of blocks from the Port Authority Bus Terminal this also has a superb, central location for travelling around the island and beyond 24-7 using the subway (don't just get taxis - the Metrocard for subway and buses is great value and the system very easy to understand thanks to uptown, downtown and crosstown services).
If I had a single criticism about the rooms it was with the usual door slammers. If people are too selfish to stop door rooms slamming then that's hardly the fault of Yotel but self-closing mechanisms with dampers might help.
Summary: a flawless stay at the Yotel which gave a great foundation to an excellent week in New York and I can't wait to go back (to the Yotel and Manhattan).

title: A trendy new hotel with lots of stylish young people
body:
A trendy stylish ultra modern hotel that models its rooms after ideal airline cabins, it has an eager, young staff that tries and succeeds to be friendly and helpful. Although they almost apologize for the small size of the rooms, they are (a) bigger than many in NYC and (b) beautifully designed for comfort. Our queen bed converted electronically from a flat bed to something like a couch (which gave one more room). The location is superb -- near Broadway, the Actor's Studio, and literally around the corner from several brand new off-broadway theaters.
To be sure, we encountered a few glitches: (1) we we couldn't utilize the self-check-in because they misspelled our last name on the pre-paid reservation, and (2) our room was missing some of the amenities, which we only discovered on the 2nd day when they appeared. I thought the lunch creative and very good though typically NY pricey. Lots of attractive people from France, Germany, and Europe plus a few older couples like ourselves. We'd go back again if we wanted to be in this area.

title: just nice!
body: very clean and stylish rooms. free wifi and free coffee/tea/muffins in the morning. pc at lobby is also available for free. perfect location at times square, market, subway and bus station in the near. friendly hotel stuff and service.

title: Should have been an "A"
body: I'll start with the positives, and there were many. Great location. Loved the layout of the room. Super quiet. Automated check in was easy and efficient. I wanted to love, love, love the place. BUT, when it came to the little things that were meant to make the Yotel unique-- felt they dropped the ball. The galley on our floor (19) was a disaster. The coffee machine was constantly breaking down, and I ended up emptying the very dirty, very wet disposal tray myself several times in an (unsuccessful) attempt to get it working. Spoke with several people who had also called down to "Mission Control" to report problems-- but it remained problematic for all three days of our stay. The desk's suggestion to use a galley on another floor was less than satisfactory. I don't want to have to go from floor to floor in my leisure wear to get a cup of coffee. On our last night of a special celebration weekend, we opted to avoid the hyper loud lounge and enjoy a bottle of champagne in our room. Unfortunately, the bar would not let us have a couple of wine or champagne glasses to take with us-- offering us only plastic cups (which we already had available in the bathroom of our room). Disappointing. I've never had a hotel refuse such a simple request. At the end of the day, it's the little things that make a big difference. Probably won't return.

title: Perfect
body:
Everything is well-designed, useful, meaninful and perfect. As locaiton is the first important thing for turists, Yotel is very close to Times Square and subway and also Penn station.
I have stayed 2 nights and it was really good experience. Air condition is a bit noisy. The meals are served as tapas, so be carefull if you are too much hungry, will not be enough. But the taste is perfect.Crew was heplful and satisfactory. Definitely, will choose YOTEL in next trip to NY.

title: Great feel, great stay!
body:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Yotel in New York City and it was a great stay. We stayed 5 nights and booked the hotel online. The hotel is 3 blocks from Times Square and it is surrounded by many different things like Burger King, CVS, Subway (food) and 2 blocks away you can take a subway at Port Authority. The hotel is very hip. Checking in took us about 2 minutes. They have kiosks where you can check in with your last name and number of stays as well as with your credit card. So that was really easy. Then you choose how many room keys you want and they come out of the slots, and you're all set.
The rooms are quite tiny but a perfect size for a NYC stay. The bed retracts and can be transformed into a couch with the push of a button. This way you'll also have more space in the room to walk. The bathroom is great, it's all glass doors and stuff, but there's a curtain so it's not completely see through from the room. It was clean and room service was great.
Also, in the morning they served breakfast muffins, all kinds, banana, nuts, chocolate. They also serve free coffee all throughout the day downstairs. Also, all floors had a galley where you could get free coffee, tea and hot chocolate.
Checking out was also done at the kiosks. Also, if you have some time to kill, the guys in the lobby will take care of your suitcases, store them for you and make sure there's a ride ready for you to take you to the airport at whichever time you want. They provide a sort of a shuttle service (with Escalades!) that costs you 60$ including tip (to JFK), which is the same amount you'd pay for a taxi.
So, overall, excellent hotel!! The only thing is that breakfast was limited. Muffins aren't something I like to have for breakfast every morning.
Also, I found that the beds were not very soft. They were kind of hard. I slept comfortably but woke up with back pains.

title: Great location, uncomfortable beds
body:
I have mixed feelings about this hotel. It was located in a great spot (two blocks from Times Square) but the beds were really uncomfortable! After a long day of walking around, all I wanted was a comfey bed… :(
Here are my thoughts:
-The room and hotel itself were really neat and modern. It may be worth checking out just for that reason.
-The staff were very friendly and helpful.
-The “galley” was a nice feature. You have 24 hour access to free hot beverages. 
-The room doesn’t come stocked with any toiletries, so bring your own. There is a drugstore right across the road in case you forget something.
-The shower is one of those rain shower heads, and there isn’t much pressure, so showering kinda sucked.
*Now here’s the most important thing I will tell you… You can apparently ask housekeeping for a mattress pad, if you find your bed too hard. We didn’t find that out till we were checking out, but that would have made our stay much more enjoyable.
All in all, not a bad place, and if you can get it at a good price, its worth it. However, in the future, if I had a choice of another hotel that was the same price and a decent location, I might stay somewhere else.

title: yotel in new york
body: After reading several reviews i had a few mixed feelings about this hotel . The hotel is stylish and very modern , check in was easy , plenty of staff on hand to help you to your room with your bags explaining all about the hotel on the way . Rooms are small yes but they are perfectley formed ! the bed was one of the most comftable i have ever slept in , The room was spotless the bathroom area came with plenty of shower gel / shampoo so cant understand reviews about none been available !? .We did have a prob with the shower but "jim i`ll fix it " turned with within 2 mins and sorted the prob , the shower was amazing very hot water and fab to use , no dripping shower head and no further probs. We got clean towels and pillow cases every day . The gallery was a short walk away with plenty of hot drinks and cold iced water , there was a vending machine for fizzy drinks . Free maps in the room and more available on request to plan your day out . The location was perfect not too far to walk to the centre of Times Square but not too near to hear the traffic noise and general New York noise . This is a amazing hotel , with pleasent and helpful staff who made our stay perfect . Rooms laid out perfect and nothing is too much trouble , I would definatly reccommend anyone who is going to New York to stay at this amazing hotel . PERFECT !!

title: Modern, compact room
body: I loved the room. It is inspired by an airplane cabin(think Virgin America) It was quite nice. The service was great, room was quiet, lighting was awesome. The only real drawback was the bathroom, it may not be private enough for some. Be careful what you eat. There is just a curtain that separates it from the sleeping area.

title: Great, frun atmosphere
body: Great hotel with just enough space for everything to be comfortable. The atmosphere is upbeat and youthful with fun music playing and a general buzz around the building. All of the staff is more than friendly.

title: We loved it!
body: I was traveling with a friend and we loved the hotel! It´s walking distance (5 minutes) to Times Square and where the inter-states buses drop you off. We recomend and will be back for sure!

title: Great hotel, TERRIBLE beds
body: This hotel has all the elements of being a GREAT hotel--it's very well designed and fun. The restaurant is good. The staff is great. The rooms are relatively quiet (I requested an upper floor to cut down on street noise). The rooms are very small, but well designed. The only real drawback--and for me it will be a dealbreaker for staying there in the future--was that the bed was beyond uncomfortable and the bed linens were stiff.

title: nice hotel, incompetent staff
body: Asked for a specific room (2426) two months ahead of time. Get my room key, go upstairs to find the room not ready (mind you, around 7PM...). When I come back down to the lobby to complain, I am told I could be upgraded for 'only' $50 per night. Seriously? After that annoyance and me being a little unfriendly, I got a free upgrade. Nice, but could have been nicer. Overall, the hotel is still as nice as the first time. However, some of the design flaws should be fixed (shower splashing...).

title: Yotel Perfecto!
body:
Couldn't recommend this hotel enough. 
Self check in was so easy to use. First impression of our cabin room was great. Really clean and tidy. It seems small but there are loads of little spaces to put all your clothes and other bits and bobs. the bed was great, love the way it slides in and out to switch between a bed and sofa. The techno wall was perfect, plug in your iphone/pod and you've got your own disco :)
The bathroom was perfect, large sink area with huge mirror you could light up, large shower with big monsoon shower head and gorgeous aromatherapy shower gels provided. If your a girl with long hair maybe take your own hairdryer, the one provided was like someone breathing on my head....but that might be to do with the voltage??
Our room was cleaned everyday and new towels were provided.
The galley on each floor was great to go grab a morning coffee before you go down for a bit of breaky, a free coffee machine and fresh water and ice. There was also a drinks machine, microwave and fridge but we didnt need to use these.
Complimentary breakfast was a huge selection of muffins, tea and coffee. There are other breakfast options available for a price but we preferred to go out and find a diner for an authentic NY breakfast.
the dohyo bar was really cool. Set down by the restaurant with cool Japanese paintings on the walls, the bar holds a multitude of spirits and beers. The happy hour cocktails go down well but you have to have a Cosmopolitan......when in Rome and all that.
Staff were super friendly and knowledgeable about the area.
Location was perfect, just a couple of blocks away from Times Sq. Go have a wander up 10th right onto 43rd and back down 9th, loads of diners and deli's and you're really close to Bowlmoor Lanes....amazing bowling with 50 lanes!!
Dont bother searching the internet for an average hotel, go here now!!

title: Yotel is Awesome!
body: This hotel is at a great location, the rooms are amazing and I love the purple color. The price is great as well. Such a different type of hotel that makes you feel like you're in the future. I also loved the rooftop. Everything is so efficient at Yotel. Probably the best hotel in NYC if you don't mind the small rooms.

title: love jazz
body: stayed one night at yotel. great experience. great use of space (queen room). staff was very nice. location to subway, times square and port authority within a couple of blocks. will stay there again

title: Yotel Dreamy
body: When you find a nice rating deal on this hotel, please DO NOT HESITATE TO BOOK! Wonderfull interior, modern & great tunes. Room was small but in no way smaller then any other hotel in NY. Location is a dream, next to biggest subway station & only 3 blocks from Times Square, yet just far away not te be stuck in the wildness of it all. I will book this every time when I go back to NY!

title: I love this hotel!!
body: Hip atmosphere. Great rooms. Very helpfull staff. Great location. Hi-speed wireless internet. This hotel has everything i wanted or needed. Would stay here again!

title: Don't go here to sleep!
body:
This hotel is a great experience but don't plan on sleeping. I must be getting old - I'm not even 30 yet - but this place would be perfect for you, if you don't care that you are sleeping on a thin mattress (much like a futon) placed upon what feels like a concrete slab. You can hear everything that is going on in the hallway - so hope that you are placed on a floor with quiet people (we were not that lucky...). And I hope you are close with whomever it is that you're staying with because they are more than likely going to hear you poop at some point during your stay. The curtain that separates the bathroom and the bedroom isn't as sound proof as you'd think.....
I thought that I was getting a good deal, super close to the convention center, but after a day of walking around NYC and standing at a trade show booth, this was not the hotel experience that I wanted. 
If only the beds were more comfy, I would have given a much better review!!

title: SIMPLY BRILLIANT
body: Just returned from a weekend stay at the YOTEL in NYC and it's nothing short of BRILLIANT...the design and efficiency of the place is remarkable. Kudos to whomever designed the layout and flow of the facility :-)!!! The staff was equally remarkable, especially Jessica at the "desk on 4" and Christopher at "ground control", they were both very accommodating to the our group of 8 and went above and beyond to accommodate our wishes. HIGHLY recommend, can't wait to return :-)!!!!!! /Gail

title: vacation at yotel new york city
body:
we stayed 5 nights and the hotel and it was very nice:
clean, great location, very good assistence if needed and fun!

title: It's the Bed, Stupid
body:
As for many other reviewers here, we thought this was a fun and funky hotel let down by a poor sleep experience. The compromise required to allow the installation of retracting beds is that the mattresses on said beds are pretty thin and that the base itself isn't sprung. The end result of which is an uncomfortable and unappealing experience. Throw in a total lack of bathroom privacy and the comfort level drops even further.
It's a real shame, because the hotel wins in so many areas. Staff were great, environment was cool and stylish (although they might come to regret the light colour scheme, which is already showing signs of wear and tear) and we thought the galley with free (and good quality) coffee was a nice touch. Check in was a breeze (with help and a free upgrade to a corner room offered without asking) and the Yobot is awesome. Location is ok too, a bit of a walk to the subway, but not too far. 
Would we go back? In current guise, no, probably not. If they changed the beds, then yes, we might just...

title: Retro vision of the future in today's NYC
body:
Not only the city will be unforgettable--this hotel will grant you a unique experience.
Travel to outer space without leaving Manhattan. Beautifully designed pod rooms that look like a space ship. Quiet rooms, small but beautiful and well equipped with many amenities.
Great hotel--fun, great service, clean, conveniently located.
Best place for the price range.

title: Great hotel!
body:
Nice clean hotel. Great crew. Ideal sleeping concept. Good location. (near the bus/train/metrostation and Times square) 
The bed is indeed a bit hard but for a week it's OK.

title: Yotel - you will not regret it!
body: A fantastic hotel, superb value - great staff and great facilities on site. Trendy and fun without being overly so. Cabin's aren't as small as you imagined and are fantastically thought out. Beds extremely comfy, not sure why others - galley on each floor if you need water/hot drink etc Lovely bar & reasonable restaurant on site - We will definitely be back to stay again.

title: Yotel rocks!
body:
Fun, clean, high-tech hotel in New York, a few blocks from Times Square. Highly suggested!
Rooms are new, smartly configured.
The only drawback (and the reason why I'm not giving 5 stars): the breakfast. Muffins are good for one day, but at some point you get tired of it. A la carte is available but it's pricey (although the quality of the food they cook is quite high).

title: Yotel great hotel
