body: Our stay at the yotel was amazing the hotel room was lovely and warm,spotlessly clean,very quiet considering how noisy it is outside and plenty big enough for the two of us.The beds were very firm but comfy just what you need after a full day exploring new york.Staff were very friendly and approachable,always willing to help in any way.The complimentary breakfast was muffins and coffee but my own choice would be fresh fruit juice as an alternative to coffee but was nice anyway.The cooked breakfast was really nice and very filling a little pricey but your on holiday treat yourself.Overall a very enjoyable and memorable stay would definately stay again.Thankyou for making us feel so welcome.

title: Yotel
body: Purchased an overnight visit through Groupon for my husband and I to do a getaway weekend. Very clean, contemporary hotel. The Yobot was really cool and interesting to watch. Rooms are small, bed IS very uncomfortable, as stated in other reviews. If this would be an IKEA store as a hotel, this would be it. An FYI, there are three Cadillac Escalades parked out front that are for the use of people staying at the hotel. Something we were unaware of. Charges start at $25 and up depending on where it is you would like to go. Good price through Groupon, although I don't believe we would visit again as I would wish to stay in a more roomier room!

title: Best stay in NYC definetly!
body:
The hotel is very well located, very close distance to Times Square. Walking distance to many places in Manhattan. The room I stayed in has a beautifull free view from NYC. I could see many buildings including New Yorker and the Empire State. It's all about being young (even though I'm getting older...). Beautifull people from all over the world everywhere in the hotel. Staff helpfull. Never mind for the fact that the room is small nor that it doesn't have walls between bedroom and bathroom. (The most common complain I previously read from other guests...) It doesn't really matter at all, unless you're buying an assembled delta wing or don't feel confortable with the person who stays with you in the room, if anyone.
I really reccomend Claudio's Pizza, about 500 feet from the hotel, just crossing 42nd street, same side. Best pizza outside Brazil, ever!

title: Cool hotel !
body:
We stayed in this hotel in Januari 2012. The looks are great, the room are cool. There is a free breakfast (muffins and coffee) just to start you up. Nice bar with great cocktails. There is a asian restaurant inside too. We didnt eat there.
As i mentioned the rooms are cool. The staff is helpfull. Contact the hotel if you want a taxi from the airport. Its a nice car with a helpfull taxidriver. 
We would go again there.

title: swag
body: this hotel is really cool. the music is really nice, the staff is very helpful. they have the best muffins served at breakfast! the cabins are clean, and the beds are comfy. i'd stay here again!

title: Great hotel...Great experience
body: The staff at Yotel were outstanding. The rooms were great and the view was outstanding. The staff went out of their way to make sure my stay was perfect. Dom Lendjel went so far as to come back and check with me to make sure everything was to my liking. Will definitely stay there again.

title: Brunch on 4th floor
body: We came here for brunch and it was amazing. The decor, atmosphere and drinks were great. Hotspot in NY definitely worth the trip.

title: Great for the money.
body:
The hotel is nice. Its got a great location. Close enough to Times Square, but just far enough away so that its not crazy busy all the time. Basically in Hells Kitchen so there are so many food choices you will have a hard time deciding what you want. I used groupon for almost every meal to help me decide and get a good deal. Tons of places deliver to the hotel as well. The M42 bus stops right outside the hotel and gets you across town to TSquare, Bryant Park, Grand Central, and 5th Ave in no time. Also, a plus not to be overlooked is having a 24 hour CVS right outside the door. You don't have a ton of room to store food/drinks or snacks in your room so being able to go to the CVS and get whatever, whenever was really nice. The Halal cart right outside the door is great too. The rooms are small, but very efficient. You really can't beat it for the money. Free wi-fi and a simple free breakfast were good to have. The wi-fi was not very strong, but it worked. The Galley is also great. There is one on every floor. We used the hot chocolate and espresso all the time. It was great to have. The only downside is the comfort of the bed. They are nothing but an organic pad on a hard wooden surface. Its cool that they slide up and down to give you more room, but the "mattress" is not much more than a down pillow-topper. 
Overall, a great hotel for the money. You really can't beat it.

title: ...decent cheap place to stay if all other options have failed...
body:
With a cheap room rate for a Saturday night ($145.00), my girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel on a very cold and wintery day.
Pros:
-Location-any place for that price in Midtown can’t be beat.
-Cleanliness
-Design-very 2001 Space Odyssey-expect a bigger version of those pods that the 
-Japanese business class stays in during the week so as not to miss any work. 
-Showerhead-just great, like a heavy tropical rainstorm, spent way too much time in there. 
-Looks like a great 4th floor outdoor bar which we will be visiting when it warms up. 
Cons:
-When the weather is warmer, that bar is going to be a madhouse, and noise will be a problem.
-small, very hard bed (which is your sofa until you need it).
-Staff-nonexistent until you get to the 4th floor, and then it’s 1 person who is less than thrilled to help.
-very small towels, no extra blanket, no ice machine on the floor. 
-no door between the sleeping area and the toilet-a thing sheet at best. 
Need a cheap place to stay in mid-town, this is it. But I won’t be staying again

title: Great value, great location.
body:
Me and my husband came here in feb 2012. Hotel has a great location 10 min walk to times square. The staff are really helpful when checking in and mission four are too. The rooms are small but have everything you need. Only down fall is storage one for your suit cases (no where to put these, ours were in the bathroom) second is for your clothes, two small drawers which my undies went in.... and three hangers.... which for a girl is bad enough let alone my husbands shirts and so forth aswell. 
I think this hotel would be more for couples and adults rather than children, i may be wrong but this is the feeling i got. (especially on a sunday afternoon in the Dohyo bar at around 4pm till 7pm its like a night club and have to go past this when leaving the hotel or going up to your room.)
High light is the shower very big and very spacious. The bed is electronic will go from a 
"sofa" down to a bed great space saver. 
All in all lovely hotel would recommend and stay again.
Wilst in New York you should visit a toy store called FAO Schwartz. In there a workshop called Muppets wotnot workshop, where you can make your own muppet choose the body eyes, hair nose and outift there brilliant!

title: New York Virgin!
body: This being our first trip to New York city I highly advise a stay at Yotel if your looking for something a little different. The staff are charismatic, knowledgeable and exceedingly helpful. The hotel is spotless and fun with its high tech gadgets. Great if your traveling with teenagers. Accessible location with most attractions in walking distance. Great morning muffins!

title: My 30th bday in NYC
body: The Yotel is fantastic, new, modern, clean, helpful and sooooo jazzy. With their electric folding beds for a comfy couch in the day, to their iPod doc under the TV to play your tunes and the Galley on each floor to make a brew or coffee and ice dispenser. Everything you need for a good bas to set off on your travels around New York :)

title: Outstanding
body:
This hotel is the best I've stayed in in NYC. Ultra modern, comfortable, perfect location and very reasonably priced. 
They had a minor hick up this evening when I arrived, and couldn't activate their proximity room keys. Within 10 mins I had been upgraded to a room with a private balcony, as well as two food vouchers. The front of house staff went out of their way from the minute I walked through the door.
This will be my first stop every time I come to NYC now, well done Yotel!

title: Great Stay
body:
Hotel is a ten min walk to Time Square and Port Authortity Bus Terminal which has a subway stop for getting aroung town. 
Staff are friendly and willing to help or let you get on with checking in and out if you know what your doing. We were greeted and wished well by lobby crew each time we entered and exited the hotel and also got help hailing a cab in the pooring rain with crew member opening his umberella for us to stop us getting wet while getting into cab. Excellent!
Room is clean and modern looking as is the whole hotel and was cleaned by maid service daily to a good standard. TV in room has loads of channels to flick through, the bed is interesting being electric and moveable but importantly it is comfortable and when moved out into room does not completely block walk way. 
Bathroom area is good and clean and although can seem odd with no door to shut out from rest of room does have a curtain to slide accross for bit of privacy if wanted. 
Would advice you ask about up coming events in hotel or use the free computers with internet access in the mission control area which will have this info as there can be some good stuff going on in the evenings here. 
Did not try and food here so can not comment on that but overall very pleased with our stay here and would recommend it as a good clean comfortable base with good helpful staff to use while you go off and explore New York.

title: Great New Property
body: I have to say the Yotel far exceeded my expectations. I expected cramped quarters, the rooms are by design, small, yet so well layed out that it feels much larger. The amentieis are awesome, staff was busy yet friendly. I've found a new home in New York City.

title: Awesome!
body:
My partner and I stayed here for 5 nights! The location and the price was great. Yotel has a great feel and the service was spot on. Our only regret was we missed the Sunday brunch, we only caught the last 1/2 hours and it had a great atmosphere, the music was great!! We met the owner of the hotel who kindly recommended places to go around new York in which we did. we were delighted because they were all great! 
A memorable trip!

title: Great location, very comfortable.
body: Easy walk to times square and subway stations. Room is very well sound proofed. We spent most of our time touring, having a small room was no issue at all. Happy hour bar service was pretty poor, interesting how some one can ignore you when they are standing right in front of you. This was our 3rd trip to NY, I will return again to this hotel next time.

title: minimalistic best
body: 1. Heated towel rack, 2. espresso/ coffee on your floor 24/7, 3. great food choice and price in Hell's Kitchen, 4. two blocks to Hudson River, bicycle rental and Manhattan cruise, 5. great subway and bus access, 6. largest cafe terrace in Manhattan to hang out, 7. close to Broadway shows and Birdland jazz club, 8. great bed, 9. iphone/ ipod dock

title: Amazing hotel
body:
Just back from a 7 night stay and cannot recommend Yotel enough! I had read reviews before booking and was aware the rooms are small... But I was surpised to find our room was actually bigger than I expected. Even with the bed down there was plenty of space to move around, and the holes under the bed are a perfect size for suitcase storage. The coffee machine in the galley is great - I know some people prefer to have tea/coffee facilities in their room but for us, the short walk to the end of the corridor was no problem at all. The muffins served at breakfast are absolutely delicious as well.
The hotel is easy to find and well located for transport links, food and drink, and of course Times Square is only a short walk away but far enough to be away from the big crowds. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the whole hotel was clean and well maintained. We would definitely return!

title: Very Affordable in a Prime Location
body:
I previously stayed at the Yotel in London Gatwick and was pleasantly surprised with that experience. Thought this would be a great experience for my 3 sons while in NYC as I didn't want to stay with family. 
This Yotel is centrally located to everything; Times Square a few blocks away, JKF 20 minutes by car, 24 hour CVS across the streets, loads of restaurants and the subway. 
We had standard rooms on the 26th floor. The room was bright with a great view, very clean, hot shower with great pressure, and enough room to move about and the beds are the most comfortable beds. The price was just as great at $129/night. Parking garage at the Yotel is $39.00/night. The rooms are sound proofed very well from the NYC streets. Didn't hear a honk, until I opened the window.
Overall, definitely would recommend, felt safe, great price, good food, very clean, funky and modern ambiance and the staff was excellent especially Simone at Mission Control.

title: Excellent place to stay in NYC
body: Our group of seven gals on a weekend experience to NYC LOVED the Yotel. It added to our NYC experience. We enjoyed the atmosphere, the friendly staff, and the overall accommodations! The gallery was so nice to have in the evening when we returned to the hotel--a cup of hot chocolate on a cool evening! There were several eating places near the Yotel--walking distance. We walked to the theater, subway, Times Square, etc. The group all stated they would return to the Yotel. Although the hotel advertised the rooms were compact--they were excellent. The features that were new to us, no check in desk, the beds, made the experiences even more fun! We thought we were the only ones in the Yotel--so quiet. When we returned late at night--we were pleasantly surprised by the security outside and inside the Yotel. No additional charges for the gallery, printing of boarding passes, etc. Thank you Yotel!

title: Cool Hotel, great location
body: We stayed at Yotel for 6 nights on our first trip to NYC. The location is very convenient to Times Square and Hell's Kitchen. It is very funky and different. The staff were all very knowledgeable and friendly. The place is very clean and tidy at all times. The only real downfall is that the other guests seemed intent on slamming their doors at all hours. Soft closers on the doors would be nice. A door on the toilet room would be bonus too!

title: Fantastic Hotel
body: The hotel cannot be faulted, great location, reasonable charges per night and spotlesly clean. Have stayed in several hotels in NY but the Yotel is the best. The rooms are small but compact and have everything u need. Staff are very nice and helpful

title: If sleep is not a priority...
body: The Yotel is hip and modern and cool and everything else you've been reading here. The rooms are small but well organized. I definitely would have gotten claustrophobia if staying here more than a day or two. Luckily we only stayed here one night. I say luckily because it was impossible to sleep! First of all, the bed which looks really neat is hard as a rock. I like a firm mattress but this was more like sleeping on a slab of marble. No way to get comfortable in that thing. Also the noise is a problem as we could hear every time someone came in or out of their room, which was constantly all through the night. You can also hear everything going on in the halls...lots of talking. There are many nice touches and the staff was terrific but I found myself wishing I could go home in the middle of the night....which I definitely would have done if I didn't have plans for the next morning. But I don't think most of the guests were here for a good night's sleep.

title: Yuck
body: I appreciate the concept of this hotel and thought the modern twist on things was fun. It wasn't very clean though and they didn't clean once while we were there (2 nights). We splurged for the terrace that came with a jacuzzi and when we got in the room we found out that the jacuzzi wouldn't be turned on and filled with water until next month. Little disappointing. The club that the lobby floor is on transforms into a night club that's certainly fun while your there but didn't expect to still be able to hear the music when I got to my room, four floors up. Overall, great location and decent price but I wouldn't go back.

title: Yotel, the Best!
body:
Oh, wow! I don't know where to start. I was a little skeptical because I had read reviews that said it was noisy, rowdy, small, uncomfortable, and so on. My experience was totally different. Mind you, we are a mature couple who traveled with a 17 year old and two 20 year olds. As we entered, we were greeted by a couple staff members. It was an experience. There is no traditional hotel lobby at Yotel. It looks as if you are stepping into a club. They quickly took our luggage and took us to FOUR. That is the fourth floor where there is a small reception counter. The super friendly girl, helped us get both rooms on the same floor, both with great views, and way before check-in time. The room was immaculate. It was very modern, European-style. We have traveled to many European cities before, so we knew what to expect. It is small, but there is enough room and cubby holes for everything you need. There is a room in every floor where you make yourself a fresh cup of coffee or tea-free. There is a soda vending machine as well as a water one. At night, the place is full of life. The lobby-FOUR-turns into a club. If you want to be part of the action you can, if not, no one bothers you, nor the music interrupts your activities. We were there during St. Patrick's weekend and the place was full of people celebrating.
The bathroom,as people have said before has no door to separate it from the bedroom, but it does have a curtain. There was no need for one. 
I recommend this hotel for those who like things that are different. For those who don't care about luxuries or extras. This hotel has what you need. Oh, location....EXCELLENT!

title: Modern Atmosphere and futuristic cabins
body:
This (Y)hotel offers everything you need for an trip to NY. The rooms (cabins) are small but clean and nice furnished. With free Wifi and the opportunity to connect your phone to the TV you can enjoy your time. 
Brackfast is simple but if you have additional wishes you can order lots of things a la carte.
The terrace is amazing - you can enjoy just a drink or even a nice dinner...
Furthermore: it is just a few minutes walk to Times Square and Broadway.
Over all we can recommend this hotel!

title: Practical
body: Small but practica rooms. Agree, a door to the bathroom would be a plus. Walls rather thin... can hear your neighbor...Staff very helpful. Quality of bedding and linnens very good. Clean room Great location. Would strongly recomend more security in every floor at all times!

title: Great surprise
body: It was clean, great location, great value for money. I was surprised at what we got for the amount of money we paid and the staff was friendly. The rooms are small but well laid out the only thing I would say that could be a little better would be a door in the bathroom other than that it was fantastic

title: A great, if somewhat pretentious, hotel experience
body:
For a business trip to NYC, I booked two nights at the Yotel. I'd previously seen the hotel listed before and thought about coming here with my wife, but we ended up at another property.
I think, all things considered, we would have done better staying here. For openers, my base rate was $199 per night for a small room, via Priceline. Secondly, while the room was small (think Eurosmall), I found it to be laid out perfectly, with plenty of room for my needs. There are a number of touches here that gave my room far more functionality than I might expect from other, more costly places:
 • The bed raises and reclines, much like a hospital bed. This enables you to sit up in the bed, without propping 17 pillows behind your back, and allows you to comfortably work at night, or in the morning.
 • There's a flat-screen TV built into a wall-mounted unit directly opposite the bed, with an iPod jack at the bottom of the unit.
 • A small desk is located immediately to the right of the bed with two AC outlets. Two goosenecked overhead lights are built into the wall behind the bed.
 • While there's no closet in the room, hangers are provided with a clothes rod that juts out from the wall to the left of the bed. It's well placed, and unobtrusive.
 • The bathroom flows directly off the sleeping area, with separate areas for sink, toilet and shower. It's located by the window, but you have the option of drawing sheer or opaque window covers.
Now, if you stay here, you need to get over the fact that this hotel is über-sleek, über-kitschy and über-pretentious. For instance: 
 • Purple neon outlines the hotel....excuse me, Yotel....as you drive up.
 • There's a Tumi- designed robot in the main lobby that stores your luggage. No bellhop. 
 • Your room is not a "room." No, my friends, you stay in a "cabin."
 • Likewise, your front desk is not a "front desk." It's "Mission Control." 
 • The TV can be framed with mood lighting, either yellow, orange, or purple, by working a combination of two light switches to the left of your bed.
 • If you're the overly modest sort, the shower/toilet area will leave you aghast. Yes, you can close the door to the toilet. But it's a glass door with white linear splotches Same with the shower. There are two sheer white modesty curtains that you can draw to block the view of the entire bathroom area.
Fine. But you also get free muffins and coffee in the morning. That's a nice touch. And they're good muffins...not the mini-muffins you see at other hotels.
All in all, I'd definitely stay here again. It's a great location, great accommodation (once you get used to the quirks), and a solid value.

title: space age gem
body:
my husband and i spent a long weekend in new york over the st patrick's day holiday. on our previous visit, we stayed in a radisson hotel- which was ok, but nothing special. on this occasion, i decided to live a little dangerously and book the yotel. i was intrigued by the description on the internet, and it looked funky and interesting. we were not disappointed. i could not recommend it highly enough. the staff are polite and extremely helpful. the hotel itself was stunning. it is just off theatre row- less than a 10 minute walk from times square. "mission control" - ie reception is on the fourth floor- where the bar, restaurant, terrace is. there is free internet access there too. a free continental style breakfast is served there every morning- muffins /tea / coffee . there are tea / coffee / hot chocolate facilities on each floor of the hotel, together with ice water and fridge.
the room ( or pod), was state of the art. hi tech enough to make us laugh- but not too gimmicky. there was a queen size bed- very comfortable, which can be moved at the flick of a switch to move closer to the wall to give you more room during the day. there is a flat screen tv / big double shower cubicle etc. all new, sparklingly clean .....
take the airlink bus from the air port. it will take you on to your hotel if in manhattan. it costs $15.50 each way. the nearest big station to the hotel is the port authority terminal. you can also access times square underground from there.
we went to the MOMA, natural history museum, chrysler building, the empire state building at night and took the circle line cruise on the hudson and east river. go at night- the lights of the city are beautiful. invest in a city pass for $89 each. it allows entry to 6 tourist attractions - and is great value. the weather is very mild at the minute, and we walked through central park / past the dakota building on the way. 
a highlight of the trip was seeing a show- wicked at the gershwin theatre- amazing. 
a great restaurant is smyth and wollensky's steakhouse. expensive but worth it- and lily'ss bar and restaurant which serve tasty, reasonably priced food. 
bring walking shoes- a lot of the city is easily accessible on foot. cab's are not too dear- but don't expect the cab drivers to necessarily know where they are going. the subway system is great for getting to the financial district / wall street area- or ground zero- if you wish to see it. the 9/11 memorial itself is fully ticketed and you must get your tickets in advance. they will give you a time etc to be there at.
a fantastic trip!!!

title: Funky Cold Medina (started bad then got good!)
body:
My wife and I booked a weekend getaway through Travelocity and got a good deal at this hotel. We go to NYC to get a city fix once or twice a year and have stayed at every type of hotel from the Women's Republican to the Waldorf Astoria. We are in our mid 40's and though this hotel might be fun. Overall, it is a very clean, very European feeling place. We arrived around noon and were able to get right in our room. The premium cabin is really a closet, but hey this is New York, right? It seemed fine because we were not going to spend much time in the room anyway. The problem started at night when we got back. From around 2 am to 4 am there was a party next door. A very loud party. Picked up the phone to call the desk and it rang twice. THen dead. That was repeated for about 30 minutes before i got dressed and went down to "Mission Control". I spoke with the front desk person who said my cabin number before I could. She said that she could hear me but my phone must not have been working right. (so did you think of sending someone up to check with me since I called 5 times?????) Anyway, she called security, Elvis came up and cleared them out and everything was quiet. The next morning, clearer heads prevailed and we were upgraded to a new room. WHAT A DIFFERENCE! This room was HUGE! We had a terrace and a hot tub and a regular size bed. The rest of the weekend was great!
The location is nice, though don't get fooled that this is near Times Square. It is a full three blocks from it. 
This is definitely a young hipster hotel, I couldn't see my parents dealing with the open bathroom and shower, though it was fun for us. A solid weekend.

title: Design place!
body:
We spend 2 nights at YOTEL and we are very pleased. The hotel is very design and have un good uniformity in all the places, from the "mission Control" to the Bar and the Room. In fact it is not "room" but "cabins". The name is appropriate because it's smallbut well thinked and functionnal... in addition to have a nice spaceship design. There is no fridge or coffemaker inside the cabin but every floor have a small kitchen with a fridge and self-service coffe and hot chocolate.
It's 3 block west from Time Square, count 10mn to go walking. Hell's kitchen is just above with a great choice of restaurants.
And obviously there is the robot at the entrance to store your luggage. Very funny!

title: Surprisigly awesome!
body: Yotel was great. Easy check in at 10 am on day of reservation. Room was small but clean with modern amenities. Traveling with my son, we got the cabin with bunk bed which rocked. The lower bunk was a queen that was a craftomatic which adjusted to your needs. The galley on the floor had fridge and free coffee etc. Great location just a few few blocks from times square but away from the madness. My 16 yr old son loved it. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: We loved this funky place. We loved the 'help yourself galley' that offered coffee and teas when you want them.
body: The hotel is close to Times Square and the hotel is very funky. The beds were hard and I mean hard, so ask at the front desk for a foam topper. Other than that we loved the whole experience. They have restaurants and outdoor seating on balcony and a neat bar. Everything is a funky purple glow!!!!! Rooms are nice size. We had the Queen bed with the two bunks for our two children. They have a beverage galley with fridge and microwave. You just help yourself. It was a great experience!

title: A glimpse into the future
body: We stayed at Yotel for 3 nights. The hotel is well located and has a futuristic feel (including the cool luggage storage robot in the lobby). Check-in was smooth thanks to the help of one of the helpful bellmen. Our room was small but the modern and well thought out amenities and facilities helped it seem bigger than it was. The adjustable bed was definitely a quality addition. The galley was useful as well. My girlfriend fell ill on our last night & morning there, but Mission Control was kind enough to allow us a late check-out. The bellmen downstairs and on the 4th floor were extremely helpful & we appreciate their assistance in storing our luggage and helping us get a taxi. Suppose the price could come down a bit considering the size of the rooms, but overall a great stay.

title: Cool stay at yotel
body: Great spot to get to anything . Hip place to go have drinks and food . Just a fun place to visit

title: Great vibe hotel
body: Fun futuristic hotel, really for younger people. very clean and close to time square.

title: Very nice stay at yotel
body:
Design of the room was optimal. Next time I would try to stay at yotel again. Everything we needed was there and was well working. 
Also the service was good and always someone was there to answer questions.

title: Top notch
body:
My other half and I stayed here for 4 nights and have to say that we very impressed. The hotel was so well planned out, clean, had a great vibe and the staff were incredibly friendly, nothing seemed like too much trouble although there was 1 incident where we were left waiting.
We ordered food from the restaurant (really good and fairly priced) to eat in our room and were told they would call us when it was ready. After 30 minutes and no news we went down and were told its just come out and I was about to call you, despite the ticket showing it ready 15 minutes before. 
Shame she had to lie but this was such a minor incident in what otherwise was a fantastic hotel. Strongly recommend it to all.

title: Yotel New York a Fun, Friendly and Funky experience
body:
We recently stayed at the Yotel in NYC for three nights to celebrate a friend's birthday. We found the Yotel to be an incredible experience. The rooms are not huge - they are not meant to be. Everything is compact - including the bed that is like an automatic futon, like a hospital bed only fun!
The staff is extremely helpful and friendly, the rooms are clean and you really can't beat this location.
All in all a great experience and would definitely stay here again!

title: Excellent stay
body: Great location and staff very helpful. I was happy with my stay at Yotel and i will stay there again. Close to every good places in NYC

title: excellent... but might be a bit too hip for some
body:
Shared a room with a girl friend for a week of relaxing and shopping. Very happy with the experience for the most part, and quite affordable given the quality you get.
Location: Excellent. At 42nd street/10th avenue, the hotel is a brisk 5 to 10 minute walk to Times Square, and there are SO many amazing restaurants around. Highly recommended are Kodama Sushi (45th/8th avenue), Shake Shack which are both about 5 minutes away. Nook is a little bit further away but you MUST go there for brunch.
The Times Square subway is 5 minutes away, so it's really easy to get around town. We walked quite a lot as well, which we enjoyed.
Staff: Very friendly, helpful and they know their stuff.
Rooms: We had a double cabin, and it looks exactly like the pictures on the website. Not very big, but it's enough space for two girls and an obscene amount of shopping bags, which is saying something. The bed is electronic and we had a lot of fun moving it up and down... though it does remind me of a hospital bed. Plenty of light, had a gorgeous view of the sea from the bathroom window, great shower.
Pantry: For some odd reason the pantry was hotter than a sauna, but you get ice, water and free coffee, and there's a vending machine.
Hotel itself: Very trendy. Its theme is space and the cleaners call themselves cabin crew... a bit weird but you get used to it. Lots of purple, sleek designs and fast lifts. Guests are quite a mixed bag, but lots of young people.
BUT....
Noise: I arrived at the hotel at about 10 pm on a Saturday. When I stepped out of the lift on the 4th floor lobby, VERY LOUD club music hit me like a brick wall... not the best thing considering I was exhausted and was looking forward to some peace and quiet. I can't imagine how loud the rooms on the lower floors will be, but thank God we were on the 23rd floor and didn't hear a thing.
Another thing... the same night, we were awoken by what was apparently a fight between two girls and a guy at like 5 am. It was a bit scary as there was a lot of angry yelling and we heard a girl say 'let her go! let her go!' We rushed to call 'Mission Control' and didn't get through the first couple of times... the whole floor was probably calling and it was sorted out in about 15 minutes. Nothing like that happened again but we always locked the door at night just in case.
So overall, I really enjoyed the hotel, service was excellent and it was always nice to get back to our room at the end of the day. Some minor problems with loud music and party people milling about on the weekend, but that's just in the 4th floor lobby where the lifts to the hotel rooms are located, so it's easy enough to forgive.

title: great!
body: We stayed 4 nights in Yotel. Check-in was really easy, we were immediatly helped. Check out was the same. Our bags were stored so we could walk a last time in NY. Rooms super clean. Small but it doesn't feel like that. Breakfast muffins were good, and the free drinks in every galley were definitly a plus! For a next stay, i would choose Yotel again. It was great !

title: Great location, interesting concept.
body: This new hotel is very clean and well run. The rooms are called cabins and they are very small....there is glass sliding door to the bathroom, a large screen tv on the wall and a bed that is similar to a futon (there is a button on side of adjacent desk to lower bed). There is a small room on each floor with an expresso machine..you can also make hot chocolate or tea. My only complaint is that even though the rooms are well insulated from outside noise, there was no insulation from the hallway noise..we could hear everything in the hallway loud and clear.

title: "Unique"
body:
Visited my daughter in New York...and decided to try a different hotel.
 After reading many reviews, selected Yotel.
 When arriving, you can't miss it...especially at night! The purple lighting outside sets it apart.
 Afraid I didn't ask the gentleman who assisted me with check-in his name, because he was very helpful and courteous. (If it helps Yotel, he was tall, with salt and pepper hair..and a nice accent. :)
 Anyway, after he showed my how to check in, he directed me to the next floor where the actual manned desk was.
 From there I went to my room. To be honest, the rooms are very small...and if you're claustrophobic, you might want to look elsewhere. But I found it to be charming...and interesting. Having to push a button to extend and retract the bed was fun...no closet space, but there was a hook for hanging your clothes.
 Not a big fan of the doorless restroom. I stayed there with my daughter, so there weren't any awkward moments...but I could see this being a little uncomfortable if I had traveled with a friend.
 Enjoyed the break room, where coffee and tea were always available...and thought it was entertaining that there's obviously a club on the premises. Since I stayed on the weekend, there was quite a crowd going into the club through the lobby, but employees checked our key cards to make sure we were guests. That made sure no strangers were randomly roaming the halls.
 I would use Yotel again...it was in a fairly convenient location...only a few long blocks away from Times Square. And there's a grocery store nearby, if you don't feel like selecting a restaurant...but then, that's part of the NYC experience!

title: Close to everything
body: Efficient and helpful staff, close to Times square but realistically in Hells Kitchen but no drama there as only a short walk, food on Four restaurant some of the best we had during our stay although the drink prices are quite high. Big thank you to the guys in lobby area who go above and beyond helpfulness, at check in to hailing cabs and for recommendations . For some great views spend a little more on the corner cabins as they have plenty of space and our one was right beside the galley area so getting a coffee in the pj's did not seem out of place, we found on an Irish site www.getabed.ie and prices were very reasonable but remember there is a city tax to add onto final price at check in

title: Not the best.....
body:
I've been to NYC many times and know it can be small and expensive. But this place is very small, we have the one room w/bunk, there is no door on the bathroom. Also, it's on 10th ave, which is a little out of the way, 2 avenue (longer blocks) from the subway. Service isn't the best either, some people are very nice, others seem to have an attitude. Nobody would clean our room either till I called, granted we'd wake up a little late, 10ish, but hey, we're on vacation and they never came back to clean it later in the day when we were gone. 
Would not recommend it....

title: Fantastic place to stay
body:
Very clean and staff was amazing, really helpful and nothing was too much trouble.
Loved the quirkiness of the hotel and cabins were just what we needed.
Good to be able to come back after a busy day sightseeing and link to the wifi to share pics with family members and chill and enjoy a drink.
We made use of the little kitchen on our level and loved the hot chocolates when been out in the cold.
Defo recommend the hotel to friends and family and also want to try out the ones in London.
Although just out of Times Square, i liked being able to come away from the square and also being closer to true NYC.

title: one of the best hotels ever!!!
body: i can honestly say this mite be one of the best hotels ive stayed at in a long time i have no complaints. i would defiantly stay here again and recommend this hotel to others. we also bought the new york pass in advance...very easy to use.

title: Outstanding hotel, great room and service
body: I have stayed in many hotels in NYC over the years and I can't remember a nicer experience than Yotel. Great service, affordable price, super clean room, very modern decor and efficient room distribution. I will definitively stay there again. This place really rocks!

title: Thank You Yotel.
body:
I can't say enough about this hotel. Being Irish, we went to New York for St Patrick's weekend and although the city was alive and crowded the Yotel Hotel handled the hoards of guests with ease and convenience. Self check-in and check-out makes it extremely fast and easy.
All hotel rooms in New York are tight on space but the Yotel handles this with a convertible bed that turns into a couch at the touch of a button. Fantastic idea for more floor space during the day.The galley on every floor is a fantastic idea as it offers more amenities than any in-room service and the coffee & hot chocolate are lovely. The complimentary muffins (great selection too) & hot beverages at breakfast are fantastic for starting your day and carried us to lunch time.
We dined in the Japanese restaurant and i can't say enough about how tasty the food was although one should order approx 8 dishes between two to really appreciate the variety of tastes and textures. The hotel is less than a 10 minutes walk down a straight road from Times Square which makes its a perfect location. 
The staff are amazing and very helpful. After checking out, I arrived at the airport to realise that one suitcase had been left behind and the Yotel staff got one of their drivers to bring it to me in rush hour traffic and I still caught my flight on time. 
To finalise, you would be mad to stay anywhere else in New York.
Thank you Yotel for a fantastic holiday. We'll be back.

title: Everything you need for a short stay in Manhattan
body:
I recently returned from a stay at the Yotel in New York with my girlfriend and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. 
The location was excellent, a couple of blocks away for the 42nd st Port Authority which connects to most of the major subway lines. The muffins for breakfast are adequate and the free coffee is great but I'd recommend the Westway diner, a block away on 9th Avenue.
The rooms are clean and just about the right size for a short stay however for longer stays you may find yourself wanting more space especially if there are two of you, for a sole traveller the room size would be fine regardless of the length of stay.
I never had the chance to try the hotel bar/restaurant unfortunately. The bar was more of a nightclub of a weekend which might not appeal to some travellers however noise could not be heard from our room which was directly above on the 14th floor.
The staff were attentive and helpful at all times.
Overall I'd deffinitely reccomend the Yotel and would stay there again.

title: Fun in the Big Apple
body: Great hotel, modern clean and helpfull personal. near timesquare and two blocks away from the subway. Relax atmosphere. The room is fully equipped.

title: Fancy hotel close to Times Square
body:
Sleeping at Yotel is an experience: starting from the check-in machines in the lobby, and passing through the robot that organizes your luggage in cabinets, the fourth floor where you can find a concierge, an asian restaurant and a nice terrasse, and finally to the "cabins". The "cabins" are a concept of small spaces where all the things that you need are organized in a very ergonomic way, with the goal to save space. By the end, you have a small bedroom, but it happens that it is very comfortable, with an incorporated bathroom in it. I recommend you have a look at the site to see some pictures. 
Beside this, the hotel is well located, at a 10min walking distance from Times Square. The hotel offers you free access to coffee machines 24h/24h, and a basic breakfast with fresh muffins and coffee. 
I really recommend this hotel to travellers that want to explore the city and want to stay in a nice and modern hotel in the centre, but don't bother too much about the size of the room.

title: Very good atmosphere
body: I spent 5 days in NYC and I can say that Yotel was one of the good memories that I have from NYC. The crew is efficient and the service is great. Everything is faster, check in and check out. The modern decor and atmosphere are the key points. I definitively will be back again.

title: Very different and it works
body: Great value, good service, the queen size Cabin was fine for one person for a couple of nights, but if staying longer or traveling with my wife would want to upgrade to the king size. Restuarant and bars have a good vibe, service very good, breakfast was good.. A welcome change to the Marriott or Hilton chains . Can't see this place working for families though.

title: Nice Hotel For The Price
body: Yotel is a new hotel in the theater district. It is about a 10 minute walk to many of the Broadway theaters. So, if theater is your thing, this is in a good location with tons of restaurants between the hotel and the theaters. The hotel is very modern in design, and is, for the most part, very comfortable. Many reviews have commented on the small rooms ("cabins"), but I did not find this to be a problem because the rooms are laid out very well. Also, I was by myself. The open shower is not as public as other reviewers intimate. The only criticism I have is of the bed. The bed reclines to a sleeping position from a sitting position (which I did like). However, the bed is very hard. I mean like a board. I found out upon check out that you can request an extra pillow top for the mattress. By all means, do so! Also, make sure when it is time to go to sleep, that you leave the bed somewhat inclined; do not lower it all the way. It is much better that way. All in all, this hotel provided me a nice clean, quiet, and affordable respite from daily activities. (Stay on a high floor to avoid street noise; I was on the 25th floor...what a great view!) This is not a place for small children.There is a lot of activity on the fourth floor at night (nightclub).

title: Great Hotel
body: We stayed 4 days at the Yotel and found our experience great. Since the minute you walk inside the crew greets you and are very helpful. You Check in is on the computer and it takes one minute. We stayed on the 23rd floor and our room had a great view. The room was clean, comfortable and the beds were great. The room is a cabin style so they are not spacious and big but for New York City; they are very nice. Ultra modern and very clean. Great value, great service. Short walk to Port Authority and about a 15 minute walk to TimeSquare. Two blocks from the hotel there are great restaurants. The 4th floor has music, bar, computers, and restaurants. The staff is friendly and super informative. We requested fresh towels everyday and we got them within 5 minutes of requesting. Our rooms were cleaned everyday. There is nothing negative I can say about this hotel. The only con I could think of is the bathroom does not have privacy. Its got a white curtain that separates the bathroom from the bedroom. We enjoyed our stay at the Yotel!!

title: Awesome for those who love to have a good time! Party Central!
body: We loved our stay here. Great venue!!! Looking forward to revisiting!

title: Yotel
body:
The hotel is new and modern. The corner room was excellent: clean, bright, great view
Our room was handicap accessible. this meant that the shower was large, stand-up (no tub) and not separate from the rest of the bathroom (no shower door or distinction between shower floor and the rest of the bathroom floor -this left the entire bathroom floor wet). The other bathroom issue in this room (though not a problem for me or my guest) was the bathroom door. It was a large sliding glass panel hung from the ceiling. it had some decorative squares on the glass but did not obscure the view by any means. Also, the glass panel did not "seal" it only covered the opening, so, there was no sound sound damping either.
I don't know if all the corner rooms are this way, but it wasn't an issue for us.
If you were in a wheelchair, this would be a perfect room

title: Yotel?... YO YES!! Great hotel in a fab location!
body:
Stayed here from 15th March to 30th March so 14 nights. Wasn’t sure what to expect as read mixed reviews on here. I was very impressed and thoroughly enjoyed my time here.
ROOM - Cabin style. Bed can be converted into a sofa and bed at night. Myself and my boyfriend found it very comfy and I am a fussy sleeper and I slept great. Good choice of TV channels, lovely smelling shower gel to use, plenty of storage (even for 14 nights worth of clothes) free safe and fantastic view! Room was cleaned everyday. Free galley on each floor serving lattes, cappuccinos, mochas, teas and water with ice machine available all in room cost. Asked for a higher floor room when checking in and ended up on the highest possible on the 27th floor, well worth it for the views!
LOCATION - 3 blocks from Times Square. Approx 10/15 min walk. Bus stop right outside hotel on 42nd Street takes you right across town and stops and every avenue. Brilliant places to eat on 9th and 8th avenue. I would recommend Southern Hospitality if you want an all American meal and Smiths bar on 8th avenue 44th street for a lovely New York strip steak and karaoke and cheap drinks on a Tues night. Plenty of takeaways nearby and we were fine to take food up to our room.
STAFF - Couldn’t have been more helpful and friendly. Greeted on arrival and every time we existed and came back we were greeted with a friendly smile and a hello. All the staff were fab couldn’t fault them at all.
HOTEL - It is a funky modern hotel with a really cool vibe about the place. I can see why it may suit some but not others but I really liked the concept of the place as its nothing like anywhere I’ve stayed before. There is a nightclub there that you can go in for free on Saturdays. I didn’t as I didn’t want to. It obviously got busy there in the nightclub and bars because of this but it didn’t bother us as the rooms are far away enough from the noise. There is a lovely terraced area with a bar which in the summer I can see getting busy but looks like a really nice place to be.
OVERALL - I would DEFINETLY stay there again without hesitation. The location was great and the hotel even better.

title: Very Clean and modern, good location
body:
I spent quite a lot of time looking through reviews of NY on here and elsewhere too. Yotel got good reviews and was well priced (for a NY Manhattan hotel) at £135 p/n, inc tax (beware all hotels, as everything in NY, have a marked price and tax is added to this, Yotel were upfront and showed this charge , but it'd be better if they (USA) included VAT as we do, annoying when you get to cashier and it's always a few dollars more! You could get cheaper but only marginally (as far as I could see) and what really swayed it was all the reviews seemed to say CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN! I had reserved a room in a small Chelsea guest house but when I went back the reviews for that were less good than I remembered and I had no en-suite, although room had a shower. That room was only £25 cheaper than Yotel and I'm glad i moved over. So...
I liked the location (10th Av at 42nd Street), really easy from the airport (air train and one subway ride to within a 5 min walk of hotel), and 9th has become restaurant central since I was last in NY and so you have plenty of food choices nearby and it's a 20 minute walk to Central Park. The room looked EXACTLY like the room on the website, which is nice and the white linen and towels had that new feeling. The shower great, the room has a bed that remotely folds down for a full king size bed and then you can also have it lifted up so it's more like a day bed , good for reading and makes the room more spacious. All touch of a button. Lots of pillows and good quality shampoo and gel, the safe is nice to have, free Wi-fi and I could see uptown NY skyline from my floor-to-ceiling window and to the left the Hudson river. All good. They say breakfast is included but this consisted of unlimited muffins and tea or coffee. Nothing else (no juice, bread, nothing, unless you wanted to pay from the menu). On each floor they have a kitchen and it has a fridge and microwave, as well as a water/ice machine and a coffee machine. This is really good and actually made nicer coffee then you'd get in many delis. 
One review said the staff were inattentive, I found them really helpful but you have to ask, you login on the computer and the luggage storage for your last day is great - everyone seemed to take a picture of it. If you like hotels where you are very aware of the staff then I can see the Yotel approach could be jolt - you could check-in, have breakfast daily, check-out and store baggage all without saying a word to staff. I quite liked this, I felt as though I'd rented a small apartment rather than being very aware of being a guest. Coming and going feels anonymous, again some people might not like this. I did. 
Room gets cleaned daily and again I have to say I find it hard to believe you could find a cleaner room. It's very modern, moulded plastic and glass, with purple mood lighting if you want it and you have an iPod dock for music.
If I was making another trip to NY (boy do I wish I was!), then I'd definitely check out Yotel again, but I think I was particularly happy as I got a good price - they do an early booking no-refund/cancellation rate, which is the one I took advantage of, so if you are at all unsure of your exact dates, or your dates are subject to change, then do be careful. They use a c/c to secure the full amount but you are only charged on check-in (all on touch screen computer, but nice staff there to help if computers confuse you). If you take the flexible booking then it's more and so how competitive it would then be I couldn't say. 
I heard no noise from the rooms around me, except in the hallway coming and going. Didn't get in way of sleep, though the noise from next door's shower was really loud, but there's only so long a person can shower for and so you just have to tolerate it a few minutes. Considering you couldn't hear any other noise then this is a really small gripe. The rooms aren't huge but it's NY!
There is a restaurant, bar and terrace on the 4th floor which is also the start of the hotel, so you walk in ground level and check in on the computer and then take the lift to 4th and then another lift to your room. I was on 15th with great views, I guess the higher up you go the better the views (it went up to 25 floors I think)... I don't think it matters which side your on, you'll have uptown, the Hudson river of downtown views, all equally good in their way. If you get allocated a room near the galley (kitchen), I'd consider asking to move. I wasn't but each time I went to the galley for coffee or water I thought of the people in the rooms either side...
This is a very modern (if Apple did hotel rooms...), clean hotel centrally located. I think you'd be hard pressed to find a room of this standard anywhere near as affordable. Staff are there if you need them but the hotel caters to people who aren't put off by a touch screen login...I'd definitely tell friends to check out the Yotel website and you'll probably work out if it's the hotel for you from their site.
(Trade Centre memorial very moving, get a free ticket in advance online or be at the 9/11 Memorial site at about 9.15 to bag an entry ticket for that day. Also, take the subway over to Brooklyn, walk around the beautiful houses (Truman Capote "Breakfast at Tiffany's" lived at 70 Willow Street), have a coffee and cake and walk down to the riverside walk which has breathtaking views to Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty and then walk across the Brooklyn Bridge to Manhattan. Brilliant afternoon (all this takes a couple of hours and is free (except coffee and cake!). A highlight of my trip.

title: Excellent
body:
Very interesting hotel at 10 mns from Time Square and 5mns from the Subway, well located!
Nice service, very polite and open minded personal. 
Everything you need to enjoy your stay in New York

title: Great Hotel
body: A great experience from start to finish. Excellent staff. We had 2 rooms booked and were on different floors, we didn't even have to ask to change them, the staff offerred to do this and within minutes we had 2 rooms practically next door to each other. The galley on each floor was excellent, the coffee and hot chocolate tasted so good that you would never have thought it was out of a machine. The staff could not do enough for you. Security is great as you need a room key to operate the lift and their is a safe in the room. The hotel is well situated for times square and many attraction. I went with teenagers and they loved the hotel especially the robot that stores your cases. The complimentary selection of muffins is great and many breakfast palces are within a short walk away, try al fresco just 2 blocks away...they will even deliver.I highly recommend this friendly hotel.

title: Good location
body: Recently spent 4 nights at Yotel and was very impressed. We were on the 25th floor with great views! It's a very modern hotel and the free wifi on the 4th floor is very handy. The rooms are a fair size, clean, comfortable and were cleaned every day. Loved the huge TV screen too! The toilet/shower are ok but make sure you know your partner well! There is a galley on every floor where you can get free tea/coffee/chocolate. Also a vending machine for coke, water etc. The staff are very helpful and friendly. I must admit that I was surprised by the price of the drinks in the bar though. My husband had a beer and I had a vodka and coke and it came to $20, which I thought was quite steep. Apparently its "the area"! The hotel is about a 10 - 15 minute walk from Times Square which is very handy. Feel free to ask any questions.

title: top location, top hotel!
body:
Staff were very helpful from the start to the end of our holiday. Great concept, rooms although compact are not cramped and we had a great view of Manhattan. 
Location is ideal for exploring the city! highly recommended.

title: Fun Concept, a little too much
body:
I travel to New York City twice a year and I always try to stay at a different hotel in a different part of the city. I chose Yotel, because the images and concept looked and sounded good and it was basically in Hell's Kitchen a neighborhood I wanted to walk around.
Getting to Yotel was easy. I got off the E train at the 42nd St. MTA station and walked 3 blocks down 42nd street to 10th Ave. Upon my arrival I was directed to a terminal like at an airport to check-in and was offered assistance by one of the friendly doormen/bellhops/whateve special name they had for them. 
Once you check-in and recieve you RFID room key you take an elevator to "four" where "mission control" (basically a front desk) Dohyo and elevators to the "cabins" (the rooms). In this elevator you have to scan your keycard to be able to access the floors. This is done because on "four" is a dance club on most night and keeps non-guests from accessing the floors. Most of the time I was in the elevator taping my card to the sensor and nothing. A lot of people during my 4 night stay were having this issue.
The room was of course small, and I knew that going into this stay, but it is laid out nicely and the room is really functional. The matress as stated in many reviews was like a futon typ matress, or one you find at Ikea. 
The free wi-fi was great and fast.
My room was not cleaned very well the next to last day I was there, the bathroom area was not touched, the garbage was not emptied only the bed was made.
The location was a further walk then I would have liked. The closest subway is the MTA terminal and if you don't want a to pay for a cab to travel thruought the city you're going to start your trip from on of the Times Square stations.
The price per night was all over the place. A low of $146.50 to a high of $263 for a Saturday night. For what you get in the room and the location I thought is was a little high. I could've had a room in the Times Square area for that price at a larger start rating with more amenities.
I the galley area on each floor contained a microwave, free purified water and ice, and a free coffee and tea. There was also a refrigerator that was based on the honor system of people not stealing anything from there.
I liked the concept of the rooms, the location is OK, but good if you want to explore Hell's Kitchen, and the rates were all over the place each night and that was with a "March Madness Special," which is not something I knew when I booked off their website. Those words appeared on my invoice at check out.

title: Fantastic, modern hotel in a great location
body: A very modern hotel in a great location. Rooms are very clean with comfortable beds. Staff are friendly and really helpful. We really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely return and recommend to others.

title: Fun Modern Hotel
body: The Yotel is is a modern hotel with compact comfortable rooms with excellent staff in a good location being 10 minute walk to 42nd Street Subway and 15 from Times Square. The double bed converts to a sofa style seat at the touch of a button for watching the large TV. I would recommend the food which is Japanese in style and good value if you get it at the bar between 5-7 pm, if a little limited in choice. Main menu is reasonable in the restaurant and has a larger choice.

title: Great hotel (but not for the budget traveller)
body:
We stayed here for a total of nine nights and didn't regret it at all. Check-in took all of two minutes (everything's automated) and a very nice doorman showed us up to our room and explained how the hotel worked, from the free wi-fi to the free daily breakfasts. 
The location is great too. We were pretty much in Hell's Kitchen, which was a temporary relief from the bright lights of Times Square. It's also easy to catch a cab around here. 
The rooms are like pods - everything there is functional and is laid out to make the most effective use of space. Some may feel it is a little cramped, but hey, you don't want to be spending most of your holiday stuck in the hotel room. We loved the shower gels (there were two - one for day, and one for night), the selection of channels on the HD TV, as well as the very fast wi-fi.
They dole out the same muffins every morning, so if that gets too tiresome for your palate, take a short walk to the Market Diner on 11th Avenue between W 43 and 44 St. 
We hardly used the subway, but our cab fares to touristy places like the Meatpacking District and SoHo came up to about USD$10. 
Pros: Friendly staff, free wi-fi, state-of-the-art rooms, the galley, easy check-in and check-out, took a Megabus to Boston one day and the pick-up point is right beside the hotel
Cons: The walls are pretty thin, so be careful what kind of noises you make in your room. Also, because the toilet is exposed to all in the room, I wouldn't advise those who have been friendzoned to share a room here.

title: Too much neon and overpriced
body: This is a tourist hotel. Do not go here if you are there on business. You will be annoyed after a minute on the 4th floor. The elevators are packed and stop on every floor. It's excessively neon. I'm still fuming at the price. Microscopic rooms. Grr. Don't go.

title: Fun, very clean and shiny and good value
body:
I recently stayed at Yotel for a three night business trip in NY and it offered comfort and good value for money.
It's a fun experience and doesn't blow the travel budget and i'm likely to stay again in the very near future. I'm in my late twenties and really enjoyed the quirkiness and party vibe, but I wouldn't necessarily recommend it to some of my older clients.
It isn't in the coolest part of NY, but it's not out of the way either and easy to get to places of interest - I used cabs a lot and it was always very easy to pick up a taxi outside the hotel.
The staff are friendly and although the rooms aren't huge, I think that they are good value for NY. If there is more than one of you in a room, you'd probably only want to stay for a handful of nights (which is what most people tend to to in NY anyway).
Will certainly stay again and have recommended it to friends and colleagues.

title: Spring break with teenage daughter
body: We stayed 3 nights the w/o March 12. I was visiting with my 19 year old daughter. We both absolutely LOVED the hotel. It was perfect location and the vibe of the hotel was great. Staff was very efficient and friendly. Appreciated the free muffins in the morning to get us going. Rooms were perfect for the 2 of us. Super clean which I am adamant about when traveling and very modern. Loved the heated towel rack. Perfect spot for quick getaway. Only con is the bathroom but no worries for mom and daughter! :)

title: Fabulous!
body: I was a little hesitant to stay at the Yotel after I heard the rooms were tiny. I was so please to find out how easy and comfortable this hotel was! I stayed for the New York Auto show and the location is perfect if you are going to the Javits Center. You can walk to a lot of nearby restaurants / shopping. It was overall one of the best stays I have had in New York. If there will be more than one person staying in the room I don't know if you will be comfortable, but for one person, you can't beat it. The bar was super fun also!

title: Good for girls trip...wouldn't stay with family
body:
Stayed here for a girls trip to NYC. Cool modern hotel. Very clean, but rooms were small. I read people saying the beds were uncomfortable, but i didnt think that was the case. Great terrace and nightlife. I also thought it was a good value for the money.
I would recommend for a friends trip but probably not for families.

title: Great hotel but slightly pricey
body: Everything was great for this hotel - location, cleanliness, comfort, convenience. Except the service is fair (not very understanding manager), only muffins provided for breakfast (for the price you pay, should extend proper breakfast, even motel that cost USD100+ p/night provides breakfast) and the Galley's coffee machine wasn't fixed for a long time making it inconvenient for customers.

title: Good hotel at Times Square
body:
It was a very good hotel. In the middle of NYC. 
We just had to walk 10 or 15minutes and we were directly in at the Broadway. 
The employees are very friendly and helpful!

title: Very Clean with outstanding service in an eclectic atmosphere
body: As we arrived earlier than expected a crew member assisted us in check-in earlier. They were kind enough to upgrade us to a room with a view of the Manhattan Skyline. We were also assisted with Yobot so we could check our bags which can be done before or checkin or for the day after checkout. The galley was awesome, water, cappuccino, and expresso. There might've been hot cocoa but I didn't notice. Although the premium queen cabin was small it was perfectly cozy for a couple like us who was celebrating our 19-year anniversary. I am not too happy about offering this lovely review because I want the place to stay CLEAN and hope that guests will keep the place perfect so all can experience.

title: Not Terrible, But Not Great
body: We stayed at Yotel for 5 nights starting April 5. It was our first trip to New York, so I don't know how the Yotel compares to other New York hotels, but I was not overly impressed. There were good things and bad things though, of course. We were travelling as a family and the bunk beds were a great option for us. It was also very clean and quiet (on the 16th floor) and we really liked the galley on each floor with the coffee machine. Free lattes are a great perk! But they aren't kidding when they say the rooms are small. There was only one chair in there for four people and it was very difficult to spend any extended amount of time in our room. The bathroom situation was also interesting. It was a beautiful big bathroom with a waterfall shower head, and there was a door on it, but there was no closing or locking mechanism on the door, and it didn't go all the way to the ceiling, which made for some privacy issues. Our biggest problems were with the beds and the concierge. The mattresses were thin and as hard as rocks. I've stayed at hostels with better quality beds. Apparently there were mattress toppers available but that information wasn't given to us until the day we checked out. It would have been nice to know that at check in, rather than check out. Because of the beds alone, we wouldn't stay here again. And the concierge, Ari, was horrible. He told us there was no point in trying to get Broadway tickets and the TKTS booth because there wouldn't be any available, and that we should buy tickets from him instead. This was a blatant lie made to try to sell us overpriced tickets from the hotel. We also tried to make dinner reservations at a particular restaurant and were told that the restaurant we wanted didn't take reservations, but that we could get reservations at a restaurant HE suggested. Another blatant lie. We declined and tried to walk in to our restaurant of choice and were told we couldn't get in WITHOUT a reservation. We also asked him where we should go for brunch. He made a suggestion and we asked him to make us reservations. He then looked at us like we were crazy and said "Oh there's no way you'll actually be able to get in there". Why make the suggestion then?! Overall, he was utterly unhelpful bordering on outright rude. The rest of the staff were very nice and helpful, though. The location wasn't terrible, but I thought it was out of the way; at least a 15 minute walk from Times Square and kind of out of the way. It wasn't the worst hotel I've ever stayed in, but I would not recommend it unless you can get it for cheap.

title: Exciting few days in NYC
body: It was great fun staying at the YOTEL! We loved the location, the friendly staff, the design and the positive vibe it had!

title: Futuristic! Fun! Fabulous!
body: My daughters and I went DC and New York for spring break 2012! We had a wonderful time!!! Yotel was a great experience for my girls first time to the big Apple. We walked everywhere! Why? because Yotel was that close to everything. Time Square 2-3 blocks away?? The room was clean comfortable and really cool!!!! I love it and will probably stay there only when I return to NYC. The service was great! The 4th floor was out of this world! The Bar, the restaurant, the club, the terrace! Its something for everyone! Well worth the money spent which was not much for everything you got!

title: Will stay again!
body: The hotel itself is cute, very compact, perfect for a night in the city. It's very clean, which is a super plus. Also the staff is amazing, super helpful, and very friendly. For this reason alone I would stay here again!

title: excellent hotel
body: Excellent location, Clean hotel, Excellent service, Amazing room,

title: everything you could want
body: went to nyc for easter for 5 nights. absolutely loved yotel... check in was quick and simple to use.. key cards for lifts and very secure as you can only access your floor with your card key (be sure to swipe your card in elevator or you could be standing a long time. we asked hotel about an upgrade it wasn't possible but we did get a great room on the 21st floor with an amazing view!!! complimentary breakfast was fine but we only took it 1st day as needed something more substantial . kitchen was great for coffees after a long day sightseeing. rooms totally soundproof. didnt really like that the toilet didnt have a door its not very private. rooms cleaned every day. only used bar once during happy hour but found it very expensive so we did not drink at yotel. we sat at the bar yet they reccomended 15-20 percent waiting tip on bill for 2 drinks even though we weren't waited on.. only bad experience was being woken at 4.30 am for a fire alarm and a real life fire we were evacuated down the stairwell.. it cannot be helped and staff dealt with it wonderfully we were back in our rooms before 5am but having a nights sleep broken in new York is not a good thing. would have been nice to have been re inbursed or something else as a means of an apology but then again glad we wern't left to burn in bed.. over all had a great time at yotel even though it is just a base to stay, conceirge are very helpful but i would not book anything through the hotel as it is more expensive. check out team were great helpful, got out luggage and flagged down a taxi.

title: Loved it!
body:
As soon as you arrive at the Yotel, it's clear that you're in for something slightly different. At night, the neon purple frontage of the hotel casts a glow over the entire street and as you enter the revolving doors, you are struck by the lack of any reception area. The reason for that is very simple - the reception is on the fourth floor. Check-in is done on the ground floor by touchscreen computer and there are always plenty of staff around if you need help. As you enter the Yotel, you can't help but notice the Yobot (a fully automated luggage robot), but more of this later.
Take the lift to the fourth floor and you start to get a feel for the hotel. Reception is in front of the lifts (sorry, 'elevators') and it's on this floor that you'll also find the bar, dining area (where breakfast is served) and nightclub. The first lift only runs between floors one and four, so you now catch a second lift to your floor. In our case, this was the 25th. You use the swipe card you were issued with at reception to select the floor you want in the lift - just hold the card in front of the reader and it will automatically select your floor. The lifts are great - very quick and very quiet (and this comes from someone with a real dislike for lifts). On entering the room, the first impression is maybe that it's a little small. Everything's certainly very compact - the bed, for example, is on a remote control, so that during the day it's raised with the back up (great for watching the flat screen TV in front of you) and at night you simply press the button to lower it so that it becomes flat. The toilet and shower are not behind a closed door - there is simply a clear glass 'wall' that slides across, so probably not the hotel for any couples with major inhibitions, or perhaps for those in the early stages of a relationship. The shower is great - very large (large enough for two people, in fact!) with a good thermostatic control. The window to the room can be partially opened, but to be honest, you're in the heart of New York and even on the 25th floor, it's noisy - 24 hours a day. With the window closed, you really don't get any outside noise and if temperatures are high, all rooms have air conditioning which you can set to the desired temperature. The views from the 25th floor were great - particularly at night, and our room looked over towards the Hudson River.
My wife's main concern when we arrived was the lack of wardrobe/drawer space. There is no wardrobe as such, but two areas for hanging shirts/trousers/skirts, with hangers supplied. There are also a limited number of small drawers, but in truth, we ended up living out of our suitcases for the five days we were there. I was slightly worried at my wife's initial comment regarding the lack of storage space, but I have noted her comment on leaving the Yotel at the very end of this review, which may tell you a lot. There is also a safe in every room, which is free, so keeping money/credit cards/phones etc. in the room is no problem. You simply choose a four digit PIN and enter this into the safe. Just don't forget your PIN!
We were not expecting breakfast, so were surprised to find that there was a free breakfast everyday, between 7.30 and 10.00am. There is tea and coffee, as well as herbal teas and water. The only food on offer is muffins, but there are a variety to choose from - cranberry, blueberry, banana, nut etc. You can upgrade to a more substantial breakfast if you wish, but I've no idea how much this costs. To be honest, if you want a big breakfast, there are any number of diners around that offer good food at reasonable cost. I would recommend the Tick Tock Diner over on 8th Avenue (near the New Yorker Hotel). As you sit and eat your muffins (which are good), you'll notice the birdsong that permeates the air. This is piped 'music' and I thought it all just added to the 'quirkiness' of the place. There is proper music in all other areas of the hotel, including the lifts.
The location of the Yotel is excellent. Walk up 42nd Street and you are in Times Square in around 15 minutes. Walk down 42nd Street and you can be at the Hudson River in the same time. This is where the Circle Line boat cruises go from, so it's an easy walk to go and book your tickets for a trip that I'd highly recommend. If you turn right out of the Yotel and cross over 42nd Street, continuing along 10th Avenue, there are a few restaurants, but 9 times out of 10, you will probably gravitate towards Times Square, where as you would expect, there are restaurants and bars everywhere.
On every floor in the Yotel, there is a galley kitchen. You are free to access this 24 hours a day (using your swipe card) and there you have free iced water, tea and coffee (the machine will do hot water, Americano, Latte, Mocha, Hot chocolate, Chi etc. etc.), a fridge which you are free to use and even a microwave. There is also a drinks machine, with bottles of Coke and Sprite etc., for $2 each. This was something else we weren't expecting and it was really nice to be able to make tea or coffee anytime we wanted it. You can spend a small fortune on these things when you're away for a few days, so to have it included in the cost of the hotel is a real bonus.
The staff at the Yotel were always polite and helpful. The only issue I had was with the concierge who I spoke to about the Circle Line boat cruises. I knew there were 1, 2 and 3 hour options, yet he was telling a different story. When he eventually decided there was a 3 hour trip, he said this only ran once a day at 7.00pm. I knew this wasn't true as I'd spoken to other people who had taken the cruise during the day, so left it there, walked down to the Hudson River and booked it myself. On reflection, I guess he wasn't selling Circle Line cruises but those of a rival company, though I don't know why he couldn't tell me that. As the Circle Line dock is only a 15 minute walk from the hotel anyway, I would make your own arrangements.
We flew into Newark Airport. Before we left the UK, I booked a bus from Newark to NYC online (USA Coaches). For the two of us, this was only $54 return and if you do the same, you need to get off at the Port Authority Bus Terminal on 42nd Street (the buses also stop at two other places). From there, it's a very short walk down 42nd Street (i.e. away from Times Square), to the Yotel. Easily manageable, even with a couple of suitcases.
I must also mention the food seller just outside the Yotel (at the corner of 10th Avenue and 42nd Street). You will find these all over NYC and I'm sure they are all much the same, but if you want a quick snack, I would highly recommend the chicken or lamb gyros. Really tasty and only $4! The Yotel do not mind you taking food into the hotel, either.
Now for the Yobot! If, like us, you are checking out of the hotel in the morning, but not flying until later that day, then the Yotel will store your luggage for you. Or rather, the Yobot will, Just use the touchscreen to request a large or small bin, enter your name and a pin no., and the Yobot will pick up your cases and store them in the wall of boxes in front of you. You'll get a printed receipt with a bar code, Just scan this on your return and the Yobot will retrieve your luggage for you. At all no charge. In truth it would be much easier to give your bags to someone to store in a room somewhere, but where's the fun in that? It can only handle one person at a time, so try and avoid queues, but it's great fun and I guarantee that you'll leave with at least one photograph of it!
We loved the Yotel. It's fresh, it's funky and it really grows on you. It has a large gay following, so if this bothers you, then you'd best go elsewhere, but I would highly recommend it. The atmosphere is very friendly and the beds extremely comfortable and clean.
I mentioned earlier that my wife had a initial concern on seeing the room that there was not enough storage for clothing. She was a bit fraught about this as she likes to unpack and put everything in place before relaxing.
