It's true that there wasn't a lot of storage space, but then how much time do you intend spending in the room? We were out all day, every day, and shattered when we returned. Anyway, her departing comment was not something I'll forget and was very telling (especially if you know my wife). ''If we come back to New York, I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else but the Yotel.'' My sentiments exactly.

title: Good value for price and very clean
body: Very clean and fast internet access available throughout the hotel. There is what they call "the galley" on each floor, which gives the guest access 24/7 to complimentary coffee, tea, and ice water. A microwave is available there as well and you can buy soda through a soda machine. The personnel are friendly and helpful. Nice outdoor view from the 5th floor, especially at night. Perfect for petite people or someone on a business trip. The restaurant is pricey for the portions, but there are many nearby places to catch a bite. It is closeby to many shows, the movie theatre, cuisines, shopping, and the train station as long as you are "mobile," which most people are. For your convenience, there is a blowdryer, flat screen tv, and iron. Bring your own soap as their eco-friendly soap doesn't smell pretty at all. Would recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: Our stay at Yotel New York
body: It´s a modern, very clean and well situated hotel in New York. We loved the Lavazza coffee machine, we hope it will be there always.

title: Fabulous hotel!
body:
We stayed at the Yotel for 5 nights at the beginning of April, and we LOVED it! The staff are all very pleasant and helpful, and are happy to help you with anything you need. The room was small but had everything we needed. The bed was very comfortable and everything was spotlessly clean. Each floor has a galley, which is a small room with tea and coffee making facilities, as well as a microwave and fridge (all free!) and drinks machine. This was a fantastic facility and the coffee machine made lovely lavazza coffee! The fourth floor had a great little bar area, and the happy hour between 5-7pm was great value, with glasses of wine at 4 dollars (bargain!). The hotel was in a great location, too, taking roughly 10 minutes to walk into the centre of times square. Taxis were also easy to flag down right outside the hotel. 
I will certainly be staying here again when I return to New York, this hotel is perfect.

title: Great hotel within walking distance of many iconic NYC sites!
body: Having read previous reviews on this hotel for my first visit to New York, I thought it would be a safe bet. We were greeted in reception and shown how to check ourselves in, extremely hassle free and no hanging around! The first elevator takes you up to the fourth floor which is called 'Mission control' - this is where you will find the 'front desk', bars and restaurant area. Exiting on floor four, turning round a corner you access the main lifts to the rest of the hotel - we were on the 21st floor. The elevator was super fast and whisked us up to our floor in no time. Our room was as expected as I had previously looked at footage on YouTube. Yes it is compact, but we were not in New York to stay in our room! It was fresh n funky, the queen size bed was very comfortable. If you are staying here, make sure you are happy with the slight lack of privacy when using the toilet and shower - yes there is a screen for privacy, but you can still hear everything......Tea, coffee and water facilities were available on each floor in a Galley kitchen area at the end of the corridor. All in all, the accomodation was great for self sufficient travellers such as ourselves. To top it all, the location of the hotel was great for all the sites we were planning to visit. Highly recommended!

title: GREAT hotel for teens!
body: GREAT hotel! Lots of fun for teenagers. They even have "cabins" with bunk beds. Great view of the city, too. We loved the "galley" that was next to our room and provided expresso, etc. We also loved the efficiency of check in and check out. The "Star Trek" kind of theme was fun,too.

title: What a hotel?!
body: I have never stayed at a hotel like Yotel. The concept is really fantastic. I strongly recommend this new, hip, extremely well located hotel - and it wasn't even expensive!

title: HIP,FUN AND SUPER CLEAN!!!
body: I am in NYC at least 5 times a year for a week period - business related .I am a 36 year old traveled business woman, and hate unorganized and dirty hotel rooms, but when I had to book a last minute-budget conscious trip to NYC I found the Yotel on Priceline and thought I was going to get a DIRTY room since the price was EXTREMELY reasonable for the location. As soon as I stepped in the Yotel my jaw dropped. OMG what a cool place this it. But the WOW factor was in the cabins ( rooms ) Crisp clean white sheets, clean smell ,organic shamppo and body wash . flat screen TV and overall a very hip and fun atmosphere. Very moderne and the sfaff rocks! I would never stay anywhere else but the Yotel.. F-A-B-U-L-O-U-S!!!

title: Great location, Good Amenities, Fabulous Brunch
body:
Last weekend, I stayed at the Yotel NYC with my 17 year old son. Both he and I loved the fact that the hotel offers a "Bunk Room". (Mom got the bottom Queen bed, and he got the spacious twin bunk... great option.) The location is fabulous. Right on a bus line, one block from Port Authority Bus Terminal and Subways, and in Times Square's/Theater District's backyard. The room was extremely clean and well appointed. Every incidental was well thought out and usable. We had more towels in our cabin, than I've seen at a suite at the Marriott. Neither my son or I considered the glass enclosed bathroom a privacy issue. The curtains work well for privacy, and the bathroom was meticulous. (If you don't want to hear anything, dock your i-pod into the radio or watch HDTV while your companion is using the facilities... both amenities work great.) And another thing, the room is quiet. You don't hear noise from the hallway, your neighbor's room, or the street. The galley was a nice touch. The "hot drink maker" did run out of hot chocolate overnight, but there's always free coffee or tea. My major recommendation about the Yotel though, is the $35 for two hour, all you wish to consume weekend brunch at Doh Jo on the 4th floor... splurge a little. The food comes out in small plates, the drinks flow, everything is delicious, and the waitstaff are happy to help. The key here is to start with a bunch of hot and cold foods first, because the twist is the 2 hour time constraint. (If you attending a Theater Matinee like we were, get to Doh Jo at 11:15 AM... the set up is perfect to make a 2:00PM curtain... just don't have too many Mimosas.)
 My one caution to a traveler is that a 3:00PM check in is just that... 3:00PM. They may say they'll try to get you an early check in, but don't depend on it. If arriving to NYC earlier, just check your bags, and go enjoy exciting and energetic NYC. The awesome and fashionable Hotel, along with all the helpful Crew Members will be there when you get back... and so will your luggage.

title: Really Loved Yotel
body: We were graciously greeted and walked through the processes at every touch point. Something you would not expect at a trendy high tech hotel. We loved our room and the location. Hotel was full of international guests mostly Euros which added to the experience of visiting NYC.

title: Yotel New York
body:
My sister and I recently visited New York for our 21st birthday and stayed at Yotel. 
We absolutely loved the hotel, the room was comfortable, in a great location (10 mins walk to times square) and the staff was really friendly and helpful.
Despite the fact that the hotel hosts one of New Yorks popular clubs, according to our taxi driver Kanye West and Jay Z go there, our room was quiet and we had no trouble sleeping. Our taxi driver also told us that Adele stays in this hotel whenever she visits New York!! 
Each level has a room where you can help yourself to tea and coffee, so this was our first stop each morning! 
Our flight wasnt untill the evening so after checking out, we left our luggage in Yobot, this is a brilliant idea. 
Overall, we wouldnt think twice about going back to this hotel and really recommend it. :D

title: Trendy good located hotel
body:
We stayed in the hotel for 3 days with 2 teenager children and there is nothing to comment on this hotel.
great location, great food, spacious and modern rooms, nice ambiance,...
perfect for a stay in new York!

title: EXCELLENT EXPERIENCE! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
body: We arrived from South Africa after a very long flight and the crew member checking us in, said that check in wasn't until the afternoon. But when we said we had flown internationally, she immediately made a plan to get us into our room. I cannot recommend Yotel highly enough. The food in the restaurant was also superb. Very convenient to Times Square. The room was spotless with all of the modern conveniences you would expect. Service in general was amazing ... it was definitely the best hotel / accommodation experience we have had in New York (at a price that we could afford)! I would recommend an upgrade to the corner room / cabin ... amazing views!

title: Gotel Yotel
body:
Thank you, what a great stay. The hotel is under a year old and is clean and trendy. The cabins are not as small as you expect and are an experience to stay in. The bed is firm, which I like, however the staff did offer me the option of a under mattress. All the amenities you need are in the room, safe, nice body wash, TV etc. Each floor has and a galley where you can make as much tea and coffee that you want. 
When I arrived I was greeted by a friendly member of staff who helped me to check in. The 4th floor is the restaurant and club. I did think that the noise of this could be disturbing, however it wasn't, and it only added to the vibe of the place. It is close to Times Square and the subway.
The staff did their best to help you with anything they could, I would stay here again no worries

title: HORRIBLE BED I AM LAYING IN IT NOW AND WISH FOR A COT
body: As a business traveler this bed did not allow for one night's sleep. The bed retracts and extends with the push of a button, kind of like a recliner. I am actually laying in it right at this very moment, and I just heard the neighboring room's bed retracting through the paper thin walls. I cannot sleep on the mattress that seems to be made out of wood. There is a large indent where the bed folds on itself when it retracts which has made it difficult for me to sleep. I am not normally picky about my hotels or beds since I do travel frequently. I was not concerned about the small size of the room. I would be fine with it if it weren't for the poor insulation, noise level, and worst of all the very uneven, rock hard bed. Ps I weigh about 120 lbs, so it is not as though I am a huge person struggling with this bed.

title: WOW!
body: Great view, very nice and well design room, small but very good planned. Great staff, very much helpful, good recommendations. We had great stay!!

title: Cool High Tech Hotel
body: My daughter, I and two of her girlfriends stayed at the Yotel in NYC for her 13th birthday celebration. We loved the cool, space age design and hip feel of the hotel. The room was spotlessly clean and bright. However the hotel lacks some common amenities, like hair conditioner and lotion in the bathrooms. When I called for a disposable toothbrush, "Mission Control" informed that they did not carry any for guests. One of the beds in the room lacked a blanket although this was brought to the room quickly upon request. The outdoor patio and restaurant are beautiful (again with a sleek, Japanesse design) and perfect for lounging after a day of sightseeing. The Yotel offers a free continental breakfast with delicious muffins, but again some puzzling lapses in service, like no juice or plates from which to eat. This seems inexplicable for a hotel of this caliber and detracts from what otherwise would have been an A+ experience.

title: Yotel Times Square
body: Great Hotel Experience. Excellent style, great postion and stunning crew. The room looks small at the beginning but it's a fake first impression; there are a lot of spaces that can be used. Excellent wifi service (free). Absolutely recommended!

title: Wonderful staff and wonderful stay
body: Stayed here with my 12 year old daughter. She absolutely LOVED this hotel. The room was clean and big enough for the two of us. We stayed in a premium Queen cabin. The bathroom was clean and we were not bothered by any noise-- we were on the 15th floor. Each floor has a galley with hot tea and coffee, microwave, ice-- great touch -- The staff was exceptional. Everyone was friendly and helpful. My daughter wondered if everyone in NYC was so nice. Our room was not huge but it was exactly what we were looking for -- safe, clean, and pretty cool. Will definitely stay again--

title: Very nice hotel
body:
My uncle and I just spent 5 nights at Yotel and we actually liked it a lot. It's 5 minutes walk from Times Square, with everything you need around. The crew is very nice, attentive, helpful.
The cabins are just as shown on the pictures, very futuristic and original. The rooms are a little small for two people, and the bed big enough. 
In my opinion, this is a hotel perfect for the youth since there are a lot of parties going on in private rooms, there's always loud music being played, the staff is quite young.
They provide you with anything you need.

title: Small rooms but all you need
body:
Stayed at the Yotel end of March for five nights, the rooms / cabins are small but have lots of the latest innovations, a bed that moves back electrically, ipod station, flat screen TV and we had a view of the Hudson river. A robot will deal with your left luggage and an automated check in system, access to the internet and free printing, handy for those boarding passes.
The hotel was about a ten minute stroll from times square, close to the coach stop which brought from the airport. Breakfast was buffet style with cakes and pastries etc.
Good price, good position clean well maintained hotel.

title: NYC YOTEL
body: Service is quick. View is great on high level but room is very small. Would stay in their corner room again.

title: YOTEL Times Square.
body:
I stayed here with my girlfriend for 5 nights. We both thaught YOTEL was great! Check in was uncomplicated and quick. The crew on FOUR gave us any info we needed and directed us to our room on the 15th floor. Our premium Queen cabin wasnt the largest, but with the (rather fun) robo-bed folded, there is enough room (besides, its NYC, you wont use your room for much but, showering, sleeping and, well, you get it...). The aircon is quiet, WiFi is mega quick (and free) shower and bathroom is good. Some guests may not like the lack of a proper door/wall (its glass) and the "privacy curtain" between the bedroom and bathroom area, but its a neccesary evil to allow light into the room.
The hotel decor is pretty cool, running with white walls back-lit with neon purple. Loads of cool touches everywhere, even the turbo powered elevators, with 8-bit style music!
There is a galley on every floor with free tea,/coffee/hot chocolate, a shared fridge and microwave and soft drink vendor ($1), so make sure you have $1 bills when you check in, if you want a cold drink. The free breakfast muffins are ok, but a bit bland and boring. There is a CVS pharmacy, dunkin donuts, 7 eleven and a couple of pretty decent diners within a 5 minute walk of the hotel.
Times Square, subways and the Port Authority building are within a 10 minute walk along 42nd street. Also, for travel to and from JFK/Newark airports, there are express busses every 10 minutes from each terminal to W41st street (back of the port authority building) and vice versa. The fare is $15 each, which is cheaper than a taxi (JFK is $45 + tolls, Newark is $80 + tolls).
Pretty hard to find fault with YOTEL Times Square, its clean, friendly, quiet and cheaper than most nearby hotels but with a higher star rating!
RECCOMEND!!

title: perfect stay in an excellent city
body: very stylish hotel * perfect location * friendly staff * free lavazza-coffee and w-lan * big tv-screen with a lot of chanels * bed with interessing features * party if you want to...

title: Yotel - Stay April 2012
body:
Small compact rooms - what you expect in new york
Trendy bar and resturant
Easy check in and check out process
Clean and NEW
The cabins are really cool and I really enjoyed the area that we were in

title: excellent experience
body:
Me and my wife Cannot speak highly enough of this hotel ,Its situated in a great position of manhatton .the hotels amenities are second to none, and also unique making this a wonderful experience.
Has for the hotel staff we cannot speak highly enough of them in assisting us from the time we arrived right up to leaving. Also can we just say hello and a massive thankyou to (yousef) going to recommend you to head office many thanks mate .
TO all the staff keep up your outstanding work!!
MR AND MRS Keeting

title: Very funky
body:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights last weekend. We were a bit skeptical about the hotel when we booked it - we thought it might be a bit garish. We were very pleasantly surprised. There was a terrific atmosphere in the hotel. It really is as cool as it looks. The room was indeed quite small, bit was very comfortable and was well cleaned every day.
We made good use of the galley to make coffees and for ice.
The staff were very helpful at all times.
The location was perfect - just a short stroll Times Square. I really can't fault the hotel at all.

title: Fantastic hotel!
body: Great location (only 2 blocks from Times Square) with free wifi, free breakfast muffins, all-day free galley on every floor (with iced water and hot drinks including fantastic hot chocolate).

title: Perfect Stay
body:
Just came back from a 4-night stay at the Yotel Times Square. Yes, the rooms were small, but as may others have pointed out, it's what you can expect when you're in New York. What stands out is how clean the hotel is and most importantly, how helpful and attentive the staff is. Everyone from the check-in guys, to the staff on FOUR, to the guy that hailed us a cab was warm, friendly, and willing to go the extra mile to make sure we were happy. 
We never heard a neighbor, loved having coffee and water around the corner at all times, and really got a chance to relax in our room during our downtime. Quick WiFi (and free!)
Again, the rooms are small, but very well appointed with great uses of space (Hint: put your luggage under the bed). The glass bathroom really wasn't that big of a deal (draw the curtain, close the door and turn on the shower. Done).
We loved coming back and having the option to participate at club events on FOUR. Security was great too, they had the hotels up to the room on "lock", so you didn't have "wanderers" in the hallway.
The location of the hotel was perfect, with plenty of options to eat on 9th.
Finally, the Yobot held our luggage after we checked out so that we could still explore before our flight in the afternoon.
Next trip? Yeah, you better believe I'll be back at the Yotel!

title: Yotel became the highlight!
body: I stayed 5 nights at the Yotel April 12-16. I was currently on vacation with one of my friends. We came mostly for the NY Imats show, but our hotel experience turned out to quite pleasing. So much that some days we would get out of bed late just because we enjoyed the room so much. I really had no problem with the size of the room. So comfortable, the ipod jack in the wall.... omg we had our own party in there.Not to mention some of the nights there we did not even need to leave our hotel to party because we were already at the place to be. They even made sure no one made it on the floors where the rooms were located. VIP treatment!There was a galley on every floor where there was ice water and other beverages available. Free muffins and coffee and tea for breakfast. The crew was so helpful and polite. Not once did I enter and exit with out someone addressing me. Over all I enjoyed my stay and will be back at the end of this year for my next vaction. Keep up the good work Yotel!

title: New and clean!
body:
Some people might think this is a young person's hotel and granted it is very trendy with the weekend club, DJ brunch etc but there was a wide variety of ages of guests staying.
We were on the 15th floor and had no issues with noise from the club, traffic or other rooms! The room is perfectly laid out and makes great use of the limited space - it certainly feels larger than it is! I have stayed in similarly laid out hotels in Europe with the open-plan bedroom, shower, toilet etc and am fine with it although it might be a bit wierd for families and friends! The futon style bed was very comfy - granted it was quite firm as some people have mentioned but that it how we like it!
The free muffins and drinks are a godsend! Beforehand we had thought why would anyone use this with so many food options in the city but it was a perfect little start before heading out!
The Yobot was great for storing the luggage after checking out as our flight was not until the evening.
Recommended - we will be back.

title: Yotel New York
body:
The Yotel New York was a comfortable, unique and interesting property. The staff were friendly and efficient, the food in the restaurant was very good and the "cabin" was cleverly engineered to avoid any claustrophobic feeling from the small space.
The location is just close enough to Mid town attractions while being far enough away to give guests the opportunity to enjoy the city without feeling you are overwhelmed.
While this was a business trip I would also stay for vacation. The neighborhood is interesting and warrants further exploration.
All in all an excellent choice for any visit to New York.

title: Yotel Is Very Nice!
body:
We have been there last month!
We enjoyed the hotel because is really modern and beautiful!
The breakfast is ok!
The location is excellent because is 5 min next times square!
The service is very good and Dom is really kind!!
The only problem is the bathroom in the same room of the bedroom...they are divided only by a tent!
Next time we will sure come back!
Alessio & Marica from Italy

title: Clean, modern, nice.
body: Trendy New York hotel, I stayed there on business and found my little room perfect for relaxing after a long day at work. The restaurant has an outdoor terrace that is very nice on a sunny day. Food and drinks were a bit spendy, but all good. If you're looking for a spacious room, then this is not the place for you. The location was very handy for walking around if you want to be near Times Square. Would have been fun to stay there with friends to check out the DJ they had playing.

title: Small but nice
body:
Good location, small rooms (cabins) but practical built. Free small breakfast. All you need for a nice stay in NY. Helpful staff in the lobby - if you need some support. 
If noisy guests on the same floor pass your room in nigh ttime you might wake up. The door didn't keep out noice from the corridor. The public is most young - but even we up in the ages enjoy our stay.

title: Trendy, Clean & so different
body: We stayed there on April break and loved it. The staff was so helpful with any questions we had. It's in a great location if you want to see a broadway show or walk to Time Square. The breakfast is ok and dinner there was great. Rooms are cool looking with a terrific rain shower. I would stay there again without hesitation.

title: Friendly staff, Love the Yobot
body:
I stayed solo on an April Thursday night last-minute trip (for sightseeing, not business) and dropped my bags off that morning at 11am into the Yobot luggage storage until I checked in later that afternoon. The hotel staffer in the lobby was very helpful walking me thru the screens of the Yobot and explaining that I could also put my luggage into Yobot bin after checkout next day and leave it for several hours until I was going to be leaving the city by Amtrak. This is a great free service and you know your bag is safe since it's up on a wall where no one can get at it. If you have bigger luggage that won't fit in a Yobot bin like the lady in front of me they also take that and store it for you somwhere if you want.
Room was small but I knew that before booking and it had everything I needed anyways. I'm 6 feet 2 inches tall and I had no problem fitting in the queen bed. Room was extremely clean, cleanest hotel room I've stayed in anywhere. Booked thru their website the night before I arrived and was at least $200 cheaper than anything in the area, even hotels with lower guest ratings.
Great minor details such as being able to hook up your Ipod/mp3 player into the TV to play music through the TV speakers; simple alarm clock built into wall so not taking up space; nice lighted bathroom mirror; AC is on automatic sensor and kicks on within a minute or so of walking into the room; free internet/computer use down on 4th floor for people like me who are tourists and not on business with laptops; the galleys on each floor have a good variety of free coffee, tea, etc. I had the free hot chocolate and it was good. 
Staff was great, friendly and had answers immediately with any of the hotel or area questions I asked them. Wish I had another night or two to stay there and would spend more time on 4th floor where all of their activities are. Popped down there around 11pm and there was good music and a bar but plenty of more private seating areas if you had a few people with you. It was raining so the huge outdoor seating area wasn't being used. It's good also because the public is allowed into the 4th floor restaurant area but the elevators to guest room floors you need to swipe your room card just to be able to press an elevator button to get to a guest floor because of a chip in your keycard. This is better and safer than other hotels I've stayed in where people could get on a hotel elevator and be wandering around the floors.
I don't have any real negatives, the shower head could have angled back more for my liking but that's probably because I'm on the tall side and am used to the shower head I have at home.

title: Fun room, but very uncomfortable mattress.
body: Mattress felt like a pull-out couch in someone's den. Deal breaker for me--I wouldn't choose this hotel again. Small room, but efficiently designed and very clean. Good location just a few blocks from Time Square--close enough to the action, but not right in the middle of it.

title: Yotel Hotel - Great Value and Location for NYC
body: Yotel Hotel offers close proximity to Times Square, the Theatre District, a major subway station, and a busline. The service was excellent and the property was very clean and well designed. Checking in and out couldn't have been easier. The staff actually walks up to you to offer assistance, rather than waiting for you to ask for help. The room was small, but provided what you needed in an efficient use of space. If you're in NYC, you're going to spend very little time in your room anyway! My Queen room was less than $200 a night, and that's difficult to find in such a great location in Manhattan. You could take the 42nd bus to 5th Avenue for shopping, dining, etc. Oh - and coffee, tea, and an assortment of muffins was included each morning. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: Yotel Hotel Room
body: The Yotel was very clean, staff was helpful and friendly. The beds are a little hard, but got used to them after the first night... kinda like futons. Could have more counter space ... none in the bathroom .. but it is minimalist so it adds to that whole concept. Close to everything. We enjoyed our trip!

title: Modern + Hip = Yotel
body:
I travel alot and this hotel is very nice and clean. I love the whole hightech vibe this hotel has. I had a corner queen on the 25th floor facing the hudson. There are only one of these rooms per floor. Check facebook on occasion for a discount. I saved 15% using a code I found on face book. The club on the 4th floor was packed all 6 nights I was there. The room I had was plenty large enough for 1 or 2 people. Bag storage isnt a big deal. You can leave it with the Yobot or put it in your room. The Bed isnt super hard its about like a futon on the floor. Once you get used to it you wont notice it unless you have back issues.
In my review I have some positives and some negitives. It all depend on what you are looking for.
Now the good
+++++ The Yotel is super claen and very high tech...
+++++ There is a galley on every floor with free coffee and a ice machine. It also has a fridge
 To test the whole community fridge I left 2 cokes wih my name on them and they were
 never moved. I saw plenty of people leaving left overs in there. This is super handy..
+++++ Everyone who works at the Yotel is super friendly.
+++++ The view from my room is the best I have ever had in NYC
+++++ There is a CVS out front...Handy for snacks 
+++++ My room was next to the galley but I never heard anyone.Its not an issue.
And now the bad..
------ I wouldnt call it "Times Square" I mean you are a block away fom the Hudson. 
 Its in Mid Town West if anything. 
------ Its about a 8min walk to the closest subway stop. Its like 4 blocks east.
------ The "Rain Shower" is called so because its like you are trying to shower in a rain shower,
------ The sink doesnt drain the water out of the sink. There isnt enough of a grade on the inside 
 of the sink to make the water flow to the drain. After you brush your teeth the water
 hangs out in the sink. I felt obligated to coral the water and toothpaste into the drain.
 If I had to pour out a drink I had to use the shower drain.
----- There is a Subway sandwich place and a Food emporium close. Out side of that food is
 a block away. Papya dog and 99 cent pizza place.As far as a nice place you got to walk
 a couple blocks..
------ The restraunt on site is expensive. For breakfast I had french toast and a coke and it
 was $20..The dinner and lunch didnt aeal to me. I m a steak and burger kind of traveler.
If I can find a good deal I would love to stay here again. The negitives are far less than the positives. I am a sucker for gadgets and high tech. The Yotel is a must stay..

title: Modern & space age
body:
Stayed at the Yotel recently for 7 days.
It was only built in 2011 so as expected everything is clean & modern, a bit space age in fact. Not the usual style of New York hotels.
The location is in Hell's kitchen, about 10 minutes walk from all the hustle & bustle of Times Square. The closest subway station is part of the Port Authority bus terminal about 5 minutes walk away. It's nor right in the middle of everything, but still close enough.
Each floor on the hotel has a galley kitchen which you all share. It has a free coffee machine, a fridge, microwave & vending machine.
The rooms, or cabins as they call them are fairly small, but sufficient. Why would you go to NYC to stay in your room all day? They have an adjustable sofa bed, a good sized LCD television & a nice powerful shower (no bath)
We were on the 19th floor & you had nice views of Hell's kitchen & the Hudson river across to New Jersey.
It's advertised as 'bed & breakfast' The breakfast is just basically unlimited muffins, which are nice & coffee. You can order a full breakfast for a charge.
The Yotel also has a large roof terrace which I guess would be pleasant in the summer months.
We enjoyed our stay here & would definitely stay at this hotel again if & when we come back to NY.

title: Great Hotel!
body:
The hotel is excellent. It has a unique, modern vibe. The initial impact is slightly strange as you checkin as you would at an airport (but staff are on hand to make it easy) and then you go up to the 4th floor to the main lobby and access to the rooms. 
The rooms are really modern with electronic reclining beds. The rooms are cosy and comfortable - exactly what you need after a day stomping around the city.
This is a really accessible hotel, 3 blocks (10 minute walk) from Times Square and 2 blocks from Port Authority Bus Terminal and Subway (which gives you great access to the rest of Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens as well as Woodbury Common shopping outlets).
The breakfast buffet was good - a variety of muffins and yoghurt/cereals.If it's a nice day, you can take your breakfast out to one of the outside terraces. There is a also a galley on each floor, with complimentary teas, coffees and hot chocolate. 
There is a nightclub in the hotel (4th floor) which seemed lively (although we were always too tired by the end of the day to make the most of it!)
Overall, a very good hotel and would definitely recommend it

title: BEST WEEK EVER!!
body: Absolutely, amazing hotel! Very chic and classy. Great amenities, food, and customer service!

title: very good place
body: This hotel is wonderful and near Times square. The cabins are modern with beautifull view on buildings. Ask Emmanuel (member crew) because he is THE BEST and very friendly. The muffins at the breakfast are very goog ! We have loved this hotel and we will ask it at our friends.

title: They call them cabins for a reason
body:
Was in NYC for a weekend and did a search for hotels and ended up deciding on the Yotel. I've always been a sucker for 'techno-funky' hotels when it's for a short stay so the neon glow of the Yotel had me like a moth to a flame.
The hotel is on the edge of Hell's Kitchen, which from what I understand earned it's name a few years ago but certainly doesn't now. It's within walking (comfy shoe walking) distance of Times Square and Central Park (about a 30 minute brisk walk). The neighbourhood is quite busy and there were small indications of the local party teens mentioned in other reviews but nothing glaring. 10th Ave is a very busy street though and car horn honking is a virtual olympic sport in New York City in general. It did stay quite loud through much of the night and sleeping while not a real issue was a little interrupted.
The hotel has all the 'check-in process' of a Euro boutique hotel with initial check-in on the main floor where there's a robot arm to store luggage in a wall of 'lockers' if your room is not ready. It's a fully automated check-in system that has staff constant lingering around making me wonder why someone is standing over my shoulder telling me to type my name. There's a lounge on the fourth floor that is quite small and tame compared to Times Square hotels but still pleasant, if $12 rum and cokes can be pleasant.
The rooms are called cabins and there's somewhat of a cabin feel to the rooms. Our Queen bed cabin measured in at 170 sq ft. The bed actually reclines backwards to allow for extra floor space during the day. The shower is the 'rainfall' standing type without a door which always leaves me leery of slipping on exiting. Overall it's a fairly functional room if, like ourselves, you're there to see the city not a hotel room. There is a desk so it could be minimally functional for business travel but I wouldn't do it personally. There appears to be an option for a similar room with bunk bed options that suggest they can sleep 3-4. I can't personally see anyway that many people could co-exist in such sized rooms.
All in all a decent spot but there are far better values to be had, with much larger rooms, and half the price. Those hotels are a short train/cab ride from the city but they're not 'in Manhattan'. Didn't get any replacement toilet paper after the maid went through and it was two requests later before any arrived but no other issues.

title: Very good modern hotel
body: Excellent location, 5 minutes walk from Times Square, at 42 st so it's very convenient for transportation (Subway or train at Grand Central). The way of check in (kiosko), is curious and impersonal, but it's ok. The rooms are small but modern and has a great view. Bed is comfortable. The breakfast offered was poor. The ambiance feels good, there is a bar with a good offer of drinks, and a disco that moves on weekends. Very good choice.

title: YOTEL the boss liked it.
body:
Just spent three nighs there for business. I booked the rooms and my boss liked his room. It had everything you needed. Great shower. 
Its in a good location. Easy to get to everything. I would go back again.

title: Did I Just Book a Cruise?
body:
Stayed here for one night while on business. I chose this hotel because the event was at Yotel so I didn't have to go far after the party. Checking in was a little strange and inpersonal but I didn't mind it and I like that it was under 1 minute to get my key. When I first walked into my room, I practically walked into the bed. The rooms are tiny -- i guess that's why they call them cabins. The beds require you to press a switch so they unrecline but nonetheless, very comfortable. The bathroom is very tiny but modern and the view was really great. I decided to eat outside -- there was just no room for me to eat in my room comfortably. In the morning i had to call the front desk but here they call it "mission control" and I felt kind of ridiculous requesting "mission control". 
Location was not my favorite. As a native New Yorker, I like to be as close to the train as possible -- this was too far west for me (and way to close to the nutiness of Times Square).

title: Amazing Hotel, Horrible Brunch, and a VIP Concierge
body:
The Yotel is AMAZING! From the moment we got into the lobby to the day we left was just amazing service and experiences all around except for a few minor things.
We stayed there for 5 nights in the middle of April. I had been emailing the hotel for some information in mid-march, things like flat rate cabs from JFK to the hotel and back, also travelling with a group of for I had asked if our cabins could be side by side and on a higher floor as it was our first time in the city. I was emailed back saying to rest assure that my requests have been already meet, and that the inquiry about the flat rate would be passed on the concierge who would email me back with the information. I’m still waiting….
When we arrived at the hotel in the early afternoon around 1ish, we used the automatic check-in (super cool) but we were on the 9th floor, and not next door to each other (9th floor is the second lowest floor for guest rooms). Chris the bellhop on duty at the time came over and asked if we needed help and saw that we were on the 9th, and took up to the front desk on the 4th, and asked if there was anything available on the higher floor, we got the 27th the highest floor, services at it’s best.
The Brunch was 40-45 bucks a person and was all you can eat for two hours, sounded great!! But far from it we went at 2pm the place was packed, we were limited to 6 plates at a time, they are small plates and there were 4 of us. We also waited 45 minutes to get our second order, which came after our 3rd order, but only half of it. Stilling waiting on my meatballs…. so at the point 1hour and 15 minutes in, we had shared 2 salads, sushi, sliders and scrambled eggs (keep in mind they are serviced on tea size plates), then the service was rude when she asked us how everything was, and I said still waiting and she replied with “well, yeah, anything else though”. Not Impressed.
The Concierge that was working at 4-6ish on April 14th was a joke! We had asked him about good clubs to go to and he replied with, “ Umm, it’s hard for me to tell people because I only go to VIP clubs that are guest listed and so I don’t go to like regular clubs”
Umm clearly he does not know anything about the job title of a concierge!!!
The hotel itself was amazing; love the vibe, the hospitable staff, and the room. The rooms are spot less, small but perfect because really your in NYC how much time you really gonna spend in the room. The beds, despite many reviews I read, are very comfy, and I slept like a baby! The muffins in the morning were good too, but 4.50 for chocolate milk is kinda robbery. The city is amazing, and the dinner in their restaurant was great, over priced but a great service made it a great experience (the server gave us more incite about the city then the concierge). The Terrence was great, spent a lot of time there.
I will definitely come back to the Yotel! It is by far one of the best hotels I have stayed in. Not a huge fan of time square but love this place, I will be back!

title: Modern sometimes at the cost of functionality
body:
Wrapped up a weekend in NY, we stayed at the Yotel. The presentation and interior designs are pretty impressive. Its a pretty new property so the rooms felt new and clean. We stayed in a Queen two bunk room. The layout was comfortable and the view was impressive.
My annoyances with the room were mostly cosmetic but worth mentioning.
curtain controls are kind of hidden and not really obvious. 
The shower was large but there is no real division between the shower and bathroom floor so water gets out on the floor eventually. I always am annoyed with hotels that use this type of shower design, Its such a nuissance. Like even a small lip or drain along the edge would be great. Nothing is more annoying than going into the bathroom with socks and stepping on a puddle. Same sort of deal for the sink. Its a flat box basin, takes awhile for the water to find itself down the drain. Its mostly due to the design of the sink really. I'm sure the drain is just fine. 
I didnt like not having body lotion within the toiletries, there's two types of soaps to choose from but not one body lotion? Seems strange.
Also the bathroom doesnt lock. Not sure if that's just particular for this room but it would probably be an issue if i was bunking with a coworker or something. 
The highlights are, easy checking-in, you dont have to stand in line or deal with anyone, you just punch up your reservation on the self service kiosk and youre done, im a big fan of self check-in at airports so I love hotels that let you do that to check-in also, the rooftop area bar is great, the drinks are pretty good, pricey. But the view is fantastic, you get a feel for being in the big city.
I'd probably stay again if there was a good deal.

title: A truly unique experience
body:
The good things: The Hotel was clean, safe, quiet with good shower water pressure, a well functioning toilet and a firm (maybe a little too firm) mattress. Room rate included excellent flat screen TV, Wi-Fi, 24 hour self service galley which provided coffee, expresso, hot chocolate and a shared refrigerator and microwave on each floor. Free breakfast included good coffee and all-you-can-eat muffins (a $20 or more savings).
The unique things: rooms are very small, like cruise ship cabins. The bed doubles (somewhat) as your couch. There are nooks and crannies for storage areas for just about everything. The bedroom is by the door, with bathroom by the window (a reversal in normal arrangements). It is not designed for spending a lot of time in your room. A motion sensor turns on lights, heat, etc when you are in, and everythings turns off once you leave. Check-in and out is by computer, but there is always a helpful staff person available.
The not so good: No privacy in the bathroom (you hear what is being done on the toilet, and see the person sitting). No kleenex. The location (10th and 42nd) is really a good mile and one-half from Times Square, so be prepared to walk (it's a mile to the nearest subway).
This is a hotel for young people, although we enjoyed ourselves (late 60's). It delivers great value.

title: Yotel is like a good mix of IKEA and Japan. You get all you need in a tight place.
body:
Went to NYC for 5 days with my wife and had a most lovely time. The hotel has a good location being on the corner of 42nd street and 10th ave. Take a few min to walk over to where that action is on 7, 6 and 5th ave but no problem for us since walking is what we do all days.
The rooms are small but not in a direct negative way, you have all you need there unless you want to socialize with friends on the room as that would not be feasible.
The rooms feel super fresh and clean and everything was well maintained TV was big (32 inch) with lots of good channels (all in english) and WiFi worked great most of the time, some problems getting connected when too many tried to connect at the same time but no major.
We tried the hotel's tapas like asian restaurant one night and the food was really great! Small plates but everything we ordered could be shared for two and we ordered a total of 4 dishes + wine, drinks and dessert.
The only real things to think about or complaints would be:
The cabins for 2 have just a glass wall for the shower and WC and the rooms only window just outside (big window starting from the floor), as there is nothing indicating if this is a true reflective window having at least frosted the glass wall would have been a good idea since now the windows shades were left down most of the time. There is also no real door to the bathroom or the WC just a thin curtain so don't stay here unless you really feel comfortable with who ever you share the room with. Sound proofing is not only lacking from WC to room but there are also no sound proofing between the doors and frames so you can hear a whisper from the corridor outside and also noise from other rooms traveling through the corridor.
If booking through sites like expedia and possibly others this hotel will be shown as having breakfast included in price. The complementary breakfast is just coffee/tea with a muffin. So unless your ordinary breakfast is made up from sweets and pastries. You might feel a little let down by this on arrival.
Drinks in the bar are really over priced and the bartenders are friendly but not good. Drinks lack any sort of finesse and some where not even good. If the bartender have to wipe his hands after handing over a drink that got totally smeared down after spilling when mixing he could guess that his guest have to do the same thing and wipe the glass before serving it.
But all in all we had a wonderful time in NYC and this hotel served us well so I would recommend this hotel to any couple (that is not completely new) and I would definitely stay here again if not for the fact that I like to try new things.

title: Great, modern and comfy!
body: Stayed there for four nights because my original hotel was overbooked, they transferred me to Yotel and I couldn't be more satisfied. Great location, small room, but clean, new and with an amazing Hudson River's view. The only uncomfortable part is that there is no door between room and bathroom/restroom...only curtain..which is not very private at all! Excellent location..only 3 blocks from Times Square, but enough to be apart from the noise.. the hotel is impersonal, there is no people at front desk, everything is computerized, check in, check out... but with usual American mood you won't miss that at all! The upper floors are restricted to private parties, a lot of people (teenagers) coming and going..I wouldn't recommend it for family or senior couples..

title: Value for money
body: We had a great stay within walking distance of TimesSquare and the theatre district. The staff were extreemly helpful and we had a small but very clean, comfortable room with all amenities required for a stay in the city. I would highly recommend it as being great value for money and a novel high tech experience.

title: NYC Never Sleeps.
body:
We visited NYC for my partner's 30th Birthday. The trip had been a surprise from me to him and I'd emailed Yotel in advance asking for a room on a high floor, they didn't disappoint. 
We stayed here from the 25th Feb until 1st March 2012. I choose the hotel as my partner loves gadgets, and after looking at photographs of the hotel and reading reviews I thought he would love it and he did. Staff were helpful and accommodating. We never really got use to the time difference and so would often wake early in the mornings. This is when the gallery on each floor of the hotel comes in handy, as we would go make ourselves hot chocolate or a coffee. The rooms are modern. I never felt that the room was too small even with the bed out. I loved all the quirky little lights, storage ideas and décor; I felt that the most had been made of the room and space to create something different. The bed was comfortable and we weren't disturbed by other guest arriving back late at night. The Yobot is also a cool idea and fun making the hotel feel friendly and enjoyable, it’s definitely a talking point. All the staff working in the entrance to the hotel were friendly, wishing you good morning and helping with transport and directions if needed. 
The hotel is a few minutes walk away from Times Square which is busy and exciting especially at night. Close to the hotel is a diner called Theatre Row Diner we enjoyed breakfast here in the mornings which were large and set us up for the day we often didn't need anything but a light snack mid-afternoon. 
The hotel is in a great location for getting the subway to other parts of the city, as the nearest subway in a few minutes away at Times Square. We visited Downtown and I really liked this part of the city it seemed calmer which was a nice contrast from the hustle and bustle of Times Square. The city is also nice and easy to walk as well. Whilst in NYC we went to a New York Rangers Ice Hockey game at Madison Square Garden which was easy to find from the hotel on foot. As long as you don't stray too far from the beaten track NYC feels safe during the night time as well. During our stay in NYC we saw many of the great sights and sounds of NYC and Yotel was a great base for us. We would definitely without a shadow of doubt stay here again when we next visit the city that never sleeps.

title: Excellent hotel
body: 5days-4nights, everything was perfect, all you need is in this hôtel, Well located and everybody at the hôtel wants to help you. It was perfect, many thanks to everybody. You can chose this hotel, for me it's the best for the price. You will be at home and there's happy hours too! And don't Forget, there's the breakfast included.

title: Good value for money and location
body:
I went to NYC with my wife for 8 days. The hotel is location is great. You can walk to time sq in about 15-20 mins but you can always take the bus (M42) or taxi if are exhausted from all the sightseeing. Nice street food next time with a posh supermarket nearby.
The only problem is the mattress. If you sleep in spring mattress at home, it's really uncomfortable. Also, do not book this hotel if you need privacy in the toilet.

title: A good hotel in Manhattan
body: We stayed two nights at Yotel. A beautiful hotel located in Manhattan New York City. My colleague suggested this hotel. We stayed two days with my wife and we were very pleased with this hotel for a holiday. I would recommend it to anyone. You can find high quality service and cleanliness at an affordable price.

title: Fantastic Hotel Close To Times Square
body:
We stayed for 5 nights at the start of May in this lovely boutique hotel.
Check-in was simple and performed via one of the several computer terminals in the lobby. We were directed to the room by one of the helpful staff on the hotel's main floor, which is referred to as 'Mission Control' or 'Four' in the Yotel literature.
The room is of adequate size and the electric, retractable bed a fantastic idea to create more space during the day. The bathroom is essentially in the same room as the bedroom with a small partition separating the two and while we were fine with this situation I'm not sure how friends would cope as the shower and toilet are clearly visible from the bedroom (there is a small curtain that can be drawn between the two but it didn't look like it would obscure the view completely). The only problem we experienced was if one of us needed the bathroom during the night the light would wake whoever was sleeping, however when weighed against everything else this was a trivial concern.
Each floor has it's own galley kitchen where free tea, coffee, hot chocolate, cappuccino and ice/water are provided. This was particularly useful when we didn't feel like popping down to Four for the muffins and drinks at breakfast time.
WiFi in the hotel is provided free of charge and the signal strength was excellent.
The hotel is located in the Hell's Kitchen area of Manhattan. It is a rather modest area and on the walk to the hotel from the subway station we were a little apprehensive after speaking with a local who told us of the "homeless people and wh0res" that frequent the area (we say this having spent all our lives in Wythenshawe, Manchester). We didn't see any problems in the area and though there were quite a few homeless people around it was no more than in other parts of the city. I wouldn't let our initial misconception perturb anyone and we were happy to walk back in the early hours of the morning as the area was constantly busy. Aside from the immediate vicinity the hotel is walking distance from tourist hotspots like Times Square, Madison Square Gardens and Central Park, and the 42nd Street Port Authority Bus Terminal subway station a mere 2 blocks away has connections all over the city, including to/from JFK airport.
We tried a light meal in the hotel, out on the roof top terrace (which is billed as New York's largest outdoor hotel terrace), and it was excellent - the chicken wings were the nicest I have ever had and the Japanese beer was wonderfully thirst quenching on a sunny New York evening. Since it was happy hour it was very reasonably priced too and the service was good.
Check-out was simple and since our flight wasn't for a few hours we left our bags with the staff at the lobby (the Yobot was broken which was a shame) who offered to order us a taxi for the airport when we were leaving.
All in all a fantastic stay in a brilliant hotel, close to everything we wanted/needed. When we return to New York we'll definitely return to the Yotel.

title: Modern, pop and very good location
body:
We stayed 1 week in Yotel and it was great. Clean, cool atmosphere, good location.
Crew very gentle. Maybe the family room is a little bit too small 
We'll come back !

title: More than expected
body: You will be suprised how fabulous this affordable hotel is. We received first class treatment and the amenities are endless. The hotel clerk NR was awesome. He was so helpful and friendly. The location was good, the hotel was clean and staff was just so pleasant. The cabins are small but meets the travelers needs. Loved it and I will for sure stay here again when I return in December.

title: Not a clean room and staff walked unannounced to a very unprivate room!
body: If you don't mind tiny, I mean seriously tiny, bed touching the door tiny, having to clean up previous guest hair balls, staff walking in unannounced, no privacy in room, bad elevator smells and loud music, unfriendly staff, hmm what else can I stay, then this is the place for you. Not a good NY value. Spend the same amount and stay somewhere nice! Oh and I've slept on more comfortable mats in a tent in the wilderness.

title: Brilliant
body:
We stayed at the Yotel for 5 nights around St Patrick's and were so pleased with what we got. The cabins are small, but really don't feel it as the space is so well used.We thought the bed was really comfy and liked the way it moved back for more space. We were really impressed with the complimentary muffins and coffee each morning. There are a few places to get fresh fruit etc just around the corner if you get sick of the muffins! 
we found the staff very helpful and very friendly. Location is good as is a short walk to Times Square and literally just around the corner from The Port Authority Bus Station, so it was handy to get the bus from the airport straight in.
The Yotel has a pretty trendy bar for those who want to dance the night away!
Will def go back as was so nice and clean and really handy.

title: OMG!!! WOW!!!! WOW!!!
body: best hotel i have ever stayed at ! three of us , we had the corner room with the queen bed and bunk bed overhead! amazing view from the bedroom and very clean and comfy bed . The best part was the doorman whom flagged us down taxis and gave a great intial 1st day tour of the hotel { IAN } and the other best part was our waiter in the hotel restuarant was { RICKY } can i just say that this was the best service and food in NYC ! OMG!!! u have to try out all of thier tapas on the menu , very reasonable priced !!!! Will stay again ! no complaints at all !!!

title: Good but the checkin system is worst......
body: Yotel is a nice place to stay at NY, you are close to the most important things of the big apple, the rooms are clean and with spectacular view, Im stay in a corner room and all was excellent, the worst part is the checkin system and that the crew don't respect the time for checkin, they tell that you can checkin at 3pm but that´s not true, I came back at 3pm to check and they tell me sorry but your room is not available.... WHAAAAA????? They give me another great room and everything now is ok.

title: Brilliant first experience of New York!
body:
I was really excited to go to Yotel and wasn't dissapointed when I got there. Checking in took about a minute and we were in our room within about 3- that was without any interaction with staff yet. Loved the free muffins every morning and the Galley area on each floor with unlimited tea, coffee, cold water and chai- which was a new experience and highly reccomended. 
Every time we left or returned we were greeted by the friendly staff on the ground floor who are always there to help, and would offer to flag us down a taxi if required.
The hotel is about a 5 minute walk to Times Square and a major subway station which connects most subway routes (I would reccomend buying a week pass even if you're only going for 5 days as it is $30, allows unlimited subway travel- even to other boroughs like Brooklyn- and is a lot more convenient than buying a different ticket every day.)
Overall I would definitely come back to Yotel, and I think it would suit any type of traveler whether young or old as I saw a very diverse age range who all seemed happy at Yotel. 
Oh! and the free wi-fi was really helpful for planning where we would go the next day, and even if you don't have a smart phone there are 3 or 4 computers you can use on FOUR which are always available.

title: More than just another gimmick
body:
When I checked out Yotel online, I was a little hesitant about booking it as It came across as a little gimmicky and with little substance. I was so wrong. Stayed there for 4 nights recently, May 2012, and loved it. Check in was so easy and straight forward. We were brought to our room via control (reception in other languages), toured the restaurant and taken to the room. Compact, perfectly laid out, good bed. Great complementary muffins in the morning although, the coffee from the Galley on each floor is much better than the drip coffee served for breakfast. Great concierge team at the front door. Always on hand to help with cabs. 
Perfect location for midtown. Got a deal at the time for about €750 for 4 nights. Worth it and would stay there again!!!

title: Easter in NYC
body:
We flew into Newark, cost about $75 for Car Service for the 4 of us. Took about an Hour 8:30-9:30am. The Yotel staff took great care of us, took our bags, gave us a claim # and we were on our way. We got back to the Hotel around 4pm, and a staff member walked us right through the Kiosk Check-in. We we're on the 10th floor. It's a different setup, you take an elevator from Ground level to the 4th floor. This is where they have Mission Control (There version of a Front Desk), Restaurant & Bar.
You then take a different set of Elevators up to your room. The Rooms are small, make Cruise ship rooms look big ;-) The bed during the day is a couch, but at night you hit a button and it turns into a bed (it is not a great bed). The bathroom area is a strange setup. You have a glass enclosure for the shower, with the toilet right beside it. The only door is when your on the toilet, it's glass as well. They should have the door on the shower enclosure, cause it does get a little wet in front of the toilet when somebody showers.
Now, we did have a Fire in the Yotel early Sunday morning 4:30 am'ish. The Yotel staff handled it great, and we were all back in our rooms by 5:15.
Checkout was just as easy as Check-in. It's kinda nice that they don't have extra charges like other hotels.
Overall, this is a great location to see NYC. It's very Clean, Staff very helpful (even after asking for a working hair dryer 3 times) and very futuristic feeling. Now, I wouldn't classify it as a Destination hotel, but for visiting NYC and wanting something Clean, Close and reasonable price, this place is ideal for that. We were so tired every night, that the firmness of the bed didn't matter ;-)
Our only concern would be 5 years down the road, how is the quality going to stand up.

title: Fantastic Hotel
body: The hotel was ideal for us. I stayed with my daughter and the location was perfect for walking to places of interest, for the subway and buses. There's a airport bus that stops outside the port authority bus terminal which is 5 minutes walk away and the subway is in the same location. The hotel staff were friendly and the hotel itself was spotlessly clean. the room we stayed in was compact but well organised. My daughter particularly appreciated the 'hot chocolate' machine in the galley room on our floor! The bed was extremely comfortable - there is nothing like a really good bed when you are 'walked out' with aching feet and legs. We loved the chilled funk and soul music at breakfast time and the décor of the place. We also loved the little touch of 'birdsong' in the morning. The security system was well set up with only access to the particular floor you are staying on and the 'main' breakfast/restaurant/ customer desk/bar 4th floor. We appreciated hearing music on the 4th floor but being insulated from it on the floor we were staying on. We had only one slight problem, we couldn't quite get to grips with the air-con settings in the room but I think that could have been resolved if we'd asked a member of staff to help, as it was we only thought about it when we were going to bed and were too tired to do anything about it then. I really hope the good reviews don't mean the price is put up as I would really like to stay again!! Thanks

title: Yotel a perfect hotel for Javits Center attendees
body:
I have been looking for a good hotel near the Javits Center for many years.
Yotel is the first convenient, comfortable, and affordable hotel that I have found. The rooms are modular and though compact, are extremely well equipped and most have wonderful west side and Hudson River views. There is a galley on each floor that accommodates guests own food in a refrigerator and dispenses ice, water,coffee,tea, and fancy lattes 24 hours a day. 
The dining room serves excellent small dishes for evening hors d'oeuvres or light dinner. There is a happy hour from 5 to 7. A glass of wine and a few halibut sliders are under $20. The Terrace is a lovely place to have dinner in the warmer weather.
If your work or play is on the west side, this is the place to stay. Convenient to Broadway, 42nd St bus stops right outside the door.

title: Yo Yo Yo, Check This Place Out.....
body:
Let me first tell you that I would never knowingly book a place like this. The uber-hip, trendy, vibe-y hotels like this are usually big on style, and short on substance. I definitely prefer a more traditional hotel experience. However, I ended up booking here thru a blind site, and was immediately disappointed when I received the confirmation and saw what I got.
With that being said, this hotel far exceeded my expectations, and I must say that not only did I enjoy it, I admired it! Most New York modern hotels are heavy on the black and dark color tones. This place is bright, and white, and it's also immaculately clean. You check in on the ground floor, thru an automated kiosk. This is the fastest check in I have ever had in an NYC hotel. From walking thru the front door to my room in about 2 minutes! It was also during a peak check in time of 7pm.
You go up to the 4th floor ( which is called Mission Control) and then catch another elevator up to your room floor. All of the social action is on the 4th floor: the Outdoor space, bar, restaurant, and gym.
The rooms are tiny, but very well laid out and with high ceilings so they don't feel claustrophobic. The bed is actually a couch, but folds out to a bed with one button. The bathroom has all high quality soaps and comfy towels.The only beef here is the lack of privacy in the business part of the bathroom. There is merely a curtain which separates your sounds and smells from whoever might be on the receiving end in the adjoining bedroom.
Overall, the rooms are very comfortable, and very laid out. I will warn you that the location is off the beaten path and there is not much around the hotel. You are definitley not in the action, or that close to it if you stay here. You will get a very comfy and cozy experience if you do stay here, and Yo, if you're not that hip like me, it might help to make you one cool dude!

title: Enjoyed our stay
body: When we first arrived at the hotel, the door-man/mission control/cabin crew was SO helpful and friendly. He helped us get checked in and took our bags up to the room. He showed us around a bit and got us settled. We stayed 4 nights here. The futon was perfectly firm enough for my husband and I. The room was perfectly sized for the two of us. The location of the hotel was convenient for us, especially located so close to a CVS Pharmacy, Dunkin' Donuts, Times Square, and many other places to eat. It was great to also have the Galley for water, ice, and hot cholocate any time we wanted.

title: convenient to javits center
body:
yotel is a very good place to stay so that you can walk to javits center- the rooms are small, but contain everything you need. the rooms are well thought out and have windows that open which are important to me.
the weekend i was there was very rainy so I assume there were more people dining in the hotel than usual- i write this because the service at the restaurant ( for dinner ) was poor.
i think they also need a little more front desk help

title: Small - Fun - Cool
body:
Small rooms, great location, and nice staff make this a great place to stay. I have stayed in small hotels before and this one has the small design concept down without crowding you in.
Stay here if:
You are alone or with a spouse you love
If you like trendy and fun new spaces
Like that your bed is power and folds into a sofa
Free coffee 
Don't stay here if:
You are prude - the shower and the toilette are only hidden by a curtain. You can't hide any of your personal bathroom matters
If you like a real sofa or need more space. They do offer large rooms but they are very expensive and they do not offer many.

title: EXCELLENT HOTEL!!!
body: All the reviews are right in the sense that the rooms are built for absolutely no more than 2 people, but those 1 or 2 people in the room will be very satisfied! Rooms are clean and adorable, staff is incredibly helpful and friendly (especially valet and bellmen). This hotel is such a breath of fresh air from all the other standard NYC hotels. Almost everything is self-serve (check in was a BREEZE, the Yobot bell service was awesome and convienent), but there is always someone around in case you need help. Lots of amenities in your room! I will definietely be staying here again my next trip to the city. the beds are a little hard but I was always so tired it really didnt matter anyway I still slept like a baby

title: Clean, hip, and fun
body: Stayed there with 4 others. Really liked the atmosphere. There was also a young and hip crowd at all times. Good food. Upgraded to the king bed and well worth it for the size of the room. Made our friends jealous. Beautiful view too. Bed's are a little firm, as agreed by everyone, but not uncomfortably so. Staff was excellent all the way around.

title: Yotel Yeah!!
body: Excellent price and service. Rooms are small but comfortable, staff is excellent and facility is excellent also. only gripe would be no room service but thats all!

title: Fun hotel. Can't wait to go back.
body:
First, everyone is right: the beds are terrible. That being said, it's a fun place to stay and I would go back in a heartbeat. 
Value: excellent.
It's the cheapest place I've ever stayed in NYC, besides a fleabag hotel in the 90's when I was broke. It's clean, relatively secure, and the hip factor is a 10. Love the Yobot, and love that the hotel doesn't have 20 people with their hand out for a tip. Free internet, too. What hotel in NYC has free internet? Those two things alone saved us probably $20/night.
The free breakfast is a joke, since it's a muffin. It's not even a very good muffin, and probably scares people off from eating in the restaurant later, which is too back, since I like the restaurant. The terrace area of the restaurant is wonderful.
On the flip side, every floor of the hotel has a galley with a Lavazza coffee machine which will make you a really tasty espresso drink. Much better than Starbucks, and free. I had at least two a day during my stay. 
Rooms are cool, but small, but then most hotel rooms in NYC are small. You can see through the shower and bathroom, so only come with someone you want to see naked, and don't mind seeing on the toilet. 
The bathroom sink is too small to stick your head into, just in case you like to wash your face in a basin at night like my wife. It is a good looking sink, however:)
The bed is a fun gimmick, as it rolls out from it's couch position to a bed position. What's not a fun gimmick is how poorly it sleeps. It really is like a futon bed. We were so tired from all the walking that we didn't care all that much, but just be aware. Pillows were nice, though.
For $200 Yotel is hard to beat, so we'll definitely be back on our next trip to the city.

title: Great hotel!
body:
This was a great, fun hotel!
Yes the rooms are small, but all hotel rooms in Manhattan are small, so that is just something you have to deal with when travelling to NYC! However, the rooms were very functional and I found that they actually worked quite well for the small space. It's a very "funky" hotel, with friendly and helpful staff in all departments. 
We did find that the beds were hard after the first night, so the next morning we went and asked for a mattress topper, and the maid added a duvet underneath the sheets as well, which made it much more comfortable for the rest of the trip. The staff was very accomodating with this request. 
It's in a great location, being only 2 blocks away from 9th Avenue and its abundance of great restaurants! (The famous Amy's Bread is also on this street - a definite stop!!). The hotel is also only about a 10 minute walk up 42nd street, which will take you right into the heart of Times Square craziness!
There's also a CVS right across the street, which is convenient for purcashing any snacks or toiletry items.

title: Clean and comfortable without the cost!
body:
So glad to finally find somewhere in NYC that is affordable without being grotty.
The rooms are small, but efficient. They have everything you need to be comfortable without wasted space.

title: Small rooms but really well designed
body:
Stayed here on Mother's Day weekend with my 27 year old daughter. It was a great location and we walked to and from Times Square every night and felt quite safe. Two blocks away from some great restaurants on restaurant row.
As everyone says, the rooms are small, but they are really well designed and there seems to be a place for everything. The futon/bed made watching tv and using our laptops more comfortable than sitting in a normal hotel room where you have to prop yourself up with pillows. The mattress was uncomfortable the first night, but I asked for more "padding" and the maid put a duvet under the sheets and it was great after that. The curtain across the bathroom provided enough privacy for us, and it was great that there was a window that actually opened. Awesome to let some air into the room so it was never stuffy feeling. The room was spotless ad very bright. Lots of lighting.
Overall we loved Yotel and would have no problem recommending it. Would stay there again in a heartbeat!

title: Not Worth It!!
body: First off when we got to the hotel. We thought wow this looks great!! same with the service checking in and the room at the first glance. I had to take a nap as i was jet lagged. My friend had taken a shower and after had woken me up to see that our room was flooded. As the majority of the showers in the hotel are wheelchair accessible which is a nice gester it ruins the customers experience because then we had to change rooms. We had a beautiful room with a great view and when we moved had a horrible view. The service was attroish at the 4th level and we never got our room cleaned. I strongly suggest that you spend a little more money and actually get what your paying for instead of what you think your paying for.

title: Do something about the beds and we'll be back!
body:
We had a very nice stay at the 23th floor of Yotel, a young, modern, conceptuel hotel at the corner of 42nd and 10th. The hotel offers complementary breakfast, you'll have to do with muffins and coffee. On every floor there is a coffee machine (with good coffee ;-)) in the Galley. When a machine is broke after 5PM, you'll have to go to an other floor because the concierge is not willing to come up and fix this thing before noon the other day...
Yotel offers fast wifi, which is nice to staying in contact with homebase.
The room was okay, not so big and a little uncomfortable because the lack of space for your luggage. But, as said, we had a very nice stay.
We will not get back here before Yotel changes the beds. Since my wife suffers from back problems the very (extreme) hard suspension had not done her no good... In here opinion, there was actually no suspension at all.
The staff is very helpful and suggested us to ask for an extra mattress the next time but we do not think that is the solution...
Anyhow; please update us when you have new beds and we'll start saving money to come over again!

title: Welcome aboard
body: Small and small on purpose. Small can be bad. Think of the back of coach on an overseas flight. But small can also mean efficient. The "Cabins" in the New York Yotel hotel is the latter. Everything you need is there, it's just closer together than you are used to. The rate was about 200 bucks cheaper than anything else I was able to find during graduation week in Manhattan. All in all, a good deal for a pleasant and efficient room.

title: Modern hotel in a not-so-modern hood
body:
I quite enjoyed my stay at the Yotel. It's fun, modern, clean, safe, and only a few blocks away from Times Square and the subway. The staff are very friendly and always had a smile on their face, no attitude here to be found. 
I stayed in a basic room and they are tiny. They are not rooms, but rather "cabins". It does have a certain ship feel to it. I liked how the bed converted to a a couch at the push of a button. Very clean lines. Also, if you wanted to listen to your ipod, attach it to the tv and there's a great sound coming from the speakers. The shower head was wonderful and very relaxing. There is not enough room for a tub. Each floor is equipped with a galley, which you can stock up with fresh water or coffee. In the morning (up until 10 am), you can get yourself a coffee or tea and a muffin. The muffins are really good and I recommend the cranberry orange muffin. Yum!
Of the few cons of the place, I found the heating/cooling the most frustrating. My first night, the room was just not getting cold. Finally, around midnight, I broke down and called the Mission Control for some help. Shortly afterwards, 2 men came by and tried to repair the heating/cooling system. They said they fixed it but they found the system still noisy, and suggested I move rooms. I had flown the red eye the night before and I tend not to sleep on planes. At this point, I just wanted to sleep and declined to move rooms at that point in the night. Unfortunately, I couldn't sleep at all because the heating/cooling was so inconsistent. I mentioned this the next morning to the mission control and they readily agreed to move me. I ended up going to the top floor and was given some complimentary coupons for the hotel restaurant. I find I need a cooler room for me to have a good night sleep. However, I found that the temperature in the room would not stay constant. When I thought I had reached the desired temperature, it would soon change. This was frustrating because I kept waking up throughout the night, either too hot or too cold. If I was Goldilocks, I would not be happy. 
The Dohyo, the restaurant on the 4th floor offers a selection of small plates. I didn't find the staff here to be particularly service oriented, in comparison to the rest of the staff. One morning, I was going to use one of my coupons and was going to order a yogurt parfait. The server told me they weren't ready, which I found strange, seeing that it was 9:30. When they were ready, they couldn't serve them because they didn't have the proper lids that fit them. Later that day, I wanted to order the cheesecake (which was very good, chocolate and chiptotle). When I asked if I could have a side of ice cream (it was a hot afternoon), I appeared to confuse the wait staff because they never had such a request before and required the assistance of 2 servers. I didn't realize my request was so complicated. But these points are relatively minor. 
The 4th floor is quite fun. You can grab a table, catch up on your email or facebook as you make your plans for the day. There is free wi fi throughout the hotel and if you need a computer, there are at least 4 computers available that you can use. There is also a really great outdoor patio that also has a bar.
The neighborhood is in Hells Kitchen. It's not rough, although walking past the Port Authority on 42nd can be a bit sketchy. If you're looking for some great places to eat and not wanting something very touristy, I suggest going up 9th Ave. There are some really fun places to check out.

title: Fantastic!!
body:
Loved every quirky aspect of this hotel, stayed 4 nights and was sorry i didnt stay longer.
Room was a good size, hotel was very clean and relaxing. Bed was comfy, easy check in and out.
Room had everything needed for an enjoyable comfortable stay in the big apple.
Staff encountered were very friendly, helpful, informative and couldnt do enough for you.
Dont hesitate to book this hotel you wont regret it.

title: Super Clean and convient location
body: My teenagers though this hotel was super cool. It was definetly different in the decore. But it was super clean and spa like. It is located a little walk from the time square center but not bad at all. Came with muffins and coffee in the morning so we didn't have to buy breakfast. The only problem we had is that somewhere on our floor someone decided to smoke pot and the whole floor got smelly. Then my youngest daughter got a headache.
