The room was cool looking, but it was a bit awkward to get around with no size, even for a NYC hotel. I think I would've completely hated it if my husband were with me. This hotel is definitely for the traveler who doesn't want to spend a lot of time in the room.
My remote was broken, which wouldn't be a big deal except there is no other way to turn on the tv. I called the front desk and he said he would send someone up. Half an hour later I called to check on the status. Then an hour passed I called again. Finally after an hour and 15 minutes I was very tired and just wanted to go to bed so I called and told them they could just handle it tomorrow.
I also realized after using the restroom that there is no handsoap or bars provided. Ew. I used some shampoo, but just thought it was an oversight from housekeeping. I stopped by the front desk, reminded them about the remote and left for work. After work I came back, I checked on the remote before leaving for dinner. As it was still not working, I went by the front desk and asked for the manager. The girl was very nice and assured me it would be fixed by the time I returned from dinner. I also asked about the handsoap and she said it isn't provided, but you can buy it at the front desk. EW. So the entire hotel doesn't wash their hands?! I used purel like crazy the rest of my stay. After dinner I stopped by the desk and found out my remote was fixed and had only needed batteries. So nothing complicated, and one little bit of initiative would've made my stay much more relaxing.
The fact that I had to follow up with the front desk 5 times to get some batteries tells me I won't be staying again. 
Cabs are non existent on this street, you are better off walking for a bit to a better corner rather than wait in the long cab line in the morning.
Oh yeah, and the bed feels like a fold out futon. If I wanted to reminisce about crashing with friends in college, I could do it for a lot less money. I'm just a little to old for all the spiff and no real amenities.

title: yotel.... you better call it motel
body:
we chose to stay in a modern well located hotel in New York. 
First of all the web site of the yotel is presenting this hotel in a way that gives you the filling that all the spaces shown are for the guests of this Hotel.
That is wrong. It was thursday about 22:00 when i decided with my wife to go down to the terrace for a quick drink. We went down there was a party going on on the 4rth floor, the place was packed with people living outside of the hotel. We try to find a place to sit outside, which was not easy to find, when we finally found one a waiter of the hotel said to us you cannoy seat hear this space is reserved for the party.. WHAT THE HELL!! IAM I STAYING IN THIS HOTEL OR NOT?
THAT WAS IT? I WILL TELL YOU EVERYTHING THAT ARE NOT RIGHT. PAY ATTENTION.
1. You pay only to stay in a tiny rooms. ...motel style
2. No privacy in the room, toilet has no door, only a certain separates you from the toilet. Imagine smells, sounds...funny a.
3. No toilet brush available.
4. No place to put your clothes, bags, etc. The room is okay if you travel alone for just a day.
Motel style..
5. When someone close the door on the floor you hear it, no good sound insulation
6. The aircondition is like a huge blower, that never stops, and has no options to reduce the fan speed or sound.
7. 4th floor is a disco, too loud sound, you are about to go out for a dinner and your forved to pass from a floor full people. you fill like the motel starts from the 5th floor and up.
8. Breakfast, muffing coffee had it only for the first day of our stay,we chose to pay to eat outside
Paying for another 20 dollar every morning fora decent breakfast. Breakfast at the yotel too expensive.
9. Cleaning the tiny room, average clean. Motel like...
10. The location is great.... Thats is well mentioned.
Sorry about my english, hope you enjoy your staying in the beautifull New York.

title: Really tickled with this hotel
body:
I don't know if Yotel has changed their bedding since receiving previous complaints of uncomfortable beds, but I thought it was quite comfortable. The hotel was spotless, my room was well designed, the location was terrific for my conference.
I was only in my room to crash at night, but it was perfect for that purpose. I liked the galley on the floor and made use of having espresso or tea - a really nice touch.

title: coooool!
body:
The atmosphere is clean crisp, modern and fun and for the money (in NYC) I think this hotel is a bargan! ( I did get it on sale for less than $200.) I used to stay at the POD ...but Yotel has the free muffins/coffee /water and a rooftop with awesome views of the city for around the same price. My 16 yo son loved it too!
Walking distance to times sqare and close enought to the NYC port (was in NYC for a cruise)

title: OUTSTANDING EXPERIENCE!!!
body:
A friend and I needed to book a hotel in Times Square to conduct business and booke the Yotel on a whim. To my dismay, this was one of the Best hotel stays I've ever experienced
and I travel quite often! Yotel Hotel was Super CLEAN and Chic.Our room was super small but clean. Our sheets where pure white and even smelled good. Surprisingly, the carpet was even clean. The Customer Service was Amazing. Each staff member greeted me with warm smiles and great attitudes (did I mention everyone was easy on the eyes,lol).
The unlimited coffee and tea in the Gally didn't hurt either. The breakfast muffins were fresh and totally delish!!! Location was good as well,it was just a few blocks from all the action. 
MUST EXPERIENCE IT FOR YOURSELF!!!

title: Quirky and cheerful
body:
We stayed at the Yotel New York for four nights. Our stay got off to a rocky start when we waited for almost two hours to check in, being shunted around from one staff member to another. It was the Pride weekend in New York and hotels were fully booked and guests were late checking out. 
While we were initially annoyed about the delay, the spectacular view from our 27th floor corner room, combined with the minimalist decor, made it worth the wait and the hotel sweetened the deal with a couple of $10 vouchers for F&B. After that, our stay was smooth sailing and very enjoyable. 
The hotel room itself was very comfortable and we were right next door to the pantry so we had easy access to drinking water, free coffee and tea and a vending machine. Breakfast each morning was a choice of free muffins and coffee or paid-for options from the a-la-crate menu. At $9.99 for eggs, bacon, toast and a hot beverage, the paid-for option was fairly reasonable. 
The hotel's location made it an ideal base to explore mid-town Manhattan. The nearest Subway station was a couple of blocks walk away and we were able to walk to most mid-town attractions including the Empire State Building, Top of The Rock, Times Square and even Central Park.
We loved practically everything about this hotel, from the quirky decor and music, to the 'Yobot' robotic luggage concierge. And the best part was that it did not cost us a fortune. Would we go back? Certainly.

title: Brilliant Experience
body:
Visited New York from the 20th - 25th June and had a fantastic time. Myself and my partner were very pleased with the room on the 12th floor, it looked exactly as we had seen on the internet. Neither of us had a problem with the bed and thought it was very comfortable, particularly the pillows!
While we were in New York there was a heatwave, with temperatures reaching 39c. The air con in the room was great and much needed! The shower was lovely, and you're provided with two different types of shampoo and shower gel. While on the topic of free things at the hotel, the galley (where you can find free tea, coffee, hot chocolate, ice and water) was very useful, and the free muffins at breakfast were really tasty.
The one slight complaint I'd have would probably be about the location. It wasn't awful, but the only real landmark it was close to is Times Square, and I think I would have preferred it if the hotel was towards the East, rather than the West. It is about a 10min walk to Times Square subway station and you pass Port Authority bus terminal on the way.
Location wise, it is extremely close to a Food Emporium (supermarket), pharmacy (selling lots of food and drink) and a Subway sandwich shop, for when you need any snacks or drinks for your room.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel and would be very happy to stay here again on another trip to NYC.

title: CHIC, TRENDY, UNUSUAL BUT UNEVEN
body: We stayed at YOTEL for a combo business and pleasure trip. It is a well-designed property and more hotels would do well to copy the space-saving ideas. The whole futuristic tech-heavy look is fun, interior design is great. But services and staff are important too, and that's where YOTEL mostly fell short. We came in having to film a TV interview late that afternoon then had a nationally televised event to attend after. This was made clear when we booked, but we still had to wait for rooms. As a result, we were rushed to prepare for that and the staff attitude of not caring one whit really didn't help. The check-in portals didn't work during check-in/ check-out & the concierge desk wasn't exceptionally helpful. Beware long lines for the YOBOT at peak times. You have to check your luggage in on the 1st floor when you enter (impossible if you're not checked in yet), then you have to proceed to the 4th floor "mission control", walk to another set of elevators, use your key to activate the elevator, THEN you can get to your room. The galley is an OK idea, but it would be better if the machines in the galley actually worked. I had to travel up and down floors to find microwaves or coffee machines that worked. Housekeeping starts bright & early there, so be ready for the constant "knock knock" up and down the halls. The beds are hard, which is fine if you like that. But they're more like thick pads on a hard platform. The work desk was extremely small & there was no place to put toiletries in the bathroom. The sink was shallow and had a thin rim, so I had to pull down the shower seat and store cosmetics, hairbrush etc on that. It was either that or the floor. They say they offer toiletries, but that's really 2 bottles of shower gel bolted to the wall. You get 2 choices: "GET UP" or "GET DOWN". They smell amazing but the pumps don't dispense much and they both turn your hair into straw. Make sure to bring your own. The view was great, and the lighting was nice and more than adequate. The electronically controled window blinds were a very touch. Location is really good and very convenient. Free local calls is a plus, but my phone never worked. Wi-fi is everywhere, and that's very nice. Overall, I had the impression this is a hotel for Gen Y-ers who are there more for pleasure than business. I may stay again if I'm not on business, otherwise I'm going with something more traditional.

title: Amazing hotel
body:
If you love products made by Apple, you'll love Yotel.
I loved every part about this hotel, staying here made me think... finally someone has got hotel accommodation right.
This hotel is like no other, from the moment you walk in, the place has been designed for modern, tech-savvy, social and intelligent people. Everything has been considered, from the distinct scent that fills the place, through to the mood lighting - it is a REAL example of intelligent design.
The rooms are tiny, yet there is everything you need and there is a place for everything. If there were only a single thing I would complain about, the beds were very hard and not particularly comfortable. Everything else was amazing.
I loved the free Wifi, the gym, the free breakfast and coffee, electronic checking without having to deal with a stuff hotel desk. What I loved about the design of the place is that your room is where you sleep, shower and keep your stuff, but they've created cool social spaces throughout the hotel that you don't spend much time in your room, but can hang out in their lounges, conference rooms or bar.
Perfect place for business, couples and solo travellers... perhaps not the type of place for a family or people who like to camp out in their room all day long.
This without question will be my hotel of choice every time I visit NYC.

title: Excellent Hotel with Short walk to Times Square.
body: This hotel met my very particular standards. I wasn't too sure about the location but definitely was happy that I picked this place. Located at 10th and west 42nd, this hotel was amazing located only 3 blocks away from Times Square. It was a great walk to the main attractions including short walk to Herald Square for shopping (34th). Many great restaurants along 9th including 5 napkin burger!, another location plus. 24 hour store across the street for water or toiletries etc. Check in was easy, hotel patio is 5 star and room was typical of Yotel with cube design. Little touches such as the nice shampoo and free beverages and breakfast were great additions. Room service was prompt and always clean. A+ hotel and will stay here again. Staff were friendly and helpful and enjoyed and cool atmosphere.

title: Great hôtel for couples or singles
body:
I loved my stay. The staff was friendly and swift. The room was quite small but well designed. I wished there was more variety for breakfast, but there is a supermarket across the street. The terrasse is superb (in summer). 
A great place for couples who wants to be in a hip place!
The rooms are clean (changing sheets and towel daily) but the commons spaces would need more attention (washrooms, common kitchens on each floor).

title: Excellent
body:
- great location. 5 min walk to port authority (bus and subway station)
- our standard cabin had enough space to put 2 big suitcases and to storage all our things. 
- if you can ask the hotel for a room upgrade. We have payed extra 10 usd for day to get a room in24th floor. it has better views and less trafic noise. for 10 usd it's was a very good deal.
- galley "kitchen" has a microwave, water, ice, hot drinks as coffee, chocolate, etc for free. 
- great muffins at breakfast with hot bevarages for free. you have to pay for natural juices or a special breakfast.
- most frequented by young travelers, modern environment with fashionable parties at 4th floor.

title: Yo is the only way to go
body:
Our family of 4 had an extended stay of 8 nights and found alll 10 out of 10 
Room located on the 15th floor was next to the galley was a room for the disabled of which we are not 
Noice due to being located next to the galley was minimal 
The product offerred in the galley was excellant: ice,ice water, different coffees, hot chocolate and standard soft drink vending machine 2.00 dollar charge for soft drink 
Bathroom was surrounded by 3 walls and a glass door (very private) and very good amenities such as body lotions and hair gel 
The room for 4 has a sofa bed that converst to a bunk bed and the queen bed does not move like in the smaller rooms but is quite comfortable 
There is much storage space under the bed and a separate closet that had a door and a 3 drawer unit along with a safe , hangers , iron and a small ironing board 
The room also had a desk tha had 3 other drawers that were used as clothes storage
The noise level was at null 
The one time that we used the restaurtant we found the food delicious and the service very efficient 
The music was very contenporary as was the whole hotel in design 
Parking was great and the charge was approx 40.00 per day no valet 
The locatioin was great as it was within a 10 minute walk to the Port Authority subway stop and within 15 minute walk to Times Square 
Suggest to buy a subway metro card for 7 days unlimited use fo the subway at a cost of 29.00 with access to busses it would have costed 59.00

title: Perfect choice!
body:
We stayed for a one week (7 nights) in this new (opened in June 2011) marvelous Hotel Yotel. I usually avoid to give 5/5 ratings but this time there is no option.
We arrived to Yotel by taxi from JFK (45$ flat price + 5$ toll + tip) and faster than we had reached out of the cab, the bag boy of Yotel had already loaded our pags to trolley pag. Then he directed us check in that was made using kiosk. After 1 minute of checking in we took a lift to 4th floor which is known as FOUR. Our pag boy explained us the function of this floor: mission control (concierge desk), restaurant, terrace, etc. It was also possible to buy tickets to Broadway or sightseeing tours, etc. in this floor using the kiosks. Also free computers & printing possibility in this floor. Then our pag boy took us in to our floor and carried our pags in to our room (don't forget to tip).
We stayed in Premium Cabin Queen -room. Size is pretty small for a Hotel room, 16 sqm, but it is well designed. Bed automatically transforms into sofa by pushing a button. WC and shower are behind courtain and textured glass wall. You of course can easily hear your partners action in bathroom but just ignore it or tune the voice up of your wide LCD-TV and enjoy about 40 channels for free. There is also one big window in the restroom: have you ever even thought about sitting down and "doing your business" at the same time when looking at the Manhattan's bustle? Me neither. But now I have done it. Sweet. Bed is good, pillows maybe too soft in my opinion. Enough mirrors for two persons. It would have been great if it would have been more storage space but few hangers and your own bag as a wardrobe was a workable solution. In every room there also is an effective and efficient air-conditioning that you can set by yourself. You also have free WiFi and free safe (with an 4-digit password that you may decide), flatiron and hairdryer. Towels changed daily.
In every floor there is a Galley where you can get free coffee, tea, source of water, crushed ice. It also offers you a microwave and fridge. Soft drinks cost 2$ (from the machine).
Yotel offers you tasty muffins, coffee and tee for free on every morning until 10 am. There is also possibility to buy more extensive breakfast from the wide range of choiges. We gave it a shot - delicous, can't complain, but a bit pricey. There are three great A-rated breakfast-cafes nearby Yotel in 42th street on the way to Times Square. Another choice is to cross the 10th Avenue and get something from CVS or to go to Subway (restaurant, not a train).
Yotel's Dohyo -restaurant is worth of try. It offers you small, shared plates and the bar builds the best drinks. Nice place to end your busy day. Better way is to go Hell's Kitchen -restaurant area on 9th Avenue, only few minutes away.
Checking out was also done with kiosk on the lobby, fast and easy. After that you were able to left your bags at hotel by using the great automated bag-storage-robot, Yobot. Maybe a bit slow way to do it (if lots of people doing the same thing simultaneously), but so cool!
I really advise you to end your searching for a great hotel with a great value in New York. I've done it for you and Yotel is the answer - trust me. In addition to the above mentioned facts, the location of Yotel is absolutely great. It's only 10-15 minute walk from Times Square and you can't get lost. 42th street is wide and traveled, not an small scary alley. There is also only 5 minute walk from hotel to the Port Authority Bus Terminal for taking a bus or a subway. Easy way to get anywhere in New York - or even further.
Yotel is way to go!

title: Funky!
body:
I stayed two nights at the Yotel in June and was very impressed. Yes, the Cabins (not rooms!) are small and compact in design, but very comfortable and really well fitted out. The best goes up and down with the flick of a switch and makes the space very flexible. The bathroom is well fitted and all glass - with a curtain for privacy if you need it! I was very happy with my room - its all very new and very clean. At the end of each corridor there are free tea and coffee stations too. For breakfast they offer complimentary coffee and muffins.
The restaurant offers great food and has a very lively atmosphere. They also have the most amazing outdoor roof terrace - a really big plus! In the evenings the bar is fun and we spent one great evening meeting people.
This is not your normal hotel by any means, but i do recommend it. The regular cabins are perfect for a business traveller or even a young couple. The service was excellent at all times.
I hope to see more Yotel's appearing around the world soon - a great concept.

title: Yotel New York - perfect for a short stay
body:
The hotel is unique (not traditional) - so maybe not for everyone. But while its different its a hotel I would recommend. 
The check-in is self service which is a bit of a shock and from then until you get to your room you don't meet anyone as everything is automated and works. The rooms are very small (they are actually called pods!) but very clean and compact. Again, once you get used to it - no problem. There's not alot of space for luggage but as I was there for only 4 nights it wasn't an issue. The location is perfect - 5-6 minutes walk to Times Square and around the corner from the subway. 
Wi-Fi available, light breakfast is included, Internet access for printing boarding passes etc - would definitely stay there again.

title: Swanky hotel with innovative and practical designs
body: I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Yotel! Despite the fact that it is a rather long walk from Broadway area, the very clean room (snug and comfortable for a solo traveller) was really well-designed and provided all the necessary amenities (flat-screen TV, safe, shower, queen-sized bed, work table and chair, wireless internet) in the most space-saving and modern fashion. There is a futuristic feel about the place, and it is really, really! one hotel you must try!

title: Yotel is our new favorite stay in the City
body:
We stayed 3 nights at the Yotel. The service was impeccable, the room was clean and nicely furnished. Being claustrophobic I was a bit worried about the size, but the floor to ceiling window and strategically placed mirrors made me very comfortable. The public spaces were well maintained and user friendly. Even the elevator music was a cut above the norm. Mission control
was always available and knowledgeable with appropriate answers for everything. We found staff everywhere we went and for everything we needed, always on hand to facilitate our needs.

title: Fantastic Hotel
body: I loved Yotel because of its affordability (by New York standards!), its hi-tech features, ease of use, cleanliness, compactness and having just about everything I would need on a trip where i use my hotel for sleeping and shower! The location was also very convenient and the views from my room beautiful (it is certainly worth paying a little bit extra to get a "View Cabin" on floors 24 and above).

title: goochie
body: Stayed with my husband and two adult son. fantastic hotel ,fun and great atmosphere.great staff and very helpful,rooms were lovely with great views from our corner cabin. This hotel is very different from the traditional hotels that i have been in before so go try, theres everything you want here.

title: Hitch
body:
Prior to staying at the hotel I did have certain reservations due to some of the things I had read on trip advisor, I was very pleasantly surprised by my experience and this just goes to show that this is only one persons perception and not always a true reflection.
The cabins are lovely and comfortable and I did not find them small at all. There are neat little areas under the bed to place suitcases out of the way. 
I was expecting a basic room and was surprised when we arrived to find a hairdryer, iron an ironing board. Had I have known I would not have bought a travel iron and hairdryer.
The bed!! We LOVED the bed it was amazing, it was so comfortable to sit on when it was its upright position and if you wanted to chill and watch the tv. According to other people's feedback they complained that it was hard and like sleeping on a hard board, not the case it was extremely comfortable. I would love one for my bedroom!
The room was always cleaned my only negative is I think they forgot to hoover the carpet but that is not a biggy.
The breakfast muffins were a delight and a nice start the day.
The crew are amazing. Very helpful and speedy check in. Always offered to hail us a cab if we needed one. Gave great advise on where places of interest where, recommend restaurants etc. I found every crew member very friendly approachable and offered an outstanding level of customer service.
I would most certainly stay here again and would definatly recommend it.
Well done Yotel and thank you for a very enjoyable and relaxing stay.

title: Funky, fun, great food and reasonably priced
body: We stayed at Yotel for the first time recently and had a great experience. We have two kids and stayed in the cabin room that has a bunkbed, which our boys loved! The atmosphere is very lively and youthful. The food and service were excellent!

title: Yotel New York Review
body:
The service was excellent, the food was fantastic and people were very friendly. I would recommend this hotel to anyone that has a sence of adventure, because it is more of an experience than your normal hotel. The convenience of being in the middle of Manhatten 
is also a big plus, because you are so close to so many attractions eg: just a few blocks 
from Time Square.

title: Yotel was the greatest experience!
body:
Me and my husband stayed for our Honeymoon at Yotel for 7 days. The first thing that comes to my mind when I think about our stay at Yotel is the crew, I have never in my life met a nicer and more professional crew. Even though you think that nobody is going to greet you because everything is computerized, you are met by people that greets you and helps you. Yotel is fresh, futuristic, modern and special. The rooms are fresh and clean, always clean when you are back from a day spent in NYC. eve if you have a smaller room you dont feel it is so small because the windows are big and the class doors to the bathroom and toilet makes everything much bigger. The complementary breakfast was not my cup of tea, since you only get coffee and muffins. the al la carte breakfast is expensive, you can get much more for less money just across the street. The food however, the lunches and the dinners are awesome and fully price worthy. The tapas inspired food is awesome, I loved the food, it is fresh and delusions.
We will definitely come back to Yotel, and Yotel made our holiday worth wild.

title: Great location and great value
body: We stayed for 8 nights and thoroughly enjoyed the stay,Rooms are small but not a problem as I doubt you'll spend too much time in them, Free use of Macs with internet was a great service. Decor and ambience was fantastic and the use of technology and innovation is impressive as were the free breakfast muffins...perfect. Location is great too with about a 10 min walk to Times Square and great for the Port Authority. Pity there was no pool...with hindsight upgrading to a jaccuzzi room would have been worth the extra expense as it was a particualry hot week.

title: Hotel, Yotel, Holiday Inn...
body:
This is my second time visiting the city. The purpose of this trip- A girls holiday. Prior to arrival I had highlighted that it was one of our parties birthday, at E-Check in the said girl recieved a recipt with best wishes and a round of complimentary drink- A very nice touch! 
I was concerned by some reviews highlighting the room size- The room was compact but with adjustable beds and many other futuristic quirks more that suitable for 3 girls, of which I was very impressed. Staff were plesant and helpful throughout our stay!

title: Great design hotel - great accomodations
body: Yotel is a very nice design hotel with great common space accomodations : terrace with 2 bars, big lounch, TV rooms etc with very friendly young people to serve the guests. Although I wasn't able to join the weekend brunch, it looked fantastic.

title: Yotel is lots of fun; excellent experience
body: I'm a granny compared to the average age of the other guests, but boy! did I have fun Beginning with AnnaMaria, reservations manager (who did everything possible to meet our needs in an extremely friendly and personalized manner), all personnel at Yotel followed suit. The room design is clever, beautifully designed and actually often made me smile. I felt hugged in it, and though space often means a lot to me, I was surprised and impressed at the efficiency and charm of the room. The menu at the restaurant is very appealing and affordable, and I will be sure to have a meal there next visit. Breakfast could have been crowded and difficult; but service moved smoothly. I will try to stay at Yotel again; hopefully, it won't get so popular that I'll be closed out.

title: A Great Little Hotel!
body: From the friendly and efficient staff, to the fun-techy rooms, to the cleanliness and outstanding location, this is a wonderful little gem. The rooms are small and as such are actually called "cabins"--so if you're expecting lots of space, this is NOT the place for you. But if you appreciate efficient use of a nice, clean space, you'll enjoy your stay. Also, be sure to use the highlight--the YOBOT--for storing your luggage if you arrive before check-in or want to tool around the city and need to keep your things before you leave; it works great, it's free, and is just plain really fun!

title: Good stays overall. Some minor blips
body:
Good points: Really helpful staff, clean rooms, plenty of complementary amenities that you can help yourself to - tea, coffee, hot chocolate, breakfast muffins, free printing, wifi and local calls from your room - something that most hotels charge for.
Negatives: Not really all that convenient on 10th Ave and rather removed from any particular 'New York' vibe. It's quiet and If you want to be close to times square, it's a good affordable location but finding somewhere in Chelsea or West Village is also quiet and definitely has more atmosphere.
A couple of clueless staff messed up our reservation, and had to refund our credit card later on. We stayed twice at Yotel and the first time, 9 days was great, without any hiccups but the second time a lot seemed to go wrong. First the reservation, then trouble with a package and our room, despite being the same type as our first stay, was considerably smaller and didn't have an ipod dock/clock/radio that the other one did.
Overall, great hotel that I may stay at again. The only reason is I'd pick another is location, downtown, that would be more convenient with better atmosphere.

title: A great stay in a great location!
body:
I have never been to New York City and was really excited on what New York had to offer..before booking our trip, I was researching hotels especially closer to Time Square since it was my first time and my boyfriend had not been there since high school. We wanted to be closer to the 'touristy' areas but also close enough to move around New York as well..When searching, the prices of hotels were making me become very nervous of how much this trip was really going to cost..I then found out about Yotel which is a newer hotel and I thought, "hey, why not give it a shot". I'm so glad that I did because we found such a great deal for it and it was so close to Time Square!
We caught a cab from La Guardia Airport (which took about 30 minutes+ because of traffic) but going back to La Guardia only took us about 20 minutes..the taxi cab cost about 36 dollars which isn't too bad! So we finally arrived to our hotel and it was 'futuristic!'. 
When you arrive for check-in (we were lucky to have an early check-in as we arrived around 9:30 am), you literally go to these kiosks and there's a guy that helps out and you just punch in your name and you get as many cards as you want and thats it! 
So you go up this elevator to the 4th floor which is where the restaurant, MISSION CONTROL (where you can buy your tickets to attractions etc) and also concierge. Then you have to take another elevator to your room floors-you have to swipe your card inside the elevator to get to your floor level (we didn't know about this until the second day as our floor level would always get skipped and we would just end up taking the stairs).
Let's talk about the rooms! So you walk into your room, and honestly..its not the biggest space but your room in new york is really to sleep in..(well for me anyways!) we walked in and the 'futon couch' is kind of like those hospital beds that recline with a push of a button-the beds were comfortable for the two of us, they were a bit on the hard side but they were fine! The bathroom was interesting though..lets just say if you're not comfortable with the person you're going with, you might not want to share a room at Yotel..haha..there aren't any doors so you can see, hear anything you want..there is a little curtain but really..it doesn't leave much to the imagination! The room was great-had amenities and there's a little safe and also a small ironing board which we used! Then on each floor there's a galley which there's an ice/water machine, tea/coffee/hot chocolate machine which is complimentary..they also had a microwave and a fridge that everyone on the floor shared..I left a vinagrette and some cookies I had bought and none were taken (think dorm room style!)..
They also have this thing called YOBOT, which if you are checking out and your flight isn't till later you can store it with YOBOT..when we were checking-out, there was a huge line to use it and thank goodness our luggage was too big to fit in so we passed the line!
Location is also great! Its about a 7 minute walk to time square..theres some restaurants and things nearby but just walk 7minutes and you'll get to time square and the subway station
Overall..I would definitely recommend this place for the price, location and the experience. Next time I'm in New York..I will definitely stay here again! FYI-fastest check-in and check-out I've ever encountered! 
Thanks Yotel for the wonderful NY Experience!!!

title: A fantastic stay
body: We have just come back from a week at Yotel and cannot fault it. Superb staff, comfortable well designed rooms, good location and excellent value for money. We will certainly return.

title: my first NY trip
body: Our room was a little bit to small for 3 persons, but really nice and clean. Excellent crew, friendly and helpful. My daughter and I enjoyed our free breakfast at the terrace, everyday. We liked to stay at yotel and we will try to come back as soon as possible.

title: Very cool and funky hotel
body:
Good location, cool hotel, very cool rooms!
5 Min walk to times square, 3 min walk to Broadway. Free WIFI, Free coffee and water all day, free filter coffee + muffins between 7am - 10am

title: 4th business trip in NY, here is best
body:
Very advanced concept hotel.
Pros:Reasonable price, Nice location, free wifi, free breakfast, free coffee on same floor,Excellent crew, Nice and big terrace(NewYorker is gathering at night), Clean room, good business facilities(Meeting),Lovely japanese concept pictures.
Cons:Small for 2 people, open bathroom

title: The place to be in NYC
body: I'm just back from a 7 night stay at Yotel and will definitely go back. I've been to NYC 8 times over the years and this is by far the best accommodation I've stayed in, and I've stayed in some nice NYC hotels. The staff are really friendly and helpful and the facilities are first class. Me and my Fiance were on the 27th floor so the views over Manhattan were amazing. The hotel is also surrounded by some great restaurants not too far from Times Square and not as expensive as Times Square. I would honestly say that anyone who rates Yotel any lower than "Very Good" really should consult their psychiatrist.

title: Would stay again
body: Went to NYC with two teenagers to see Broadway shows. The Yotel was in a convenient location and the kids loved the room. The room was small, but very clean and modern. Can't wait to return!

title: Long weekend with friends
body:
Went to NYC for a holiday with 3 friends. We stayed at Yotel in the Theatre District of Manhattan. Had a brilliant time. The hotel is clean and cleaned daily. Has a swanky lounge and rooftop bar, great cocktails; all accessible day and night, free wifi and free use of macs and printers. Occasionally a DJ played music. 
Its best to email queries instead of phoning in advance.On arrival the staff were very friendly and helpful with our room setup and our iphone docking station. Breakfast is very basic but with so many cheap options near by it doesnt matter. 
Gets full marks from me!

title: The Jetsons would love this
body:
I just stayed at the Yotel on July 1 and really loved this hotel. They were offering a great rate online and then offered an upgrade for a city view for a nominal fee. The rooms are very small and are called cabins, but every space is well utilized.The bathrooms are very beautiful.
The entire hotel has a very futuristic feel to it including the luggage storage system in the lobby. I don't think I ever seen such an unusual system.
We also visited the 4th floor terrace.Great bar to have a cocktail outside.
Location is perfect not far to Tmes Square.Since we do not spend that much time in the room the size did not bother me at all. The staff is very friendly.Check in & out is a breeze.
 We would definitely consider staying here again

title: Amazing Hotel, 10m from Time Square
body:
So different but so good!
Different concept but feels like home, on the 4th floor sometimes a little bit noisy but is OK the rooms only start on the 8th floor
A very clever concept for the rooms trying to take advantage of the space, small but very functional
the employees are all very very kind and always there for you
A nice surprise for the breakfast, milk, coffee and muffins limitless, its for free!
I really enjoy it and when we return to New York for sure we will stay here again
If you are mind open go and try You'll not regret, 100% recommended

title: Interesting concept, reasonable price, good service.
body: Nice hotel rooms very clean. Special concept (see their website) and reasonably priced (except for 4th of July where the price was excessive $299 for a room regularly at $149). The price decreased at the last minute ($190) but it was too late for us to change our plans. The parking price is high ($39/day) but similar to other places in the area. 2 blocks from Times Square. Yobot is a new concept but very slow when you have to wait in line for 30 minutes to leave your luggage.

title: Brilliant hotel, very cool, perfect for young couples and singles
body: This place was perfect, if I go back to NYC there is nowhere else I would rather stay. The rooms are great, the bar is fantastic and the staff are friendly. The location was perfect and the beds were really comfortable. Highly recommend, very cool.

title: My second stay - Still loved it
body: I really love the Yotel for value, service, vibe, room and location.

title: I will always come here.
body: I have stayed here twice and I love this hotel. I like the modern day look it has as well as the convenience to everything within the city. I even have my friends that met me there compliment the hotel. I will be back soon!

title: Ultra modern and chic
body: An excellent hotel! Ultra modern, chic and state of the art furnishings. The photos on the hotel website are worth viewing. The entire hotel is non-smoking, a plus for those of us who detest having to walk through smoke to get anywhere. The "cabin" we stayed in was not large (typical for Manhattan), but the storage space for clothes, toiletries, etc. was more than in some regular hotel rooms. The room was very bright. The queen bed was partly up against the wall to save space, and with the touch of a button, it slid out for sleeping. Do not be deterred by the lack of reception desk. There is an excellent "crew" (staff) to help with the kiosk check-in, check-out and any other matter requiring assistance. There is also a concierge on the fourth floor to assist with maps, tickets, restaurants, etc. There are a number of computers for your use on floor 4 as well. Breakfast is not included in the price and is typically expensive, but is convenient and very well prepared. There are 2 bars (indoor and outdoor on the terrace) which serve a variety of drinks. Each floor also has a "Galley" which has water, ice and complimentary coffee and tea. There is a parking garage directly accessible from the hotel elevator. Prices are reasonable. Our 6 night stay was very enjoyable. The hotel is on 10th Ave. The Metro Red Lines are 3 Avenues away at 7th.

title: They get the little things wrong
body:
We got into this hotel on a deal so it was inexpensive (< $150) and its small size was not an issue for us. The room was comfortable but was spartanly appointed. The bed was a futon and my old back doesn't handle those well anymore.
The staff is enthusiastic and helpful, but there were many things that were not done properly. The coffee maker in the galley had only decaf coffee one morning, had no cups on another, and wasn't working on the third. We could never make a local call without calling 'mission control'. The TV remote only worked from an odd angle (that took me ten minutes to figure out!). The sheets didn't fit properly on the bed so we found ourselves sleeping on the plastic undersheet. The elevator lobby is too small so getting off of the elevator was difficult as the people waiting to get on had no way to get out of our way.
As I said, these are all small things. Does that warrant a three-star rating? I wouldn't rate it four, so three becomes the only number left.

title: Funky & Fab - do it!!
body: Love this hotel! Just returned from a long weekend in New York, first time. Yotel was around a 5 min walk from Times Square - great location. It's the cleanest hotel I have ever stayed in, and room was cleaned every day. Room was small but roomy enough for 2 of us - cool mood lighting. Bed was wicked, comfy and it reclined! The Terrace bar was always packed in the evenings. Hotel staff really helpful with arranging cabs etc (only waited about 2 mins). Luggage robot thing is really useful on last day. Can't praise this place enough, even the lift music was funky!!

title: A contemporery experience
body: More than just a place to stay, Yotel present you with a true NY experience. Contemporary, young, green and overall fun the stay provides you with warm and happy feelings. It places you at the best posible location within reasonable prices, and most importantaly excellent utilization of space and atmosphere. I was introduced to the hotel by a colleague on a business travel, and will defenitely return every time in town.

title: Yo-yotel
body:
Modern, nice and cozy hotel in New York City. There's a pantry in every floor where you can have nice coffee and drinks.
Times Square is walking distance from the hotel, but that would be a pretty loooooong walk,

title: Interesting concept
body:
A real experience. I had just won this hotel on a travel website, but had good idea it was this property before I booked. I really wanted to just try it from curiosity. Would have loved to have a place like this years ago, but maybe getting a little older and this place maybe a little too hip. 
That said, as I was staying at another property the night before and the Yotel was near the diner I chose for breakfast, I stopped in and asked about early check-in....It was 7 am, Well, if they have a room, they check you in.... or help you to use the kiosk I should say. This really impressed me as I was on just a quick weekend over from Europe for just 2 nights. 
The sunday brunch would have been great if I was not traveling alone. The whole hotel is an excellent concept. 
The little kitchen area on each floor is nice, but it did lead to one maybe un-intended trait, young guests congregated on my floor outside the kitchen and were sitting all around on the floor of the hall and it did not really look "nice" and I would not want them right outside my door. 
The upper lobby was really a part of the night club late and as I had a key issue and had to wait over 10 minutes to get attention and then had clerk on phone the next day for 5 minutes while I waited, was not overly thrilled with the service, but that is sort of the idea. It is kind of a self service concept and very good for what it is. 
A very social atmosghere.

title: Fun Overnighter!
body: My 16 year old daughter and I stayed at Yotel during our stay in NYC. It was close enough for us to walk to the theater, Times Square and the bus station. Our room was spotless and very comfortable. We loved the sleek designs of everything. We had a great time.

title: Would go back
body:
Just a few blocks away from Time Square and Broadway, you couldn't be better located. You can be in the busy, lively part of the city in a less than 10 minute walk, but without all off the lights and noise outside of your bedroom window. The Subway is also close, along with Port Authority Bus Station. After having enough walking, we got a taxi back from a few midtown attractions and never spent more then $10.
After hearing horror stories of NY hotels being the size of a closet, I was worried. Now, the rooms (or cabins as they like to be called) are small. But the best moves into a sort-of sofa, adding a good four feet to the space. We had two girls with large suitcases and we didn't find the space too much of an issue. The bed's aren't amazingly comfortable and I wouldn't recommend it to someone with a bad back problem, but I slept comfortably. 
There is also a lack of privacy as the bathroom doesn't have a door, just a curtain, which would be a problem for some. 
On every floor is a kitchen with fridge, microwave, ice, cold water and hot drinks. All free and accessible 24/7. And the coffee was awesome.
The roof terrace is also great. Not as expensive as you would think.Great food, cocktails and view. We ended up there most nights. The staff were helpful and friendly.
My only real negative, which is currently unresolved, is the cleaning staff. Our rooms were spotless everyday, apart from one where they didn't clean but it would appear they took my iPod. This happened on the day before checkout so would have probably been more aware of keeping valuables in the safe otherwise. 
I wouldn't say don't stay here before of that, just don't be an idiot like myself and leave something like that in full view.

title: YO YO YO YOTEL, IS NOT JUST A HOTEL
body:
AND IT'S A MISTAKE TO CALL IT A MOTEL.Our first room was small with no view. But Enoch upgraded my family to a room with a view on the 25th floor. The best view we EVER had over looking the Hudson.The Concierge and Enoch N., in customer care were excellent resources.
 We walked from the Mega Bus stop to YOTEL NYC ($37.00 for 3 round trip from Pittsburgh, Pa.!!!) and made our reservation on the Grey Line 3 day double decker bus tour with 3 event/meal tickets.(Make GL reservation on internet and pick up tickets in person at 42nd street station to save tax and $5.00 on price per. person.)
 Highlights included eating lunch in all the famous dellies and $8.00 Tai lunch at YUM YUM. The sightseeing cruise on the Hudson is mandatory. China Towns NY Noodle shop was the best meal at the lowest price! The 09/11 Memorial is extremely touching. The Zoos are free on Wednesdays and museums have free hours on certain week nights.
 The only disappointment was muffins and coffee are the only free choice for breakfast every morning. Yotel would be smart to offer yogurt , fruit or oatmeal and rotate these choices. We walked across the street to the grocery store for fruit and Burger King and used chain coupons we collected.
The best surprise was that our Mega Bus stop was in front of Yotel! We had the desk hold our bags and played pool and rested in a private T.V. room until it was time to get on our bus! AWSOME!
 We will be back for the third vacation in NYC soon and will definatly call Enoch for a room with a view! Thank-you YOTEL, we miss you. Loved the free coffee galley!!!

title: Best experience ever!!
body:
Stayed at Yotel for 7 days and all I can say it was absolutely an amazing experience!! It was my first time in New York and this hotel was just perfect, super close to Times Square and all the other things to see, the subway was super close so you could go everywhere very easy. The staff was super friendly and helpfull. Next year I'm coming back for 2 weeks with my best friend and hopefully we can stay at the Yotel again!! 
Breakfast were just muffins, coffee and tea but that was enough, but we didnt need anything else for breakfast :)
rooms were a bit small but everything you needed was there! and be honest how much time do you spend in your room while in a city like this?!
Yotel was just absolutely amazing!

title: Yotel is THE hotel
body:
Trendy, great rooms, close to everything, fun to stay in, love the adjustable bed, the muffins in the morning are divine, the wi-fi is not only fast but free. This is my second stay here and I have loved it both times. My daughter was addicted to the free coffee machine in the galley - apparently it makes brilliant coffee! And I didn't think the walk to Times Square was long at all. We went a different route each time and saw some great stuff. The Port Authority is really close, meaning you have easy access to the subways and can get anywhere and everywhere quickly and easily. There are always taxis out the front, and there are a few buses that run right past (either down 10th of 42nd) so you have easy public transport to anywhere you want to go. Get a Metrocard, and do it like a true New Yorker!
(And I accidentally clicked on the review for a pool....but there isn't a pool. Sorry!)

title: Compact rooms but excellent design and extras.
body:
The minimalist but hyper-functional design of the Yotel is pretty unique - not just in NYC but in all the world cities I've visited. 
Most rooms are "Premium Queens", those on the higher floors have great views over downtown or the Hudson depending on which way the room faces.* Although these rooms are small (around 150 square feet) they are nicely laid out so that it's comfortable for two people, with the only shortcoming being a lack of much hanging space, and the use of a strange bed which is adjustable to maximise space when not in use - but as a result has a harder mattress than a typical hotel bed. Also the Air Conditioning, although effective when it works, is unpredictable and will often blow out lots of cold air one minute and then leave you sweltering the next.
Nice touches include: adjustable lighting, great free toiletries, complimentary coffee and muffins on the lobby level each morning, and a free high-end coffee machine on each floor (no fridge in the room, instead a communal fridge in the 'Galley' on each floor which also has an ice/water machine, microwave and drinks vending machine (paid-for). 
There seem to be lots of different special offers floating around for Yotel so its worth keeping an eye on the hotel site to secure a good rate - I stayed for a week in July and paid an average of about $150 per night including taxes.
There is a very popular terrace/restaurant worth visiting for the sun and view, although table service is pretty terrible (and non-existent in the evening). 
---
* A word of warning, the hotel windows are not as tinted as they look from outside - a friend who lives over the road is constantly amused/disturbed by naked Yotel residents who don't see the need to use either of the blinds provided on each room window.

title: Wow! This place is great
body: I like everything about this hotel. It's great value, clean, the people are friendly, it's in a good location yet a quiet area. I'm telling everyone I know about this hotel. For one or two people this is the place to go in NYC.

title: Scary at first turned out to be Wonderful
body:
It was a little shocking at first, but then you realize how much space you really need- which is not much! and we stayed five days. Fast elevators! We will definitely stay there again. Note: it will help to be very close with whomever you are sharing a pod with- not much privacy in the bathroom area.
Easy to walk to Broadway shows and to the Javitz center for our convention. Saved so much money not having to pay for taxi's. 
There is NO room service, but order at the bar/restaurant GREAT FOOD AND DRINKS get it to go if you want to eat in your room.

title: Leading the way in hotels of the future
body:
Traveled with my daughter to New York and chose to stay at Yotel out of curiosity and great price.
We were pleased with every aspect of our stay. Our "cabin" as they call the rooms, was very comfortable. It is a small space but very well planned out. It reminded us of a cabin on a cruise ship. The bed was comfortable and the cabin was quite soundproof. The galley on each floor has an espresso machine that makes great coffee drinks. To our surprise there were complimentary muffins and coffee available in the morning. I will definitely stay here again. Other hotel chains should follow the example of Yotel.

title: Everything you need and nothing you don't
body: Modernist minimalist masterpiece of a hotel off of Times Square. Perfect crash pad for exploring NYC. Free muffins in the morning to get your day started off right and a beautiful rooftop bar/restaurant that's not outrageously overpriced. Aesthetically chic. Would stay here again anytime.

title: Great value...would stay again...but hard beds
body: The rooms are well designed and equipped. Everything has been thought through. The galleys are convenient for free, tasty beverages if you're not a Starbucks snob. The free muffins for breakfast were very good and plentiful. Did not feel like it would be a super welcoming place for young families, but we did see a stroller or two while we were there. The beds need serious reconsideration. Our whole party (three rooms, six people) complained of very hard beds. If you're sensitive to this and would lose sleep, pick another place. If you can tolerate it, everything else about this hotel was great. (Walk down 42nd not 41st to access the entrance on 10th Ave whenever possible...41st is a little less savory...nothing extreme, but 42nd is just more populated and pleasant to walk.)

title: Ok
body: The cabins and the view are very nice. However, this time I got a cabin with not perfect cleanliness. There were footprints and hair in the shower. Additionally, next day I had some bites at my leg. I do not know if these were bed bug bites and if I got them in yotel, because I could have also gotten them somewhere in the city. Nevertheless, I asked to change the cabin and my request was very easy and satisfactory fulfilled. However, I would have appreciated if my concerns regarding bed bugs would have been taken more seriously. What I really annoyed me during my stay was that internet access was not possilbe. I think it is kind of embarrising that in such a modern-apple-style hotel one of the basic options for modern communication/service was not available. To be clear about this: Of course WIFI was available, but you could only reach the log-in side. After loging in the connection was so slow that it was not possible to access any site. Overall, I still gave an average rate for the hotel due to the fact that it is hard to get a good affordable hotel in new york. Nevertheless, I will not consider the hotel for further stays.

title: Great time at Yotel
body: Very nice and modern Yotel, with very friendly people. We where there for 5 nights and we had a great time sleeping there, sitting on their terrace and they had a good snack menu's. Only 10 min walk form broadway. We liked the Yotel very much.

title: yo!! YOTEL
body: My daughter found Yotel in one of her magazines and we just had to try it out. The location was good. It is however 3 blocks from Times Square. The walk up 42nd street is much better than going up 41st. The rooms are kind of small and there is really no place to put your luggage once you are in the room. It was fun and hip and seemed to be a popular spot for many people. We had to catch a bus to Providence and the Megabus stop is just across the street which was convenient. The closest subway is 6 blocks away. Overall it was fun for a new experience. I would not recommend Yotel for a family.

title: Great value, would stay there again!
body: The hotel is modern & cool. The prices are great for the value you get. The location is perfect, even though it's on 10th avenue (41th Street), a short walk will get you anywhere, isn't that what NY is all about, walking everywhere! :) You can even have a morning run on the trail (5-8 min walk from the hotel) alongside the West Side Highway looking at the Hudson river. Rooms are small but are we only there for sleeping? We were. Rooms are clean and well designed, bed is a bit hard and when room is close to the Galley, you can hear the door trafic late at night (a bit bothering). I recommend and will surely go back.

title: Great Location
body: Very good location, close to the heart of New York, but very small rooms which they call it cabin, no room for your luggage, carpets are not clean and needs to be cleaned, very good for single or young couple, complimentary morning coffee and muffin which was nice. overall pleasant to stay in.

title: Would live there if that were possible
body: This was my 4th stay at Yotel New York. A few days before my visit, I received an email stating that I was eligible for an upgrade. $18 dollars for a King cabin, $75 dollars for the jacuzzi suite. That is pretty amazing, I chose the King cabin, as I have only ever stayed in the regular premium cabins. It was quite lovely and the view was beautiful. I loved the room which was large but believe it or not I missed the elegance of the regular cabin. But that's my quirk. Staff was attentive and courteous as usual, internet was quick and easy to access, roof terrace on four was breezy and comfortable in the New York heat. Overall, I loved every minute. I should mention that have a new program that allows you to rent a bike for $3. I noticed this after I had spent $20 renting a bike in Central Park. My next visit will include this perk!

title: Essentials on a box
body: I stayed at Yotel in NYC on a recent business trip. The stay was booked by my corporate travel department, and mainly chosen on proximity to my work location and price. The room was unique, but very neat and clean. its certainly a different experience. If you are easily confused by self check-in, RFID Room keys, ATM like processes..etc, then dont stay here. The small / cozy size of the room was different from my normal corporate travels, however it was comfortable for a single traveler on an overnight stay. I'm not sure I would recomment the location for any more than a traveling party fo two, or for a long trip. Somtimes you want to have quiet space to yourself in your own room to relax..and at these locations they have community space instead of personal space.

title: Very cool
body:
This hotel constantly surprised me. Ok I was sceptical to begin with, I'm 6'5" and I was booked into a "cabin" it didn't look big. We arrived and tried out the automated check-in, it didn't work, or it sort of did and I got a key but no idea for which room as the printer had run out of paper. A quick look of despair towards the ever helpful staff and it was sorted. Then up to my "cabin", when I first opened the door and looked in I thought that there was no way I could fit in the bed, happiness returned on finding the little button that turned my sofa into a full sized bed - very clever, very efficient, very nicely designed room. I've stayed in smaller hotel rooms that have tried to be bigger, this doesn't try to be anything other than a meticulously designed small room, and it does it perfectly.
As for the rest of the hotel, the position is great, close to the river for walks away from the hustle, easy to get a cab from, and close to Times Square for the subway and everything mid-town has to offer. The 4th floor bar and restaurant area is great, I'll take any chance to sit outside in New York and relax and sitting up there as the sun set was brilliant.

title: Poor showing for Yotel
body:
I stayed at Yotel on 7/18 and the experience was lackluster. I was in "cabin" 2337 and although I checked in during the dinner hour, I quickly left for dinner and did not return until after midnight. **The city was near one hundred degrees this week.** When returning to the cabin the room was in the high 80s. I figured it was part of the "green" approach to the place so I did not think much of it, turned the AC down to 70 and quickly went to sleep. By 3:00am I awoke in a pool of sweat, went to the AC controls and found that the room had not cooled below 78 degrees. In addition, when I went to the bathroom to get a cool towel, the lights in the bathroom did not work. I then went for the light in the cabin entryway...no luck there either. The only lights that worked were near the bed and they provided no light into the bathroom.
The next morning I went to the fourth floor lobby to checkout and mentioned my problems to the desk staff. One of them asked me in an attitude if I had called the desk staff about the AC problem. I let her know that at 3:00am I didn't consider that an option. The other employee curtly asked me my cabin number and neither of them offered so much as an apology for the experience.
Staying at Yotel saved my company $50-75 but it was not worth it. Next time I'll be a slightly less, good corporate citizen and stay at a Hilton or Marriott.

title: Very Cool EXCEPT the Beds are HORRIFIC
body: So it's a real shame that the beds are so uncomfortable or should I say the "futons". The concept here is very cool. I have to give this a poor rating as th ebed is th emost important piece to me in a hotel. Isn't that the main purpose of a hotel? T have a good nights sleep?. The room was very small but it had everything I needed. The lighting was excellent and the decor was super cool. It was also super clean. TThe TV was ca nice HD on the wall, the shower was super clean and nice and I had a nice view out my window for a non view rool. BUT the bed was so uncomfortable that my back still hurts two days later. The more I think about it the more upset I become. I stayed here for business so I didn't mind the very small room. I'm in the office all day and then out to dinner in the evening hours so I spend little time in the room and what's most imprtant to me is to be able to get some sleep and those mattresses are so thin that I could not get a good nights sleep so where is the value? I'd prefer to pay an extra 100 or even 200 bucks for a comfortable night sleep. Another bit of a negative is the location. The surrounding are is kind of rough.. Also, I had a really bad experience in the restaurant. The staff was completely overhwlemed and the place was only 1/4 full. I would go back if they changed those darn futons otherwise it's back to my old standards in NY where I can wake up in the monring refreshed and not grumpy with a very sore back.

title: Clean, well-appointed & friendly
body:
I stayed here with another adult + 2 children in a premium cabin with a double bed and bunk beds. It was a surprisingly large room, with really good storage space (hooks on the entry wall, good closet, under-bed space, clever shelves next to the bed & around the TV) The staff (ground crew) were helpful & friendly throughout our stay. We enjoyed and made good use of the galley (free coffee / hot chocolate & water / ice water, shared fridge & microwave), and the kids particularly enjoyed our view and watching the city bustle 20-something floors below. The only noise that made its way up or into our room was an occasional siren and the usual hallway door sounds - all totally manageable. We had a short walk to many great places to eat along 9th Ave & a do-able walk to the subway at either Port Authority or Times Square. It was not cheap, but we felt that our money was well spent given that we were 4 people, the high quality of the hotel, and relative prices of hotel stays in Manhattan. 
P.S. The logo / retro-modern-spaceship aesthetics of the Yotel were cool.

title: Yotel is awesome
body: I stayed with my teenage daughter in a small room with one queen sized bed. Had a great view from the room. Only a short walk to Time's Square (a couple of blocks) and if you go the other way it's not a bad walk to the water which has a nice boardwalk. You can't beat the price and the decor is very trendy and cool. The rooms are small and compact, like a large cruise ship cabin but I liked that. Everything at your fingertips. The beds were not the most comfortable, but I'm not that picky. They did feel more like a futon, but for the price, I'm OK with that.

title: yotel is not just a hotel!
body: Unique check-in experience and although the room was small, it was adequate for my business travel. Also the location is outstanding.

title: Sexy, Swanky and Futuristic!
body: This hotel was great!! It is more for the young and hip or just hip!!! My husband and I absolutely had a ball! We stayed a quick two days, and our stay was excellent! We even purchased the shower gel "get up". The staff was awesome! "thanks Renee"! We actually arrived into NYC very earlier, and we were actually able to check in at 11 AM with no extra charge! The lounge and bar was phenomenal! Thanks for the Expresso Martini Aaron. The rooms are for the sustainable, Eco friendly person. The design is totally based on saving space, and utilizing every inch of your square footage! It works though. If you are the traditional hotel toom type of person, this is not for you! The COMPLIMENTARY freshly baked muffins and coffee is a perfect start to your morning! It is right in Hell's Kitchen and that means you are within walking distance of some wonderful, delectable, affordable NYC dining! Times Square is just a short walk as well! This is our official NYC hotel!

title: Loved The Yotel!
body:
My husband and I snagged a deal on two nights at the Yotel through a TravelZoo deal, and we were not disappointed (and we had very high hopes!).
Check-in was super easy and convenient. Our room was small, but we expected it to be. Despite its size, it was very clean and the space is used really well - the fact that the bed was adjustable (which saved space when it was sitting upright) was awesome! We stayed in room 1703 and had a really nice city skyline view. 
The muffins that were offered every morning on Four were really nice, too! I expected them to be those small, cheap grocery-store-in-a-box kinds, and while they weren't gourmet muffins, they were really good quality! They had a different assortment every morning including banana walnut, cranberry, blueberry, chocolate chip, chocolate chocolate chip and corn. My husband made good use of the gally on our floor, and he said the coffee and lattes were really good, too.
The location was really convenient. There's a CVS right across the street, tons of pizza places and restaurants, a food emporium, a health food type store, a Pinkberry, etc. I wish more trains were a bit closer because that's all we use when in the city, but they weren't really that far. Some are located in Port Authority, which is just a few short blocks away (a 5 min walk), and of course, there was the Times Square station a few more blocks away, which would get you anywhere you wanted to go. There was a lot in the area readily available to you.
And, let's face it, the Yobot is pretty freakin' cool. 
My only complaint is that to get to your room from the ground lobby, you have to first take an elevator to Four, and then get off to "transfer" of sorts to another set of elevators to get to your room. But that seriously wasn't even a complaint - just something that after a long day of shopping (or, in my case, if you really, REALLY have to pee after a long train ride) was every so slightly annoying.
I would highly recommend the Yotel to anyone, especially if you can get a good deal. It lived up to the hype for us, and it felt like a real experience rather than staying in a typical hotel.

title: Great Hotel, Good Location
body:
We booked Yotel based on Tripadvisor reviews and the fact we got an awesome deal through Expedia.
Upon arrival you are greeted at your taxi by the fellas who handle the check in downstairs. This person then checks you in. He then took us up to our "cabin" and gave us a quick run through things in room and hotel facilities.
We were on the 18th floor in a corner right away from the lifts which had a view down to river. Rooms where a little small but sufficient for my wife and I ( not forgetting this is NYC). Everything looked quiet new and worked as it was supposed to. I could understand how " Bathroom" situation could be a little uncomfortable if you are not "close" with the person you are staying with!
Yotel was well located, an honest 15 minute walk from one end of Time Square. It is actually only 2 blocks from Port Authority Subway however IMO they are 2 BIG blocks. 
The staff downstairs really know their city and job. They have excellent advice and tips and thought nothing of pulling out their personal phone to google the nearest laundry for us! We walked to Empire State building ( on the boys advice) one morning and it took around 20-25mins at a casual pace. Was actually a nice walk with all the locals heading to work. We arrived at Empire State building at 815am and went straight to the top, no queues at all!!
Hells Kitchen was only one block away with some great restaurants and bars. They were all reasonably priced. 
There is a DHL,UPS and Post Office all within 1 block if you need to post anything home.
The only cons are:
Although a good system in principle the "Yobot" luggage storage system is just too slow. If you have say 3 or 4 couples in front of you with say a bag each you would wait around 15minutes to even get to the machine.
It seemed every time you used internet in the room you had to " log in ". Whether this was due to my lack of computer skills I'm not sure.
However i would have no problem staying at Yotel again at the price i paid.

title: I want more Yotel's
body: Yotel was a unique awesome experience. The only reason i was able to afford going was because of the groupon deal i got. But it was great. The lobby is self serve and it was quick and easy. The room's are immaculate and futuristic. It is tiny though! Do not expect anything large. Also, the bathroom is seperated from the bedroom by a clear glass wall with a curtain. Do not expect much privacy from that. But the views are awesome. There are bars and restaurants in the hotel. It's not a long walk to Penn Station or TImes Square. One of the best parts was during the day we had to check out at 11 and were still spending the day in the city, so we checked our bags for free and it's all computerized. You type in a password and a robot will check your bags!! Fun to watch! I would stay here again in a second if i could afford it!

title: spaced out!
body: My partner and I spent five days at Yotel to celebrate my birthday in June. From the moment we walked through the door until we left five days later, we were incredibly impressed. Let's start with the hotel staff, because that's what stands out in a good hotel. All the staff were friendly, helpful, interested and went the extra mile for us. The room was excellent, very well thought out, comfortable, airy, and with a brilliant view of the hudson. The bar and facilities were top notch. Suffice to say we were present at happy hour a few times. In all, hats off to Yotel for a fantastic birthday in New york, We will be back, that's for sure.

title: Let's have more Yotels!
body: We have taken advantage of Yotel Groupon offers several times now and with that discount, Yotel is one of the finest hotel bargains in NY. We have recommended it to friends who want a clean and comfortable place to stay in NYC for a reasonable price (even without the Groupon discount) and they too were pleased. Someone has paid attention to certain details that we liked very much -- the bedside reading lamps, the inclusion of drawers as well as two clothes-hanging bars, several hooks/knobs for hanging towels and clothes, etc. The vertically oriented safe was very easy to use. Don't forget the K-cup coffee machine in the gallery. Only thing I missed there was a nondairy creamer for us lactose-intolerant types -- but soy milk was available at the coffee and muffin included breakfast.

title: Loved it!
body:
Very happy with my recent stay at Yotel. The service we received at check in was excellent. We were very lucky our room was ready for us at 9:30am. The parking garage is very convienent. 
The cabin was just fine. Clean and bright. The view was nice. The muffins were very good. We had to cut our stay by one night, due to an unforseen emergency. When I called to let them know and explained the reason the man was very understanding. I would love to stay here again in the future.

title: Good location, very functional, very clean
body:
I've stayed at this Midtown/Hell's Kitchen hotel for 8 days total this past June and the overall the experience was really good.
On the plus side, I would list the originality of the hotel/rooms, the modern touches and efficient use of space (although the rooms are quite small, you never feel tight), the free coffee/tea on every floor and complimentary muffins evry morning on main level, and the location (2 blocks from Port Authority). I've read elsewhere that there was not much to do in the area but found a lot of bars and restaurants of all kinds on 9th and 10th avenues going northward. It is not as crowded as the rest of midtown which can sometimes be awful, the atmosphere is really nice and there are lots of places to go near the hotel if you don't feel like going too far some nights.
A few caveats I found: the hotel has a rather modern and young atmosphere, which as I said was fine for me, but may annoy travellers more used to traditional/chain-like hotels. Yotel is not hiding this though, just go on their website and you'll get a good feel if this is your thing or not. If you travel as a couple I'd say you need to be pretty close/relaxed, as the rooms are small and bathroom area separated by a curtain only. Finally and this is the only point that really bugged me, the hotel is clearly in full marketing mode to attract new crowds of locals and get a reputation. Problem with that is that the otherwise fantastic terrace gets crowded half the week with your typical hipster crowd. On some evenings you will not even get access to the main terrace if there is an organised event. Pretty lame when you actually stay at the hotel. On a related note some of the staff, especially bartenders and the like, feel entitled by this phenomenon and act like they own the place. Don't expect many smiles from some of them, and one or two can be downright rude.
Apart from this, again really cool stay and overall experience!

title: Great location, trendy atmosphere
body:
We stayed at Yotel for 6 days during a city-trip to New York City in the beginning of May. The location is quite goood : It's a 10-minute walk from Times Square,and you have the Subway at 2 blocks. In the other direction, you have the Hudson river bank with the USS Intrepid on display, and a park with a bike rental.
We had a standard room, which was not big, but cosy and well thought-out. On every floor, there is a 'galley', where you can get free coffee (Italian Lavazza) and several other hot beverages, along with a sink and a microwave if you want to prpare a sandwich or something. There's a Food Emporium accross the street.
Yotel does Happy Hours each night, where they offer drinks at reduced prices, which you can combine with 'tapas'-like small dishes for 4USD a piece. The choice is ok, and the quality is top-notch. 
There's no official breakfast included. The restaurant (Doyo) offers a buffet of all kinds of muffins and hot drinks for all the guests. That's free. If you want something specific (omelette, fresh orange juice, ...), you can order à la carte in combination with your muffins.
I loved the hotel, even though the streets in the neighborhood get very congested on a friday and saturday until after midnight, so it's not really quiet. It's very good value for it's price, and well situated, I loved the geeky side (you checkin on a computer, the reception is called 'mission control' and they have this Yo-bot taking care of your luggage) and will surely come back.

title: Good location, good experience
body:
We decided to stay at this hotel based on Tripadvisor recommendations and we were not dissapointed. The hotel room was clean, bright, and functional (we loved the bed that transformed into a "sofa"); the water and shower pressure were good; and the fourth floor staff were quite helpful. Also, the location of Yotel is excellent: it's in a safe area and just a short walk away from Times Square (and, similarly, close to several Subway stations). The only drawback was the elevator: often the elevator key card reader did not work - you have to swipe your card to punch in your room floor - and so we got stuck going up and down past our floor. Very annoying! 
Other than that, I would definitley recommend Yotel. We would stay again!

title: Great landing / launch pad in NYC
body: Clean, efficient, eco-friendly, good location -- great option if you can get a decent price. Price is sometimes way too much but we got it for around $160 / night, which is good value for money. Wish they had a pool and better gym option -- it's OK but small, stuffy room.

title: New York!
body:
My daughter and I stayed here for the second part of our trip to New York City. We both enjoyed the room, and even though small, it was well designed. There is a gallery on each floor with water and coffee, which was a bonus. Also free coffee and muffins in the morning, helped us start the day, as we are not big breakfast people. Although, I had very few interactions with staff, they were all very attentive and happy to help you out. 
Bathroom in the room is only seperated by curtain, so if you have issues with that, you may want something else. 
Good location, only 2 blocks from Subway, which we used a lot! Lots of resturants on 9th Ave, with decent pricing.

title: Great Hotel!!
body:
Stayed in January 2012.. we picked the hotel based on trip advisor reviews and we were definitely not disappointed! Even from the outside, the hotel is ultra modern looking!! We were greeting by an employee who showed us how to check in.. took all of 1 minute!! Room was very clean, bright & we had great views of the hudson river!! Loved the bed which transforms into a sofa at the touch of a button!! Even though the room was small, there was still ample storage space.. the bathroom is also ultra modern with a curtained glass wall separating it from the main room so be warned! 
Yotel is in a great location less than 10 mins walk from Times Square and less than 5 to the Port Authority Bus Station.. we felt safe walking back to the hotel each night.. we had a late flight home but there was no problem leaving our luggage at the hotel while we enjoyed the last bit of sight seeing.. we will definitely return!

title: Average
body:
