My wife and I stayed in July 2012 and after reading the reviews we thought it would be better than it was. The rooms are small but nothing to complain about, there is a definite issue with privacy, make sure you go with someone your comfortable with. I read complaints about room size and privacy so I expected those things, what I didnt expect is the trickle that came out of the shower. I use a water saving shower at home but these showers were ridiculous, after a hot day walking around Manhattan you need a decent shower, 
Another Issue we found was if someone near by has their window open and they open and close there door it slams. I guess its something to do with the pressure in the room or something which makes the door soft close when the window is closed. Anyway if your neighbors are up early, you are too.
The position is good if you want to be near Times Square and Central Park, the staff are nice and helpful and the check in and check out was hassle free. 
I think it was an ok hotel but I would not recommend it to a friend, mostly because of the touristy position and not the Hotel itself.

title: very friendly service
body: quick and easy to move around, very efficient service, easy parking on ground level. would stay there again. This was a family vacation for four and we were very comfortable in a queen plus 2 bunk cabin.

title: Efficient, modern accommodations
body:
Yotel is different in lots of good ways, and I appreciate their innovative approach to provide an efficient and effective space at a reasonable price. Here's what I especially liked:
+ very clean.
+ very quiet. (no street noise; minimal HVAC noise)
+ spacious, light, and modern feel.
+ bathroom is filled with natural light.
+ motorized bed/couch (in premium rooms).
+ versatile common/lounge area.
+ free hot drinks down the hall.
+ reasonably-priced take-out food service.
+ very responsive management.
In general, the hotel is wonderful. These are the only nits I had...
- take-out food service ends at 10pm.
- there's a coat hanger bar above the luggage bench with a rectangular metal end-cap that can will hurt your head if you aren't careful.
- the black-out blinds aren't effective since there are gaps that let the light through on the sides.
- no in-room fridge (but there's a shared fridge down the hall).
- video input is not accessible on the TV (despite being advertised as a 'media wall')

title: Please keep this up, Yotel!
body: We stayed 6 nights in this hotel and it simply enhanced an otherwise already great holiday. After a long day out exploring the exciting city, it's always nice to return to a clean, nicely made up room for a pleasant shower and good night's sleep and Yotel delivered all that throughout our stay. Yes, the room may be small, but there always was still space to move around, even with four large suitcases and a multitude of shopping bags. The room also came with most of the amenities we could ask for. Many of the reviews highlighted the lack of privacy because only a curtain separates the bathroom from the bedroom, but we found this to be a non-issue for the most part, the curtain was opaque enough and concealed the shower and toilet areas very effectively. Minor gripe is that there were no shelves in the shower area for extra toiletries - we had to place our bottles of shampoo, facial cleanser etc on the floor instead. Check in and check out were hassle free and there was always the friendly and reliable staff around to lend a helping hand. Location is great as well - approximately 10 minutes from Times Square, and it feels safe walking back even late at night as the streets leading to the hotel are wide and well-lit, and the lobby itself is located along the brightly lit and bustling avenue (very reassuring not to have to walk through any dark dank alley/side street). Hopefully the hotel continues to upkeep its rooms and facilities and not let maintenance standards slip as time goes by... will definitely be back if that's the case!

title: Great Location in a Great City
body:
Enjoyed a 4 night stay at Yotel in New York. Great location with easy access to all the tourist 'haunts' - Times Square, River Sightseeing Cruises, Big Bus Tour etc.
Hotel staff were extremely helpful and we could not fault them. As other reviewers have stated the rooms are quire small but at the end of the day you don't visit New York to sit in a hotel bedroom, so they are perfectly adequate.

title: YO... Tel! Don't Miss This Place
body: So I loved the Yotel. It was a small space but I loved the vibe. Very clean! Great Staff. I visited the NYC Yotel with my son. It was cool and fun exactly what I hoped for. The most interesting feature was the robotic arm that stored luggage in the lobby. Bed was comfortable though I wasn't sure that would be the case when viewing the futon style automated couch/bed

title: Would come back
body: The hotel is nice and makes you feel as if you are somewhere in Tokyo with all the modern design inside. The location (although near times square) is somewhat out of the way and far from the action. It is about a 15min walk to the nearest subway. The rooms are somewhat small but the hotel has a vibrant atmosphere that is good at night. We were able to rent four bikes for $3 a piece because the hotel had a partnership with a nearby bike rental shop which was great. We crossed the Brooklyn bridge by bike and got to explore alot of the city for this reason. I would go back.

title: Special trip
body:
This is a great hotel,really clean and very helpfull staff.my wife and I stayed here with my twenty year old daughter and we all loved it.the free tea,coffee,water and ice are an added bonus but you also get free muffins at breakfast time which are beautiful .
The hotel is also very handy to the port authority when arriving and departing new york.

title: July 27th and 28th
body: Yotel was great! My 14 year old daughter thought the Yotel was the best part of the trip and could have spent more time in the hotel room/Yotel enjoying herself. We stayed in a ADA room and loved the big windows with nice views of the Hudson. Fun and efficient and would come again!

title: A definite "repeat" hotel....Really Dig Yotel...
body: My third time back to Yotel... first with Sister, then with Hubby, then with friend... A Very clean, upbeat "young" hotel... good atmosphere, bar, music and love the "galley" to get something to drink at any time.... Keep those special fares comin!!!... Also love Groupon!!! Great central location... walkable to lots ... theater, shopping, piano bars..... great time each time I've gone... Joanne Forte Hampton Bays, New York

title: Good Value but some drawbacks
body:
Just finished a five night stay with my boyfriend and overall we agree it's good value for money. The rooms are small, the beds a little too firm, however for the $170 we paid per night, we're not complaining. 
The biggest drawback for us was location in that we thought it would be much closer to times square than it actually is. It's about a 15 minute walk to the Times Square subway. 
it's pretty new as well and there a trendy patio on the 4th floor. Also, everything was very clean.

title: A unique experience in a hotel.
body: The room was awesome, very clean and just as nice as the online photos. We had plenty of space. The view was amazing. They upgraded us at no charge to a larger room. Very happy that we selected this hotel. I loved the modern atmosphere & decor. It was within walking distance to times square, so location was also great!

title: Unique Hotel Experience
body: This place has a really cool feel to it. It takes a self serve approach to high quality hotels. The compact, but comfortable rooms have all the amenities that you need from a hotel with all the non-sense eliminated. Was in town for some business banking and to watch a Redsox Yankees game. It is about a 5-7 min walk to subways, not bad but there are 2 bus lines that are really close if you dont wanna walk. Lots of great shopping and eats surrounding the hotel. A great hotel, I love the the overall product, as with anything great I wish it was a little cheaper but definitely worth it. Oh, and it does feel like the W Hotel... except the Yotel is better. By comparison the W is usually more expensive and comes with a lot of features and amenities that normal people will never need to use. Yotel gets the nod.

title: Room Did Not Have A Bed!!!!!!
body: everything else was great. How can a Hotel in a major city (i have stayed in small towns and other countries with comfortable sleeping) NOT have a bed!!!! there was a motorized slab of hay which resembled the foundation of a bed...all it needed was a box spring and mattress. I had to go spend $75 on an inflatable bed for my cabin. this ruined my vacation to nyc (inflatable bed is not comfy, but at least I didn't wind up in traction)

title: Great, but a bit gimmicky
body:
Just got back from Yotel after a short trip to NYC with my partner. Overall we had a great stay, but I did feel that some aspects of the hotel were a little bit style over function. 
The hotel is centrally located; literally a few blocks away from Times Square and just a short walk to the subway, meaning you can get almost anywhere in Manhattan fairly easily.
The décor is futuristic, almost space-age in theme (the reception area is called Mission Control and rooms are referred to as “cabins”). Standard room sizes are fairly small, but this is to be expected in NYC. However, the room we were eventually put in (corner cabin on the 22nd floor) was actually surprisingly big. I’d definitely recommend requesting a room on the corner high up, as the views across the city through the floor-to-ceiling windows – especially at night – are breathtaking.
The rooms themselves were spotlessly clean, modern and equipped with everything you’d need for a comfortable stay. The hotel provides free Wi-Fi in all its rooms and I loved the free tea/coffee/ice on each of the floors. A really nice touch. 
The downside for me was the overall feeling of a lack of customer service/warmth from the staff - mostly because you don't ever really interact with them. The check-in/check-out procedure is all done on computer screens in the reception and the short-term luggage check is done by a computerised robot arm!?! This is where I felt the hotel let itself down the most. If there are issues at check-in (as we found when we didn’t get the upgrade we’d requested and paid for) it was difficult to find anyone to speak to about it (and actually resulted in us not getting the room we were promised for the first night of our stay). 
Also, the luggage check is way too gimmicky: fun for a few minutes, but just time-consuming and unwieldy once the novelty factor has worn off. It actually lost one of my luggage items which resulted in me having to wait for almost 30 minutes for a member of staff to find again and then being made to feel like a criminal when I had to prove the bag was mine to the security guard. Worst thing was, they didn't even apologise for their mistake. This could’ve been easily avoided by having an actual person check the bags rather than a computer. I can see why the hotel might think that computerising everything adds to the whole “hi-tech” experience, but for me, it just detracted from the warmth and reassurance you’d get from dealing with real people. 
Saying that though, the positives definitely outweighed the negatives at this hotel and when we got the room we were promised, we were more than happy with it. It’s also good value for the location and standard of the rooms, and there are some nice touches to the place. I feel like if they lost a few the gimmicks, this has the potential to be a really top-notch hotel.

title: Great hotel in NYC!!
body:
We just came back from a 4 night stay at Yotel, and we loved it there. Yes, the rooms are small, but you don't need more than that. It's comfortable, and they got lots of space all around the room to put your stuff. I gotta say, you don't bring in a girl you just met, cause the toilet is so close to the bed, with only a glass door, not sound proof...you gotta ask yourself, am I ready to share that much?
The staff was incredible. Always there to help, very polite. We only had a problem with one employee, the guy at the muffin / coffee place in the morning. He kept hitting on my wife, and all the girls around. Very innapropriate.
But overall, great experience, very clean, well located. There is a parking in the basement of the Yotel, which was nice. We'll go back to Yotel for our next time in NYC :)

title: Love, love, love YOTEL
body: This trendy, friendly, clean hotel near Time Square has a futuristic-mission control type atmosphere. The rooms give you the feeling that you have traveled into the future. The "bed" is a couch when you enter, but with remote control, it glides into a comfy bed. The views are terrific. The outdoor terrace bar lounge is worth every $ you spend. The complimentary muffins and free coffee in the galley are a bonus. I can't wait to go back.... Sandy from Wisconsin

title: Great choice for solo travelers!
body:
This is a great hotel if you are traveling to New York by yourself, want to stay within walking distance to Times Square, and don't want to pay very much compared to similarly located hotels.
As should be obvious from all the other reviews, this is NOT a great hotel if you will be staying with more than one person, unless you are comfortable having that second person observe the finer details of your bathroom business. 
Luckily I was visiting solo, and thus had no worries about the lack of bathroom privacy. The Yotel was my home base for a crazy last-minute trip to New York, and it was a great choice from my perspective. Here's why:
1. The tiny rooms didn't bother me because A) It's Manhattan; B) I was staying by myself; and C) folding up the electric bed really does give you a lot more room. Plus a floor-to-ceiling window with a great view of Manhattan makes everything better. 
2. Almost every Yotel employee I talked to was super friendly and helpful. Especially the guy manning the Yobot. Speaking of the Yobot, it's definitely gimmicky, but also cool to know no one is going to mess with my luggage!
3. The free muffins and coffee in the morning more than sufficed as my breakfast. There were lots of varieties to choose from, and all were perfectly decent.
4. The "galley" concept worked great, except when the coffee machine was full of single-serve packets and needed to be cleaned out (and I was in no mood to go without coffee). Thus I ended up making a huge mess as I emptied the cup receptacle. Whoops. Well, at least I (and those who came after me) could drink my morning coffee as God intended.
The shared refrigerator in the galley is a great idea in theory, but I was certain it would lead to rampant, anonymous food theft in the dead of night when the hard-partying crowd came back in from the clubs. However, I put 4 bottles of Dogfish Head 90-minute IPA in there on Friday and not a single one disappeared during my stay (well, except the ones I drank of course). Now, that's a beer even I might consider stealing from a communal fridge. Apparently, the honor system works. And it is nice to have the convenience of a fridge with a grocery store right across the street.
5. For the price, it's hard to beat the location. The Yotel is just 2 blocks from the 42nd street / Port Authority station, where you can catch tons of different trains to go anywhere you want. It's within easy walking distance to Times Square, fun bars in Hell's Kitchen, or Shake Shack on 8th when you need a quick burger fix. If you need to stay in the Times Square area, this is a comparatively non-touristy option.
6. Technology-wise, the WiFi was fast, the plugs were plentiful, and the TV was huge. You can only access your floor via keycard swipe in the elevator - so I felt very secure.
Now, a few minor complaints:
1. The housekeeping is inconsistent, and you are only provided with one toiletry item (a 2-in-1 body/hand wash and shampoo). 
2. The Yotel is like IKEA during the day, and Studio 54 at night - I'm talking purple lights, heavy bass music, and bouncers. But not every night, and not super late - I got home at 2am Saturday and could have heard a pin drop. However, I made myself scarce between 6 and 10pm. 
3. It would sometimes take me 10 minutes to get from my room down to street level because there are two separate elevator banks which need to be navigated, and the elevators do not always arrive in a timely manner.
4. The electricity in your room is dependent upon your key being present. This is a European thing which I rarely see in US hotels, and yes I know it's to save energy, but come on. It's 100 degrees outside, and I have to come back to a stiflingly hot room and wait for the air conditioning to kick on until it senses my key card???
Overall, there was more good than bad for me. I got a really reasonable room rate, and if I were taking another solo trip to NYC, I would definitely consider the Yotel!

title: Excellent experience, I would highly recommend to anyone.
body:
Four of us (girlfriends) travelled to NYC in July 2012. We stayed in two rooms at the Yotel. Location, staff, room, cleanliness, everything was amazing. It was absolutely worth the money (not that expensive) and it was perfect for our needs. Wifi was fantastic, continental muffins and coffee were perfect. Everyone who works there was extremely helpful and friendly. 
The continental breakfast was great, muffins and coffee/tea, really hit the spot. There is also other food for purchase at reasonable prices. The atmosphere, decor, and music was very cool. It was definitely somewhere I would highly recommend and stay again. They really know how to maximize the space in the hotel rooms. The shower gel/shampoo is provided in the shower and by the sink. I also bought a bottle to bring home because it smelled so amazing and was also organic. 
Cleaning service was also fantastic. Our room was always spotless when we returned and we were given new towels every day.

title: Perfect NYC location!
body:
We drove into the city and the location of Yotel was perfect. We parked directly underneath the hotel and took an elevator up to the lobby. The staff is professional, friendly, and incredibly helpful. We are a family of four - not the typical clientele for this hotel. Most people were couples or small groups of people in their 20's and 30's; however, everyone made us feel welcome - possibly because our kids are older and well-behaved. We stayed in a room with a queen bed and the sofa that converted to bunk beds, and it was perfect for us. The room was comfortable and clean. We were two blocks from Times Square, which allowed us to walk to many destinations or to easily get the subway. We were not able to check in when we arrived, but we used the storage system, and it was not only convenient, our kids thought it was very cool. I cannot say enough about the friendliness of this staff. Customer service is clearly a priority at Yotel, and it made our trip much more pleasant to know that we could ask questions without feeling like we were bothering anyone. We would absolutely stay here again: excellent value and perfect location!
I would caution anyone who needs absolute privacy: the bathroom door is open at the top, so there is not much privacy. You cannot see through the door, and the bathroom is spacious, but if you are someone who really needs "alone time," this bathroom might make you a little uncomfortable. It worked for us, and it was much bigger than many hotel bathrooms, but it is worth mentioning.

title: Modern, clean, efficient stay at great concept in NYC
body: I was spoiled with a corner cabin, great views, room had everything a business traveler needs, lots of outlets, nice dock for my iphone at bedside, decent lighting, decent size bath for NYC hotels. There is a lot of action/energy in the lounge, if thats what you need. Convenient location to Times Square and A,C,E subway. Clean, modern, efficient check in/check out. They have it right.

title: Excellent hotel experience.
body: During a recent business trip, I had the pleasure of staying at Yotel. It is the perfect hotel if you are traveling alone. It's a bit small and the rooms lack privacy if you are with someone but if it is a solo trip. Yotel is perfect. The checkin and out are very fast and efficient, the rooms are clean and organized and the price is excellent.

title: The greatest choice for couples in New York city
body:
Great hotel, clean, bright, excellent location, affordable. From the moment we opened the door we fell in love with the room. It is very important to have a comfort and privacy in a clean and modern environment on your vacation for your hard earned money, we got it all.
TV, air, internet and everything else you need on your trip was there, all inclusive...even the "galley" concept worked great, the coffee was great and you could have as many as you wanted. 
Our room was always spotless when we returned and we were given new towels every day.
We were nicely surprised with professional, friendly, and incredibly helpful staff. Yes, we had a good time. Only thing I would ad to the room is a tiny little fridge, everything else is just good the way it is - excellent. I would recommend it to everyone and I would stay there definitively again.

title: Great clean rooms, small but perfect
body: Check in/out were really easy and quick, room was small and clean, didn't have a problem with the size as I spent most of my time out of the room. The staff were really friendly and helpfuly. Free internet in the lobby and wifi in you room, there is also a small gym and lots of rooms with couches and TV's. Would definitely stay here again.

title: Yotel in New York-Wonderful experience.
body: This is a great place to stay. The rooms are not huge but the hotel is wonderful. Easy walking distance to Times Square, restaurants and Broadway shows. It is located in a very safe neighborhood. Grandkids 17 & 18 walked to and from Times Square many times as late as midnight. No problems. The staff is wonderful-very friendly and helpful. Galleys with coffee and water on each floor. Great muffins and coffee on the fourth floor every morning. Great place to stay.

title: holiday in new york
body: we had a fab time in new york.......we stayed at the yotel it was fab.....rooms small but u just sleep there....room cleaned every day...... views from hotel r fab..........tea and coffee machines on same floor in its own room....staff very helpful and friendly......they have club nights with famous djs .....10 min walk from centre time sq.....a very modern hotel......we would stay here again......we love new york... xxxxxx

title: Modern, hip, Euro-style hotel
body: Located in a fairly quiet, but not unappealing, area west of Times Square (Tenth Ave. at 42nd St.), the Yotel offers, clean, modern accommodations. The rooms are tiny (like a cabin on a cruise ship), but well-designed and functional. Being a new building, I noticed no 'dents or scratches' in the room. The hotel is more suitable for young people (singles and couples), but is not unwelcoming to others. The small room size and the fact that it's just outside of the Times Square area (and two long blocks from the nearest subway) mean that the prices are reasonable--yet there is a good level of style and comfort for the price. There is a very attractive restaurant/lounge area on the fourth floor offering views of the city and a small plates/tapas-like menu. Free muffins, coffee and tea are offered in the morning. Each floor has a room with an ice machine, pop machine, and microwave oven. There is no mini-fridge, bar or snack food items offered (for sale) in the rooms.

title: Great value, great location
body: Rooms were small but modern, very well designed and clean with free wifi. Location was excellent and only 5 mins walk from Times Square. Free coffee and muffins were nice in the mornings. Didn't try restaurant. Staff very helpful. Would definitely go back!

title: Cute but too pricey
body: High coolness factor and cute cabins, but bath was not clean, floor dirty and coffee machine (a good idea) was not working. Price, at almost $400 for a night, was well-beyond appropriate for what received.

title: Modern Funky Hotel
body: We stayed for 4 nights at yotel. It is a fabulous hotel so modern and quirky very different from other hotels in NY. Fantastic location 5 min from times square but far enough out of the hustle bustle to get a good nights sleep. Muffins and tea/coffee offered every morning which was nice. Internet was also free in the hotel at the reception. Rooms were small but very cute and put me in mind of a wee space cabin. Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who was thinking of going to NY you wont be dissapointed!!!

title: Yotel, hotel, wowtel, funtel, greattel!
body: What a great concept, check into your private cabin, everything you need in a great little space. Staff are great! They will bend over backwards for you. Check in and out where fast and easy as it is done through a computer screen, spits out yours keys when you arrive and swallows them up when u check out. Totally fantastic visit!

title: Yotel has got it right
body: We need more hotels like Yotel. My husband and I love to travel and although we like to stay at nice hotels we don't want to spend an arm and a leg on an over-luxurious hotel with all sorts of amenities that we won't need- especially when in a city like New York where one's hotel room is just a place to sleep. At the same time we don't want to stay in run down hotel. Yotel has struck the perfect balance. Everything is ultra new and clean as well as chic and modern. The rooms are tiny but they are well designed. The restaurant is great and I recommend it for dinner especially if you arrive late on your first night (as we did). There are also free muffins and coffee in the mornings.The vibe of the hotel is very cool (designed for a young, hip crowd). However this isn't a hostel filled only with 20 somethings. It's fun and fresh while being suitable for all ages (at least anyone who doesn't mind a fun and lively vibe). At night you could hear a pin drop on the hotel room floors. The customer service at the hotel was also excellent. Everyone working there had a great attitude. We got a great deal on the hotel @ $164/ night. For that price and considering its central location, this was a great value.

title: Pricey space themed hotel
body: High price with complimentary breakfast limited to muffins and coffee, very small room, and not overly helpful staff. It may be convenient to Times Square but there are more nicer, much more afforable places accessible via the Subway.

title: If Ikea went into the hotel business....
body:
Just returned from 4 nights at Yotel and the experience was very pleasant overall. Rooms are definitely minuscule but like many have said, you don't feel overly compromised for it. I will say this. ...I missed an actual bathroom with a door (thats not clear glass anyway) I dont care how close you are with somebody....it's unpleasant to feel so exposed. Here is where you do miss the extra space between the bathroom and the sleeping area. 
The staff are very helpful, the rooms are very clean, and the location is excellent. On the negative side, the beds are like futons- I guess this is why they can convert up and down. The first night was uncomfortable for both hubby and me but subsequent nights we seemed to get used to it or were too exhausted to notice. The bedding and pillows were nice so I requested a couple of extra pillows and placed them under me which seemed to help a bit. It was so hot and humid this past week we didn't really take advantage of the outdoor terrace but it was nice. On the weekend it was hopping. We were told by a waiter on restaurant row that Sunday brunch at Yotel is very popular with drag queens and gays and I'm sure it's a hoot to people watch on the 4th floor but we ended up shopping instead. A very fun, young vibe prevails here overall. For the excellent value, cleanliness and location in expensive NYC, Yotel is a great find.

title: Sweet
body:
Upgraded to a corner room with a view onto the Hudson and 42nd street which was great and I think a slightly larger room. Had a disconcerting leak coming through the celing in the bathroom but staff attended to this quickly and efficiently. Good location, you can easily walk to the Port Authority bus terminal, tourist ferry routes and Times square. We also walked one afternoon the length of 42nd street from the UN via Grand central station.
Friendly helpful staff - just dont leave it too late to try and flag down/arrange a cab to the airport!
Great free breakfast muffins, free water & coffee etc. + a fridge for any food you want to store
Also free wifi

title: Great hotel
body: A new and great concept. Rooms are small but well designed and adequate. Have everything you need and then some. Great rates for a Times Square NYC hotel. Really enjoyed our stay and will definitely go back. Hope more hotels like Yotel.

title: Fun,Lively, Easy, Contemporary !
body:
New concept, easy as boarding a plane in First Class, well organised in short but perfect space.
Helpful, welcoming staff with no snobishness as often seen in many hotels. 
Great music for every time of day, joyful Terrace where you long to hang around at all ours. 
Well situated, walking distance from the High Line so then to Meatpacking, Greenwhich, Times Square and Midtown, and subway of course ACE line getting you every where .

title: Business & Pleasure
body: Premium queen cabin was small be very well-appointed. Staff was courteous, friendly and available to respond to needs relatively quickly. I enjoyed the custom bath gels rain shower. The main floor staff is always very attentive to your needs as it relates to check-in, luggage storage, and hailing a taxi (which is very important in the city). The Kiwi-Crush Martini which is available in Dohyo Restaurant on Four is a must have!

title: Great and stylish place
body: My wife and I spent two nights at Yotel New York. I liked it very much - my compact room had everything I needed. I'm happy that we upgraded to Premium view cabin - what a nice view! Hotel's parking was expensive, I found a fantastic deal through Groupon at Icon Parking just one block away - for $16/day for my SUV! You will love their huge patio, morning muffins and coffee.

title: Innovative ideas - with a number of issues. Great location!
body:
Having once been for a drink at the Yotel, we decided to stay there and this is how it was...
The idea at the Yotel is that people do as much as possible in self service. Nobody who stays in a Yotel for the first time manages through the process on the computer with out help from the staff. Our reservation was first not found, there was no information, how many keys we get... And as we then finally had checked in, a bell boy told us to go and check inn again in the 4th floor to change the room if we did not want to live directly on the top of the restaurant(very nice of him). So we took the lift up to the fourth floor where there is a front desk and checked in again! A normal check in right away at the arrival would have saved us a lot of time. Older people and people not used to using computers would be totally lost and not feel welcomed. As we were going to take a late afternoon train on the next day out of NYC we asked the bell boy, how long we can keep the cabin. He said it is always 24 hours. We found the idea of having our cabin (hotel room) for 24 hours very innovative and pleasant and asked him if it really is like that and how great it is... The next day I just happened to look at the note we had gotten at check in and saw that the check out time is 11 o'clock. I rang the front desk to enquire, which information given to us is right. the lady at the front desk said in a very rude way: "nobody has told you that you could stay 24 hours, our check out time is always at 11am!" She told me I was a lier and said that I had made the whole thing up with the 24 hours!!! As I asked for her name, she hung up.
Our cabin was small but we did know that as we booked in. Everything is still rather new, clean and well maintained. The bath room is in the cabin with the toilet behind a see through shower cabin. Should you wish some privacy in the bath room or the toilet, a curtain can be closed to separate the rest of the cabin from the sanitary area. 
We had asked earlier on at the front desk if we were to check out at the desk, or downstairs at the computer. We were told to do it downstairs at the computer so there we were again, as at check in. The screen said to insert the key, but it did not say in which of the three slots. One of the bell boys behind our backs yelled at us; "not there, the second slot from the bottom". The computer did not find our reservation, not with the key and not with my name. The bell boy came over, asked for our cabin number, wrote it down and said; "it is ok then, put the second key into the slot all the way down". Again, this was much more complicated and took more time than checking out with someone from the beginning on. Earlier on we had already asked about leaving the luggage at the Yotel till the afternoon so we knew about the automatic storage. None of the bell boys standing around, chatting helped us. As the whole process did not work again, someone behind our backs yelled; "keep pressing it!" As we finally had the first box open and lifted the first heavy suitcase in, we thought again - how would anybody manage again, who could not lift the luggage themselves... Writing your name and a code takes lots of time and the touch screen is very unpleasant to use. Every letter has to be given in a number of times and even a short name needs a number of corrections. After about 15 to 20 minutes we were still lifting one suitcase after another in and out of the storage boxes and waiting for the machine to lift the boxes slowly in and out, start the process again and so on... As we were finally done and all our luggage was in the storage I asked the bellboy who had been commenting our doings from the chat circle in the back if it would not have been easier if he would have just come over and helped us - he laughed at my face and walked away! We decided that we would reserve an hour for getting the luggage out in the afternoon, not to miss our train. As we came back, we were lucky to find only one person in front of us getting his luggage out - so in just over 10 minutes it was our turn to try our luck with the machine. After having had lots of trouble again giving the codes in on that not well working touch screen. We thought again how much nicer it would have been to have one of those bellboys help people with the luggage in stead of standing around in the chat circle and having to do everything our selves. How many of the people behind us in the queue for the luggage machine missed their flights and were late coming where ever they were going...

title: Quick trip
body: Great service even though it is a boutique hotel. The only down side is the shape of the sink because the water did not drain as fast.. But other than that, great location. Close enough to walk to all of the "touristy" spots, but far enough to not have to deal with the heavy foot traffic. The food on the 4th floor was great. Didn't like one plate and the manager did not hesitate to offer a different plate. Great service again. I will def come back!

title: Yobot FTW
body:
It was a great experience at Yotel. The cabins are super modern and we got a free upgrade to a room with a view. Some of my friends who live in New York had always passed the Yotel and wondered what was in it, so you can tell that the design is just great. It is a little bit of a walk from Port Authority, and the nearest subway station is Port Authority (about a 5-10 minute walk). 
I think the service I most appreciate is when the Cabin Staff cleaned our room even though we didn't put up a sign to notify them to do so. We were still sleeping the first time they came around, so it shows that they made an effort to make sure all rooms are clean with new towels for all their guests. 
We also really enjoyed the quick WiFi, shower and the funny cabin crew at the main floor. I have read these reviews before my trip and was a little worried about the mattress. It is a little thin and not as comfortable as some beds in other boutique hotels, but my boyfriend and I enjoyed our sleep anyways. The room is really well designed and makes use of every space.
Truly a great hotel. Great value. Will come back again.

title: Alive and full of energy!!!
body: This hotel was a lot of fun. It is full or energy and the hotel staff is excellent. If you are looking for something diffferent and for a great price, this is it. The bars are awsome!!! The food is great and priced reasonably.

title: Futuristic Fun!
body: This hotel is something futuristic from the moment you walk through the revolving door. Up from the lobby to FOUR, the floor where it all happens - the daylight complimentary breakfast, the afternoon lunch, or drinks out of the patio with a look at the NYC lights. Check out local events on a Kiosk or talk to one of the Mission Control Staff. Either option is very informative. Free internet access from the computers on FOUR and free WiFi throughout the hotel. Take the elevator up from FOUR to your Cabin and feel free to relax on the futuristic futon/bed. This is by far a large room for NYC standards to relax or get cleaned up to spend the night out on the town. The rooms are very clean and hotel staff is very friendly. If you forgot the toothpaste, you can find some down on FOUR at Mission Control. If you're looking for a good night's sleep, this is the hotel. There may be a party on FOUR, but you would never know it. The hotel was very quiet!!! We were even there for the fourth of July. We watched the fireworks from the window. I loved this hotel for my 14 yr old and I. We will make it our hotel for all future stays in NYC. Thanks YOTEL for a wonderful experience in NYC!!!!

title: Great modern hotel
body: We stayed there for two nights. Great location. Walking distance to Time Square. Very clean and well organised room. We stayed in a premium view queen cabin. The bed was very fancy which was able to lengthen and shorten. The terrace and the front desk area are very contemporary.

title: Fantastic! Would definitely stay again!
body:
Fantastic hotel! The staff was so friendly, the hotel was hip, modern and very clean. I enjoyed the free WiFi as well as the access to free computers on the main level. Coffee and muffins are available for free every morning which meant we never had to buy breakfast. This hotel is located about 4 blocks from the heart of Times Square which for the money, is totally worthwhile. There is a pharmacy conveniently located across the street as well. The room is small but is really well designed to make the best use of space. The bed was comfortable and there was always hot water.
I would specifically recommend this hotel for young adults but anyone would enjoy.

title: Great place to stay!
body: My 14 year old son and I stayed at Yotel for one night. We had so much fun. My son loved all the extra features and the overall theme of the hotel- especially being able to plug his Ipod into the tv, the moving bed, and the neon lights. The room was small, but so are most in the city, and they used the space very well-so much room for storing things. The muffins for breakfast were very good and made our first meal of the day easy. We felt very comfortable in the area with no problem walking back to the hotel at night after seeing a show. I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Small but clean
body: This hotel was perfect for two people. I can't imagine bringing a family to this hotel. The room was compact but everything looked clean and new. Don't expect a ton of privacy between the bathroom and bedroom- there just isn't that much space between the two areas. This hotel was about a 15 brisk walk to Times Square and a $10 cab ride to China town. The roof top bar offered a great place for us to meet our friends who were local. We would definitely stay again.

title: Lovely
body:
Fantastic. When you arrived at the reception, you feel in Times Square. Different hotel with automatic reception. You have to check in alone but some staff are around if you need help.
Good situation, near Subway and Times Square.
Litte room but very funny for couple in my point of view. We didn't try the restaurant but it seems cosy.
I think it's a good deal for young person and couple. Really good experience.

title: Can't wait to go back!
body: Very pleasant stay after a shaky check in. I had prepaid my room but they didn't have a record of it so it took 30 minutes to figure it out. At that point, I wasn't too impressed with this hotel. But after that, we had a a great time. The room was very small but it had everything you needed and was very clean. There wasn't alot of privacy but it's perfect for two people. We loved the outdoor patio where we had drinks and breakfast. The location was great as we pretty much walked everywhere. The rate was good for a hotel that close to Times Square. WeIf yo would definitely stay there again!

title: Total joke of a "hotel". I think I've been punked
body: The bed was a FUTON! Hard as a rock, got no sleep the four nights I stayed. Called the front desk and all they could offer for the horrible beds was a higher floor with a better view. Secondly, it was a complete pain to take two different elevators to get in and out of our room. If you enjoy shopping at IKEA and have the desire to spend several nights in their store, Yotel is the place for you.

title: Rooms small but perfectly formed....
body: Rooms small but perfectly formed....my daughter and I stayed here for one week and can highly recommend it. The 'cabins' have everything you need and the reclining beds are a brilliant idea...comfortable as well as cleverly providing extra space. The bathroom, although in the room, is screened off for privacy with glass doors and curtains so we found that fine. The staff are very helpful, especially the lobby staff. Our only negative was the hot drinks machine wasn't working on our floor for the whole week (and not on the floor higher or lower either) - clearly this is a problem Yotel need to adress as this was the one thing that made our stay less enjoyable - there are no facilities to make drinks in the rooms themselves. We found the fridge and microwave in the kitchen on the floor very useful though. Free muffins and drinks for breakfast felt like a treat and the terrace outside was refreshingly pleasant - even the piped birdsong felt fun! Altogether would highly recomend this hotel for service, comfort, location (we walked easily to Central Park and Times Square) and sheer style...well done Yotel ! Di & Bekah H.

title: Great Hotel--but did not sleep
body:
Positive:--
When I arrived at Yotel in the afternoon. I thought it looked like an upscale futuristic hotel, I checked in very easily at the kiosk, i was asked if I needed help, the staff was friendly and nice.. Took the elevator to 4 and then to my room, you tap your card key on the elevator which is a good security measure. The halls were very clean and quiet, I got to my room which looked so fabulous, i loved the decor, very modern.very Ikea. The view overlooking the hudson and the new high rises was spectacular. I did not think the room was small at all, perfect for 2 people. The bed adjusts up and down, very nice feature, there is a purple light that comes out behind the tv,,I found it super relaxing... The galley down the hall, has coffee machine with free espresso, cappucino, latte,,, ice, and a soda vending machine. loved this.
It was very quiet, i did not here anything at all -all night. except when someone opens a door my door shakes.. I was out at night and the 4th floor was empty, nobody at the lounge/restaurant/--hotel empty as well..I was surprised.but it was quiet and staff/security very nice and friendly/professional.. When i was checking out though, they seemed overwhelmed with people.
The hotel is located in area which is in a recent renovated and built up -upscale area of Hells Kitchen, Luxury high rise condos, rentals, co-ops, right by such as MIMA right by,,residential area.. its is away from the craziness of Times Square, yvery quiet et only just 2 blocks away.. you are also about 3 blocks away from Hudson River Park where The Circle Line/Intrepid is.. Perfect to take a cruise or just relax in the park and take in the view.......then just walk back to your hotel. Just across the street from the hotel is a 24 hour CVS which is a drugstore/sells food. Across the street is also the Food Emporium-supermarket.. 
If you walk down from the hotel 10th ave to Times Square on broadway or from broadway walking back to 10th ave to hotel,, i would use some precaution at nigh time, that small stretch of blocks is shady and some weird. people around.... The Covenant House is located right next to Yotel,, on 41st st--its a homeless shelter for teens and runaways.
Negative:
The Room- I always do a bed bug inspection when checking into a room. I used my flashlight to inspect and look around the bed and room. I did not find any bed bugs visible. I did notice the console next to the bed where you store your laptop in was so filthy and disgusting, it looked like it had not been cleaned in a year. If i didn't use my flashlight to look in, i would have not known. Room was clean but not spotless. If you are sharing the room with a friend/relative it can be awkward with using the bathroom. I feel the hotel should have installed a sliding door to divide this area instead of the curtain.......I was pretty comfy lounging in the bed watching tv -very relaxing but when i went to bed it was horrible. I went to bed and adjusted the bed all the way down.. I am easygoing and don't mind sleeping on a couch but this bed was very hard. What other people say is true, very uncomfortable. On top of that I started itching, I ignored it but it continued. I put the lights on, did not see bed bugs, but i did notice some black pepper like spots on the sheets.. I ignored it, went back to bed. itched again. I just could not sleep and just stayed up all night, sitting in a chair.. it was only a 1 night stay....I did put my bags in the shower for precaution if it was bedugs, i didnt have any bites but i did feel itchy.. Maybe its the linen/sheets they used that caused the itching or maybe the detregent chemicals they are washing it with...
Its really too bad about the bed, if this didn't happen i would give it 5 stars :(

title: Beyond expectations
body:
The location is bliss! Close to Port Authority and a few minutes walk from Times Square. Also really close to Hudson River and the jogging track. It's easy to reach almost everything from Port Authority Terminal. A big difference among other hotels is that Yotel cabins are very well sound insulated. The shower needs more pressure. I was at the 17th floor and the view was great! I will definitely go back and recommend to my friends. 
The included "breakfast" is nothing but muffins and coffee. If you want juice you have to pay like $4 for a small one, not a great experience on that. The Galley on every floor is really useful if you have leftovers from a diner or something, you can use the fridge, get some ice and buy sodas at an affordable price, but if you want something more, there's a convenient CVS across the street recently opened. 
It's true that the air con is noisy, it seems that always is running on high fan speed, that could be improved.
The people from mission control and the bell boys are always willing to help, very friendly!

title: A Great Hotel Experience
body:
Initially my wife and I could not understand what this place was about. Rooms are "Cabins" ??? As soon as my wife and I walked in (for our weekend stay) we realized this was something different and pretty amazing. Every staff person we encountered was warm, friendly and helpful. We loved our room (#1729) Nice view down 42nd St toward the Hudson, only partially blocked by a building across the street. Everything in the room was sleek and new. Climate control was perfect and very quiet, practically soundless. We liked the bed that could be partially turned into a couch. It was very comfortable. 
The 4th floor offers an enormous terrace. I don't think there can be many places that match it in NYC. We did not eat there, but hung out there in the morning. After we returned to the Yotel from breakfast on Sunday we were greeted on the 4th floor by dancing and music at noon!
Location is 10th Ave and 42nd street. This is 2 long blocks to a subway which is pretty close.
Caveats: 
1. At busy times the robotic system for checking luggage is useless. It takes a while for each person to read the display, press the right buttons and wait for the robotic arm to take the luggage. At one point on a Sunday morning there were 30 people lined up. Grab a "Cabin Crew" member and they will take check your luggage the old fashioned way.
2. We asked for a recommendation for breakfast and the staff sent us to the Theatre Row Diner just a block away. It was a very bad choice, especially given all the wonderful places to eat in NY,

title: yotel ay ee oooo
body: We've stayed at Yotel twice in the last year. It's mod and comfortable. Location is mediocre in terms of proximity to subway and "destinations" except the Theatre district. It is located in Hell's Kitchen, so there are some great restaurants. The terrace is lovely and has wonderful views.

title: If you can sleep on a futon.....
body: ...then this hotel will suit you fine. Exceptionally clean, the "cabins" are compact but include nearly everything you may need. Our room on the 11th floor was quiet and offered a nice view. Bring earplugs if AC blowers bother you. Only two drawbacks: the beds are all futons, and thus very firm, with no "give' to them. When requested, a blanket was provided to place underneath the sheets, but it was still uncomfortable for this side-sleeper. Sumptuous linens. The gimmicky "Yobot" was functional but quite slow, so allow extra time to store or pick up luggage in case there is a line of folks in front of you.

title: Family trip to NYC
body: Our stay at the Yotel was very pleasant. It was very clean, efficiently run and the staff was helpful. We loved the complimentary muffins and coffee every morning, they were delish and saved us from grabbing something on the move. We loved starting and ending our day on their lovely terrace. They were a quick 20 minute walk to Times Square and the neighborhood you walked through was very nice. When we were leaving our limo was hit by a car and had to wait for a policeman to come. The young man, Christopher, who had helped us load our luggage quickly went in and got the manager. The manager of the Yotel got us two brand new SUV's for the same price as the limo so we didn't have to wait for the police report. I would highly recommend Yotel. The cabins are not large, but in NYC the only time you are in your room is to sleep and change your clothes. It was perfect for our needs.....and the children loved the "high tech" look of the place.

title: Great NYC hotel
body: Father and daughter visit, three nights. Cabin cozy, clean, fun. TV worked well. Futon bed was hard at first but we got used to it quickly. At night, other clients were noisy as they returned from clubs at 2-3AM; see if you can get far from elevators! Muffins and coffee at breakfast were delicious. Staff were very friendly; the international clientele added a nice touch. We heard Spanish, French, Russian in the elevators. Good view out of our 25th floor window. We will definitely return!

title: Excellent Stay
body:
Great location only minutes away from Times Square. 
We loved the rooms - we opted for a terrace & hot tub which was well worth the extra money.
All the little extras really added to the experience:
- ipod connection
- Kitchen on each floor
- Extremely comfortable beds
- FANTASTIC shower gel (seems unimportant but was really good!)
Two things let the hotel down, the check in process was difficult because they were doing work to the rooms on the 8th floor (the rooms with hot tubs / terraces) so we were asked to move, but we did get compensated, and found the staff to be very helpful.
Also, we thought the showers were not powerful enough 
But all in all, very minor stuff.
I'm travelling to New York again shortly, and I'll definitely be staying at Yotel.

title: Love the purple
body: We really enjoyed our two night stay. (Friday and Saturday night) We never heard any noise! In fact, we even commented how quiet it was in our room. Our cabin was comfortable, modern, clean, and met all our needs. Starting the morning with muffins and coffee on the terrace was a great way to start the day. We look forward to another stay around Christmas time! We highly recommend the Yotel.

title: I would recommed to all of my friends!
body:
Last year My husband and I went to Europe, and we found great hotels with cheaper prices and we were getting a little disappointed with NY, until we found Yotel. The idea is great! A kind of luxury hotel with a great price, close to everything you need. The rooms are small, but good enough for 2 or 3 people, the bathroons are great (with the best organics soaps). The AC works fine, the lobby is great and the restaurant at the hotel is also very nice.
It's 3 blocks from times square, staff is really friendly and you can hear no noisy even being so close to the center of NYC.
I went with my husband, my parents and my brother, and we all loved it. I will definetly stay there again in the future.

title: Exceptionally nice
body: I recently spent 3 nights at the Yotel New York City. This was my first visit to the city and I was really excited. I searched very frequently for deals on hotel stays and really found every one very expensive. The Yotel was reasonable for my budget. They call the rooms cabins. I felt it was bigger than I expected. The beds were hard as I was expecting that as I read several reviews and everyone stated that the beds were hard. I simply called the "cabin crew" and requested several pillows to use as part of the mattress. The hotel itself was very clean. Check in was exceptionally fast and efficient. Staff very nice and meeted our needs each time we needed help. Even if we looked like we needed assistance they were there for us. We had a nice view of the Hudson and watched the boats pass by. The terrace bar was beautiful and clean. Drinks were nice as well. The morning coffee was delicious as were the muffins. On the weekends they offer brunch and it is fantastic. For forty dollars you get all you can eat and drink, and this includes alcoholic beverages. I think younger people found this hotel inviting as we found more younger people than older ones. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying in New York. I found it to be delightful.

title: Yotel Best Hotel
body:
My daughter and I have just returned from our first visit to New York and could'nt have stayed at a better hotel, right from the moment we stepped out of the taxi we were greeted by very helpful and friendly staff and that contiuned for the whole of our week long stay. Before going I requested a mattress topper for our bed after reading some of the reviews about the beds and that was already on the bed when we got there as for the bed we found no problem with it and managed to sleep very well every night.
I can honestly say that we never heard any noise from the club that they have in the hotel and only ocassionaly heard other people close their doors. The gallery was a brilliant idea especially the cold drinks machine with ice, after a day out in the heat to come back and get iced water was brilliant. Also we left things in the firdge and it never got touched. As with the room I can honestly say that we left money, jewellery and even my daughter's iphone in the safe as it broke while we were their and everything was still there when we got back every day I make this comment after reading some people had troubles with the safe but for me I can say that I felt more than safe leaving things in it.
It's in a great location literally a 10 minute walk if not less and your right in the middle of everything Madam Toussades, Ripley's, amc cinema which me and my daughter went to on our first night in New York and of course times square, but the hotel is just far enough away to take you away from the hustle and bustle of time's square if you choose to. Even walking back from our night at the theatre to see ' Wicked' which was brilliant and arriving back at the hotel after 12 at night we felt perfectly safe in doing so in the area.
The Empire State Building is a bit further but if you take a steady stroll to it and let's face it why rush then it is around a 20-25minute walk from the hotel but a nice walk.
Everything in the cabin was well spaced out and did'nt feel small to me and my daughter at all even when the bed was down you could easily still move about the room, which got clean towels and the bed made every day upon our return and the cleaning staff also were very polite and always had a good morning to say to us.
Sitting on the terrace eating muffins and having a coffeee or tea in my daughter's case was a great way to start the day.
All in all a great stay and just wish it could have lasted longer, would have no problem recomending this hotel to anyone, great staff, great location yotel is the best.

title: summer 2012
body: Great location in new-york. We travel with 2 teenagers and it was perfect. The bed is very comfortable and the vue of the room ( in the corner) was extra. The breakfast on the terrace is very great too. A very good place.

title: Simple but Good
body: Hotel was very trendy/hip. We are not, but didn't seem like many of the other guests were either so we didn't feel out of place. We stayed in the upgraded room with a bunk. It's bathroom actually had a door, but it didn't go all the way to the ceiling. It was pricier than the one w/o the bunk and looking back I think I'd just have had our 6 y/o sleep in the bed with us rather than pay the extra cost. Location wasn't bad. Walk to Times Square and nearest subway was about .4 miles (10th Ave to 8th Ave). 99 cent pizza was just around the corner. Breakfast was just muffins. I wish it was more. Staff was great. Access to the nearby pools would have been nice.

title: Refreshing and interesting.
body: Stayed 2 nights in late July. Room was small (but much bigger than Yotel at London Heathrow Airport) but it was cleverly designed. It was not a conventional hotel and the location is not at the best spot. Staff were very nice and helpful. I must say the air condition was extremely quiet (compared with other hotels I stayed in NY), TV was good, room was clean. Free muffin tasted so good in the morning. The lobby area on the 4th floor was very noisy in the evening but my room was quiet. They don't have a closet in the room, therefore I wouldn't recommend for long term stay. Port Authority was nearby with good connection to the airports. On the whole I found the hotel refreshing and interesting.

title: Unforgettable
body: An awesome visit of New York City with my two wonderful daughters. Pretty well located nearby Time Square in Yotel, we had a joyfull 48-hours experience visiting, sightseeing and being at Mary Poppin's spectacle. What a great time we had: 9.8/10.

title: Catherine
body: Brilliant stay at the hotel. I really enjoyed myself. Location is fantastic and the room was always very clean, modern and very comfortable. I would definitely stay there again and again. The gallery is such a good idea and it suited me perfectly. Breakfst muffins were delicious. I thought it was a bit expensive when I booked the hotel, but once I stayed there, it was worth every dollar.

title: Great place for couple
body:
Very small room, very ennough for 2 ppl. 
The 2 occupants basically need to be a couple to avoid awkwardness of having the other hearing everything you do in the bathroom coz there really isn't a bath"room" there. 
very nice for a couple. You can see your other half taking shower through a clear glass if that is your thing.
YoBot is very cool, you can store your luggages after check out. 
Must check out at 11am, no late check out. 
garage is $39 per night, no in/out privilige. Cheaper than most other parking places.
Very friendly staff. 
Have water and coffee supplied at every floor. 
You can get a deal from hotel.com or yotel Website sometimes.
Overall an excellent stay for single or couple.

title: Poncey but functional
body:
Nice, clean, modern, functional, funky but a bit poncey. Staff were stand-offish.. Breakfast is just muffins and coffee (not great if you're glutin intolerant) and not good value if you're paying over $300 a night.
Overall though, a great experience.

title: More hotels should be like this
body:
Talk about efficient use of space. The rooms are very small in dimension but don't let that fool you. Everything you need is right there when you look and you'll come to appreciate the smart use of space in this hotel. There should be more hotels like this.
The bed turns into a lounge chair during the day (motorized). The glass door shower is comfortable. The towel rack is heated to keep your towels warm. There is a spacious in-wall save, fold down ironing board, etc. Plenty of shelves, cubes and holders to satisfy your storage needs.
On every floor there is a gallery where you can find a fridge, microwave, ice machine, water, and coffee machine for all kinds of coffee beverage. The location of the hotel is excellent, everything is within walking distance.
I stayed there for a week and enjoyed every bit of it. Highly recommended.

title: Fun little place
body: It lives up to it's billing. It's like staying in an Ikea overnight. Don't be bashful, you definitely would get a full view of your roomie in the shower, as there's nothing but glass separating the bathroom from the room. Has a nice outdoor dining terrace, and a decent enough bar (though the bartenders are not very knowledgeable). I'd stay there again.

title: Like staying in your iPod!
body:
This hotel is very cool, white and funky (just like your iPod!) 
It is exactly what it said it was....small "cabins" are all you need and very efficiently laid out (I didn't come to New York to stay in my room). Great value in a good location (although it is Hells Kitchen, not Times Square....but close to everything). 
Staff were very friendly despite the self-serve concept (self-serve checkin and the coolest 'yobot' to look after your bags after check-out!)
My only complaint would be that the terrace bar played terrible music late at night....clearly catering to a very young crowd. My husband and I would have enjoyed a few more nightcaps but the music gave us a headache (and we like music!)
We'll definately be back.

title: Perfect location, excellent service.
body:
We stayed at the Yotel Times Square in August. Conveniently located about 10 minutes walk from the bustle of Times Square the hotel offered super-clean and modern rooms with emphasis on technology and efficiency. They upgraded us to a suit as our room did not have an extra bed due a reservation glitch. It was not the biggest hotel room I have seen but space was very adequate for me, my wife and 2 kids. Glass washroom and shower was surely an unusual thing but we did not have much problem with it. Floor kitchen or “Galley” as hotel calls them had a fridge, ice machine and quality Italian coffee maker with Lavazzo supplies. Very good idea, actually. 
All in all, we had a very pleasant stay and would probably return there.

title: Excellent hotel and modern concept
body: This hotel has a complete offer of modern concept about the future of hotel. Beautiful place with a excellent service, I spend the better day in my life in this place. I recommend a 100% with the great price and great location, and beautiful concept.

title: Comfortable, reasonable, modern, and friendly
body: Great location, friendly staff, comfortable room; altogether terrific spot! We walked to the nearby restaurants and thetres, using a cab only once. The staff was very freindly and helpful. |Although the rooms are small, the bed is very comfortable, and we spent very little time in the room in any case. It was also very reasonable for a New York hotel. Would go back in a New York minute.

title: A new experience
body:
I was staying there for the New York Gift Fair at the Javits Centre. The hotel is extremely well located for the exhibition centre as it is about 5 minutes walk away.
The hotel looks very funky and the staff in the entrance and the reception staff are extremely friendly and helpful.
The bedt was a little hard but then I am used to sleep on futons in Japan so not really an issue for me.
My room was cleaned daily, I just wish the cleaner did not leave things behind. One day, it was gloves and another day something else.
The bar looks busy as obviously the new trendy place to go to. A few issues with service at the bar as not always easy to identify staff from guests. Although service at the bar was attentive, if you are seating, forget it, I may still be waiting for my drink if I had not gone to the bar myself.
I will definitely stay there again next time I am in New York.

title: Great place to stay in NYC
body:
I had a very good experience with Yotel.
The building is very good loking, the rooms are confortable and full of design features.
Check in and check out are totally on line, so it's very quick and easy.
Yobot stores your luggage after the check out, so you can continue to visit the city.
Free wi fi connection in every room and free breakfast composed by tasty muffins complete the picture.
Very good hotel!

title: The coolest place we've been to in a very long time
body: Stayed 4 nights in Yotel, Times Sq. It was quite an experience - a visit to the future. Rooms are very modern, the bed was sooooo comfortable and I loved the way you could operate it to move up and down. Room had everything we needed, travelled without kids so we didn't need any extra space. I would definetely recommend this place and I would definetely come back or stay at Yotel in some other city. Staff was always friendly and helpful. Complimentary muffins with tea or coffee in the morning were great. Loved the Yobot in the Lobby. Perfect place to stay during our gettaway from kids.

title: 1st stay at Yotel NYC
body: Best room for the money in NYC...Clean,Modern and comfortable.Great westside location.Good "on the premises" restaurant.Lots of good nearby bars and eateries.Appeals to young and old alike has a "hip" european feel.The type of guest are diversified many being european..Great staff very charismatic,great attitudes seemed to like working there.No major complaints although I would suggest to supply ice buckets and notepads in the rooms and some kind of an incentive for repeat stays.I am in NY on an average of 10 times a year.I had made it a point to try to stay in a different hotel each visit with the price of rooms avg. approx. $300.00 per night.I think Yotel has broke me of this routine.I will definitely be a repeat guest at the Yotel NYC.

title: cool idea
body:
Yotel is close to Times Square, about a ten minute walk. It is also close to the Port Authority where one can catch the subway trains to all over town. 
The hotel itself was very cool. The rooms are very compact with the beds converting from short to long with the push of a button. There is only a curtain between the bathroom and bedroom but a glass sliding door divides the toilet from the rest of the bathroom. We found there was still enough privacy to be comfortable.
We found the showerfloor could have been a little cleaner and the stuff at the mission control a little friendlier but othewise it is a place we would certainly recommend.

title: Hotel Yotel Holiday...
body: I recently stayed at Yotel in NYC while on holiday. I loved it. From the moment I walked in, I new I was going to like it. Although a minimalist hotel, there is so much eye candy surrounding you. The check in process took less than 2 minutes. When you're on vacation, the last thing one needs after a long flight is a 1 hour check in process. The check in kiosks are brilliant. I had so much energy because of the quick check in process that my surroundings enticed me to go out. The hotel has plenty of cool visuals that just make you want to hang out there. The bar, the public areas, the restaurant and the roof top patio were all fantastic. My room was small, but perfect for NY standards. We had a great view. Beds were clean and comfortable. The concept of the bed folding away is brilliant. The ambient and mood lighting in the room was divine. Because I was in NYC where the city never rests or sleeps, I really only used my room for very few hours, but boy did I enjoy those hours. I highly recommend this place for young, active folks. We walked to all the hot spots in Chelsea (restaurants and bars! -- awesome). Times Square is very close. Other points of interest weren't that close, but given that it's NYC, everything is walkable, at least to me. And I enjoyed the walk. The hotel staff is friendly, young and hip. I especially loved the free coffee and espresso in the kitchen located on every floor. Such a great touch!! All in all, a great experience and I will certainly stay there again.

title: different, quirky, loved it
body: Imagine a room on a cruise ship, efficient to the max when considering space usage etc. The room was tiny, but that did not cause a problem. There was a kitchenette nearby offering refrig space, microwave and a nice coffee maker. Paid a little extra for the 'view' option, money well spent. Check in and check out processes were amazingly efficient.

title: Couple's break
body:
Absolutely great location, just far enough away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square to relax but close enough to walk (10 mins).
Amazing terrace for meals so you can eat outside but away from the traffic, best spare ribs I've ever had, would highly recommend them. Could have done with a bit more variety in the included breakfast though, only so many days I can eat muffins in a row.
The room was always cleaned and prepared to a high standard, view was very good (23rd floor) and facilities were good, TV, Hairdryer, shampoo, body wash, facecloths etc. no conditioner though.
Overall a great stay in a great location with friendly and observant staff.

title: Good Hotel
body: My husband and I stayed in March 2012 for 5 nights. My only complaint was the comfort of the bed. If there was a pillowtop or some sort of egg crate it would have been excellent. The atmosphere is hip and young. The rooms are just the right size to sleep and crash after spending a day in the city. Not far from Time Square or subways.

title: Yotel, only for youngsters?
body:
In Feb. 2012, we booked a week in the YOTEL (NYC) with 4 young adult kids (20-25). So we got three rooms. Nice location (2 blocks away from Times Square = +/- 10 min. walk). Nice reception, very friendly staff, very tidy. The rooms are OK, enough space, even to NYC standards.
We expected a hotel full of youngsters, but no: mostly families or couples in their 40's. Breakfast = everyday the same if you book it in advance: muffins, muffins, muffins (all varieties :-))
Tip: book a dinner in the Japanese restaurant (4th floor of the hotel): you'll be dazzled.
One small remark: to us, the music in the lobby situated on the 4th floor was too noisy. On the other hand, you don't have to stay there for hours...
Have fun and enjoy your stay!!!
Bob

title: Giggly comfortable
body: If your in New York City, check out Yotel. Clean, New, and just a lot of fun to stay at. The room my wife picked out was the smallest one they have and we did not get in each others way. Everything has a place and is just so well thought out. Although TripAdvisor has it as Time Square West...I would have to say that it is more like Hell's Kitchen. Don't be frighten of the neighborhood name. most all of Manhattan has been gentrified in some fashion or another and this area is as well. Great restaurants with in a few blocks and yes it is close to Time Square. After a Day out in the city you get to come back to a sanctuary that just make you giggle the from the time you walk into the hotel (yotel) till you get to your room. Go to their site to see all the rooms they have. don't be shocked by the size of the rooms they are really small and fashion them selves as a space ship cabin... the whole experience is just so wonderful

title: Great spot
body: Just checked out of our 6 night stay at yotel and we were both very impressed. Great location good service clean rooms etc, as stated rooms are small but still functional, didn't notice the lack of size too much, a small mini fridge would be perfect in the rooms but the galley option isn't too much of an inconvenience, the ice water machine in the galley was out of order for the majority of our stay but, we booked well in advance and got 6 nights under $1000 so it represented great value, all in all a great hotel that we will recommend,if your not a highly strung person do not hesitate to stay here

title: Compact living, nice location and clean rooms
body:
This hotel is nice, especially if you plan to spend your times roaming the streets of New York and not spend time at the hotel except from sleeping. The rooms are very small but very fresh. Only bad thing is that the toilet is not 100% separated from the rooms, it's behind glass walls and a curtain. Not problem but special.
The check in is through computers on the ground floor, there is staff to help you but basically the concept is that you do the check in on your own.
Breakfast (containing coffe and muffins) is included in the price. 
Location is nice, very close by Time Square but at the same time not on a busy street.

title: Awesome Awesome!!!!!
body: Stop looking now. This is more than you can find for this price. Really, this hotel is wonderful. I stayed there for 4 days. Let me tell you some of their features: if you arrive early and they have a cabin that you reserve ready, they make an early check in for you, for FREE; they offer coffee, hot chocolate, tea, water and ice on every floor, for FREE; they offer a breakfast with coffee and muffins, for FREE; the cabins are clean, beautiful and modern; Really, the hotel by itself is an attraction. Near to times square and most of the touristic spots in NY. I can't wait to come back there again. I can't think how they can get better.

title: Not a good choice
body:
The rooms are very little and really unequipt, crew is not friendly or professional, the bar is nice with opportunity to meet new people. The higher priced rooms are also not good and are missing basic stuff like a minibar, a door to the bathroom, bad air con (wither freezing or none), no coffee machine, no cups etc...
House keeping through away my business receipts which I get refunded for, they were neatly packed on the table which indicated they were not trash, Very unprofessional, crew handling that followed was also very bad and unsatisfactory.

title: Yotel - I Love It!
body: This is the best hotel concept ever. I love the easy check-in and check-out via kiosk. I love the location near Times Square and lots of dining options. I love the Sunday Brunch with tapas and sangria, all you can eat and drink in 2 hours for $40...and the DJ was good too. Love the cabin accommodations, very clean and very comfortable for one or two people. Yotel has the best community / social environment I've ever seen in a hotel. The other hotels need to take note.

title: Funky good value hotel
body:
Convenient location. Great rooms - small but well designed & functional. You are not paying for the big room or the big bathroom - but you are in NY - the room is just for sleeping & for that it works. Opening window & we were on a higher floor so we had a view of the Empire State Building - which was great.
Great coffee, free muffins for breakfast, cool terrace bar, friendly helpful staff.
And affordable. What else do you need.

title: fun and crazy
body:
excellent hotel, very clean and friendly.
i stayed there for 4 days
wonderfull breakfast and lovely free muffins and coffee
my corner room on 26th was sunny, the view on skyscrapers perfect 
stop loking and choose it !!

title: Always a pleasant, consistent stay
body: This is my third stay at Yotel for business, and it has never disappointed me. As an architect, I appreciate its simple, modern and well-detailed vibe. Always good music in the background, and very hip - think "W" but without the high-end attitude. The rooms are well-planned, details are higher end and custom, and super-efficient - they may be on the smaller side, but you never feel cramped, especially with all of the lounges, terraces and bars on the lower levels. Besides, when you're in New York, you're spending most of your time outside exploring the City, not running laps in your room! The restaurant is great and the hotel staff supportive and attentive. It is a different hotel experience from that of a typical 'American' hotel - but with an open mind, it is a unique and rewarding experience! More hotels should be like this. Period.

title: Brilliant Base for a Few Days in NYC
body:
After planning a trip to the States and booking flights on a bit of a whim, I booked this hotel from a Travel Zoo offer that gave 45% off during July and August, a brilliant offer!
I had looked up the details of the hotel online, and was quite excited about staying so close to Times Square in such a modern hotel.
When I arrived at the hotel, I was not disappointed, checking in was quick and easy using a self service computer (with staff on hand to help if you needed it) and making my way unto my room was again simple.
The room was small, yet I was expecting that, and really comfortable. The bed, which converted into a sofa at the touch of a button, was really comfortable and the air-con was really efficient and made the room a good temperature within seconds of entry. I was traveling solo so this didn't effect me, but would say that if you were travelling with friends the lack of privacy in the bathroom might be a problem.
The staff were friendly and helpful regardless of the time of day.
Breakfast was simple yet tasty, muffins and tea/coffee, and you could order extras from the menu, if you wanted more.
I ate at the hotel one evening and the food was delicious, small portions, think oriental tapas, but great 'end of a long day' snack, and reasonably priced.
All in all a great hotel, I would definitely recommend it and would look to stay at a Yotel again if they open other city centre locations.

title: Good Hotel
body:
The Yotel was a great place to stay at a decent price for New York City. The room was clean and had everything we needed. Even though the room was small it wasn't a problem as we were always out exploring the city and hardly in the room. Every floor has an automatic coffee machine that will make espresso, latte, cappuccino, coffee or tea; there is also a common fridge and microwave available for use. Coffee and delicious muffins were available every morning in the dining area.
