When you take a look at their website you can view the rooms and yes they do look like that. The terrace is great. After a long day you can really enjoy a drink and relax whilst listening to the music choice of the dj. We didn't try the restaurant but the menu looked ok. The breakfast is ok with muffins and coffee, thee or juice. We decided to have breakfast at a nearby diner (Theater Row Diner on 42nd) and enjoyed it so we returned to this diner a few times.
Pro's: location, price, design, wifi, friendliness of staff (they arranged for our group to have all of our rooms on the same floor without us asking for it).
Con's: some of us found the mattress to be to hard, the bathroom is not very private so if you share a room with someone you don't live with it could be awkward.

title: Stylish NYC hotel
body: I was in NYC and spent 4 nights at the Yotel. It offers value for money and I like the style and location of the hotel. The bar and rooftop terrace are also a great meeting point and fun place to spend an evening. Very friendly staff. Layout of the Premium Cabin is very well designed, they actually feel bigger than they are. Still, for a longer stay they are rather small. Coathangers and shelves are fine for 1-2 nights but for a longer stay I'd prefer some cabinet space so I can unpack my suitcase. Should have upgraded to a suite.

title: Great Room, Great Hotel, Great Location
body: We stayed at the Yotel in September for 5 nights and enjoyed every minute! The room we took was a Premium Queen and was great for space. The motorised bed is great fun and very practical. It is a firm bed, but you do get used to it very quickly. We had a room to the rear of the building, which gave a us a great view of the Empire State Building. The rooms on the front look out over 42nd Street, which is a more attractive view although much noisier. The checking in and out is very simple and the Yobot is great fun to watch. Food and drink at the restaurant is very good quality and not too expensive - the view and atmosphere on the terrace is quite amazing.

title: Fantastic stay
body: Myself and my girlfriends stayed here last week for 3 nights and had the most fantastic time. The Yotel is amazing, super cool, modern and stylish. It is in a fantastic location, only 5 mins walk to Times Square, so central. The staff are amazing, every single one of them from concierge, to housekeeping to the front door staff, so friendly and so helpful. We stayed in the VIP suite and adjoining suites and all I can say is WOW!! The rooms are massive and the VIP suite is incredible with a totally awesome terrace. And what a view and what a great hot tub!!!! Also it is so great having free wifi, free computers to use, free breakfast with yummy delicious muffins! I would highly highly recommend anyone coming to NYC to stay at the Yotel. Thank you Yotel for an amazing time, I will be back!

title: Loved it!
body:
Really enjoyed our stay in a Executive View Cabin. The room was on the corner of the building with two floor to ceiling windows. The room looked towards the Hudson River and we could just see a glimpse of Times Square. 
The room was really clean and fresh and we felt the size of the room was pretty typical of a hotel room. 
The gallery with cold water and free tea and coffee was a great idea, espically when it was right next to our room (we didn't have and issues with noise either). 
Location was great - a bus stops just around the corner but it is also an easy walk to Times Sqaure.

title: Excellent, actually
body: Small rooms, but totally adequate. Everything nicely designed and also functional. Among the best staff we ever encountered at a hotel, friendly and helpful and modern attitude in the very best meaning of those words. Terrace and bar also very good, and free, excellent coffee around the clock. Breakfast very basic, just a muffin.

title: A tiny five star hotel
body: A modern hotel for youngsters and the location is good, the rooms are tiny but the designs are great! If you prefer a good view of the city, the Premium View Cabin is your choice. The 4 is a great place for relaxing except weekend evenings.

title: A very different experience for me
body:
We had a 12 night stay at this hotel in Sept 2012 and it was very different to the reviews we had read for this place. 
Our experience:
1. money STOLEN
2. dirty rooms - previous guests rubbish was still under the curtain separating the bathroom and bed area
3. 'gallery' facilities were often broken - coffee machine didn't work, no cups
As for the stolen money, I do admit fault that we didn't lock it in the safe (learnt from another review where money was stolen from the safe) nor in our luggage, but it wasn't exactly left out for all to see. LIving in a hotel for 12 nights, you tend to put things away in drawers and shelfs. The money i had was tucked away and you really had to go thru our possessions to get to it.
If housekeeping was that thorough, makes you think huh. The thought of someone going thru all your stuff while you put trust in their professionalism.
So 'mission control' was no help, they just hand you over to the security team and even when i gave feedback to them, I was pretty much ignored.
It's not all negative thou, the security team are doing their best, interviewing staff and updating us.
It wasn't a lot of money and I dont expect to hear from them again but it's a downer on the whole experience. Up to you what you make of this review.

title: Good in lots of ways, not so good in others
body: Maybe I'm the wrong demographic for Yotel (I'm 52) because I would've traded the robot, groovy lighting and free breakfast muffins for some cupboard space and a bar fridge in our room. My 16 year old daughter and I stayed in a premium cabin for 10 days and I got very tired of having to drag my suitcase out from under the bed to access my clothes. Some more wall hooks would've helped. And the air conditioning blasts the poor person in the top bunk - it goes on and off (loudly) all through the night. Having said that, the Yotel staff were lovely, it's really clean and neat and the kitchen puts out some great food. There's also a communal kitchen on each floor where you can make a good coffee and store your wine (of course, it could easily get nicked). Hell's Kitchen is a great area to explore - many good restaurants along 10th and 9th avenues and if you're a walker like me, you can hoof it to Central Park in the north and Greenwich Village in the south from there. So, if you can afford a bigger room than we had and you can handle the hard bed, go for it!

title: Great value in a purpose driven hotel
body:
Aside from one disappointing evening in one of the lounges, customer service was exceptional. While the room is compact, my wife and I agree that the purpose of our stay was to enjoy the Hotel and more importantly New York. 
The time we spent in the room was comfortable and we did not feel claustrophobic. On more than on evening, I was able to pull out a computer and work at the workstation in the room. Prior to arriving, we were slightly concerned about the space in the room. The space is not a problem.
The staff were fantastic (for the most part). The front staff helped us check in, took our luggage to the room, showed us around the hotel and explained the service they offered.
The one negative experience revolves around a visit we made to the bar. We were ignored by serving staff who were consumed with a personal conversation. I believe this was just two staff members who are at fault. When I went to the bar tender, we were greeted politely and our order was taken. Sadly the experience of being ignored really frustrated us and our one guest and this is the only reason for the 'non-excellent' rating.
We also had a pleasant experience checking out. While waiting to store our luggage, the staff noticed the long line up to the "YoBot" (A machine that stores your luggage) Because not all luggage can be stored with this innovative machine, the staff were able to help reduce the length of the line up by finding guests with luggage unable to be stored by YoBot and manually store their luggage. This was a great experience of how staff used their genius to improve customer service.
This hotel was also quite a bit less expensive than other ("Traditional") hotels. I believe we save about 33% of what we could have paid else were..
The location is great - About 4 or 5 blocks from Times Square, 3-4 blocks from a subways station and just a block or so from some really great restaurants.

title: Love this place
body:
This is a great place to stay, love the decor, the music, and the feel of the hotel. I was in NY on business and also had a weekend to kill, and the hotel was perfectly located for both. It's close enough to Times Square to be central to everything, but far enough away to be clear of the tourist chaos.
The staff are great, helpful and enthusiastic. It's not luxury, and it's a very different hotel experience, but it's really well thought out and it works.
It's not good for families with young children, or for people who aren't into their music (contemporary, electronic). 
I stay in lots of places, but rarely write reviews unless the place either stands out or totally sucks. With Yotel NYC, I'd return here in the blink of an eye....

title: Great location for exploring NYC
body:
Booked Yotel through Hotwire and got a great rate.
4 people travelling including 2 single men so the fact they don't offer 'twin' rooms meant we had to pay extra for the guys to have a queen cabin with a bunk - literally a bunk bed over the double bed. The bunk was a decent size and as we were more interested in exploring New York than lounging around in our rooms it really wasn't an issue.
The galleys located on each floor mean you can get coffee, hot chocolate etc at any time for free and the free drinks and muffins available 7am-10am every day are great. My personal favourite were the banana and walnut ones but they were all delicious.
Every area of the hotel was immaculate, they even pump a lovely scent throughout the hotel so everywhere smells fresh and clean - a godsend when you end up sharing a lift with lots of hot and sweaty tourists!
My only grumble was I was overcharged for my laundry when we checked out - but I was too tired after 5 days on the go I didn't have the energy to complain!
It's only 2 blocks from Times Square & the nearest Subway with loads of bars and restaurants within waling distance if you can't face another Subway ride after trekking around the city all day!
I would definitely return to this funky hotel.

title: Super trendy and different kind of experience
body:
This hotel was really cool. When you walk into the lobby, you see this giant robot behind glass. This robot takes your luggage to hold it if you want to walk around the city before of after check in. It's their way of "holding luggage". Not sure of the price as we didn't use it.
You will check in on the kiosks and they give you a key and your "cabin" number. Head to the elevator for your room, but you stop on the 4th floor. Here are the restaurants, bar, etc. A bit confusing now, because we were looking at how to get to the 20th floor where our cabin was. You have to go to your right and it's around the corner.
The cabins were really cool for the right type of person. Small rooms, flat screen tv, the bed was a bit on the hard side and it reclined and you can also sit up. Kind of like an electronic futon. One foot to the bathroom, which was separated by a curtain. Shower, no tub and small vanity but for some reason it didn't feel as small as it was. I loved it, but my husband longed for a full size room. No shampoos or soap, but everything was in a dispenser.
The area was not really Times Square, but hell’s kitchen. They are supposed to have a great brunch, but we didn't go. This place was in a "trendy & fabulous" area and seemed to cater more toward that clientele. We went to Druids restaurant which had wonderful Irish cuisine.. Best fish and chips ever!
Check out was super early at 11am! And they wouldn't give me an hour later to check out, which was annoying, but their right. You just go to the kiosk to check out and that's it. 
To sum it up, it's a cool place for the right person, but I wouldn't return. I suggest you go on youtube to check it out. We moved over to the Park Central in Times Square, which was more of what we were looking for.

title: I cried for 6 nights
body: If you are traveling for busines, this should be the last place you will want to stay. After working a long day, I would come back to my room and honestly cry. My marketing department picked the location for a recent show that I had to attend and let me say, the bed is absolutely ridiculous. It's not a bed - it's actually a futon with 1 inch of padding. I would prefer to sleep on the floor but there is no room to even try and attempt it. I would have gladly switched hotels but due to the convention, all rooms were booked. The 1 star is because it's clean but if you are looking for a place to stay more than 1 night, look elsewhere. This is the type of place for a early 20"s person that is going to New York just to party and won't be sleeping much. And by the way, it took me 3 days to try and figure out how to turn off the purple neon light in the room. Talk about a complete nightmare.

title: Yotel the Coolest Hotel in NYC
body:
Travelled with my girlfriend to New York and choose Yotel because it looked cool and different from the usual choices and location seemed to be pretty good. 
We booked a Corner room which was on 16th floor and was fantastic, the views were stunning and the room was clean and spacious with a suprisingly confortable bed!!!. The gallery was a great idea, and being able to pop (in our case next door) to get ice cold water or a coffee, hot chocolate etc was fantastic. They had a fridge and microwave in there aswell. 
What suprised us the most was the location was absolutely fantastic, with almost everything we wanted to see so easy to get too. 
The hotel itself was clean, modern, with very helpful staff, (loved the music too). Too be honest we couldnt fault it, it excelled our expectations in everyway. 
There was a diner we used for breakfast just 2 blocks up 42nd street called the Theatre Row Diner which was fantastic, we kept going back for breakfast as it was so delicious and reasonably priced. 
The soundproofing was suprisingly good, didnt have a sleepless night at all. You do still hear the sirens and hooting, but it wasnt loud enough to effect sleep.
When we return to NYC City Yotel will without a doupt be our choice of hotel again. Right now having withdrawels from the whole experience :(. Would go back tommorow.

title: Great hotel, something a bit different
body: My wife and I stayed here for three nights in July 2012. It was a great hotel and was totally different from any other hotel we have stayed in. We got an upgrade to a room overlooking the hudson which was in the end was fantastic to watch the 4th of July fireworks! The room was the Premium Queen Cabin, and although quite small when the bed is down flat it is fine when the beds back is in the more upright position. We dined at the japanese style restaurant on the first night and although it was expensive it was very good food! The staff were very friendly throughout the hotel.

title: So much design that it doesn't work
body: Yotel looks promising when you enter; all that crome and funky stuff, old bicycles hanging from the ceiling and what have you. But once you get to your room, your "cabin", you discover that it's tiny and doesn't have a single table to put your laptop on. The toilet/shower area has no door, just flimsy curtains. There is a transparent sliding door to the toilet, one that doesn't close entirely and you might as well do your business outside the room as everything is audible and visible to the rest of the people in the room. My daughter and I decided to take turns, while one had a shower and went to the toilet, the other one went down to the lobby. The beds are hard as concrete and the bunk bed above the queen size bed didn't even have proper bedding- a nasty polyester blanket instead of a duvet cover. Hideous. And cleaning in the morning; that proved to be difficult. We went out for 3-4 hours in the morning and left the sign on the door handle saying "please clean the room", but when we came back it was just as we had left it. I dashed down to the reception and complained and they promised to "sort it out". The restaurant doesn't serve breakfast after 10 o'clock, actually at 10.30 we were offered coffee and from the menu all kinds of Oriental dishes, like Sushi and stuff. So we had to go to Starbucks. In a way the hotel seems promising with that modern look, something different and green. The front staff was helpful, but when I came down and complained about something, such as cleaning, other people were complaining about the same thing. It seems like things don't work like they should do at this hotel and all these flaws are camouflaged by the funky appearance. Stupid tourists are easily trapped, I suppose. Certainly I am no exception.

title: A completely faultless Hotel
body:
Checking in is extremely easy using the screens in the main reception . The rooms are very modern and clean and linen on bed changed each day. Showers are very powerful and large cubicles. On each floor there is a room with a coffee / cappuccino etc machine which is free and available 24/7. There is also an ice machine and use of the fridge to store any food. 
The hotel is well situated as it is only a short walk to the centre of New York.
I would definitely recommend this hotel .

title: Love the Yotel
body: I've stayed at the Yotel over 20 times this past year. All business travel and its been great each time. Friendly staff, clean rooms, exceptional dining and rooftop experience. I recommend it to everyone who's traveling to NYC.

title: Absolutely FABULOUS! Great location, amazing hotel!
body: Stayed for a girls weekend in late September and had an AMAZING experience at Yotel. 10 out of 10 on rooms, decor, staff, comfort and location. This is a funky, modern, hip, and slightly quirky hotel which is great for couples, groups of friends and even families with kids. The location cannot be beaten - it's handy for Times Square, theatres, and dining options and we loved walking to and from Central Park and just taking in New York. There's a well-stocked grocery store right around the corner and you can buy wine/beer etc less than a block away. The rooftop bar is huge - a trendy hangout with a good mix of people. Go - you won't be disappointed! We absolutely LOVED it!

title: Loved It
body:
We have just returned home from visiting New York, staying at Yotel Hotel for 5 nights and we loved it.
We were greeted on entering the hotel by Emmanuel who was so friendly and genuine. Emmanuel assisted up with check in and went through everything with us about the hotel, assisted us to our room and surprised us with a fantastic view of the Empire State Building. 
The room itself was very clean, bright, different. I loved the purple lighting in the room, it was a lovely relaxing feature. The room is small but adequate. The room has everything you need including hairdryer, iron, safe. Also liked the tray feature that is available to enable you to get breakfast and bring it back to your room. I just felt the room had a nice feeling to it and felt cosy. The only negative thing was that the bed was a bit hard but we got used to it after the first night and I would not let this put you off. Great views as mentioned above.
There is a galley on each hotel floor which provides tea, coffee, hot chocolate, ice and a drinks vending machine which was a nice feature, it was lovely to get back from a day out exploring to have a cup of tea and relax in bed.
We found the hotel to be surprisingly quiet, I was expecting it to be noisy with a lot of young people, I am young but not the partying type but the hotel was fine, not noisy at all.
Breakfast provided each morning which consisted of tea/coffee and muffins which were fine, better than nothing.
We found the staff to be friendly. The hotel will keep your bags free of charge on check out if you have a late flight and want to explore New York some more. On returning to the hotel to get our bags, we needed a taxi to take us to Penn Station and Emmanuel got us a taxi straight away outside the hotel and brought our bags out. 
The hotel is in a good location, close to Times Square but a nice distance away from it to return in the evenings away from the hustle and bustle. Hotel is also close to subway at Port Authority and I would advise you to use the subway, it is a great, quick and cheap way of getting around (purchase the Metro Card which you can both use if you are a couple). We also did a lot of walking around the city so make sure you have comfy shoes with you.
There are lots of restaurants in neighbourhood, it seems to be in the Hell's Kitchen area. There is a really great pizza place just one block up from the hotel called Capizzi and if you like pizza I would advise you to try it, the pizza is delicious. The food in New York is great and I would recommend the deli restaurants located throughout the city, especially Olivia's Deli in the Downtown area (near World Trade Center) and the Pax Wholesome Foods which are located throughout the city.
If you are flying to/from Newark Airport use the Air Train (Penn Station) to get to and from the city as it is so much cheaper.
We would definitely return to Yotel Hotel and would recommend to friends and family.

title: yotel great spot
body: if your looking for a modern place in a great position this is it, easy check in through touch screen and theres even a guy there to help should you get confused. the rooms are small but big enough and very comfy beds, i had an amazing view of the city through my window. nice bar on the 4th floor seemed very popular. coffee and muffins galore for your breakfast in the morning as well. very close to all the city has to offer, only a 5 minute walk or so to times square, empire state and other attractions.

title: No Customer Service!
body:
The front desk staff have no customer service skills. We paid over $1,500 per night to stay in a VIP suite for our first family vacation to New York and not only was there NO VIP service upon check in, the four people behind the mission control desk didn't even look up from their cell phones and computers to say hello and we were the only guests at the desk. After about 10mins a woman at one of the computers said "Can I see your IDs." This was the first greeting/acknowledgement provided. After another 10 mins of the woman staring at her computer, I requested she give us the keys to our room while she finished the checkin. This was the longest check in I have ever experienced and there were no other guests at the desk, but four hotel employees. 
During our stay I called the front desk to ask how to work the fireplace in our suite, mission control said they did not know but they would send someone up--no one showed up. When I called because a beverage in the galley was out they told me to go to another floor, I went to every floor in the hotel and every galley was out. The beverage was never refilled during our entire week long stay. The "Queen bed" in the VIP suite is a cheap sofa bed with a metal bar that cuts into the middle of your back, a cot would be far more comfortable. I requested an extra mattress pad to cushion the terrible thin mattress and was told the hotel does not have any for the sofa bed. We paid over $1500 a night for a sofa bed that no one should ever have to sleep on, I am shocked they did not put an actual bed in the second room of the suite. When I asked the concierge for a restaurant suggestion in the theatre district she replied, "I don't know of any." I could go on and on with examples of their lack of basic customer service skills such as greeting guests with eye contact and a hello, but the point is, the people running this hotel DO NOT CARE ABOUT THEIR GUESTS' COMFORT OR HAPPINESS. If you like tiny rooms and being ignored, this is the place for you.
Bright spot: Cam at the front door/street lobby always greeted us with a smile and helped us with our bags. If he ran the hotel it would be a better place to stay.

title: It's fantastic!
body:
The localization is perfect. 3 blocks to subway, 5 blocks to Times Square and 2 blocks to Javits Center.
It was very good for my type of trip.
I ordered somethings from Amazon and others e-commerce sites, and I've received all of them perfect, when I arrived in Yotel, at night.
The employee's suport is amazing. If you need (and request), they help you.
The Yotel is extremely practical and functional for the needs of most travelers. It hasn't extreme luxury, but delivers exactly what it promises.
I would certainly recommend for a friend.

title: All style, no substance.
body: The hotel really is in a good spot in Manhattan. The design and appearance is fantastic. The lobby is flashy and upbeat. Unfortunately, that's where it stops. Once you actually need service from the front desk for anything, you're out of luck. Repeated asking for things that should already be done gets old fast. And don't get a suite. They're great rooms, but the only thing "VIP" is their prices for them. Noticeable difference between housekeeping personnel, too. Some are great, some not so much. And please, please don't get me started on the fire alarm in the middle of the night that nobody at the hotel seemed to have a clue about. All in all a disappointing experience. We checked out early and relocated to a better hotel for the last 2 days of our trip. Won't be returning.

title: Small, cozy, quiet
body: Yes, the rooms (I stayed in a "premium cabin") are relatively small but the space utilization is the best I've seen! The rooms are very quiet, climate control is excellent, and I felt comfortable and cozy, but never claustrophobic. The smallest rooms are great for an individual or couple.

title: nicola procter
body: This was our first visit 2 new york my husband picked this hotel because it looked different and cool we loved it! when we arrived there was staff 2 help book us in with the computer then we got 2 our room it looked cool dont get me wrong it is small but we werent spending all our time in there just sleeping! the bed was great loved the button 2 change from lie down 2 the sit up postition ! on every floor there was a room with free coffee ,chocolate etc.. and cold water and ice you could get muffins free in the morning but we went across the road 2 broadway deli and it was great the food and prices ! on level 4 there was computers u could use free 4 30mins which was great i used it 2 look up show and where places were ta also 4 facebook it had free wifi also if u had your laptop of phone with u which i thought was great ! we loved new york i will be returning and i will b staying at yotel 4 defo the staff was friendly and helped u out when ever asked we didnt drink much in the bar as my husband found it expencive but i think most hotels charge more this is a great hotel it was only 2mins 2 hells kitchen area on 9th ave and a 5min walk 2 times square

title: Does exactly what it says on the tin
body:
Stayed here 28th september to 4th october 2012, 2 couples, 40th celebration. Check in all fine, computerised system worked well. We had emailed ahead to ask for high floor rooms and adjacent rooms but were allocated a room on the 10th and one on the 14th......... A chat to the reception team on the 4th and we were sorted with 2 rooms next to each other on the 27th floor. Rooms clean, streamlined, no frills, all white, lotsa gadgets. Everything worked, regular patrols by staff along corridors to alert us when we left a door ajar made it feel secure. Muffins and tea/coffee in the morning all beautifully fresh, bar trendy and modern, all staff helpful and friendly, food in restaurant tasty and well made. Free maps and directions on request. Very quiet, no noise from any other rooms. Bed a lot more comfy than I thought it would be. Central for most things - 10 mins walk to Times Square, 5 mins to subway. Rang of ages staying here, a few younger groups but a younger demographic than most hotels I think, don't think my parents would like it.
Downsides; hot water for tea not working in galley one morning, rang down to be told to try another floor so went down ( in pj's) and that one didn't work either......
Lack of privacy in the bathroom would be a problem for some couples - no door, an opaque curtain does not stop noise or smells........ there are toilets elsewhere though.
Would def stay here again

title: A modern hotel inside Manhattan
body:
A modern hotel inside Manhattan. Fun ambiance mood. The rooms are small, but very well organized and super clean. Everything square foot is meticulously designed. The furniture is custom made for a hotel perspective. The rooms are surprisingly quiet. We get a very nice view from the 26th floor. Wifi signal was good. The self check-in / check-out service mostly works. The perfect place if you don’t want/need to talk to anybody. Walk distance to Time Square. Affordable price overall. 
On the bad side:
We got some issue with the elevator.
The mattress can be a little hard for some.
The bathrooms don’t offer much privacy.

title: A great place to stay!
body:
I stayed one night at the Yotel and wish it could've been much longer! It is a very fun and comfortable place to stay. The outdoor terrace is magnificent. A perfect place to relax and enjoy a drink. The prices for food are very reasonable for the city. The room was small, but, to be expected in NYC. After all, they are called cabins! 
Check in and out was very easy on the computers. There are plenty of staff to help if you get stuck along the way. Breakfast was surprisingly good - the muffins and coffee a perfect way to start the day. 
Location is good - just a few blocks from Times Square, so a very easy walk. There are many restaurants and shops within walking distance.

title: family stay
body:
an excellent atmosphere,great location,innovative hotel.free breakfast included but it was no varied(cofee and muffins).free internet station and free wi-fi.we found the galley most usefull.
we certainly going to recomend of this hotel to our fellows

title: great place overall.
body:
Nice expérience. everything is fine. Cabins are nice, clean and well thinked!.

title: A great place when exploring NY
body:
Stayed here for 4 nights and found it all to be very good. 
The price gives you value, the location perfect, breakfast, wifi and friendly staff all add to recommend the hotel. 
Personally I think the beds were way to hard and also the "no door" for the toilet can be bad for some couples or friends staying together. 
The fire alarm went off one night when we were staying there. Think it was a bit caotic so maybe the management should drill the staff a bit more on fire safety and evacuations. 
But all in all I would recommend this place and if I need a decent place to stay in NY on a lower budget I would def come here again.

title: Awesome place
body: My fiancée and I stayed at the Yotel for two nights in September, our third visit to NYC. We'd previously stayed at a local family owned B&B and a national chain but this time, we decided to try something a little different to the norm. Before we travelled there were several mixed reviews of Yotel on tripadvisor, some good and some not so good. Thankfully, our visit to Yotel was awesome from the moment the taxi dropped us at the front door. The welcome was warm, check-in efficient and the corner cabin was futuristic, spacious and comfortable. The terrace bar, breakfast muffin and free wi-fi added that something extra to our stay - we can't wait to return and strongly recommend the Yotel for those who'd like something a little different without compromising quality and central locality.

title: Great Place to Stay
body:
I had read about this hotel on Tripadvisor, so I knew that when I checked in, that I would need to go to the kiosk to register and get my room key. A gentleman greeted us at the door, waited to see if we had any questions then handed us a map of New York and explained where everything was. The subway for the A C E is just a couple of blocks away on 42nd street (5 minutes).Times square is about a 10 minute walk, Rockafeller Center is about 1 mile and the United Nation building is about 1.5 miles. We couldn't believe how close we were to everything. the elevator in the lobby takes you up to the 2nd floor, which is the public lounge/bar and resturaunt area. You use your room key to take another set of elevators to the "cabins".
 I was rooming with my husband, and I didn't think that it was too small. There is free wi-fi, and it worked great on my Kindle Fire. The bed reclines from a sofa to a bed. I didn't think it was too hard and slept very well in it. The sink is separated by a curtin, in addition you can pull the glass door to the Toilet/shower area closed, if you need more privacy. I do have to agree with another reviewer, bring your own shampoo and conditioner. There is no conditioner and the kind of shampoo that is offered is a little hard on your hair. It's more of a body wash/shampoo kind of thing. My husband didn't really care for the smell of the body wash, so you might want to bring a small bar of soap. The TV was great and you can make FREE phone calls anywhere in the United States on the room phone. The rooms were always clean and comfortable and I have no complaints. 
As for the breakfast, we were able to have a variety of muffins, coffee, tea and whole or skim milk. Usually, the muffins consisted of blueberry, chocolate with chips, corn, cranberry-orange and bannana-walnut. They were moist and delicious. The galley is on the same floor of the room and offeres latte, mocha, tea, hot chocolate and ice/water. If your traveling, I would recommend borrowing the breakfast cups with lids, as there are no lids for the cups in the galley. The coffee in the galley is very good and again, is free. Also, a bottle of pop is $2.00, which is pretty reasonable. From the staff, you get the service used for a more expensive hotel. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Good option, great value and location for NY
body: The location is great just walking distance from Times square. A subway station (Port Authority Bus Station) is just a couple of blocks away. Rooms are small but not uncomfortable. Very clean, very modern. The luggage robot is a hoot! All floors have a "galley" open 24 hours where you can make yourself a cappuccino, tea, etc and it's for free. No breakfast buffet but you get free coffee and muffins in the morning. NY is kind of expensive and this hotel was a real value for your money.

title: New & funky!
body: Hotel is located in Times Square and opened "brand new" in 2011. Got an awesome deal through CBT Group via Groupon. Complimentary breakfast & free high-speed internet were a major plus. Downside... the rooms are small, which is typical at most NYC hotels. Be sure to check out their automated valet/luggage system... called "Yobot"... it's really cool. Check-in is similar to when you arrive at the airport (100% automated). They also have a large terrace area... which was a nice place to grab drinks before we headed out for the evening.

title: NOT for adult business travelers who may need to actually WORK
body:
WORST hotel room I have ever had in my life. The room was small and poorly designed. The work space (if that is what it can be called) was small and cramped, there was more room in the shower!
The bed was as hard as concrete and I lived on pain pills for two days. The room priced at OVER 300.00 + tax is overpriced and over valued. 
I should have paid 100.00 + more and stayed at the Marriot at 54th & Lex, which Is where I will be next time for sure.
The ONLY reedeeming thing about the hotel was the excellent wait staff in the restaurant.

title: Great hotel
body: This hotel is ideal for a trip to New York, the rooms utilise space really well and have some fantastic views of the city. It is located in a nice area and it's just a short walk to Times square, also close to a subway station from where you can access all of the city. In the hotel you get free high-speed wifi and each morning you can get free coffee and muffins, each floor also has a galley where you can get free hot drinks 24 hours a day. Have no complaints about this Hotel and would happily stay here again.

title: Worst hotel stay I have had
body:
We stayed in the VIP Suite, and the second bedroom had the worst bed I have ever slept on in my life. The hotel staff and management are pretty clueless, not friendly, and they don't know the meaning of the word customer service.
We were so disgusted with the how we were treated that we checked out early. The person that checked us out didn't even bother to ask why we were leaving early.
I have received better customer service at a Motel 6 than this place. We were charged an outrageous amount of money to be treated poorly.
The concept of the hotel is pretty cool, but it's not worth the money and really poor service.

title: Loved Yotel
body:
Clean, bright, informal, friendly place to stay - perfect for a business trip with fast wifi access throughout the hotel. I believe there was wifi in each cabin, but had slight difficulty accessing internet a couple of times late at night when I should have been sleeping anyway, so no big deal!
Warm, friendly and very helpful staff - nothing too much trouble for them.
Location is great - it's a short walk to a huge variety of good places to eat in Hell's Kitchen, easy walk to Macy's and other shopping on 34th St and short 2 block walk to Port Authority and access to Subway and rest of the city.
I'd read on Tripadvisor that beds were uncomfortable, so was a bit apprehensive as there's nothing worse than a bad nights sleep, but I found mine firm but very comfy and I slept like a log! Loved the button that moved the bed from flat to upright position which was ideal for watching TV from. 
Cabin Crew left the room really clean and made up well. They replaced all the towels daily - something I'd be happier not having done as it's more environmentally friendly, but there was no option for this unless I told the Cabin Crew myself. Some hotels in Europe have a rule - leave the towel in the shower base if you want it replaced, hang it up if you want to reuse, which I much prefer - it may be a small drop in the ocean, but if lots of people were to do it...
I found other guests a bit noisy going to and leaving their rooms during the night, which is down to their lack of consideration, not the hotels fault. Otherwise you could hear a pin drop during the night on my floor.
I loved, loved, loved the muffins for breakfast - they were really good, even though they are very unhealthy - but I looked forward to this treat every morning! The coffee ran out here quickly, but was always replaced after a few mins wait.
I will definitely stay here again - I spent a full 7 nights, and I'm more than happy to return again.

title: Cool, Clean & Convenient
body: what more can you ask for... except for maybe Cheap. And yes, the rates are VERY competitive for the NYC area (very close to Time Square). Yotel is big on economy, high on style and has (almost) everything you need in a cool hotel. No room service and no on demand movies. Cabins are small but furnished in a way to mitigate claustrophobia. Staff is very helpful. Food prices are a bit high, but all in all, a great stay. Would definitely go back next time I'm in town.

title: The staff has no idea of what's going on
body: I was all too excited to stay at this "Jetson" like hotel, all to find out it is really like an Ikea hotel, everything was so small, the bed was uncomfortable, and while it does look modern and has great features the service was terrible. Non of the staff was sure about anything, so my questions went like this "Is the rooftop open?" the response I got, "no" it is closed for an event" I said that the guy downstairs told me it would be open to guests as well, I got oh yeah that is true. and this went on all night. Also the alarm went off in the middle of the night and security got on the loud speaker and told people to go to stairwells and then false alarm and then back to evacuating, like they had no clue. this was went on from 12:45am til about 1am. So annoying. Th food in the little restaurant area to the left of the 4th floor has he driest wings I have ever eaten, they were not fresh at all. I was so disappointed :( Oh and it took me like 10 minutes to figure out how to turn off the lights in the room.

title: second visit
body:
Our second visit wasn't as excellent as the first, but he overall experience was good. My only complaint this time around was the bed. It was considerably harder than the last time we stayed here, which made sleeping somewhat uncomfortable. Futons can be hit or miss with me and this one was definitely a miss.
The rooms are small, but adequate, and very clean. As I mentioned in my first review of this hotel, the bathrooms are "unusual" The sliding glass door is really cool but diminishes privacy. The shower is awesome

title: Amazing Yotel
body: This is a really fashion hotel. It's situated only 10-15 min. walking to Times Square. The atmosphere is really young. Views, free muffins buffet and terrace are really amazing. Tiny rooms but enough for a young couple. Friendly stuff.

title: Girl at front desk..
body:
As I was checking in thru the kiosk in the ground floor I approach a young lady by the name of Nardory because I was having a difficult time checking in. She was not very friendly and seems that she did not want to be bother with me. I felt that she was very rude and unprofessional and had an attitude problem.
I am a buisness traveller and has stay in this hotel on many occasions. I asked her if she knew what she was doing an she stated that she was in training. I then ask to speak with someone with more knowledge that can assist me, she stated that I would have to wait for a manager.
I was trying to get eye contact with her because i needed help with my reservations and she was ignoring me. If i am going to get this kind of treatment from this young lady i would rather stay some where else.

title: Not bad at all
body: I have stayed at the Yotel 3X in the past year, all for business. The hotel has a great location and is very clean and well kept. Rooms are small, as most are in NYC, but a good value for the price. Outdoor bar is nice, with a good happy hour every day. Food is so-so, but you are in NYC, so why would you eat in a hotel? Overall a pretty good place for a night or two.

title: We spent a week here and loved it
body: As four pensioners, we did wonder beforehand if we would cope with the high tech aspects of this hotel. When we arrived, tired and a bit confused, the staff took over and smoothed the path to our 'cabin.' Everyone we came across was helpful and friendly. The rooms are small, comfortable and very clean. The views are great. The position is very central and our group would certainly recommend it. Don't worry about the tech bits - we got quite expert and enjoyed it.

title: Great Location, Great Value
body: This is our 2nd stay at the Yotel this year and once again, I was impressed with the level of service and overall pleasantness of our stay. We were travelling with another couple for a long weekend in NY (3 days, 2 nights). We arrived well before check-in time, but the staff were accommodating, parked our car, helped us stow our bags and told us when our rooms would be ready. The rooms were ready right when they said they would be and check in was easy and uneventful. Although everything is automated and can be done "self-serve", we find that there are always plenty of staff on ground level and they are always standing by to assist. I recognized many of the staff from our previous visit 5 months ago and assume that the level of staff retention says something about hotel management. Whenever we needed directions, restaurant suggestions, a cab or assistance with buying tickets for a broadway show, the staff were extremely helpful, knowledgable and friendly. The rooms are small, but extremely efficient and clean. They are probably not ideal for two friends but work perfectly for a single or couple. Everything is designed smartly from the heated towel racks to the placement of the plugs. And, although it's not right in your room, the kitchen with water, coffee and tea is great to have on your floor. It's nice to be able to grab a coffee or tea on our way back to our room after being out shopping all day. The free muffins in the morning on the 4th floor are also a nice perk - the muffins are delicious and the lounge area is very comfortable. Computers are also available on the 4th floor for anyone who needs to quickly look something up or log into email etc... There is a 30 minute time limit on each of the 4 computers available which ensures that people can get on. The only complaint I would have would be that the elevators were very slow at times. The hotel does not offer room service but that was not an issue for us. Finally, the location is great. Just a short walk to the subway, times square and broadway but far enough away that you're not right in the middle of the madness. We considered staying at other hotels which were similarly priced but there was no comparison from an overall service point of view. The rooms might be a bit bigger, but many of the other hotels are old and tired, don't have free wifi, don't have a comfortable lounge with fresh baked muffins or the great staff that this hotel does. The vibe here is young and hip - and we're not, but we'd definitely stay here again!

title: New, Clean and Great Value!
body:
I have recently stayed at Yotel in NYC and I'd highly recommend this place to anyone who is looking to stay at a decent hotel with reasonable price. 
WHAT I LIKED:
1. NEW: Brand new and clean hotel with very hip decor. The feeling was like staying at one of the studio apartments in NYC.
2. BED: Comfortable bed with handmade organic mattress and Egyptian cotton bed linen which definitely helped my sleep quality and especially overcoming jet lag
3. VALUE: All prices include free WiFi and free calls within the U.S (this is definitely a big plus)
WHAT I DISLIKED:
1. LOCATION: Though the location is pretty good in my opinion (10 - 15 minutes walk to Times Square), but it may be more ideal for leisure trip than business trip.
2. NOISE: Some noise was experienced during the weekend as some very drunk fellows would make noise in the hallway in the middle of night 
3. YOBOT: The ideal is cool, however the luggage storage process took a bit longer than usual and it'd be nice if the process can be improved
In a nutshell, I'd definitely go back and stay in Yotel in my next trip!

title: The Return of the Yotel
body:
After having had a great time staying here in 2011, when we decided to visit NYC again this year, the decision to stay once more at Yotel was very easy. 
This is my previous review: http://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g60763-d2079052-r118195497-YOTEL_New_York_at_Times_Square_West-New_York_City_New_York.html
Things have changed a bit ever since. Mostly for the better. We were offered bigger rooms at special rates as part of their eStandby Upgrade program. So we took advantage of that and upgraded to a huge room with a hot tub on the terrace. This was totally worth it for a two week stay. There were some minor issues with the billing later on but Linda (special commendation to her) cleared all that up for me in no time. 
They've gotten really busy. And that was perhaps the only negative point. Last time around, someone greeted us upon arrival and helped with our bags etc. None of that was present this time. It's not a big deal but it somehow felt like the personal touch was missing just a bit. Oh well, at least you always have Yobot :)
In conclusion, this is a great hotel, with friendly service and an absolutely unique experience. Everybody should stay here at least once. And yes, when we're back in NYC, we'll stay here again.

title: High expectations but kinda disappointed.
body:
I was an in town guest last night, having to stay somewhere for the night while my floors were being done. I was blown away by the great TA reviews and rushed to book my room.
At $321 for a "first class room", I was "ok" but not thrilled. First of all, the kiosk wouldn't allow me to check in. I had to go up to the 4th floor and wait for 30 minutes while they checked to see if my room was ready. After about 20 minutes I went back to the girl and told her that I needed her to personally go see if the room was ready. I found that to be a lack of strong hospitality skills - if the maintenance or housekeeping person isn't answering or getting an answer for your patiently waiting guest, do it yourself. Take charge, make decisions. I was sitting there like an idiot for 30 minutes after telling her that I was exhausted. And this was at 5pm, well after check in time.
Aside from that, the things I didn't like...
- You can't charge your bar or restaurant charges to the room - "we're a separate company" - most hotels have independent vendors that allow you to bill directly to your room. I have NEVER been a hotel bar or restaurant that refused a charge to a room. Figure it out people.
- NO glasses - all plastic cups. I came back with wine (thank god I had the wine store open it). The Yotel bar refused to lend me a glass. I was shocked, especially since I spent $40 at the bar earlier that night. So I went to my room and had to peel the saran wrap off a flimsy plastic cup in the bathroom like I was staying at a Toledo Airport Travelodge or something. So cheap and really angered me, at $321 a night.
- Kleenex is in a cheap little plastic pouch instead of being readily accessible
- Cheap and cheesy "spaceship" furniture - like a massive TV-case with plasticky shelves that will never be stored with books. Either stock the shelves or ditch them for simplicity.
- No room service
- The shower was marketed as a "monsoon shower" - not really - its just a basic shower with a square head.
- The bed is overly firm - no box spring - just a rather thin mattress inside a bed frame
Things I liked: 
- Very clean room
- My first cabin had a cozy couch with a lot of space to sprawl out
- Great bathroom products that I was considering buying
- Amazing pillows that I was considering buying
- The galley on each floor has awesome free Lavazza coffee with takeaway cups
- Free wifi, which was pretty fast
- The happy hour at the bar is good and the menu looked interesting
- Even though I was on the 8th floor, had a nice view
- A little foldable map of NYC, very nice touch
- Bright airy bathroom with a huge window overlooking the city
All in all, I was disappointed more than I was jazzed, especially by the check-in, plastic cups, bed quality, etc. But liked certain elements.
Bottom line, I would probably not bother to stay here again. Tons of choices in NYC and it didn't draw me in.

title: NYC's funkiest hotel rooms?... but pricey
body:
So. You want a very different hotel experience in NYC and the Yotel certainly does that. Everything about this place is quirky and funky. Instead of a left luggage room they've got a YO-BOT which is a giant Robot that takes your case, it's very cool. As is the lift and Mission Control (Reception!).
The room was cool, small but every available space is well used. Loved that in design they'd factored in places for your iPhone! Also the folding bed is cool. 
The location is amazing, just 10 minutes walk from Time Square. 
The walls in the cabins (rooms) are paper thin and the doors are noisy when closing them, so don't expect undisturbed sleep. 
A couple of things we had issues with.... on booking.com I paid for a premium view room - on arrival this wasn't available. Also on check-out the reception staff were quite arsey about sorting this and charged me the full 'with view' tariff - even though we hadn't had that. I complained when I got home and they did refund the costs but its just hassle you don't need. 
One other thing that felt like unnecessary drama are the guys outside the hotel trying to flag cabs, they're far more of a hindrance than benefit... avoid them, walk round the corner and you'll get a cab much easier.
I would recommend this hotel for how cool it is...!

title: Yotel is not a notel... but the location?
body: My husband and I recently stayed at the Yotel, NYC. We loved our room and the view AND the fact that you could open the windows for some fresh air. The rooms are clean and FUN and reasonably priced. The service at checkin was great, people were very friendly. After that, we were a little disappointed.The staff in the restaurant/bar seem a little disgruntled. The purchased breakfast left a little to be desired. However, the appetizers later were delicious! The drinks were great (strong).... I am not one to enjoy being in the midst of madness (Times Square) so the location would be the only reason that I might not return to Yotel, NYC.

title: First visit to Manhattan
body:
Difficult to add anything that hasn't already been covered in previous reviews. We stayed in the basic queen cabin which was small but well designed and adequate for the 6 nights we stayed. The crew in the hotel were polite, friendly and helpful from check in to check out. The room was clean and fresh on our return each night. We used the galley for chilled water and took advantage of the lovely muffins and fresh coffee to go from the 4th floor most mornings. The beds are firm as they are luxury futons not traditional sprung divans. The hotel has reliable super speed wifi throughout.
The location is good on 42nd Street at 10th Avenue. A five minute walk takes you to Port Authority Bus terminal and Subway (coaches leave for all three airports). Another five or ten minutes takes you to Times Square and Broadway. You are also really handy for all the restaurants in the Hells Kitchen area which is about ten minutes on foot.
If you are looking for traditional old style hotel then this is perhaps not the hotel for you however if a bit younger (or young at heart) looking for a modern well run hotel the Yotel fits the bill.

title: The future is here
body:
Yotel - it's a funky young and very modern place. Everything is extremely functional and thought through. The bed (I booked a premium cabin on the upper floors) is convertible into a lounger, on the press of a button. The entertainments set is fabulously big and it's easy to plug in your own iPod. But what I especially liked about this place - there is no chichi reception area, but a few friendly guys quicky explaining how to use the self-service check-in terminals.
I loved the spacious room set-up: there is no wall blocking your view, but a floor-to-ceiling window. A daylight bathroom. Fantastic! The rooms are not necessarily huge by NYC standards, but they feel much lighter and airy because everything is white and open space. No dusters or other distracting nonsense drawers or else.
The floors' galleys are great: free tea, coffee and a soft drink vending machine make a traveller's life so much easier than an obscenely expensive minibar. 
The baggage store room is fully automated, and everything here is pretty self contained. Excellent! No queues or other talks.
Tried the food downstairs at 'Four' too. Food's been lovely, but remember to take your credit card when picking up the food, they won't put it on your room - that's a bit inconvenient, but once you know - go for it.
You ring them, you pick up your food, sorted - no in-room service fuss!
Another plus is the complimentary coffee/tee/muffin grab-and-go breakfast. Very handy in the mornings. It's beautiful to sip your first coffee on their terrace.
OK, here's the trick: the Yotel is on 10th which is a bit off the trail. No probs with fun travellers, but with be being on business a bit of an annoyance to get hold of a cab in the mornings - it's hard to stop one, though the doormen were more than helpful.
One thing they could do better: divert the lifts as it can take you 'ages' to reach to top floors with other guests stopping on the lower floors. But it's bearable, and just a side note.

title: A good experience
body: The hotel was perfect, all new , clean, and near times square. the rooms are modern and equipped, and beautiful views.People are friendly and very attentive.The common area very modern and stylish.The value for money is very good for the prices that are in new york.

title: Sacraficed comfort for glam
body: Our 4 night stay turned into a one night stay after we realized this was not a hotel for us. It's very space-aged looking and modern upon arrival. There's a big robotic arm that takes your luggage which I guess is cool but alerted me that maybe priorities were out of line here. We opened the door to our 'cabin' and were shocked. It was tiny. And I mean tiny for NYC. The small bed folded up in the wall (our motorized bed was broken so it wouldn't go back) with a very small bathroom attached with no door just a glass slide. There was a 'desk' where I'd hoped to get work done but it had to hold our luggage since there was no other room. And the bed. If you can even call it that. The reason we left after one night. Neither my husband or I could walk the next day. We're both tall - maybe the bed is better for one small person, but it was awful for us. Especially for the price we had paid. I woke up the next morning so unhappy. The staff was kind and allowed me to cancel my reservation for the next 3 nights and we went down the street to a less expensive but much more comfortable hotel and were quite happy. If you're into hip and space-aged maybe this is for you. If you want room to walk, a door to close on the bathroom, and a bed to actually rest comfortably in I wouldn't recommend it.

title: Yotel - NYC Great Value and Location
body:
Great Service, Great Location, Great Price
Clean and free 24hr coffee 
The breakfast muffins are awesome!
Cocktails on the terrace are a must!
You can walk to restaurants, theatres and Central Park
Would stay there again, definitely

title: Yo'll love Yotel
body:
I stayed in the Yotel in September 2012 and found it a quirky experience. I was sharing a bunk bed room with my friend for four nights. The location was really handy, and plenty of storage for us both. The only downside is the air conditioning fans are right by your head if you are sleeping in the bunk, so you wake up with ice on your nose! Me and my friend shared the bed in the end, to save us both from hyperthermia! 
The staff were great and hailed you cabs within seconds, and every morning we had free muffins and coffee on the terrace which is a lovely quiet start to your busy day in NYC. 
A good feature is your keycard only works in certain elevators so people visiting the resturant cannot access the rooms without a card. 
The galley with the vending machine, fridge and microwave was extremely handy storing all the cheesecake you cannot manage to eat! (not that ours ended up in the fridge...)
Although I did not enjoy the city as much as I thought I would, I would highly reccomend staying at the Yotel.

title: Small but very nice rooms
body:
A "cabin-style" hotel, centrally located near Times square. Very efficient check-in.
Very nice bed! The room is tiny, but that should not be a surprise. The room has what you need (if you dont need a lot of space). Wifi, TV, nice shower...
Relatively cheap (although not compared to European cities). 
All in all a nice experience!

title: Glamorous however bed not comfy
body: I love the hotel. The softness of the bed is horrible for the price we payed however I will probably stay again. If I found it at a cheaper rate. The service was very pleasant an helpful. Very Gay friendly Hotel. We stayed for two nights. The hotel is walking distance to Time Square. We didn't get to experience what the hotel has to offer because we were so busy.

title: Yotel
body: Was a great stay with a simple, elegant, and efficient room. Loaded with all the features you need and a couple extras. Overall the value of the location was not bad either for the price. If you head to a musical or the theater it is all just a walk away.. Elevator music was cool and the morning sounds delightful.

title: Take it if you can
body:
I stayed here 4 nights this month, during a visit to NY. I had a bad opinion about NY hotels, because you pay a lot for what you get. I found this hotel for an excellent price, and I changed my idea about New York hotels. 
I think that in the future will be difficult to get a room available here, but for now it's my best choice in NY.
Brand new, totally different from any hotel where I've stayed before (and I travel a lot...), good location, nice view, good price, free wi-fi, breakfast included, friendly staff, all this near Times Sq.
If you are old fashioned, and expect a waiter to open you the door, don't do there.

title: Fantastic Hotel
body: Fantastic hotel, 10 mins. walk from Times Square. Hotel room small but adequate, very clean and ultra modern. Staff are very friendly. No coffee/tea facils. in room but there is a kitchen with machine and kettle on each floor. Shower good and bed comfy. Coffee and muffins for breakfast are tasty, free and you can have as many as you want, but there are lots of alternatives in area. I will definitely stay in this hotel when I go back to New York.

title: Amazing
body:
Having just returned from NYC after never being before I just want to share my experience with you all. I chose this hotel as I liked the look of the place and its newness. This hotel did not disappoint it was spotlessly clean and the front of house staff on the door were so friendly and very helpful nothing was too much. The reception staff were as equally helpful and our check in was swift and painless.
When we got to our room it seemed a little small and something that I had not experienced in other hotels very modern and capsule like. When we unpacked what little we had brought we started to relax and enjoy our space. Our hotel room was only to sleep as we had so much planned and it did more than its job clean comfy and a great base for a weeks shopping and sightseeing. Only ate once at hotel and it was lovely and the galleys for free tea and coffee, water , soft drinks and ice were great and so easy to use and spotlessly clean . Overall amazing holiday great hotel and central for everything but still quiet enough to sleep and rest. Fully recommend this hotel and New York very safe for a mum and teenage daughter travelling alone.

title: I highly recommend YOTEL
body: It was my first stay at Yotel and I wasn't sure what to expect. But from now on, I will stay nowhere else. The room was well-lit, cozy, clean, and the staff nice and helpful. The floor-to-ceiling window that opens is a nice component. When I got stuck during Hurricane Sandy, they were extremely accommodating. My favorite thing was the galley kitchen on every floor! Very handy and what's not to like about limitless cappuccinos?

title: A great stay ay YOTEL
body:
We have just returned from a four night stay at Yotel during Hurricane Sandy and we're very pleased that we chose such a great hotel. As soon as we arrived it was clear to see that the hotel was extremely busy and all the staff were working very hard to accommodate people. Nothing was too much trouble, we needed an engineer to snap a broken padlock off of my partner's suitcase, and they were with us within 15 minutes. Throughout Hurrican Sandy, the hotel continued to impress, laying on complimentary lunches and films, and making it easy for us to extend our stay had our flight been delayed.
The hotel itself is clean and modern and we didn't find the rooms too small, turning the bed into a sofa is a nice space saving idea. Having access to water/tea/hot chocolate from the Galley Kitchen was really useful at the end of a long day. The hotel is in a great location, 10 minutes from Broadway/Times Sqaure and close to lots of bars and restaurants on 9th Avenue.
Overall, we were very happy that we booked YOTEL, it was nice to return to such a great place after being battered by the wind and rain. Our only complaint is that there aren't more Yotel's across the world for us to visit!

title: BRILLIANT
body:
My Mum and I stayed at this hotel for a girly weekend in New York. The location was perfect - 10 minutes walk from Times Square and very close to the subway. We felt safe walking in the area at all times. The hotel staff were friendly and efficient from the minute we arrived. The room was very small but just what we needed and it was nice to feel like you were paying for what you needed rather than for extra space or fancy decoration. The room was spotlessly clean and the towels were changed each day. The access to free hot drinks and filtered water was very helpful as was the fridge. 
We got stuck in the hotel during Hurricane Sandy. The staff could not have been nicer. They extended our stay without question and reduced the price of the room by $100 a night - seriously impressive. When we managed to squeeze onto an earlier flight they were delighted for us and did not charge us for the nights we thought we would be staying for. They put on special meals while the hurricane hit and the staff all worked really hard. 
There is storage for luggage if you have an evening flight and a very cool robot to put the bags away!
I could not recommend this hotel more. It is certainly not luxurious and plush but it is totally effective and good value. The staff are lovely and the location brilliant. I was recommended the hotel by a friend and i will certainly be recommending it again.

title: An excellent location and great rooms for a city break.
body:
I stayed at the Yotel New York for 7 days. We arrived past midnight and were slightly worried as our booking said our room would only be held until midnight, however this was not a problem. One of the doormen helped us to check in on the computers and told us exactly where to go for our room, he even offered to help us with our suitcases.
We found our room easily, following his instructions, and were pleased to see a nicely made crisp white bed. The lighting in the room was good- you could put on the gentle purple light or a yellowy glow light so you weren't blinded in the night or as you woke up in the morning. The bed was really comfy and the adjustable mattress was great fun - especially after a long day's walking and shopping.
The only issue we had with the room was the lack of privacy in the bathroom. We understood there would be a curtain separating the two sections of the room but didn't realise quite how open plan it would be! Being friends that have known each other for over ten years this wasn't a problem but I can imagine for less acquainted people it could be embarassing or awkward.
We were on the 20th floor and had a great view of the Empire State Building!
The Galley Kitchen was brilliant. We didn't mind not having tea or coffee facilities in the room, it was great having filtered water and ice at the push of the button. The microwave also came in very handy when we were stuck indoors due to Hurricane Sandy.
The hotel staff were really good during the storm. No body knew what was happening but they did their best to keep people calm and informed. Lots of people were evacuated to the hotel and you could see the staff were busy but they always kept a smile on their face, despite not knowing what the weather would bring. The day after the storm Yotel put on a buffet lunch as everyone was stranded at the hotel and everywhere was shut due to lack of power etc. This was very welcome! They also converted the Studiyo into a cinema for the afternoon which was great and meant we were able to escape the 4 walls of our room for a change of scene.

title: Love The Hotel - Just Not The Location
body:
Just a bit off the beaten path for my likes since I need to get to subways or walk to client sites. Otherwise it is a fine location if you don't mind a short walk to get into the heart of things.
The hotel itself was even more fun this time than last time I stayed there. I was able to take advantage of the lobby (was closed for special event last time) which is spacious and very "social". If you need some privacy there are rooms behind glass ringing the lobby. The room itself is small but it is built for small space and I in no way felt closed in. The bed folds into a couch with the push of a button. I also ate "room service" which means you order and head down to pick it up. No problem at all and had I known how cool the restaurant was, I might have just ate there. The food was GREAT, but the portions VERY small and relatively expensive. I would actually rate at 3.5 (just not a 4 star due to location??)

title: Very Unique and Fun to Stay
body: This was one of the highlights of our night in New York next to the play and the food the Yotel was a must revisit place in NY. They made our visit one to remember the staff was the best the rooms make you feel you are on a cruise ship with a view of New York city plus breakfast was amazing. I recommend you check out Yotel this is a Must Visit place especially if you want to gain points with your other half

title: Yotel is small and cute!
body:
We had lost power during Hurricane Sandy and decided to check into the Yotel Hotel. The staff was a little overwhelmed, which is to be expected since the Hurricane and Marathon were happening at the same time, yet they were always calm and cool.
The rooms are tiny, but they are really clean and futuristic looking. The bed was very comfortable. If you're okay with small quarters that have a fun, kitschy feel to it, then you'll love this hotel. It was much more awesome than we expected!

title: Great concept!
body:
We've been at the Yotel for a business trip for 6 nights. The rooms are really small but extremely functional. The architect is a genious! The robot which stores your luggage is really something special you'll never would expect. We've been there during hurricane Sandy and had to spend 2 entire days in the hotel. They have offered a complimentary hurricane Sandy lunch buffet which was really great. The only negative point is, that you can't put your bar and restaurant spendings on your hotel invoice. You always have to pay your consumtptons cash or by credit card. This is something unusual for me as I'm used to just sign the bill and it will be on my invoice upon check out.
Overall I can really recommend the Yotel!

title: We will stay here every time we go to New York
body: What an awesome hotel! We booked four nights at this hotel for our first trip to New York and absolutely loved it! The hotel is modern and streamlined and every attention to detail is thought of. We found the staff helpful and pleasant, and the free breakfast and coffee/tea was a lovely part of our stay. The rooms and building are pristine and well taken care of. We found the bed extremely comfortable and the design of the white-on-white (with purple accents) rooms and hallways just perfect. The location was great for us to walk right to Times Square and to local restaurants and theatres. Highly recommend!

title: Impressive
body: Stayed here for 4 nights, I do not have one negative thing to say about the hotel. Clean. Quiet. Excellent use of space in hotel room! Would definitely stay there again! It is very sleek. Hotel staff at entrance very friendly, each and every day!

title: It really is chic, cool and hip
body:
I stayed at Yotel in 10th Ave for two nights post Hurricane SaNDdy. It was very cool, and the room views were amazing of the ManhattaN skyline. THe bed was suPER COMFORTAble and the rooam ultra clean.
I love the self servIce bar for tea and coffee on each floor and the restaurant DohYo was excellent. If I had onecrticism its the staff. they are not well trained In hospitality in my opinion and the wait staff weerre inatteantive and unhelapful. would not stop me from staying again though

title: Impressive in every way
body: There are great reviews on the location, service and value of this hotel already which I wholeheartedly agree with and will not repeat. One thing that really impressed me was the standby upgrade offers Yotel emails you a few days prior to check-in. I opted in for the cheapest upgrade at $14 a night to a corner view room. However when we arrived, there were no corner view rooms available. The check-in staff kindly upgraded us to a larger room but still only charging us the lower rate. The other thing that was a highlight for me was the free real coffee that was available - a great way to wake up to a day of sight seeing in the city.

title: Wonderful!! Solo groovy
body: This hotel was so great. I chose it because it was close to Jacob javits center.. Walking distance for this year2012 NY Comicon. It was just myself and my 13year old daughter, who just loved this hotel. The rooms are so well thought out, using all its space efficiently. The staff was super helpful and polite---no attitude whatsoever. The little "kitchen" area is private and well stock Ed with free beverages, ect.. We can't wait to stay here again for next year's Comicon. The restaurant and free coffee, teas and variety of muffins in the morning are the best!!

title: Look what the wind blew in
body: My family of four stayed in a premium queen cabin with bunk. The room was small but well equipped. We arrived shortly after Sandy and the hotel was short staffed which appeared to somewhat effect the cleanliness of the room. Under the circumstances though it was a nice stay. There is a galley on each floor where you can grab a coffee or latte. The morning muffins were also a nice touch and our kids loved the bunk and the yobot. The beds are somewhat hard. Finally our view from the 27th floor was great.

title: Annoying things about an otherwise nice hotel
body:
On the first night I was awake several times with blinking lights somewhere on the ceiling coming from some thing like a smoke detector or something. Plus they are multiplied in the mirror positioned right next to the door. I'm a light sleeper. I could not sleep well after a transatlantic flight and woke several times and those blinking lights were kinda creepy. Don't think that can be eliminated somehow. Had to get used to.
The overhead shower lacks power. If it were an ordinary shower which you might take off the rack it would be more handy as water pressure is insufficient. So don't expect envigorating nice hot streams of steaming hot water - just a quick wash. 
My usual complaint - complimentary coffee and tea at breakfast were horrible. Did not touch coffee after trying and stuck to tea. Had to use 2 or three bags per cup to get some brew. I also had two, sometimes three muffins! Sorry! On my last morning i noticed a small sign "Please take one muffin per person"! Made me feel really mean! Tried the $19 breakfast once - not worth the price. 
Okay these are just whims. I enjoyed Yotel.

title: Liked the Yotel
body: Great staff and crew! Very nice view (26th floor on the Hudseon river). Very good bed, slept like a bay. Nice selection of tv channels. Good muffins for breakfast, with coffee to go. Very practical! Liked it very much. I wish to go back one day.

title: Excellent Hotel
body: Superb hotel. Location is very good, walking distance to all uptown areas. Staff are extremely good and willing to help. We stayed there during hurricane Sandy and cannot say enough about how good the staff were during the difficult time, hotel was full but the hotel is so well run and friendly it did not miss a beat. Rooms were comfortable and well designed. Galley on each floor was great, had a fridge in there where you could leave leftovers and was always there the next day. Would stay here again and would recommend it to everyone.

title: With Hurricane Sandy at NY
body: Yotel Time Square is a futuristic hotel, central located in midtown manhattan.. Subway a few steps away.. many places of interest are reachable by feet.. small but clean and good conceveid cabins.. pretty friendly and helpful staff.. well prepared - enough food/drinks - during the hurricane sandy..

title: Yotel NEW york
body: Ecceller place to STAy. Last month Ii came to ny only with my daughter 8year old?She chose from web yotel hotel and we loved that choice very much! So now we invite all THE people to nave out beautiful experience. Be' sure choose yotel hotel!!!!!

title: Clean but rude
body:
The pro's- Check-in went quickly with the automated (with attendants standing by), our room was very clean everyday and a great shower. Check out went smooth along with holding of bags while we went out during the last day.
The cons- One of the bellman was very rude to my wife while assisting another guest. Two different occasions (and two different girls) the hostesses were EXTREMELY rude to us, so rude I almost checked out right there. Our waiter was very polite but seemed to be the only one in our area, so very slow. Food was very average. The galley on our floor was dirty with no working coffee or water. The walls were very thin.

title: Great hotel for a short visit
body: Modern, even futuristic, hotel 3 blocks from Times Sq. Rooms are small for 2 guests but well engineered and actually quite comfortable and relaxing. Great bar and restaurant with free muffins and coffee for breakfast. Helpful employees are everywhere!

title: excellent staff
body: small but cute room only amenity not provided was hand lotion (little odd). Excellent desk and restaurant staff. Location is terrific -near the pony bar and 5 napkin burger - as well as times square. Will stay again.

title: Good Value. Clean. Efficient.
body: Very Good Hotel. Good automatic check in and out, avoiding lines. Good location. Rooms are weel equipped and clean although small. Very good for sleep over, not many activities or enterteinmant in house.

title: YOTEL the best
body:
Clean. Quiet. Fast check-in and very fast check-out. Full services. Muffin, coffee and water free are great. Near the Highline and near the Public Library. In the middle of restaurant area.
During Sandy days YOTEL offers a lot of help for food and facilties at a good price. Not problem to have may room at a good price for my forced staying.

title: Love it!
body:
This is a great find in NYC. There are a lot of great restaurants around and it was a new neighborhood for me to explore. I had a small cabin the first two nights and paid for an upgrade to a suite the rest of the stay. The suite was big and lovely.
Pros: free wifi, a techie's dream, complimentary breakfast or hot one for $9.99, great staff, work rooms and great food.
Cons: Staff is a bit overwhelmed and could not anticipate when my room would be ready and kept giving me conflicting information and thanking me for my patience. No room service.

title: A Hotel Experience!
body: Great location! Walking distance to Javits Convention center and Times Square. The check in kiosk was quick and easy. Free muffin and coffee breakfast was better than the usual stale bagels that I've had at other hotels. They also have a tasty lunch menu. Rooms are small, especially if you have a lot of luggage. No closet, just a couple of short rods to hang clothes and a couple of drawers. Friendly and helpful staff. Will definitely be back!

title: New York experience
