body: This was a great experience Very different and the service was great The robot in lobby to store your luggage was convenient and fun to use. Rooms small but very functional. Morning continental breakfast was just right and served in a relaxed atmosphere.Just close enough to walk to Times Square and jazz clubs and Broadway Shows.

title: Does the Job not much more
body:
Located on 10th Avenue in Midtown the Hotel was an okay distance from Times Square but not really convenient for other attractions such as Central Park, Top of th Rock or Bloomingdales. If you do not mind walking for a good 15- 30 minutes then the location is fine.
Clean rooms but very compact - do not visit New York if you like your own personal space! It was a little uncomfortable for us in the bedroom during Hurricane Sandy as we were locked up for 48 hours and did not have a lot of space to move about (had to sit on the bed all day), however I think this was really a one off experience and hopefully not everyone will be trapped inside! Staff okay, they are not really bothered about Customer Service or 'going the extra mile', this is a Hotel for convenience not luxury.
Hotel offers free WiFi and 4 computers for guests to use in the Reception area - very handy when looking up attractions, shows, restaurants, ticket prices etc. There is also a concierge there, however most of the time we found that it was closed (presume it is perhaps a 9-5 thing?).
Yotel provided food during Sandy, however we were very disappointed to be charged $18 each for lunch and $25 each for dinner, whilst we would have been happy to make a small contribution for the cost of the food we did feel that they were 'cashing in' on the situation. Was also disappointing that they offered no help or information on 'what to do' in a Hurricane or in the event of evacuation especially as most of their guests would never have been in a Hurricane before

title: Loved it
body:
I was attracted to Yotel as part of our honeymoon stay for it's location, price and how cool it looked.(Check out the Yobot) 
We arrived late night and were helped easily through the check in station and up to our room from the friendly front door man, took about 5 minutes from getting out taxi to being left alone in room. Rooms are small but they are very well laid out with shelving mods, hanging space and a connector to run your ipod through the tv. 
They provide hand / body / hair wash at the sink and in shower however I didnt like the smell of it so bought my own shower gel, just personal taste.
You really have to be very comfortable with who you're sharing the room with when it comes to using the toilet as it's only seperated from the bed by 2 shower style curtains and a sliding shower door so make sure you have the tv volume up :)
The bed design looks great as you just press the button to move it down for sleeping and press it back up to create more space during the day. However, it wasn't the comfiest to sleep in. Maybe it's because I'm not a skinny person but the metal bar under the mattress was digging into my hip bone whatever way I slept so I was awake on and off a number of times each night.
The galley on each floor is a fantastic service offering free hot drinks, water, ice and a vending machine with soft drinks for $2. We stayed on floor 21 and it seemed to be the only one who's air conditioning wasn't working. It was boiling hot everytime you opened the door and there was never any ice in the machine.
We had to go to other floors a number of times when the coffee machine was needing emptied, there was no coffee pods re-filled, no cups or milk. I would recommend doing what we did after a few times of not being able to get a drink on our floor. Go into the galley, take the number of coffee cups you need for the next drink and keep them in your room. It saves having to check other floors around you or having to go down to Floor 4 ( the main reception area) and asking for items to be filled and/or having to get coffee from the breakfast area.
We endured Hurricane Sandy during our stay so were stuck in the hotel a lot more than we had planned which is probably why the coffee cups kept disappearing. The rooms are a bit too small to be in all day and there is only 1 desk style chair on wheels so you have to sit on the bed a lot. The staff were generally good but no-one told us anything that was happening with the Hurricane situation, we had to go ask ourselves what their policy was as ourselves and many other guests were due to check out but all the flights had been cancelled. 
The woman was helpful in looking up details for us to call airline to rebook (all local and US calls are free from your room) and Yotel were offering a 'Hurricane Rate' for all us travellers who had no choice but to stay extra nights.
We found the food prices to be very costly especially when we looked on 'Sandy' night, so we did what a lot of other guests were doing, went to the pizza place a couple minutes up the street, great food for a fraction of the price. 
One of the best things about Yotel in my opinion, is their free Wi-Fi service. It was a godsend being able to communicate with friends & family back home who were worried about the severe weather and also being able to kill time online while we had to stay indoors.
I would definately stay at Yotel again, highly recommend it especially if you're looking for somewhere a bit different from the norm.

title: Almost all I needed
body:
The rooms are well designed, very neatly decorated and despite small one feels comfortable. Power sockets conveniently distributed where needed, safe box and ironing board in room, good gym, relative to location not expensive.
What I was missing:
1. Stability and signal of wifi internet. I was often losing connectivity for dozens of seconds.
2. Plain water in room or in the floor kitchens (there is coffee and tea and a vending machine for other soft drinks, though)
3. There is an iPod connector to the TV but would be great to be able to play music through the TV speakers from e.g. an Android smartphone

title: Fantastic room, great location!
body: We were looking for a modern hotel that was the same in real life as it was in their promotional photos - Yotel was perfect! The location was excellent being only a few minutes walk from Times Square / Empire State Building. The view from our room was incredible and we were able to see the Empire State Building and the New Yorker. The room itself has more tech in it than our house! The room was small in comparison to regular hotels in New York however, everything was really nicely designed and well thought out, making it a fantastic place to stay, night after night. The bed was exceptionally comfortable and we slept soundly every night. We even had to stay in our room for an extended duration during Hurricane Sandy and were never put off by the space. A phone that is free to use for local numbers was exceptionally useful when booking reservations for restaurants. The hotel itself is wonderful with friendly and helpful staff and plenty of amenities. Each floor has its own Galley where unlimited hot and cold drinks are available as well as a vending machine. They even had actual tea bags! Our towels and bedding were replaced twice during our 7-night stay. The self check-in / check-out and Yobot are all easy to use and intuitive - there are always staff around to help in these areas should you need it however. We absolutely loved our stay, couldn't have wished for a better room, holiday and trip even despite Hurricane Sandy landing the day after we arrived. We'd have no hesitation to stay at Yotel again and would definitely recommend it whole-heartedly to anyone.

title: Still can't beat what you get for the price, but my room this time was not as well kept
body:
Whenever I go to NY for more than a few days, I always go to Yotel. The staff are super friendly and helpful, and overall I enjoy the room and it is exactly what I need. This was my third stay, I stayed on the 12th floor and felt that the room was clean, however the walls and surfaces in the bathroom did not look so well maintained as other rooms I've stayed in at the yotel (i.e chipped, scuffed, etc.). Still had a great stay, and I will be back.
Did not catch any of the crew member names' in the lobby, but they were all FANTASTIC

title: Really good place to stay - let down a little by breakfast
body:
I stayed in the Yotel in November 2012, in what was described as a Premium Queen cabin. I'm from the UK, so I didn't find the room size that small (theres room for a double bed and a desk and chair in the main section of the room), and the clever layout, with lots of hanging space and cubby holes meant that it didn't seem cluttered. I was on floor 20, and had a lovely view of the Empire State Building and New Yorker hotel, and (if I craned my neck slightly) I could see down to the World Trade Centre site and the new building they're putting up. 
I was worried about the bathroom - although I was travelling with my partner, a girl still likes a bit of privacy! However, the bathroom is split off with a glass wall which is then covered with a full length / full width curtain which solves the privacy issue nicely. I was very happy with the shower but it's important to remember it's a "rain" style shower, so even though the showerhead is huge, it's a gentle shower rather than a "rip your skin off" experience. The shower gel / bodywash provided comes in two scents, a nighttime one which is quite relaxing and a daytime one which is - um - an acquired taste, I think!
There are no water / coffee / fridge facilities in the room, and you are instead encouraged to use the "galley" which is a shared kitchen area on each floor. Anyone who has ever lived in a student hall of residence can imagine what this is like, and while the idea is done reasonably well, I wouldn't have felt confident of anything I put in the fridge being there when I came back for it as there was nothing to stop anyone else from taking it, and if you are the type who wakes up in the middle of the night wanting a drink, it's a good idea to remember to prepare one before going to bed as, depending where you are in the hotel, you could have a fair old trek to the galley (I am not sure if the water in the room was drinkable or not).
Breakfast is complimentary coffee and muffins on "Four", the reception floor for the hotel proper, although you could pay for a more traditional cooked breakfast if you wished. In keeping with the minimalist ethos, instead of a plate to put your muffin on, you got a napkin. There were also not enough tables for everyone who came to eat breakfast. Add these two things together and what happened was that every possible seating surface on "Four" was covered with people either spilling muffin crumbs everywhere, or muffin crumbs that people had already spilt, which kind of put you off sitting there. It made it impossible to eat the muffins in any kind of polite way, either. Which was a shame, because they were very nice!
Location-wise, it's at the top of Hells Kitchen and round the corner from the Port Authority Bus Terminal. I wrongly assumed this meant it might be dubious but I felt perfectly safe there, it looks like the Port Authority has been cleaning up. It's an easy walking distance (I'm British and reasonably fit) to Times Square and an enjoyable stroll up to Central Park and the Guggenhiem...the subway is also an option but I enjoyed seeing NYC itself rather than just a series of subway stops. 
I didn't use the bar or the restaurant, so I can't comment on those. I got this hotel for $210 a night inc taxes (NYC hotel taxes really stack up), and for that price I was very happy.

title: Great hotel for price in New York
body:
This is a fabulous hotel. Small rooms but with everything you need. Good options with the 'Galley' on each floor instead of in room mini bar.
Great downstairs bar and central to get around the city. Great service, quick check in. Will definitely stay again. There is a small but good gym. 
Only issue was being told that Envirosense ride to airport was only $5 more than a yellow cab. Nope. Cab from airport is set fee of $52 for yellow cabs. This was $75 plus we had to pay the toll of $7.50. So quite a difference in cost.

title: Good location and nice staff!
body:
This was my second stay in this hotel. 
The staff is helpfull ! 
You have free wireless.
Very nice breakfast (delicious muffins)
Nice view!Close to times square and city center.
Good quality/price ratio for NY!
I would go back, and reccomend it from every point of view!

title: Good value-for-money. Small rooms. So-so location.
body:
I stayed at the Yotel in connection with a business trip in October '12. The hotel is located 3 streets/2 blocks from Times SQ, so location is fine if your business is in the mid-/up-town area. The conference I was attending was 4-5 blocks away, so it was within walking distance.
The hotel is located "behind" the Port Authority Bus Terminal which is not exactly providing the best NY scenery. You could pay to get your room at a higher floor though. When you hit the street, you just wanna get away from there. Nothing is happening between 10th where the hotel is and Hudson river, but it's fine if you're heading for a morning run. Not much is going on in the very proximity of the hotel either, so you need a longer walk if you want decent food outside of the premises.
Free Wi-fi, complimentary "breakfast" (= coffee, tea and muffins), nice looking interior, friendly staff makes this a hotel I'd consider using again and definitely recommend to others looking for hotels in this price-range.
Overall the price vs. location vs. the small rooms makes it a reasonable choice for a nice hotel i NYC. You get what you pay for, so I guess that isn't too bad.

title: Funky theme, clean, modern room
body: I stayed here for one night for business. My room was very quiet, there was barely any hallway or street noise. The open glass of the bathroom and large window made the small room feel not so tiny. However, it was very compact and would have been difficult for more than one or two nights (or more than one person). The bed was not terribly comfortable, but was clean and fine for the one night. On each floor, there is a galley where you can make your own coffee, tea and fill up water bottles. I appreciated this more than an in-room minibar or coffee maker. I'm from the area and travel in for business often. I'm not a huge fan of the area this hotel is in (off-skirts of Times Sq, near Port Authority) but is an easily accessible area.

title: Great Price/Location/Quality
body: Yotel is a unique hotel experience, very modern and clean. Just blocks from Times Square, Javits Center, and many Theaters. Staff (crew members) are all very freindly and willing to help with just about anything.

title: A very good stay at the Yotel, despite Sandy !
body:
We spent 9 nights in a 4 sleeps Premium Cabin, and we really appreciated our stay. It was during the Sandy's events, and the crew was particularly nice. The bedding is very good, the hotel's location perfect (very close to Times Square, but Hell's Kitchen, where the Yotel is, is a better place to live, more "human" and specific). We really enjoyed the Galley (free coffee and chocolate "à volonté" on each floor), the fourth floor, the free wifi everywhere... We didn't ate at the restaurant but it looked (and smelled) good (there is a lot of take-away pizzas or wings or everything you want near the Yotel, and we often prefered this solution because we was really tired after our big walks in NY, and we were impatient to relax in our room !). There is also the awesome Landsome Road Pub 200m of the hotel, with a huge choice of tap beers (I recommend the Stone IPA, Indian Pale Ale).
During the storm, the Yotel was an amazing shelter, the crew was very calm and helpfull.
A *very* nice stay !

title: Cool futuristic hotel!!
body: Great hotel cool cabin styled rooms, Great location, walking distance form Times Square and Jacob Javits Center. Bed was a little on the hard side but it was fine for me. The room was a little on the small side but that is the norm for New York. Enjoyed staying here and will again my next time in New York...

title: Modern, clean in a great location!!!
body:
We spent a night at the hotel and even thought we did not eat at the hotel we were at the bar for a couple of hours. The bar has an incredible view of the skyline of NY City. The room was small and very modern looking. We had a partial view to the Hudson River but one can ask for the highest rooms where the view is much better.
The walk to Times Square is short and beautiful.
I would stay there again!

title: Good room, pity about the bar staff
body:
Rooms are compact, but fine for a couple of days. Not sure that it was really "times square" but not too far off. Bathroom was a little disconcerting, with a calico (read see through) curtain across the shower area and a glass door that didn't close flush with the wall for the toilet. Nothing much was left the imagination of the other occupant of the room. All that aside the room was everything that was promised by the website.
Pity about the bar staff - they clearly want a certain type of customer, of which a couple in their 30's who don't want to get overly dressed up (jeans & t-shirts) to have a beer were not the type. Service was slow (not a busy time). 
In summary, stay at the hotel, but find another bar, of which there are plenty around, to have a drink after a day of sightseeing.

title: WOW
body:
I'd highly recommend the Yotel...European in flavor...bright, clean...great breakfast value. Great location, just a 10 minute walk to Times Square.
The gym while small had sufficient eqipment for a good workout.

title: Good location but noisy corridor & aircon, bed not so comfy
body:
It is refreshing to see a new hotel embracing modern technology and design, that is priced competitively.
We stayed at the Yotel for 5 nights and found the location to be perfect for exploring the city, just a short walk to/from Penn station as well as Times Square. 
Although the free wifi and coffee/water in the galley are great to make the stay convenient, for me the primary service a hotel can provide is a good nights sleep, unfortunately this is where the Yotel falls down.
The noise from the corridor especially was a big problem, because of the size of the room you are practically sleeping next to the entrance door which is in no way noise insulated, you can even see light around the door from the corridor. The weekend party go-ers returning back at 2,3,4,5am don't whisper or tip toe into their rooms. 
This is a common problem of hotels but one hotel had the solution - provide an additional door between the entrance and bedroom, but given the design or the hotel this is unlike to happen.
The aircon system was also very noisy and was needed through the night, the vent pushing cold air directly onto the head of the bed.
We did not find the staff particularly smiley or ready to assist, even at the bar I was told happy hour had finished half way through the hour, nice! :-/ The coffee machine broke after a few days but was not repaired for the rest of our stay even after reporting it. The cleaners left a bottle of chemical detergent in the room - good job we didn't have kids! The next day the cleaner took our daily tip, folded the toilet paper, but didn't remove the detergent bottle or do any other cleaning.
The restaurant was charging premium prices for a "hurricane Sandy" buffet and weekend menus, we took our money elsewhere for the ambiance and quality of food.
If you were on business for one or two nights, I could see that this hotel would appeal, but as a couple on holiday it missed the mark.

title: Super Smashing Great!
body: Hi just got back from a 7 night stay in yotel and thought it was fantastic. The location is spot on which means you can walk everywhere. The rooms are brilliant and really modern. The staff were friendly. I am due back in NY in Feb and I will definately stay there.

title: Nice corner room
body:
Cool, easy, bright, clean, free wifi, friendly and helpful staff, but a bit uncomfortable futons.
Free checkroom for luggage after checking out and airport service for about 90$ available.
Great location in the heart of Manhattan.

title: Very cool concept and a well appointed room
body: Very cool concept and very comfortable stay in a very clean and well appointed room. The hotel is in a very good location near Midtown, the Ferry Docks and Times Square, Many good attributes: free Wi-fi, quick and good continental breakfast, nice casual and cool bar for a cocktail. The room was very clean with all of the amenities needed and then some, including a very cool towel warmer that really pays off in cooler months.

title: Food
body:
We thing that your food was to exspencive on the hotel, to many cakes in the morning.
when we order from the menucard the menu was soo small.
But we can say that is not the last time in your Yotel.
Best reguards 
Mads and Carina

title: Great hotel in Manhattan heart
body: I arrived two days after the passage of hurrican Sandy and I was very worried about that. But Yotel was working in every way. Very new and cool. Absolutely Hiper-technological! Beautiful room on 22nd floor, clean and well serviced, but the bed was very tough for my painful back and legs. Location is very good and this has permitted me to walk up and down the centre of Manhattan, despite the fact the underground was closed by flooding. I hope in future to come back in New York and surely I'll stay there again.

title: Won't stay there again
body:
Confusing check in process. Staff just watched me fumble my way through check in. Elevators often say going down, but really going up, and vice versa. Elevators slowwww. Rooms way too small for someone used to Marriott properties... Water pressure in my shower was terrible. Tapas style dinner - portions too small for the price. 
On the plus side... Breakfast food from menu and ala carte were both good. Very clean. Well maintained. Good location - close to Javits.
In summary, I'll find another hotel next time.

title: Fun and different
body:
Stayed at Yotel for one night and had a great time. Yes, rooms are small, but it's expected in NYC and they have the rooms laid out very efficiently. The galleys on each floor with coffee (and espresso - nice!), water, fridges, and microwaves is so convenient, especially since everything in NYC is so expensive. 
We didn't eat there, although the food looked fabulous. We did hang out in the bar for awhile that night and it turned into a semi-club. There was a DJ and a meet-up going on; it was really energetic and then suddenly it emptied out. Probably because the DJ was awful. But it was a lot of fun.
Very young crowd, a lot of business people. Had a European feel.
Location was fantastic. We walked there easily from Penn Station and then to Rockafeller Center in the morning. 
I would definitely stay there again, although only for short trips. The tight quarters could admittedly get old after awhile.

title: Great hotel
body: Excellent value for money. Rooms very small but very efficient; probably too small for two people with a lot of luggage. Friendly, helpful, efficient staff. Excellent free muffins and coffee in the am. Same for free coffee and amenities in each floor's "galley." Hotel is gimmicky but extremely well thought-out. Everything works exactly as intended. Excellent electronics set-up; free computer usage - very useful if you don't carry a laptop. No giftshop - I don't care; but no newspapers to buy. Some people still use print media and the CVS across the street doesn't sell papers; takes some searching to find an outlet. You need to be a bit of a neatnik to cope with the size, layout and amenities of the room. If you are, you will be delighted and intrigued. Very quiet rooms with wonderful views of New York if you have one of the "premium" rooms. Bed is very firm, but I slept okay. Only drawback is distance from subway. Yotel is in a gentrifying neighborhood and you have to walk through some pretty sketchy blocks to get to the subway, about one-half mile away.

title: Fab location but rude bar staff
body: Location was excellent, staff at check in were very helpful, even at 3.30 in the morning. Room was fantastic and good value for money, high standard of cleanliness and loved the free hot drinks in the galley - fantastic idea. The only negative thing about my stay was the bar staff, they were so rude, on our last day we had checked out of our room and sat in the green area, when we tried to order lunch we were told that we would have to sit in the bar, which we didn't want to do, the woman said that if we wanted to order food to eat in the comfy chairs then we would have to have a takeaway - ie our food bagged up - simply ridiculous considering we were paying guests. When I ordered the food, a rice dish I was told abruptly that there wasn't any rice so would need to order an alternative, when I asked what the alternative was I was told to look at the menu (considering most of their dishes are sushi which include rice I was left bewildered).

title: An hostel priced as an expensive hotel!
body: Yotel was maybe cool at the beginning but now its rooms are overpriced and not rational for the service given. During my stay (7 nights) I had to experience wrong (too small) and dirty sheets (with nasty spots), missing towels, sometimes missing sheets (on the bulk bed), poor service... The staff was not really helpful, they just told me "sorry, we'll ask to change the sheets...). For the rates I faced I thought at least to have a better and more professional solution. It's really not a good investment to spend 300 bucks / per night for such a small, cheap room. The location is good if you need to spend time at the Javits Exhibition center or around Times Square area... but you can really find better hotels in the area!!!

title: The Mold Room
body: Unfortunately I don't have a good review about the Yotel. I was hoping for a better experience but I didn't get what I was looking for. I like the entire kiosk check in process. Its very simple and keeps things moving so you don't have to wait in line to check in. It's a little of a pain having to go from 1 elevator to the next to get from the ground floor up to the floors with the rooms but even that is okay. The rooms are small but this is expected in NYC. The problem I had was that the room had a very strong smell of mold in the cabin and bathroom. After check-in, we were only in the room for maybe 15 minutes so on our way out, we stopped at Mission Control to let them know. Unfortunately nothing was done about the smell. It would have been great if our room was moved or at least house keeping went in and did something. But when we got back, it was the same over powering smell. There were 2 adults and 2 children in our group and the smell bothered everyone.

title: Yotel is one hellavu hotel
body: Service and staff were excellent. Close to Jacob Javits - 8 min walk. 10 min walk to Times Sq. Cabins provide all space you need - good funcationality. Perfect for the biz traveler. Muffin and Coffee comp bfast was excellent - and if you need a nighttime hot bev - each floor has LaVazza Machines for your coffee, espresso, latte, cappucino, and even hot chocolate! WiFi worked great.

title: Chic Design, Great Location
body:
My wife and I live in Staten Island but we had a big night planned out and decided to get a room in the city for the night. I had eaten at FOUR inside Yotel before so I already liked the chic design. The location on 42nd and 10th is great for anyone visiting NYC. Your in close proximity to Times Square and the Theatre District, but just far enough away so you don't have to deal with the throngs of other tourists day and night in that part of town.
One thing to note; the standard "premium cabin" rooms are VERY small. Something like 150 square fee. Some may find this suffocating. We upgraded to the "executive view" cabin which was a good deal bigger, and had floor to ceiling windows with great views of the harbor. 
The hotel does not employ very many staff (compared to other hotels). They encourage check-in and out to be done via kiosk on the 1st floor, use a "robot" to store luggage in lieu of bellhops, and only have 1 person at reception. I suppose its a good way to keep costs down and we didn't notice any real drop off in service because of it. They don't offer a lot of the amenities you'd see at a higher end hotel, but we didn't need any of that.

title: Superior Customer Service at the Yotel
body: I enjoyed a two night stay at the Yotel. The hotel was very "hip and happening" but even an old guy like me was made to feel comfortable. The thrust of this review is to point out the great customer service I received from Gina Mignon, head of guest relations. I experienced a small problem and it was resolved by Gina expertly and efficiently. I'll be looking forward to my next visit to the Yotel!

title: Excellent Stay!
body: great hotel, great location. our room was small, as most reviews mention but it was clean and modern. it had more than enough for the two of us. compared to the other hotels of this price in the area, you really can't beat the location and added amenities. use the concierge! he was awesome.

title: Friendly Hurricane Sandy shelter
body:
We were supposed to depart the day Sandy hit NYC, and had to extend our stay a couple extra days due to flight cancellations. The staff were friendly, helping us bring our luggage to our rooms. Checkin was efficient through the machine. The double set of elevators is a little annoying, but we never had to wait long.
The rooms were sufficient and fairly well designed, for the price it was worth a stay. Location is pretty easy to get a taxi at, but a 10-15 min walk to the nearest subway station.

title: It fit the need
body:
We stayed here for three nights and had a mostly enjoyable experience. The rooms are NYC small but ours was clean and the location was convenient to what we wanted to do. The coffee/espresso/cappuccino machine was great and saved us several bucks a day. We arrived before Noon and the check in Kiosk did not work for us. We had to go up to Mission Control and they checked us in pretty quickly and told us that our room was available. During our stay we did not have any issues other than checking out. Standard check out is 11:00am, we asked about a late checkout and were offered an additional hour for free or told that for an additional $50.00 plus tax we could stay until 3:00pm. We decided to go ahead and check out but found that only 2 of the 5 elevators were working. After waiting about 15-20 minutes for an available elevator we finally decided to haul our luggage down the stairs. We checked out at Mission Control on the fourth floor and we told that we could store our baggage with the Yobot on the first floor. Unfortunately Yobot was broken. After waiting another 15-20 minutes or so a staff member came out and started checking bags and giving out claim checks. The check out that should have taken 5 minutes ended up taking about an hour.
The hotel is a short walk to Times Square and a short walk to the Subway. There are the obvious Times Square locations to go to but there are also a lot of bars and restaurants north of 42nd and 10th Ave that are easy to get to. The area north of the hotel felt more secure while walking late at night versus walking south of the hotel. Unfortunately I did not know that the Space Shuttle is only a few blocks west of the hotel but I do know that for my next visit.
All in all I was satisfied with our stay but with so many places to stay in NYC I would try something else the next time.

title: Funky concept works, most of the time.
body:
The thought that ran through my head throughout our stay at the NYC Yotel was that this is the kind of room I could expect if Apple, Ikea and WestJet collaborated and built a hotel. 
Wasn't sure what we were getting into. You read the reviews, do your research, make the reservation and kinda cross your fingers. Well, it worked out for us with Yotel. Found an online deal which made our 3 night stay in NYC a week before the US Thanksgiving affordable. 
We booked the basic room, but with a view which cost a little extra but was worth it. Being on the 24th floor we had a south view all the way down to the WTC site and on the left the Empire State bldg and the New Yorker. 
The room (Queen cabin) was tiny iPodish and Ikeaesque functional with the WestJetlike theme and friendliness. The bed was kinda like a sofa but at night you could flatten it out to sleep with a touch of a button. Works better than a Murphy bed. The shower (no tub) was a walk in with a wonderful overhead stream of water that was really nice. 
When we arrived, we checked in via a bank of computers on the main floor. With our key fobs in hand, we then took an elevator to the 4th floor which housed the concierge, more computers (for guest access), a restaurant area and other stuff we didn't explore. We then took another elevator to our room near the top. For most of the visit we didn't have an issue with the elevators with the exception of late Sunday afternoon. It seemed only one of the five elevators were working from the 4th floor to guest rooms creating a real back up and wait.
Each floor has a galley with a vending machine for bottled pop and juice ($2), a filtered water/ice/ice-water dispenser, and a complimentary coffee machine with reg and decaf pods to make espresso, latte, caps, mochas, americanos and hot water. No coffee machine in room, but no matter. The galley machine was great, except when it broke down. We did call and let them know and it was looked at real quick.
When we first walked into the room we were not disappointed with its size but with the cleanliness of it. The floor in the bathroom area was not properly sweeped, there were visible splatters (of coffee/drink) in several places and dark smudges around the bathroom light switch - yewww! The room was missing a controller for the t.v. but one was brought soon after we asked.
We didn't hear the city noises in the room and our sleeps were peaceful. The complementary coffee and muffins in the morning were a treat. The muffins were fresh, tasty and there was a good choice. 
We would stay again at this Yotel. The location was great, both close enough and far enough away from Times Square and only two easy blocks to the subway.

title: Good not Great location; but the price was great
body: For the price you pay perfection cannot be expected. Complaints are minor. Yobot not working, but staff member there to provide claim ticket and store luggage. Elevators slow in the morning, but considering we were on the 24th floor that is to be expected. Coffee and Muffins are complimentary in the morning. If you wanted a glass of OJ it was $4. Otherwise, the stay was enjoyable. Rooms are small, but clean and well designed. Staff was very friendly and helpful. On our way to the hotel we walked a bit on 41st to get away from the crowds on 42nd. It felt a little rundown so we ventured back to 42nd. Walking back to the hotel at night we felt safe but stayed on 42nd or north.

title: Cool Hotel not far from Times Square
body:
Fun hotel not far from times square. Kiosk to check in (but they will help). Small rooms with a fun layout but clear doors with a curtain so if privacy is an issue - BEWARE!!
Nice lounge with indoor and outdoor seating. Our phone did not work but that was not a big deal.

title: Loved it
body:
Location is great if you're visiting NYC, walking distance to Times Square.
Easy check-in, stuff is friendly and helpful, rooms are tiny, but very cozy and have a nice vibe to it. 
Definitely recommend for younger crowd, people who don't mind trade extra space for extra (modern) style. Fun place to stay, there's pretty busy club on reception level.
Restaurants are bit expensive for what it is, but food is good.
Overall: loved it!

title: Fun ,Friendly and Functional Accommodation.
body:
We have just returned from a five night stay to celebrate my 50th. I can only think of one negative comment and that is you have to sometimes wait ages for the lift, especially on days when lots of people are checking out. This hotel is great value, very clean, lovely staff and a good location.The rooms have been so well thought out and use all available space with the bed going from half size to full size by touch of a button. Others have made comments about the privacy aspect, I do not feel this is a problem at all. There are two blinds at the window, one blackout the other more like a thick net curtain but in the form of a roller blind, the shower is surrounded by glass which has small circles in cream all over it and the toilet is next to the shower so you can close the sliding door if you want privacy. If you require more there is a curtain that you can pull across on the bedroom side from one side of the room to the other. Must just mention the lovely shower /hair wash in the room two types and both smell gorgeous. Fresh clean white towels, flannels and bed linen. Hair drier, iron, desk T.V and free Wi-fi. The little kitchen with free hot drinks and cold water machine is a lovely touch There is also a cold drinks machine where you can purchase coke etc and a microwave if you should need it. Breakfast is very laid back with a great selection of muffins ,tea or coffee that's free other items are available if you wish to pay for them. We sat looking out over the patio area in the soft seats with the bird song that plays in the background each morning, very pleasant way to start the day.Just beware of the small round tables as they are not very stable!!Or you can use the tray in your room and collect what you want and eat in bed! We did not partake in any other meals or entertainment in Yotel so cannot comment on any of that.
 I would not hesitate in recommending this hotel to anyone. Well done to you all at Yotel and thank you for a lovely stay.

title: As fun as it looks!
body:
My husband and I stayed here for a convention at the Javitts Center in October. The location of this hotel is perfect; the convention center, times square, and the ship terminal (where the Intrepid and it's newest addition, the Enterprise space shuttle) are a short walk away. Also, like most of Manhattan, there are many options for eating and shopping.
The hotel is as cool as it looks. The check in process is quick with a self service kiosk in the main lobby. The elevators bring you to the fourth floor, where mission control, bar and restaurant are located, along with the elevators that bring you to the room floors.
We stayed in a standard cabin with the queen size futon that folded up to give more room when not sleeping. The beds were comfortable, and although the mattress is thin enough to fold into a futon, it was thick enough to be very comfortable to sleep on. The room is small but is set up well. The biggest concern I had was the privacy issue with the bathroom due to the lack of a true separate bathroom area, but it was not an issue. There is a curtain that pulls across and a sliding glass door that can be closed. May be a little awkward if you are not close to your travel companion, but there is a degree of privacy.
The room had a few maintenance issues that could be addressed with a little paint and repair work, but not a big deal. The only other issue was the noise that could be heard from the hallway, but it is to be expected in most hotels. Perhaps a little more insulation around the door would help with the noise, but once again, not a deal breaker.
The free coffee, filtered water and fridge on each floor are a nice touch-make sure you bring your room key to access the galley- and the free muffins in the morning are very yummy. The robot on the first floor will store your luggage for free on day of check out if you want to visit the city some more, and although it seems like a gimmick, it is actually very efficient for both luggage check in and check out.

title: Cool Concepts
body: We weren't sure about this place since it was cheap by comparison for prime NY city, but it was great! Really beautiful and very space efficient. Self Check-in was easy. Doors use an RFID card so no swipe cards that get de-magnetized. The room looks really small at first, but then I was constantly surprised at how much was included in the room. Excellent interactions with the staff. Great 'galley' (tea/coffee/hot chocolate/ice/microwave/refrigerator/vending room) on each floor. Comfortable bed and I loved the shower products.

title: Fun, trendy, hip, value!
body:
Great a fun hotel. Just enough space (although I was traveling alone).
Was a bit chilly at night - very light comforter. But I never did ask for more blankets.
On the YOUNG side for sure, very international and quiet up on the floors.

title: Yotel New York City - cool vibe, neat place, great food
body:
Cool hotel well situated in NYC, rooms have a retro yet modern feel to them, international clientele, well sound insulated, reasonable (for NYC) price, excellent food and really pleasant wait staff.
Only hitch was long wait for elevators, since 4 out of 5 were all broken at one point. Was fixed within the day, and then all was OK.

title: What a great place for a short stay..
body: We stayed at Yotel 11/21 - 11/22/2012. When we checked in the staff were delightful. JJ came and helped us check in on the do it yourself terminals. The manager came over to put both of our rooms next to each other on the 21st floor. No problems! The rooms are small but perfect for a quick trip and they are CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN. I loved the bathroom set-up but many reviewers her do not. I loved the electric bed, just hit the button if you want to watch television and you will be in the sitting position. I do agree with the bed not being so comfortable but it didn't keep me awake. The proximity to Times Square is perfect, just a quick walk. I would stay at YOTEL again in a minute!

title: Awesome hotel!
body:
Stayed at this hotel for two nights (14th and 15th of November 2012) as part of my first solo trip and my first trip to New York. I loved the modern interior design and the courteous and friendly staff. The room I got was great! Everything was clean, as excepted. Some people note the small size of the cabins (Which is what Yotel refers to their rooms as). But for a single person, there is more than enough space.
Location was great (Within walking distance of Times Square) and free wi-fi to boot.
I did have a couple of meals there at the Dohyo restaurant on the fourth floor (Breakfast and dinner). Definitely tasty but not my favourite meals, so I did find the prices a tiny bit high relative to the food I got. But in the end, it's personal preference so I highly recommend the restaurant regardless: Great atmosphere and friendly staff!
I would definitely book again with Yotel in a heartbeat!

title: Wont be back!!
body: When we 1st arrived outside we thought the Yotel looked very modern, new and fresh, That didnt last very long, after trying to get attention of someone to help us check in on the lobby we finally got some help and headed to our room, we where expecting small but this was just a disgrace we had no where to put both suitcases we basically had to live out our cases as we had no where to put our clothes, that aside we headed out to explore. Coming in from a long flight and a few hours in the city we where ready to head to bed, but what a unpleasant surprise when we pressed the button to lay our bed down, it was so thin and also felt as if we had a plastic bag underneath that wasnt very comfortable to sleep on, while pulling back the sheets we noticed a few dirty stains but decided we comment on them in the morning as we where so exhausted. After a few hours we both woken up basically crippled it was like laying on a bag of nails each night - we did ask for a extra mattress or a topper to put on top but we where told from mission control on FOUR that this wasnt possible, when we asked if there anything else we could do, we where told to like it or leave basically. This put a very sour taste in our mouths before we even had our 2nd night! We changed the room door sign to "please clean my cabin" and headed out, CLEAN? that has to be a joke, there was still somebodys hair in our shower not been cleaned properly before we even set foot in, the sink had what looked like splashes of blood in it and the toilet pan was dirty!!!! All this aside we decided to be brave and keep staying here - what a big mistake!! We left our christmas shopping bags by the side of the bed, only place we could leave them as there was no space.. we came back to them being basically scattered across the floor what was making us think was somebody in our bags? The lift was very annoying needing two sometimes they wouldn't move and nobody would explain why, this was we later found out from a french guest that sometimes you have to keep your key on as a fob style to make it move, well thanks to yotel for not telling us this.. On our last night we asked what would we the recommended way to traveling back to Newark airport to catch our flight back to scotland, we where ignored for about ten minutes then to be told 'He didnt know' We wont be back to this hotel again, for the money you pay for this place you are way cheaper having another hotel, with cleaner services, softer beds and house keeping who arent having a peek around your bags and god knows what else. Shame really as we could have made this city break amazing and instead it ruined our full stay in NYC!

title: Highly recommended for young crowd
body:
I stayed at Yotel for 4 nights with a friend during our visit to NYC. Reasons why I LOVED Yotel:
1 - Very CLEAN and modern (rooms are spotless, hotel is sparkling clean, computerized check-in, Yobot stores luggage, etc.)
2 - ROOMS are great (really neat, free wifi, comfy beds, flat screen tv, oragnic toiletries, lots of storage space and in-room safe)
3 - STAFF is amazing! (friendly and helpful when selecting rooms and setting up wifi, spent lots of time giving directions and advice, friendly and cheerful during breakfast, quick service when we asked for extra hangers, greeted us each time when we came and went)
4 - LOCATION is great (right on 42nd, with bus stop in front and subway 2 blocks away)
5 - FREE breakfast, tea, coffee, water (and a clean, safe shared kitchen/"galley" on each floor)
6 - CROWD is young, hip, European travellers - no annoying families or older people (really popular club on Four)
All in all, we were very comfortable and felt welcomed and really happy to be at Yotel. I wouldn't stay anywhere else in NYC!

title: Cool Yotel!
body:
It's hard to find good accommodation in a great location in NYC that doesn't break the bank. We stayed at the Yotel in a corner room late August/September and were very pleased with the Yotel experience. Good value for money. You do your own check in, but there's staff there to help if you need it, and up to your cabin you go. It was spacious (corner room,) the view was fabulous!! I awoke to the sunrise each morning to photograph the sun hitting the skyscrapers. The sunset just in front of the room was equally fabulous. 
As we are big on shopping we don't spend too much time in our hotel room in NYC, but need a comfortable place to crash and a clean bathroom to start our mornings. I was not happy with the bed which was way too hard. I can't believe they purchased those beds for Yotel, a big flaw, having beds that are not comfortable. The bathroom was nice but a little tired perhaps, so a little spruce up in the bathrooms, changing the carpets and new more comfortable beds, we'd easily make Yotel our favourite hotel in NYC. 
We ate at their rooftop terrace one night. The food was good, small portions (more like tapas,) and the service prompt. There's several other good eating out options in the area, just a few blocks away in Hell's kitchen. I also loved the close proximity to Times square without it being on the actual crazy part of Times square. 
We're going back to NYC in March next year and have already made a booking at Yotel. On my wish list I have a more comfortable bed, apart from that there wasn't really much to criticize about the Yotel. P.S Looooved Yobot, safely handling our luggage!! Could watch it for quite a while.

title: cool hotel
body:
not an ordinary one, sophisticated, high tech, perfect location
staffs are super friendly, check in was done within minutes
the galley in our floor was sadly under repair, but no big deal since we can use the ones in other floors.. 
however, room is a bit small for those traveling with 2 big luggages but fortunately very clean

title: Fantastic Experience
body: We visited Yotel to watch the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. Found the staff friendly and helpful, and the room, while small, was very ingenious in the use of space. I would definitely recommend and will be going back!

title: Love this hotel!
body: I love this hotel! Great location, Rooms were great, bigger then expected and had everything you needed in them. The whole hotel was very clean. Gallery on each floor stocked with tea, coffee, hot choc and water was fantastic plus there was a great selection of breakfast muffins. Also found theie was plenty of staff to help when the technology wasn't behaving!

title: Very modern, clean,but small
body:
it's a nice hotel in a good location to stay for a weekend city trip. very modern rooms, it's nice to have complimentary coffee and water on each floor. The rooms was tiny. but clean.
Otherwise I would say, it is too expensive for the size of room and little service they offer. no personal check in, self checkin like in the airport.

title: It really is a cabin
body: We booked the Yotel due to price. The booking process was for a group was very difficult. It was clear that they don't handle groups or were too new. It was so hard to get the right person on the phone. When I finally did a few days later they did a great job. The room is a shock. It's tiny about 800 sq feet. It is fine for one person, for sleeping only. I would not be able to share this room with anyone else. It's just too small. It was a good value but I'm not sure I would stay again...

title: Interesting first experience.
body: I really like the concept of this hotel - attractive design. I was traveling by myself and location was very good. The hotel was very clean and pleasing inside. Continental breakfast was small but tasty. The hotel only provides shampoo and body wash - which is fine but if you need anything else take it along with you. I did not find the cabins to be small - they were rather comfortable. . I thought the staff was not particularly helpful and the yobot line got long because one of the guests had problems but nothing that can't be fixed. Was it a good value? Not sure.

title: Brilliant location, Great value and Great Staff
body:
My partner and I stayed at Yotel between 15th - 19th November, it truely is a brilliant new style hotel.
Located on 10th Avenue 42nd Street it is a 15 minute walk from such places as Rockafella Centre, Empire State Building and Madison Square Garden. It's also a short stroll to the nearest subway which is located on 8th and 42nd, the bus port is also between 8th and 9th.
Positives
The Location - As above
Check-in - quick tap on the computer located in the lobby and room card were dispensed.
Staff - always helpful and welcoming, smiles on faces.
Wifi - Wifi is all over the hotel and in rooms also free of charge which isn't always the case
Free map - the map in the room was invaluable and used on a daily basis locations of landmarks and subways even more helpful.
Rooms - Very clean and tidy and cleaned everyday, yes the rooms aren't huge but they are brilliant designed and layed out so we never felt cramped. I've seen a few reviews about the beds being uncomfortable. Yes they are hard but I had a great nights sleep every night as did my partner.
Floor Kitchen - Each floor had a kitchen with fridge to store food/drink, also coffee and tea making facilites which are free of charge
Negatives
Drink prices - The drink prices are pretty ridiculous $10 for a beer which was about 2/3rds of a pint and $10 for a small glass of wine is pretty outrageous. I appreciate that the bars do turn into a night spot, but after a long day you want to come back to the hotel for a drink. Something we did once and never again. Maybe a compromise where guests get a discount on drinks and people who come for the club pay the normal prices?
All in all though a great stay and I really can only think of the drink prices as the only negative, I would definitely reccomend and will be using the hotel again.
Thanks for the hospitality
Neil Stretton

title: Great Hotel!
body: Yotel in NYC is a great option for travelers in New York, Manhattan. It has a good return over the investment, excellent and friendly crew services. Overall, Yotel offers clients with a creative solutions and amenities. I strongly recommend it.

title: Yotel Yotel Yotel it's not just an ordinary hotel
body:
We enjoyed an excellent 3 night stay at The Yotel in mid November. From start to finish we found the hotel to be just what we needed for our busy 4 days exploring New York.
We flew into Newark Airport and took the air train and NJT into Penn Station in Manhattan. The walk from the train station to Yotel was fairly simple and a nice introduction to the streets of New York - up 8th Avenue and along 42nd Street. If you have lots of baggage to carry then a taxi will take you there too very quickly. 
On arrival we were greeted by one of the concierge team who assisted us with the electronic check in. He also advised us on the hotel facilities and dining options. Our room was on the 10th floor and we found it to be compact but versatile - Yotel have thought of pretty much everything you need for a comfortable stay. Large TV, Iron, Iron board, alarm, air con, ipod / pad connector, toiletries, secure safe, and even a little pocket map of New York. 
The bed folds away into a couch at the touch of button - we found the bed to be comfortable and slept well on all nights of our stay. The bar / restaurant downstairs can be quite lively in the evenings but we couldn't hear a thing in our room. We found rooms to be a bit too warm for our liking - it was November and cold outside and the room service kept putting heat on at 74 degrees ..... however a quick blast and we had the room at our more favoured 70 degrees F. 
Coffee and muffins are provided as breakfast and we really enjoyed this a start to our busy days. We didn't eat in the hotel at any other time so we can't comment on food in the restaurant. The bar was busy and probably a bit too noisy for our liking (we must be getting old) - but we were able to get a drink and find a quieter seat away from the music. Service in the bar was like the rest of the hotel .... excellent. 
As for New York we had a fantastic time - visiting all the great sites. Our favourites were Brooklyn Bridge (Walk), Central Park (Skate), Empire State Building (Sunset), 911 Memorial (time for refection). The city has it all and we will have to return again so we can see the many parts we didn't have time to visit on this trip.
Our check out was the same as check in and the same gentleman helped us with the process. As we had an evening flight - our baggage was securely stored for collection later in the afternoon.
The hotel is located a couple of blocks from Times Square, so it enjoys a nice central location but in a quiet location thus enabling a peaceful nights sleep.
Overall a great stay in a well run hotel - we will happily stay in the Yotel again when we return to The Big Apple.

title: great location
body: This hotel is in a great location, 10 mins walk from times square. this meant that we could go out for the day, go back to the hotel for a break , and back out again in the evening. very clean, small room, but perfectly adequate for crashing out at night. area was fine to walk at night. only down side was that the breakfast that we tried on the first day, was VERY expensive.

title: Best stay possible
body: This was one of the nicest hotels I have stayed at in the New York area. The cabins are kinda small, but bigger than other hotels I had stayed in before. The atmosphere is real cozy and a lot of space to relax in the label or have meetings. A little pricey, but its walking distance from the festivities.

title: Cool and clean!
body:
Cool and clean sum up YOTEL.
The cabin we had wasn't huge (there were 4 of us) but for a 3 night stay it was fine. The design values are excellent and there is a real vibe to the place. We had great night at the bar and ate in the restaurant - the Japanese decor is a nice touch and there is a pool table tucked away behind the main dining area.
The staff are friendly and the place attracts a youngish crowd, location is good (10 mins from Times Square). All in all my first time in NY, so nothing to judge it against, but would stay there again, great hotel.

title: How bad internet ruined the experience
body: First of all I want to say that I enjoyed the room. It's small but very functional and the reclinable bed is great. There are some drawbacks in that you don't have a sofa or a minibar, but it's no big deal. All that being said, the wireless (there is no wired) internet is terrible. When you call the desk, they tell you that due to occupancy the internet is unreliable and that there's nothing you can do other than come downstairs and use the public computers which log you out after 30 minutes and where you have to work standing. I spent my time in cafes in the area as a result. Not cool

title: Decent location, clean, modern, no frills experience
body: Rooms are small but clean and modern. No privacy as the bathroom only has a curtain from the bedroom. Decent location. Would stay again. Cool bed! No room service and the galley is pretty limited. New York is competitive within the hotel space...could probably get more for your money elsewhere.

title: Great for a short trip!
body:
Great location just a short walk from times square and very modern and clean.
Would come back again any time. Perfect hotel for a five night stay in New York. 
Cabins were well laid out and thought through. Plenty of places to eat and drink nearby.

title: Great hotel
body:
This hotel is very modern and the rooms are reasonably compact. They were actually a little more spacious than I'd expected (I'd recently stayed at the Yotel Gatwick - THAT'S small!). The room was very clean and the space was used in a very efficient way. The bed was really comfortable - I'd seen other reviews saying it wasn't that great, but I rather like a firm bed. It was great to be able to convert it gradually from a sofa to a bed. The bed linen was very soft and the pillows super comfortable. The bathroom was wonderful - really great shower with plenty of hot water, decent-sized towels and a good sink/vanity area. The TV was great (HD with HBO etc - I was there during a huge storm and needed this!). I had a standard room on the 16th floor and had an amazing view of the city and new WTC. The hotel as a whole felt very safe. The location was fine, though perhaps not quite as close to Times Square as the description makes you think. The staff were able to store my enormous bag when I checked out and got me a cab when I left.
There were two negative things about my stay:
1. The internet connection, which they describe as 'super strong'. Strong it may be (in that I never got cut off from the router), but UNBELIEVABLY slow. To the extent that I couldn't even send iMessages. Skyping or going on Facetime was out, as was browsing the internet. Seriously, how can a hotel as great as this mess up something as basic as fast internet?
2. The staff in the breakfast area. On the first morning I asked the staff what flavour the muffins were (none were labelled). They didn't have a clue. The next morning, after waiting by the elevators for 20 minutes for one to show up and eventually walking down 12 flights of stairs, I asked a member of staff if I could charge a hot breakfast to my room. She said I couldn't, and I'd have to pay. Explaining that my purse was in my room, that I was a guest and I didn't want to spend another 40 minutes commuting to my room, I asked if we could find a way around this. She did not want to play ball, and was really rude about it. 
Overall, it was a good and comfortable stay. Just don't forget your purse if you want to have a decent breakfast, and be prepared to go elsewhere to get online.

title: So so.
body:
The staff at the hotel was wonderful. The rooms are high-tech. The beds are hard but have nice linen. Not a great location because it's a 20 minute walk to the closest subway station. 
One thing that I'd never experienced before is a lobby with such a strong scent. It was the Abercrombie of hotels. Enjoyable perk: Free coffee, mocha, and hot chocolate machines on every floor.

title: Aspires to be modern, but 3rd World
body:
This hotel aspires to be ultra-modern, but they fail at the basics.
No hot water. Really? Give me a break.
Very slow wi-fi speed, reminds me of dial-up.
Cold rooms, won't let you go beyond 72F. 
Rock hard mattresses.

title: Excellent Cool Place
body: Small rooms but fun and clean. Premium cabin suitable for solo or couple only. Two kinds of all over body soap provided in walk-in glass shower. Won't be a lot of privacy for bathroom area if 2 but there is a glass door for toilet and a sheer curtain for entire bathrooom area. Can be great views from some rooms! Second stay and will stay again. Prices vary greatly depending on date if stay.

title: Great hotel and great value
body: Yotel is not your typical hotel and it actually adds to your experience. Everything you need is provided efficiently and you don't get overcharged as a result. It is not a hotel for those that are seeking the large suites but if you are seeking a clean, well maintained and modern place to sleep and shower, then it is absolutely perfect -- and everyone that works there was extremely friendly and went out if their way to be helpful. Highly recommend.

title: Fun Hotel
body: I absolutely LOVED staying at the Yotel. The ambiance is very retro-ish...not your typical, traditional hotel...but definitely a fun place to stay. I'm a big aroma person, and the Yotel always smelled very refreshing. It's really close to Times Square, and only 2 blocks away from the subway station.The staff were super welcoming and helpful, especially NJ. On our last night, a member in our party had a personal crisis and NJ went above and beyond to help her resolve the issue. While the rooms are not very spacious, they are cozy. I would definitely stay at the Yotel on my next trip to New York, which I hope will be very soon :)

title: Nice hotel
body:
Nice location, close enough to Times Square, without the permanent buzz. We had a west view over the Hudson river and Jersey, nice. I slept like a log the whole week (thank you jet-lag + walking 10mi everyday), so obviously the mattress was good for me. When sharing a room with a friend, a spare blanket would have been nice.
The AC panel is not super user-friendly, it was not simple to turn the fan off (was blowing air in the face when in the bed).
Otherwise the rooms are very functional. WiFi was a bit binary, speedy at times, laggy 5 minutes later.
Light and noise from the hallway came into the room a little easy, better insulation please.
On our last day the restaurant staff was confused, I couldn't manage to get what I ordered despite repeating twice and sending my plate back. One lady really looked like she wanted anything but be there and help us. They were ok the other days.
The breakfast menu is a bit short, I quickly settled on what I'd get 6 days straight. Muffins and coffee are free otherwise. We didn't try lunch, but dinner was good.
Upon check out, the Yobot (robotic arm storing your luggage in lockers) in the lobby is a nice touch, to look at and to have a final stroll/visit before heading back home.

title: Highly recommended.
body: My partner & I recently stayed at the Yotel for 4 nights. We were extremely excited as we pulled up outside as it looked like a great location/hotel. Check-in kiosk were extremely easy to use & quick. Staff were on hand to greet us & offered assistance. We were directed to our Premium View Cabin Room which was fantastic, we had a great view of New York & a glimpse of the Hudson River. The Yotel is modern, clean, fresh, well presented. Staff are friendly & always on hand for help & assistance. Our room was fantastic, its a good size & is practical. It is close to Times Square, 5-10 minute walk. Food is fantastic and good for value. Atmosphere is great & free tea, coffee, water & muffins available in the morning. Checking out is just as easy & quick as checking in. This Yotel hotel is highly recommended & we would stay there again if we returned to New York.

title: perfect stay
body:
i book hundreds of rooms yearly for my company all over the world. i also book hotels for myself locally in manhattan for both business and pleasure.
i work in the entertainment industry and sometimes get caught up in a crucial project that makes my 45 minute commute back and forth to bay ridge untenable. 
during these times i tend to book rooms within walking distance to my office. during these trips i basically book a tiny room to sleep in. im going to sleep and shower and then go right back to work with as little hassle as possible. it means i will come and go at odd hours, probably blast through typical check in/check out times.
and when i am finished with one of these projects (or when i get a fat bonus because of them) i usually stay locally to celebrate.(and finally unwind) during these stays i tend to choose more grand accommodations, 
Most hotels i deal with are either one of the other. The Yotel can accommodates both. 
First off, a hotel i stay in has to have patient staff. i can be snappish and i have a low threshold for hassle. 
with the yotel, its all about the staff. never mind that the building itself is a work of art. the rooms, (and the tiny ones are really tiny) are also sculpture. tiny or not, there are few hotels in manhattan which give you the kind views scene out of just about any window of the hotel from any shower.
the lighting and mood of the room could be altered by a few brilliant lighting choices from sleepy to romantic to excited to get ready for a night out.
the larger rooms (and there are plenty of those) are OFF THE CHARTS beautiful. entire walls of views. press a button and the walls go from white to skyline. a corner room at the yotel is about the most beautiful experience i have had in a hotel and i have had a few.
there are a few hotels i love in manhattan, and the yotel is in the top three. i like this place so much i considered renting an insane apartment in the attached MiMa building.
i write this review because i think good work should be rewarded. Inoch from the front desk and Yusef from downstairs are perfect examples of everything that is right about this hotel.
this is one of the few hotels in manhattan where the staff will really really help you without breaking the rules of the place (im not comfortable when employees go against rules for tips or whatever) the thing is they are helpful because the hotel is setup in such a wy to BE helpful.
i mentioned inoch and yusef because they conveyed the hotel's business in a way that improved upon an already great situation.
book a room there while you can. once the world discovers this place it will be a million dollars a night.
oh, and for a tiny bit of balance, i hear they are changing the mattresses and while they arent AWFUL they arent perfect either. but im already booking a few rooms for next week.

title: Love it, love it, love it!!
body:
Located right near Times Square and so accessible to everything else that you might want to do while in the heart of New York. What a great hotel! For great value, great location and comfort I would go there every time - in fact I do!! I know some people think it's a bit expensive, but that's New York - you won't find other hotels right in the centre that offer such good service for this price.
The rooms aren't spacious/luxurious, so if you want the lux treatment you might want to go elsewhere. But let's face it, when you're visiting New York, you won't be in your hotel very much! The beds are very comfortable and, though the rooms are small, you won't hear the noise from your neighbours. Block-out curtains also means that the never-ending lights of the city will not disturb your sleep.
Travelling with a young child isn't always easy and hotels aren't always so cheery to see them, but the Yotel was different. My son loved staying there - he felt so welcomed. The staff were so good to him and the hotel room was comfortable enough for me to share with a child. The staff gave me some wonderful ideas for places to go and things to see with a small child too.
The food in the restaurant is really yummy and quite different to the standard hotel restaurant menu (and the portions aren't supersized, which is great). The free coffee/tea and breakfast muffins are a great idea for people who just want to get up and go, but the option of a proper sit-down breakfast is good too. The only drawbacks in the restaurant are: a) it's a little pricey; and b) there aren't any children's options.
And there's a galley on each floor - what a great idea!!! Tea, coffee, hot chocolate etc. Super convenient.
But watch out for the staff - they are possibly the most helpful, courteous and downright friendly people you will meet while in New York!! They make this good hotel a truly great one and your stay will be unforgetable.

title: Swanky place with a great location
body: The first thing that hits when you get to this place is the swanky, futuristic decor which such a nice break from the staid, monotonous look of other hotels. And it only gets better from there. The automated checkins and super friendly staff are a joy. The rooms are convenient and you get what you pay for. They have optimized on space, with their sliding beds and closet space but all of it has a nice charm of its own. Share the room with someone whom you are comfortable with and it can be quite a cosy experience. The lounge areas are inviting with being in your face. All in all, would love to go there again.

title: Great but bring your own TP.
body: Check-in process was easy but we were confused by the crew member about our room number and what floor it was actually located on. Upon entering our room it smelled like smoke. Mission control instantly assigned us another room (on a higher floor) and asked housekeeping to investigate and ionize the previous room. The rest of our stay was quite pleasant. Location was excellent. We managed to return to our hotel room a few times during the day easily. I do have one tip for everyone bring your own toilet paper!

title: Great hotel
body: Good hotel, decent price for a great location near Times Square (10-15 min walk to the nearest subway, 15-20 min walk to Times Square and most Broadway theaters). Yotel is pretty unpretentious, relaxed and with a cool 'design hotel' vibe. Really friendly not over-pressuring staff. Serviceable free breakfast - coffee and muffins. No problems with the room or the bed. Hit and miss Wi-Fi.

title: Proximity to times square and techy feel makes it a bit of a winner
body:
Booked a 3 person room for a night. Thought it was decent considering its proximity to Times Square. List of pros and cons below. 
Pros 
Close, as in walking distance to time square and most of the action in Manhattan
Really good transport links around 
Loads of restaurants nearby 
Efficient check in/check out system, all of which is electronic - no need to join long lines 
Clean rooms 
Cons 
Rooms a little small 
No full breakfast option although the muffins and coffee provided was sufficient.
Pricey. That being said, there are few things as good nearby for this price
Overall i would say that it is worth it if you are travelling with a group i.e. someone to split room costs with and don't mind small spaces.

title: Great hotel in the middle of everything!
body: This was a weekend trip with my daughters, aged 18 and 23, and I'm glad I chose Yotel. It's funky and fun and we really enjoyed our stay. It's close to so many great restaurants, Times Square, shopping, etc. The room was a bit small (we had the queen bed with 1 bunk), but you could make more room by sliding the bed up into a futon. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and the galley was awesome! The only complaint I have is that the bed just wasn't comfortable. The bunk was better, but the bed is really just a futon mattress. Other than that, I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: Simply cool
body: Just how do they do it? Brilliant, uber-cool spaces, all the amenities you might need in a hotel, great little restaurant and of course the funky Yobot that stows your luggage into cubby holes. This is the address to me the next time I visit NYC. Only bug bear is the crowd of people who come to the bar and spill over (drunk) to the other areas of the hotel, and cause a little ruckus every now and then.

title: CAN'T WAIT TO GO BACK~~
body: i just checked out of the yotel today and was extremely pleased with my stay. My reservsation check in was 3pm yesterday. I went there at 1 to see the yobot and if i couldnt check in till 3 then i would make use of the yobot which is a robot in a class casing with storage bins that store your luggage before check in and even after check out! however i was greeted in the lobby by friendly staff and helped me at the check in kiosk to see if my room was ready 2 hours before check in and it was....at no extra cost. we got settled in our room which was located on the 17th floor with a nice view at night. we left the hotel and went off to explore and shop!!!! came back to the hotel around 530 and was able to take a quiet peaceful nap til 8pm. then i was out and about again til midnight. i check out this morning at 11am once again with the help of the awesome staff and stored my stuff with the yobot til i was ready to catch my bus back home at 4. this hotel was my first hotel in nyc and i dont think i would stay anywhere else. it was a great experience and i can't wait to return soon and really experience all the hotel has to offer including the restaurant/lounges/outside terrace. i stayed in a queen cabin which had a queen bed and bunk beds at $279 a night! totally worth it! mini kictchen on every floor which had a hot drink machine that offered coffer/cappucino/expresso/hot chololate all for free as well as water and a soda machine microwave and refrigerator. the one on our floor happened to be located right outside our room. its nice because its in its own room and u can only get in using your room key. i wont go on anymore. u get my drift.......i cant wait to go back!!!!!!

title: Great vibe, modern and easy for getting everywhere! Most of all though, clean.
body:
We stayed here for 3 nights tail end on Nov beginning of Dec and after reviewing all of the other choices of hotels I could have chosen, we were glad we chose Yotel! Having done lots of research, we got exactly what we expected. Can't understand though some of the previous reviewer comments. 
Yes the room was small but I would say 'functional' and perfect only for a short stay as there isn't a lot of hanging space although there are plenty of shelves and cubby holes. The issue of privacy I can't understand as there is a door for the toilet shower plus 2 blinds on the window; one blackout and one that let's light through. There is a curtain that you could draw right across the room that stops you seeing into the bathroom if that's an issue but as I told my wife 'hey, you've seen it all before!' I can't see why you would choose this type of room if you weren't a couple etc? I can understand if you were in a family room that it would be hard but for couples it's fine. As I said, the curtain obscures totally! As for the beds, yes they are a little hard; loved the electric controls to get it up and down but they could be more comply (I do have to point out though, I did sleep OK and they certainly are not the hardest I have slept on!)
As for the 'Galley' this always had plenty of stock in it, even at the busy weekend period and it is dead handy having it nearby when you fancy a coffee. Also, we found the breakfast absolutely fine. Yes the place gets busy but it was constantly replenished when we were there, even at 0900 on Sunday AM which is probably the busiest time! The muffins are delicious; I recommend the cranberry ones!! We opted for the $9.99 breakfast each day and never had to wait to be seated. The service was excellent and we had eggs (scrambled or fried) with bacon and toast plus coffee and with tax and tip, this came to $25 which I thought was reasonable. This also set us up with something warm before the hectic days ahead.
The location of Yotel is fine for getting around. It's in a busy part and the only time we felt remotely unsafe was when we walked past the Port Authority Bus Station but we did this numerous times day and night and nothing happened so it was probably us being overly concerned. We walked everywhere and normally walked down 42nd and hung a left up 9th Ave where there are lots and lots of eating places. This is where I would recommend everyone to use whilst at Yotel, it's got something for everyone! We ate in a nice Italian and a Pizza place and the price was reasonable for NY prices!! 
Getting there, we used the Newark express bus as I got fares for $5 each and is only a short 5-10 minute walk to the Hotel. If your flying into Newark and are on a budget, I would recommend this (I think it's $16 each way) and is certainly cheaper than than using yellow cabs and as is goes direct from the Airport to the PA Bus Stn (first stop) we arrived in 40 minutes.
Overall, I would thoroughly recommend Yotel and wouldn't think twice about staying here again but only as a couple. I would probably think twice if we came with my daughter in tow!!

title: Great place....great location
body:
Went to NYC for a holiday weekend. Found Yotel while searching for a hotel on hotels.com. Never heard about the hotel concept until this trip. 
What a great place to stay. Love the concept. Definitely will stay there again. 
Right along 42nd Street and only a few blocks from Time Square. Close to Javits Center and the Piers.

title: terrific location and very clean but hard bed
body: My husband and I were staying in NYC for four nights. The rooms are compact but the space is used efficiently. Checked in late on the first night. The staff were welcoming and checkin process was smooth. The rooms are clean and the shower is fantastic. Since we had limited time in NYC our days and nights were full of sightseeing so, for us the priority for the hotel was to provide a comfortable bed. We slept there the first night and checked out the next morning, in search of a better bed.

title: Fun hotel next to Time Square
body: What a cool hotel at a very reasonable price. The best use of space I have ever seen. The rooms are small but you have everything you need. If you are looking for space, the terrance and dining room and bar are huge. Plenty of room to hang out. The food was great...loved the sushi!!
